Estimation of agricultural carbon abatement costs using a marginal-productivity-based production-input model: evidence from Fujian Province, China
abstract: The shadow price of agricultural carbon emissions serves as a key indicator for quantifying the cost of carbon reduction in agriculture and for reflecting the associated opportunity costs. It has substantial theoretical and practical relevance for the green development and low-carbon transformation of agriculture under the dual-carbon goals. It holds significant theoretical and practical value for advancing green development and low-carbon transformation in agriculture under the dual-carbon goals. Drawing on marginal productivity theory, this study classifies agricultural carbon emissions as a production factor, builds a translog production function model, and employs ridge regression to address multicollinearity. Using panel data from nine prefecture-level cities in Fujian Province (2010–2023), we measure the shadow prices of agricultural carbon emissions across cities and conduct robustness tests via stochastic frontier analysis (SFA), exploring spatiotemporal evolutionary patterns and the drivers of regional disparities. The key findings are as follows: (1) Fujian’s agricultural carbon emission shadow prices show an overall sustained upward trend, with the economic opportunity cost of per-unit carbon reduction rising consistently across cities. (2) Significant regional disparities exist—the average shadow prices in eastern and northern Fujian remain among the highest in the …

title: Effect of boron nitride nanoplatelet loading on the thermomechanical performance, thermal stability and X-band electromagnetic interference shielding of carbon-fiber/epoxy laminates
abstract: Abstract Woven carbon-fiber/epoxy laminates containing 0, 0.5, and 2 wt.% boron nitride nanoplatelets (BNNPs), relative to the epoxy resin mass, were fabricated using the same processing route. Their thermomechanical behavior, thermal stability, and X-band electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding were evaluated using dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and shielding effectiveness (SE) measurements over 8–12 GHz. At 0.5 wt.% BNNP, the glassy storage modulus ( E ′) increased from 9.3 to 11.2 GPa, and the rubbery plateau modulus increased from 0.33 to 2.1 GPa. The loss factor (tan δ) peak temperature shifted from 95.84 to 105.23 °C, while the temperature at 5 % mass loss (Td5) increased from 305.95 to 314.04 °C. The residual mass at 900 °C increased from 68.53 % for the neat laminate to 72.38–72.93 % for the BNNP-containing laminates. The band-averaged total SE values were approximately 50, 46, and 43 dB for the laminates containing 0, 0.5, and 2 wt.% BNNP, respectively. Although the SE curves crossed at several frequencies, the band-averaged values decreased with increasing BNNP content. Among the formulations tested, the 0.5 wt.% BNNP laminate showed the most favorable thermomechanical response, with a reduction in band-averaged EMI shielding relative to the neat laminate.

title: PENGARUH FILLER BIOKARBON DAN CARBON BLACK TIPE N990 TERHADAP SIFAT DINAMIK KOMPOSIT KARET ALAM
abstract: Abstrak Material viskoelastik berbasis karet alam (NR) sering digunakan dalam aplikasi peredaman getaran, sehingga membutuhkan sifat dinamis dan peredaman yang memadai. Perilaku dinamis dan peredaman getaran komposit NR yang diisi dengan biokarbon turunan biomassa dan karbon hitam N990 diteliti dalam studi ini sebagai respons terhadap pengaruh jenis dan kadar pengisi. Pengisi biokarbon disintesis dari pati singkong dan kayu asam jawa melalui pirolisis, diikuti dengan penggilingan bola. Pengisi ini kemudian dimasukkan ke dalam NR dengan kadar 15, 30, dan 50 phr. Pengujian geser dinamis dan Analisis Proses Karet (RPA) diimplementasikan untuk menilai sifat dinamis komposit. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kinerja dinamis komposit NR sangat dipengaruhi oleh jenis dan kadar pengisi. Kekakuan geser, modulus geser efektif, dan kapasitas peredaman getaran semuanya meningkat dengan peningkatan kadar pengisi. Dibandingkan dengan senyawa NR kosong, biokarbon pati singkong meningkatkan modulus geser kompleks sebesar 159% pada pemuatan 50 phr, sedangkan biokarbon kayu asam jawa meningkatkannya sebesar 109%. Karbon hitam N990 hanya menghasilkan peningkatan sebesar 62,5%. Rasio redaman yang sesuai pada 50 phr meningkat dari sekitar 0,35% untuk karbon hitam N990 menjadi 0,85% dan 1,35% untuk biokarbon pati singkong dan kayu asam jawa, masing-masing, menunjukkan peningkatan kemampuan komposi…

title: Optimizing cross-border CCS policy: an integrated energy–carbon–cost framework for source–host credit allocation
abstract: Cross-border carbon capture and storage (CCS) can support industrial decarbonisation where emissions and storage resources are unevenly distributed. Existing optimisation studies mainly minimise techno-economic cost and rarely integrate energy penalties, country-level emissions accounting, domestic-versus-export allocation, and source–host credit sharing. This study develops a mixed-integer linear programming framework that selects domestic or export storage, shipping routes, offshore pipelines, and sinks while tracking operational emissions, costs, and source–host credit allocation. An anonymised Japan–Malaysia case includes two Japanese sources, two Malaysian sinks, and a domestic screening pathway. Domestic Japanese storage costs USD 0.327 billion/year, compared with USD 0.484 billion/year for full export. Under the Combined Competitiveness scenario, a combination of a lower Malaysian service fee, equal source–host credit sharing, and an upper-end published domestic-storage cost selects full export to MY-Sink 1 at USD 0.426 billion/year, with the capability of storing 2.674 MtCO<sub>2</sub>/year after shipping loss. Credit ownership changes economic and national accounting outcomes without changing routing. Malaysian storage and injection, shipping, and credit values give the largest local sensitivity responses. In summary, the framework provides a transparent method for ass…

title: Photochemically Mediated Oxidative Cross-coupling of Aminopyrazoles with 1-Thiosugars for the Synthesis of Thioglycosides
abstract: Abstract By harnessing visible-light excitation of a photocatalyst to initiate a single-electron transfer (SET) process, thereby activating glycosyl thiols to generate thiyl radicals and promote their coupling with aminopyrazoles, this work establishes an efficient photocatalytic strategy for C–S bond construction. This process involves radical addition for thioglycosyl incorporation, followed by oxidative deprotonation to furnish the target products in yields of up to 90%. Consequently, this method enables the efficient synthesis of diverse thioglycosylated pyrazole derivatives under mild conditions, exhibiting a broad substrate scope, excellent functional-group tolerance, and promising scalability, thus providing a green and sustainable synthetic approach.

title: Unraveling multi-behavior coupling in construction fall-from-height accidents: a complex network perspective
abstract: Purpose Evidence remains limited on how unsafe behaviors connect and progress directionally within construction accident sequences. This study investigates these relationships using 329 written fall-from-height (FFH) accident investigation reports from Jiangsu Province, China. Design/methodology/approach Text mining was integrated with complex network analysis. Unsafe behavior nodes were identified through coding and topic modeling, while a convolutional neural network was used to extract progressive and parallel relations from accident narratives. The resulting directed network comprised 71 nodes and 217 edges and was analyzed using degree, node strength, betweenness centrality, and shortest-path measures. Findings The resulting network exhibits a heterogeneous structure, with a limited number of unsafe behaviors occupying prominent positions across multiple structural measures. The analysis further identifies recurrent behavioral pathways linking unsafe acts during FFH accident development, indicating that documented accident processes involve interconnected rather than isolated behaviors. The identified directional relations represent reported behavioral progression in accident narratives. Practical implications The findings can support safety interventions that move beyond isolated unsafe acts by targeting structurally important behaviors together with their associated beha…

title: Room-Temperature Palladium-Catalyzed Aminative Suzuki–Miyaura Coupling of Arylthianthrenium Salts and Mechanistic Studies
abstract: Abstract The development of novel catalytic transformations that repurpose classical reagents to directly access structurally diverse products from the same starting materials has garnered significant interest. By eliminating the need to separately synthesize and purify new reagents, the chemical space reachable from existing functionalized intermediates can be increased multifold. Nitrogen insertion strategies can convert the C–C bond formed in traditional Suzuki–Miyaura coupling into a C–N–C bond, substantially expanding the explorable chemical space. Herein, building upon the arylthianthrenium salt strategy, we have developed a room-temperature palladium-catalyzed nitrogen-atom insertion coupling reaction, providing a new retrosynthetic disconnection strategy that can be directly applied to the late-stage functionalization (LSF) of complex drug molecules. Notably, this intermolecular three-component aminative coupling proceeds smoothly at room temperature, which not only aligns with the principles of green chemistry by obviating the need for heating apparatus and light-irradiation equipment, but also reduces energy consumption while enhancing reaction safety. To probe the mechanism, control experiments were conducted, and the catalytic reaction was monitored by NMR spectroscopy. Based on these results and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the barrier for the over…

title: Controlled Interfacial Electronic Coupling in Chemical Vapor Deposition-Grown WSe2 Monolayers on Au(111)
abstract: Abstract We report on the controlled growth and interface engineering of high-quality WSe2 monolayers on Au(111) using ambient-pressure chemical vapor deposition (CVD) combined with comprehensive surface-sensitive characterization in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV). The as-grown films exhibit a selenium buffer layer, which enables the formation of a weakly coupled WSe2 phase at the metal interface, as revealed by scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and low-energy electron diffraction (LEED). Annealing in UHV removes the selenium buffer layer and leads to the emergence of a pronounced moiré superstructure and a transition toward a strongly coupled WSe2 phase. Furthermore, this transformation is accompanied by pronounced modifications of the electronic structure, including phase-dependent changes in the valence band structure observed by angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES), a hybridization-induced metallization measured by scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), and a significant decrease in the work function determined by field emission resonance (FER) and ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy (UPS). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm strong WSe2–Au hybridization and the presence of the mid-gap states for the strongly coupled phase, whereas the Se8 buffer layer weakens the interaction of WSe2 with Au, so that its electronic structure is close to that for t…

title: Annulative Suzuki–Miyaura Coupling for the Synthesis of Highly Fluorescent Near-Infrared PAH[ b ]-Fused BODIPYs
abstract: Abstract A one-pot annulative Suzuki–Miyaura strategy was developed for the synthesis of highly fluorescent, near-infrared (NIR)-emissive polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH)-fused BODIPYs. Tetrahalogenated BODIPYs reacted with 1,2-bis(pinacolato)boryl arene or alkene via a fourfold cross-coupling/annulation cascade under Pd(PPh3)4 catalysis, furnishing phenanthro[b]- or naphtho[b]-fused products in 32–70% yields without isolation of intermediates. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed slightly twisted frameworks (dihedral angles: 3.17–10.01°), and NICS(0) calculations confirmed strong local aromaticity. Photophysical studies displayed intense absorption at 658–675 nm and narrow NIR emission at 670–690 nm, together with small Stokes shifts (≤322 cm–1) and high fluorescence quantum yields (ΦF = 0.46–0.68). Their weak solvatochromism and substantial HOMO–LUMO overlap indicate that the emissive excited states are predominantly locally excited (LE) in character. Cyclic voltammetry demonstrated narrow electrochemical band gaps (1.51–1.70 eV) and low LUMO energy levels (–3.82 to –3.88 eV for 3a–c and 4e), while DFT and TD-DFT calculations showed that the lowest-energy excitation is dominated by a HOMO → LUMO π → π* transition. This modular annulation strategy provides concise access to rigid PAH-fused BODIPYs that combine efficient NIR emission with high fluorescence efficiency,…

title: Supramolecular Aggregate-Functionalized Biomass Radiative Cooling Aerogel for Building Energy Conservation
abstract: Abstract Biomass aerogels have emerged as promising passive radiant cooling materials, offering a sustainable strategy for mitigating global warming. However, simultaneously achieving high solar reflectance, flame retardancy, and mechanical robustness remains challenging, substantially limiting their deployment in complex environments and long-term energy-saving applications. Here, we report a supramolecular aggregate-functionalized biomass aerogel (AMPx), which integrates effective radiative cooling, fire resistance, and mechanical stability. The aggregate is synthesized through supramolecular self-assembly reactions, using melamine (ME) and phytic acid (PA) as building blocks. By incorporating these aggregates into the sodium alginate matrix and utilizing directional freezing technology, the honeycomb-structured AMPx is prepared. The resulting aerogel exhibits a high solar reflectance of 92% and an atmospheric window emittance of 94%, enabling a temperature reduction of 11.4 °C relative to a commercial aerogel under direct sunlight. Building energy simulations further predict annual cooling-energy savings of up to 54.79%. Moreover, sufficient incorporation of ME-PA aggregates endows AMPx with rapid self-extinguishing properties. Interestingly, incorporating ME-PA aggregates increases the aerogel’s compressive strength and modulus to 3.71 and 12.17 MPa, respectively, represent…

title: Cross-stress transcriptomic integration in Marchantia polymorpha reveals stress-specific expression of regulated cell-death-associated genes
abstract: Regulated cell death (RCD) contributes to plant development, stress adaptation, and immunity, but whether RCD-associated genes show conserved transcriptional responses across diverse stresses remains unclear. Here, we performed a comparative reanalysis of publicly available Marchantia polymorpha RNA-seq datasets to investigate recurrent and stress-specific expression of RCD-associated genes. We uniformly processed 36 RNA-seq samples from three independent studies, yielding nine stress-versus-control comparisons: eight abiotic (seven from one study and an independent high-light experiment) and one pathogen infection. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified for each of the 9 stress datasets compared to their respective controls, which were then examined for shared DEGs among different sets of stress vs. control comparisons. A curated list of 14 RCD-associated genes previously identified in M. polymorpha were used to examine conservation of transcriptional response. Integrated expression data were additionally examined using weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) after batch correction of dataset. Of 34 DEGs shared across all nine comparisons, only 12 changed in the same direction in every comparison. The 34 genes included two transcription factors, an AP2/ERF-family factor (Mp5g22160) and a bHLH factor (Mp2g00890), which were upregulated in infection a…

title: Associations between Vehicle Safety Systems and Pilon Fracture Severity Are Revealed by Using a Novel Objective Quantitative Fracture Energy Metric
abstract: <div>Pilon fractures are a severe lower-extremity injury sustained in motor vehicle crashes, characterized by high-axial loading that drives the talus into the tibial plafond and frequently results in poor long-term functional outcomes and post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA). Despite advances in surgical management, clinical complications remain frequent in 20–50% of cases in literature, which highlights the need to identify modifiable upstream risk factors in the motor vehicle crash environment. The Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) is the predominant tool for crash injury severity analysis, and it classifies all closed pilon fractures uniformly as moderate (AIS 2) regardless of comminution or imparted energy and poorly predicts long-term functional outcomes. An existing fracture energy severity metric quantifies the acute mechanical energy delivered to bone during fracture and has been linked to PTOA development. This study represents one of the first multivariate applications of the fracture energy metric to crash data, examining how occupant demographics, crash kinematics, and vehicle safety systems relate to pilon fracture severity. Fifty belted occupants with Orthopaedic Trauma Association (OTA) Type B or Type C pilon fractures were identified through the Crash Injury Research and Engineering Network (CIREN) database. Local pollution challenges in the global energy transition: air quality near hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical plants in the Congolese Copperbelt
abstract: Abstract The Congolese Copperbelt is a major source of copper and cobalt for the global energy transition, but mineral processing creates substantial and poorly documented local air-pollution risks. This study presents a multi-pollutant, multi-directional, and seasonally resolved assessment of ambient air quality around one hydrometallurgical plant in Kakanda and one pyrometallurgical plant in Lubumbashi. We monitored SO₂, NO₂, PM 10 , PM 2.5 , total suspended particles (TSP), Cu, and Pb during four campaigns in 2022, along with meteorological conditions and Air Quality Index (AQI) calculations. Most mean concentrations were below Congolese regulatory limits, although SO₂, Cu, and Pb showed episodic exceedances. By contrast, SO₂, NO₂, PM 10 , and PM 2.5 frequently exceeded the 2021 WHO health-based guidelines. Raw peak concentrations reached 6.0 mg/m 3 for SO₂ in the northern sector of the hydrometallurgical site and 5.0 mg/m 3 for NO₂ in the northern sector of the pyrometallurgical site. SO₂ dominated at the hydrometallurgical site, whereas NO₂ dominated at the pyrometallurgical site, consistent with the respective process profiles. The most severe conditions occurred in July, at the peak of the dry season, when the eastern sectors reached AQI values of 373.20 (Hazardous; SO₂-driven) at the hydrometallurgical site and 239.93 (Very Unhealthy; NO₂-driven) at the pyrometallurgica…

Prioritising BIM–immersive technology integration in Vietnam: a delphi–AHP study
abstract: Purpose Despite growing attention to building information modelling (BIM)- immersive technologies (ImT) integration, limited empirical evidence shows how technical and non-technical criteria should be prioritised in emerging construction markets or how these priorities relate to institutional conditions. This study aims to address this gap in Vietnamese building projects. Design/methodology/approach A sequential modified Delphi-analytic hierarchy process (AHP) design was adopted. The Delphi process validated 53 integration criteria, followed by an AHP involving 15 Vietnamese experts. Criteria were assessed across five attributes and interpreted through Institutional Theory as a post-prioritisation lens. Findings The results show that BIM-ImT integration in Vietnam is driven mainly by foundational capabilities. Technical priorities include computational processing, semantic data exchange, sensing integration, interface usability, model accuracy and data standardisation, whereas photorealistic rendering and cloud optimisation receive lower weightings. Non-technical priorities include user familiarity, workforce confidence, effective tool use, cost considerations, system oversight and collaborative effectiveness. These patterns indicate that organisations prioritise stability, usability and operational readiness over advanced technological features. Practical implications The find…

title: Looks like a surgeon? Impact of anthropometry on the kinematics of surgical novices: counterbalanced cross-over design study of minimally invasive surgery
abstract: Abstract To investigate the relationship between anthropometric measurements of surgical novices and their upper-body kinematics during laparoscopic (LAP) and robotic assisted (RA) tasks. A counterbalanced crossover design study was conducted. Participants were assigned by systematic alternating allocation to first perform tasks on an Inovus laparoscopic trainer (LAP) or da Vinci Xi system (RA) in a simulation suite, whilst wearing three motion analysis sensors (upper left and right arms, and mid thoracic). In total 57 surgical novices (33 female, 24 male) were recruited. Kinematic data were available for 54 participants. Height, elbow height and arm span of female participants were significantly lower than male participants, 165.6 ± 5.42 cm, 107.9 ± 4.9 cm and 163.2 ± 10.2 cm versus 181 ± 8.3 cm 118.3 ± 6.6 cm and 182.7 ± 10.3 cm respectively ( p < 0.0001). Greater jerk and angular velocity were demonstrated for LAP versus RA tasks ( p < 0.0001). Significant interactions between anthropometry and surgical modality were observed; decreasing elbow height correlated with significantly greater angular velocity during LAP tasks (interaction p < 0.001; jerk p = 0.005), whereas no such relationship was observed for RA tasks. The interactions for height did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. There is an inverse relationship between anthropometric measure…

title: Exploration of Innovative Paths for Empowering Art and Design Teaching with AIGC
abstract: Against the backdrop of the continuous advancement of the Belt and Road Initiative and the "going global" of vocational education, the art and design major of China's vocational education is confronted with numerous challenges in overseas school-running, such as the shortage of cross-cultural teaching staff and the great difficulty in the local adaptation of teaching resources. Under such circumstances, it is necessary to transform the teaching paradigm from the previous "skill-oriented" model to a "creativity-oriented" one.This study adopts the methods of literature analysis and case study to establish an evaluation and teaching model framework of "AIGC Intelligent Assistance – Cross-cultural Integration – Dual-teacher Collaboration". Combined with relevant empirical cases, it explores how AIGC can boost the going global of vocational education and its practical paths from three dimensions: curriculum reconstruction, evaluation upgrading and faculty construction.The research finds that AIGC can break down the barriers among language, culture and teaching resources through a cross-cultural translation mechanism. Its "teacher-student-AI" ternary collaboration model has achieved practical results in overseas school-running regions, serving as a key support for reshaping overseas teaching and cross-cultural communication paths.Studies show that the innovative path established rely…

title: Awareness and adoption of industry 4.0 technologies among construction professionals in Ghana: a gendered perspective
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine gender differences in awareness and adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies among construction professionals in Ghana, addressing limited empirical evidence on whether male and female professionals experience different levels of engagement with emerging digital construction technologies in a developing-country context. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 350 construction professionals in Ghana. Gender-disaggregated analysis was used to examine differences in Industry 4.0 awareness and adoption. The study was informed by Diffusion of Innovations (DOI), the Technology–Organisation–Environment (TOE) framework and Gendered Organisations Theory. Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, partial least squares structural equation modelling measurement-model assessment, reliability analysis and K-means cluster analysis were used. Findings The results indicate moderate-to-high overall awareness and adoption, with a statistically significant gender-associated difference. Male respondents reported higher overall awareness/adoption scores than female respondents. K-means analysis identified distinct high- and low-awareness/adoption groups, indicating heterogeneity in digital engagement. The gender difference is interpreted through organisational and institutional conditions discussed in the TOE fr…

title: Advanced computational fluid dynamics for catalytic reactor design, multiphysics modelling, optimization, and digital transformation
abstract: Abstract Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is transitioning from a predictive flow-simulation technique into a central enabling technology for the design, intensification, scale-up, and digitalization of catalytic reactors. This review critically synthesizes advances reported across fixed-bed, packed-bed, fluidized-bed, trickle-bed, slurry bubble-column, monolithic, membrane, and microreactor systems, spanning chemical, petrochemical, environmental, and energy applications. Rather than treating reactor configurations and numerical methods independently, the review establishes a multiscale framework linking hydrodynamics, heterogeneous reaction kinetics, porous-media transport, heat and mass transfer, radiation, catalyst-scale phenomena, and reactor-scale performance. Particular emphasis is placed on the evolving integration of Large Eddy Simulation, Direct Numerical Simulation, Population Balance Models, artificial intelligence, Physics-Informed Neural Networks, digital twins, and high-performance computing. Their capabilities are critically compared in resolving conversion, selectivity, pressure drop, thermal gradients, species transport, catalyst utilization, and multiphase interactions, with explicit consideration of the trade-offs among predictive fidelity, computational cost, scalability, and industrial relevance. The influence of turbulence closure, mesh resolution, reac…

title: Reinforcement learning in construction engineering and management: a scientometric review of intellectual structure, thematic evolution and application maturity
abstract: Purpose Reinforcement learning (RL) addresses sequential, stochastic decision processes across construction engineering and management. This study aims to analyze the intellectual structure, thematic evolution and empirical maturity of RL across the asset lifecycle to inform evidence-based industry adoption. Design/methodology/approach A corpus of 1,198 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science was systematically screened and analyzed. Scientometric mapping with Louvain community detection delineated thematic clusters, while a three-level rubric classified deployment maturity across simulation, controlled testing and operational field demonstration. Findings Six research fronts structure the discipline, comprising building energy at 52.8%, infrastructure maintenance at 17.4%, autonomous robotics at 11.7%, scheduling at 6.3%, safety monitoring at 3.7% and structural design and materials at 3.2%. Output expanded from 2020 onward, representing 92.7% of the corpus, led by policy-gradient and actor-critic architectures. Across all fronts, 85.7% of studies remain in simulation, 12.3% achieve controlled testing and 2.0% achieve field demonstration, with 20 of 24 trials in building operations. Practical implications Facility managers can evaluate RL controllers against operational metering data where field validation exists. For earthmoving machinery, crane operations, dyna…

title: Lesson design through the lens of variation theory: comparative insights from Sweden and Türkiye
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how primary school mathematics lessons are implemented in Sweden and Türkiye when teaching the same object of learning and deepen understanding of how instructional design is shaped by contextual conditions and professional practices. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in variation theory, the analysis focused on how teachers vary and make discernible aspects of the object of learning through instructional enactment. A cross-case design was employed to initially compare instruction in 16 primary mathematics lessons, eight each from Sweden and Türkiye, to analytically identify four shared content areas: mental arithmetic, algorithms, problem-solving, and statistical graphs. Swedish teachers followed the model of learning study and planned lessons collaboratively, while Turkish teachers had no prior knowledge of variation theory and enacted lessons based on national subject plans (e.g. textbooks and curriculum documents). Teachers' enactment of the object of learning during instruction was analyzed using the framework of variation theory to identify patterns in how aspects of the object of learning were made visible. Findings The results revealed significant differences in the dimensions of variation of the object of learning in instructional design. Swedish teachers employed the dimension of contrast and meta-representational talk to emph…

title: Realizing the Noumenal Republic: Forst and Kant on Representation and Institutional Design
abstract: Abstract In The Noumenal Republic , Rainer Forst understands democracy as a demand for justice grounded in the ‘right to justification’. This right stipulates that justificatory reasons must be (i) reciprocally and generally justifiable in their content/form and (ii) generated through procedures in which all affected figure as co-authors. Despite the numerous strengths of this theory, I argue that Forst’s account encounters a problem when addressing the justification of commonplace cases of representation: although each dimension independently provides normative space for justifying representative practices, their simultaneous application generates mutually undermining outcomes. After showing how Kant deals with this issue, I invite Forst to further elaborate on how his Kantian democratic theory plays out at an institutional level.

title: Developing AI Literacy OER: A Literature-Informed Rubric for Design and Review
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly entered higher education classrooms, and AI literacy is now widely treated as a core competency for university learners. Yet university-produced and openly licensed AI literacy materials remain scarce, uneven across regions and disciplines, and often tied to a single commercial tool. This study addresses the supply problem through literature-informed rubric development. A narrative synthesis of a purposive corpus drawn from AI literacy frameworks, AI literacy pedagogy, open educational resource (OER)-enabled pedagogy, and recent AI-in-OER guidance was conducted to derive a seven-principle rubric for AI literacy OER design and review. Each principle pairs evidence with a concrete design and review cue: what an OER author can build and what a reviewer can inspect. The synthesis also identified five recurring topic domains that organize AI literacy OER across courses and institutions: tool-agnostic prompting, output evaluation, bias awareness, accessibility, and citation and integrity. The study contributes a rubric, a topic domain structure, and design and review cues that operationalize the rubric. It does not report empirical effectiveness data but is offered as a foundation for future learner outcome studies and independent rubric reapplication.
venue: Journal of Open Educational Resources in Higher Education

title: Injection Target: An Unexamined Variable in Botulinum Toxin Therapy for Chronic Anal Fissure
Rethinking Formative Feedback in HyFlex and Applied Contexts: A Distributed, Time-Decoupled, and Multi-Touch Design Framework
abstract: In applied learning, we aspire to design a course structure with formative feedback as close as possible to the point of applied learning. However, in practice, logistics do not always allow this clean and simple integration. HyFlex learning environments further challenge instructional design by allowing students to tackle learning activities asynchronously, away from other students who choose the in-person class experience. This study examines the design strategies for learning and formative feedback in four undergraduate applied learning courses in manufacturing and engineering technology. A cross-case analysis examines how learning is configured when students engage with preparation, application, feedback, and reflection at different times and through different modalities. Findings demonstrate a learning support structure distributed across instructional structures and activities, time-decoupled, with multi-touch exposure. While these patterns emerge in HyFlex classes, they apply to many traditional applied learning course environments. This paper proposes a conceptual framework that serves as a design lens for partially asynchronous applied learning environments.

title: Design of a fixed-time multi-layer neural network controller for underactuated autonomous underwater vehicles
Revolutionizing the tomato cultivation: advances and frontiers in virus-resistant tomato breeding
abstract: Plant viruses are major pathogens that significantly reduce the quality and yield of tomato crops. The most influential viruses belong to the genera Crinivirus, Begomovirus, Tobamovirus, and Potyvirus. Tomato breeders have successfully incorporated virus-resistance genes, such as Ty, Sw, Tm, and Pot 1, from wild germplasms into cultivated varieties. However, the challenge remains that most resistance genes confer only qualitative resistance, making them vulnerable to new viruses, recombination, and mixed infections. To our knowledge, this review is the first to systematically compare the synergy and complementarity among three antiviral breeding strategies—conventional R-gene pyramiding (e.g. Ty, Sw, Tm), RNA interference (RNAi)-based transgenics, and CRISPR/Cas genome editing—in tomato. We also innovatively incorporate the emerging genus Amalgavirus into the antiviral framework and propose targeted countermeasures against its escape mechanisms, including synthetic NLR decoys and Cas13-mediated transcriptional degradation. Using the three breeding methodologies, we concluded by outlining the difficulties and offering recommendations for future improvements in tomato antiviral breeding.

title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with virtual knockout analysis identifies FOS as an epithelial-associated candidate gene in chronic atrophic gastritis
Digital virtual ward versus standard of care for acute atrial fibrillation: A single centre non-randomised pilot comparison of clinical outcomes and cost
abstract: Abstract Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) incurs significant healthcare costs, mainly from acute hospitalisations. Digitally-enabled models could provide hospital-level care at home for selected patients, but evidence in acute care remains inconsistent. Methods In a propensity score-matched, non-randomised comparative study using real-world data (January–December 2022). Adults with acute AF admitted to the AF virtual ward (AFVW) were matched 1:1 to standard-of-care (SOC) inpatients meeting AFVW eligibility criteria. The primary outcome was a composite of emergency readmissions, urgent care attendance, or death within 90 days. A separate cost analysis was undertaken from the National Health Service (NHS) secondary care perspective. Results Ninety-one AFVW patients were matched to 91 SOC patients. The primary outcome did not differ at 90 days (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.34-1.10). Emergency bed-day use following readmission was higher in AFVW cohort (0.42 vs 0.07 per spell; ratio 6.04; 95% CI 2.70-15.90), although the readmission rate itself was similar (7.7% versus 7.0%). Thirty-day emergency attendances, outpatient appointments, and mortality were similar. In a separate, clinically screened but non-propensity-matched population (75 AFVW, 315 SOC patients), mean direct secondary-care cost per patient was £948 versus £1,631, an adjusted saving of £642. Religious Tolerance in the Foreign Policy of Indonesia: Soft Power, Religious Diplomacy and Normative Export
abstract: This article explores how Indonesia has transformed its domestic experience of religious tolerance and of moderate Islam into a resource of foreign policy. It analyses the Bali Democracy Forum, the Bogor Message, the Religion of Twenty forum and the transnational activities of Nahdlatul Ulama and Muhammadiyah, and sets out through them the principal mechanisms of Indonesian religious diplomacy. The article argues that Indonesia does not export a ready-made political model to other Muslim countries; rather it brings into the international arena a normative experience centred upon the compatibility of Islam, democracy, national statehood and religious diversity. The study conceptualizes this process as religious soft power and as normative export. (CC

title: The Dark Side of Utopia: Institutional Erosion, Secret Power, and Democratic Backsliding in the Star Trek Universe
abstract: Abstract “When push comes to shove, are we willing to sacrifice our principles in order to survive?” Doctor Julian Bashir asks at the end of “Inquisition” (1998). The Star Trek franchise has attempted to answer this question for nearly thirty years. I argue that the Section 31 storyline, introduced in Star Trek: Deep Space Nine and revisited in subsequent series, is an allegory for democratic backsliding. DS9 treats the secret, unaccountable Section 31 as a scandal, while Star Trek: Discovery treats it as routine. This mirrors the slow erosion of norms Levitsky and Ziblatt describe. American surveillance after 9/11 followed a similar path. The on-screen evolution of Section 31 raises the question of why the public accepts such organizations. Perceived threat leads citizens to trade civil liberties for security. Many Americans also dislike visible political conflict and prefer decision-makers without an obvious agenda. Trek initially depicts Section 31 as successful but still abhorrent, so the objection is not about effectiveness. But the allegory does have limits. We rarely see the Federation’s politics on screen, and we never see political parties depicted. Trek , therefore, places the threat to democracy outside internal politics. Real-world backsliding happens within it.

title: SEASONAL SURVEILLANCE OF MOSQUITO EGGS AND LARVAE IN VILLAGES SURROUNDING THE CHANA POWER PLANT, SONGKHLA PROVINCE, THAILAND
abstract: ABSTRACT Mosquito population dynamics in industrial-adjacent communities are driven by complex interactions between seasonality and anthropogenic habitats. This study investigated seasonal abundance, species composition, and spatial oviposition patterns of mosquito eggs and larvae surrounding the Chana Power Plant, Thailand. Ovitraps and larval surveys were conducted across 3 seasonal phases (preoutbreak, outbreak, and postoutbreak), using a census approach. Data were analyzed via chi-square tests and a 2-part Hurdle model (logistic and negative binomial regression) to account for zero inflation and overdispersion. Mosquito dynamics exhibited a decoupling of oviposition stability from larval abundance; ovitrap positivity showed no significant seasonal variation, whereas larval indices—House Index (HI), Container Index (CI), Breteau Index (BI), and Pupal Index (PI)—peaked significantly during the outbreak phase. Aedes aegypti exhibited a significant increase from preoutbreak (60.61%) to postoutbreak (86.44%); odds ratio (OR) = 4.14, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.50–11.51, P = 0.01. Conversely, Ae. albopictus declined from a preoutbreak peak (45.45%) during the postoutbreak phase (OR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.14–0.85, P = 0.02) . Spatial analysis revealed a significant indoor oviposition preference during the outbreak (61.49% vs. 39.18%, P < 0.001), with Ae. aegypti favoring domestic c…

title: Advances in Plant Electrical Signals for Plant Health Monitoring and Smart Agriculture
abstract: Plant electrical signals are fast electrophysiological responses to environmental stimuli, physiological regulation and stress. Because they often change before visible symptoms appear, they are attractive indicators for early plant-health monitoring and for sensing in precision agriculture. Research in this area has moved from recording single action potentials to analyzing the plant electrome, and now draws on flexible wearable electrodes, implantable and electrochemical sensors, machine learning, multi-source data fusion and edge-cloud computing. This review follows the technical chain from mechanism to application. We first summarize the physiological basis of the main signal types and how they relate to biotic and abiotic stress. We then compare acquisition technologies, including conventional electrodes, flexible wearable devices, microneedles and electrochemical sensors for biochemical markers. Next, we discuss preprocessing, multi-scale feature extraction, and recognition with conventional machine learning, deep learning and multi-source fusion. Finally, we examine applications in environmental sensing and stress identification and outline the remaining obstacles to field use. Most published results still come from laboratory or greenhouse studies with small datasets and non-standard protocols. Progress toward field deployment will depend on standardized acquisition and…

title: Understanding Reactive and Proactive Extremism - The Transforming Power of Safety in Education
abstract: This article examines extremism as a psychological and relational challenge, focusing on education’s role in preventing violent extremism. Drawing primarily on psychological perspectives, the article suggests that violent extremism is often rooted in emotional distress and disconnection, and in unmet needs for belonging and significance that may interact with ideological narratives. The Transforming Power of Safety (TPS) model and the related concepts of reactive and proactive extremism are introduced as a conceptual framework to illustrate how emotional disconnection may shape pathways to violent extremism. The model suggests that emotional safety and belonging may support regulation, connection with self and others and reflective capacity necessary for democratic participation. The discussion highlights the implications of this understanding for educational practice and argues that preventing violent extremism requires moving beyond ideological counterarguments by adopting trauma‑informed and relational approaches that foster emotional safety and strengthen the capacities supported by the TPS model. Education is understood as a humanising force with the potential to counter disconnection, strengthen democratic resilience, and address the challenges of polarisation and disinformation in contemporary society. Keywords: violent extremism, emotional safety, Transforming Power of …

title: Excessive mitochondrial fission in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury: Pathophysiological relevance and potential cardioprotective modulation by plant-derived interventions and electroacupuncture
abstract: Myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MI/RI) remains an unresolved problem despite reperfusion therapies, including percutaneous coronary intervention. Mitochondria are central mediators of reperfusion-associated cardiomyocyte injury, with excessive fission implicated as a potentially important mechanism linking acute metabolic stress to fragmentation, bioenergetic failure, and cell death. Reactive oxygen species, Ca2+ overload, mitochondrial permeability transition pore opening and membrane-potential loss promote dynamin-related protein 1-centered (Drp1-centered) fission, often involving mitochondrial fission factor, mitochondrial fission 1 protein and site-specific Drp1 phosphorylation. By disrupting mitochondrial networks and oxidative phosphorylation, this process contributes to cytochrome c release, apoptosis, microvascular dysfunction and impaired recovery. Impaired mitofusin 1/2-mediated and optic atrophy 1-mediated fusion limits repair and quality control, supporting investigation of this fission-dominant imbalance as a target for cardioprotection. Preclinical studies suggest plant-derived natural products, multi-component botanical preparations and electroacupuncture may influence this imbalance. Reported effects include attenuated Drp1 signaling, altered fusion-protein expression, preserved membrane potential, inhibited permeability transition, reduced oxidative str…

title: Integrating Communication and Cognitive Theories in Virtual Reality-Based Physics Learning: Achievement, Engagement, and Social Interaction in Senior High School
abstract: This two-school quasi-experimental study examined a bundled immersive virtual reality (VR) instructional model for Grade 11 optics that combined structured communication with cognitive scaffolding. Of 120 screened students, 102 entered four intact classes and 60 complete cases (30 per condition) were analyzed after six 90-minute sessions. Achievement was assessed before and immediately after the intervention; engagement questionnaires and structured observation captured additional outcomes. Posttest achievement favored the integrated VR condition (M = 82.63, SD = 6.91) over conventional instruction (M = 74.28, SD = 7.44), mean difference = 8.35, t(58) = 4.50, p < .001, Cohen's d = 1.16. A baseline-adjusted analysis similarly favored the VR condition, F(1, 57) = 20.45, p < .001, partial eta squared = .264. Cognitive, affective, and behavioral engagement and observed social-interaction quality were also higher in the VR group. These results pertain to a combined instructional package rather than an isolated VR effect. The four-class allocation, 50\% complete-case retention, short duration, and absence of delayed assessment constrain causal and longitudinal interpretation.

title: Cultivating Discovery: Building a Research-Centered Learning Ecosystem Through Authentic Undergraduate Applied Research in Plant Science
abstract: Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experiences (CUREs) emerged as powerful approaches for promoting student engagement, scientific literacy, workforce preparation and applied learning. However, despite the increasing adoption across different Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) disciplines, comparatively few published examples describe organismal and plant science CUREs, particularly at primarily undergraduate institutions (PUIs). This reflective case study describes the development and evolution of an eight-week-long Plant Physiology (BIO 440) CURE at Missouri Western State University (MWSU), centered on investigating the effects of the allelopathic molecule L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (L-DOPA) on plant growth and development.

title: Attitudes and perceptions toward the use of artificial intelligence chatbots for peer review in medical journals: a large-scale, international cross-sectional survey
abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence chatbots (AICs) are increasingly being considered for use in scholarly peer review to assist with tasks such as identifying methodological issues, verifying references, and improving language clarity. However, concerns remain regarding their reliability, ethical implications, and transparency. Evidence on how medical journal peer reviewers perceive the role and impact of AICs is limited. This study explored reviewers’ familiarity with AICs, perceived benefits and challenges, ethical concerns, and anticipated future roles in peer review. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of medical journal peer reviewers. Corresponding author information was extracted from MEDLINE-indexed articles added to PubMed within a six-week period. A total of 72,851 authors were invited via email to participate; those who self-identified as peer reviewers were eligible. The 29-item survey assessed familiarity with AICs and perceptions of their benefits and limitations in peer review. The survey was administered via SurveyMonkey from April 28 to June 16, 2025, with two reminder emails sent during the data collection period. Results Of 66,679 email invitations, a total of 1260 respondents provided survey responses (response rate: 1.9%), of whom 1157 met the eligibility criteria, and 1077 answered the main survey questions. Most participants were…

title: Peer Learning for Applied Engineering Technology Education
abstract: This study examines the implementation and student perceptions of a flexible peer learning approach in applied engineering technology education, with the goal of combining peer collaboration with student autonomy in a practical, workplace-like learning environment. The approach was used in MET 132 (Manufacturing Methods) and MET 372 (Programmable Logic Controllers) through in-class assignments and laboratory-based activities. Unlike traditional peer learning models with assigned groups, students were given full autonomy to collaborate freely with classmates or work independently. Activities were also designed as open-book and open-note, allowing students to use course materials, previous examples, digital resources, and other approved resources. Data sources included instructor reflections and student responses to open-ended survey questions. The findings showed that students generally valued the flexible structure and reported that peer collaboration helped them discuss questions, confirm their understanding, solve problems more efficiently, and experience workplace-like collaboration. Although some challenges were noted, including unequal peer support and occasional difficulty following multiple discussions, students generally viewed flexibility and freedom of choice positively. These findings suggest that combining peer collaboration with student agency can provide a practic…

title: Longitudinal bidirectional associations between executive functioning and peer victimization in the early school years: A parallel growth model approach
abstract: Abstract Peer victimization during early schooling has been linked to executive functioning (EF), yet little is known about their longitudinal associations. This study examined bidirectional associations between peer victimization and EF using four waves (2013–2016) from the Early Childhood Longitudinal Study–Kindergarten Cohort (nbaseline ≈ 13,840; 49% female; Mage(baseline) ≈ 8 years; US sample). Applying bivariate latent growth modeling, results indicated that peer victimization followed a nonlinear trajectory with an initial decline followed by stabilization. Lower intercept-level EF predicted less steep declines in peer victimization (βs = [−.11, −.12]; ps = [.002, <.001]). Importantly, higher intercept-level peer victimization was associated with greater increases in cognitive flexibility over time (β = .17, p < .001). These findings inform understanding of cognitive adaptation to early social stressors.

FINANCIAL SECRECY, CHARACTERISTICS OF CORPORATE TAX HAVENS AND TAX REVENUE PERFORMANCE: CLASSIFICATION OF COUNTRIES THROUGH CLUSTER ANALYSIS
abstract: This study aims to identify country profiles based on financial secrecy, corporate tax haven characteristics and tax revenue performance. The analysis includes 49 countries and three variables: the Haven Score of the Corporate Tax Haven Index (CTHI), the Secrecy Score of the Financial Secrecy Index (FSI) published by the Tax Justice Network, and total tax revenue as a percentage of GDP from the OECD Global Revenue Statistics database. K-Means clustering was used to classify the countries and the classification was compared with Ward.D2 hierachical clustering. The results of the correlation analysis show that there is a significant negative correlation between financial secrecy and tax revenue and there is no statistically significant relationship between corporate tax haven characteristics and tax revenue. The clustering analysis identified two different country profiles. The first cluster consists of 32 countries with lower Haven and Secrecy Scores and a higher average tax revenue ratio. The second cluster is composed of 17 countries with higher Haven and Secrecy Scores but a lower tax revenue ratio. The average tax revenue difference between the two clusters is 14.60 percentage points. Overall, the results highlight different country profiles in the sample concerning financial secrecy, corporate tax haven characteristics and tax revenue performance.

title: Vehicle Front-End Architecture as a Driving Factor in Occupant Injury Risk during Vehicle-Guardrail Impacts: A Hybrid III Dummy-Based Numerical Study
abstract: <div>The performance of Midwest Guardrail Systems (MGS) during impact with electric vehicles (EVs) has raised concerns with recent observations demonstrating a higher susceptibility to rail failures. These failures are hypothesized to be related to EV-specific design, including variations in front-end geometry and inertial properties. Current guardrail evaluations rely on two vehicle types, a small car and a pickup truck, potentially overlooking sensitivity to front-end geometry variations, potentially leading to unanticipated impact responses. Additionally, the extent to which geometry influences occupant injury risks and trends during vehicle-guardrail impact remains insufficiently investigated. The objective of this study is to quantify the influence of vehicle front-end geometry on occupant injury risk during vehicle-guardrail impacts using finite element (FE) simulations. Occupant injury risk is analyzed using Hybrid III anthropomorphic test device (ATD)-based injury criteria and flail space-based vehicle severity metrics to identify trends and relationship between geometric variations and injury probability. Front-end geometry data from the Insurance Institute of Highway Safety (IIHS) were analyzed to identify parameters and ranges associated with adverse MGS performance. Cumulative damage sequential preventive maintenance strategy for shock resilient machines with prior usage and non-constant shock magnitude
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a modified cumulative damage sequential preventive maintenance (CDSPM) model that addresses the limitations of traditional cumulative shock sequential models by incorporating three realistic factors often ignored in maintenance planning: prior damage in used machines, shock dampening effects and non-constant shock magnitudes. The research seeks to provide a more practical decision-making tool for industries, particularly in developing countries, that rely heavily on fairly-used equipment exposed to complex shock environments. Design/methodology/approach The study modifies the existing CDSPM model by introducing a non-zero initial damage state (R0 > 0), a shock dampening factor αl which is defined as the proportion of shock damage absorbed by the machine. This provides a mathematical mechanism for representing the protective effect of built-in shock-resistance components. The effective shock damage transmitted to the machine is represented by 1-αl100% with 0⩽αl⩽1. This formulation distinguishes between the physical magnitude of an external shock and the actual damage transmitted to the machine. It therefore provides a theoretical basis for incorporating mechanical protection into stochastic reliability models rather than assuming that the entire shock magnitude contributes directly to cumulative damage. title: Direct Enantioselective Construction of C3-Nitroalkylated Pyrroles by an Amine-Catalyzed Michael/Paal–Knorr Strategy
abstract: Abstract Despite the electron-rich nature of pyrrole, the development of methods for its enantioselective C3-functionalization remains a significant synthetic challenge. In this work, a direct catalytic asymmetric synthesis of unblocked C3-nitroalkylated pyrroles has been established through a one-pot sequential process. This process involves an amine-catalyzed Michael addition of succinaldehyde to various nitroolefins, followed by an in situ Paal–Knorr cyclization with primary amines, for the rapid synthesis of a broad range of C3-nitroalkylated N-alkyl, N-aryl, and NH-pyrroles in good yields and high enantioselectivity. Broad substrate scope and functional group tolerance enable efficient access to diverse chiral pyrroles, with gram-scale synthesis and late-stage functionalization highlighting the method's practicality.

title: Artificial intelligence and knowledge management capabilities for green business transformation: governance, environmental strategy and financial resilience
abstract: Purpose As digital technologies and knowledge processes become increasingly central to organizational strategy, firms are required to translate these capabilities into effective governance and sustainability-oriented practices. In knowledge-intensive and highly regulated industries, understanding how such capabilities shape strategic outcomes remains a critical research challenge. This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) and knowledge management (KM) capabilities jointly enable insurance firms to develop governance strategies and environmental mechanisms that enhance financial resilience and drive green business transformation. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in dynamic capability theory (DCT), this study develops and empirically tests an integrated framework using data from 288 insurance firms based in the USA. The relationships among AI capabilities, KM capabilities, governance strategy, environmental strategy, financial resilience and green business transformation are examined using confirmatory factor analysis and Hayes’ PROCESS macro. Findings The findings demonstrate that AI and KM capabilities act as complementary dynamic capabilities that significantly strengthen governance and environmental strategies. These strategies in turn enhance financial resilience, which subsequently enables green business transformation. The results highlight how the in…

title: From digital knowledge strategy to sustainable performance: evidence of a dynamic capabilities pathway in developed vs developing economies
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine digital knowledge strategy through deliberate and emergent planning approaches to build dynamic capabilities (DCs) for innovation and achieve sustainable performance (SUP) gains amid environmental dynamism (ED) in developing and developed economies, particularly under regulatory obligations imposed by mandatory compliance regimes. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a quantitative research design, gathering data from Brazilian and English firms in the variety sector. A total of 302 responses were obtained and analyzed using structural equation modeling. Findings This study reveals that digital knowledge strategy influences sustainable through DCs in sensing, seizing and transforming into prosperous and emerging economies. The post hoc analysis, using generalized additive models, shows that firms with high levels of digital knowledge strategy to achieve higher DCs and SUP under ED in both countries. However, under these conditions, digital knowledge strategy, innovation-related DCs and SUP appear more developed in the UK than in Brazil. Practical implications This study contributes to practitioners’ understanding of how digital knowledge strategy can help firms achieve better performance outcomes across diverse contexts, reinforcing the importance of investing in digital tools to enable effective strategizing. Originality/value As the…

title: Visible-Light-Induced Ruthenium Catalytic Strategy for C−H Activation and Aza-Michael Addition of 2-Arylquinazolin-4(3 H )-ones with Olefins
abstract: Abstract A visible-light-mediated versatile synthesis of pyrrolo[2,1-b]quinazolin-9(1H)-one derivatives has been developed by merging Ru(II)-catalysis with photocatalysis via C−H activation and intramolecular aza-Michael addition of 2-arylquinazolin-4 (3H)-ones with various activated olefins under ambient reaction conditions with high efficiency and good functional-group tolerance. Mechanistic investigations were conducted through control experiments, UV−visible spectroscopy, H/D labeling studies, kinetics isotope-effect experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), and light on−off studies to gain insight into the reaction pathway and the role of photocatalysis in the transformation. The present methodology was demonstrated to be effective for scale-up synthesis, enabling the efficient synthesis of the cyclized product, thereby highlighting its practical synthetic applicability.

title: Does leadership–infrastructure fit explain digital readiness?
abstract: Purpose This study tests whether digital readiness depends on the strategic fit between transformational leadership and digital infrastructure in micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Rather than treating infrastructure as a mediator of leadership, this study examines whether leadership and infrastructure must be aligned and jointly strong for readiness to emerge. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected between August and October 2024. The retained analytical file contained 500 de-identified questionnaire records and nine study indicators. Three equal-weighted component indices were constructed. Leadership and infrastructure were centered on the common value of 4.0 to preserve their substantive equality line, after which polynomial regression and response surface analysis (RSA) were estimated using HC3 heteroscedasticity-consistent inference. Findings The data do not support the expected strategic fit explanation. The polynomial model explained 1.0% of the variance in digital readiness (R2 = 0.010; adjusted R2 = −0.0001; robust F(5, 494) = 0.959, p = 0.442). The leadership × infrastructure term was not significant (b = −0.107, p = 0.311), and neither the line-of-congruence slope (a1 = −0.062, p = 0.283) nor the line-of-incongruence curvature (a4 = 0.086, p = 0.639) was significant. Thus, high leadership-infrastructure alignment was not associated with high…

title: Dual-source interactivity and self-construction in phygital retail: outcome pathways
abstract: Purpose Phygital retail research has largely treated physical–digital convergence as a technological design challenge, leaving consumers’ self-construction underexplored. This study aims to examine how physical and digital interactivity relate to self-extension and self-expansion, and how these pathways connect to shopping well-being and place and brand attachment. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on socio-technical systems theory and self-construction theory, the authors conceptualize phygital retail as a dual-source interaction system centered on consumer self-construction. Survey data from 634 consumers with recent phygital retail experience were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling and multigroup analysis. Findings Self-construction does not map onto a fixed physical or digital source; effects depend on whether interaction affirms the existing self (self-extension) or opens new self-possibilities (self-expansion). Both pathways positively relate to shopping well-being in phygital retail, which supports place and brand attachment, with self-expansion showing the stronger association. Practical implications Service managers should avoid assuming that more interactivity automatically produces stronger customer outcomes. Phygital service design should instead prioritize interaction cues that help customers either incorporate the service environment in…

title: Structural and operational barriers to food waste mitigation across traditional fruit and vegetable retail profiles in Mexico
abstract: Introduction Reducing food waste in the retail sector is crucial for food security, yet traditional retail vulnerabilities are often overlooked. This study aimed to characterize marketing dynamics, the frequency of suboptimal produce, and waste management practices in fruit and vegetable retail outlets to identify the primary causes of food waste and propose targeted strategic interventions. Methods Using an observational cross-sectional design, a convenience sample ( n = 180) across four Mexican states was stratified into four commercial profiles: municipal markets, produce stores, grocery stores, and open-air markets. Statistical analyses included Pearson's Chi-square tests ( χ 2 ), K-means cluster analysis and Multiple Correspondence Analysis. Results Self-reported responses associated food waste with infrastructural and supply-chain constraints at the point of sale. The reported analysis did not detect a statistically significant association between marketing cluster membership and self-reported weekly waste in this sample. The Multiple Correspondence Analysis identified exploratory associations among retail format, sampled location, deterioration susceptibility, and reported utilization practices (e.g., household consumption, animal feed, or landfill disposal). These findings identify format- and context-specific interventions for future evaluation; such as adequate roofs/…

title: Structural failure of marginal scarcity pricing: a common architectural root of retailer insolvency, risk–volume separation instability, and VoLL-dependent investment signals
abstract: Abstract Liberalised electricity markets exhibit three recurring pathologies typically treated as separate policy problems: retailer insolvency under regulated price caps, instability from the separation of volume risk and price risk, and the sensitivity of investment incentives to the administratively determined value of lost load (VoLL). This paper argues that these pathologies share a common architectural root: the marginal-pricing paradigm assigns too many incompatible functions to a single scarcity price. The claim is formalised through three structural lemmas. Lemma 1 shows retailer insolvency is a mathematical consequence of combining capped retail revenue with uncapped wholesale cost exposure under any finite equity buffer, given a sufficiently prolonged shock relative to that buffer. Lemma 2 shows risk–volume separation instability is unavoidable whenever a retail intermediary cannot simultaneously control consumed volume and charged price under a retail price cap. Lemma 3 proves that expected scarcity rents and the free-entry capacity level are continuous, strictly monotone functions of an administratively chosen VoLL, for which no market-internal principle identifies a unique correct value; gross producer operating surplus at fixed capacity is likewise monotone in VoLL. The lemmas are calibrated to the GB market using published bill-decomposition, supplier-failure an…

title: Developing Emotional Intelligence and Resilience in Respiratory Therapy Education: An Open-Access Perspective
abstract: This conceptual paper examines the role of open-access higher education institutions in addressing the critical healthcare workforce shortage in the United States, particularly in high-demand specialties such as respiratory therapy. Drawing on literature related to open-access education, emotional intelligence, resilience, simulation-based learning, and workforce development, this paper proposes a conceptual framework explaining how reflective simulation experiences and structured debriefing may foster emotional intelligence and resilience among respiratory therapy students. By expanding access to education for both traditional and nontraditional learners, open-access institutions can create more inclusive pathways into healthcare professions. The proposed framework suggests that intentional development of emotional intelligence through reflective educational experiences may enhance adaptability, persistence, workforce readiness, and long-term professional engagement. Aligning curriculum design with workforce needs while emphasizing both cognitive and affective skill development may produce competent, resilient, and workforce-ready graduates. This conceptual paper offers a foundation for future empirical research and presents a potential strategy for strengthening workforce retention and addressing ongoing respiratory therapy workforce shortages.

title: Improving crustal boundary interpretation in deep seismic reflection data using multi-attribute machine learning with forward modelling validation along seismic line 07GA-A1 in Northern Queensland
EKSPLORASI INTEGRASI INQUIRY DAN PROJECT-BASED LEARNING SEBAGAI DASAR PENGEMBANGAN MODEL IMED UNTUK LITERASI MULTIMODAL SISWA SMP
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of digital information requires students not only to produce multimodal content but also to explore, evaluate, and process information critically. This study aims to identify multimodal literacy learning needs, explore existing inquiry and Project-Based Learning (PjBL) practices, and formulate the preliminary characteristics of the Digital Ethnopedagogical Multimodal Inquiry (IMED) model. An exploratory qualitative approach employing a multisite case study design was conducted at three junior high schools in Langsa, Indonesia. Data were collected through classroom observations, semi-structured interviews with six Indonesian language teachers and 12 students, and an analysis of instructional documents and student products. Thematic analysis was conducted by examining data within each case and comparing findings across cases. The results indicate that students have produced various multimodal products and used digital technology in learning. However, inquiry practices tend to focus on information retrieval, while information evaluation and processing remain inconsistent; PjBL is more prominently oriented toward product creation. The integration of these approaches has not yet established a coherent learning sequence. Local wisdom has also not been systematically incorporated as a source of inquiry. These findings provide a basis for formulating the prelim…

title: Beyond employability: unpacking China’s national-strategic model of work-integrated learning
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine China’s distinctive work-integrated learning (WIL) model through conceptual theory building, comparing it with Western and Asian counterparts to identify its unique institutional features. Design/methodology/approach The study develops an integrated macro-meso-micro analytical framework synthesising skill formation regime theory, institutional logics, and symbiosis theory. Drawing on government policy document and institutional case reviews, with Modern Industry Colleges (MIC) and Colleges of Future Technologies (CFT) as illustrative exemplars, the framework conceptualises the broader industry-education integration infrastructure that incubates and sustains WIL. Findings China’s WIL model – characterised by state-directed coordination, platform-based organizations (MIC and CFT), and policy-dominant institutional logic – constitutes a “national strategic” type, fundamentally diverging from Western employability-focused approaches. The institutionalisation of hybrid organizations that integrate multiple functions under joint governance structures represents a significant organisational innovation. Originality/value This paper provides a systematic comparative analysis of China’s WIL through a novel multi-level framework, contributing to the diversification of WIL scholarship beyond Western-centric perspectives and offering a new typological cate…
venue: Higher Education, Skills and Work-Based Learning

title: Pemodelan Prediksi Kerawanan Banjir Bandang Menggunakan Machine Learning Random Forest (Studi Kasus: 8 Nagari di Sekitar Batang Malana, Kabupaten Tanah Datar)
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memetakan kerawanan banjir bandang menggunakan algoritma Random Forest pada 8 di nagari sekitar DAS Batang Malana, Kabupaten Tanah Datar. Metode penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif spasial berbasis machine learning algoritma random forest dengan memanfaatkan 13 variabel prediktor yaitu Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), Stream Power Index (SPI), dan kemiringan lereng (Slope), arah lereng (Aspect), Profile Curvature, Plan Curvature, curah hujan rata-rata 10 tahun, curah hujan kumulatif 7 hari, tutupan lahan (Land Cover), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), jarak terhadap deforestasi, geologi, dan gerakan tanah serta kinerja model dievaluasi menggunakan Area Under the Curve (AUC). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa algoritma Random Forest mampu menghasilkan model prediksi kerawanan banjir bandang dengan kinerja yang baik, ditunjukkan oleh nilai AUC sebesar 0,828. Peta kerawanan yang dihasilkan diklasifikasikan ke dalam lima kelas kerawanan. Sebaran kelas kerawanan tinggi hingga sangat tinggi terkonsentrasi di sepanjang koridor DAS Batang Malana dan jaringan sungai lainnya pada 8 nagari di wilayah penelitian yang berhulu di Gunung Marapi.

title: Advancing Open and Culturally Responsive Teaching and Learning in Public Colleges
abstract: Open educational resources (OER) have been widely adopted in higher education for their cost-saving benefits, yet their potential to support innovative, student-centered pedagogy is less understood. This exploratory study examines how instructors in a statewide grant program implemented OER-enabled open educational practices (OEP) and culturally responsive education (CRE) strategies. Through a 2-year mixed-methods study involving instructor interviews, observations, surveys, and student data, we explored how support for professional learning influenced instructional redesign using OER-enabled open and culturally responsive practices and how students experienced these practices. Instructors adopted practices that increased student voice, inclusivity, and peer collaboration, while students in redesigned course sections reported stronger engagement, emotional connection, and participation—especially among Pell Grant-receiving students who showed gains in academic performance. Findings underscore the importance of sustained professional learning and institutional support to realize the transformative potential of OEP and CRE in higher education.

The Effect of Lead-Up Games Based on Performance-Simulated Situations on Bodily-Kinesthetic Intelligence and the Learning of Selected Basic Soccer Skills among Students
abstract: Backgroud: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of lead-up games based on performance-simulated situations on the development of bodily–kinesthetic intelligence and the learning of selected basic soccer skills among seventh-grade students. Methods: The researcher employed an experimental approach using a two-group design (experimental and control) with pre- and post-tests. The study population consisted of 157 students, and a final sample of 50 students was selected from Ibn al-Mu’tam Middle School in Tikrit, with 25 students in each group. The experimental group underwent a six-week instructional program based on performance-like preparatory games, consisting of two instructional units per week for a total of 12 instructional units, with 12 minutes allocated to practical activities in each unit, for a total of 144 minutes of actual exposure, while the control group learned the same skills using the conventional method. The study employed a kinesthetic-motor intelligence scale consisting of 24 items distributed across three dimensions, along with soccer dribbling, handling, and stopping tests. Results: The results showed equivalence between the two groups in the pre-test, followed by a statistically significant improvement in all variables for the experimental group; the mean physical-motor intelligence score increased from (56.68±6.27) to (64.48±6.58), rolling t…

title: Quasi-oppositional-based learning Schrödinger algorithm for weight optimization of the aircraft torque link component
abstract: Abstract This work presents an improved Schrödinger-based optimization approach incorporating quasi-oppositional learning to enhance solution quality in structural weight reduction problems. The method was applied to the design of an aircraft torque link, where mass minimization was performed under a maximum allowable stress of 250 MPa using finite element analysis. The optimized configuration reduced the mass from 4.053 kg to 3.115 kg, corresponding to a 23.14 % decrease, while the maximum stress reached 239 MPa and remained within safe limits. Under identical computational effort (500 function evaluations), the proposed approach achieved lower mass values than other algorithms. The results indicate that the developed strategy is well-suited for lightweight aerospace components and similar high-performance engineering applications.

title: Mapping hybrid Infotech competencies for workplace learning: a bibliometric taxonomy and theoretical framework
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the growing demand for hybrid information technology (IT) roles that blend technical, strategic, and cognitive skills. It proposes a theoretical Nomological Framework that conceptualizes how multidisciplinary competencies may connect digital transformation with organisational outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A rigorous three-stage analytical procedure was employed, involving data normalization of 114 Scopus-indexed articles, mathematical clustering via VOSviewer to identify thematic patterns, and theoretical synthesis grounded in the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory. Findings The study proposes a taxonomy of hybrid IT competencies and a nomological framework that categorizes multidisciplinary competencies and their development approaches. Four competency domains, Foundational (Red), Strategic (Green), Synergistic (Yellow), and Cognitive (Blue), offer a structured basis for developing future-ready IT professionals in the digital workplace. Research limitations/implications By moving beyond simple skill-listing, the proposed taxonomy provides a theoretical basis for examining competency transitions. It provides a structure for understanding how human capital fosters resilience in volatile digital markets. Practical implications The findings inform the design of evidence-based workplace learning and competency development ini…
