title: Perceived Mentoring Needs Among Faculty Members at a Metropolitan University - A Needs Assessment Pilot
abstract: Background: Faculty development is directly related to student success. While faculty-to-student mentoring is common in academia, especially in applied learning practices, a less common phenomenon is faculty-to-faculty mentoring. To facilitate the process of mentoring within and between faculty, it is necessary to understand their perceived needs. Purpose: The purpose of this study is to identify and evaluate the perceived mentoring needs of faculty members within a metropolitan higher education institution. Identifying the specific areas where faculty members require guidance and support provides valuable data for designing an effective, faculty-to-faculty mentoring program that would prove beneficial to support both students and faculty. Methods: Utilizing a survey technique, an electronic needs assessment questionnaire consisting of six major domains including effective classroom teaching, scholarship knowledge and skills, contributions to the institution and profession, college and university resources, career development skills, and leadership/management was distributed with respondents self-reporting their perceived mentoring needs. Results: 52 respondents completed the questionnaire from an initial 110 responses, representing a response rate of 10.9% of the university faculty. Faculty members expressed different mentorship needs based upon teaching experience and profess…

Alumni engagement in university-based incubators: experiential learning, embedded communities and entrepreneurial ecosystem value
abstract: Purpose Universities are increasingly recognised as central actors within entrepreneurial ecosystems, extending their traditional missions of teaching and research to include innovation, commercialisation and venture creation. Within this evolving landscape, incubator alumni – those who have completed university-based incubation – have emerged as critical yet under-theorised contributors to ecosystem development. This paper explores the role of incubator alumni engagement through a single case study of one successful, international provider. Design/methodology/approach The research comprises a qualitative case study of the Edinburgh Business School (EBS) Incubator at Heriot-Watt University, operating across its Edinburgh and Dubai campuses. It draws on both secondary sources of data relating to the case and on data from semi-structured interviews with incubator managers and staff, from which a thematic analysis is presented. Findings Findings include that beneficiaries of alumni engagement include current incubator participants, the incubator and the university. The embedded and experiential nature of alumni involvement is central to the value realised by each of these; properties that cannot be replicated by traditional educational methods and relationships. Alumni themselves are also found to be beneficiaries and realise both affective and business-related rewards, further co…

title: Advancing Your Career: Advice from County Economic Development Directors – Engage!
abstract: The focus of this paper is on the advice county-level economic development directors offer students looking to move forward with their career. Based on a 2024 survey of these practitioners across the states of Iowa, Kansas, Missouri and Nebraska, the offered advice speaks to skills necessary to pursue a successful career not only for those interested in economic development, but for students across numerous fields who anticipate a career with members of the public and other professionals. Findings also have relevance for those in higher education responsible for program and course development. The career advice from these professionals is heavily about the value of soft skills – communicating, networking and the relevance of work experience in acquiring these skills. Ultimately, the advice stresses the importance of engagement with others. Implications for students and the academic programs in higher education that serve them include the value of internships, collaborative projects and volunteerism.

title: Teaching That Connects: Lessons from a Community-Engaged Learning Course
abstract: This article draws on three years of implementation of a community-engaged undergraduate and graduate course, Bilingual Language Acquisition and Education (BLAE), to identify five transferable lessons for instructors designing experiential learning partnerships. Co-taught by faculty from linguistics and education, the course embedded university students in a Latinx dual-language (DL) primary school community, where they conducted bilingual language assessments, implemented literacy activities, and presented findings at a school-site poster session. Although the course focuses on bilingual education, the authors frame each lesson broadly, inviting instructors across disciplines to consider how community-anchored, applied learning experiences cultivate deeper intellectual engagement than instruction alone can achieve. Additional lessons address how authentic participation supports professional identity development and how structured reflection transforms experience into transferable understanding. This contribution argues that meaningful community engagement requires prioritizing relationship-building over transactional interactions, designing for reciprocity rather than charity, and treating students and community members as genuine research partners.

To Watch or to Read? Comparing Student Perceptions of Written and Video Feedback During Formative Assessment
abstract: Feedback is an essential component of formative assessment. Advances in technology have generated alternatives to traditional written “margin-comment” feedback that may benefit students in several ways. This study surveyed 59 college students about their perceptions of written and video-recorded feedback, comparing social belonging, perceived instructor care, perceived usefulness, perceived effectiveness, and general student preference across the two feedback modalities. Results indicated that students felt a greater sense of belonging when receiving video feedback and perceived that their professors cared more about their education. However, students did not show a clear overall preference for either form of feedback nor did they perceive either form to be more useful or effective for promoting learning. These results suggest that video feedback may be a useful instructional tool for supporting students’ social needs. However, conclusions are limited by the study’s small sample and reliance on student perceptions rather than objective measures of learning and performance.

Logistics Optimization Practices and Performance of Eye Health Non-Governmental Organizations in Kenya.
abstract: Access to eye care in Kenya remains limited, particularly in rural and underserved regions, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) play a pivotal role in bridging this gap. However, delayed deliveries, stock-outs of critical items such as intraocular lenses and ophthalmic drugs, high transportation costs and weak inventory management continue to undermine the timeliness and reach of eye health programmes. Logistics optimization has therefore emerged as an important approach through which eye health NGOs can improve the availability, accessibility and cost effectiveness of their services. The purpose of this study was to establish the influence of logistics optimization practices on the performance of eye health NGOs in Kenya. It examined four practices, namely demand planning, inventory rationalization, collaborative logistics and last-mile delivery. The study was anchored on the Demand Management Theory, Economic Order Quantity Model, Social Exchange Theory and Service Quality Theory. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, targeting the 27 eye health NGOs in Kenya listed by the American Academy of Ophthalmology in 2024, with logistics officers, procurement officers and store officers as the units of observation. Primary data were collected using a self-administered structured questionnaire, which was pilot tested on eight respondents; all Cronbach’s alpha coefficients…

title: Direct parameterization of paired rainfall-runoff events for peak discharge estimation: an event-based framework for flood risk assessment
abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of event-scale peak discharge is essential for flood risk assessment and infrastructure design, yet conventional hydrologic modelling approaches often require extensive calibration procedures and computationally demanding optimization. This study presents a parsimonious event-based framework for estimating hourly runoff hydrographs and peak discharges through direct parameter estimation from physically consistent rainfall-runoff event pairs. The framework integrates precipitation event identification, streamflow baseflow separation, and event pairing with a process-based hydrologic model combining the Natural Resources Conservation Service Curve Number method for precipitation loss estimation and the Natural Resources Conservation Service Unit Hydrograph method for direct runoff transformation. Model parameters, including catchment lag time, peak rate factor, and seasonal Curve NumberPrecipitation relationships, are estimated directly from observed rainfall-runoff events, eliminating the need for inverse numerical optimization against an explicit likelihood or objective function. The framework is evaluated across seven catchments with varying drainage areas within the Housatonic River Basin, using a leave-one-out cross-validation approach. Results demonstrate consistent performance across catchments, with negligible bias and similar residual error c…

Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses reveal UTF1-associated spermatogenic dysfunction and identify ACTRT2 and AKAP4 as biomarkers in non-obstructive azoospermia
abstract: Introduction Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) is a severe male infertility disorder caused by spermatogenic failure, and UTF1 is critical for maintaining undifferentiated spermatogonia and regulating germ cell development. This study aimed to explore the role of UTF1-related spermatogenic dysfunction in NOA and identify potential diagnostic biomarkers. Methods We integrated NOA transcriptomic datasets with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from Utf1 conditional knockout and normal mouse testes. Bioinformatic analyses and machine learning were applied to screen biomarkers, while functional enrichment, immune infiltration, cell-cell communication, and pseudotime trajectory analyses were performed together with histological validation in Utf1-deficient testes. Results Spermatogonia, Sertoli cells, and spermatids were identified as key cell populations. ACTRT2 and AKAP4 were confirmed as consistently downregulated NOA biomarkers and were integrated into a well-calibrated nomogram. These two genes were associated with cytoskeletal remodeling and meiotic regulation. NOA was also characterized by altered immune infiltration and cell-cell communication, whereas Utf1 deficiency impaired testicular development and spermatogenesis. Discussion Collectively, UTF1 deficiency was closely associated with spermatogenic dysfunction and microenvironmental remodeling in NOA, while ACTRT…

title: IMAN: An Integrated Colorimetric Sensor for Direct Detection of PD-L1 on Extracellular Vesicles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality, yet early diagnosis remains difficult, highlighting the need for sensitive, noninvasive methods. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) and their surface proteins (e.g., PD-L1) are promising biomarkers; nevertheless, current EV detection requires time-consuming purification, sophisticated instrumentation, and long measurement protocols, resulting in high expenses and operational difficulties. This study developed an integrated colorimetric sensor, IMAN, based on a strategy of “Immunomagnetic Microbeads (IM) capture + Aptamer(Apt) recognition + Nanozyme (N) catalysis”. IMAN employs magnetic beads modified with antibodies against CD9 and CD81 to directly capture EVs from serum, eliminating the need for time-consuming prior isolation; combined with a one-step colorimetric readout, the entire workflow can be completed with only ∼40 min of hands-on time, requiring no complex instrumentation. The PD-L1 protein on the EV surface is specifically recognized by a nanoparticle-bound nucleic acid aptamer. Signal generation is achieved through the catalytic oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) by a platinum-gold bimetallic nanozyme (Pt@Au). The facile IMAN colorimetric method demonstrated a relatively broad dynamic range (107–1010 particles/mL), high specificity (unaffected by 100 pg/mL soluble PD-L1 in serum), and reproducibil…

T2 mapping of individual fascicles of the sciatic nerve at 7 T using multi-echo spin–echo
abstract: Abstract Objective Neuropathies can selectively affect individual fascicles within peripheral nerves, but diagnosis is limited by MRI spatial resolution and signal-to-noise ratio. This feasibility study aimed to leverage 7 T MRI to measure sub-millimetric T 2 maps of sciatic nerve fascicles in healthy subjects. Materials and methods Accelerated multi-echo spin–echo sequences were acquired in six healthy volunteers at 7 T. Acceleration included generalised autocalibrating partially parallel acquisition (GRAPPA) and GRAPPATINI, which integrates GRAPPA with model-based accelerated relaxometry. Extended phase graph (EPG) modelling of signal decay was used to compute T 2 maps. Quantitative maps were visually assessed and T 2 values were extracted from regions of interest. Results High-resolution imaging (0.4×0.4x3.0 mm 3 ) enabled visualisation of individual fascicles. T 2 values were lower in fascicles (57.0 ms) than in the non-fascicular intraneural compartment (76.2 ms) and intermuscular fat (132.7 ms). Compared with GRAPPA alone, GRAPPATINI reduced acquisition time (11:05 to 3:35 min) while maintaining fascicle depiction and T 2 consistency (mean difference: 1.45 ms). Overlaying T 2 on S 0 maps enhanced fascicle delineation, facilitating anatomical interpretation. Discussion This approach demonstrated the feasibility of high-resolution T 2 mapping of peripheral nerve fascicles a…

title: Multi-Electron Transfer in Zinc-Based Batteries: Unraveling Redox Mechanisms Toward Next-Generation Self-Powered Technologies
abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of autonomous IoT networks and wearable electronics has intensified the demand for photo-rechargeable zinc-based batteries (PRZBBs). While realizing high overall energy conversion efficiency intrinsically relies on cathode materials capable of multi-electron transfer reactions, current literature largely treats the fundamental electrochemistry of aqueous zinc batteries and the macroscopic engineering of solar-integrated devices as isolated domains. This review bridges this critical gap, offering a unique positioning by establishing a unified analytical framework that directly links fundamental multi-electron redox mechanisms to the dynamic architectural requirements of PRZBBs. Moving beyond a conventional cataloging of material classes, we critically evaluate diverse cathode platforms, including transition metal oxides, Prussian blue analogues, organics, halogens, and sulfur. Our incremental contribution lies in decoupling how specific multi-step reaction kinetics, distinct voltage plateaus, and dominant charge carriers dictate solar cell coupling strategies, particularly concerning maximum power point matching and intermittent charging adaptability. Furthermore, we critically and systematically assess the practical bottlenecks of these chemistries, such as shuttle effects, kinetic limitations, and voltage hysteresis, that hinder scalable integratio…

title: Bridging nature-based solutions, smart technologies, and traditional wisdom for sustainable water management: a multi-decadal evaluation of bamboo-based systems in degraded ravine landscapes
abstract: ABSTRACT Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are increasingly recognized as sustainable approaches for addressing water insecurity, land degradation, biodiversity loss, and climate resilience. However, robust long-term field evidence quantifying their hydrological and ecological effectiveness remains limited. This study presents a multi-decadal (1985–2025) evidence synthesis evaluating bamboo-based NbS for restoring degraded ravine landscapes in India by integrating long-term field observations, experimental watershed investigations, hydrological monitoring, project datasets, and peer-reviewed literature. Results demonstrate that bamboo functions as living hydrological infrastructure by enhancing rainfall retention, increasing infiltration, reducing runoff and sediment transport, improving soil quality, and accelerating ecological recovery. Bamboo-based interventions reduced runoff by 80–90%, soil loss by 85–95%, and sediment yield by over 90%, while stabilizing gullies within 2–3 years. Infiltration increased substantially (up to ∼140 cm h−1) together with improvements in soil organic carbon and micro-ecological conditions. Economically, bamboo systems generated annual returns of ₹33,500–48,000 ha−1 with internal rates of return of 18–22%. The study proposes an integrated Nature-Based Hydrological Engineering framework, establishing bamboo as a scalable, climate-resilient solution fo…

Human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells alleviate fluoxetine-resistant depression-like behaviors in mice by multi-target effects in the hippocampus
abstract: BACKGROUND Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) remains a major clinical challenge due to the limited efficacy of conventional first-line antidepressants. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), which possess potent immunomodulatory and neurotrophic properties, have emerged as promising therapeutic candidates for neuropsychiatric disorders. Human bone marrow-derived MSCs (hBMSCs) are one of the most widely used sources. However, their therapeutic potential and their underlying mechanisms in the context of TRD have yet to be fully elucidated. AIM To investigate the antidepressant effects of hBMSCs in a TRD-like mouse model and to explore the potential molecular mechanisms involved. METHODS A mouse model of fluoxetine-resistant depression (FRD), defined as an early stage of TRD, was established by combining chronic unpredictable restraint stress with corticosterone administration and validated by the lack of behavioral response to fluoxetine (FLX). hBMSCs (2 × 106 cells) were administered via the tail vein twice weekly for 4 weeks. A battery of behavioral tests was conducted to evaluate depressive- and anxiety-like behaviors. Immunofluorescence staining and western blotting were performed to assess microglial activation, astrocytic integrity, neuronal survival, and hippocampal neurogenesis. RESULTS hBMSC treatment significantly ameliorated depressive- and anxiety-like behaviors in FRD mod…

title: Can organizational image and corporate social responsibility foster citizenship behavior of the employees: a mediational query through organizational identity
abstract: Purpose The present research, based upon psychological ownership theory, tries to find out how organizational image and perceived corporate social responsibility (CSR) influence the organizational identity and organizational citizenship behavior (OCB). The present research also tries to find out the role of organisational identity (OI) as a mediator between organizational image and perceived CSR. Design/methodology/approach Survey research using purposive random sampling was conducted in chemical and heavy manufacturing industries in Kolkata, India (N = 243). The survey consisted of a questionnaire measuring the above variables. The data were collected from employees in managerial and supervisory positions. Findings Results were analyzed using SPSS V.25 and Smart-PLS v.4. The mediation model was tested using path analysis. Results show a full mediation effect of organizational identity on the relationship between perceived CSR and OCB and partial mediation of organizational identity on the relationship between organizational image and OCB. Practical implications The results of the present work can have managerial implications. The results of the present research can be used to increase organizational identity and how it can imply a lower attrition rate. title: Prioritizing sustainability indicators in the coffee supply chain via the fuzzy SAW method
abstract: Purpose This research identifies, classifies, and prioritizes sustainability indicators for the Colombian coffee supply chain. Given the industry’s challenges and growing international demand, the study aims to enhance supply chain sustainability by analyzing the most relevant variables based on global standards. Design/methodology/approach Indicators selected from a literature review were assessed by experts using a fuzzy scale to address subjectivity. A fuzzy simple additive weighting (SAW) method then employed to prioritize the indicators, with final weights and rankings obtained though Minkowski-base defuzzification. Findings Forty four indicators were refined and evaluated by 15 experts. These indicators were ranked by importance, allowing for their specific prioritization within social, environmental, and economic sustainability dimensions. The results highlight a subset of high impact indicators that are closely linked to productivity enhancement, performance management, and operational decision making across the coffee supply chain. Research limitations/implications The primary limitation of this study pertains to the expert selection process and the collection of Likert-scale assessments. Although 25 experts were initially invited, time constraints prevented full participation. However, the final panel of 15 is considered methodologically sufficient given their extensi…

title: Human Resource Management Strategies for Lecturer Performance Development in Higher Education Institutions
abstract: This study aims to analyze human resource management strategies for lecturer performance development in higher education institutions, focusing on the case of UIN Raden Mas Said Surakarta, Indonesia. Effective human resource management is essential for supporting lecturers’ professionalism, academic productivity, and institutional performance. This study employed a qualitative case study approach. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and document analysis, with informants selected purposively based on their relevance to the research objectives. The data were analyzed thematically to identify management strategies, implementation challenges, and opportunities for lecturer performance development. The findings indicate that lecturer performance development requires an integrated human resource management strategy encompassing effective academic governance, continuous professional development, performance-based incentives, periodic monitoring and evaluation, and the strengthening of academic culture and scientific collaboration. However, implementation faces challenges related to coordination, information system integration, incentive transparency, and outcome-oriented performance evaluation. These findings highlight the importance of aligning human resource management policies with institutional objectives and lecturers’ professional needs. This study pro…

title: Employee performance and intrinsic CSR attribution: organizational trustworthiness and trust propensity
abstract: Purpose This study aims to understand how intrinsic corporate social responsibility (CSR) attribution is formed and how individual characteristics, such as the desire to benefit others (i.e. other-concern), can be boundary conditions that influence employees’ responses to intrinsic CSR attribution. Design/methodology/approach Dyadic data were collected from 327 employees and their supervisors in a Vietnamese telecommunications enterprise. Covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) was employed to test the theoretical model. Findings Findings show that organizational trustworthiness and trust propensity are important determinants of intrinsic CSR attribution. Moreover, the relationship between intrinsic CSR attribution and extra-role performance is positive and further enhanced by employees’ other-concern. Practical implications Organizations should focus on building organizational trustworthiness to enhance employees' intrinsic CSR attribution. Furthermore, selecting employees who align with the organization’s CSR values can further amplify CSR positive impact on workplace behaviors. Originality/value Despite the importance of intrinsic CSR attribution on positive employee outcomes, little is known about how intrinsic CSR attribution is formed. This study addresses this gap by examining antecedents of intrinsic CSR attribution. Furthermore, it investigates the under…

title: Corruption and subjective well-being in Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how corruption is associated with subjective well-being by distinguishing personal bribery experiences from the broader regional corruption environment. Design/methodology/approach This study uses Afrobarometer Round 8 and the 2014 Americas Barometer to examine 849 subnational regions across Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean. This study analyzes the association between subjective well-being and two dimensions of corruption: individual bribery experiences and regional corruption intensity. The models account for individual and regional economic conditions. Additional analyses examine sector-specific corruption and gender differences. Findings Higher regional corruption intensity is consistently associated with lower subjective well-being, even after accounting for economic conditions. In Africa, regional corruption is associated with lower well-being, whereas individual bribery is not significantly associated with well-being, with administrative corruption showing the clearest sector-specific association. Originality/value This study contributes to research on corruption and well-being by distinguishing individual bribery exposure from the wider regional corruption environment. This study shows that corruption matters as not only a personal experience but also a contextual governance condition that shapes citizens’ daily lives. This study…

Right Iliac Fossa Mass: A Diagnostic Dilemma
abstract: Introduction: A right iliac fossa mass presents a frequent surgical challenge. In tuberculosis endemic regions, hypertrophic ileocecal tuberculosis can closely mimic cecal carcinoma clinically, radiologically and colonoscopically. Case Presentation: A 40-year-old male presented with a palpable RIF lump, intermittent abdominal pain, anorexia and weight loss. Laboratory investigations revealed anemia. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography scan demonstrated asymmetric circumferential mural thickening (21 mm) of the cecum and ascending colon with luminal narrowing, intramural calcifications and pericolic lymphadenopathy, suspicious for malignancy. Colonoscopy revealed a friable, non-negotiable ulceroproliferative mass. Colonoscopic biopsy demonstrated granulomatous colitis with epithelioid cells and multinucleated giant cells without evidence of malignancy. Due to severe luminal stenosis and persistent suspicion of malignancy, right hemicolectomy was performed. Histopathological examination of the resected specimen revealed caseating epithelioid granulomas, Langhans giant cells and tuberculous lymphadenitis, with no dysplasia or malignancy, establishing a diagnosis of hypertrophic ileocecal tuberculosis. The patient was subsequently initiated on antitubercular therapy. Conclusion: Hypertrophic ileocecal tuberculosis can simulate cecal carcinoma at every diagnostic step. While uncom…

title: PENINGKATAN MINAT BELAJAR IPA MELALUI PENERAPAN PEMBELAJARAN MENDALAM DENGAN PRINSIP TEACHING AT THE RIGHT LEVEL PADA MURID KELAS VIII
abstract: Penelitian tindakan kelas ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan perubahan minat belajar IPA murid kelas VIII melalui penerapan model Discovery Learning dengan pendekatan Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL). Penelitian dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus, yaitu materi tekanan hidrostatis melalui percobaan botol berlubang pada Siklus I dan Hukum Archimedes melalui percobaan benda dalam air pada Siklus II. Subjek analisis terdiri atas 25 murid yang memiliki data lengkap untuk dibandingkan pada tahap pra-siklus, Siklus I, dan Siklus II. Data minat belajar dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner berisi 12 pernyataan yang mencakup empat indikator, yaitu keterlibatan aktif, perhatian dan fokus, perasaan senang atau kenyamanan, serta ketekunan dan kemauan berusaha. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif melalui perhitungan rata-rata skor dan indeks persentase. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rata-rata indeks minat belajar meningkat dari 95,89% pada pra-siklus menjadi 96,33% pada Siklus I, kemudian mencapai 99,33% pada Siklus II. Peningkatan dari pra-siklus hingga Siklus II sebesar 3,44 poin persentase. Pada Siklus II, seluruh indikator mengalami peningkatan dibandingkan Siklus I, dengan keterlibatan aktif mencapai indeks 100%. Hasil ini menunjukkan kecenderungan peningkatan indeks minat belajar selama pelaksanaan tindakan. Namun, indeks awal yang tinggi dan penggunaan kuesioner sebagai instrumen utama …

title: Pengaruh Financial Technology, Self-Control, Gaya Hidup, dan Pengetahuan Keuangan terhadap Perilaku Keuangan Mahasiswa di Kabupaten Wonosobo
abstract: University students show high financial inclusion but lagging financial literacy: among students the gap reaches 22.66 percentage points (SNLIK 2025). This raises the question of whether convenient digital financial services actually produce sound financial behavior. This study analyzes the effects of financial technology, self-control, lifestyle, and financial knowledge on the financial behavior of university students in Wonosobo Regency, both partially and simultaneously. A quantitative causal-associative design was applied to a population of 10,625 active students. The sample size was set with the Slovin formula (e = 10%), cross-checked with a statistical power analysis (GPower), and drawn purposively, yielding 105 respondents who had used financial technology for at least three months. Data were collected with a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed by multiple linear regression (IBM SPSS Statistics 27). Financial technology, self-control, and lifestyle had no significant partial effect, whereas financial knowledge had a positive and significant effect and was the dominant predictor. Simultaneously, the four predictors were significant (Adjusted R² = 0.920). Variance decomposition shows that about 88% of the explained variance is shared among predictors, so the non-significance of the first three variables reflects small unique contributions rather than the absence of a r…

title: Entrepreneurial opportunity evaluation for financial technology decision
abstract: Abstract Purpose Financial technology (FinTech) is increasingly associated with digital transformation and broader sustainability-oriented economic objectives. Although previous studies have extensively examined technological and organizational determinants of FinTech adoption, less attention has been given to the entrepreneurial cognitive processes associated with strategic technology investment decisions. This study examines the relationship between Entrepreneurial Opportunity Evaluation (EOE) and Financial Technology Decisions (FTD) among Thai financial institutions and assesses the mediating roles of Risk Re-Categorization (RRC), Financing Constraints Alleviation (FCA), Information Asymmetry Reduction (IAR), and Operational Efficiency Incentives (OEI). Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted among Chief Financial Officers (CFOs) of firms listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET). Data were collected from 32 financial institutions and analyzed using Hayes’ PROCESS macro with bias corrected bootstrapping to examine the proposed mediation model. Findings The findings indicate that Entrepreneurial Opportunity Evaluation significantly influences Financial Technology Decisions both directly and indirectly. title: The Impact of Algorithm-Aware Leadership on Patient Safety Voice Behavior among Employees at Baghdad Teaching Hospital: The Mediating Role of Algorithmic Justice and the Moderating Role of Psychological Safety
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the impact of algorithmic mindful leadership on voice behavior for patient safety among employees at Baghdad Teaching Hospital in Iraq. This was examined in light of the transition toward using digital and algorithmic systems in work organization and administrative decision-making, and the critical need to balance digital outputs with human judgment. Furthermore, the study sought to test the mediating role of algorithmic justice and the moderating role of psychological safety in the relationship between algorithmic justice perception and voice behavior for patient safety. The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach. Data were gathered fieldwise using a questionnaire distributed to a sample of medical and nursing staff at Baghdad Teaching Hospital, yielding a total sample size of (227) respondents. The results revealed a statistically significant positive direct effect of algorithmic mindful leadership on voice behavior for patient safety, indicating that avoiding pure mechanical reliance sends reassuring signals that motivate staff to break organizational silence and predict potential risks. Moreover, the findings proved that algorithmic justice plays a partial mediating role in this relationship, highlighting the importance of employees' perception of fairness and transparency in digital systems as a prerequisite for speaking up responsi…

title: Percepción de las personas adultas mayores en el respeto a su derecho de igualdad y no discriminación en el acceso a la justicia en el estado de Hidalgo
abstract: This research analyzes the implementation of the existing regulatory framework on equality and non-discrimination in the state of Hidalgo, as a real guarantee of access to justice for older adults. To this end, a survey was conducted with 50 older adults in the municipalities of Pachuca and Tizayuca, Hidalgo, covering sociodemographic dimensions, perception of treatment, equality, and proposals for improvement, systematizing the information through descriptive and content analysis. The findings indicate an institutional culture that heavily relies on stereotypes, paternalization, and infantilization of older adults, resulting in obstacles to the full exercise of access to justice. It is concluded that while in the state of Hidalgo possess a robust regulatory framework aimed at ensuring the protection of and access to justice for older adults at all times, normative efficacy remains symbolic in practice, as access to justice is hindered by a lack of enforcement within daily institutional operations.

title: Assessing the Impact of Healthcare Resources on Birth Outcomes at Private and Public Hospitals in Saudi Arabia
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of healthcare resources on birth outcomes in public and private hospitals in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The study examined the effect of five main resources: obstetricians and gynecologists (OB/GYN), pediatricians, midwives, OB/GYN-specialized hospitals, and hospital beds, and investigated their contribution to key maternal and neonatal health indicators, namely normal and abnormal deliveries, maternal mortality, pregnancy and childbirth complications, and infant mortality. The study was motivated by the scarcity of empirical research on this relationship in the Saudi context and by the importance of healthcare providers and infrastructure in reducing maternal and infant mortality and informing healthcare resource allocation. The study adopted a quantitative approach and relied on secondary data as the main source of information, collected from the annual Statistical Yearbooks published by the Saudi Ministry of Health for the period 2017 to 2023. Data were analyzed using Microsoft Excel and the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), employing descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, and standard deviation) and linear regression analysis. The findings indicated a strong and statistically significant relationship between the number of OB/GYN physicians and normal deliveries, with an R² value of 0.898, while no statisticall…

title: Synthesizing Information-Driven Insider Trade Signals
abstract: Abstract We propose a novel approach to synthesize presumably information-driven insider trading signals for the cross section of stocks. We find that the resulting straightforward composite strategy can often forecast returns in a global sample. This predictability is strongest in equal-weighted portfolios, short holding periods, and insider-buying signals, and it improves further with global diversification. Cross-country analysis reveals that varying insider trading restrictions between countries have limited explanatory power for the performance of the composite strategy. Overall, the results are consistent with a short-term informational advantage of insiders, which might be due to the skillful interpretation of non-private news.

title: Substitution effect of lottery consumption on household risky financial asset investment – based on the moderating role of FinTech
abstract: Purpose This paper empirically examines the impact of lottery consumption on household risky financial asset investment. It further investigates the moderating role of FinTech development and the heterogeneous effects of financial literacy and regional characteristics. Design/methodology/approach Based on data from 2017 to 2019 waves of the China Household Finance Survey (CHFS), combined with lottery sales data from the Ministry of Finance of the People's Republic of China and the Peking University Digital Financial Inclusion Index, this paper employs Probit regression and a PSM-DDD approach to strengthen causal identification. Findings The results indicate that lottery consumption exerts a substitution effect on household risky financial asset investment. Moreover, the development of FinTech weakens this substitution effect through multiple channels, including reducing transaction costs in financial markets, improving information transparency, and enhancing social interaction. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the moderating effect of FinTech is more pronounced among households located in eastern China, households residing in first-tier cities, and households with higher levels of financial literacy. In particular, the differences between households in eastern versus central and western regions, as well as between households with high versus low financial literacy, are espec…

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Reducing Agency Costs and Improving Corporate Governance Efficiency: An Analytical Study
abstract: This study aimed to analyze the role of artificial intelligence in reducing agency costs and improving the efficiency of institutional control, considering the rapid developments in the adoption of artificial intelligence technologies in auditing, control management risk, and corporate governance. The study addressed a research problem arising from the limited theoretical foundation and the scarcity of Arabic literature and research examining the relationship between artificial intelligence applications and agency costs, particularly their three dimensions: monitoring costs, bonding costs, and residual loss. The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach and an inductive analytical approach by reviewing and analyzing relevant literature, previous studies, and specialized reports published during the period 2020–2026. The study concluded that artificial intelligence could contribute to the reducing of agency costs by enhancing continuous monitoring, improving the quality and timeliness of information, reducing information asymmetry, supporting decision-making, and enabling the early detection of errors, fraud, and managerial deviations. The findings also indicated that artificial intelligence applications in auditing, control, and risk management facilitate a shift from ex post control to proactive and intelligent control, thereby enhancing institutional control efficiency,…

abstract: Abstract We compared perioperative outcomes after robotic (rRC) and laparoscopic right hemicolectomy (lapRC) and assessed temporal changes in surgical approach and minimally invasive completion. This retrospective cohort included patients operated between January 2023 and March 2026. Primary outcomes were operative duration, open conversion, and 30-day morbidity. The main comparison was unadjusted, supplemented by elective and propensity-score-matched analyses. Temporal trends included all screened patients, including primary open procedures. A total of 221 patients were analyzed, including 122 rRC and 99 lapRC procedures. Median operative duration was greater with rRC than with lapRC (264 vs. 200 min, p < 0.001), whereas conversion to an open procedure occurred less frequently after rRC (4% vs. 20%, p < 0.001). Overall morbidity (28% vs. 35%, p = 0.246) and major complications (12% vs. 12%, p = 1) did not differ significantly. Median lymph-node yield in carcinoma resections was 26 versus 25 (p = 0.249). The conversion difference was not statistically significant in the overall elective cohort or the matched analysis of 32 pairs. Across all 390 screened patients, increasing robotic use coincided with decreasing primary open surgery (p = 0.014), while the increase in minimally invasive completion was not statistically significant (p = 0.075). Robotic right hemicolectomy may offe…

title: The intention of followers of financial digital influencers to follow their recommendations
abstract: Purpose Financial digital influencers on social media have become important sources of financial information. However, the mechanisms underlying followers’ trust and follow these recommendations still need to be better understood. This paper aims to measure the factors that explain followers’ intention to follow financial digital influencers’ recommendations. Design/methodology/approach A survey was conducted among the target audience of followers of financial digital influencers, obtaining 421 valid responses, and structural equation modeling was used. Findings The results show that all hypotheses were supported, and that parasocial interaction, information quality, and the need for information directly affect followers’ intentions to follow financial digital influencers’ recommendations. The most significant factor in the follower’s behavioral intention is the need for information. Originality/value A new hypothetical model was created that integrates followers’ perceptions of parasocial interaction, the quality of information characteristics, the financial attributes of digital influencers, and the need for their followers’ information. Despite its parsimony, the model considers various drivers of digital influencers’ followers’ intentions and is specifically aimed at this underexplored context. This study’s main contributions are identifying factors that explain digital inf…

title: Seeing it in a new light: do cross-disciplinary comparisons improve understanding of economic and financial concepts?
abstract: Purpose Analogies can simplify complex new material by relating it to ideas students already know. Making cross-disciplinary connections also makes the material more engaging, accessible and memorable. This study aims to perform a controlled empirical test to examine whether providing cross-disciplinary analogy examples enhances students’ learning. Design/methodology/approach The authors first teach four concepts in the “conventional” way as typically taught in introductory economics and finance courses. Then, for each concept, the authors ask students how well they think they understand the concept and give them one test question related to the concept to gauge their actual understanding of the concept that was taught. Then, the authors provide analogous examples extracted from other disciplines and everyday life related to the concept. Finally, students complete a second survey similar to the first one. The goal is to determine whether the analogies have improved students’ self-perceived understanding of the material. Findings The authors find strong evidence of an increase in students’ self-reported understanding of the material and actual performance after exposure to analogies. Students who are less familiar with the concepts prior to the class benefit from the analogy examples the most. About 40% of the students report that examples that cross-reference their major facili…

Winding-configuration-switching-based field control method and coil design for transcranial magnetic stimulation
abstract: Purpose To improve the field-adjustment flexibility of conventional transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) coils and reduce the system complexity of multicoil arrays, this study aims to propose a single-coil field-control method based on winding-configuration switching (WCS). Design/methodology/approach An analytical electromagnetic-field calculation model for arbitrarily shaped TMS coils was developed and validated against finite-element simulations. A reconfigurable prototype coil was then fabricated, and its electrical parameters, preliminary high-voltage loading performance and static magnetic-field distributions were experimentally tested. Findings The analytical model agreed well with finite-element results, with maximum errors of 0.83% for the magnetic field and 1.26% for the induced electric field. The calculated results showed quantifiable shifts in the induced electric-field focal positions under two winding configurations. Prototype measurements agreed with analytical predictions, with maximum-field deviations of 0.87% for WC1 and 3.15% for WC2, and peak-normalized errors below 5% along the selected diagonal line. Originality/value The proposed WCS method enables reconfigurable field control by changing the effective turns and current directions within a single coil, providing a new route for low-complexity TMS coil design. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces with liquid crystal technology: a hardware design and communication perspective
abstract: Abstract With the surge of theoretical work investigating Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) for wireless communication and sensing, there exists an urgent need of hardware solutions for the evaluation of these theoretical results and further advancing the field. The most common solutions proposed in the literature are based on varactors, Positive-Intrinsic-Negative (PIN) diodes, and Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS). This paper presents the use of Liquid Crystal (LC) technology for the realization of continuously-tunable extremely large millimeter-wave RISs. We review the basic physical principles of LC theory, introduce two different realizations of LC-RISs, namely resonant versus delay-line architectures, and highlight their key properties that have an impact on the system design and RIS reconfiguration strategy. Moreover, the LC technology is compared with the competing technologies in terms of feasibility, cost, power consumption, reconfiguration speed, and bandwidth. Furthermore, several important open problems for both theoretical and experimental research on LC-RISs are presented.

United we litigate, divided we legislate: divergent feminist legal mobilization in South Korean statutory rape law reform
abstract: Abstract Scholars have examined how legal mobilization unifies or divides social movement organizations, largely treating it as a singular process. Yet, social movement organizations united in litigation may diverge in legislative reform. Drawing on the case of South Korea’s statutory rape law, I show how organizational identities rooted in distinct ideological orientations and commitments to different victim populations remained implicit during collaborative litigation. When a legislative opening emerged from changing political opportunities, some organizations advanced age-based protections while others resisted, interpreting age-raising as undermining transformative reforms of rape law toward a consent-based definition of rape. The findings demonstrate that legal institutions mediate how organizational identity shapes responses to political opportunities: litigation enables bracketing differences, while legislation exposes divergent interpretations. This paper contributes to an understanding of how legal mobilization and movement factions are structured and operate.

title: The restricted Erlang-R queue: finite-size effects in service systems with returning customers
abstract: Abstract We study a restricted version of the Erlang-R queueing model that has both server and space constraints, in which the space restriction is administered by two types of admission policies: blocking or holding in a pre-entrant queue. This model, in which customers occupying spaces may be either “needy” (requiring attention from servers) or “content,” captures a wide range of service environments, such as medical units, contact centers, and courts. We study the interplay between the two resource constraints and the reentrant queueing structure. We analyze the connection between staffing, space, and policy decisions and the system performance as a tool for optimizing resource utilization and in determining stability and performance. We develop product form and many-server approximations of performance measures when the blocking policy applies, and then utilize these results to determine approximations for the holding policy as well. We show that system dynamics are captured by a single measure of the fraction time a customer is “needy” in the network, and that returning customers should be explicitly accounted for both in steady-state and transient environments. We show that capacity allocation of both resource constraints (servers and space) should be considered jointly, and derive methodology to determine it. We show that applying a holding policy requires more resources…

abstract: Digital transformation calls for Islamic educational leadership grounded in Islamic values to address the challenges faced by Generation Alpha, particularly regarding the validity of information, digital ethics, the protection of learners, and the cultivation of good manners. This study aims to develop a conceptual model of Islamic educational leadership based on Islamic epistemology. The research employs a qualitative approach through a literature review with a conceptual synthesis of the literature on Islamic epistemology, educational leadership, digital transformation, and the learning characteristics of Generation Alpha. Analysis was conducted through the identification of themes, the comparison of theoretical ideas, and the mapping of relationships between concepts. The results of the synthesis produced a model comprising four components: the epistemological foundation; principles of reasoning and decision-making; digital leadership actions; and educational outcome orientation. This model positions the integration of revelation, reason, and empirical experience as the foundation for decision-making, guided by the principles of tabayyun, amanah, justice, and the public good. title: Sustainable Business Models for Climate Resilience: Adapting Organisational Strategy in an Era of Environmental Uncertainty
abstract: This study investigates the application of climate-resilient sustainable business models in the manufacturing and agricultural value chains in Africa and Asia. In the context of heightened environmental volatility and regulatory scrutiny between 2020 and 2024, the study investigates adaptation strategies that are reasonably economical and ecologically viable for addressing specific regional issues. Employing a mixed-method design, quantitative analysis from 87 firms was supplemented with qualitative case studies from 12 industry leaders. The evaluation model incorporated business model innovation, resource use efficiency measurement, and adaptive capacity assessment through executive and sustainability officer interviews. Data collection was done longitudinally over 36 months, factoring in seasonal and periodic extreme weather shifts. The study identified four emergent business models with exceptional resilience: climate-responsive supply chain restructuring, community-embedded production, circular economy integration, and ecosystem service valuation. Implementing these models resulted in 28% reduced disruption costs and 17% increased resource efficiency during extreme weather events compared to traditional models across both continents. abstract: Background: Acute pharyngitis is an inflammatory condition of the pharynx associated with symptoms such as throat pain and difficulty swallowing. In Ayurveda, the condition is considered in relation to Galagraha. Objective: To evaluate the add-on effect of Katphaladi Churna administered with Darvyadi Kwatha Kavala compared with Darvyadi Kwatha Kavala alone in acute pharyngitis. Methods: This randomized comparative clinical trial involved 70 patients allocated to two groups of 35 each. Group A received Darvyadi Kwatha Kavala with Katphaladi Churna (3 g three times daily with honey), while Group B received Darvyadi Kwatha Kavala alone. Treatment continued for seven days, with assessments at baseline (Day 0), Day 3, and Day 8. Outcomes included dysphagia, throat pain, fever, tonsillar enlargement, lymphadenopathy, and pharyngeal redness. Results: Both groups demonstrated significant overall clinical improvement. Mean overall percentage improvement was 64.72% in Group A and 52.71% in Group B. Between-group improvement in dysphagia statistically favored Group A (post-treatment mean score 0.77 ± 0.55 vs. 1.06 ± 0.42; p = 0.016). Between-group differences in throat pain and tonsillar enlargement were not statistically significant. title: Hybrid Optimization-Driven Machine Learning for Intrusion Detection in Cloud Environments: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Cloud computing has become the backbone of modern digital services, but its shared and distributed nature makes it an attractive target for cyber-attacks. Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) built with machine learning and deep learning are now central to cloud security, and a large body of recent work tries to improve them with metaheuristic optimization for feature selection and model tuning. This paper presents a systematic literature review of hybrid optimization-driven machine learning frameworks for intrusion detection, with a focus on cloud and cloud-adjacent (IoT and IIoT) environments. Following a PRISMA-based review process, 30 peer-reviewed studies published between 2008 and 2026 were selected and analysed. The review organises the literature into four themes: cloud intrusion detection with feature selection, hybrid and improved metaheuristic optimization methods, CNN–LSTM and other optimized deep learning models, and foundational or survey work. A comparative analysis of the feature selection method, optimizer design, classifier type and data-balancing strategy used in each study is presented, along with the trend of publications over time. The review finds that although metaheuristic feature selection and CNN–LSTM classifiers are both well studied on their own, very few studies combine a hybrid dual-optimizer search with a CNN–LSTM classifier specifically for cloud n…

abstract: Income-tax filing in India is no longer a form-filling task. Pre-filled data, the Annual Information Statement (AIS), a default new tax regime and an expanding set of return forms mean that two taxpayers with similar gross income can face very different filing paths. This paper reports a practice-based study carried out during a twelve-week on-the-job training placement (11 May – 3 August 2026) at a Pune-based tax-advisory firm that combines professional review with workflow automation. It asks (1) how taxpayer profile shapes the filing pathway, (2) when the old tax regime outperforms the new regime for individuals in Assessment Year 2026–27, and (3) which control points in a hybrid advisory workflow reduce avoidable error. The paper contributes a fourteen-stage filing workflow with explicit control points, a rule-based ITR applicability matrix, a transparent regime-comparison model with computed break-even deductions, and a case-complexity score. Using the model, a salaried taxpayer with ₹18 lakh gross salary needs about ₹6.42 lakh of old-regime deductions beyond the standard deduction to match the new regime, a level that few salaried taxpayers reach. Case-mix and process-performance figures in the paper are illustrative and are labelled as such; they demonstrate a measurement design and are not verified firm records. abstract: Background and Aims: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection is one of the most prevalent chronic bacterial infections worldwide. Literature describes several endoscopic signs that might predict H. pylori status. However, random biopsies according to Sydney system are still widely used for its determination. We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of endoscopic characteristics in predicting H. pylori infection. Methods: This is a monocentric prospective study including all consecutive patients who underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy in one-year timeframe. In each procedure regular arrangement of collecting venules (RAC), fundic gland polyps (FGPs), linear streaks, hematin spots, diffuse redness and intestinal metaplasia were described. H. pylori infection was histologically investigated. Results: A total of 421 patients were enrolled (F: 222, 52.7%, median age 54.1). The presence of RAC both in greater and in lesser curvature and FGPs were significantly associated with lower prevalence of H. pylori infection, by contrast, diffuse redness was associated with a higher prevalence (p<0.0001). Considering the interaction effect by the optical evidence of intestinal metaplasia, RAC and FGPs maintained their significance with an OR of 0.05 (0.02-0.13) and 0.11 (0.03-0.53), respectively. abstract: The rapid development of digital technology has transformed pharmaceutical services through the integration of modern pharmacy systems, increasing the need to understand the factors influencing public adoption of pharmacy services. This study aims to examine the effects of perceived modern pharmacy features, service quality, and product quality on public interest in using pharmacy services among residents of Banyuwangi. A quantitative explanatory approach was employed using a cross-sectional survey design, with 100 respondents selected through purposive sampling based on the criteria of being at least 18 years old, residing in Banyuwangi, and having visited a pharmacy within the past six months. Data were collected through an online questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression with JASP software. The multiple linear regression results indicate that the overall regression model is statistically significant (F(3, 96) = 1043.157, p < 0.001) and explains 97.0% of the variance in interest in using pharmacy services (R² = 0.970). title: From Rules to Autonomous Agents: The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence, Human-AI Integration, and the Governance of Agentic Systems-A Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence has evolved from rule-based symbolic systems into learning architectures capable of perception, prediction, content generation, reasoning, planning, tool use, and increasingly autonomous action. This qualitative literature review examines this transition as more than a technological chronology. It interprets AI evolution through five interrelated dimensions: technological evolution, capability expansion, changing human roles, human–AI integration, and governance. Drawing on contemporary peer-reviewed literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026, the review identifies seven thematic developments. AI has progressed from encoded rules toward learned representations and goal-directed action; generative AI has expanded AI into a general-purpose content collaborator; agentic AI adds planning, memory, tool use, and iterative task execution; human roles increasingly shift from operator toward collaborator, delegator, and governor; human–AI complementarity remains conditional rather than automatic; effective deployment requires calibrated rather than maximal trust; and governance requirements increase as AI systems acquire greater operational agency. The article proposes the Evolution–Capability–Role–Integration–Governance (ECRIG) framework to explain these relationships. The framework suggests that sustainable benefits from advanced AI emerge when techno…

A Synthesis-based Method for Design Space Exploration in High-Level Synthesis of RISC-V RV32IM Microprocessors
abstract: High-Level Synthesis (HLS) is a hardware design technique that interprets an algorithm-level description and transforms it into a digital circuit to implement the desired behavior. To obtain optimized RTL (Register-Transfer Level) descriptions for a given parameter and respect design constraints, design space exploration (DSE) is a fundamental activity. The most common way to do this in HLS is through pragmas (directives that provide additional information to the compiler to transform the high-level code), and different combinations can lead to different design implementations. In this research, the main goal is to propose a method to explore the design space and perform subsequent optimizations for the high-level synthesis of microprocessors that implement the RISC-V RV32IM instruction set. We aim to contribute to the definition of criteria to explore and evaluate the various solutions that can be obtained by varying the configurations that impact the HLS steps, with a focus on area and power. With our method, we obtain improvements in these metrics, with the best being 16.39% for area and 3.62% for power. The results show that our method can improve the quality of results with an easy-to-apply approach, without the need to build complex exploration methods, while preserving the benefits of a higher level of abstraction provided by HLS.

title: The 2026 Election Bill as an Arena for Oligarchic Cartel Adaptation: Constitutional Court Decisions and Meaningful Participation in Contemporary Indonesia
abstract: This article examines Indonesia's 2026 Election Bill as an arena of oligarchic cartel adaptation within the country's electoral democracy. Building on prior research concerning oligarchic cartelization in the legislative process of the 2017 Election Law, it situates the analysis in the current context of Constitutional Court decisions, meaningful participation, and the regulatory agenda for the 2029 elections. Using a socio-legal approach and a conceptual-policy analysis design, the article examines five mechanisms of oligarchic cartel adaptation: legislative agenda control, the conversion of Constitutional Court decisions into new legal norms, the formalistic absorption of public participation, threshold redesign, and financial opacity. The article argues that electoral law reform should not be understood merely as a technocratic agenda, but as a contested field between democratic participation and oligarchic wealth. Constitutional Court decisions and meaningful participation may open opportunities for democratic correction. However, such opportunities can be neutralized when the legislative process remains controlled by actors who benefit from electoral rules. The article contributes by operationalizing the concept of oligarchic cartel adaptation as an evaluative framework for the 2026 Election Bill.

abstract: This study aims to describe students’ responses to hybrid Project-Based Learning (PjBL)-STEAM through a plastic-waste collage project in Grade VI IPAS learning. A quantitative descriptive design involved 27 students. Responses were observed through ten indicators: interest, active participation, understanding of instructions, response to digital media, collaboration, responsibility, creativity, problem solving, communication, and reflection. The overall score was 999 out of a maximum of 1,080, equivalent to 92.50% and categorized as very positive. Interest and collaboration obtained the highest percentages, while communication/presentation was relatively lower but remained in the very positive category. The novelty lies in mapping students’ responses to the synergy of two learning processes—concrete project activities and guided digital support—within Hybrid PjBL-STEAM using plastic waste as an authentic context. The findings imply that technology should strengthen visualization, documentation, and data presentation, while hands-on experience, collaboration, product development, testing, and reflection remain central to elementary IPAS learning.

Learning epithelial elasticity via local tension remodeling
abstract: Abstract Biological materials such as epithelial tissues continuously remodel their internal structure in response to mechanical forces, but whether this adaptation amounts to a genuine form of physical learning has remained unclear. Here we show that an active vertex model of epithelial sheets, equipped with a single local, mechanosensitive tensionremodeling rule, exhibits the three canonical hallmarks of learning matter. First, at the scale of a single junction, repeated contractile pulses produce habituation: a diminishing, history-dependent response that encodes a memory of prior stimulation. Second, at the tissue scale, a localized stimulus writes a long-range mechanical memory that biases the response to a later, distant stimulus. We derive a continuum theory showing that this memory is transmitted as a system-wide elastic bias and predict its dependence on tissue size and remodeling rate. Third, under cyclic bulk driving, the tissue can be trained to a target mechanical state, autonomously tuning its Poisson ratio to auxetic (negative) values through directed remodeling rather than designed geometry. We further derive an effective viscoelastic memory kernel that distinguishes this adaptive tissue from a passive vertex model. title: Deep Neck Infection From Maxillary Sinusitis With a Fungal Ball in Diffuse Panbronchiolitis
abstract: Maxillary sinus fungal balls are typically noninvasive and confined to the sinus cavity in immunocompetent patients. We report a rare case of rapidly progressive deep neck infection associated with maxillary sinusitis and a noninvasive fungal ball in a patient with previously unrecognized diffuse panbronchiolitis (DPB). A 72-year-old woman with asthma presented with progressive right facial swelling and leukocytosis. CT showed bilateral calcified maxillary lesions consistent with fungal balls and inflammatory extension from the right maxillary/nasal floor region to the parapharyngeal and submandibular spaces. Chest high-resolution CT showed findings consistent with DPB. She underwent endoscopic sinus surgery, medial maxillectomy, transcervical abscess drainage, and tracheostomy. Histopathology showed septate hyphae without tissue or vascular invasion. Cultures grew Aspergillus fumigatus from sinus contents and Pseudomonas aeruginosa from the neck abscess. This case highlights the potential severity of fungal ball-associated sinusitis when mucosal necrosis, bacterial infection, and impaired mucociliary clearance coexist.

title: A Multi‐Blockchain Structure in the Carbon Market Trading: A Case Analysis in the Chinese Carbon Exchange
abstract: ABSTRACT We propose a novel multi‐blockchain framework for carbon futures trading to enhance innovation and liquidity in China's national carbon market. Our approach introduces: (1) a tailored trading framework that integrates standard operations with regulatory requirements from multiple authorities; (2) a design of four distinct blockchain types to ensure data privacy and seamless system interaction; and (3) a cross‐chain mechanism for data consistency, verification and compliance. Experimental results validate the model's effectiveness. This work supports China's dual‐carbon goals by advancing carbon finance through a secure and efficient trading system.

title: Distribution system operator discretion and procedural protection of market participants in EU electricity network access
abstract: Abstract This article analyses how EU electricity law organises procedural protection when access to distribution networks depends on the discretion of distribution system operators (DSOs). It argues that network access is not framed as an automatic subjective right but operates through a model of regulatory obligations: DSOs make technically grounded, case-by-case assessments, constrained mainly by the requirements of objectivity and non-discrimination, and corrected primarily through national regulatory authority dispute settlement and ex post judicial review. The article’s main contribution is to shift the focus from “who has access” to how discretion is allocated, limited, and made legally accountable under the requirements of the rule of law (legal certainty, predictability, and effective control of discretion). A functional comparison with EU electronic communications law shows that telecommunications law embeds more explicit procedural structuring, which supports predictability and has coincided with the development of a richer body of case law at EU level concerning regulatory discretion. By contrast, distribution-level electricity access disputes remain largely channelled through national regulatory and judicial frameworks, leaving procedural clarity and timing more fragmented across Member States. The article concludes that in discretion-based access regimes, the qual…

title: Thị trường chứng khoán Việt Nam và chính sách thương mại thời Trump: Sau mỗi cú sốc là sự ổn định?

ESG Performance, Disclosure and Environmental Intensity: Implications for Profitability in Emerging Market Energy Companies
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between ESG performance, environmental intensity, greenwashing, and profitability in energy companies operating in emerging markets. An unbalanced panel of 95 publicly listed companies from Asia, Europe, and Latin America over 2015–2024 is analyzed using dynamic panel‐data models. ESG performance is found to be positively associated with profitability, while environmental intensity exerts a negative effect. The positive impact of ESG performance is stronger in larger companies, suggesting that organizational scale enhances the benefits derived from sustainability initiatives. Greenwashing, measured as the gap between ESG disclosure and ESG performance, is negatively associated with profitability, indicating that sustainability claims are penalized when they are not supported by actual ESG outcomes. The results also show that the COVID‐19 pandemic and the Russia‐Ukraine conflict reduced the profitability penalty associated with greenwashing. The findings highlight the importance of disclosure credibility and ESG performance in emission‐intensive industries.

abstract: Background: The efficiency of health services is a fundamental indicator of health system performance, and macroeconomic conditions are linked to it through public budgets, the cost of imported medicines and equipment, and households' ability to pay. This study examined the association of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), exchange rate, and inflation with the efficiency of health services in Iran across distinct regimes over 2000–2023. Methods: This applied, analytical time-series study used annual data for 2000–2023 collected from the World Bank and the Central Bank of Iran. Technical efficiency was estimated with an output-oriented Banker–Charnes–Cooper (BCC) data envelopment analysis model with five inputs and the inverse crude mortality rate as the output. The association of the cyclical components of GDP, exchange rate, and inflation with efficiency was estimated with a two-regime Markov switching regression controlling for COVID-19, in Python. Results: Mean technical efficiency was 0.969; 11 of 24 years lay on the frontier, and the lowest score occurred in 2021 (0.739). The two-regime model outperformed the linear model (bootstrap p = 0.005). abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of leadership style and organizational culture on employee performance through motivation at the Community and Village Empowerment Office of West Tanjung Jabung Regency. The study population was all employees of the Community and Village Empowerment Office of West Tanjung Jabung Regency, with a sample of 49 respondents determined using a sampling technique based on the characteristics of the study population. title: Changes in forage yield and botanical composition in a species diversity by harvest height by frequency experiment over 3 years in Hawke’s Bay
abstract: There has been considerable interest in regenerative agriculture and the potential impact of diverse forage mixtures and grazing to higher residuals on pasture production and soil quality. This study evaluated the species mixtures at three defoliation heights and two defoliation frequencies. The experiment was carried out over 3 years at a summer-dry site in Hawke’s Bay. The treatments were: mixtures of six cultivars of four species (ryegrass/clover) and 18 cultivars of 16 species (diverse), defoliation heights of 5, 10 and 15 cm to replicate normal, lax and very lax grazing, and defoliation frequencies of 4 and 8 weeks, over the 3 years. Total dry matter production was 23,910 kg/ha for the diverse mixture compared with 19,060 kg/ha for ryegrass/clover and decreased from 29,410 kg/ha for the 5 cm defoliation height to 21,200 kg/ha for 10 cm and 13,840 kg/ha for 15 cm, with no effect of defoliation frequency. As defoliation height increased, so did the amount of dead matter, and thus feed quality would have declined. The greater dry matter production in the diverse mixture was likely to be at least partially due to the presence of chicory and plantain.

Plasma rich in growth factors (PRGF), a leukocyte‐poor autologous platelet concentrate, represents a biologically active diluent that may modulate the biological response to CaHA. title: Dynamics of a regulation mechanism of variable geometry
abstract: This research is motivated by the functional demands of mode selector valves in variable cycle engines, leading to the design of an innovative eight-sector, over-constrained regulation mechanism. It employs eight curved-plate links arranged symmetrically to convert rotational inputs into smooth reciprocating translational motion of a movable octagonal ring. This kinematic configuration enables the precise and repeatable positioning essential for reliable mode selector valve operation. A comprehensive dynamic analysis of this multi-rigid-body system is then undertaken, serving a dual purpose. First, it establishes the theoretical foundation for accurately determining the external loads experienced by the mechanism under various operating conditions. Second, it supports the development of a control algorithm capable of computing the driving forces required to achieve the desired open/close motion. Together, these capabilities form the basis for reliable and efficient actuation of the mode selector valves within a variable cycle engine environment. Building upon a prior kinematic analysis of valve operation, this study investigates the dynamics of the over-constrained system. The dynamic model is formulated using momentum and force screws, a screw mechanics approach that preserves all the strengths of the Newton-Euler method while offering a key computational advantage. title: The Influence of Transportation Costs, Monthly Income, Digital Wallet Use, and Financial Planning on the Frequency of Online Motorcycle Taxi Use
abstract: This study examines the relationship between transportation costs, monthly income, digital wallet usage, and financial planning and the frequency of online motorcycle taxi use among students in the Management Study Program at Pamulang University. A quantitative approach was employed using purposive sampling. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to seventh- and eighth-semester students who used online motorcycle taxi services. Of the 255 questionnaires distributed, 150 valid and complete responses were included in the analysis. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and hypothesis testing. The findings indicate that transportation costs, monthly income, and financial planning have positive and statistically significant relationships with the frequency of online motorcycle taxi use (p < .001 for each variable). In contrast, digital wallet usage has a positive but statistically insignificant relationship with usage frequency (t = 0.467, p = .641). Simultaneously, the four independent variables are significantly associated with usage frequency (F = 147.496, p < .001), with an R² value of .803, indicating that the model explains 80.3% of the observed variation in usage frequency. These findings highlight the relevance of economic conditions and financial management behavior in understanding students’ use of online motorcycle taxi services, while su…

title: Climate, Nature, and the Uneven Expansion of Financial Governance
abstract: ABSTRACT Financial authorities have developed extensive climate‐related policies, but nature‐related financial policy remains less widespread. Using data on individual policy instruments across 116 jurisdictions from 2000 to 2025, this paper compares the adoption, policy areas, binding status, and source of climate‐ and nature‐related policies. Nature‐related policies appear in 27 jurisdictions, compared with 60 for climate‐only policies. National nature adoption is positively associated with a larger existing body of climate and environmental financial policies, mainly through the broader environmental component rather than climate‐specific policy. Climate‐only policies are used more frequently in prudential supervision and credit allocation than policies that combine nature with climate or broader environmental concerns. Nature‐related policies have a higher mandatory share over the full period but a lower share than climate‐only policies in 2023–2025. In the European Union, broad EU‐level coverage coexists with limited national issuance. The paper contributes a common framework for comparing climate and nature policies and distinguishes EU‐level coverage from national policy development. The results show that the climate‐nature gap concerns not only adoption, but also where policies are used, how binding they are, and which level of authority issues them.
