الكفاءة الذاتية الإرشادية المُدرَكة وعلاقتها بالتنظيم الانفعالي البين شخصي لدى طالبات قسم علم النفس
abstract: هدفت الدراسة الحالية إلى التعرف على مستوى كلٍّ من الكفاءة الذاتية الإرشادية المُدرَكة التنظيم الانفعالي البين شخصي لدى طالبات قسم علم النفس، والكشف عن طبيعة العلاقة بين المتغيرين، واختبار إمكانية التنبؤ بالتنظيم الانفعالي بين الشخصي من خلال الكفاءة الذاتية الإرشادية المُدرَكة. واتبعت الدراسة المنهج الوصفي الارتباطي، وطُبِّق مقياس التنظيم الانفعالي البين شخصي (IERQ) ومقياس الكفاءة الذاتية الإرشادية المُدرَكة على عينة متاحة قوامها (118) طالبة من طالبات قسم علم النفس بجامعة جدة خلال العام الجامعي 2026م. وأظهرت النتائج أن مستوى الكفاءة الذاتية الإرشادية المُدرَكة كان مرتفعًا (م = 3.94، الوزن النسبي = 78.9%)، في حين كان مستوى التنظيم الانفعالي البين شخصي متوسطًا (م = 3.50، الوزن النسبي = 69.9. كما كشفت النتائج عن وجود علاقة ارتباطية موجبة دالة إحصائيًا عند مستوى (0.01) بين الكفاءة الذاتية الإرشادية المُدرَكة التنظيم الانفعالي البين شخصي (r = 0.497)، وظهرت ارتباطات دالة بين أبعاد المتغيرين، باستثناء بُعد الهدوء والسكينة الذي لم يرتبط ارتباطًا دالًا بالكفاءة الذاتية الإرشادية المُدرَكة. وأظهر تحليل الانحدار الخطي البسيط أن الكفاءة الذاتية الإرشادية المُدرَكة تفسر (24.7%) من التباين في التنظيم الانفعالي البين شخصي ونوقشت النتائج في ضوء الأدبيات النظرية والدراسات السابقة، واختُتمت الدراسة بمجموعة من التوصيات التطبيقية والمقترحات البحثية.

title: Tunable Wrinkled Topographies Reveal Feature-Size-Dependent Regulation of Neuronal and Glial Spatial Organization
abstract: Abstract Purpose Mechanical cues presented by biomaterial surfaces are powerful regulators of cellular behavior, yet how topographical feature size differentially regulates neuronal and glial spatial organization remains poorly understood. Although anisotropic surface architectures have been shown to promote neural alignment and neurite outgrowth, systematic comparisons across multiple topographical regimes within a common material platform have been limited. Methods To address this gap, we developed a scalable wrinkle-based nanofabrication platform capable of generating anisotropic MXene topographies spanning characteristic nano-, submicron-, and micron-scale regimes. By varying multilayer thickness, the platform enabled systematic shifts in characteristic wrinkle dimensions while maintaining a common material composition and surface chemistry. Results Using this platform, we found that distinct regenerative processes exhibit different responses across the topographical regimes. While all wrinkled topographies effectively aligned Schwann cells, the nanoscale topographies produced the greatest cellular elongation. In contrast, submicron and microscale topographies showed greater early neuronal alignment, whereas the submicron topography showed the greatest neurite extension while maintaining strong directional guidance following differentiation. Conclusions These findings revea…

Glial-Mediated Neuroimmune Regulation in the Brain–Heart Axis: Regional Involvement, Autonomic Imbalance and Cardiovascular Remodelling
abstract: Bidirectional communication between the brain and heart involves neuroimmune mechanisms, yet the contributions of glial responses in different brain regions to autonomic dysfunction and cardiovascular remodelling remain incompletely understood. This narrative review integrates evidence on microglial and astrocytic regulation of the brain–heart axis, focusing on autonomic brain regions and their molecular responses to cardiovascular injury. We examine how inflammatory, humoral and neural signals engage glial cells and influence neurovascular integrity, neurotransmitter homeostasis and neuronal excitability. Particular attention is given to angiotensin II signalling, purinergic pathways, NLRP3 inflammasome activation and oxidative stress as mechanisms linking glial responses to altered sympathetic–vagal balance. Across hypertension, myocardial infarction and heart failure, studies report glial alterations in multiple brain regions, with selected experiments supporting contributions to autonomic regulation and cardiovascular outcomes. However, regional involvement does not by itself establish distinct glial states or region-specific functions. We therefore distinguish regional distribution, molecular/cellular heterogeneity and causal function within a defined region, and propose a framework for testing how anatomical context, cellular state and disease stage may influence glial ef…

title: Exploring the role of COVID-19 pandemic preparedness in Norway’s Ukrainian refugee crisis response
abstract: Aims: The aim of this study was to explore how and in what ways COVID-19 preparedness in Norway shaped the organization and delivery of the country’s response to the Ukrainian refugee crisis and identify lessons learned from the overlap of the pandemic and the refugee crisis to strengthen Norway’s preparedness for future crises, as perceived by the participants. Methods: A qualitative study with in-depth, semi-structured, individual interviews was conducted among 10 individual, civil society, and government actors who worked in relation to both the COVID-19 pandemic and the Ukrainian refugee crisis. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Results: The following four themes emerged, including both positive and negative consequences of the end of the pandemic overlapping with the beginning of the Ukrainian refugee crisis: (1) pandemic-shaped mindsets and momentum in crisis response, (2) adapting pandemic resources for refugee crisis response, (3) participation and power in crisis decision-making, and (4) lessons learned: continuity is key. Conclusions: This study provides an enhanced understanding of how selected Norwegian actors perceived the role of COVID-19 preparedness in the Ukrainian refugee crisis response. Participants identified both strengths, such as the reuse of resources and coordination structures, and challenges related to communication and participation in…

title: Supraventricular Tachycardia as a Cardiopulmonary Stress Response to Traumatic Chylopneumothorax and Diaphragmatic Hernia: A Case Report
abstract: Background: Supraventricular Tachycardia (SVT) is a heart rhythm disorder characterized by an increased heart rate originating from the Atrioventricular (AV) node in the atrium. It is characterized by an Electrocardiography (ECG) tracing showing a narrow QRS complex (<120 ms) and a rapid, regular heartbeat. Blunt trauma to the thoracoabdominal region can cause diaphragmatic hernia and chylopneumothorax. Both conditions could escalate the progression of cardiopulmonary stress, such as heart rhythm disturbance (arrhythmia). Case Illustration: We report a case of a 30-year-old woman who presented to the Emergency Room with sudden palpitations 1 day ago. Physical examination revealed a restless appearance (Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS] E4V5M6), blood pressure 146/94 mmHg, pulse rate 155 beats per minute (bpm), respiratory rate 30 bpm, temperature 36 °C, and saturation 95% on room air. In the thoracic region, dull percussion was found in the lower left hemithorax, decreased left lung base sounds, bowel sounds were heard, and tenderness was observed in the left costovertebral angle in the abdominal region. ECG examination showed the presence of SVT with a heart rate of 176 bpm. The patient was initially managed by performing a vagal maneuver, but it failed. The patient was then transferred to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), underwent further diagnostic examinations, and received further th…

The experiences of patients, their families, and carers during care from alternative ambulance response units: A scoping review
abstract: Purpose of the research In response to increasing demand and the changing nature of patient presentations and to maintain emergency response capability, ambulance health services are adapting their approaches to health service delivery. Initiatives include dispatch of alternative response units (ARUs) that deliver tailored care for patients with non-time-critical needs. As advocated by both the World Health Organisation and the Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care, routinely capturing patients’ experiences of care is imperative to evaluate and strengthen such innovations in healthcare models. To inform the development of a valid and reliable patient-reported experience measure, this scoping review aims to identify currently known key constructs of experience as described by patients and their families or carers when receiving unscheduled care from ARUs. This scoping review was informed by mixed-methods guidance, searched databases MEDLINE Complete, CINAHL Complete, APA PsycInfo, Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection, and grey literature. Major findings Three studies conducted in diverse settings and applying heterogeneous methodologies were identified. Concepts reported by patients, their families, and carers about their experience highlighted the convenience of receiving care within their home while avoiding unnecessary attendance at hospital, receivi…

Exploratory Multimodal Machine Learning for Hazard Response Detection in Semi-Automated Rural Driving
abstract: Partially automated driving systems require drivers to remain cognitively engaged and prepared to respond to unexpected roadway hazards despite reduced direct vehicle control. In rural driving, low visibility and sudden animal crossings pose unique safety challenges to driver readiness and response capability. This study presents an exploratory multimodal machine learning framework for hazard-response classification under semi-automated rural driving. Using a high-fidelity driving simulator, EEG, eye activity, behavioral, and subjective workload data were acquired under manual and Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS)-supported conditions. Pre-hazard event-level features were evaluated using logistic regression, random forest, and multilayer perceptron classifiers with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. Random Forest achieved the highest mean classification accuracy, although performance was constrained by class imbalance and limited sensitivity to brake events. Feature-importance analysis identified SART situation-awareness score as the most influential feature, followed by NASA-TLX workload, pupil-diameter change, and EEG-derived measures. These findings support multimodal hazard-response classification for future driver-readiness modeling.

abstract: Background: Pelargonium graveolens is traditionally used for its anti-inflammatory and wound-healing properties. However, its effects on phagocytosis, nociception, and tissue repair remain poorly characterized. Methods: Polysaccharides were identified in the extract. Tyrosinase, elastase, and collagenase inhibitory activities were evaluated in vitro. Systemic phagocytosis was assessed by the carbon clearance assay in rats (n = 6/group; oral extract, 300 and 600 mg/kg for 12 days). Anti-inflammatory and antinociceptive activities were evaluated using carrageenan-induced paw oedema (n = 5/group; topical 3% and 6% cream) and plantar thermal tests (n = 6/group), respectively. Wound healing was evaluated separately using only the topical 6% cream for 15 days in rats (n = 6/group; topical 6% cream), followed by histopathological evaluation. Results: The extract contained D-glucose (72.76 ± 3.64 µg/mL) and polysaccharides (2.89 ± 1.55 mg GE/g DE). It inhibited tyrosinase (IC50 = 340.80 ± 28.61 µg/mL), elastase (IC50 = 761.67 ± 14.62 µg/mL), and collagenase (IC50 = 456.55 ± 6.14 µg/mL) in a concentration-dependent manner. Phagocytic activity increased, reaching a phagocytic index of 0.023 ± 0.005 at 600 mg/kg. Topical 3% and 6% creams were evaluated for anti-inflammatory activity, with the 6% cream showing the highest effect (83.36 ± 0.78% inhibition at 240 min) and increased paw withd…

title: Organ-specific depth of response to CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in B-cell lymphomas
abstract: Abstract Background CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy (CART) has transformed treatment of relapsed or refractory (r/r) large B cell lymphoma (LBCL); however, organ-specific response patterns and depth of response (DoR) remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated organ-specific imaging response and the impact of spatial disease patterns on progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Materials and methods In this retrospective single-center study, 109 consecutive patients with r/r LBCL treated with CD19-directed CART between January 2019 and May 2025 were included. Baseline and follow-up CT or PET/CT was analyzed using structured lesion tracking. Up to six target lesions per patient were assessed according to Lugano criteria, and the sum of the products of diameters (SPD) was calculated. DoR was defined as percentage change in SPD from baseline. Associations with PFS and OS were evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox regression. Results Among 109 patients (median age, 65 years [IQR, 57–71]), 65 (59.6%) had extranodal disease at baseline. Baseline tumor burden was higher in patients with extranodal than nodal disease (median SPD, 3573 mm 2 [IQR, 1314–9708] versus 1998 mm 2 [IQR, 1347–2921]). title: PASTORAL RESPONSE TO PEACEFUL COEXISTENCE BETWEEN CHRISTIANS AND MUSLIMS IN OGBOMOSO
abstract: Ogbomoso in Oyo State, Nigeria is one of the great locations in Africa, with peculiar ethnic groups and a multi-religious cultural setting including Christianity, Islam and African Traditional religion. This article examines the crucial roles expected of Pastors and other religions leaders in fostering peaceful coexistence and sustainable development. The article argues that peaceful coexistence, rather than movements aimed at connecting the partition is a panacea for sustainable development along the boundaries. Specifically, peaceful coexistence enhances development along the boundary corridor. Religions supposedly do not make us hate one another, but not enough to make us loved one another due to hatred and no peace. This is exactly the case in Ogbomoso, Oyo State, Nigeria. Religion that is supposed to keep people in love has turned into pillar of enmity among religions adherence in Nigeria.

title: Development and Performance Evaluation of a Mountain-Focused WRF Rainfall Forecasting System: A Case Study of the July 2025 Heavy Rainfall Event in South Korea
abstract: This study evaluates a Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) system with a 500 m horizontal grid spacing developed to provide mountain-focused rainfall guidance for forest disaster preparedness in South Korea. The system uses operational 1.5 km Local Data Assimilation and Prediction System (LDAPS) fields provided by the Korea Meteorological Administration as background and lateral boundary conditions. Quality-controlled Automatic Mountain Meteorology Observation System (AMOS) observations, excluding rainfall, are assimilated using three-dimensional variational (3D-Var) data assimilation. The resulting forecasts (DA_AMOS) are compared with LDAPS for the 16–20 July 2025 heavy rainfall event using 500 m gridded and in situ AMOS rainfall observations. Compared with LDAPS, DA_AMOS better reproduced observed accumulated and maximum rainfall magnitudes, with smaller regional station-mean accumulation errors in 13 of 15 administrative divisions with eligible AMOS stations. DA_AMOS generally showed smaller forecast errors at observed rainfall intensities ≥ 10 mm h−1 but larger errors under near-zero-rainfall conditions. During 45 observation-selected extreme-rainfall hours, DA_AMOS reduced mean absolute event-hour bias from 46.14 to 41.74 mm h−1 (9.5%) relative to LDAPS, although substantial underestimation remains. These findings support complementary guidance on rainfall magnitude, t…

title: Synthesis of Nitrogen‐Containing Heterocyclic Scaffolds and Applications in Scaffold Hopping: Development of an Aripiprazole Analog
abstract: Heteroaromatic ring systems play a crucial role in drug development because they modulate physicochemical properties and expand the range of molecular interactions compared to non‐heterocyclic aromatic rings. They are also widely represented among approved drugs. Among heteroatoms, nitrogen is the most prevalent in the diverse scaffold space of heterocyclic drugs, including those generated by fragment‐based drug discovery approach. In this work, we show the synthesis of a set of novel or underexplored nitrogen heterocyclic fragments, obtained in three to five steps in moderate yields. In total, 12 fused [6,6] saturated/unsaturated bicycles were synthesized, which fulfill the general rule of fragment‐like compounds. These heterocycles increased the fragment space of the CRAFT library and showed potential application in scaffold‐hopping strategies for drug design. As a proof of concept, 2,6‐naphthyridin‐3‐ol 2 was used to replace the 7‐hydroxy‐3,4‐dihydroquinolin‐2(1 H )‐one core of aripiprazole 41 , generating 3‐(4‐(4‐(2,3‐dichlorophenyl)piperazin‐1‐yl)butoxy)‐2,6‐naphthyridine 40, that effectively blocked cocaine‐induced hyperactivity in rodents at 20 mg/kg without inducing catalepsy, displaying a pharmacological profile similar to aripiprazole and demonstrating promising antipsychotic potential.

Outbreak Cast-ML: Short-Term Disease Outbreak Analysis and Case Forecasting Using Machine Learning
abstract: Timely estimation of disease trends can help public-health teams plan testing, staffing, beds, medicines, and community communication. This paper presents OutbreakCast-ML, a reproducible machine-learning workflow for analysing reported outbreak data and producing short-horizon forecasts of daily cases and cumulative burden. The workflow combines data validation, daily incident-case derivation, exploratory visualization, time-ordered validation, and a comparison of a seasonalnaïve baseline, statistical time-series forecasting, and supervised regression models using lagged features. The supplied figures are included as illustrative historical visualizations of COVID-19 trends in India, including daily reported cases, cumulative cases, state-wise counts, and a Prophet-style forecast with trend components. These images are treated as reference graphics rather than evidence of current or independently validated model performance. No new numerical accuracy claim is made because the underlying dataset and model outputs were not provided for independent reproduction. The paper defines an evaluation protocol using MAE, RMSE, MAPE where mathematically appropriate, and predictioninterval coverage. It also discusses data quality, reporting delays, uncertainty, ethical communication, and the need for human review before operational use. The proposed contribution is a transparent end-to-end …

title: An Integrated Housing Intervention for People Involved in the Criminal–Legal System: Contributors to Successfully Moving Along the Housing Continuum
abstract: Objectives: People impacted by the criminal–legal system face challenges to securing and sustaining permanent housing. This study was designed to deliver an integrated housing, medical, and behavioral health services intervention to individuals with criminal–legal involvement. Methods: After a baseline needs assessment, participants were linked to services and completed quarterly study visits for up to 12 months. We used descriptive statistics to assess frequency and multivariate logistic regression to assess correlates of housing status at last follow-up. Results: Between June 2019 and November 2023, 187 participants were enrolled in Project CHANGE (Comprehensive Housing and Addiction Treatment Network of Greater New Haven). At baseline, 43% of participants were unstably housed, 37% were homeless, and the remaining resided in a shelter or institution. At the time of last follow-up, 49 participants (26.2%) reported improved housing outcomes, and an additional 121 participants’ (64.7%) housing situation did not worsen. In multivariate models, individuals who were older (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.1; 95% CI, 1.0-1.1), unstably housed at baseline (AOR = 7.6; 95% CI, 3.8-15.9), and enrolled in the study for longer (AOR = 1.2; 95% CI, 1.1-1.3) had higher odds of being housed at last follow-up, whereas those with high-severity substance use had lower odds of being housed (AOR = 0.…

title: Impact of input channel grouping on CNN-based kinematic prediction from inertial gait data
abstract: Accurate gait analysis is fundamental to assessing mobility, diagnosing neurological disorders and monitoring rehabilitation progress. Optical motion capture remains the gold standard for kinematic parameters, but its high cost, need for specialised laboratories and limited capture volume restrict clinical use. Wearable inertial measurement units offer a low-cost alternative for continuous monitoring in natural environments, yet deriving clinically meaningful kinematic variables from raw accelerometer and gyroscope signals remains a signal processing challenge. Deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), can learn hierarchical features directly from raw sensor data, potentially eliminating hand-crafted feature engineering. This study investigates the impact of input channel grouping on the prediction performance of a bespoke CNN architecture for kinematic signal regression from inertial data, specifically for predicting the stride length normalised to body height. We used data from the Machine Learning and Data Analytics Laboratory at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, comprising 101 gait trials with synchronised triaxial accelerometer and gyroscope data from both ankles and reference stride length from a GAITRite walkway. The CNN took a 400×12 input matrix: 12 sensor signals (6 per ankle), 400 time steps. Two input representations were com…

title: Machine learning-based real-time prediction of lighting classes in adaptive road lighting systems
abstract: This study presents a machine learning-based framework for real-time prediction of road lighting classes in adaptive lighting systems. A field implementation was conducted on Buyukdere Street in Istanbul using two years of traffic and meteorological data. Lighting scenarios were developed in line with EN 13201 standards, and simulations with dimmable LED luminaires ensured compliance with lighting quality requirements. Hourly traffic flow and vehicle speed were predicted using Extreme Gradient Boosting and mapped to appropriate lighting classes via a rule-based matrix. This predictive approach enables the field-installed system to determine the lighting class in advance for each hour rather than after the period has elapsed. Six months of field data were used to validate the approach across seasonal and daily variations. The models achieved R 2 scores of 0.864 and 0.822 for flow and speed predictions, respectively. Predicted lighting classes reached 92.1% and 89.7% agreement with reference classes in two directions. The resulting energy savings closely matched those obtained from measured traffic-based classification, reaching 32.1% compared with non-adaptive M2-level lighting. The results demonstrate the feasibility of data-driven adaptive lighting for energy-efficient urban road operation while meeting the lighting class requirements prescribed by the standard.

title: Federated Explainable AI-Based Alzheimer's Disease Prediction With Multimodal Data
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder whose early diagnosis benefits from combining several kinds of patient data-brain imaging, cognitive tests, clinical records, and genetic markers. However, these data are sensitive and distributed across hospitals, which limits the central pooling that conventional deep learning requires, and clinicians are reluctant to trust black-box predictions. This paper presents a conceptual framework that unifies three ideas: multimodal fusion to improve accuracy, federated learning (FL) to train a shared model across institutions without sharing raw data, and explainable AI (XAI) to make predictions interpretable. We describe a layered architecture, outline a training and explanation workflow, and discuss an illustrative evaluation plan on public datasets such as ADNI and OASIS. We emphasise that the reported analysis is a design-level study rather than a completed experiment, and we identify open challenges in data heterogeneity, communication cost, privacy-utility trade-offs, explanation faithfulness, and clinical validation.

title: Computational Chemistry‐Driven Advances in Eco‐Friendly Insulation Gas Research: Multi‐Dimensional Prediction, Synergistic Screening, Stability Evaluation and Molecular Design
abstract: ABSTRACT Sulphur hexafluoride has become a priority substance for greenhouse gas mitigation in electric systems. An ideal substitute should simultaneously satisfy requirements for dielectric strength, boiling point, global warming potential and chemical stability; however, these metrics are deeply coupled and mutually constraining at the molecular level. Computational chemistry, encompassing quantum‐chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations, is transforming this field from empirical trial and error into a computationally guided design paradigm. This review organises the theoretical methods and key advances of multi‐tiered performance prediction, synergistic screening, stability evaluation and molecular design. Multi‐level prediction frameworks for core performance are converging into integrated synergistic computation, while screening combined with Pareto multi‐objective optimisation has enabled a multi‐dimensional global optimisation. Stability assessments have elucidated the mechanisms of self‐decomposition and interfacial reactions. Molecular design has progressed from functional‐group hybridisation and H/F substitution at the single‐molecule level to synergistic component optimisation in gas mixtures. Prediction of Surface Roughness in Non-Traditional Machining Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Surface roughness decides how a machined part behaves in service. It affects fatigue life, wear, sealing, friction and, in many cases, whether a part is accepted at inspection at all. Non-traditional machining (NTM) processes such as electrical discharge machining, wire EDM, electrochemical machining, laser beam machining, abrasive water jet machining and ultrasonic machining are now routine choices for hard, brittle and geometrically complex parts. Their surface texture, however, comes from thermal, chemical or erosive mechanisms that are stochastic and strongly coupled, so it is hard to predict with classical physics-based models or with simple regression equations. Over the last two decades, machine learning (ML) has become a practical alternative. Artificial neural networks, support vector regression, tree-based ensembles, fuzzy and neuro-fuzzy systems, and more recently deep learning have all been used to map process parameters and sensor signals to roughness values. This paper reviews that body of work. It first outlines the main NTM processes and the way roughness arises in each, then summarises the factors that influence it and the traditional prediction approaches (empirical, statistical and analytical). The discussion then turns to the ML techniques most often applied, a survey of representative studies, a side-by-side comparison of the techniques, and the benefits th…

Prediction of Mortality by using Red Blood Cell Distribution Width in Patients with Sepsis and Septic Shock admitted in an Intensive Care Unit of a Tertiary Care Hospital in Bangladesh
abstract: Background: Sepsis and septic shock progress rapidly, but early and accurate risk stratification can help prevent poor outcomes. Previous studies have shown that red blood cell distribution width (RDW), which reflects variation in cell size, plays a potential role in assessing disease severity. Aims: To identify the relationship with the outcome in adult Bangladeshi patients with sepsis admitted in ICU. Methods: This prospective observational study was conducted in the Department of Critical Care Medicine, BIRDEM, over six months. A total of 63 patients with severe sepsis and septic shock were enrolled based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Patient demographics, comorbidities, laboratory parameters including RDW, and SOFA scores were evaluated and analyzed. Results: The mean age of patients was 50.3 ± 13.5 years with a female-to-male ratio of 1.5:1. Mean RDW was 15.5 ± 1.0% at admission, 14.8 ± 1.6% on day 4, and 13.9 ± 2.2% on day 7. Elevated RDW on day 4 and day 7 was significantly higher in non-survivors (p < 0.05), being 15.2 and 10.0 times more frequent, respectively. RDW (%) also showed a positive correlation with SOFA score (r = 0.478, p = 0.010). Conclusions: This study found that elevated RDW on the 4th and 7th days was significantly associated with ICU mortality in patients with sepsis and septic shock. title: Các nhân tố liên quan đến năng lực sản xuất cây trồng: Bằng chứng thực nghiệm từ các quốc gia châu Á và hàm ý cho phát triển vùng nguyên liệu nông sản ở Việt Nam
abstract: Năng lực sản xuất cây trồng đóng vai trò nền tảng đối với an ninh lương thực, công nghiệp chế biến và phát triển vùng nguyên liệu. Sử dụng dữ liệu bảng cân bằng của 32 quốc gia châu Á giai đoạn 2002–2022, nghiên cứu phân tích mối liên hệ giữa chỉ số sản xuất cây trồng với các yếu tố sinh thái, đầu vào kỹ thuật, kết nối số, thương mại, đất đai, đầu tư và trình độ phát triển kinh tế. Mô hình tác động cố định hai chiều, với hiệu ứng cố định theo quốc gia và năm, được sử dụng làm mô hình chính; sai số chuẩn được phân cụm theo quốc gia. Kết quả cho thấy phân bón có mối liên hệ thuận chiều và ổn định nhất với chỉ số sản xuất cây trồng. Độ mở thương mại có mối liên hệ nghịch chiều tương đối nhất quán, song mức ý nghĩa thống kê thay đổi tùy theo phương pháp suy luận. Các mối liên hệ của kết nối Internet, đất nông nghiệp và đầu tư trực tiếp nước ngoài (FDI) phụ thuộc vào đặc tả mô hình, trong khi diện tích rừng, GDP bình quân đầu người và tích lũy vốn gộp chưa cho thấy mối liên hệ ổn định. Các kết quả được diễn giải như bằng chứng tham khảo về mối liên hệ thống kê, không hàm ý quan hệ nhân quả. Trên cơ sở đó, nghiên cứu gợi mở một số hàm ý chính sách cho Việt Nam, tập trung vào nâng cao hiệu quả sử dụng đầu vào, thúc đẩy số hóa nông nghiệp, tăng cường liên kết thị trường và bảo vệ hệ sinh thái.

Toward Caregiver Flourishing: A Framework for Sustainable Capacity in Dementia Care
abstract: Burden frameworks document what dementia caregiving extracts but offer limited vocabulary for how care holds together over time. This article develops flourishing, sustainable capacity under conditions, as a complementary framework. Drawing on 20 in-depth interviews with family caregivers in Emilia-Romagna, Italy, and the rural Midwest United States alongside 12 months of fieldwork, I describe four domains where caregivers performed ongoing work: connection (mobilizing actionable support), mastery (building routines and lay expertise), identity (preserving selfhood beyond care), and meaning (locating difficulty within purpose). The comparative design examines whether these domains appear across differently organized contexts; they appeared in both, although each took form according to local logics of obligation and selfhood. Caregivers sometimes reported profound strain while demonstrating expertise that had sustained care over years—a pattern suggesting burden and capability may operate as distinct dimensions. The framework offers vocabulary for describing not only what caregiving costs but also what caregivers build.

title: Physics‐informed prediction of shear capacity in RC short columns using a constrained genetic algorithm
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of shear strength in short reinforced concrete (RC) columns is critical for seismic safety assessment, yet existing design provisions often exhibit significant scatter or excessive conservatism due to complex interactions between slenderness, axial compression, and arch action. This study presents a dimensionally homogeneous closed‐form shear strength model for short RC columns, optimized using a genetic algorithm (GA). Trained on a dataset of n = 99 shear‐critical rectangular columns and validated against an independent, out‐of‐sample dataset of n = 24 specimens, the model integrates non‐linear slenderness decay ( a / d ) −0.3912 and axial load enhancement terms. An applicability domain (AD) assessment using the Williams plot ( h * = 0.1515) suggests that the training domain resides safely within statistical leverage bounds. Out‐of‐sample verification demonstrates the proposed model's precision, achieving a coefficient of variation of COV = 16.8%, outperforming standard design codes including ACI 318–19 (COV = 31.0%), ASCE/SEI 41–17 (COV = 30.7%), and Eurocode 2 (COV = 204.3%). Error tracing across the unseen dataset reveals that prediction overestimates occur when elements transition from direct diagonal strut action into intermediate flexure‐shear regimes or under severe axial splitting. title: Designing a Model of Organizational Capacity Appropriate for Social Cohesion (Case Study: Public Hospitals in Tehran Province)
abstract: Background: Public hospitals play an important role in the healthcare system, and strengthening their organizational capacity is essential. Social cohesion, through improving human interactions and relationships, may contribute to enhancing the organizational capacity of these institutions. This study aimed to design an organizational capacity framework aligned with social cohesion in public hospitals in Tehran Province. Methods: This applied-developmental study employed an exploratory mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, experts were selected through purposive sampling, and 18 in-depth, semi-structured interviews were conducted. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis. In the quantitative phase, 222 participants were selected through stratified random sampling and using Cochran’s formula from a population of 526 managers and specialized staff working in public hospitals in Tehran. Data were collected using a researcher-developed questionnaire, whose validity and reliability were assessed and confirmed. SPSS 32 was used for descriptive data analysis, while Smart PLS 4.1.1.8 was used for confirmatory factor analysis and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results: Thematic analysis identified seven dimensions of organizational capacity: cognitive, emotional, spiritual, interactional, infrastructural, leadership, and sustainability capa…

title: Các nhân tố ảnh hưởng đến khả năng tận dụng ưu đãi thuế quan của doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa trước các hiệp định thương mại tự do thế hệ mới
abstract: Nghiên cứu này phân tích các nhân tố ảnh hưởng đến khả năng tận dụng ưu đãi thuế quan từ các hiệp định thương mại tự do thế hệ mới của doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa tại Việt Nam, trọng tâm là Hiệp định Đối tác Toàn diện và Tiến bộ xuyên Thái Bình Dương và Hiệp định Thương mại tự do giữa Việt Nam và Liên minh châu Âu. Dữ liệu khảo sát từ 385 doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa có hoạt động xuất khẩu tại năm vùng kinh tế trọng điểm trong năm 2025 được phân tích thông qua kiểm định độ tin cậy thang đo, phân tích nhân tố khám phá, phân tích nhân tố khẳng định và hồi quy tuyến tính. Các kiểm định về sai lệch phương pháp chung, giả định hồi quy và tính vững của kết quả cũng được thực hiện. Kết quả cho thấy cả năm nhân tố gồm kiến thức và nhận thức về hiệp định thương mại tự do, năng lực đáp ứng quy tắc xuất xứ, năng lực quản trị doanh nghiệp, năng lực tài chính và sự hỗ trợ từ Nhà nước và hiệp hội đều có mối liên hệ thuận chiều và có ý nghĩa thống kê với khả năng tận dụng ưu đãi thuế quan. Trong đó, năng lực quản trị doanh nghiệp có hệ số hồi quy chuẩn hóa lớn nhất (0,318), tiếp đến là kiến thức và nhận thức về hiệp định thương mại tự do (0,289). Mô hình giải thích được 67,6% sự biến thiên của biến phụ thuộc. Trên cơ sở đó, nghiên cứu đề xuất một số hàm ý quản trị và chính sách nhằm nâng cao khả năng tận dụng ưu đãi thuế quan của doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa Việt Nam.

title: Antimicrobial activity, physicochemical properties, antioxidant capacity, and elemental composition of yerba mate (Ilex paraguariensis)
abstract: Abstract Yerba mate ( Ilex paraguariensis ) has attracted considerable interest because of its diverse bioactive properties. To provide an integrated characterization beyond the evaluation of a single biological property, this study investigated the antimicrobial and physicochemical characteristics of water, ethanol, and methanol extracts, together with the antioxidant capacity and elemental composition of yerba mate. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated against foodborne pathogenic bacteria ( Bacillus subtilis , Escherichia coli , Enterococcus faecalis , and Staphylococcus aureus ) and yeast species ( Candida albicans and Saccharomyces cerevisiae ) using the agar well diffusion method. The water, ethanol, and methanol extracts were tested at their experimentally determined extract concentrations rather than after normalization to a common dry-extract concentration. The results revealed that the extracts exhibited no antifungal activity but showed varying levels of antibacterial effects among the tested extracts and microorganisms. Under the tested experimental conditions, the methanol extract produced the largest inhibition zones, particularly against S. aureus (18.67 mm) and B. subtilis (18.33 mm), and showed the lowest MIC value (43.75 µg/mL). Recent Advances in Microbial Community Composition of Fermented Soy Whey and Its Mechanism for Biotransformation of Soybean Isoflavones
abstract: ABSTRACT Fermented soy whey (FSW), a traditional natural tofu coagulant, harbors complex microbial communities that drive soy‐protein coagulation via organic‐acid secretion and enhance the bioavailability of soybean isoflavones, conferring desirable flavor characteristics and health‐beneficial bioactivities. However, several critical knowledge gaps restrict its scaled‐up industrial deployment. The dynamic regulatory connections between microbial community temporal succession and metabolite biosynthesis during spontaneous FSW fermentation have not been fully deciphered. Interspecies interactions inside highly heterogeneous microbial consortia remain ambiguous, and the whole‐fermentation system is exceptionally sensitive to fluctuating environmental conditions. This review synthesizes prior literature together with cutting‐edge multi‐omics datasets to systematically dissect the temporal dynamics of FSW microbial ecosystems. Enzymatic mechanistic analysis delineates key catalytic and metabolic pathways responsible for transforming soy isoflavone glucosides into aglycones and subsequent bioactive derivatives. title: Bankability as a Mechanism for Sustainability Implementation in Public–Private Partnerships
abstract: ABSTRACT Infrastructure public–private partnerships (PPPs) may formally incorporate sustainability commitments while lacking the financial capacity required to support their implementation over long concession horizons. This paper examines project‐level financial architecture as a structural condition shaping that capacity. Using an analytical single‐case study of a Mediterranean port redevelopment PPP, we combine project finance simulation with sensitivity and scenario analyses. The findings analytically illustrate how a project may be economically profitable yet remain below a minimum analytical financeability threshold, thereby creating financial pressure on non‐revenue‐generating sustainability components and increasing their exposure to potential deferral or renegotiation. Sensitivity analyses identify debt tenor and cost of debt as threshold parameters, while scenario analyses indicate that dependence on a dominant revenue stream may create incentives to prioritize commercial activities over non‐revenue‐generating commitments. The study contributes to sustainability strategy research by conceptualizing bankability as an enabling financial condition—rather than a guarantee—of sustainability delivery and by framing commercial drift as a potential structural risk associated with concentrated revenue architectures. Reducing Image Classification Errors in Convolutional Neural Networks Through a Fuzzy–Possibilistic Abstention Mechanism
abstract: A growing number of applications consume labels produced by convolutional neural networks (CNNs), yet most deployments return only the top-ranked label with no indication of how trustworthy it is; because modern networks are systematically over-confident, a high softmax probability does not by itself certify a correct decision. This paper proposes a lightweight abstention (“I do not know”) mechanism that can be added to a deployed CNN without retraining and that reuses its single forward pass. In contrast with mostly statistical treatments, uncertainty is modeled with fuzzy logic and possibility theory: three interpretable indicators (the complement of the winning probability, a Mamdani fuzzy membership for the object-to-camera acquisition distance, and a Pedrycz/Goguen fuzzy similarity between the two top-ranked classes) are aggregated with a maximum t-conorm into a possibility (uncertainty) function and its complementary confidence. The method is evaluated on twelve video sequences spanning several object categories and with two CNN backbones (VGG16 and ResNet-50). On the objects for which the backbone has a corresponding ImageNet class, a quantitative risk–coverage analysis shows that the full possibilistic rule orders predictions for abstention better than the maximum-softmax-probability and top-two-margin baselines (mean area under the risk–coverage curve, 0.148 versus 0.1…

Eco-Efficiency Under Synergistic Carbon and Pollution Reduction: Identifying Development States in China’s Beef Cattle Sector Using Unsupervised Machine Learning
abstract: Reconciling livestock supply security with synergistic reductions in carbon emissions and environmental pollution is a major governance challenge for China’s beef cattle sector, as provincial production systems differ substantially in resource endowments, production organization, and upgrading capacity. Using a balanced panel of 17 major beef cattle-producing provinces from 2010 to 2023, this study develops a state-based framework to diagnose provincial heterogeneity. We first estimate provincial eco-efficiency using a slack-based measure (SBM) model with undesirable outputs, which jointly accounts for desirable output, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and pollutant discharges. We then apply K-means clustering, an unsupervised machine learning method, to a multidimensional feature space covering eco-efficiency, environmental intensity, input structure, production scale, sectoral specialization, and the agricultural fiscal expenditure context to identify empirically coherent development states. The results reveal four distinct states: factor-intensive, moderate-scale eco-efficiency, scale-driven low-intensity, and extensive high-pressure. The four states exhibit systematically different production–environment configurations and structural characteristics, demonstrating substantial heterogeneity across provincial beef cattle systems. title: Effects of Water Content on the Pitting Behavior of X65 Steel in Supercritical and Dense-Phase Carbon Dioxide Environments
abstract: In the study, the corrosion behavior of X65 pipeline steel was investigated under the pressure of 8 MPa in both supercritical (SC) and dense-phase (DP) CO2 environments with different water contents from 18% to 1000% relative humidity (RH). The results revealed the significant phase-dependent shift in the critical water content required for corrosion initiation. At 18% RH, no corrosion was detected in SC CO2 after 120 h of exposure, whereas DP CO2 environment led to a low corrosion rate (1.3 × 10−3 mm/a). At 60% RH, corrosion was detected in the environments of both phases (1.7 × 10−2 mm/a for SC and 2.0 × 10−2 mm/a for DP). These results indicated that the critical water content required for corrosion initiation in DP CO2 was lower than that in SC CO2. This difference might be attributed to the substantially higher density and viscosity of DP CO2, which promoted water condensation and stabilized the liquid film on the steel surface. Corrosion rate gradually increased with the increase in water content and peaked at of 0.57 mm/a in SC and 0.68 mm/a in DP CO2. Pitting occurred in DP CO2 environment with different water contents, but pitting was absent in SC CO2 environment with the water content below 80% RH. title: Rice starch–activated carbon composite films for potential cosmetic facial sheet mask applications: physicochemical and mechanical characterization
abstract: Abstract The widespread use of synthetic facial sheet masks has raised concerns about their environmental impact. In this study, rice starch (RS)–activated carbon (AC) composite films were prepared by solution casting and characterized to assess their potential as biodegradable cosmetic mask substrates. The surface morphology of the films changed after AC incorporation, with thicknesses ranging from approximately 0.2 to 0.3 mm and the moisture content increasing with increasing AC loading. The water contact angles ranged from 48.95° to 63.85°, indicating hydrophilic surfaces, with the RS + AC (0.4 g) film exhibiting the lowest measured contact angle. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy suggested predominantly physical interactions between the RS and AC, whereas differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray diffraction characterized their thermal transitions and structural features. Compared with the neat RS film, the RS + AC (0.4 g) film exhibited lower tensile strength and elongation at break. MTT assays performed on AC powder revealed that the cell viability of L929 fibroblasts and HaCaT keratinocytes was above 90% under the tested conditions; the complete composite films were not evaluated for cytotoxicity. title: Carbon Disclosure Quality, Stakeholder Accountability and Corporate New Quality Productive Forces: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
abstract: Whether mandatory climate disclosure is a compliance cost or a productive investment is now a central policy question. We study the quality rather than the volume of carbon disclosure and ask whether it is associated with higher new quality productive forces among Chinese listed firms. The evidence covers 1660 A-share firms over 2015–2022 (13,280 firm-year observations). The association is positive and survives firm fixed effects, so it is not driven by time-invariant firm characteristics, but it is modest: one standard deviation of disclosure quality corresponds to 3.7 per cent of a standard deviation of the outcome within firms, against 14.4 per cent across firms, and it falls to 1.4 per cent once firm-specific linear trends are absorbed. Because four research-input items carry 92.3 per cent of the index weight, the association is best described as one between disclosure quality and research-intensive productive capacity; it remains intact when those four items are removed from the index. Financing constraints and internal control transmit little in the cross-section, analyst attention transmits the largest cross-sectional share but does not survive firm fixed effects, and report-based attention transmits negatively. Neither the green-finance pilot nor institutional ownership amplifies the association once firm effects are included. We read disclosure as an accountability pra…

title: A Perspective on the Development of Novel In Situ Remediation of Contaminated Sediments Using Black Carbon
abstract: Abstract The field of contaminated sediment remediation was disrupted two decades ago by the emergence of a new way to reduce risk in situ through the amendment of black carbon sorbents─activated carbon and specialized biochars. This required a paradigm shift from a focus on reducing pollutant mass to reducing exposure through bioavailability control. Sorbent amendment technology has advanced from laboratory and pilot field demonstrations to full-scale applications at many sites and has recently been incorporated in USEPA records of decision at Superfund sites. This perspective summarizes critical points in advancing the new technology: 1) accurate problem definition recognizing that sediment pollutant mass reduction does not necessarily lead to risk reduction, 2) breakthroughs in bioavailability science and unraveling the role of native black carbon in sediments, 3) demonstration of pollutant bioavailability reduction with strong sorption, 4) quantitative descriptions of the process, 5) addressing the challenges of mercury, 6) understanding unintended consequences, and 7) development of freely dissolved concentrations as a key bioavailability metric with regulatory and stakeholder engagement. The lessons learned in this journey from early science through technological maturity can help inform other technologies that are in development to address evolving threats to the environ…

title: Role of End-Tidal Carbon Dioxide as a Non-invasive Predictor of Fluid Responsiveness in Mechanically Ventilated Patients with Shock
abstract: Background: Circulatory shock remains a leading cause of mortality in the intensive care unit, with inadequate tissue perfusion and impaired oxygen delivery as its defining pathophysiological features. Fluid resuscitation is central to early haemodynamic management, as volume expansion increases venous return and augments cardiac output through the Frank–Starling mechanism. However, only approximately half of haemodynamically unstable patients demonstrate a meaningful rise in cardiac output following a fluid bolus, and indiscriminate fluid administration in non-responsive patients carries well-recognised risks including pulmonary oedema, prolonged mechanical ventilation, and increased mortality. Accurate identification of fluid responsiveness prior to fluid administration has therefore become a fundamental component of modern critical care practice. Static haemodynamic parameters such as central venous pressure have been shown by meta-analysis to be unreliable predictors of fluid responsiveness, and dynamic indices such as pulse pressure variation and stroke volume variation, while more accurate, require invasive arterial monitoring and strictly controlled mechanical ventilation. Renewable energy investment and corporate dividend policy: An empirical investigation
abstract: The study explored whether dividend policy could serve as an innovative funding option to finance Energy Transition Plan (ETP) in Nigeria. This study is a pioneer study that explored the possibility of establishing green dividends in Nigeria and at the global scale. The study obtained information from 400 shareholders of manufacturing companies through a structured questionnaire survey. It used SmartPLS to estimate the links between variables as well as indicators and their link with other variables. The study used a bootstrapping approach to generate statistically reliable estimates of interaction effects. The result of setting a dividend policy (SDP) to renewable energy investment (REI) revealed a positive and significant association. The study suggests the need to create a new strategy to manage the shareholders' dividend raised by the management. This will include the future benefits of the dividend used, the time expected to repay the dividend and the benefits attached. By implication, the study contributes to global calls relating to sustainable development goals, which have gained acceptance not only from the company's management but also from stakeholders within the society. This will enable the United Nations to assess the potential benefits of the diverse use of shareholders' funds in attaining the United Nations Framework commitment. title: The impact of real-digital integration on green economic efficiency in the Yangtze River Economic Belt
abstract: Abstract The integration of the real economy and the digital economy is a crucial driver for regional high-quality development and green transformation. Using panel data from 108 cities in the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YEB) during 2006–2022, this study employs the patent co-classification method and super-efficiency SBM model to measure real-digital integration (RD) and green economic efficiency (GEE), empirically examining their relationship. The results show that: (1) RD levels across cities show an upward trend but with widening regional disparities exhibiting a Matthew Effect; GEE follows a spatial pattern of upstream > downstream > midstream. (2) RD is significantly associated with higher GEE. (3) This association operates through three channels: green finance development, green innovation capacity, and artificial intelligence applications. (4) The relationship is stronger in upstream and downstream cities, non-resource-based cities, post-2015, and service-oriented cities. These findings offer policy references for governments, enterprises, and financial institutions to advance green transformation through RD.

Enhancing Safety and Performance in Energy Storage Systems: Strategies for Mitigating Lithium Dendrite-Induced Separator Penetration and Internal Short Circuits
abstract: Abstract The growth and penetration of lithium dendrites through separators during cycling is a root cause of internal short circuits, posing a major safety threat to high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries. This review systematically analyzes the electrochemical mechanisms governing dendrite growth, summarizes advanced characterization techniques, and critiques mainstream suppression strategies, including electrolyte engineering and all-solid-state batteries. To address challenges under high-energy-density demands, a nonaqueous precipitation method─a solution-based interfacial engineering technique that offers inherent compatibility with roll-to-roll processing─is discussed as an emerging strategy, which constructs a synergistic three-layer interface system to simultaneously achieve mechanical blocking, homogeneous ion transport, and dynamic self-healing. By elucidating fundamental mechanisms and mitigation strategies, this review further underscores their critical implications for enhancing the safety, longevity, and reliability of next-generation batteries, proposing an industrially viable pathway toward high-safety, long-cycle-life energy storage systems for electric vehicles and grid-scale applications.

title: Biomass Gasification and Wood Gas Dual-Fuel Diesel Engines for Decentralized Power Generation: A Critical Review of Integration, Performance, and Research Priorities
abstract: Substitution of diesel with biomass producer gas in compression ignition (CI) engines is a promising option for decentralised, carbon-neutral electricity generation. However, despite decades of research, commercial-scale gasifier-engine systems remain rare. This review critically examines the last decade of research on wood gasification and dual-fuel diesel engine operation, with the aim of identifying the integration challenges that have prevented commercialization. We consider the gasifier types, gas cleaning systems and engine performance data from a systems perspective, providing a meta-analysis of diesel substitution, efficiency derating and emission trade-offs. The results show that fixed-bed downdraft gasifiers are favoured for small-scale applications because of their low tar yield, while fluidized-bed gasifiers are more versatile in terms of feedstock but need more advanced gas cleaning. The technical issues are tar, gas quality and engine control. Dual-fuel operation generally provides 60-90% diesel substitution and 90% particulate matter reduction, but also increased CO and unburned hydrocarbon emissions, especially at low load and high gas substitution. Importantly, we identify that optimisation of components (gasifier, filter, engine) has reached a plateau; the next step is co-design and model-based control. Identity verification in virtual shareholders’ meetings: normative foundations and legal consequences
abstract: Abstract The digital transformation of corporate governance has rendered virtual shareholders’ meetings a permanent feature of modern company law. While electronic participation enhances accessibility and cross-border engagement, it raises fundamental questions concerning the reliable identification of participants. This article examines identity verification in virtual shareholders’ meetings of private limited companies under Estonian law, with comparative references to German law. The analysis is based on the understanding that identity verification is not a mere technical formality but constitutes a structural precondition for the lawful formation of the company’s collective will. Although Estonian law permits electronic participation by default, it does not prescribe any specific authentication standards. The legal requirement that only shareholders or duly authorised representatives may exercise membership rights therefore remains unchanged, while the technical means used to ensure compliance vary. The article adopts a functional perspective on identity verification. It examines different forms of authentication that may be used in virtual meetings, including the Estonian state e-identity, other digital identification means (such as those recognised under the eIDAS framework), as well as situations where no formal digital identification is available. title: Soil Biogeochemical Cycles and Their Influence on Crop-Environment Dynamics in Changing Climates
abstract: Soil biogeochemical cycles regulate nutrient availability, soil organic matter dynamics, greenhouse-gas exchange, and crop productivity, but their functioning is increasingly modified by climate change. This review synthesizes the major processes controlling carbon (C), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), sulfur (S), and silicon (Si) cycling in agricultural soils and examines how these interconnected cycles influence soil-crop-environment relationships under changing climatic conditions. Warming, drought, excessive soil moisture, altered precipitation, and elevated atmospheric CO2 can modify microbial activity, organic-matter turnover, nutrient mineralization and immobilization, redox conditions, nutrient losses, and greenhouse-gas emissions. Their effects are strongly context dependent and vary with soil texture, pH, organic-matter content, drainage, microbial communities, crop type, and management. The review further evaluates how plant nutrient acquisition, rhizosphere processes, and plant-soil-microbial feedbacks connect biogeochemical cycling with crop performance and environmental outcomes. Conservation agriculture, organic amendments, biochar, and microbial inoculants may improve nutrient retention and soil resilience, but their effectiveness depends on soil, climate, amendment properties, and management history and may involve agronomic or environmental trade-offs. title: Molecular Identification of Pottiaceae Mosses from Southern Kazakhstan
abstract: Pottiaceae mosses remain insufficiently represented in molecular datasets from Central Asia, limiting comparisons with specimens from other regions. This study evaluated molecular support for the identification of 16 voucher-linked specimens collected in the Western Tien Shan, Kazygurt Mountains and Kazygurt village of southern Kazakhstan and generated nuclear ITS1 and ITS2 and chloroplast trnT–trnL sequence records. ITS2 comparisons with selected GenBank references recovered strongly supported groups for specimens assigned to Syntrichia intermedia, S. virescens, S. princeps, Geheebia siccula, Tortula subulata and Vinealobryum vineale, with ultrafast bootstrap support of 96–100%. Placements of S. ruraliformis, T. mucronifolia and Barbula unguiculata received 92–93% support, whereas the placement of S. ruralis was less strongly supported and relationships involving S. caninervis remained unresolved. These findings provide molecular evidence consistent with several working identifications while demonstrating the limited resolution of a short ITS2 region for some taxa. The ITS1 and trnT–trnL records complement the ITS2 dataset as publicly available sequence resources. Together, the voucher-linked records expand the molecular representation of Pottiaceae from Kazakhstan and provide a foundation for future taxonomic and multilocus studies.

Characteristics of Boundary Layer Height Variations in Global Arid Regions and Their Sensitivity to Influencing Energy Factors
abstract: ABSTRACT Global warming has intensified the negative impacts of drought across most arid regions worldwide, leading to significant changes in the spatial pattern of surface energy, which in turn affects the structure and development of the upper atmospheric boundary layer ( ABL ) in these regions. Based on monthly mean ERA‐Interim reanalysis data from 1979 to 2018, this study examines the spatial distribution and variation trends of boundary layer height ( BLH ) over different arid regions of the global land, and quantitatively evaluates the sensitivity of BLH in seven typical arid regions to the two dominant energy terms required for ABL development‐namely, surface heating ( SHF ) and ABL ‐top entrainment ( H e )‐during the annual, warm‐season and cold‐season periods. The results show that the long‐term annual mean BLH over the global arid regions is approximately 841.8 m, nearly 200 m higher than that over more humid regions, with substantial regional differences. Specifically, in the driest and hottest regions‐West and South Asia (WSA) and North Africa (NAF)‐ BLH is relatively high, at approximately 951.2 and 932.1 m, respectively, while in South America (SAM), a relatively cold and humid region, BLH is the lowest at only 728.0 m. The differences in BLH among arid regions are influenced not only by the partitioning of surface energy but also by atmospheric dry‐wet conditions…

title: A Data-Driven Stochastic Multi-Objective Energy Management System for Sustainable Interconnected Microgrids, Integrating LSTM Forecasts and Hybrid Storage Systems
abstract: The research proposes an EMS for grid-connected microgrids which incorporates deep learning predictions, stochastic optimization, and multi-carrier storage systems to optimize cost of operations and greenhouse gas emissions. By jointly reducing operational costs and carbon emissions, the suggested approach will facilitate the transition to sustainable, resilient, low-carbon energy systems. Quick-acting battery storage and slow-reacting hydrogen are used for shaving peaks and balancing energy supply, while decision-making is robustified against the uncertainty associated with renewables through Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS). The LSTM-based model forecasts 24 h ahead multi-step PV and wind generation outputs. Five algorithms, namely, GA, PSO, GWO, NSGA-II, and the Hippopotamus optimizer (HO), are evaluated for two different microgrid structures (MG1, MG2), using hypervolume metrics and a Wilcoxon rank-sum test conducted on 30 independent runs. The findings indicated that HO provides the best spread and dispersion of the Pareto frontier, along with highest hypervolume, being statistically similar to PSO (p > 0.05), while proving significantly superior to GA and NSGA-II, which get stuck within a highly inefficient region. GWO is overestimated in terms of Pareto convergence, since it is possible at one certain point only. This is impossible in real life, as proven through a peer-to…

Aqueous Zinc Batteries as an Accessible Platform for Interdisciplinary Energy Storage Innovation
abstract: Aqueous zinc batteries (AZBs) are often discussed as safer and more sustainable alternatives to lithium‐ion batteries. This comparison is important, but it may understate another distinctive value of AZBs, namely that they provide a comparatively accessible experimental platform for battery innovation. Because many AZB components can be handled in air and aqueous media, researchers can assemble cells, test ideas, and inspect failed devices without the infrastructure required for many nonaqueous batteries. Here, we argue that this practical accessibility is itself scientifically important. It allows AZBs to serve as a testing ground for ideas from electrochemistry, materials science, physics, engineering, and data science, while also lowering the entry barrier for early‐career researchers and groups entering battery research from adjacent fields.

title: Design and Performance Study of a High-Energy Asymmetric Supercapacitor Featuring a Graded NiCo2O4@NiWO4/MXene Cathode and a Hydrophilic Carbon Nanotube Anode
abstract: To design an asymmetric supercapacitor device with high capacitance, high energy density, and excellent cycling stability, a NiCo2O4@NiWO4/MXene ternary composite cathode and a hydrophilic carbon nanotube (H-CNTs) anode were constructed and matched for device assembly. The NiCo2O4@NiWO4/MXene cathode with a “nanowire@nanosheet” core-shell hierarchical structure was prepared through a two-step hydrothermal method combined with high-temperature annealing, while hydrophilic carbon nanotubes were obtained by concentrated nitric acid modification. The microstructure, crystal structure, elemental valence states, and pore characteristics of the electrode materials were systematically characterized by SEM, TEM, XRD, XPS, and nitrogen adsorption–desorption measurements. The results showed that the introduction of Ti3C2Tx MXene formed an effective conductive network, while the core-shell hierarchical structure provided abundant electrochemically active sites and increased the specific surface area of the ternary composite to 156.4 m2/g. In a three-electrode system, the NiCo2O4@NiWO4/MXene electrode exhibited a specific capacitance of 1830 F/g at 1 A/g and retained 983 F/g at 15 A/g, while the H-CNTs anode delivered a specific capacitance of 774 F/g at 1 A/g. Based on the working potential windows, specific capacitances, and charge balance relationship of the positive and negative electro…

title: A numerical re-look at the partial separation model for stacking fault energy
abstract: Abstract Stacking fault energies (SFEs) are fundamental to deformation mechanisms in crystalline materials, yet discrepancies between theoretical predictions and experiment remain. Here we evaluate the Olson–Cohen (OC), Ising, and partial separation (PS) models using a unified EAM/MEAM interatomic potential framework to enable a controlled comparison of the different approaches. For most fcc metals, the PS model predicts SFEs consistent with the OC and Ising models, whereas larger deviations occur when equilibrium partial separations are too small for the model to remain valid. Similar material-dependent behavior is observed for concentrated alloys. Simulations of Ni reveal that finite specimen thickness can influence the apparent PS-based SFE, a size effect expected to intensify in materials with wider separations. Furthermore, simulations of metastable fcc Co demonstrate that the apparent partial separation is sensitive to boundary conditions. These results clarify the applicability and limitations of the PS approach and highlight the importance of carefully verifying specimen size and boundary conditions when determining SFEs from partial separations.

title: On the Mitigation of Ni3+-Induced Losses in NiO Hole Transport Layers for Metal Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract NiO is widely investigated as a hole transport layer (HTL) in p–i–n metal halide perovskite solar cells. While previous studies have focused on improving device performance by lowering NiO film resistivity through increased Ni3+ content, Ni3+ states, particularly at the NiO surface, act as trap states and trigger redox reactions with the perovskite. This study investigates the performance of devices based on plasma-assisted atomic layer deposited (ALD) NiO film, NiOAlanis, characterized by a ∼2.7% higher relative average Ni valence and low resistivity (4 ± 1 Ω∙cm), compared to thermal ALD NiO film, NiOBu-MeAMD ((1.9 ± 0.3) × 104 Ω∙cm). NiOAlanis-based devices yield a poor power conversion efficiency (PCE) of ∼2.4%, compared to devices based on NiOBu-MeAMD (∼14.0%) and commonly used Me-4PACz (∼17.1%) or PTAA (~15.6%), primarily due to a low JSC (∼4.5 mA/cm2). X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals that a redox reaction occurs between formamidinium iodide of the perovskite and Ni3+ states of NiOAlanis, leading to an interfacial charge-extraction barrier. To improve device performance, we report on an H2 plasma treatment of NiOAlanis (“NiOAlanis,H2 pl.”), which decreases the average Ni valence to ∼2.2%, relative to NiOBu-MeAMD, and increases the resistivity to (1.1 ± 0.1) × 104 Ω∙cm, indicating a decrease in relative Ni3+ content. Consequently, NiOAlanis,H2 pl.-based de…

title: Insights Into Electrolyte Effects on Interfacial Kinetics and Transport in Porous Redox Flow Battery Electrodes: A Multiparadigm Modeling Study
abstract: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage owing to their decoupled energy and power densities. Electrolyte formulation plays a key role in determining the electrochemical performance of RFBs, influencing interfacial kinetics and transport within porous electrodes. Herein, we develop a multiscale modeling framework to investigate the coupled effects of the electrolyte concentration (methyl viologen (MV) and NaCl) and the fibrous 3D microstructure on the porous transport and electrochemical kinetics in organic RFBs using a kinetic Monte Carlo model. We link this interfacial kinetics to the advection–diffusion transport in stochastically generated carbon felt electrode microstructures through lattice Boltzmann method simulations via an interpolation‐based coupling. We use two performance descriptors, the fiber‐averaged rate of potential loss and convective area fraction, to quantify the kinetics and transport effects, along with their interplay. While increasing MV concentration enhances the interfacial kinetics, it limits the transport within the electrode microstructure. The interfacial kinetics shows to be nontrivially governed by the supporting electrolyte. A surface area–permeability trade‐off appears across microstructures with different electrolyte concentrations. This multiparadigm modeling workflow provides mechanistic…

title: Evaluation of a multidimensional physical performance test battery in young female volleyball players: Inter-trial reliability and principal component analysis
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate an integrated multidimensional physical performance test battery and explore its underlying structure in young female volleyball players. Forty-five female youth volleyball players aged 11–14 years (mean age 11.87 ± 0.97 years) completed a battery comprising bilateral handgrip strength, reaction distance, T-test agility, and Y-Balance assessments, together with vertical jump, core endurance, and sit-and-reach flexibility tests. Within-session inter-trial reliability was evaluated using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC(3,k)) and coefficient of variation. Performance variables were standardized using z-scores, and measures in which lower values indicated better performance were sign-inverted. Pearson correlations were used to examine bilateral relationships, and principal component analysis (PCA) with Varimax rotation was performed to explore the underlying performance dimensions. Age-group differences were examined using ANOVA or Kruskal–Wallis tests, as appropriate, with Bonferroni correction applied for multiple comparisons. A composite performance score was calculated as the unweighted mean of the six retained component scores. Handgrip strength, vertical jump, and Y-Balance performance demonstrated good-to-excellent within-session inter-trial reliability, whereas reaction distance showed moderate-to-good reliability with greater inter-…

title: Network Meta‐Analysis of Static Cold Storage Versus Dynamic Organ Preservation for Liver Transplantation
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Donor organ scarcity and increasing use of extended‐criteria donors have driven the development of dynamic preservation methods to improve outcomes following liver transplantation. Hypothermic machine perfusion (HMP) and normothermic machine perfusion (NMP), controlled oxygenated rewarming (COR), and ischemia‐free liver transplantation (IFLT) are dynamic preservation methods that have been compared with traditional static cold storage (SCS). However, no randomized clinical trials (RCTs) have directly compared HMP with NMP. The aim of the present study is to conduct a network meta‐analysis (NMA) of RCTs to compare the effects of available dynamic preservation strategies on clinical outcomes. Methods Electronic databases were systematically searched for RCTs evaluating dynamic preservation methods in human liver transplantation. Eligibility criteria included reporting of at least one of the following primary outcome measures: early allograft dysfunction (EAD), biliary complications, and graft survival. A random‐effects Bayesian NMA with a non‐informative prior was conducted. Results Thirteen RCTs were included with a total of 1888 recipients and assessed 5 interventions. Autonomous Charging and Battery Swapping for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles: A Review
abstract: Focused on enabling fully autonomous aerial operations, this review provides a comprehensive analysis of the working principles, efficiencies, and representative systems of major unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) charging and battery swapping methods. These paradigms are systematically evaluated with a particular emphasis on their autonomous execution potential. The analysis critically examines how the technical strengths and engineering trade‐offs of various approaches, including alignment tolerance, payload constraints, and environmental adaptability, influence their suitability for real‐world deployment. Additionally, essential supporting technologies such as precision landing and battery management systems are briefly outlined. Ultimately, this comprehensive evaluation serves as a practical reference for selecting and optimizing automated energy replenishment solutions tailored to autonomous UAV missions.

title: The Bounded Utilization Regime: Reconciling Revenue Efficiency and Residual-Value Risk in Vehicle-as-Income-Stream Models
abstract: The claim that a privately owned motor vehicle constitutes a viable income-generating asset once matched to platform demand rests on a boundary condition: the utilization rate at which telematics-enabled efficiency gains offset the accelerated depreciation and resale-value volatility that intensive use produces. Studies quantifying the revenue benefits of higher utilization stop short of pricing in the residual-value discount that the same mileage generates in the secondary market. Studies quantifying that discount rarely connect it back to the utilization decision that produced it. This article formalizes the floor and ceiling conditions that bound viable operation as a conceptual model, collects the underlying cost and utilization parameters from the transportation-economics literature and compares them with independent data, and proposes that the vehicle-as-income-stream thesis is viable within a bounded interior range, provisionally the sixty-five to eighty-five percent utilization band. Below the floor, fixed costs remain unrecovered. Above the ceiling, mileage-driven depreciation and resale discounting are expected to erode the marginal revenue that higher utilization was meant to secure. The analysis frames utilization as a two-sided constraint: a specific band to be held, with candidate implications for financing terms, replacement schedules, and commission design.

title: Can a preview of an upcoming curve mitigate the effects of cognitive load on expert and non-expert drivers’ vehicle control?
abstract: Abstract The lack of theoretical and empirical coherence makes it difficult to ascertain how cognitive load, induced by a cognitive secondary activity, impacts the driving performance of non-expert and expert drivers. Even less is known about strategies that could mitigate potential impairments, precluding the development of effective countermeasures. Fourteen UK advanced police drivers (experts), and twenty experienced non-professional drivers (non-experts), were recruited for this study to examine whether a road sign previewing an upcoming curve could reduce the effects of cognitive load on driving performance. Differences between experts and non-experts were observed only in longitudinal control, while cognitive load primarily affected lateral control. When the road sign was present, experts reduced their speed both when approaching and negotiating curves, whereas non-experts slowed only within the curve. Although the road sign had a minimal impact on lane deviations when approaching curves under cognitive load, it effectively reduced deviations and improved steering smoothness in curves, irrespective of cognitive load. These findings underscore the task-specific nature of driving expertise and suggest that anticipatory visual cues can enhance safety and performance of expert and non-expert drivers even in situations when they are cognitively loaded.

title: Aircraft Critical Component Status Detection for Preflight Inspection via Unmanned Ground Vehicle Platform
abstract: Traditional preflight critical component inspections rely heavily on manual visual checks by maintenance crews, resulting in inefficient detection processes, significant safety risks, and high omission rates. The civil aviation industry urgently requires automated inspection solutions to enhance safety and efficiency. However, existing computer vision approaches are constrained by challenges such as complex lighting variations on aprons and significant scale variations of targets. To address these issues, this paper proposes an autonomous unmanned ground vehicle (UGV)-based detection framework for preflight critical component status detection, enhancing the intelligence of preflight inspections by using a UGV to support maintenance personnel in round-the-plane inspections. Specifically, we propose an aircraft critical component status detection method for preflight inspection via a UGV platform to accurately identify the states of nine key components (e.g., landing gear pins and electronic equipment bay doors) in apron scenarios. The luminance generation branch and multiscale detection branch are designed and introduced into the proposed algorithm to achieve state-of-the-art performance in preflight critical component status detection tasks.
