title: Performance Evaluation Of RT-PPP, Network RTK, And PPP Techniques In Vehicle-Based Kinematic GNSS Positioning
abstract: The need for real-time positioning is of critical importance, particularly for emerging technologies such as intelligent navigation and autonomous vehicles. Although the desired level of accuracy can be achieved in static positioning, the accuracy attainable in kinematic applications may vary considerably. In this study, real-time Precise Point Positioning (RT-PPP), CORS (Continuously Operating Reference Stations)-based Network RTK (Real-Time Kinematic), post-processed PPP (CSRS-PPP), and Post-Processed Kinematic (PPK) solutions were comparatively evaluated using kinematic data obtained from two dual-frequency geodetic Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers mounted on a land vehicle. The test was conducted on 22 April 2021 at Yıldız Technical University Davutpaşa Campus, with a 1 second sampling interval over an approximately 52-minute trajectory. The results showed that the post-processed CSRS-PPP solutions achieved horizontal RMS accuracies of 1.8 cm and 1.3 cm for the GR-5 and HiPer SR receivers, respectively. The Network RTK method provided a horizontal RMS accuracy of 4.5 cm for FIX epochs; however, the accuracy degraded considerably when non-FIX epochs were included. The RT-PPP solution remained at the decimeter level, with RMS errors of 16.7 cm in the horizontal component and 25.1 cm in three-dimensional positioning. The results indicate that RT-PPP is not s…

title: Feasibility Limits in Corridor-Wide EV Fast-Charging Station Planning for Sustainable Transport Electrification: An MILP Study of Puerto Rico’s PR-2
abstract: Planning fast-charging infrastructure for electric vehicles (EVs) supports sustainable transport electrification. This study identifies when a corridor-wide plan along Puerto Rico Highway 2 (PR-2) becomes infeasible and which modeled constraint limits it first. A mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model with 229 candidate sites across 27 municipalities, integer 150 kW port decisions, a 3 MW per-site ceiling, corridor coverage, and a shared upstream-capacity screen is solved for a February 2024 baseline and six electrification scenarios under an upper-bound demand assumption. The baseline is feasible with 30 stations, 178 ports, and 26.7 MW, whereas all six future scenarios are infeasible. San Juan and Guaynabo, which hold one-third of the island’s registered EV stock but four candidate sites each, exhaust their candidate-set capacity first, at closed-form thresholds of 1.78% and 3.38% electrification, versus 8.99% in the calibrated-2030 case. This threshold reproduces the MILP shortfall to four decimal places in all six infeasible scenarios. At a screening fraction of 0.20, removing the upstream screen changes neither feasibility nor shortfall. Restoring 2030 feasibility would require at least 21 and 11 represented 3 MW sites, versus four each. Under the modeled assumptions, these findings support examining candidate-site limitations before upstream grid reinforcement in s…

An Operational Digital Twin for Electric Bus Depot Charging Infrastructure: Validation and Scenario Analysis at a Sub-Saharan African Fleet
abstract: Charging infrastructure for battery electric bus (BEB) fleets must be sized against the timing of demand, not only its magnitude: an accurate per-trip energy estimate cannot on its own establish whether a depot’s chargers, contracted grid connection, and dispatch schedule can recover the fleet’s energy deficit without breaching demand-based tariff thresholds. This is especially consequential in resource-constrained settings, where notified-maximum-demand penalties and steep time-of-use differentials turn a mistimed charging load into a direct commercial liability rather than an operational inconvenience. Yet pre-investment planning tools typically treat vehicle energy consumption, dispatch scheduling, and charging infrastructure as separate problems, so a validated demand estimate rarely translates into a validated depot load profile. This paper presents an operational digital twin that converts the per-trip arrival state-of-charge predicted by a companion rolling stock twin into a depot-level charging load profile for the Golden Arrow Bus Services (GABS) electric fleet at the Arrowgate depot in Cape Town, South Africa. The twin reconstructs each bus’s daily duty chain from scheduling data to determine its available charging window, then simulates session initiation, power draw, and duration against these windows using charging behaviour parametrised from depot Open Charge Poin…

title: Nghiên cứu hành vi sử dụng dịch vụ xe buýt điện của người dân tại thành phố Hà Nội: Ứng dụng Mô hình Chấp nhận và Sử dụng Công nghệ Hợp nhất
abstract: Xe buýt điện là một giải pháp giao thông bền vững và thân thiện với môi trường. Bằng cách ứng dụng mô hình chấp nhận và sử dụng công nghệ hợp nhất (UTAUT), nghiên cứu tập trung khám phá hành vi sử dụng dịch vụ xe buýt điện của người dân tại thành phố Hà Nội. Thông qua khảo sát bảng hỏi, 200 phản hồi của hành khách đã từng sử dụng dịch vụ được phân tích bằng phương pháp mô hình cấu trúc bình phương nhỏ nhất từng phần (PLS-SEM). Kết quả cho thấy ý định sử dụng chịu tác động bởi lợi ích kỳ vọng, nỗ lực kỳ vọng, điều kiện thuận lợi và sự quan tâm về môi trường; hệ quả là ý định sử dụng ảnh hưởng tích cực đến hành vi sử dụng. Từ đó, nghiên cứu đề xuất một số giải pháp giúp doanh nghiệp và cơ quan chức năng thúc đẩy hành vi sử dụng dịch vụ xe buýt điện của người dân.

Pathogen nutrient acquisition strategy mediates the strength of diversity–disease relationships in natural grasslands
abstract: Summary The relationship between biodiversity and disease risk is a cornerstone of disease ecology, yet predicting its direction and strength remains challenging. Pathogen nutrient acquisition strategies may be key to resolving this context dependency, but their roles in mediating diversity–disease relationships are poorly understood. Here, we combine a large‐scale survey spanning 2000 km in natural grasslands with advanced statistical modeling to demonstrate that pathogen nutrient acquisition strategy is a critical mediator. We show that diseases caused by biotrophic pathogens (e.g. rusts and powdery mildews), which depend on living host tissues, exhibit a significantly negative diversity–disease relationship, whereas diseases caused by necrotrophic pathogens (e.g. leaf spots and blights) show no significant relationship. Furthermore, the strength of this negative relationship for biotrophic pathogens is amplified in regions with higher disease severity. Bayesian structural equation modeling reveals that plant species richness directly reduces biotrophic disease severity, while for necrotrophic pathogens, precipitation is the primary driver of severity, with no direct effect of richness. Our findings provide a trait‐based framework linking climatic drivers, pathogen nutrient acquisition strategies, and the strength of diversity–disease relationships. These results enhance our …

title: Vernacularity as tactic and strategy: architecture and the politics of designation
abstract: Abstract Who essentialises the vernacular? Essentialising attributions of vernacularity within a nation-state, as also those of Orientalism at the international level, may represent both co-optation and marginalisation of the subaltern by political or expert authorities. It may also represent an act of resistance, resilience, or ‘subversive archaism’ against such forces. Essentialisation is always a social process – often a speech act (heritage designation offers a pertinent example) or its architectural equivalent. Using examples mostly from Greece and Thailand– both countries with an ambiguous relationship with European colonialism – we can connect the real dangers and potential benefits of designating specific buildings as vernacular with the similar ambiguities inherent in the concept of ‘local knowledge’. It is only by stripping vernacularity of its derogatory implications and by accepting the common human capacities realised in all architecture that we can confront the inequalities often generated by the selective attribution of vernacularity to rural and marginalised populations and trace these inequalities to their European colonial sources.

title: Strategic Sustainability Evaluation of Industrial Symbiosis Partners for the Textile Industry: A Robust Fuzzy Decision Analytics Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Technological advancements have transformed production processes, revealing the inadequacy of traditional resource management approaches. This necessitates redesigning industrial systems based on collaborative models. Industrial symbiosis (IS) aims to create a sustainable production ecosystem by generating economic and environmental value. However, decision‐making models addressing uncertainties in IS partner selection under advanced fuzzy approaches remain limited. This study supports IS implementation and sustainable resource management in the textile industry by identifying the most suitable symbiotic partner under uncertainty. The evaluation considers cement and ready‐mixed concrete, ceramics, packaging and recycling, agriculture and greenhouse cultivation, chemical and industrial chemicals, and construction sectors. The study proposes the fuzzy skewness impact through distributional evaluation (F‐SITDE) and fuzzy multiple normalization rating analysis (F‐MUNRA) model, an integrated fuzzy multicriteria decision‐making (MCDM) framework for uncertainty handling. F‐SITDE determines criterion weights, while F‐MUNRA evaluates alternatives. The results show the packaging and recycling sector performs best. Comparative analysis confirms robustness. The framework offers a systematic methodology for decision‐making and contributes to SDGs 9, 12, and 13.

title: The Effect of Plyometric Exercises Combined With Visual Cues on Offensive Decision-Making Speed and Lower-Limb Explosive Power in Young Handball Players
abstract: Backgroud: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of plyometric exercises combined with visual cues on offensive decision-making speed and lower-limb explosive power in young handball players. Methods: The researcher employed an experimental approach using a two-group design an experimental group and a control group with pre- and post-tests, as this was deemed appropriate for the nature of the problem. The sample consisted of 20 players from the Army Sports Club’s youth handball team in Baghdad for the 2025–2026 season, who were randomly divided into two equal groups of 10 players each, after excluding goalkeepers and verifying the homogeneity of the sample and the equivalence of the groups. The experimental group underwent plyometric exercises combined with visual cues that specified the direction of movement or the type of offensive decision required, for a period of eight weeks at a rate of three sessions per week, whilst the control group performed plyometric exercises at the same intensity without visual cues. The speed of offensive decision-making was measured using a light-based offensive situation test that measures decision time, whilst lower-limb explosive power was measured using a vertical jump test. El uso disuasivo de la flagrancia y sus implicaciones en la representación del poder penal: una mirada desde la presunción de inocencia
abstract: Objetivo: Analizar la instrumentalización de la flagrancia como mecanismo disuasivo y de representación simbólica del poder punitivo en Ecuador, considerando sus implicaciones para la presunción de inocencia. Metodología: Se desarrolló una investigación cualitativa de carácter documental mediante el método dogmático-jurídico. Se examinaron disposiciones de la Constitución de la República del Ecuador y del Código Orgánico Integral Penal, reformas normativas, jurisprudencia de la Corte Constitucional del Ecuador y de la Corte Interamericana de Derechos Humanos, así como literatura especializada en garantismo penal y criminología crítica. El análisis se organizó en torno a las garantías procesales, la celeridad judicial y la función simbólica del castigo. Resultados: El análisis identificó tensiones entre la calificación de la flagrancia y la determinación de la responsabilidad penal, así como riesgos para la presunción de inocencia derivados de la exhibición pública de personas aprehendidas. Asimismo, evidenció que la celeridad procesal y la comunicación institucional de eficacia punitiva plantearon desafíos para la protección de las garantías procesales cuando se privilegiaron frente al examen riguroso de los elementos de convicción. Conclusiones: Se concluyó que la flagrancia, aunque constituye una institución procesal legítima, no sustituye la comprobación de la responsabilida…

title: The Muted Sonic Heart of Afghanistan: Shared Musical Heritage in South Asia, Taliban 2.0 and the Dilemmas of Indian Soft Power
abstract: The Taliban’s return to power in 2021 has plunged Afghanistan into a profound cultural silence. The ban on music, the repression of women, artistic censorship, and other restrictions imposed on public and cultural life, constitute a systematic policy of social control and symbolic erasure. This article examines the role that India’s cultural diplomacy and soft power could play in the protection of Afghan musical heritage, while also analysing the contradictions of Indian foreign policy, marked by the rise of Hindutva nationalism. Drawing on an interdisciplinary approach that combines ethnomusicology, feminist studies, postcolonial critique, and international relations, the article offers a critical reading of soft power and its ethical limits in contexts of symbolic inequality and religious exclusion. It argues that the protection of Afghanistan’s musical legacy is not only a matter of cultural memory, but also a regional responsibility for South Asia, provided that it is grounded in reciprocity, listening, and the recognition of Afghan agency.

title: Patent research and analysis of technological trends of hybrid power plants for cars
abstract: The article provides a patent analysis and research of technological trends in the development of hybrid power plants for cars for the period 2014-2022, which is an urgent task, based on the need to systematize trends in the development of hybrid power plant technologies. The main advantages and problems of implementing hybrid technologies are considered, including improving energy efficiency, reducing carbon dioxide emissions, as well as challenges related to the high cost of components, limited battery capacity and life, complexity of system management and integration, as well as the underdeveloped infrastructure of charging stations. The paper analyzes the dynamics of filing patent applications and granting patents, highlights key areas of innovation such as electrical systems, energy management, energy storage and regeneration. Special attention is paid to the leaders of patent activity among countries (China, Japan, South Korea, USA) and companies (Toyota, Hyundai, Kia, Ford). In conclusion, it is noted that the main vectors of development of hybrid power plants are the improvement of energy management systems, increased energy efficiency and the integration of renewable energy sources, which contributes to the creation of more environmentally friendly and economical automotive solutions.

title: Synergistic Charge Scavenging in Pt/C‐Polyoxometalate Systems for Scalable Biomass Power Generation via Super‐Reduced Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct electrochemical conversion of unrefined biomass waste into electricity offers a sustainable pathway for decentralized energy generation, yet its practical implementation has been fundamentally hindered by low power densities and limited scalability. A fundamental bottleneck lies in the intrinsic recalcitrance of biomass, which restricts electron harvesting to shallow oxidation pathways and confines redox mediators to low reduction states. Here, we demonstrate a scalable biomass flow fuel cell (BFFC) enabled by a super‐reduced polyoxometalate (POM) electrolyte that overcomes the long‐standing electron‐harvesting ceiling. By employing a catalytic oxidative degradation strategy that promotes extensive cleavage of recalcitrant C─C linkages in the lignocellulosic matrix, we unlock deep multi‐electron reduction of POM, achieving an electron transfer capacity exceeding four electrons per molecule. As a result, the single‐cell device delivers a record‐breaking power density of 218.6 mW cm − 2 . Beyond laboratory‐scale demonstrations, we constructed a 10‐cell stack prototype, producing 59.2 Wh over 15.6 h of stable operation directly from raw biomass.

title: Driving Greater SME Engagement With Stakeholder Support for Environmental Sustainability: The Role of Resources, Barriers and Dependency Activation Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT External stakeholders are critical in enabling SMEs to achieve environmental sustainability. Yet, despite the growing availability of sustainability support, SME engagement remains limited. This article addresses significant gaps in the SME sustainability literature by mapping the support ecosystem and explaining why available sustainability resources are so underutilized. Drawing on resource dependence theory (RDT) and institutional theory (IT), we analyse 47 interviews and two focus groups with UK SMEs and support providers, revealing (i) latent and reverse dependencies, (ii) institutional and structural barriers and (iii) strategic inaction weakening engagement. Our findings advance RDT by shifting attention from dependency formation to the mechanisms that hinder it, offering a novel conceptual lens on how support relationships can be activated. This study combines academic rigour with practical relevance, providing actionable insights for policymakers and intermediaries seeking to strengthen SME–stakeholder interactions and accelerate sustainability adoption and carbon reduction efforts in line with the net‐zero agenda.

title: The Effect of Reciprocal Teaching Strategy on Student’s Attitude Towards Learning Physics
Under Pressure: Building Relational Water Stewardship Capability in Buyer‐Driven Agri‐Food Chains
abstract: ABSTRACT Buyers increasingly demand water stewardship, yet it is hard to operationalize because water risk is place‐based, collective and only partly auditable. We develop Relational Water Stewardship Capability (RWSC), the relational capacity through which buyers, exporters and intermediaries align incentives, produce credible evidence and test water‐saving practice while protecting yield and quality. Evidence comes from an abductive multiple‐case study of the Tunisian date sector: 32 interviews, 15 days of observation and 190 documents. Three mechanisms generate RWSC: reframing water as a threat to supply continuity, cofinanced field trials that yield locally credible evidence and boundary spanning to producer organizations and agronomists. Contrasting cases show RWSC fails where buyer power lacks recognition and investment and where shared objectives meet no capital at producer level. We specify three pathways from dyadic capability to collective resource and find the fiscal one binding. Over a fossil aquifer, the process slows depletion without reversing it.

title: Correction: Bacterial bioremediation as a sustainable strategy for the mitigation of Bisphenol-A
Building Eco‐Innovation in SMEs Through Circular Economy Capability: Revisiting the Role of Green Transformational Leadership
abstract: ABSTRACT Resource‐constrained small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) often struggle to translate sustainability ambitions into eco‐innovation because environmental initiatives must also support economic survival. Although green transformational leadership (GTL) is widely recognized as a driver of eco‐innovation, little is known about how it enables SMEs to develop the organizational capabilities needed to achieve both environmental and economic objectives. Drawing on the Resource‐Based View (RBV), this study examines whether circular economy capability (CEC) mediates the relationship between GTL and eco‐innovation and whether innovative climate (IC) strengthens this relationship. A repeated cross‐sectional design was employed among emerging‐economy SMEs (Study 1, n = 335; Study 2, n = 302), with each study adopting a three‐wave, multi‐source survey design with temporal separation between measurements. The hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM). The findings show that GTL is positively associated with eco‐innovation primarily by developing CEC, with CEC partially mediating the leadership–innovation relationship across both study periods. Although IC has no direct effect on eco‐innovation, it significantly strengthens the positive influence of CEC on eco‐innovation. The replication of these relationships across the two study …

title: Fuzzy logic-based controller strategy for a single-input dual-output DC–DC converter for DC homes
abstract: Abstract Effective power management systems in DC household applications have raised interest in the analytical study of specialized converter topologies and control algorithms. This Article presents the design of a Single-Input Dual-Output (SIDO) converter with control strategies, including a Fuzzy Logic (FL) controller and a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller for voltage control. The proposed SIDO converter has a 48 V input and regulated 24 V and 12 V outputs. The experimental results are validated on the TMS320F28379D Microcontroller by maintaining the output voltage at a constant level in a closed-loop configuration with sensor-based feedback. The PI controller demonstrated a settling time of 5.83 ms and a voltage regulation of 4.7%, whereas the FL controller achieved a settling time of 3.24 ms and a voltage regulation of 0.5% for the 24 V output. The FL controller achieved a settling time of 5.29 ms and a voltage regulation of 1.25% for the 12 V output, significantly improving over the PI's 19.95 ms settling time and 2.16% voltage regulation. These results show that the FL controller has a better dynamic response in terms of rise time, settling time, overshoot, undershoot, and reduced ripple during load surges than the PI controller.

title: Navigating uncertainty through education: human security and present-focused adaptation among displaced Myanmar youth in Thailand
UGSA-Net: Uncertainty-Gated Attention and Self-Supervised Alignment for Calibration-Aware Hyperspectral Image Classification
abstract: Uniform spatial weighting in patch-based hyperspectral classifiers indiscriminately aggregates spectral information, even when individual pixels are already class-diagnostic, degrading accuracy and interpretability. We propose UGSA-Net, an ambiguity-guided spatial–spectral transformer that infers a per-pixel ambiguity field without direct label supervision. A lightweight ambiguity head maps each token to a scalar in (0,1), trained end-to-end with no target of its own, so that the field is shaped only by the training losses that reach it through the token mixer. This field dually modulates the token mixer: it biases query and key projections with a spectral angle mapper (SAM) prior to emphasise spectrally similar patches, and rescales token outputs to amplify contributions from ambiguous locations. The value pathway remains unmodulated, so the network reweights spatial information without distorting the spectral content entering the mixture. The ambiguity head and the classification backbone are trained end-to-end, following a self-supervised latent-alignment stage that uses no labels; model selection jointly scores overall accuracy (OA), few-shot accuracy and expected calibration error (ECE) on validation data. Across six benchmark scenes from four sensors, under a stratified pixel-level split in which training and test windows overlap, UGSA-Net exceeds 98.9% OA on every scene …

title: Uncertainty-guided diffusion refinement of optical-flow residuals for rock thin-section image stitching
Addressing AIAA Aerodynamics Uncertainty Quantification Challenge with Sensitivity-Based and Diffusion Model Updating
abstract: This paper presents the principles and techniques employed to address the AIAA Second Uncertainty Quantification Challenge Problem for Aerodynamics. Two distinct model updating strategies for uncertainty quantification and reduction are investigated: a sensitivity-based approach and a data-driven diffusion-model-based approach. Both methods aim to infer the posterior distributions of key aerodynamic input parameters, which are subsequently propagated through either a surrogate model or XFOIL to obtain posterior-predictive lift, drag, and moment coefficients. The diffusion model shows consistent posterior-predictive responses across both the surrogate and XFOIL, whereas the sensitivity-based approach produces sharply concentrated parameter posteriors that may represent a more limited uncertainty range. Across multiple operating configurations, the two approaches produce coherent predictive aerodynamic responses despite their differing parameter posterior structures. The findings suggest that, in uncertainty quantification challenges of this type, it is not only essential to characterize multiple sources of uncertainty but equally, if not more, critical to employ an appropriate inverse uncertainty-reduction mechanism capable of leveraging the necessarily limited observational data. Designing such inverse processes to extract maximal information from sparse data remains a central …

Mechanisms for developing management decisions and their financial and economic justification
abstract: The article discusses the theoretical and applied aspects of the development of management solutions in conditions of uncertainty. The analysis of classifications, stages and methods of decision–making is carried out, from heuristic to strictly formalized quantitative ones. Special attention is paid to financial and economic justification as a tool for objectifying choice. A single example of an investment solution demonstrates the use of simple and discounted payback periods, net present value, internal rate of return, profitability index, expert assessments and a probabilistic decision tree. It is shown how different methods can produce consistent or contradictory results; the necessity of an integral approach combining objective calculations, sensitivity analysis, scenario modeling and expert judgments is substantiated. A formalized multi-criteria selection algorithm is proposed, taking into account both financial and strategic factors. It is concluded that the quality of management decisions is determined not only by the choice of method, but also by organizational culture, staff competencies, and willingness to reflexively revise assumptions. The implementation of artificial intelligence and big data technologies to improve the accuracy of forecasts and adaptability of solutions are identified as promising areas.

Design assessment and preliminary performance evaluation of a novel device for non-invasive emergency treatment of acute respiratory failure
abstract: Abstract Acute respiratory failure (ARF) requires rapid intervention to prevent patient deterioration and life-threatening complications. Early respiratory support through prehospital Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) has been shown to improve ARF outcomes. However, existing CPAP devices present technical barriers for use in out-of-hospital emergency scenarios. This study presents the design and preliminary performance evaluation of a novel portable, ready-to-use CPAP device for out-of-hospital respiratory support. The device includes a blower providing steady air insufflation through a face mask, with Positive End-Expiratory Pressure (PEEP) regulated by two fixed-point PEEP valves. To identify optimized operational conditions ensuring target respiratory support, a lumped-parameter model (LPM) was developed to simulate device–patient interaction. Input data for the LPM included experimental characteristics of the device components. Simulations were conducted using breathing profiles representing varying ARF-like conditions and severity. Additionally, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis was performed to assess the risk of CO 2 rebreathing through the mask. LPM simulations described the dynamic interaction between the breathing profile and device performances, and the consequent pressure and flow patterns during the respiratory cycle. Across all simulated conditi…

title: The library sector in context of transnational advocacy networks in European copyright reform
abstract: Library organisations often advocate for access to information, and the issues that influence that access, including copyright and open access. As these issues are technically complex and contested, advocacy requires expertise, resources, and sustained engagement across sectors and countries. This article identifies how these issues often bring the library and information sector into the sphere of transnational advocacy. A case study centred on the Article 17 of the EU Directive on Copyright in the Digital Single Market is utilised to show how library organisations act within transnational advocacy networks in information policy. The case study highlights how issue framing and consultation opportunities influence participation and relations between actors. This article argues that library and information organisations are visible in policy debates on information governance. Assessing their position in relation to other actors within an issue network provides insights into the sector’s capacity to participate in activities that influence policy outcomes.

FROM LEGALISTIC CONTROL TO REHABILITATION AND SOCIAL REINTEGRATION: Rethinking Penitentiary Law Reform for Humane Corrections
abstract: The Indonesian correctional system is currently facing a structural and philosophical crisis characterized by overcrowding, limited inmate rehabilitation programs, and ineffective social reintegration mechanisms. This study analyzes correctional law reform as a strategy to build a humane, just, rehabilitation-oriented correctional system within the framework of achieving the Golden Indonesia 2045 Vision. The study uses qualitative legal research and employs legislative, conceptual, and comparative approaches. The analysis examines a paradigm shift from a retributive approach to rehabilitative and restorative models, considering developments in the National Criminal Code through Law No. 1 of 2023 and Law No. 22 of 2022 on Corrections. The research findings indicate that Law No. 22 of 2022 incorporates reform principles, while the National Criminal Code has updated the objectives of criminal punishment by orienting them toward rehabilitation, conflict resolution, restoring balance, and respecting human dignity. However, these normative changes have not yet been fully integrated with implementation mechanisms for risk- and needs-based sentencing, individual rehabilitation, and social reintegration. A comparative study of the correctional systems in Norway, Germany, and the Netherlands shows that humanization, risk-based rehabilitation, and community participation are key elements …

title: Heart2Mind: Human-Centered Contestable Psychiatric Disorder Prediction System Using Wearable ECG Monitors
abstract: Psychiatric disorders affect millions, yet diagnosis depends on subjective assessments and uneven access to care. To address these challenges, there is a growing need for Contestable AI (CAI), a framework that extends beyond Explainable AI (XAI) by allowing clinicians to inspect, question, and revise algorithmic outputs, thereby reducing automation bias and strengthening accountability. We present Heart2Mind (Our implementation is available at: https://github.com/Analytics-Everywhere-Lab/heart2mind ), a human-centered CAI system for psychiatric disorder prediction that provides objective evidence while preserving clinical oversight. Heart2Mind collects R–R Interval (RRI) time series from Polar H9/H10 wearable ECG sensors via a Cardiac Monitoring Interface and analyzes them using a Multi-Scale Temporal-Frequency Transformer (MSTFT) that combines time-domain and frequency-domain features. For contestability, the Contestable Diagnosis Interface integrates model explanations with dialogue. Self-Adversarial Explanations compare attention-based and gradient-based explanation maps to flag inconsistent predictions, and a collaboration chatbot helps users verify and challenge outputs. On the HRV-ACC dataset, MSTFT achieved 91.7% accuracy under leave-one-out cross-validation, outperforming benchmark methods. Human-centered evaluation with the Human–CAI Consensus Rate showed experts and C…

title: Enhancing Participation, Engagement, and Reflection in Asynchronous Remote Communities Research with People Facing Stigmatized Healthcare
abstract: Stigma surrounding certain health issues remains deeply entrenched, often silencing those affected and discouraging them from participating in research, particularly on sensitive topics such as sexual and reproductive health. These barriers are especially pronounced in traditional, face-to-face research settings. The Asynchronous Remote Communities (ARC) method offers a promising alternative by enabling remote participation in structured, supportive research activities. Although the ARC method has been successfully used with people facing stigma, existing guidelines offer limited direction for deepening participant engagement, fostering meaningful interactions, and supporting reflection on sensitive topics. In this article, we present how we adapted ARC to support 26 unmarried Korean women facing stigma from cultural norms that marginalize sexual and reproductive health discussions and care-seeking. Our adaptations included improving rapport-building, including destigmatizing activities, reconsidering sequential activities and anticipating the emotional impact of activities to support constructive discomfort, and broadening criteria for evaluating activities. Over 9 weeks, these approaches deepened reflection and led to substantial changes in perception and behavior with 100% participation. We showed that our adaptations to ARC can drive personal and communal growth, highlighti…

The leading role of technological factors in the development of the global online education market
abstract: The article analyzes the leading role of technological factors in the development of the global online education market. The impact of the spread of the Worldwide Web, mobile devices, cloud services, artificial intelligence, e-learning, personalization of learning, virtual and augmented reality, information security, big data, and gamification of learning on the transformation of the educational environment is considered. It is shown that digital technologies have accelerated the transition from traditional forms of education to online formats, expanded access to educational resources, and made learning more flexible, personalized, and scalable. Special attention is paid to how technological innovations are changing the models of interaction between students and educational platforms, improving the quality of content and creating new mechanisms for evaluating learning outcomes. The growth factors of the online education market are also considered, including the development of digital infrastructure, increasing the investment attractiveness of the EdTech sector and the growing demand for distance education services. The paper emphasizes that technological factors are not only a condition, but also the main driver of further expansion of the global online education market. It is concluded that the further development of this field will be determined by the speed of innovation and…

title: Digital Module of the Eurasian Clearing Union as a Mechanism for Cross-Border Settlements in the EAEU
abstract: The article examines the development of the payment and settlement infrastructure of the Eurasian Economic Union on the basis of the Eurasian Clearing Union concept. The relevance of the study is determined by the growing use of national currencies in mutual settlements among the EAEU member states and the continuing fragmentation of existing cross-border payment mechanisms. At the same time, traditional multilateral clearing has a number of limitations related to the need to settle accumulated positions, maintain sufficient liquidity, and interact with participants from third countries. The aim of the study is to develop a mechanism for cross-border settlements using a digital module of the Eurasian Clearing Union. The article proposes incorporating such a module into the ECU architecture to ensure the issuance, accounting, transfer, and redemption of a backed digital settlement unit. The functions of the digital module operator, the principles of managed participant access, the internal and external settlement contours, and the allocation of control functions between the operator and financial intermediaries are outlined. The digital settlement unit is treated as a tokenized obligation of the operator used at the infrastructure level and not as a substitute for national currencies. A step-by-step mechanism for cross-border payments is developed in which the digital settlement…

title: Designing Independent Merit Oversight after Indonesia’s Abolition of Its Civil Service Commission
abstract: Following the abolition of Indonesia’s civil service commission (KASN) in 2023, merit oversight was transferred to bodies that also formulate and implement personnel policy. In 2025, the Constitutional Court required oversight by an independent institution. This study examines changes in the formal independence of merit oversight across KASN and two subsequent arrangements and identifies implications for institutional design. Document analysis and directed content analysis covered 14 core documents, including instruments governing the three Indonesian arrangements, the Court’s decision, four hearing records, the United Kingdom’s Constitutional Reform and Governance Act 2010, and the 1987 Philippine Constitution. An AI model coded 17 indicators using a researcher-designed codebook; blind recoding of one arrangement matched 15 of the 17 indicator codes. KASN received a score of 1 on all 14 indicators concerning independence, mandate, and separation of functions, whereas the subsequent arrangements received that score on one and three indicators, respectively. The Court required institutional separation between the overseer, policy maker, and implementer. Hearing participants disputed whether systemic independence could substitute for institutional independence. Three design options were assessed against stated criteria, without recommending a preferred option. The findings docume…

title: A Comparative MCDM Analysis of Airline Service Ratings of Low Cost Airlines
abstract: This study compares the profiles of nine low-cost airlines based on five airline service quality scores. All criteria, including the baggage delivery score, are benefit-oriented. Criterion weights are derived using PSI, LODECI, CRISUS, and a hybrid rule based on their normalized direct product. Rankings are compared using RADAR-2, TOPSIS, and VIKOR. Ranking consistency is measured via Spearman’s ρ and Kendall’s τ-b. While RADAR-2, using the hybrid weights, places Eurowings, Norwegian, and EasyJet in the top three spots, TOPSIS and VIKOR reverse the top two positions. VIKOR identifies Eurowings and Norwegian as a compromise set rather than selecting a single winner. Four airlines share a RADAR-2 score of 0.0579 because distinct raw profiles map onto the same relative relationship plateau. Weight simulations demonstrate that the leader and the entire ranking can change while the plateau equality persists. The findings describe the recorded score matrix and the aggregation rules; they do not demonstrate actual performance equality, external model validity, or the overall superiority of any method.

title: Construction of a leak detection and pressure regulation system for municipal water distribution networks integrating digital twin technology
abstract: Abstract Aging municipal water networks lose a substantial share of treated water to leakage, yet detection and pressure control are still pursued on separate models, so neither can inform the other. This paper builds an integrated system in which both functions read from and write to one continuously synchronized digital twin. The twin couples an open-source hydraulic kernel, a pressure-dependent demand closure and emitter-based leakage to an ensemble Kalman filter and a weighted least-squares recalibration step, so that heads, flows, Hazen–Williams roughness coefficients and demand multipliers are updated from multi-source telemetry rather than frozen at commissioning. Detection normalizes twin residuals against diurnal demand patterns and combines a sliding-window CUSUM statistic with a Mahalanobis joint test; the residual field then feeds a graph attention network that scores each junction and aggregates node posteriors into ranked suspect pipe segments. Regulation solves a bi-objective program over valve settings and pump speeds, weighting nodes by their leak posterior so that head is reduced hardest where water actually escapes, subject to service-head, switching and resilience constraints. Results are reported network by network rather than pooled alone. The pooled F1 reaches 0.916 and the Top-5 hit rate 0.816, against 0.836 and 0.573 for the strongest baseline, with per…

Psychometric properties of the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS): An item response theory and classical test theory analysis
abstract: Over the past two decades, social networking services have become a pervasive and integral part of young adults’ lives. At the same time, a growing body of evidence points to their negative effects on mental health and their potentially addictive nature. In this context, the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS) was developed to assess problematic social media use (PSMU). Although the BSMAS has been translated and validated in Spanish, its validity and reliability have yet to be examined in an Ecuadorian population. Using a cross-sectional design, the present study examined the psychometric properties of the BSMAS in Ecuadorian university students using both Classical Test Theory (CTT) and Item Response Theory (IRT). The sample consisted of 580 university students aged 18 to 54 years (M = 20.09, SD = 3.27), 58.4% of whom were female. CTT supported an adequate fit for a unidimensional model (CFI = .992, TLI = .987, SRMR = .046), with high internal consistency (α = .88; ω = .85), moderate associations with anxiety (r = .41), depression (r = .43), and hours of SNS use (r = .40), and a weak negative association with well-being (r = -.16), assessed with the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-4) and World Health Organization Well-being Index (WHO-5), and strict measurement invariance across sex. IRT showed adequate discrimination and difficulty parameters for the items. The inst…

title: Municipal Libraries as Community Learning Spaces: A Model for Educational Resource Management in Western Visayas
abstract: This mixed-methods study used a triangulation design to evaluate municipal libraries in Western Visayas as vital community learning spaces. The paper emphasized libraries' transformative role in supporting lifelong learning and social engagement in the digital age. Thirty-seven librarians and library staff participated in quantitative data collection, while fifteen librarians took part in qualitative interviews. The study used purposive sampling and a self-developed questionnaire under strict ethical oversight; researchers analyzed the data using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. The study found significant regional differences: libraries on Panay Island reported better digital resources and stronger alignment with academic requirements, while those on Negros Island focused more on out-of-school resources. The study found a negative relationship between the number of patrons and the adequacy of physical collections, suggesting that libraries with fewer patrons perceived their collections as more adequate. Overall, municipal libraries in the region have a strong mix of physical and digital resources but still face persistent challenges in modernization, staffing, and outreach. A limitation of this research is its focus on municipal libraries in Western Visayas, which may not represent experiences in other regions. The study's practical implications include recommenda…

Design and Implementation of HidroPond: An IoT-Based Information System for Aquaponics Monitoring and Control
abstract: Aquaponics requires timely monitoring and traceable remote control of water and feeding operations. This study designed, implemented, and functionally validated HidroPond, an IoT-based information system for aquaponics monitoring and control. Dedicated Sensor and Actuator ESP32 devices, an Arduino Nano for pH acquisition, a FastAPI backend, a Supabase database, and a Vercel-hosted web application form the architecture. Six parameters (pH, total dissolved solids, water temperature, ambient temperature, humidity, and surface distance as a water-level indicator) were aggregated for transmission at a configured three-minute interval. The actuator supports water filling, draining, pH Up and pH Down dosing, and fish feeding. During a one-day evaluation at a single aquaponics installation, all ten predefined functional checkpoints were verified across telemetry, cloud storage, web monitoring, remote control, device connectivity, and execution feedback. Command-linked feedback distinguishes submitted requests from device-reported outcomes and provides a basis for inspecting unconfirmed operations before further intervention; completion reports do not independently verify water flow, dosing volume, or feed delivery. The contribution is a field-deployed bidirectional information workflow linking telemetry, command records, execution reports, and device connectivity across physical device…

title: Digitalisation of the world economy and the transformation of the global monetary and financial system: central bank digital currencies and prospects for polycentrism
abstract: The purpose of the study is to identify the mechanisms and directions through which digitalisation, primarily via central bank digital currencies and digital payment technologies, transforms the world economy and the architecture of the global monetary and financial system, including de-dollarisation and the shift towards a multipolar model. The methods applied include comparative-typological analysis of national digital currency projects, content analysis of Russian legal acts on the digital rouble and the circulation of digital assets, generalisation of secondary aggregated statistics for 2015–2026, historical-logical reconstruction of de-dollarisation stages, and systematisation of effects and risks across the levels of bank funding, the national payment system and international settlements. The findings show that behavioural indicators of payment digitalisation outpace infrastructural ones; digital currency projects now involve 134 states and currency unions accounting for about 98% of global GDP; the largest retail project reached a transaction volume of approximately 986 billion US dollars; the US dollar share in global reserves declined from 64.1% in 2015 to 56.8% by end-2025, while the yuan share rose from 1.08% in Q4 2016 to 2.11% by Q2 2026; the currency structure of Russian settlements shifted towards the national currency. The Russian digital rouble project has a co…

title: Optimizing the Administration of Civil Appeal Cases through the Electronic Justice System to Realize the Principles of Simple, Speedy, and Low-Cost Justice
abstract: Appeal case administration continues to involve physical attendance, paper transfers between courts, and indirect costs for justice seekers. This study examines the regulation of electronic appeal administration under Indonesian positive law, evaluates its potential contribution to simple, speedy, and low-cost justice, and identifies strategies for optimization. A normative juridical method employed statutory, conceptual, and analytical approaches, supported by official secondary data and prior research. Lawrence M. Friedman’s legal system theory provided the analytical framework. The findings identify Supreme Court Regulations No. 3 of 2018, No. 1 of 2019, and No. 7 of 2022 as establishing a normative foundation for electronic filing, notification, submission of appeal memoranda, file inspection, and transmission of case files and appeal decisions. Digitizing these stages has the potential to simplify procedures, shorten waiting times, and reduce costs. However, implementation faces fragmented regulation and reliance on technical guidelines, uneven infrastructure, inconsistent administrative compliance, and limited digital literacy among some users. The study concludes that optimization requires regulatory harmonization, standardized files and contingency procedures, stronger personnel capacity and data security, and assistance for justice seekers. These priorities provide a n…

title: Respons Siswa terhadap Hybrid PjBL-STEAM pada Proyek Toilet Check System di Sekolah Dasar
abstract: Aim: This study aimed to describe first-grade students’ responses to hybrid learning integrated with Project-Based Learning (PjBL)-STEAM through the Toilet Check System project in Civic Education. Method: A quantitative descriptive approach involved 28 students. Data were collected using a four-point observation sheet covering ten indicators: interest, active participation, response to digital media, understanding of instructions, collaboration, responsibility, creativity, problem solving, communication, and reflection. The data were analysed using frequencies, percentages, mean, median, and standard deviation. Result: Twenty-two students obtained a score of 4, five students a score of 3, and one student a score of 2. The total score was 105 out of 112 (93.75%), with a mean of 3.75, a median of 4.00, and a standard deviation of 0.52, indicating a very positive response. Novelty/Implication: The novelty lies in combining hybrid learning, PjBL-STEAM, and a Toilet Check System project as a contextual Civic Education experience for early-grade students. The findings imply that digital technology should support concrete experience, collaboration, and problem solving while direct teacher-student interaction remains central.

title: Transforming Contingency Plans into BPMN-Based Disaster Management Workflows: A Design Science Research Study in Agam Regency
abstract: This study addresses the operational bottlenecks in regional disaster management caused by static, narrative-based Contingency Plans. It aims to bridge the semantic gap between legal bureaucratic prose and machine-readable BPMN workflow specifications to facilitate modern e-Government integration in Agam Regency. We applied a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology to systematically extract and transform passive policy texts into structured Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) workflows. The resulting artifact was then syntactically validated using ISO/IEC 19510 conformance checking alongside proposed expert evaluation criteria. The empirical transformation successfully reduced ambiguous legal instructions into precise operational logic, enforcing strict accountability boundaries. Although syntax validation confirmed the model's syntactic correctness, actual deployment faces anticipated non-technical hurdles; potential governance barriers, such as data silos and resistance to automated discretionary control, were inferred from the transformation process. This research provides an alternative perspective on public policy formulation by treating contingency documents not merely as passive archives, but as executable-ready "machine-readable workflow specifications." It offers a conceptual blueprint for structuring emergency response protocols in regional administrations. T…

title: Manajemen Berbasis Sekolah Sebagai Tata Kelola Kolaboratif Untuk Mendukung Relevansi Pendidikan: Studi Literatur
abstract: Aim: This study aims to analyze how School-Based Management (SBM) functions as collaborative governance to support educational relevance. Method: The study uses a narrative literature review with a qualitative-descriptive approach to publications from 2021–2026. Literature was searched through Google Scholar, Garuda, and journal websites using terms related to SBM, school autonomy, participation, leadership, planning, accountability, and educational quality. Sources were selected based on topical relevance, publication period, verifiable bibliographic information, and access to full text. Ten articles were designated as the primary literature, while other articles were used as supporting sources. Result: The synthesis indicates that educational relevance is supported by the interconnectedness of decision-making autonomy, stakeholder participation, leadership, resource management, transparency, accountability, and evaluation. Autonomy creates room for context-sensitive decisions, but implementation depends on school capacity and stakeholder involvement. Novelty/Implication: The novelty of this study lies in a conceptual synthesis that integrates these elements into a collaborative-governance framework oriented toward educational relevance. The findings imply that strengthening SBM requires linking school authority with collaboration, implementation capacity, transparency, accoun…

title: Digital-Based Tourism Destination Development Strategies to Enhance Tourism Competitiveness in Gorontalo Province
abstract: Digital transformation has changed the way tourism destinations are promoted, managed, and accessed by visitors. Digital technology is no longer limited to promotional activities but has become part of destination management, information provision, service delivery, governance, and tourism experience creation. Gorontalo Province has natural, marine, and cultural tourism resources that can be developed to strengthen regional tourism competitiveness. This study aims to analyze and synthesize digital-based destination development strategies relevant to Gorontalo Province. A qualitative literature review approach was employed by examining publications from 2022–2026 concerning tourism digital transformation, digital marketing, smart tourism, destination governance, and tourism competitiveness, supported by official regional statistics as contextual evidence. The synthesis indicates that digital strategies should be developed in an integrated manner through stronger digital marketing, accurate and accessible tourism information, smart tourism applications, human resource development, digital infrastructure, data utilization, and multi-stakeholder collaboration. title: Global weak-martingale solutions of the 3D Chemotaxis-fluid system driven by transport noise
abstract: In this paper, we consider a Chemotaxis–Navier–Stokes system in a three-dimensional bounded convex domain, driven by multiplicative noise of transport type, where the noise coefficients depend on the gradients of the solutions. Using a multi-level approximation scheme that combines semi-Galerkin projections with suitable truncations and regularizations, together with a compactness argument based on the Jakubowski–Skorokhod representation theorem for non-metric spaces, we establish the existence of a global martingale solution. The solution is shown to be non-negative almost surely. Our result extends known global existence results for the deterministic 3D and stochastic 2D settings to the stochastic 3D case.

title: Modernleşme Bağlamında Kemalizm-Nasırcılık İlişkisi: Karşılaştırmalı Bir Analiz
abstract: Bu çalışma, Doğu'daki modernleşme arayışının en etkili iki örneği olan Kemalizm ile Nasırcılığı karşılaştırmalı bir perspektifle incelemektedir. Önce modernleşme kavramı kuramsal düzlemde tartışılmakta, ardından iki deneyimin tarihsel gelişimi ile düşünsel yapısı çözümlenmekte, son olarak modernleşme tasavvurları belirli analiz eksenleri üzerinden karşılaştırılmaktadır. Nitel yönteme dayanan çalışma; Türkçe, Arapça ve İngilizce literatürün yanı sıra resmî belgelerden ve dönemin aktörlerinin söylemlerinden yararlanmakta, verileri tarihsel analiz, metin analizi, vaka incelemesi ve karşılaştırmalı analizle değerlendirmektedir. Çalışma, her modelin de devlet merkezli ve yukarıdan aşağıya işleyen birer modernleşme modeli olduğu; aralarındaki ilişkinin doğrudan aktarımdan ziyade ilham temelinde geliştiği; Kemalizm'in öncü bir deneyim, Nasırcılığın ise özgün bir ardıl olduğu sonucuna ulaşmaktadır. Karşılaştırma, modernleşme hedeflerinin genel çerçevede örtüştüğünü; ancak milliyetçilik, din-devlet ilişkileri, Batılılaşma, toplumsal politikalar ve ekonomik model bakımından belirgin biçimde ayrışıldığını göstermektedir. Developing a self-management support intervention for older adults living with osteoarthritis and multiple long-term conditions
abstract: Abstract Background Osteoarthritis (OA) affects over half of people over the age of 65, and many live with other multiple long-term conditions (MLTC). Existing self-management interventions for OA do not adequately address the complexities of MLTC and there is a lack of holistic and coordinated provision across health services. Objective To develop a personalised self-management support intervention for adults aged 65 + with knee and/ or hip OA living with MLTC, receiving care in the NHS. Methods We used a six-step intervention mapping approach supplemented by co-design activities. Thirty adults (28 living with OA and MLTCs and two carers) participated in consultations and workshops, contributing their lived experiences and preferences to shape the intervention’s development and implementation. Results The emerging intervention was informed by nine core principles to address the physical, emotional, and psychological symptoms associated with the interplay between OA and MLTC. The intervention aimed to enhance individuals’ knowledge, confidence, and self-management capabilities to interact with health and care professionals and support informed decision making about their health and care. The intervention comprised (1) personalised coaching delivered by trained healthcare professionals to reflect self-management support in the context of living with OA and MLTCs supported by (2)…

title: Communication Barriers, Project Communication Quality, and Multi-Project Management Effectiveness in Single-Consultant Parallel Construction Supervision: A SEM-PLS and IPMA Approach
abstract: Background: Managing multiple construction projects under a single construction management consultant requires effective communication and coordination among stakeholders. Communication barriers may reduce project communication quality and multi-project management effectiveness. Objective: This study aims to identify relevant communication barriers, examine their effects on project communication quality and multi-project management effectiveness, investigate the mediating role of project communication quality, and determine priorities for communication improvement. Methods: A quantitative approach supported by expert validation was employed. Data were collected from 80 purposively selected respondents across 32 construction projects. Eight communication barrier factors were identified through a literature review and initial expert validation. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and importance-performance map analysis (IPMA), followed by final expert validation. Results: Five of the 25 hypotheses were supported. Information Delay (X1) and Communication Media Mismatch (X3) negatively affected Project Communication Quality (β = −0.123, p = 0.045; β = −0.583, p = 0.021). title: The making of a one-world religion: From interfaith movements to the religious system of Revelation 17–18
abstract: This historical-documentary and theological review investigates the internationalisation of interfaith activity, the relationship between public religious cooperation and doctrinal universalism, and their possible significance for a futurist reading of Revelation 17–18. The study traces Theosophical and parliamentary precursors, initiatives of the 1920s and 1930s, Alice Bailey’s published programme for a new world religion, postwar ecumenical and interfaith organisations, Vatican II, the United Nations’ religious-fraternity initiatives, and developments through October 2026. It gives special attention to the distinct Nigerian movements described as Chrislam, the 2019 Document on Human Fraternity, the UN General Assembly’s 2020 designation of 4 February as the International Day of Human Fraternity, and Abu Dhabi’s three-house Abrahamic Family House inaugurated in 2023. A structured comparison of founding records, official texts, published scholarship and the author’s previous works differentiates interreligious civic cooperation, religious mixing, pluralist soteriology, and compulsory worship. The historical evidence demonstrates institutional growth and some explicit projects of theological synthesis, but does not independently verify a single clandestine authority directing all initiatives. From colonial correspondent schemes to digital platforms: a typology of african payment system evolution
abstract: The article proposes an original four-stage typology of African payment system evolution: colonial correspondent (pre-1960s), post-colonial national (1960s–1990s), sub-regional integration (2000–2020), and continental digital (2021–present). The theoretical framework synthesizes Balassa’s stages of economic integration with North’s institutional theory and Mundell’s optimum currency area framework. Five formalized transition criteria are proposed: settlement agent, settlement currency, routing architecture, regulatory framework, and financial inclusivity. Using these criteria, the paper classifies five African macro-regions by their current evolutionary position. Drawing on primary data from the Afreximbank Annual Report 2024, the African Trade Report 2025, and PAPSS operational statistics (2022–2026), the study critically analyzes barriers to the fourth stage: regulatory fragmentation across 55 jurisdictions, limited liquidity in national currency pairs, competition from dollar-denominated stablecoins, and persistent trade finance gaps estimated at USD 100 billion annually. A dedicated case study of Cameroon illustrates the paradox of the CEMAC zone, where monetary integration (CFA franc) coexists with low digital financial inclusion and heavy reliance on euro-denominated correspondent channels. The results offer an analytical framework for assessing the readiness of African c…

title: CUMHURİYET DÖNEMİ BASININDA TÜRKÇE EZAN UYGULAMASINA KARŞI BİREYSEL VE TOPLUMSAL MUHALEFET (1932–1938)
abstract: Bu çalışma, Türkçe ezan uygulamasına yönelik muhalefetin 1932–1938 yılları arasında ulusal basında nasıl temsil edildiğini incelemektedir. Amaçlı olarak sınırlandırılan inceleme korpusu, Cumhuriyet, Son Posta, Milliyet, Akşam, Vakit ve Tan gazetelerinde yer alan 28 haber ile Cumhurbaşkanlığı Cumhuriyet Arşivi belgelerinden oluşmaktadır. Haber, analiz birimi kabul edilmiş; kayıtlar gazete, yıl, yer, olay türü, aktör, haber çerçevesi, devlet müdahalesi ve sonuç değişkenleri bakımından nitel içerik analiziyle kodlanmıştır. Korpustaki haberlerin 23’ü 1933’e (%82,1), 12’si Son Posta’ya (%42,9), 8’i Vakit’e (%28,6) aittir; bu dengesiz dağılım, bulguların bütün basına veya topluma genellenmesini sınırlar. Haberlerde destek, kitlesel katılım ve reform söylemiyle; muhalefet ise çoğunlukla bireysel ya da sınırlı gruplar ile soruşturma, gözaltı, yargılama ve mahkûmiyet süreçleri üzerinden kurulmuştur. Sonuç olarak çalışma, toplumsal tutumların yaygınlığını değil, ulusal basının muhalefeti kamu düzeni, devlet otoritesi ve Cumhuriyet reformları ekseninde çerçeveleme biçimini ortaya koymaktadır. Altı gazeteyi aynı kodlama şemasıyla karşılaştırması ve basın temsili ile toplumsal gerçeklik arasındaki ayrımı açıkça kurması, çalışmanın özgün katkısını oluşturmaktadır.

title: Attendance Information System Success in Mandatory Use Contexts: An Integrated TAM–DeLone and McLean–TPB Framework in Higher Education
abstract: Mandatory information systems present a fundamental challenge to IS success theory: institutional enforcement guarantees usage but not acceptance, rendering conventional adoption metrics inadequate in non-voluntary contexts. This study examines the determinants of success of a mandatory mobile attendance application at a single higher education institution, investigating how technical quality dimensions and behavioral factors jointly produce user satisfaction and perceived organizational benefit. An integrated TAM–DeLone and McLean–TPB framework was tested using PLS-SEM on data collected from 140 university lecturers through an online survey. All eight hypotheses were empirically tested; seven were supported. Service quality was the strongest predictor of perceived usefulness (β = 0.399), followed by system quality (β = 0.317) and information quality (β = 0.149). Perceived usefulness (β = 0.592) and social influence (β = 0.368) significantly shaped attitude, while perceived behavioral control exerted no significant effect (β = −0.073, p = 0.299). Attitude strongly predicted user satisfaction (β = 0.825), which in turn predicted perceived net benefits (β = 0.731). This study contributes an empirically tested integrated TAM–DeLone and McLean–TPB model within a mandatory-use IS context. The findings suggest that IS success is mediated principally through psychological mechanisms r…

Multi-scale LSTM forecasting with attention-based feature fusion for anomaly detection in multivariate monitoring data
abstract: Abstract Engineering systems such as power equipment and industrial processes are monitored through multivariate time series whose anomalies appear at different temporal scales, from short fluctuations to deviations that persist over a whole operating cycle. A detector that reads a single input window has to commit to one of these scales. This paper presents MAF-LSTM, a forecasting-based anomaly detection framework in which parallel long short-term memory (LSTM) branches read input windows of different lengths, a scale-level attention module fuses their representations into a one-step-ahead forecast, and the forecasting residuals are scored with the Mahalanobis distance estimated on normal validation data. Experiments on smart meter data, two sets of high-voltage converter modulator pulses and a simulated chemical process show that MAF-LSTM achieves the highest AU-ROC and AU-PR of the five compared methods on all four datasets, exceeding the best baseline by 3.20 and 5.33 percentage points on average. An ablation study on the smart meter data quantifies the contribution of each component and shows that multi-scale modeling is most beneficial for anomalies with pronounced within-day fluctuation, where it matches or exceeds the best single-window model on each anomaly type without requiring the window length to be tuned.

title: Forecasting Weekly Influenza Detections in South Africa Using SARIMA and LSTM Models
abstract: This study compares Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models for forecasting weekly laboratory influenza detections in South Africa using World Health Organization (WHO) FluNet surveillance data. Weekly laboratory detection counts from January 1997 to March 2026 were preprocessed, regularized, and treated for missing values, yielding 1,522 weekly observations. Data were divided chronologically into training (20 January 1997–11 May 2020; 1,217 weeks) and a fixed-holdout test period (18 May 2020–16 March 2026; 305 weeks). SARIMA incorporated a 52-week seasonal period, while LSTM used a 52-week lookback window with Min–Max scaling fitted exclusively to training data. A Seasonal Naïve model with a 52-week seasonal lag was included as a benchmark. Forecast performance was assessed using RMSE and MAE, while Diebold–Mariano (DM) test assessed differences in forecast accuracy. LSTM achieved the lowest errors, with RMSE of 9.49 and MAE of 6.31, compared with 23.58 and 15.56 for SARIMA and 29.93 and 16.02 for Seasonal Naïve, respectively. Relative to SARIMA, LSTM reduced RMSE and MAE by 59.8% and 59.4%. DM tests indicated significantly lower forecast loss for LSTM than SARIMA using MSE (DM = 6.6661, p < 0.001) and MAE (DM = 9.7569, p < 0.001). The study provides an empirical comparison of statistical and deep-learning approaches …

Leakage-controlled Crowdfunding Success Prediction: Do Feature Selection and SMOTE Improve Boosting-Based Models?
abstract: Decision-making in digital financial information systems plays an important role in predicting crowdfunding success for investors, platform providers, and campaign creators. Ignoring data imbalance and the potential for information leaks in the pursuit of high accuracy actually backfires. This kind of approach creates the illusion of performance that looks perfect on paper but is actually unreliable in practice. This study proposes a leakage-controlled framework that combines Hybrid Feature Selection, RFECV, SMOTE, and boosting algorithms using a public Turkish crowdfunding dataset. The dataset contains 76.9% unsuccessful and 23.1% successful campaigns. Pearson Correlation and Mutual Information were used for feature selection, followed by RFECV for feature optimization. The data splitting stage was intentionally completed before feature filtering, and class balancing via SMOTE was applied only to the training data set to ensure that the evaluation remained objective without data leakage. Separate data testing showed that the XGB configuration, supported by GBM-RFECV and SMOTE, achieved the best results Precision, Recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and PR_AUC of 0.871, 0.906, 0.888, 0.975, 0,923, along side minority successful campaign. title: Software Defect Prediction: A Systematic Review and a Conceptual Framework for Stable, Actionable Explanations (AISD-F)
abstract: Machine learning-based Software Defect Prediction (SDP) has largely focused on improving prediction accuracy, but recent research has placed greater emphasis on making predictions understandable and useful to developers. This systematic review examines the use of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in SDP and the evidence supporting its reliability in practice. Following PRISMA guidelines, 40 peer-reviewed studies, primarily published between 2020 and 2025, were selected from IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and Scopus. The studies were examined in terms of XAI methods, explanation reliability and stability, dataset quality, and model selection. LIME and SHAP were the most frequently used methods, yet multi-run evaluations showed changes in their feature rankings across configurations, in contrast to the reliability reported by many single-run studies. Data-quality problems, particularly SZZ-related label noise, class imbalance, and multicollinearity, often had a greater effect on prediction reliability than model architecture. The review also found growing use of line-level and just-in-time prediction, although consistent validation at industrial scale remains limited. title: From Random Splits to Unseen Solvents: Quantum-Chemistry-Derived Surface Descriptors Improve Solubility Prediction
abstract: Abstract Solvent screening often requires predictions for solvents that are absent from the training data. Using 103,262 aligned BigSolDB v2.1 records, we constructed a fixed solvent-level OOD benchmark in which five solvent identities were excluded from model training, validation, early stopping, SHAP ranking, and feature selection. A compact RDKit two-dimensional baseline reaches an IID R2 = 0.954 ± 0.001 under random splitting but falls to an OOD R2 = 0.541 ± 0.019 on the held-out solvents. Under the same benchmark, adding Gasteiger charge proxies and monomer-level GFN2-xTB/COSMO σ-moment surface descriptors raises the OOD R2 to 0.756 ± 0.007. A validation-selected 47-feature representation that also includes deterministic solute–solvent compatibility features reaches an OOD R2 = 0.788 ± 0.008, an MAE = 0.413, and an RMSE = 0.574 log10 S unit under the 20-seed protocol. The improvement depends on solvent identity: DMSO, NMP, and cyclohexane show the largest error reductions, ethylene glycol changes little, and n-propyl acetate is slightly worse than the electrostatic baseline. Learner controls and pair-xTB calculations are used as supporting checks; optimized 1:1 dimers and small 1:2/2:1 clusters do not improve the fixed-OOD result. title: Climate-Driven Poverty Prediction in Nusa Tenggara Timur Using Transfer Learning-Based CNN-LSTM and ERA5-Land
abstract: Poverty dynamics in Nusa Tenggara Timur (NTT), Indonesia, are influenced by climate variability, particularly rainfall deficits and drought, which increase household economic vulnerability. This study develops a transfer learning-based Hybrid CNN-LSTM model to predict the annual poverty headcount ratio (%) across 22 regencies/municipalities in NTT. ERA5-Land monthly total precipitation and annual regency-level poverty data from 2003–2024 were integrated, yielding 484 regency-year observations. To address limited local time-series data, the CNN was pretrained on long-term ERA5-Land climate sequences and transferred to the NTT task, while the LSTM and output layers were fine-tuned using local data. The model achieved R² = 0.87 and outperformed standalone CNN and LSTM models. A 6–12-month lagged association between rainfall deficits and subsequent poverty changes was also identified, suggesting a potential anticipatory climate signal rather than direct causality. The findings highlight the potential of integrating climate reanalysis, transfer learning, and deep learning for poverty-risk prediction in data-constrained regions. However, further operational, institutional, and external validation is required before deployment for decision support.

title: Cost-Sensitive Ensemble Models for Microcredit Risk Prediction: A Comparative Evaluation
abstract: Microcredit risk prediction is challenged by class imbalance and asymmetric misclassification costs. This study evaluates cost-sensitive ensemble models and examines model-selection stability across heterogeneous credit sources. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost were evaluated on one operational microcredit portfolio and three public credit datasets using development-only preprocessing, class-balanced fitting weights, and leakage controls. Model and threshold selection used validation data with a five-to-one false-negative cost ratio and minimum specificity of 0.70. XGBoost was selected for the operational, Credit Risk, and FIN ANA sources, while Logistic Regression was selected for German Credit. On the retrospectively held-out evaluation partitions, ROC-AUC values were 0.895, 0.940, 0.461, and 0.620, with recalls of 0.364, 0.839, 0.083, and 0.483, respectively. FIN ANA showed substantial degradation under broader distribution shift. The study jointly evaluates minority-class recall, asymmetric error costs, and validation-selected operating points, showing that cost-sensitive model selection is source-dependent and ROC-AUC alone is insufficient for practical risk detection. title: Correlating Delayed Emission, Blinking Mechanism, and the Quantum-Confined Stark Effect in Single Quantum Dots
abstract: Abstract Delayed emission, a long-lived nonexponential photoluminescence tail, is widely observed in quantum dots (QDs), but its microscopic origin and relationship with blinking and the quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE) remain unclear. Here, we combine single-QD spectroscopy, time-gated photon analysis, and Monte Carlo simulations across CsPbX3 perovskite, CdSe-based, and InP-based QDs to identify a potential mechanism. Delayed emission correlates with band-edge carrier-trapping blinking, but is weak in QDs dominated by trion-mediated Auger blinking, suggesting delayed emission is not universally tied to charge-separated states. Delayed photons originate from nanosecond-scale carrier trapping and detrapping at nonradiative recombination centers: transiently trapped carriers return to the band edge and recombine radiatively. Time-gated analysis distinguishes this process from QCSE-driven intensity-lifetime fluctuations on slower blinking time scales. Furthermore, we demonstrate that delayed photons compromise the single-photon purity at a fixed excitation repetition rate. These findings establish a general framework of delayed emission in QDs.

BRICS Pay as a Mechanism for Developing Financial and Economic Cooperation between Russia and the BRICS Countries amid the Transformation of the Global Financial Architecture
abstract: The article assesses the economic implications of the potential introduction of BRICS Pay for Russian participants in foreign economic activity. The study does not focus on replacing the existing global financial architecture. Instead, it addresses a narrower question: what volume of financial resources could be released through lower cross-border settlement costs. The research is based on official foreign trade statistics, materials on the development of BRICS Pay, a comparison of existing payment mechanisms, and scenario modelling. The calculations cover Russia’s trade with China, India, and Brazil in 2025. In the baseline scenario, total current cross-border payment costs are assumed to equal 3.3 percent of the transaction value, including bank fees, foreign exchange spreads, and operational and sanctions-related risks. The cost of settlement through BRICS Pay is treated as a scenario parameter. In the baseline case, it is set at 0.1 percent. With total trade turnover of USD 309 billion, the estimated annual savings amount to approximately USD 9.9 billion. The estimated amount should not be interpreted as an increase in GDP, since no new value added is created. Rather, the calculation reflects a potential reduction in aggregate payment costs associated with the foreign trade operations under consideration.
