In the synthetic biology era, engineered fungi could mitigate carbon dioxide emissions and enhance environmental resilience
abstract: Abstract Over the past two decades, there has been a staggering increase in greenhouse gas emissions, particularly carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from unrestrained anthropogenic activities, leading to notable environmental shifts. Despite continuous efforts to reduce emissions, the world is not making satisfactory progress, which calls for immediate action to implement alternative strategies to enhance environmental sustainability. The Earth naturally absorbs and stores carbon through various processes, but merely keeping pace with ongoing human activities is no longer sufficient. Land plants and marine prokaryotes absorb CO 2 during photosynthesis and store carbon as biomass. Eukaryotic organisms also represent a valuable resource that can provide insights into the biological fixation and removal of atmospheric CO 2 . Expanding the capacities of Earth’s natural systems offers enormous potential for enhancing carbon sinks and promoting environmental resilience. Although extensive synthetic engineering of plant systems has been conducted to enhance their native carbon fixation pathways, research on microorganisms, especially fungi, has been limited. In this review, we specifically explore the role of soil-borne fungi in carbon management, elucidating their responses to environmental shifts and their potential for climate change mitigation. Beyond the B60 Ambition: Can Indonesia's Palm Oil Biodiesel Expansion Deliver Inclusive Prosperity for Independent Smallholders?
abstract: Indonesia's ambition to advance its palm oil-based biodiesel programme toward B60 represents a significant opportunity to strengthen energy sovereignty, reduce dependence on imported diesel, and expand domestic value creation. However, whether this ambition can simultaneously improve the welfare of independent oil palm smallholders remains uncertain. This article critically examines the economic, institutional, agronomic, social, and environmental conditions under which B60 implementation could deliver inclusive and sustainable rural prosperity. Employing a qualitative literature review rather than a systematic literature review, the study synthesises interdisciplinary research published between 2020 and 2026, complemented by relevant policy documents. Six nterconnected themes emerge: energy and fiscal feasibility; value-chain transmission and distributive equity; productivity and replanting constraints; institutional inclusion; environmental sustainability; and livelihood resilience. The synthesis suggests that higher biodiesel demand does not automatically translate into improved smallholder welfare because benefits are mediated by pricing structures, market access, productivity, financing, and institutional arrangements. Design and Construction of a Low-Cost, Open-Source Syringe-Based Pipetting Robot Using 3D Printing and Common Hardware Parts
abstract: Abstract Automation in chemical laboratories improves the reproducibility, precision, and efficiency in liquid handling. A three-dimensional (3D)-printed, stepper-actuated pipetting robot was developed and tested via silver nitrate (AgNO3) experiments. The system employs a rigid 3D-printed frame to secure syringes and tubing, stepper motors for plunger actuation, and microcontroller-based software to automate the pipetting sequences. The robot was evaluated for volume accuracy, reproducibility, and mechanical reliability using 5 mL syringes. The results indicate consistent volume delivery and stable mechanical performance over multiple cycles. Detailed mechanical, electrical, and software specifications are provided to enable replication and customization in other laboratories.

Design and Validation of a Dual-MAF Weighted SRF-PLL Control Strategy with Optimization-Based PI Gains for Three- Phase DSTATCOM Applications
abstract: This paper suggests a Dual–Moving Average Filter (Dual-MAF) Weighted Synchronous Reference Frame Phase-Locked Loop (SRF-PLL) control algorithm combined with optimization-based PI regulation for a three-phase Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM) operating under distorted and unbalanced grid conditions. The Dual-MAF structure selectively filters the harmonic components and provides improved estimation of the in-phase and quadrature signals before the SRF processing. It enhances the phase tracking accuracy, suppresses the oscillatory terms and improves the synchronization stability of the grid voltage with low-order and high-order harmonics. The weighted SRF-PLL enhances the phase-angle calculation by mixing fast and slow filtering paths dynamically. To achieve consistent regulation performance, the controller gains of Proportional-Integral (PI) for DC-bus voltage loop and AC-bus voltage loop are optimized by a bandwidth-oriented optimization PI tuning method. This results in faster transient response, improved damping, and increased robustness across varying grid impedances. A laboratory-developed Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)-based DSTATCOM prototype is used to validate the proposed method, and experimental results confirm substantial improvements in reference-current tracking, harmonic reduction, and compensation stability under dynamic operating conditions.

title: Visualize explore diagnose reflect (VEDR): design and pilot evaluation of a needs-based instructional model for computer hardware concepts
abstract: Mobile resources for computer hardware learning are usually developed as media products without an explicit instructional sequence. This design and development study, guided by the ADDIE framework, designed and pilot-evaluated an instructional model whose syntax, Visualize, Explore, Diagnose, and Reflect (VEDR), was derived from multimedia learning and cognitive load theory, constructivist exploration, diagnostic problem solving, and feedback-driven reflection, with an Android application as its support system. Needs were analysed with questionnaires from 90 students and three lecturers and an observation of the learning environment; three experts validated the prototype; and one intact class of 40 first-semester students completed a ten-item concept test before and after implementation. Initial understanding of hardware concepts was the students' weakest indicator (72.22%), and facilities and laboratory the lecturers' weakest (66.67%). Experts rated the design of the model's intended effects as highly valid (Aiken's V = 0.972). The class mean rose from 48.6 to 76.3, a moderate class-average normalized gain (Hake) of 0.54. The study contributes a pilot-tested instructional sequence that links each phase to a documented need and a theoretical principle; its effect relative to conventional instruction remains to be tested in a controlled study.

abstract: Data Desa Presisi integrates narrative village monographs and structured census records, creating challenges for contextual, numerical, and cross-source information access. This study designed and evaluated a locally deployed, route-aware, evidence-grounded retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chatbot that combines deterministic DuckDB queries, document retrieval, provenance, and privacy-aware routing. Evaluation used 100 ground-truth questions from Setu and Gunung Putri. Eighty-four database, monograph, and mixed-evidence questions were assessed using RAGAS and ROUGE-L, whereas 16 conversational and policy questions were evaluated through deterministic checks. Elasticsearch at a temperature of 0.1 produced the highest composite score (0.592018), although post hoc Wilcoxon tests found no statistically significant superiority over alternative configurations. The selected configuration achieved a 98.0% functional pass rate and a 97.92% numeric-match rate. Public-mode usability evaluation involving 21 village officials and staff yielded 96.03% effectiveness. Scalability testing covered pipeline construction and retrieval across 30 census inputs and 28 monographs, but did not assess concurrent users or full end-to-end production workloads. These findings provide preliminary evidence that route-aware RAG can improve transparent, evidence-grounded access to heterogeneous village data…

Y-Learn: Design and Initial Implementation of an OBE-Based Learning Platform for Group Work Monitoring and Peer Review Assessment
abstract: Group assignments often preserve the submitted product more clearly than individual participation. Y-Learn was developed to retain member-attributed contributions alongside peer records, lecturer decisions, and Outcome-Based Education (OBE) information. Using Design Science Research, requirements were derived from course outcomes, Sub-CPMK/Sub-CLO structures, assessment documents, development records, and issues observed during teaching use. The native Android artifact uses Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Firebase Authentication, and Cloud Firestore. Evaluation combined repository inspection, automated technical checks, production-console evidence, three course analytics exports, and a later black-box cycle. Version 3.3 recorded 24 passing unit tests and 10 passing governance-rule scenarios; version 3.4 was subsequently released and examined through an additional black-box evaluation. PAR 102, SFT 106, and SFT 210 contained 39, 42, and 39 normalised OBE evidence records, with assessment coverage of 48.7%, 100%, and 100%. Peer-review activity varied substantially, and unresolved records remained visible. No formal usability study, peer-score reliability analysis, or learning-outcome impact evaluation was conducted. The contribution is an implemented artifact and a traceability mechanism connecting activities, member contributions, peer evidence, and lecturer-controlled assessment.

abstract: Background: Indonesia’s Electricity Supply Business Plan (RUPTL) 2025–2034 sets ambitious renewable energy targets, yet project realization remains substantially below plan. Between 2021 and 2024, only 1,606.18 MW of the 5,096 MW target reached Commercial Operation Date, while only 8.34% of capacity entering procurement initiation during 2021–2025 progressed to Power Purchase Agreement signing. Objective: This study aims to identify the principal factors associated with renewable energy procurement bottlenecks at PT PLN (Persero), examine stakeholder perceptions of the current procurement process, and prioritize an appropriate procurement strategy to support RUPTL implementation. Methods: This study employed a mixed-methods approach that included performance gap analysis, the Kepner–Tregoe method, the fishbone diagram, SWOT–PESTEL analysis, a purposive survey of 24 respondents, and AHP. The AHP assessment involved 12 internal experts from PLN, with 10 experts retained in the final analysis after two respondents were excluded for failing to meet the consistency threshold (CR ≤ 0.10). The strategic priorities were then tested through a sensitivity analysis. Results: The analysis identified fragmented project-by-project procurement and the relatively small scale of individual projects as primary controllable factors associated with low procurement conversion. title: Modern US Foreign Economic Policy: From Targeted Protectionism to a Systemic Geoeconomic Strategy
abstract: Amid mounting geopolitical turbulence and the global economy’s shift from liberal globalization to a model of fragmented blocs, US foreign economic policy is undergoing a fundamental transformation. Donald Trump’s return to the White House in 2025 marked a qualitative leap in the implementation of the “America First” doctrine: protectionist instruments, previously applied in a targeted manner, have become systemic and expanded to new areas — from cryptocurrencies to critical minerals. The purpose of this paper is to identify the key features of US foreign economic policy in Donald Trump’s second term, systematize its toolkit, and assess its long-term geoeconomic consequences. The methodological framework is based on a systems approach, comparative institutional analysis, and content analysis of strategic documents. The empirical base is comprised of official White House materials, industry reports, and publications from leading think tanks. The study establishes that the Trump administration is implementing a three-pronged strategy: tariff pressure as a permanent negotiating tool, cryptocurrency expansion to extend the life cycle of dollar hegemony, and accelerated import substitution in the critical minerals sector. The study demonstrates the decisive role of the Project 2025 policy document, which, despite the president’s public denials, serves as a practical guide to action.…

title: Effect of pulse targeting strategy on Er:YAG laser ablation rate and efficiency in ex vivo cancellous bone
abstract: Abstract Purpose Lasers are an attractive alternative to mechanical tools for bone preparation, but clinical adoption is limited by low removal rates. This study investigated whether spatiotemporal sequencing of Er:YAG pulses can improve thermomechanical bone ablation, and how pulse separation and delivery order affect ablation rate, efficiency, and heating. Methods A prototype Er:YAG system, with galvanometer scanning, ablated cancellous bone in eight ex vivo lamb femurs. Arm 1 varied the separation between consecutive pulses (0.175 to 0.275 mm). Arm 2 compared four targeting patterns within a fixed pulse grid, maintaining constant fluence and total energy for three of the four patterns. Thermal imaging and pre/post confocal scans quantified heating and volumetric removal. Results Ablation rate was consistent across pulse separations (521 to 552mm 3 /min), while layer depth scaled linearly with deposited energy (R 2 = 0.94), decoupling depth control from throughput. Targeting strategy significantly affected ablation efficiency, ranging from 0.19–0.32mm 3 /J ( p < 0.001). Hatching was fastest and most efficient, sustaining consistently high peak surface temperatures (200–250 °C) but lower mean surface temperatures than either scatter strategy. Conclusion Ablation efficiency varied with pulse order under controlled conditions, indicating a dependence beyond single pulse dynamics…

title: Mapping Artificial Intelligence for Personalised Learning based on Learning Style: Scopus-Based Bibliometric Analysis (2006-2026)
abstract: The aims of this study is to conduct a bibliometric analysis of the development of learning style-based personalisation. The rapid advancement of AI-based learning personalisation has been accompanied by growing research attention to the role of learning style in the modern learning ecosystem. The research methodology involves a bibliometric analysis of 604 Scopus-indexed publications from the period 2006 to 2026 that were analyzed and visualized using Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and Open Refine. The results of the study indicate a significant increase in publications beginning in 2020, reflecting growing research attention to AI-based personalisation., the keywords patterns indicate an increasing association between learning style and machine learning analytics. Random Forest is one of the most commonly reported machine learning methods in the literature to identify learning styles. The findings further indicate that AI and learning style are increasingly discussed with the same research landscape. This study contributes by mapping the evolution of this field and demonstrating the convergence of educational theory and computational approaches. Further research should be extended beyond the Scopus database, combining bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review, and investigating the integration of learning styles with learner behavioral and cognitive data in AI-powered pe…

title: Evaluating Xception with Multitask Self-Supervised Learning for AI-Generated Image and Deepfake Video Detection
abstract: This study evaluates an Xception-based Multitask Self-Supervised Learning (MSSL) framework for detecting real and synthetic visual content across image and video modalities. Separate models were developed for CIFAKE images and FaceForensics++ videos. Beyond the primary binary-classification objective, MSSL integrates three auxiliary representation-learning tasks: rotation prediction, patch reconstruction, and artifact-map prediction. These tasks are intended to encourage the model to learn robust semantic and manipulation-related visual features. Experiments used class-balanced subsets of 5,000 CIFAKE images and 840 FaceForensics++ videos. For video classification, five frames were selected through uniform temporal sampling, and frame-level probabilities were averaged to obtain video-level predictions; a three-frame setting was also examined. A fixed decision threshold of 0.50 was defined a priori and applied consistently across both modalities. On CIFAKE, Xception+MSSL achieved 92.60% accuracy and 0.9797 ROC-AUC, outperforming the baseline Xception model, which obtained 79.60% accuracy and 0.8937 ROC-AUC. On FaceForensics++, five-frame MSSL achieved 68.25% video-level accuracy and 0.7365 ROC-AUC, compared with 62.70% and 0.6652 for Xception. The results indicate consistent within-dataset improvements, although cross-dataset and cross-generator generalization remain unverified.

title: Predicting Backup Non-Compliance Using KPI-Derived Labels and Machine Learning: A Proof-of-Concept Study
abstract: Ensuring backup compliance is essential for data protection and operational resilience in enterprise IT environments. This study proposes a KPI-aware machine learning approach combining weak supervision, rule-based labeling, and supervised learning to estimate KPI-derived backup non-compliance status. The approach was evaluated on 439 device instances with 33 features using an 80:20 stratified split, producing a test set of 88 instances comprising 86 non-compliant and only 2 compliant proxy labels, indicating extreme class imbalance. Proxy labels were generated from predefined KPI rules without manual annotation or independent compliance audits. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost were evaluated using AUC-PR, F1-score, recall, Brier score, and calibration analysis. Random Forest achieved the strongest comparative results, with an AUC-PR of 0.998, F1-score of 0.994, recall of 1.000, and the lowest Brier score of 0.014. However, calibration remains uncertain because only two compliant instances were available. Therefore, these results indicate preliminary feasibility for reproducing or estimating KPI-derived proxy labels and should not be interpreted as independent validation of real-world non-compliance detection. The approach provides a scalable basis for backup compliance monitoring and preliminary risk prioritization in enterprise IT systems.

Methods: This study employed a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were collected through participatory observation, semi-structured interviews with students, parents, and the school principal, and documentation. Data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. Method and source triangulation were applied to enhance the credibility of the findings. Results: The “Kipas Eco Craft” project integrated all five STEAM components through contextual learning activities. Online learning was used for concept exploration and product design, while face-to-face sessions focused on assembly, testing, and product refinement. Students demonstrated enthusiasm, collaboration skills, participation in design decision-making, and increased awareness of plastic waste. The challenges included limited digital devices and internet connectivity, restricted face-to-face learning time, work safety considerations, and differences in work pace among groups. title: Evaluation of TF-IDF and Word2Vec Representations Using Support Vector Machine for Multiclass Product Category Classification of Tokopedia Reviews
abstract: As electronic commerce continues to expand, customer reviews have become an important source for automated text classification. This research evaluates and compares TF-IDF and Word2Vec representations for multiclass product category classification with Support Vector Machine (SVM). The experiment used the Tokopedia Product Reviews 2025 dataset containing 65,543 reviews across six product categories. After text preprocessing and keyword-based text refinement, 11,239 relevant reviews were retained. The dataset was divided into 80% training sets and 20% hold-out test sets. The reviews were transformed using TF-IDF and Word2Vec, while SMOTE was applied to the training data to handle the imbalance among product categories. Classification performance was assessed through five-fold cross-validation and a hold-out test set based on accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, and macro F1-score. Five-fold cross-validation showed that TF-IDF achieved mean accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, and macro F1-score of 95.95%, 93.13%, 92.78%, and 92.93%, respectively, compared with 90.80%, 84.58%, 86.02%, and 85.19% for Word2Vec. On the hold-out test set, TF-IDF achieved 95.42% accuracy and 91.88% macro F1-score, while Word2Vec achieved 91.01% and 84.91%, respectively. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test yielded a p-value of 0.0625, indicating no statistically significant difference at the 5% signi…

title: Effects of Adversarial Training of Word Embeddings on Chinese Agricultural Pest and Disease Named Entity Recognition with BERT-CRF
abstract: Entity boundaries, confusable entity types and surface forms absent from the training data all make it harder to extract structured information from agricultural pest and disease texts. We examined whether single-step adversarial training of word embeddings with the fast gradient method (FGM) improves entity recognition when the BERT-CRF inference architecture is left unchanged. On the official 13-type AgCNER corpus, with exact matching of character span and entity type, we compared a feature-based CRF, BiLSTM-CRF, BERT-CRF and BERT-CRF+FGM, training each neural model with three fixed random seeds. BERT-CRF+FGM reached mean test precision, recall and F1 of 94.37%, 95.10% and 94.73%. Its F1 was 0.28 percentage points higher than that of the matched BERT-CRF baseline, and the paired difference was positive for every seed. F1 on unseen surface forms rose from 74.87% to 76.41%, and the overall gain remained 0.27 percentage points after test texts duplicated in other splits were removed. Mean F1 increased for 11 of the 13 types but fell for Company and Organization. FGM did not change the parameter count. The seed-42 model produced 20,670 indexed entity occurrences that can be checked against the released records and character spans. The official test set had been used in an earlier baseline study and test results informed model adoption, so these findings are exploratory; independe…

title: A Discovery-Based Learning Model Focused on ‎Higher-Order Thinking Skills in Aqidah Akhlak ‎Instruction to Enhance Students’ Emotional and ‎Spiritual Intelligence ‎
abstract: This study aims to develop and evaluate the validity, practicality, and effectiveness of a HOTS-oriented Inquiry-Based Discovery Learning (IDL) model in the teaching of Aqidah Akhlak to enhance students’ higher-order thinking skills and emotional-spiritual intelligence. This study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using a modified Borg & Gall model. The research subjects included teachers and students at a public Madrasah Aliyah in Pesisir Selatan Regency. Data were collected through observation, interviews, expert validation, a practicality questionnaire, and pre- and post-tests following the implementation of the model. Qualitative data were analyzed descriptively, while quantitative data were analyzed using Aiken’s V, the practicality percentage, the paired-sample t-test, and N-Gain. The results of the study indicate that the HOTS-based IDL model meets validity criteria with Aiken’s V values ranging from 0.77 to 0.82, is practical with a practicality level of 79.32%–80.25%, and is effective based on N-Gain values ranging from 0.38 to 0.86, which fall into the moderate to high category. The implementation of this model has proven effective in enhancing students’ analytical, evaluative, and creative abilities while strengthening their emotional and spiritual intelligence through active and reflective learning grounded in Islamic values. title: PENGEMBANGAN KOLEKSI BUKU KEAGAMAAN DI PERPUSTAKAAN MBS KERTEK WONOSOBO UNTUK MENDUKUNG PEMBELAJARAN PAI
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengembangan koleksi buku keagamaan di Perpustakaan MBS Kertek Wonosobo dalam mendukung proses pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI). Pengembangan koleksi merupakan salah satu aspek penting dalam pengelolaan perpustakaan karena berperan dalam menyediakan sumber informasi yang relevan dengan kebutuhan pengguna. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah pendekatan kualitatif dengan teknik pengumpulan data melalui observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengembangan koleksi buku keagamaan dilakukan melalui proses seleksi, pengadaan, pengelolaan, dan evaluasi koleksi yang disesuaikan dengan kebutuhan peserta didik dan guru. Keberadaan koleksi buku keagamaan yang memadai memberikan kontribusi positif terhadap peningkatan kualitas pembelajaran PAI, terutama dalam memperluas wawasan keislaman dan mendukung kegiatan belajar mandiri siswa. Dengan demikian, pengembangan koleksi buku keagamaan di Perpustakaan MBS Kertek Wonosobo memiliki peran yang penting dalam menunjang efektivitas pembelajaran Pendidikan Agama Islam.

title: A Project-Based Learning (PjBL) Model Rooted in Local History to Enhance Students’ Critical Thinking Skills and Creativity in High School: A Literature Review
abstract: History learning in high school requires learning experiences that do not merely emphasize memorization but also develop students’ critical thinking and creativity. Project-Based Learning (PjBL) provides opportunities for students to investigate authentic problems, collaborate, produce products, and reflect on their learning. However, the integration of local history into PjBL to simultaneously support critical thinking and creativity has not been sufficiently synthesized in history education. This literature review aims to synthesize previous studies concerning the potential of local-history-based PjBL for developing high school students’ critical thinking and creativity. The study employed a literature review method by analyzing relevant national and international scholarly publications concerning PjBL, local history learning, critical thinking, and creativity. The literature was analyzed descriptively and thematically by identifying recurring findings, learning characteristics, implementation strategies, and educational implications. The synthesis of the reviewed literature indicates that local-history-based PjBL can connect historical content with students’ surrounding environment while encouraging investigation, source analysis, problem solving, product creation, presentation, and reflection. These activities provide complementary opportunities for developing critical thin…

title: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Difficulty Disengaging from Social Media Among Students
abstract: Social media use can adversely affect students’ academic functioning and psychological well-being when disengagement becomes difficult. This study compared Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) for predicting self-reported difficulty disengaging from social media among university students. A cross-sectional survey dataset comprising 118 responses was analyzed, including 75 positive (63.6%) and 43 negative (36.4%) cases. The binary target represented a behavioral proxy rather than a clinically validated diagnosis of social media addiction. Using balanced class weighting and 10-fold stratified cross-validation, SVM achieved the highest mean accuracy (77.2%) and ROC-AUC (0.804), followed by RF (73.0%) and XGBoost (66.8%). However, the performance difference between SVM and RF was not statistically significant (Nadeau–Bengio corrected *p* = 0.102), while RF demonstrated greater resampling stability. The findings provide preliminary evidence for algorithm selection in behavioral proxy classification and support future digital well-being research. Interpretation is limited by the small, single-institution sample and single-item outcome measure; therefore, the results should not be used for clinical screening or institutional deployment without external validation using established psychometric instruments.
venue: Journal of Information Systems and Informatics

title: A Computer Vision-Based Framework for Multilevel Egg Fertility Classification Using L*a*b* Color Segmentation, Wavelet Texture Features, and Support Vector Machine
abstract: Egg fertility assessment is essential for improving hatchery efficiency, reducing incubation costs, and minimizing resource waste caused by infertile eggs. This study aims to develop a computer vision-based framework for three-level egg fertility classification, namely Highly Fertile, Fertile, and Infertile. A balanced dataset consisting of 1,500 manually collected candling images (500 images per class) was validated by three poultry experts. The proposed method involves L*a*b* color-space transformation, K-Means clustering for region-of-interest segmentation, Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) using the LL sub-band for texture feature extraction, and multiclass Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification. The experimental results show that the proposed model achieves 90.9% training accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-score of 92.0%, 90.9%, and 90.5%, respectively. For the independent testing dataset, the model achieves 89.7% accuracy and 89.4% F1-score, indicating good generalization capability with only a 1.2% difference between training and testing accuracy. The novelty of this research is the development of a three-level egg fertility classification framework that extends conventional binary fertility detection by integrating L*a*b*-based segmentation, LL-wavelet statistical texture features, and multiclass SVM classification.
venue: Journal of Information Systems and Informatics

title: Deep Learning-Based Object Detection for Fashion, Uniform, and PPE Items: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Deep learning-based object detection for clothing and uniform items spans two research streams: fashion and apparel detection for e-commerce, and personal protective equipment (PPE) compliance detection for occupational safety. No prior review has jointly synthesized these streams with a detection-centric scope. This study addresses that gap through a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic literature review of 1,378 records from Scopus as the sole database, identified via two Boolean queries and screened for object detection or instance segmentation of clothing, uniform, or PPE items, yielding 26 empirical studies published between 2021 and 2026. One-stage YOLO-based detectors dominate the corpus (18 of 26 studies, up to 96.9% mAP50 at 7.3 ms inference), a dominance partly attributable to an architectural constraint in the PPE-domain search query; two-stage R-CNN and transformer-based architectures remain comparatively underexplored, the latter represented by only two studies. Dataset scale is markedly asymmetric between public fashion benchmarks (up to 491,895 images) and PPE-specific collections (as few as 1,330 images), though an emerging benchmark-reuse pattern partly offsets this gap within the PPE domain. This review contributes a cross-domain synthesis benchmarked against five prior reviews, an explicit architecture-dataset-metric mapping, a proposed nine-element minimum reportin…

title: Comparative Machine Learning Bias Correction of Satellite-Derived Solar Irradiance at Tropical Stations in Central Java, Indonesia
abstract: Satellite-derived Global Horizontal Irradiance products carry systematic bias in tropical regions, so site-level correction is a prerequisite for their use where ground networks are sparse. This study compares bias-correction methods for NASA POWER daily irradiance in Central Java, Indonesia, and asks how much reported accuracy reflects algebraic dependence between predictors and the ground reference. Ten PUSDATARU stations were analysed over 2020–2024 (17,072 station-days; 8,459 from five exactly co-located stations). Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Elastic Net, and Quantile Mapping were trained chronologically (2020–2022/2023/2024) against persistence and climatology baselines, with preprocessing fitted on training data only, paired significance tests, leave-one-station-out validation, and SHAP attribution. Random Forest reduced RMSE from 3.398 to 2.674 MJ m⁻² day⁻¹ (21.3%), lowered mean bias from 0.988 to 0.221, and raised R² from 0.266 to 0.546; across ten stations XGBoost reduced error from 5.921 to 2.831. Differences among tree ensembles were not statistically robust, and the weighted ensemble gave no gain at the highest inference cost. Adding ground-observed sunshine as a predictor raised the coefficient of determination to 0.9994, identified as recovery of the Ångström–Prescott expression defining the reference (70.9% attribution). Near-perfect accuracies against suns…

title: Benchmarking Classical Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models on the Cleveland Heart Disease Binary Classification Dataset
abstract: Many high-stakes applications relied on binary classification, yet practitioners lacked equitable, methodical benchmarks that evaluated diverse model families under identical conditions. This study used the Cleveland Heart Disease tabular dataset to conduct a controlled, empirical benchmark of a regularised linear model (Ridge Classifier), tree-based ensembles (XGBoost, Random Forest), and a hybrid deep learning architecture combining Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory and Convolutional Neural Network layers (BiLSTM-CNN) on a mildly imbalanced binary classification task. A strict protocol was applied, comprising uniform pre-processing, Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) applied to training folds only, a hybrid hold-out design with internal five-fold stratified crossvalidation on the training set (70%), and evaluation using accuracy, positive-class precision, recall, F1 score, and area under the curve (AUC) on a fixed test set (15%). Cross-validation results showed that no single model dominated every metric: the Ridge Classifier unexpectedly achieved the best AUC (0.8945), indicating strong ranking ability; Random Forest and XGBoost achieved the highest accuracy (81.67%); and the BiLSTM-CNN hybrid achieved the highest recall and F1 score (0.8478 and 0.8365, respectively). These findings indicated that, for this dataset, classical and ensemble approaches remaine…
venue: Journal of Information Systems and Informatics

title: AI-Driven Dynamic Trust in Zero Trust Architecture: A Systematic Literature Review of Machine Learning, Federated Learning and Governance Challenges
abstract: Sophisticated cyber threats have exposed the limits of perimeter-based security models, and Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) has increasingly been adopted as an alternative paradigm. Purpose: This Systematic Literature Review examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) within Zero Trust frameworks, covering dynamic trust scoring, behavioural analytics and federated learning, the latter treated as one strand of AI rather than a separate paradigm. Following PRISMA 2020, 22 studies published between 2022 and 2025 were identified across IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, SpringerLink, MDPI and Nature/Scientific Reports, appraised against a five-criterion quality instrument and synthesised narratively. The studies included are few and heterogeneous, and their findings should be read accordingly. Ensemble and hybrid designs predominate (14 of 22). Twelve studies report quantitative results, of which only eight evaluate on real named datasets; reported accuracies of 95 to 99 per cent come from different datasets, tasks, threat models, and evaluation settings, and are neither directly comparable nor a field-level benchmark. Only three studies directly compare learned adaptive trust against a static rule-based baseline. No study reports live operational deployment. We identify thirteen technique categories, eleven implementation barriers, and seven eme…

When active learning fails, uncalibrated out of distribution uncertainty quantification might be the problem
abstract: Abstract Efficiently and meaningfully estimating prediction uncertainty is important for exploration in active learning campaigns in materials discovery, where samples with high uncertainty are interpreted as containing information missing from the model. In this work, the effect of different uncertainty estimation and calibration methods are evaluated for active learning when using ensembles of ALIGNN, eXtreme Gradient Boost, Random Forest, and Neural Network model architectures. We compare uncertainty estimates from ALIGNN deep ensembles to loss landscape uncertainty estimates obtained for solubility, bandgap, and formation energy prediction tasks. We then evaluate how the quality of the uncertainty estimate impacts an active learning campaign that seeks model generalization to out-of-distribution data. Uncertainty calibration methods were found to variably generalize from in-domain data to out-of-domain data. Furthermore, calibrated uncertainties were generally unsuccessful in reducing the amount of data required by a model to improve during an active learning campaign on out-of-distribution data when compared to random sampling and uncalibrated uncertainties. The impact of poor-quality uncertainty persists for random forest and eXtreme Gradient Boosting models trained on the same data for the same tasks, indicating that this is at least partially intrinsic to the data and n…

title: An Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Symbolic-Lexicon Framework for Multi-Domain Sentiment Classification
abstract: Multi-domain sentiment classifiers may return a polarity label even when the evidence behind that decision becomes fragile under domain shift. This study evaluates an uncertainty-aware hybrid symbolic-lexicon framework designed to pair each polarity prediction with a traceable accept-or-defer status. The framework combines a lexical branch adapted only on training data with training-only fitted symbolic feature states, variable-precision rough evidence, and nested score fusion. Evaluation uses the UCI Sentiment Labelled Sentences dataset, comprising 3,000 balanced English sentences from Amazon Cells, IMDb, and Yelp, under repeated within-source, pooled multi-domain, and leave-one-source-out protocols. In pooled evaluation, the framework achieved 83.73% accuracy and 83.76% F1-score, improving F1 by 0.50 points over the adaptive lexical branch. The boundary mechanism deferred 53.55% of cases and retained 92.54% accuracy among accepted predictions; however, matched-coverage logistic regression and SVM confidence rankings produced lower selective risk. The contribution is therefore a reproducible, algorithmically traceable polarity-and-deferment mechanism rather than a claim of universal predictive or uncertainty-ranking superiority.

Clinical efficacy of integrated Chinese-Western medicine therapy for metastatic colorectal cancer
abstract: BACKGROUND Systemic treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is limited by toxicity, drug resistance, and variable patient tolerance. Integrated Chinese-Western medicine is widely used in China, but its association with survival in real-world settings requires careful evaluation. AIM To evaluate the association between integrated Chinese-Western medicine therapy and survival in patients with mCRC using a target trial emulation-informed observational design. METHODS This retrospective multicenter cohort included patients with mCRC treated from January 1, 2017, to January 1, 2026. The components of the target trial emulation were prespecified. Patients were classified according to the observed duration of oral Chinese herbal medicine use (≥ 3 months vs < 3 months). The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), and the secondary outcome was cancer-specific survival. Stabilized inverse probability weighting was used to balance measured baseline covariates. Weighted Cox models were then used to estimate survival associations. Because the groups were defined by treatment duration after baseline, the estimates were interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. RESULTS Of 649 screened patients, 627 were eligible: 490 received oral Chinese herbal medicine for ≥ 3 months, and 137 received it for < 3 months. After weighting, 259 patients in the ≥ 3-month group and 111 …

title: Integrated single-cell transcriptomic analysis of brain and lymph node metastases in non-small cell lung cancer
abstract: BACKGROUND Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and metastasis remains the primary driver of treatment failure and death. Despite recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), most studies have focused on isolated metastatic sites; there is still a lack of studies that simultaneously focus on the cellular and molecular characteristics of brain and lymph node metastases in NSCLC. AIM To explore features of brain and lymph node metastases in NSCLC and to nominate candidate pathways for subsequent functional interrogation. METHODS We integrated three public scRNA-seq datasets (GSE131907, GSE186344, and GSE256491) to construct a high-resolution transcriptomic atlas of NSCLC. These scRNA-seq cohorts were heterogeneous and not clinically matched primary-metastasis pairs, comprising a total of 45 samples (including 11 primary tumors, 7 lymph node metastases, 15 brain metastases, and 12 normal controls) and 208506 high-quality cells. We systematically dissected cellular heterogeneity, the distribution of tumor epithelial subpopulations in different metastatic sites, pathway activation, and immune microenvironment remodeling during metastasis. To assess the relationship between the expression of the tumor subclusters and overall survival of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) patients, we conducted a multivariate Cox regressi…

title: AI-Integrated Computational Framework for Pronunciation Error Analysis Through Native–Learner Speech Comparison
abstract: This study proposes an AI-integrated computational framework for pronunciation error analysis through native–learner speech comparison. The framework integrates Whisper-based Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), acoustic feature extraction, statistical analysis, and machine learning to analyze learner pronunciation. Unlike previous studies that primarily rely on individual transcription-based or acoustic measures, the proposed framework integrates multiple pronunciation indicators into a composite Pronunciation Accuracy Score (PAS) formulated in this study. The framework was evaluated using a dataset comprising 45 non-native English learners and one native English speaker. PAS combines Pronunciation Error Rate (PER), Word Error Rate (WER), Pitch Similarity, Rhythm Similarity, and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (MFCC) Similarity. Pearson correlation analysis showed that Rhythm Similarity (r = 0.544) and Pitch Similarity (r = 0.510) exhibited the strongest positive correlations with PAS, whereas Word Error Rate showed the strongest negative correlation (r = −0.495). K-Means clustering identified three learner groups with distinct pronunciation characteristics within the tested dataset. Although evaluated on a relatively small dataset without validation against expert human ratings, the proposed framework provides a promising foundation for Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Train…

title: A SHA-256 driven multi-PWLCM image encryption scheme with adaptive image-dependent permutation-diffusion
abstract: Abstract With the rapid growth of digital image transmission over open and insecure communication channels, the need for robust and computationally efficient image encryption techniques has become increasingly important. This paper presents a SHA-256-driven multi-PWLCM image encryption scheme with adaptive image-dependent permutation–diffusion for secure visual data protection. Rather than constructing a new chaotic system, the proposed framework adopts three conventional Piecewise Linear Chaotic Map (PWLCM) instances within a plaintext-dependent, functionally role-separated architecture. Plaintext-derived SHA-256 information diversifies the operational initial conditions and control parameters of the three PWLCMs, while the PWLCM instances are explicitly assigned to row permutation, XOR diffusion, and column permutation, respectively. An adaptive hash-dependent flipping mechanism further introduces image-dependent spatial transformation, while the same processing framework supports both grayscale and color images. The security behavior is evaluated through histogram and chi-square analysis, adjacent-pixel correlation, global and local information entropy, differential analysis, key sensitivity, chosen-plaintext and ciphertext-based cryptanalytic evaluations, noise and cropping robustness, and statistical randomness testing. Direct randomness evaluation of the PWLCM-generated s…

title: Image-Based Asymmetric Feature Fusion Using EfficientNet-B0 and MobileNetV3Large for Multi-Class Fish Disease Classification
abstract: This study proposes an asymmetric hybrid feature-fusion network that combines EfficientNet-B0 and MobileNetV3Large in parallel for multi-class classification of eight fish disease categories. The approach is designed to exploit the complementary feature-learning capabilities of both lightweight convolutional neural network architectures while maintaining computational efficiency for potential diagnostic applications. The model was evaluated on a public dataset of 2,400 digital images, divided into training, validation, and test sets using an 80:10:10 ratio. The held-out test set contained 240 unseen images, with 30 images representing each class. As all data partitions originated from the same dataset, the evaluation reflects performance on the same source distribution rather than external generalization. The proposed architecture fuses spatial feature representations through parallel Global Average Pooling (GAP) and Global Max Pooling (GMP) layers. Training followed a progressive two-phase strategy comprising top-layer warm-up and micro deep fine-tuning with a learning rate of \(10^{-5}\) and label smoothing. Experimental results achieved a validation accuracy of 0.9667 with a loss of 0.5843, and a test accuracy of 0.9833 with a loss of 0.5375 and a macro-average ROC-AUC of 0.9998. On an NVIDIA RTX 3080 GPU, the model recorded an average inference time of 8.61 ms per image, eq…

title: Instagram Rebranding and Corporate Digital Identity Renewal: A Case Study of @Lautanluas.id
abstract: Corporate transformation requires organizations to align their digital self-representation with changes in business positioning, yet prior studies of Instagram-based corporate communication have more often examined branding, image building, or digital public relations than the operational process through which a business-to-business company renews its digital identity. This study examines how PT Lautan Luas Tbk reconfigured its Instagram identity during its transition from a chemical company to an Integrated Ingredients and Solutions Provider. A descriptive qualitative case-study design was employed using Instagram observation during 2023–2025, semi-structured interviews with one Corporate Communications officer, and review of corporate documents. Content from the official @lautanluas.id account was coded against Muzellec et al.’s four-stage framework: repositioning, renaming, redesign, and relaunching, with cross-source comparison used to strengthen interpretation. The findings show that repositioning was enacted through a new communication direction and content pillars; the renaming stage occurred only partially and is better understood as a digital verbal-identity adjustment because the corporate name did not change; redesign standardized visual and verbal branding; and relaunching introduced the renewed Instagram identity and was reinforced through continued content managem…

title: The Effect of Profitability, Audit Opinion, Firm Size, and Leverage on the Timeliness of Financial Reporting in Manufacturing Companies Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2022–2024 Period
abstract: Timely financial reporting provides relevant information for economic decision-making, yet reporting delays remain a concern in capital markets. This study examines the associations of profitability, audit opinion, firm size, and leverage with financial reporting timeliness among manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2022–2024. A quantitative approach used secondary data comprising 303 firm-year observations, analyzed through logistic regression in SPSS. Profitability and audit opinion exhibited statistically significant associations with reporting timeliness, whereas firm size and leverage did not show significant associations within the sample. These findings identify financial performance and audit opinion as relevant correlates of timely reporting in the companies examined. The study contributes empirical evidence on financial reporting timeliness in Indonesia’s manufacturing sector and offers practical implications for corporate managers monitoring financial performance and audit processes, as well as investors evaluating corporate reporting practices. The results also provide a basis for further research on the determinants of timely financial reporting.

title: Modeling the Progression from Buruli Ulcer to Cancer: A Dual-Route Transmission Approach with Environmental Feedback and Immunosuppression
abstract: Buruli ulcer (BU), a necrotizing skin disease caused by Mycobacterium ulcerans, remains a neglected tropical disease with complex environmental and vector-mediated transmission dynamics. Motivated by the potential interaction between chronic BU infection, environmental contamination, and cancer-associated immunosuppression, this study develops an integrated mathematical model describing the coupled dynamics of Buruli ulcer and BU–cancer co-infection. The proposed framework incorporates dual transmission pathways, an environmental infectious reservoir, and immunosuppression-mediated progression to the co-infected class. The basic reproduction number [Formula: see text] is derived using the next-generation matrix approach, and the local and global stability properties of the disease-free and endemic equilibria are investigated. Bifurcation analysis is performed to examine threshold behavior near [Formula: see text], while numerical simulations are used to illustrate the qualitative dynamics of the model under representative baseline parameter values. Global sensitivity analysis based on the Latin Hypercube Sampling–Partial Rank Correlation Coefficient (LHS–PRCC) method identifies the environmental contamination rate, Buruli ulcer recovery rate, and progression to the co-infected compartment as the parameters exerting the greatest influence on disease dynamics. The proposed framew…

Financial and banking interactions between Russia and China under sanctions
abstract: This article examines the transformation of financial and banking interactions between the Russian Federation and the People’s Republic of China in the context of sanctions pressure and global economic fragmentation. The relevance of this work is determined by the significant gap between record volumes of bilateral trade turnover and the growing vulnerability of the payment infrastructure servicing it, caused by the threat of secondary sanctions. The purpose of the study is to analyze the current mechanisms of cross-border settlements and develop promising areas for building an independent financial architecture. The paper applies methods of systemic, institutional, and statistical analysis. The dynamics and asymmetric structure of Russian-Chinese trade for 2020–2025 are analyzed, and payment instruments are considered, in particular, the CIPS infrastructure, dedicated communication lines, and the activities of VTB’s Shanghai branch. It is noted that, despite their status as a key settlement channel, these mechanisms have encountered infrastructural overloads and compliance restrictions. Particular attention is paid to innovative mechanisms for circumventing sanctions restrictions. The study assesses the prospects for integrating national payment systems, as well as the practical application of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), the mBridge platform, smart contracts, and …

title: How Financial Digitalization Affects Business Performance and Business Innovation in Ultra-Micro, Micro, and Small Enterprises: Evidence from Indonesia
abstract: The expansion of digital financial services is reshaping business operations across developing economies. Using Bank Indonesia’s 2023 survey of over 5,000 enterprises, this study examines the role of financial digitalization in business performance and innovation among ultra-micro, micro, and small enterprises in Indonesia. Employing inverse probability weighting regression adjustment to address observable confounder bias, we find that financial digitalization is positively associated with business performance—specifically higher revenue, sales growth, and employment—as well as business innovation, including market expansion, product diversification, and exports. However, it is also associated with higher costs, with no significant short-term gain in profit. These associations vary across firm and owner characteristics: Older firms and those outside Java and Bali experience stronger performance gains, while younger firms and ultra-micro firms show greater innovation responses. These findings highlight the importance of targeted policies addressing digital literacy, infrastructure, and regulation to support inclusive digital transformation among ultra-micro, micro, and small enterprises.

title: Research on the Impact of English Teaching Reform Based on the OBE Concept on the Cultivation of Vocational Undergraduate Students
abstract: Vocational undergraduate education is tasked with cultivating high-level technical and skilled talents. However, its English teaching has long suffered from the tendency of “generalization” and the separation of theory and practice. The problem lies in the fact that there has been a persistent predicament. The concept of Outcome-Based Education (OBE) and the ability-oriented training positioning of vocational undergraduate education are highly compatible. This provides a new path to solve this problem. The purpose of this study is to construct and implement an English teaching reform plan based on the OBE concept, and to empirically test its specific impact on the quality of vocational undergraduate education. The study adopts a quasi-experimental design and mixed research methods, with two parallel classes from a vocational undergraduate institution as the experimental group and the control group. The experimental group, based on the English application scenarios of job groups, reconstructed the goals, contents, methods, and evaluation system through reverse design and implemented output-driven project-based teaching; the control group maintained the traditional teaching mode. Data were collected through pre- and post-tests of English ability assessment, core literacy questionnaires, and in-depth interviews, and quantitative and qualitative analyses were conducted using SPSS a…

title: Service Delivery and Stakeholders’ Satisfaction in The Public Market Office of Batangas City: Basis for Policy Enhancement
abstract: This study examined the level of stakeholders’ satisfaction on the service delivery of the Public Market Office in Batangas City, specifically in terms of service quality, vendor relations, and market policies and regulations. Using a mixed-method approach, quantitative data were gathered from stallholders and clients through structured questionnaires, complemented by qualitative insights from key informant interviews. Descriptive and inferential analyses were employed to determine satisfaction levels, while thematic coding captured stakeholders’ issues and concerns. Results revealed that stakeholders generally rated their satisfaction as satisfactory, reflecting the market office’s adequate service responsiveness and professional conduct. However, aspects such as sanitation maintenance, vendor communication, and equitable enforcement of market regulations were noted as areas needing improvement. Findings underscore that satisfaction levels are influenced by perceived service consistency, fairness in vendor relations, and clarity of policy communication. Anchored on the SERVQUAL, Stakeholder, and New Public Service Theories, the study supports the principles of citizen-centered governance and collaborative service design. In alignment with SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions), …

title: Relationship between Traders' Knowledge, Attitudes, and Availability of Trash Bins and Waste Management at Rau Market, Serang City
abstract: Background: Indonesia is one of the largest waste-producing countries in the world, generating approximately 65.2 million tons of waste in 2020, with traditional markets being one of the main sources of domestic waste. Poor waste management in markets can lead to environmental pollution and increase the risk of disease among traders and visitors. Objective: This study aimed to analyze the relationship between traders’ knowledge, attitudes, and availability of trash bins and waste management at Rau Market, Serang City, in 2024. Methods: This quantitative cross-sectional study involved 78 of 360 traders selling vegetables, fruits, fish, and poultry within Rau Market’s fenced area, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through interviews and observations using a structured questionnaire covering knowledge, attitudes, trash bin availability, and waste management practices. Data were analyzed using univariate and bivariate methods with the Chi-square test at a 0.05 significance level. Results: Among the 78 respondents, poor waste management was found in 33 traders (42.3%). There was a significant relationship between knowledge and waste management (p < 0.001), attitudes and waste management (p < 0.001), as well as availability of trash bins and waste management (p = 0.002). Traders with lower knowledge, less supportive attitudes, and inadequate availability of tra…

title: From AI boyfriends to AI shopping agents? The emerging convergence of relational AI and AI-assisted commerce
abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence is becoming both relational and agentic. AI boyfriends are treated as a visible romantic exemplar within the broader theoretical and empirical domain of relational AI. This paper examines whether relational AI, including AI boyfriends, is emerging alongside AI-assisted commerce, and whether functional integration keeps pace with attention and market growth. Study 1 analyzes Google Trends data (2020–2026, six markets): relational-AI attention rises significantly in five countries, AI-commerce attention rises in all six, with substantial but non-invariant temporal co-movement in attention. Study 2 examines 44 AI-companion apps on Google Play: the category shows substantial downloads and spending, romantic positioning (e.g., AI boyfriends) shows no observable adoption penalty, in-app purchasing is universal, yet no app positions shopping as a core feature. Study 3 analyzes 181,226 Reddit posts from relational-AI communities: design-weighted coding estimates 9.1% of corpus posts contain commercial discourse, but only 0.3% involve the companion itself in consumer or purchasing decisions. We conceptualize this as an attention-market-integration gap, where attention and market realization outpace functional commerce integration. The study equips managers and researchers with guidance for engaging with the emerging AI boyfriend trend.

title: The Currency of Clarity: Strategic Communication as a Catalyst for Corporate Governance and Market Leadership
abstract: Strategic communication connects organizational decisions with the people who must understand, evaluate, implement, or challenge them. This paper examines that connection through a secondary-data analysis and a theory-informed narrative review. It considers how communication may support corporate governance, employee alignment, stakeholder relationships, and the organizational capabilities associated with market leadership. The empirical component uses a traceable Gallup series on global employee engagement and life evaluation for 2015–2024, excluding 2017 because the source does not report a global engagement observation for that year. Contextual evidence comes from Deloitte’s 2024 Gen Z and Millennial Survey and Randstad’s Workmonitor 2023. Descriptive comparisons indicate that global engagement increased from 15% in 2015 to 21% in 2024, with interruptions in 2020 and 2024; these movements do not establish changes in communication quality. The theoretical discussion integrates information asymmetry, the job demands–resources model, and self-determination theory. It develops an explanatory framework in which accurate disclosure, usable information, meaningful feedback, and consistency between messages and conduct may strengthen organizational coordination. The study does not estimate a causal effect on profitability, investor confidence, or market leadership. Its contribution …

title: The positive impact of electricity spot trading on ESG performance in energy-intensive enterprises
abstract: Electricity market reforms are vital for global energy transition. Using a firm-level panel dataset of listed companies from 2012 to 2020 and taking China’s electricity spot market pilot project as a quasi-natural experiment with a difference-in-differences-in-differences method, we examine its impact on ESG performance in energy-intensive enterprises. Drawing on a modified Coasean perspective that acknowledges transaction costs and government intervention, we propose both positive and negative pathways. Results show that electricity spot trading (EST) significantly enhances ESG performance through optimized resource allocation, improved employee governance, and enhanced operational stability, while we find no evidence that EST induces managerial short-termism. The positive effect is stronger in regions with higher marketization, particularly those with developed non-state economies, and among enterprises facing greater supplier competition. Both city-level and firm-level evidence further reveal that EST reduces carbon emission intensity, mitigating greenwashing concerns. This study provides Chinese evidence on the micro-level effects of EST and offers policy insights for advancing energy transitions through market mechanisms.

title: Dynamic response of PLA honeycomb core GFRP sandwich panels with an additively manufactured core: Experimental characterization and numerical blast analysis
abstract: This study investigates the transient dynamic response of an additively manufactured polylactic acid (PLA) honeycomb sandwich panel with glass-fiber-reinforced plastic (GFRP) face sheets through experimental characterization and finite element analysis. The PLA honeycomb core was fabricated using fused deposition modelling, while the GFRP face sheets were prepared using the hand lay-up technique. Tensile, flexural, and density tests were conducted to experimentally characterize the material properties used in the numerical model. A finite element model was developed in ANSYS using the experimentally obtained effective properties and was initially assessed against benchmark results reported in the literature. The experimental and numerical displacement–time histories under cantilever harmonic excitation at 500 Hz and 0.2 N showed similar trends for the investigated laboratory condition. A separate numerical calculation was performed to examine the early-time global displacement response under a hypothetical prescribed modified Friedlander pressure pulse using a linear-elastic material representation. The blast analysis showed maximum deformation in the central region of the panel and relatively lower displacement near the supported boundaries. Fetomaternal Outcomes and Response to Ursodeoxycholic Acid in Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy: A Prospective Observational Study from Eastern India
abstract: Background: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is a pregnancy-specific liver disorder characterized by pruritus and elevated serum bile acid levels, associated with adverse fetal outcomes including preterm delivery and intrauterine fetal death. Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) is widely used for management, but regional data on fetomaternal outcomes and treatment response remain limited in Eastern India. This study aimed to evaluate clinical profile, biochemical parameters, fetomaternal outcomes, and response to UDCA therapy in patients with ICP. Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted among 60 pregnant women diagnosed with ICP at a tertiary care medical college in Eastern India between January 2023 and December 2024. Diagnosis was based on pruritus with serum bile acid levels >10 µmol/L and abnormal liver function tests after exclusion of other causes. Clinical characteristics, biochemical parameters, and pregnancy outcomes were recorded. UDCA was administered at a dose of 10–15 mg/kg/day until delivery. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and appropriate paired statistical test was applied to assess treatment response. A p value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. abstract: Abstract Palladium (Pd)-based sensitizers are widely employed to boost the hydrogen (H2) sensing properties of metal oxide semiconductor (MOS)-based sensors owing to their outstanding catalytic activity. However, the generation of palladium hydride (PdHx) induces strong electron scattering, causing an abnormal response inversion that compromises detection reliability. Herein, we proposed an electronic structure engineering induced by alloying to suppress response inversion. Metal-organic-framework-derived In2O3 hollow microtubes decorated with PdPt alloy were assembled into sensor devices and evaluated for H2 detection. The sensor with 0.5 wt.% PdPt loading achieves the optimal performance, with high sensitivity (9.5 to 100 ppm H2), ultrafast response/recovery kinetics (3 s/4 s), and a limit of detection as low as 500 ppb. Notably, the PdPt/In2O3 sensor completely eliminates abnormal response inversion in contrast to the Pd/In2O3 sensor. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the modification of the PdPt alloy preserves high catalytic activity toward H2 while effectively hindering the diffusion of H atoms into the Pd bulk, thereby ensuring sensitive and reliable sensing. Furthermore, the PdPt/In2O3 sensor array integrated with machine learning algorithms demonstrates reliable discrimination of H2 from interfering gases, highlighting its potential for practical gas m…

title: GLP1R and GIPR gene sequencing for glycemic response to DPP-4 inhibitors in T2DM patients
abstract: Interindividual variability in glycemic response to dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitors remains a major challenge in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). DPP-4 inhibitors exert their effects by inhibiting the degradation of incretin hormones. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) are among these incretin hormones. Genetic variations in the receptor genes for these incretin hormones can influence both receptor function and incretin sensitivity. In this study, conducted on patients with T2DM receiving DPP-4 inhibitor therapy, we aimed to evaluate the relationship between variants in the relevant genes and glycemic response. Targeted next-generation sequencing (t-NGS) was used to sequence both the exons and the exon-intron boundary regions of the GIPR and GLP1R genes. A total of 42 T2DM patients undergoing DPP-4 inhibitor treatment were included in the study. Patients were divided into two groups based on their HbA1c levels: those with adequate glycemic control (≤7.0%) and those with inadequate glycemic control (>7.0%). Sequencing of the GLP1R and GIPR genes revealed 16 variants, including missense, intronic, synonymous, and non-coding region changes. abstract: Abstract Background The prognostic impact of CT-defined sarcopenia in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients who received the transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) remains unclear. This study aimed to clarify the impact of CT-defined sarcopenia on survival and therapeutic response in HCC patients receiving TACE. Methods PubMed, Web of Science and CNKI databases were searched up to April 18, 2026. Primary endpoints included the overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) and secondary endpoints were objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR). Hazard ratios (HRs) and odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were combined to evaluate the impact of CT-defined sarcopenia on primary and secondary endpoints. Results Sixteen studies with 3359 cases were included. As for primary outcomes, the presence of CT-defined sarcopenia was significantly related to poorer OS (HR = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.47–2.18, P < 0.001) and PFS (HR = 1.65, 95% CI: 1.42–1.92, P < 0.001). Besides, subgroup analysis stratified by the country, sample size, combination of other therapies, source of HR and defining method of sarcopenia manifested similar findings. As for secondary outcomes, CT-defined sarcopenia was also associated with decreased ORR (OR = 0.55, 95% CI: 0.38–0.81, P = 0.002) and DCR (OR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.37–0.67, P < 0.001). title: QUIJOTE scientific results – XII. Characterization of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power spectrum level in the QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey
abstract: Abstract We present an analysis of the polarized synchrotron emission at the power-spectrum level in the multipole range 30 ≤ ℓ < 130, using the recent QUIJOTE-MFI wide survey (10–20 GHz) in combination with Planck and WMAP data. The EE and BB power spectra are well described by a simple power-law model, with no evidence for the need of additional parameters. The best-fit slopes are αEE = −3.24 ± 0.12 and αEE = −3.81 ± 0.34 for |b| > 20○, hinting toward a steepening of the BB spectrum relative to EE at the ∼1.6σ level. The synchrotron frequency spectral indices are found to be $\beta _{\rm s}^{\rm EE} = -3.26 \pm 0.05$ and $\beta _{\rm s}^{\rm BB} = -3.25 \pm 0.10$ for the same cut, in agreement with earlier real-space analyses. We find no evidence for spatial variations of βs across different Galactic latitude cuts, within current uncertainties. The synchrotron BB/EE power ratio is approximately 0.2 over the considered multipole range, lower than typical values for thermal dust, and consistent with previous measurements. We also measure a dust-synchrotron spatial correlation in the range 0.1–0.25 over 30 ≤ ℓ < 130. Using these results, we estimate the level of synchrotron contamination in future CMB B-mode measurements, finding an average power in the considered sky masks equivalent to r ≃ 0.003 at 90 GHz and r ≃ 0.0002 at 150 GHz for the relevant angular scales.

title: Investigation and Management of Neonates Presenting to Hospital With Fever: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Guidelines for neonates presenting to the emergency department (ED) with fever, including fever at home, recommend a full septic work‐up and prompt administration of parenteral antibiotics. However, compliance is unknown. We sought to determine rates of guideline compliance in this population, reasons for non‐compliance and rates and outcomes of serious bacterial infection (SBI). Methods We conducted a single‐centre retrospective cohort study of all neonates aged ≤ 28 days presenting to the ED with documented fever 38°C. We extracted and analysed hospital data from an electronic medical record for guideline compliance, reasons for non‐compliance, rates of SBI, and clinical outcomes. Our primary outcome was the rate of guideline compliance. Results We included 475 patients, less than half (46.5%) of whom received guideline‐compliant care. The primary contributor to guideline non‐compliance was fever at home but no fever in the ED. Overall, 65/475 (15%) of patients had SBI, the majority of which were urinary tract infections (UTIs). 42/65 (64.6%) of patients with SBI had a confirmed concurrent viral infection. 107/475 (22.5%) were discharged home from ED, only one (0.9%) of whom was readmitted within 72 h. Conclusions Fewer than half of febrile neonates presenting to the ED receive guideline‐compliant care, with the lowest compliance in infants who are febrile at hom…

title: Recognizing the 2026 GOM Award Winners!
DESIGN SCIENCE RESEARCH COMO METODOLOGIA PARA CONSTRUÇÃO DE UM ARTEFATO PARA O APOIO À GESTÃO DA QUALIDADE NO SETOR SUPERMERCADISTA
abstract: A complexidade das operações no varejo supermercadista amplia os desafios da gestão da qualidade higiênico-sanitária dos alimentos. A fragmentação dos registros e a ausência de mecanismos integrados de verificação podem limitar o uso de evidências na tomada de decisão. O estudo objetivou desenvolver e avaliar um artefato para apoiar a gestão da qualidade higiênico-sanitária dos alimentos comercializados no varejo supermercadista, fundamentado na abordagem Design Science Research (DSR). Trata-se de estudo aplicado, de abordagem qualitativa, conduzido em uma unidade modelo de uma rede supermercadista do Nordeste brasileiro. O desenvolvimento seguiu as etapas da DSR e integrou evidências de observação não participante, análise documental e revisão da literatura. Foram identificadas dez classes de problemas relacionadas à gestão da qualidade, contemplando higiene dos manipuladores, higienização, controle de tempo e temperatura, qualidade da água, monitoramento, treinamento, auditorias, rastreabilidade e manutenção. O artefato demonstrou aplicabilidade ao integrar requisitos técnicos, normativos e informações operacionais em um instrumento único de apoio à verificação da qualidade. A solução apresenta potencial para reduzir a subjetividade das avaliações, fortalecer a rastreabilidade das não conformidades e subsidiar decisões orientadas por evidências.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling reveals cellular heterogeneity and organ-specific signatures in the vestibular system
abstract: Abstract The vestibular sensory epithelia, comprising the utricle, saccule, and ampullary cristae, exhibit distinct regenerative capacities and physiological specializations, yet the cellular heterogeneity and regulatory logic governing their development remain incompletely understood. Here, we generated a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of postnatal day 1 mouse vestibular organs, identifying nine transcriptionally distinct epithelial subpopulations with marked organ-specific distributions. Trajectory reconstruction revealed a conserved tri-phase differentiation cascade ( Sox2 → Atoh1 → Myo7a ) but divergent topologies: linear progenitor progression in ampulla/saccule versus branched paths in utricle. Single-cell regulatory network inference and clustering analysis uncovered 16 regulons, including Pou4f3 -driven programs in hair cells. Wilcoxon testing additionally identified Nfib as a differentially expressed transcription factor in saccule-predominant dark-cell precursors ( Kcne1 -negative at postnatal day 1). CellChat analysis further demonstrated distinct interactomic architectures: the saccule employs high-capacity plastic signaling (insulin-like growth factor), the ampulla emphasizes extracellular matrix remodeling (collagen/thrombospondin), and the utricle and ampulla share neural adhesion signatures (neuronal growth regulator/cell adhesion molecule), with quantitative …

title: Integrated geothermal applications in Türkiye for energy carbon management and resource recovery
abstract: Abstract Türkiye is important for geothermal energy not only because it produces electricity from high-temperature fields, but also because it uses geothermal resources for other innovative direct-use applications. A large part of the resource value comes from direct heat use, chemically complex fluids, separated gases, and the way these systems are operated at the surface. This review examines geothermal systems in Türkiye from this broader perspective. The study outlines the geological framework controlling the distribution of geothermal fields, with particular emphasis on active fault systems, graben structures, recent magmatic activity, and elevated heat flow. These controls are especially evident in western Anatolia, although fault-controlled geothermal circulation also occurs in other parts of the country. The paper then reviews the current use of geothermal energy in Türkiye, including power generation, district heating, greenhouse heating, and thermal tourism. After this general overview, four field examples are used to discuss newer or less conventional uses of geothermal systems. The Kızıldere geothermal field shows how CO 2 -rich non-condensable gases can be recovered for liquid CO 2 and dry ice production. The Tuzla geothermal field provides an example in which CO 2 is used at the surface to lower brine pH and reduce silica-rich scaling in a hypersaline geothermal f…

title: Assessment of the Urban Storm Water Drainage System of Kakinada Smart City Using GIS and EPA SWMM under Design Storm
abstract: Rapid urbanization, encroachment on natural drainage channels and intense rainfall have made flooding a recurrent problem in Kakinada Smart City, a low-lying coastal city in Andhra Pradesh, India. This study evaluates the performance of the city's storm water drainage network and proposes modifications to reduce flooding. Intensity–Duration–Frequency (IDF) curves were derived from rainfall records distribution, and design storms were generated with the Alternating Block Method. The study area was delineated in ArcGIS into 29 catchments and 120 sub-catchments,out of that mainly consider 5subcatchments (Three Temple(Gudari Gunta), Dairy Farm Centre, Doodh Factory, KKD Port Station Back Side, and Subbaya Gari Street Culvert). Land use/Land cover (LULC) was classified by maximum likelihood classification, and curve numbers were computed for each sub-catchment. A dynamic-wave EPA SWMM model with tidal outfall boundary conditions was calibrated against observed water levels at five locations, giving Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) values of 0.856–0.949 and correlation coefficients (R) of 0.871–0.971. Simulation of the 2-years(2022&2023) and 5-years (2021-2025) design storms, with peak intensities of 53.27 and 78.81 mm/h, showed overtopping in most of the drains.
