title: Pharmacokinetics of Famotidine in Goats ( Capra aegagrus hircus ) After Subcutaneous Administration
abstract: ABSTRACT Small ruminants such as goats are susceptible to abomasal ulceration due to adverse reactions to medications, stress, and inappetence. There is limited pharmacokinetic data regarding the use of famotidine for treatment and prevention of abomasal ulceration in goats. The objective of this study is to report the pharmacokinetic parameters after a single subcutaneous administration of famotidine. Famotidine was administered at a 1.2 mg/kg dose to six healthy goats and plasma samples were collected over a 12‐h period. The plasma was analyzed using reverse phase high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) to measure famotidine concentrations. Using commercially available pharmacokinetic software, noncompartmental analysis was used to determine the pharmacokinetic parameters. The maximum plasma concentration was estimated at 735 ng/mL and the T max was 0.64 h. The apparent terminal half‐life was 1.29 h, and the mean residence time was 1.82 h. The area under the curve was found to be 1046 h*ng/mL. Five of the 6 goats in this study had been utilized for a previous intravenous famotidine investigation, and when comparing the area under the curve to this study, the range of the estimated bioavailability after subcutaneous administration was 21.43%–135%. Future research performing a pharmacodynamic study measuring the pH of the abomasal fluid could be used to determine the effi…

Explainable machine learning-based forecasting of COVID-19 cases: a comparative analysis of maharashtra and Kerala, India
abstract: Abstract Background The Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic in India exhibited substantial spatial and temporal variation in transmission dynamics, influenced by human mobility, meteorological conditions, vaccination rollout, and non-pharmaceutical interventions. Methods This study forecasted district-level COVID-19 cases one-day-ahead in the districts of 2 Indian states of Maharashtra (33 districts) and Kerala (14 districts) between April 26, 2020 and June 20, 2021, using four Machine Learning (ML) models: Multiple Linear Regression (MLR), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. 17 explanatory variables spanning mobility, meteorology, vaccination, social gatherings, lockdown restrictions, and population density were incorporated, with separate models developed for the 2020 (pre-vaccination) and 2021 (vaccination) periods in each state. Models were evaluated using 10-fold walk-forward cross-validation, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was applied to the best-performing model to quantify the magnitude and direction of each variable’s contribution. Results LSTM was the overall best performing model, with R 2 of nearly 0.8 (NRMSE = 0.07) in Maharashtra and 0.6 (NRMSE = 0.15) in Kerala. SHAP analysis of LSTM identified mobility-related variables, particularly workplace, retail, and residential mobili…

title: GIS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED FORECASTING OF REGIONAL SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
abstract: Ensuring the sustainable development of the regional economy has become the most important issue on a global scale. In 2024-2026, growth rates in the countries that account for more than 80% of the world's population and global GDP remain below those of the decade preceding the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2025, the German geospatial analytics (Geospatial Analytics) market is valued at USD 1.45 billion, and it is expected to reach USD 2.55 billion by 2030. Therefore, using GIS technologies as a lever for forecasting regions, and studying their structural components and their impact on the formation of regional economic policy, is a pressing scientific problem.

title: Dance course participation is associated with reductions in anxiety sensitivity physical concerns in college students
abstract: Abstract College students face heightened risk for anxiety. Anxiety sensitivity (AS), the fear of anxiety-related sensations, is a key vulnerability factor for anxiety. Dance courses, which incorporate aerobic exercise, may provide interoceptive exposure to anxiety-related sensations, which may correspond with reductions in AS. The current quasi-experimental study investigated the association between participation in university dance courses relative to non-dance courses, and changes in AS over time. Undergraduate students were recruited from dance courses, including traditional dance and mindfulness-infused dance, and non-dance courses. Consented students ( N = 271) completed a testing battery online at the beginning of the academic semester (T1) and 7 weeks later (T2). This battery included the Anxiety Sensitivity Index-3 (ASI-3), demographic and engagement information, and other metrics outside the current scope. Multilevel models revealed greater reductions in AS physical concerns in students enrolled in dance courses, relative to those in non-dance courses, even after accounting for out-of-class exercise engagement and intensity ( b = -1.13, SE = 0.36, t (227.81) = -3.15, p = .002, 95% CI [-1.84, -0.42]). Artificial Intelligence-Driven Digital Twin for Disease Progression Prediction: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to integrate machine learning and deep learning techniques with Digital Twin technology to improve the accuracy of disease progression prediction and support personalised clinical decision-making. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study reviews existing Digital Twin frameworks in healthcare and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-driven Digital Twin paradigm based on temporal electronic health record data. The proposed approach develops dynamic digital representations of patients that reflect their current health conditions and predict their future clinical evolution. Machine learning and deep learning techniques analyse large-scale medical data, identify hidden patterns, and provide early predictions of patient deterioration, particularly in intensive care environments. Research Limitation: Further validation using diverse, multi-centre clinical datasets and real-time patient information is required before the model can be widely implemented in clinical practice. Findings: The findings indicate that AI-powered Digital Twins can improve the accuracy of disease progression prediction, facilitate early identification of patient deterioration, and support clinical treatment decisions. The proposed approach may also enable proactive, personalised, and data-driven disease management. Practical Implication: The proposed Digital Twin paradigm can help healthcar…

title: Q-DRFormer: Query-Position Mapping Flow Prediction with Progressive Refinement for Document Rectification
abstract: Document image rectification aims at restoring images degraded by geometric distortions. Existing U-shaped encoder-decoder methods rely on hierarchical upsampling operations to recover dense flow fields, which provide limited control over the displacement at individual grid positions, leading to spatial inconsistency and poor detail restoration. To address this issue, we propose Q-DRFormer, a novel framework that formulates rectification as a set prediction task. Specifically, we design a set of queries, where each query corresponds to a position in the flow field grid and is responsible for regressing a 2D anchor point that indicates the sampling position in the distorted input. This one-to-one design establishes a deterministic query-position mapping, enabling fine-grained control and improving the spatial consistency of the predicted flow field. Exploiting this deterministic correspondence, we further propose a progressive flow refinement strategy that progressively refines anchor points through layer-wise offset prediction to enhance fine-grained restoration. Moreover, considering the lack of downstream-task-oriented evaluation in existing studies, we apply the rectification method to scene table detection and contribute a real-world test set along with corresponding evaluation metrics to fill this gap. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Q-DRFormer outperforms existing …

title: Machine Learning‐Based Prediction of Drift Limit States of Concrete‐Filled Steel Tube Columns
abstract: This study discusses a machine learning (ML)‐based framework for estimating the drift limit states of concrete‐filled steel tube (CFT) columns. The calibration process used a comprehensive database assembled from numerous experiments reported the in literature. An ML regression model was trained based on the calibration data to predict numerical model parameters. Subsequently, 10,000 CFT column design parameters were randomly sampled, and a parametric study was conducted to investigate the influence of the design parameters on the drift limit states using an ML model and the simulation results obtained from the developed numerical model. The results showed that the drift limit states associated with slight, moderate, and extensive damage were mainly affected by the parameters related to the strength and stiffness of the CFT columns (depth‐to‐thickness ratio, steel tube yield strength‐to‐concrete compressive strength ratio, and steel tube stiffness ratio). The drift limit state associated with complete damage was primarily influenced by the axial load ratio. Additionally, it was found that CFT columns are more likely to experience moderate damage owing to the local buckling of the steel tube rather than from concrete crushing. Finally, fragility curves for the CFT frame systems were developed using the nonlinear time‐history analysis results in conjunction with the developed ML‐…

title: No-shift prediction-error expansion for high-fidelity reversible color image watermarking, a predictor-agnostic framework with cross-channel capacity analysis
abstract: We contribute a predictor-agnostic framework for reversible color image watermarking on three fronts. First, no-shift prediction-error expansion (PEE) abandons the histogram-shift step of the canonical PEE rule. The encoder instead transmits a sparse bitmap of one flag per embedding candidate, trading those side-channel bits for 8.9 to 17.5 dB of marked-image peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) against standard PEE at matched payload. Second, we prove that cross-channel context lowers the entropy-power floor on prediction-error variance by exactly 2−2I(Xc;N−c∣Nc), for any host distribution and independently of which predictor is used (Theorem 1). In the Gaussian linear-MMSE case, the floor is attained, and the PEE-embeddable set grows at every threshold (Corollary 1). On Kodak, the conditional mutual information this identifies tracks the measured variance reduction with Spearman ρ=−0.891. Third, two predictor instantiations exercise the framework, a classical four-neighbor rhombus filter and a quaternion self-attention network. The classical filter is the stronger of the two at every threshold we swept. We report the deep predictor because the framework accepts it unchanged, not because it wins. On color Kodak at 256×256 RGB, the held-out deep predictor reaches PSNR 65.03±0.53 dB at a 10,000-bit target, embedding 8348 of those bits on average. A classical predictor embeds the fu…

Cox‐PASNet With Late Fusion of Transcriptomic and Clinical Features for Survival Prediction in Diffuse Large B‐Cell Lymphoma
abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate prognosis in diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remains a clinical challenge. The International Prognostic Index (IPI) is the standard tool but relies solely on clinical variables and fails to capture the extensive molecular heterogeneity of DLBCL. Integrating transcriptomics has shown promise for improving patient stratification, yet most approaches lack biological interpretability and external validation. Here, we apply Cox‐PASNet, a pathway‐structured neural network survival model, to DLBCL, integrating gene expression with clinical features. Using a discovery cohort of 670 patients (GSE181063) and an independent external validation cohort of 233 R‐CHOP‐treated patients (GSE10846), we demonstrate that late fusion of pathway‐structured transcriptomics with IPI achieves a C ‐index of 0.700 ± 0.020 on the discovery cohort and 0.732 on external validation, statistically significantly outperforming the externally transferred IPI‐Cox baseline ( C ‐index 0.678; Δ = +0.054, bootstrap 95% confidence interval [CI] [+0.004, +0.104], p = 0.018). Incorporating cell‐of‐origin subtype further raised the external fused C ‐index to 0.745, though this additional gain over IPI‐Cox did not reach the pre‐specified significance threshold (bootstrap 95% CI [−0.0003, +0.130]). Pathway‐level explainability analysis identified apoptosis, hypoxia, IL6/JAK/STAT3 signaling, and inte…

EXPRESS: Cerebral hemodynamic reserve and the prediction of shunt-responsive reversibility in idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus
abstract: The placebo-controlled PENS trial showed that shunting improves gait but not cognition or continence in idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH). This selective response highlights an unresolved problem: even among patients who respond to temporary cerebrospinal-fluid (CSF) drainage, we cannot predict which deficits will reverse after shunting. Static structural and perfusion markers, including white-matter hyperintensity load, cerebral small-vessel-disease burden, and baseline cerebral blood flow, do not predict shunt response. In contrast, impaired cerebrovascular reactivity is associated with a favorable response, yet cerebral autoregulation has not been measured before and after CSF diversion. I propose that reversibility in iNPH reflects recoverable hemodynamic reserve, and that this hypothesis can be tested within the existing diagnostic pathway.

abstract: Background: Evening screen use, sleep, physical activity and outdoor time form part of the everyday routines through which children and young people organise rest, leisure, movement and participation. This exploratory service evaluation described patterns across these factors, examined their relationships, and identified locally relevant implications for community wellbeing activity. Methods: An anonymous, voluntary cross-sectional survey was conducted by a UK community wellbeing organisation in May 2026. Fifty-one valid responses from children and young people aged 8–25 years were analysed. The survey covered evening screen use, bedtime, sleep duration and quality, physical activity, outdoor time and mood. Associations and group differences were examined using non-parametric tests. Findings: Higher evening screen use was significantly associated with poorer sleep quality (rₛ = −0.436, p = .002) and later bedtime (rₛ = 0.407, p = .004). Older age was strongly associated with later bedtimes (rₛ = 0.659, p < .001) and shorter sleep (rₛ = −0.560, p < .001). Higher physical activity was associated with better mood on outdoor days (rₛ = 0.453, p = .001). Most participants reported better sleep after outdoor days. However, mood did not differ significantly between outdoor and indoor days in the paired comparison. Conclusion and implications: The findings suggest that screen use, slee…

title: A qualitative SWOT analysis of hospital medical service managers’ experiences during the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes
abstract: Abstract Background Disasters caused by large-scale earthquakes significantly disrupt healthcare systems; however, while existing research has largely focused on response processes, limited attention has been given to comprehensively evaluating strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement in service delivery. Objective This study aimed to examine the factors affecting hospital service delivery during the earthquake process within the framework of SWOT (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats) and to provide a comprehensive evaluation of health system resilience. Methods A qualitative phenomenological study was conducted. Data were collected through semi-structured individual interviews with purposively selected hospital medical service managers who actively served during the disaster. The data were analyzed using thematic analysis, and the findings were categorized within the SWOT framework. Results The findings were organized into four main themes based on SWOT analysis: strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats. Strengths included effective leadership and coordination, workforce capacity and resilience, operational capacity, and prior training and drills, whereas weaknesses reflected psychosocial strain, deficiencies in institutional preparedness and management, structural and logistical disruptions, hygiene and infection-control inadequacies, and coordi…

Les TI au service de l’enseignement supérieur de proximité : comment la réalité virtuelle vient rompre la distance et améliorer la persévérance scolaire dans un contexte hybride
abstract: La diminution progressive des coûts de production a favorisé une accessibilité accrue de la réalité virtuelle (RV), renforçant l’intérêt qu’elle suscite dans de nombreux secteurs, notamment en formation. En raison de son caractère immersif et interactif, la RV apparaît comme un levier prometteur pour le développement des compétences en contexte universitaire. Le présent article rend compte d’une étude menée en 2025 dans un établissement universitaire québécois visant à expérimenter, à petite échelle, l’intégration de la RV dans différents contextes d’enseignement, dans une perspective d’amélioration de l’accessibilité, de la persévérance et de la réussite étudiante. L’étude repose sur un devis mixte comparant un groupe témoin ayant suivi le cours à distance via la plateforme Zoom, et un groupe expérimental ayant bénéficié du même enseignement dans un environnement immersif en RV. Les résultats quantitatifs révèlent une différence statistiquement significative en faveur du groupe expérimental quant à la note finale obtenue. Les données qualitatives issues de groupes de discussion permettent d’éclairer ces résultats en mettant en évidence une satisfaction élevée à l’égard du cours et une perception favorable de l’environnement immersif chez les personnes participantes exposées à la RV.

title: Identifying pre-implementation barriers, facilitators and strategies for integrating a co-designed, technology-assisted parenting program within an adult mental health service
abstract: Abstract Background Children of parents experiencing mental health challenges are at an increased risk of mental health issues themselves. Parenting interventions can improve parent and child outcomes; however, parents often face barriers to accessing them. Delivering technology-assisted parenting programs within adult mental health services may overcome barriers by providing accessible, family-focused support and minimising demands on services. Yet little is known about how these programs can be efficiently and appropriately implemented in adult mental health settings. This study aimed to: (1) understand the perceived barriers and facilitators to implementing a co-designed, technology-assisted parenting program in an adult mental health service, from the perspective of service providers, and (2) use this understanding to develop practical strategies to guide the implementation of such programs in practice. Methods Individual interviews were conducted with 13 service providers ( n = 9 clinicians, n = 4 managers). Data collection and analysis were informed by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Implementation strategies were drawn from the Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change (ERIC), with the CFIR-ERIC Matching Tool used to link identified barriers with targeted implementation strategies. Results We identified 22 CFIR constructs as facilitato…

title: Weather, Terrain and Awareness Constraints on Drone Spraying Services in Rajasthan: Evidence from Service Providers
abstract: Agricultural drone spraying offers potential operational advantages, but service delivery in Rajasthan is affected by weather, field conditions and farmer awareness. This study examined constraints reported by drone service providers and assessed district-level exposure to conditions that may affect spraying. Data were obtained from a structured questionnaire and semi-structured interviews with 15 providers across eight districts. The analysis considered nine technical, environmental and awareness-related constraints and drew on published technical research, an official heat bulletin and operator accounts. Frequencies and percentages were used to summarise operators' responses, while climate and terrain evidence was used to describe exposure. Fourteen providers (93%) reported weather-related constraints, including wind, heat and rain. All 15 providers offered pesticide and liquid-fertiliser spraying, and none provided monitoring, mapping or advisory services. Thirteen providers encountered farmer hesitation, with each attributing it to doubts about effectiveness. Extreme reported temperatures included 49.0°C in Phalodi, 43.6°C in Jodhpur and 49.4°C in Sri Ganganagar (India Meteorological Department, 2024). Enhancing the Working Capacity of Sales Department Staff at the Hanoi Branch of Vietnam Express Mail Service Corporation
abstract: Rapid e-commerce growth has intensified competition in the express mail industry, making the working capacity of Sales Department staff decisive for the competitive position of the Hanoi branch of Vietnam Express Mail Service Corporation. Using desk research - synthesizing, analyzing, evaluating, and comparing secondary data within a Knowledge-Skill-Attitude (KSA) competency framework - this study systematizes the underlying theory, assesses the current situation, and proposes solutions. The findings show that frontline staffing remains thin, new employees' professional knowledge is uneven, complex complaint-handling skills are limited, and mounting workload poses a risk to service attitude. The study proposes solutions in training, recruitment, compensation, technology, and the development of a standardized competency framework, contributing to the theoretical literature and providing a practical basis for branch human resource management.

abstract: This article examined relationships among toxic leadership practices, organizational culture, and customer service quality, aiming to identify the mechanisms investigated, contextual conditions, and limits of the evidence. A critical literature review with qualitative synthesis was conducted, drawing on exploratory and expanded searches performed between September 24 and 26, 2026. The main synthesis included five empirical articles and four sources providing conceptual and methodological support. The analysis distinguished abusive supervision, leadership ostracism, organizational culture, and climate, as well as assessments provided by employees, supervisors, and customers. The studies reported relationships between supervisory practices and employee experiences, between abusive supervision and service performance, and between cultural characteristics and customer satisfaction. These relationships were investigated separately, in different settings and using different measures. The evidence did not establish a complete causal sequence linking abusive leadership, cultural change, and customer experience, nor did it support a single percentage estimate of harm to service quality. The review clarified these distinctions and presented questions for managerial diagnosis. The main limitations involved access-dependent selection, concentration in a small number of settings, and insuff…

abstract: This paper proposes a compact Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) accelerometer with a series double-hinge structure for low-frequency vibration sensing. Under external excitation, the coupled deformation of the upper and lower hinge segments enhances strain transfer efficiency and improves the sensor’s response in the low-frequency range. A two-degree-of-freedom theoretical model was established to investigate the resonant characteristics and sensitivity of the accelerometer, and its structural properties were verified through finite element simulation. Experimental results show that the sensor has a resonant frequency of approximately 84 Hz, an effective operating range of 0.5–50 Hz, and a sensitivity of 103.05 pm/g. Furthermore, the sensor exhibits excellent linearity, with an R 2 value of 99.96% and the cross-axis responses along the x - and z -directions are 10.8 and 6.4%, respectively, relative to the y -axis sensitivity.

title: Frequency-domain loss characterization for fiber loop ring-down systems using multi-harmonic spectral analysis
abstract: A frequency-domain demodulation method for fiber loop ring-down (FLRD) systems using multi-harmonic spectral analysis is proposed. By applying Fourier transform to the time-domain ring-down signals, ring-down cavity loss is extracted from the peak–valley differences of multiple harmonics in the amplitude spectrum, eliminating exponential fitting for ring-down time extraction. To mitigate the frequency-dependent amplitude attenuation induced by finite pulse width and time-window effects, a quadratic envelope compensation method is established to flatten the spectral envelope and enhance the utilization of multi-harmonic information. Numerical simulations based on an exponentially decaying pulse model show that, after envelope compensation, a strong linear relationship is obtained between the averaged peak–valley differences and the ring-down time constant, with a coefficient of determination of 0.9998. An experimental FLRD platform is further constructed to evaluate the proposed approach under bending losses ranging from 0 to 2.0 dB. The compensated peak–valley differences of the first seven harmonics exhibit a clear linear correlation with the applied loss, yielding a coefficient of determination of 0.994, in good agreement with conventional time-domain measurements. The proposed method provides a feasible approach for loss characterization in FLRD-based sensing systems.

title: Selective Hydrogenation of Furfural to 2-Methylfuran by Co–Pt/ZrO2: Electron Regulation at the Co Center by a Pt-Lean System
abstract: Abstract Furfural upgrading to 2-methylfuran represents a pivotal transformation in biomass valorization, offering a sustainable route to high-energy-density biofuels and versatile chemical intermediates. Herein, we recently synthesized a series of Co–Pt/ZrO2 catalysts and applied them as a highly efficient system to transform furfural selectively into 2-methylfuran. Results suggested that the bimetallic Co–Pt system facilitated the formation of the ZrO2 support in a tetragonal phase as well as the stabilization of both Co0 and Pt0 in reduced states. A strong interaction between Co and Pt was evidenced, and abundant Co–Pt interfaces were constructed even in the presence of Pt-lean Co20Pt1/ZrO2 system, causing electron transfer between Pt and the neighboring Co species. It subsequently changed the surface distribution of medium and strong acid sites, resulting in the promoted cleavage of the C–O(H) bond in the intermediate to produce 2-methylfuran. The stability of both the catalyst performances and the sample structure was simultaneously enhanced by the bimetallic Co20Pt1/ZrO2. 2-MF yield of 91.4% could be achieved at 220 °C with a very fast reaction rate of 3.74 mol2-MF/molCo/h.

title: On the Stability and Sensitivity of Climate‐Informed Flood Frequency Models
abstract: Abstract Reliable flood change projections under climate change are critical for water resources planning yet remain challenging due to uncertainty in climate‐informed statistical models. Conventional approaches relate flood distribution parameters to climate variables using log‐linear formulations, which can produce unrealistically large flood estimates. In this study, we develop a semi‐parametric statistical framework that constrains flood variability using a bounded logistic link function and estimates parameters from hydroclimatically analogous samples. Using 548 natural basins across the coterminous United States, we evaluate the proposed approach against log‐linear formulations from the entire sample. Model performances are assessed based on both the accuracy and sensitivity of flood quantiles to climate forcings. Results show that the proposed framework yields more stable and realistic flood quantile estimates, particularly under high precipitation conditions, and better preserves flood sensitivity. These findings highlight the value of bounded, locally informed statistical models for robust flood risk assessment under climate change.

title: Neurotrophic regulation of lipid metabolism in Alzheimer's disease: Mechanisms and therapeutic implications
abstract: Background Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder in which lipid metabolic dysregulation is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to pathogenesis. Neurotrophic factors (NTFs), beyond their established roles in neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity, may also regulate lipid metabolism. Objective To summarize current evidence on lipid metabolic dysregulation in AD and evaluate the potential roles of major NTFs in regulating lipid homeostasis. Methods Experimental, clinical, and translational studies addressing lipid metabolism, neurotrophic signaling, and their interactions in AD were reviewed, focusing on cholesterol, sphingolipid, and fatty acid metabolism and on BDNF, NGF, GDNF, CNTF, and Nrn1. Results Disturbances in cholesterol transport, sphingolipid and fatty acid metabolism, and high-density lipoprotein function may promote AD pathology by affecting membrane organization, synaptic plasticity, oxidative stress, insulin signaling, and amyloid-β and tau metabolism. BDNF, NGF, GDNF, CNTF, and Nrn1 may influence lipid-related processes through pathways including PI3K/Akt, AMPK, MAPK, and STAT3. However, evidence strength varies substantially among NTFs, and many proposed interactions are supported mainly by cellular, animal, or non-AD models. Conclusions Neurotrophic signaling and lipid metabolism may form an interconnected regula…

title: Targeted Secondary Metabolite Profiling in Eclipta Prostrata (L.) L.: Developmental Stage Dynamics, Tissue-Specific Distribution, and Stress-Induced Accumulation in Root and Shoot
Beta1 subunits enable fentanyl‐induced BK channel activation and opioid regulation of cerebral artery diameter
abstract: Ultra‐potent synthetic opioids are powerful analgesics but also a leading cause of drug overdose deaths. Calcium−/voltage‐gated potassium channels of large conductance (BK) control vital physiological processes, with their accessory β1 (encoded by Kcnmb1 in mice) subunit being predominantly expressed in smooth muscle. Thus, we hypothesize that BK β1 determines the effect of fentanyl on cerebral artery diameter. Here we report that fentanyl (0.001–10 μ m ) activates BK heteromers consisting of slo1 + β1 subunits in CHO cells, but not homomers of slo1. In ex vivo pressurized mouse cerebral arteries, pharmacological inhibition of BK or β1 genetic deletion ( Kcnmb1 −/− ) led to fentanyl‐induced vasoconstriction. Naloxone, an opioid receptor antagonist, ablates the fentanyl response in wild‐type cerebral arteries whereas mild constriction persists in Kcnmb 1 −/− arteries. Therefore, we identify BK β1 as a functional fentanyl target which acts independently of opioid receptors to regulate fentanyl action on cerebral artery diameter.

title: How Do the Frequency of Sexual Intercourse and the Division of Housework Relate to Happiness?
The effectiveness of emotion regulation training on meta-worry, mind wandering, and repetitive negative thinking in adolescent girls with anxiety symptoms
Sleep deprivation disrupts error awareness and subsequent behavioural regulation
abstract: Abstract Study Objectives Sleep deprivation is known to impair cognitive performance, yet its effects on error awareness and subsequent behavioural adjustments remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated how sleep loss affects the use of subjective performance evaluation to guide post-error adaptations Methods Thirty healthy adults completed a novel, gamified error awareness multi-rule Simon task once while well rested and once after one night of total sleep deprivation. On each trial, participants reported both their task response and subjective evaluation of response accuracy. This design allowed us to dissociate objective performance from subjective error awareness and to examine their influence on subsequent behaviour over time Results Sleep deprivation slowed responses, reduced accuracy, increased missed responses, and decreased the proportion of consciously detected errors, with impairments increasing over time on task. Both objective errors and subjective error judgements were associated with subsequent slowing. When well rested, subjective-error-associated slowing exceeded objective-error-associated slowing. This difference was reduced under sleep deprivation. Specifically, objectively correct responses judged as errors were followed by slowing relative to correctly judged correct responses, and this slowing was attenuated under sleep deprivation. Accuracy sho…

title: Institutional Capacity and Local Economic Development in Decentralized Local Authorities: An Empirical Analysis of Cameroon
abstract: This study examines the association between institutional capacity building (ICB) and local economic development (LED) among decentralised local authorities in Cameroon. It draws on the 2021 Capitalisation Survey of Achievements of the National Participatory Development Programme (ECA-PNDP), which covers 144 municipalities. Multidimensional indices of institutional capacity and local economic development are constructed from survey indicators using principal component analysis and equal-weight aggregation. Institutional capacity encompasses participatory governance, local planning, rationalisation of public investment, financial capacity and human capital. Local economic development is represented by economic infrastructure, employment, income and territorial attractiveness. The empirical analysis uses ordinary least squares regression, alternative index measures and quantile regression. The reported main regression includes 139 observations. Its fully adjusted specification indicates a positive association between institutional capacity and the survey-based LED index, with an estimated ICB coefficient of 0.0611 that is statistically significant at the 5% level. Alternative measures also yield positive associations, while quantile regression results vary across specifications. These findings suggest that administrative and financial management capacities warrant attention in ef…
venue: South Asian Journal of Social Studies and Economics

title: Mechanisms by which adaptive-capacity attributes can constrain responses of some small mammals to global change
abstract: Abstract Although habitat loss and degradation, invasive species, overexploitation, and pollution traditionally have constituted the most serious challenges to conservation of biodiversity, consequences of global change continue to rise in magnitude and spatio-temporal extent. Some taxa are known to exhibit low adaptive capacity to global change, but many other potentially vulnerable groups have received less attention, given their presumed low vulnerability. One such group is small mammals (≤5 kg), which are not perceived as particularly vulnerable despite constituting a large percentage of species of conservation concern. Herein, we identified six attributes from an existing adaptive-capacity framework that may hinder small mammals from adapting to contemporary global change: extent of occurrence, habitat specialization, dispersal distance, seasonal phenology, physiological tolerances, and reproductive phenology. We synthesize evidence for each attribute’s importance, illustrating diverse mechanisms of endangerment and response, and suggest that some small mammals may be more vulnerable to global change than previously thought.

title: Building Capacity in Paediatric Specialty Practice: Educational Priorities for Nigerian Occupational Therapy Practitioners
abstract: Background: Although occupational therapy (OT) educational priorities have been studied globally, evidence specific to pediatric practice in Nigeria remains limited, leaving a knowledge gap that may hinder entry-level practitioners' preparation for this specialist practice area. This study aimed to identify educational priorities for paediatric specialty practice among occupational therapy practitioners in Nigeria. Methodology: An exploratory mixed-method design comprising a cross-sectional survey and a two-round Delphi process was used. In Phase 1, 55 occupational therapy practitioners generated paediatric occupational therapy competencies using an online questionnaire. In Phase 2, these competencies were rated by paediatric occupational therapy experts (n = 17 in Round 1; n = 16 in Round 2). Data were analysed using thematic content analysis, descriptive statistics, and the content validity index (CVI). Competencies with CVI ≥ 0.80 were retained, those scoring 0.70–0.79 were revised, and items below 0.70 were excluded. Results: With a response rate of 57.3%, practitioners from diverse practice settings, with a mean professional experience of 4.6 ± 2.8 years, identified 46 competencies that were organised into five educational themes: basic medical and behavioural sciences; assessment and evaluation; professional values, attitudes, and skills; knowledge of paediatrics and occu…

title: Seaweed-derived biostimulants differentially enhance growth, nutritional composition, antioxidant capacity, and sensory quality of cultivated Caulerpa racemosa
abstract: Abstract Seaweed-derived biostimulants offer a promising strategy to enhance the productivity and functional quality of edible seaweeds. This study evaluated the effects of aqueous extracts from Halymenia sp., Halimeda sp., Sargassum sp., Kappaphycus sp., and Gracilaria sp. on the growth, biochemical composition, nutritional quality, antioxidant properties, and sensory acceptance of cultivated Caulerpa racemosa under controlled 35-day laboratory culture conditions. All extracts contained detectable phytohormones (indole-3-acetic acid, kinetin, zeatin, and gibberellic acid) as quantified by HPLC. Among the treatments, Halymenia extract produced the highest absolute growth (155.02 ± 25.00 g), specific growth rate (4.02 ± 0.35% day −1 ), chlorophyll accumulation, total amino acids (50.12 mg g −1 DW), protein level (11.37% DW), mineral enrichment, and sensory acceptance, which correlates strongly with growth-oriented primary metabolism. In contrast, Sargassum and Gracilaria extracts were more strongly associated with secondary metabolic and antioxidant-related responses, including higher total phenolic content, carotenoids, polyunsaturated fatty acids, and radical-scavenging activity. Crucially, Halymenia extract optimized the dietary Na/K ratio to 1.12 (compared with 3.72 in control), highlighting its potential to produce health-beneficial, low-sodium edible sea grapes. These find…

title: Counting the uncounted: suicide mortality and the limits of death registration in West Africa, a cross-sectional surveillance capacity analysis
Preserved anabolic skeletal muscle capacity in response to exercise and protein intake after critical illness
abstract: Abstract Background Low muscle mass and persistent weakness are common after critical illness, but the mechanisms behind impaired recovery are incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the skeletal muscle anabolic response to combined resistance exercise and protein intake in intensive care unit (ICU) survivors, compared to matched controls without a history of critical illness. We hypothesised that residual anabolic resistance limits muscle regeneration after ICU stay. Methods Former patients were enrolled within 3 to 6 months of intensive care unit discharge. Muscle biopsies were obtained before and after resistance exercise using a flywheel leg extension ergometer, combined with ingestion of 24 g hydrolysed protein. Muscle protein fractional synthetic rate was determined from the incorporation of [ring-²H₅]phenylalanine into mixed-muscle protein during a primed continuous intravenous infusion. Anabolic and proteolytic pathways were measured using standard assays. Group-by-time differences were analysed using linear mixed models. The primary comparison was the between-group difference in pre-to-post change in muscle protein synthesis. Results Twenty ICU survivors (60 ± 12 years, 30% female, BMI 26.9 (IQR 22.9–28.7), SAPS 3 62.3 ± 15.8) and 20 age- and sex-matched controls were included. ICU survivors had significantly lower quadriceps muscle thickness …

title: Functional capacity and body composition in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a cross-sectional study of their relationship with disease severity
An Analysis of Hospital Capacity and Available Data during the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Introduction One of the major concerns throughout the COVID-19 pandemic was whether health facilities had sufficient capacity to meet demands for care. Many states used healthcare capacity metrics to make decisions about the implementation of population-based disease mitigation measures. Methods Using facility-level data from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to examine hospital capacity and bed availability over the course of the COVID-19 pandemic, we calculated inpatient occupancy rates for hospitalizations of all-causes and COVID-19 and compared them across states, counties and on the national level. Results We found that in the aggregate, the national supply of staffed inpatient beds remained relatively constant during the pandemic despite the repeated stress of multiple COVID-19 waves. However, there was substantial heterogeneity among states and counties. Nationally, there was little association between the total availability of staffed hospital beds and reported COVID-19 cases. Conclusion Understanding how hospital capacity responds to pandemic waves is essential for future pandemic preparedness. Improved data systems, clearer staffed bed definitions and strategic capacity management are essential to ensure health systems can handle other health threats.

title: Enhancing citizens’ subjective wellbeing via electronic (e) government: the moderating effect of government capacity
Integrating network toxicology, machine learning and molecular dynamics simulation: Revealing the dynamic molecular mechanism by which 6PPD regulates lung cancer progression
Effect of Hollow Channel Cross-Section Shape on the Damage Mechanism of Reinforced Concrete Slabs Under Near-Field Blast Loading
abstract: Hollow-core reinforced concrete (RC) slabs are increasingly used for their reduced self-weight and integrated service voids, yet the influence of the internal channel cross-section shape on their behavior under near-field blast loading remains largely unexplored. Existing numerical studies on blast-loaded RC members focus almost exclusively on solid or circular-void cross-sections, leaving the systematic effect of void geometry unresolved. This study numerically investigates the contact detonation response of hollow-core RC slabs with three different channel cross-section shapes (square, circular, and hexagonal) using a coupled finite element method and smoothed particle hydrodynamics (FEM-SPH) approach in Abaqus/Explicit. The TNT charge is represented by the Jones-Wilkins-Lee (JWL) equation of state, concrete is modeled with the Concrete Damaged Plasticity (CDP) constitutive law, and an adaptive FEM-to-SPH conversion is employed in the contact region so that cratering and fragment ejection are captured without element-deletion artifacts. A parametric matrix of 48 models spanning three channel shapes, four lower-flange thicknesses (50-140 mm), and four charge masses (0.5-2.0 kg) was analyzed. The results show that the channel cross-section shape significantly governs blast resistance: the circular and hexagonal sections exhibit comparable performance and undergo approximately 2…
venue: The Eurasia Proceedings of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics

title: Current‐Controlled Inactive Aluminum Loss: Quantification, Mechanism, and Mitigation via Stack Pressure for Long‐Cycle Al‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aluminum‐ion batteries are a promising energy storage technology for high resource abundance, safety, and cost‐effectiveness advantages, but practical implementation is hindered by two degradation mechanisms in Al metal anode: electrically isolated metallic aluminum (iAl 0 ) and electrochemical side‐reaction products (iSEI Al 3+ ). Precise quantification of these inactive species and relationships with cycling reversibility have rarely been established, limiting rational anode design. Here, we develop a basic titration gas chromatography technology to accurately quantify iAl 0 and iSEI Al 3+ , revealing a current density‐dependent Al loss mechanism: iSEI Al 3+ loss dominates at low current, while metallic iAl 0 loss prevails at high current. We discover that an inorganic‐dominated interphase favors significant suppression of inactive Al formation. Applying an optimal stack pressure strategy (780 kPa) constructs tip‐localized stack pressure/electric field, effectively reducing inactive Al loss by 81.99% and prolonging battery cycling life by ≥500%. These advancements offer fundamental theory and techniques for Al anode reaction mechanism research and provide design principles for high‐performance aluminum‐ion battery.

title: The mechanism for creating “dynamical gravastar” black hole mimickers also explains formation of “little red dots”
abstract: In this paper, we argue that a high-pressure phase transition of relativistic matter to a state with negative energy density, which leads to the formation of horizonless, globally unitary black hole mimickers, also gives rise to the appearance of “little red dots”. The energy source for the dots is the release of latent energy from the phase transition, and their excess redness is a result of this release taking place in a central region of exponentially small positive [Formula: see text], and hence very high gravitational redshift.
venue: International Journal of Modern Physics D

title: Amelioration of early pathological changes in the 3xTg-AD mouse model: Mechanism of action of the Chinese herbal formula Tianqi Granules
abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline. This study investigated the effects of the Chinese herbal formula Tianqi Granules on early pathological progression in the 3xTg-AD mouse models and investigated the underlying mechanisms. After 31 days of Tianqi Granule treatment initiated at 5 months of age, Tianqi Granules-treated mice showed improved performance in the open-field test, novel object recognition test, and Morris water maze test. Amyloid deposition and glial activation were attenuated, and immunoreactivity for interleukin-1β and LC3 was reduced. Hippocampal transcriptome sequencing at multiple time points showed that, in untreated mice, early pathological progression occurred in three successive phases, with the dominant processes shifting from compensatory programs to failing homeostasis and subsequently to degenerative changes. Tianqi Granule treatment was associated with a three-phase response centered on the restoration of homeostasis and involving proteostasis, nuclear processes, lipid and carbohydrate metabolism, and redox-related pathways. Multiple biological domains were engaged rather than a single target. In males, an interferon-related program associated with Irf7 was induced early and shifted in the opposite direction under Tianqi Granule treatment during the same time window. …

title: Beyond the Vigil Mechanism: Whistle-Blower Protection, ESG Accountability, and the Case for Reform in Indian Corporate Governance
abstract: India’s corporate whistle-blower framework, built on Section 177 of the Companies Act, 2013, Regulation 22 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, and the SEBI Informant Mechanism, has expanded, yet India lacks a comprehensive private-sector whistle-blower protection statute. This paper asks whether the framework is a substantive governance safeguard or a compliance-driven formality. Using a doctrinal and analytical method, it reads the Narayana Murthy (2003), Irani (2005), and Kotak (2017) Committee reports together as a single legislative genealogy, and tests the resulting framework against the Satyam, Infosys, ICICI Bank–Videocon, and IL&FS episodes. The Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 serves as a domestic public-sector comparator. It finds that successive reforms strengthened audit-committee and disclosure structures without creating an external, enforceable right, leaving a regime that is procedurally sophisticated but substantively thin. Fragmented legislation, weak anti-retaliation remedies, uncertain confidentiality, and reliance on internal channels, together with hierarchical and socio-cultural barriers, continue to deter disclosure, weakening transparency, accountability, and stakeholder confidence. It proposes a dedicated private-sector statute, an independent whistle-blower authority, explicit anti-retaliation and confidentiality safeguards, external escalation …
venue: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

title: Molecular insights into GPR55 modulation reveal an atypical activation mechanism and glycosylation-dependent efficacy regulation
Interfacial Water‐Networks Regulate the Anodic Stability of Carbon Electrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon‐based materials are widely used in modern electrochemical technologies, yet their susceptibility to oxidation at positive electrode potentials poses a durability challenge. While this degradation has commonly been addressed through modification of the carbon material itself, the interfacial chemistry that activates carbon oxidation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that the hydrogen‐bonding (HB) network of interfacial water strongly influences anodic carbon stability. Operando differential electrochemical mass spectrometry combined with in situ attenuated total reflection surface‐enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy reveals that corrosion accelerates as the interfacial HB network becomes increasingly disrupted, implicating weakly H‐bonded water as a reactive water population associated with carbon oxidation. Guided by this mechanistic insight, we modulate the local water structure using ionomer‐defined interfaces. In a case study of chlorine evolution on a carbon‐supported single‐atom Pt catalyst, Sustainion‐defined interfaces preserve a more ordered interfacial water‐network and suppress carbon corrosion relative to Nafion‐defined interfaces, whereas the latter promote surface charging favorable for chlorine evolution kinetics. By combining these functions in a mixed‐ionomer layer, water‐network‐guided stabilization is implemented under anodic elect…

title: Electrochemical performance of waste almond shell-derived activated carbon as a hybrid supercapacitor electrode
The linking problem: emissions trading, investment treaty jurisdiction, and the globalization of carbon markets
abstract: Abstract In 2024, an arbitral tribunal dismissed for lack of jurisdiction a claim brought by Koch Industries against Canada arising from the cancellation of Ontario’s cap-and-trade programme. This article argues that the award should be read not as a case-specific outcome but as the first encounter in investment treaty arbitration with a structural problem that will recur with increasing frequency as carbon markets globalize and establish links. Emissions trading systems are dynamic regulatory instruments whose caps must contract, whose rules will change as governments respond to shifting political priorities, energy security pressures, and geopolitical disruption, and whose linking arrangements may be modified or terminated. When regulatory action impairs or extinguishes allowances held by foreign investors across a linked system, the domestic legal character of those allowances enters a jurisdictional analysis whose structure and decisive threshold vary according to the treaty definition, the arbitral forum, and the interpretive methodology of the tribunal. The article examines Koch v Canada as the first decided investment case and traces the mechanism through two further configurations under a broad asset-based bilateral investment treaty and the Energy Charter Treaty, demonstrating that the same instrument may or may not constitute a protected investment depending on a conf…

title: Controllable Preparation of Nickel/Titanium Dioxide/Carbon Nanotube Heterostructures and their Electrochemical Performance
Construction of Hydrophilic Percolation Networks in Physical Wet‐Mixed Carbon Electrodes for High‐Rate Capacitive Deionization
abstract: ABSTRACT Capacitive deionization (CDI) using activated carbon (AC) electrodes holds great promise for seawater desalination, yet its practical application is severely constrained by the intrinsic hydrophobicity of carbon surfaces. Herein, we propose a solid‐state superhydrophilic modulation strategy that physically wet‐mixes superhydrophilic MOF‐derived hollow carbon nanocages (CMNC) with commercial AC to obtain a carbon‐based pseudocapacitive electrode composite. This simple blending directly imparts superhydrophilicity to the AC surface (contact angle as low as 5.11°) through constructing hydrophilic percolation networks, which effectively alleviates the diffusion limitation of Cl − ions by optimizing interfacial wettability, while preserving the intrinsic electrochemical performance of the metal‐organic framework‐derived (MOF‐derived) nanocages despite dilution. The blending of the CMNC with different nanocarbons (activated carbon/AC, carbon nanotube/CNT, graphene oxide/GO) and its impact on wettability and CDI performance were also examined. The optimal CMNC 1 AC 1 electrode (mass ratio 1:1) achieves a salt adsorption capacity of 57.2 mg g −1 , a desalination rate of 1.91 mg g −1 min −1 , and a charge efficiency of 87.46% in 500 mg L −1 NaCl at 1.2 V. This performance approaches that of pure CMNC and far exceeds AC, yet utilizes only half the MOF‐derived material, demonstra…

title: Halogen‑Engineered Nitrogen‑Doped Carbon for Dual Nonradical Peroxymonosulfate Activation in Water Purification
abstract: ABSTRACT Peroxymonosulfate (PMS)‐based advanced oxidation processes are attractive for water purification but are often limited by short‐lived radicals that are easily quenched in complex matrices. Here we report a halogen‐modulation strategy to engineer the interfacial microenvironment of nitrogen‐doped carbon (N‐C) for robust, metal‐free PMS activation. A family of halogen‐doped carbons (NX‐C; X = F, Cl, Br, and I) is synthesized via molten‐salt‐assisted conversion of ZIF‐8, among which bromine‐doped N‐C (NBr‐C) exhibits a lattice‐strained, hierarchically porous framework with highly polarized graphitic‐N sites. NBr‐C delivers a 134‐fold enhancement in the phenol degradation rate constant ( k obs = 2.55 min −1 ) and 70.5% total organic carbon (TOC) removal within 5 min. Mechanistic experiments combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that Br doping steers PMS activation away from short‐lived radicals toward dual nonradical pathways: singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) oxidation and a catalyst‐mediated direct electron‐transfer process. The NBr‐C/PMS system maintains nearly complete pollutant removal over pH 3–11, in the presence of common inorganic anions and natural organic matter, in real waters, and under continuous‐flow operation. This work establishes halogen‐regulated interfacial microenvironment engineering as a powerful principle for designing robust, met…

title: Fabrication of large-sized robust carbon aerogel composites via pre-shrinkage-induced interfacial engineering
abstract: Abstract We report a strategy for synthesizing crack-free carbon aerogel (CA) composites by rationally matching the carbonization shrinkage of viscose fiber felts (VFs) with that of a phenolic resin (PR) aerogel matrix. The VFs were pretreated at elevated temperatures to induce controlled pre-shrinkage, followed by an in situ sol-gel transition and ambient-pressure drying of the PR precursor to produce large monolithic organic aerogels. By selecting a pretreatment temperature of 265 °C, the fibers and the matrix showed nearly identical subsequent carbonization shrinkages (26.2% versus 25.0%). This matched shrinkage drastically reduced residual stress, yielding a defect content of only 2% and a continuous, gradient interface without cracks or voids. The optimal composite achieved specific compressive and flexural strengths of 106.9 and 29.1 MPa·g − 1 ·cm 3 , respectively, along with a fracture toughness of 0.54 MPa·m 1/2 , significantly outperforming composites with mismatched shrinkages. Compared with conventional non-pre-shrunk counterparts, this design achieves a 91% reduction in residual stress and a 94% decrease in structural defects, resulting in 3.0-fold and 2.5-fold improvements in specific compressive and flexural strengths, respectively, as well as a 2.3-fold increase in fracture toughness. The design principle was further exploited to tune the matrix microstructure an…

title: Bimetallic Oxide/Carbon Fiber Heterodimensional Structure Toward Dual Electromagnetic Attenuation Functions
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving concurrent high‐performance electromagnetic absorption and electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding within a single material system at a fixed filler loading remains a significant challenge. Here, a heterodimensional structural strategy for CuCo 2 O 4 @C is proposed to reconcile dielectric and magnetic responses. The dielectric relaxation loss is dominated by Jahn–Teller distortion, coupled with contributions from carbon defects and CuCo 2 O 4 @C interfaces. The magnetic response is primarily driven by Metal–Oxygen–Metal (M–O–M) superexchange interactions that modulate the magnetic precession, complemented by the eddy current effect. The prepared CuCo 2 O 4 @C composite successfully integrates the dual functions of electromagnetic absorption and EMI shielding. The total functional bandwidth of the CuCo 2 O 4 @C composite is 4.24 GHz at a thickness of 1.8 mm, including an effective absorption bandwidth of 2.72 GHz and an EMI shielding bandwidth of 1.52 GHz. When its thickness increased to 2.6 mm, the total functional bandwidth was extended to 6.48 GHz (0.56 GHz for absorption and 5.92 GHz for shielding). This work offers a promising route for miniaturization and functional integration of electromagnetic attenuating materials and devices.

title: Modulation of Mechanical Properties in Ti3AlC2 via B Substitution and Charge-Compensation-Induced Carbon Vacancies
abstract: Abstract Tuning the intrinsic bonding and mechanical behavior of MAX phases is crucial for tailoring their performance. In this work, a series of Ti3AlC2–xBx MAX phase ceramics were fabricated via spark plasma sintering, and we systematically investigated the effects of B substitution on their crystal structure, bonding characteristics, and mechanical properties through a combination of experiments and theoretical calculations. B substitution creates local electronic imbalance within the M–X layers, which in turn promotes carbon vacancy formation via charge compensation process. The interplay between B incorporation and Cv formation induces further structural relaxation and charge redistribution. As a result, the resistance to elastic failure and plastic deformation failure is enhanced by 27.6% and 76.0%, respectively, under the synergistic influence of M–X bonds and Cv. However, under high B concentrations, excessive Cv accumulation destabilizes the Ti3C2 layers and drives the formation of Ti2AlC. Overall, this work systematically unravels how B substitution modifies the Ti3AlC2 structure, offering valuable insights into the regulation of X-site chemistry and bonding in MAX phases.

title: Emulating absent land processes reduces carbon budgets in CMIP6 models
abstract: Abstract The Transient Climate Response to cumulative Emissions (TCRE) is the cornerstone of estimates of carbon emissions budgets to future warming targets, characterising the near-linear relationship between the increase in global mean temperature and cumulative emissions of CO 2 . TCRE is derived from highly sophisticated Earth System Models (ESMs) - some, however, lack important processes known to have a large impact on TCRE. Here, we use multiple configurations of UKESM, a full-complexity ESM, to estimate how TCRE of 11 ESMs that participated in Coupled Model Intercomparison Project 6 would change if each included six terrestrial carbon cycle related processes present in UKESM, such as nitrogen limitation of photosynthesis and fire-vegetation interactions. We find that accounting for processes not included in the models increases their TCRE by an average of 21.4% implying a reduction of 16.0% ± 0.8% in the carbon budget for the transition from 1.5 °C to 2 °C.

title: Lanthanum‐Based Perovskite Oxides and Graphitic Carbon Nitride Composite Nanostructures for Electrochemical Ascorbic Acid Detection
abstract: Accurate determination of ascorbic acid (AA, vitamin C), an essential, water‐soluble antioxidant widely found in foods and pharmaceutical products and playing a critical role in human health, is important for clinical diagnosis, pharmaceutical analysis, and food quality control. Therefore, developing electrochemical sensing platforms with high sensitivity, rapid response, low cost, and simple operating principles is essential for the precise and selective determination of AA. In this study, LaBO 3 /g‐C 3 N 4 (B = Mn, Fe, Co) nanocomposites were synthesized via a solution combustion route followed by ultrasonic coupling with graphitic carbon nitride (g‐C 3 N 4 ), and their electrochemical performance toward AA detection was systematically investigated. Comprehensive structural and physicochemical analyses confirmed the generation of highly crystalline perovskite oxides and their successful integration with g‐C 3 N 4 . LaCoO 3 /g‐C 3 N 4 (LCO/GCN) displayed superior optoelectronic and electrochemical properties, exhibiting the highest electrocatalytic activity toward AA oxidation with good selectivity, excellent reproducibility, operational cycling stability over 100 cycles, and successful applicability to real vitamin C samples analyses.

title: Variable dissolved organic carbon trends in the tributaries of the St. Lawrence River driven by natural geographic features and human activities
abstract: Over the past decades, dissolved organic carbon (DOC) concentrations in boreal rivers have increased broadly. At the regional scale, however, the magnitude of these trends varies, likely reflecting differences in natural and anthropogenic catchment features that remain poorly understood. Here we examined long-term DOC trends data from 89 stations located on 54 tributaries of the St. Lawrence River (Qc, Canada) over 35 years, assessing DOC changes among catchments with contrasting natural characteristics and land-use patterns. We observed a significant increase in DOC in 46 stations (0.08–1.54% per year), and a significant decrease in 19 stations (−0.25 to −1.59% per year). When considering climatic variables and land cover features, the proportion of forested area within the watershed emerged as the most significant factor; DOC tended to increase at forest cover >60% and to be stable or decrease at forest cover <60%. Watershed slope, water area, and annual mean precipitation were also significantly associated with DOC changes. This study emphasizes the importance of accounting for land-use differences when interpreting regional patterns of river DOC trends.

title: Cluster‐Scale MoO x ‐IrO 2 Heterointerfaces Steer Dual‐Site Coupling and Interfacial Water Dynamics for Fast and Durable Oxygen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are central to renewable‐powered green hydrogen production. As the benchmark electrocatalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), conventional single‐phase IrO 2 is constrained by linear scaling relations among oxygenated intermediates, compounded by severe mass‐transport limitations and poorly regulated interfacial water structures. Here, we design a Turing‐type MoO x ‐IrO 2 heterostructure with strongly coupled cluster‐scale interfaces, which enables dual‐function Ir‐Mo synergy that breaks fundamental kinetic limitations and optimizes interfacial water structures. At the reaction pathway level, Brønsted‐acidic MoO x clusters promote water dissociation to generate reactive Mo─OH* intermediates, triggering radical coupling with adjacent Ir─O* species to form OOH* and thus circumventing the linear scaling relation. At the interfacial microenvironment level, MoO x reorganizes the rigid hydrogen‐bonding networks and increases the population of free H 2 O species, effectively alleviating concentration overpotentials under high‐current‐density operation. When integrated into a practical 25 cm 2 membrane electrode assembly, this catalyst delivers a PEMWE cell voltage of 1.71 V at 3 A cm −2 and an ultralow degradation rate of ∼9.5 µV h −1 over 1000 h, with a total platinum‐group‐metal loading of merely 0.5 mg cm −2 acr…

title: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels
abstract: Abstract Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are essential for rhythmic electrical activity in cardiac and neuronal cells, and their dysfunction underlies disorders such as arrhythmia and epilepsy. Although HCN channels share a conserved six-transmembrane architecture with voltage-gated K⁺ (Kv) channels, how voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) are coupled to pore opening remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify an extracellular pathway that couples voltage-sensor movement to pore opening via the extracellular turret helix, which acts as a critical determinant of voltage-dependent gating in HCN channels. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis of HCN4 revealed six turret residues whose substitution abolished hyperpolarization-evoked currents. Voltage-clamp fluorometry showed that these mutations preserved S4 activation while selectively disrupting turret conformational changes, thereby uncoupling VSD movement from pore opening. Structural and functional analyses further identified an extracellular interaction network linking the turret to the S1, S5, and S6 segments that is essential for hyperpolarization-dependent gating. Collectively, these findings identify the extracellular turret as an active gating hub that coordinates concerted extracellular rearrangements to transmit voltage-sensor displacement to the pore. On the basis of these results, we propo…

Liquid‐Liquid Phase Separation Modulated Thylakoid–Enzyme Interfacial Coupling for Enhanced Light‐Powered Biocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Thylakoid (TK) membranes serve as promising photosynthesis platforms for light‐driven biocatalysis, yet their catalytic efficiency is largely restricted by poor coupling between photo‐dependent NADPH regeneration and enzymatic conversion. Herein, we report a facile TK‐anchored enzyme condensate strategy to overcome this bottleneck. Specifically, the UTX‐derived intrinsically disordered region (IDR) fused with target enzymes mediates liquid–liquid phase separation to form enzyme‐rich condensates, which then stably anchor on TK membranes and spatially confine catalysis at the NADPH‐generating membrane interface. Taking carbonyl reductase Sm CR V4 and ene‐reductase Ss ER A314S as model enzymes, the TK–enzyme hybrid condensates exhibit prominently improved catalytic performance, especially under NADPH regeneration‐limited conditions, relative to freely dispersed enzyme systems. The TK–UTX‐ Sm CR V4 hybrid improves the total product yield up to 3.1‐fold, and the TK–UTX‐ Ss ER A314S hybrid reaches a 2.9‐fold higher conversion within 20 min. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics simulations validate a dynamic multivalent interfacial anchoring mode: the IDR domain mediates stable membrane binding via high‐frequency residue–lipid interactions dominated by short‐range Lennard–Jones forces (with auxiliary electrostatic contributions), while the enzyme domain remains solvent‐exposed. …

title: Uncertainties in the determination of the trilinear Higgs coupling from single-Higgs observables
abstract: Abstract Circular $${\text{e}}^{+} {\text{e}}^{-}$$ e + e - colliders operating at energies below the di-Higgs production threshold can provide information on the trilinear Higgs self-coupling $$\lambda _{\text {hhh}}$$ λ hhh via its loop contributions to single-Higgs production processes and electroweak precision observables. We investigate how well a non-SM value of $$\lambda _{\text {hhh}}$$ λ hhh can be determined indirectly via its loop contributions within a global EFT fit. Using an inert doublet extension of the SM Higgs sector as an example for a scenario of physics beyond the SM that could be realised in nature, we find that theoretical uncertainties related to the treatment of loop contributions and the truncation of the EFT expansion, which are usually neglected, play an important role in determining the sensitivity to $$\lambda _{\text {hhh}}$$ λ hhh in a global fit. The results obtained from such an indirect determination of $$\lambda _{\text {hhh}}$$ λ hhh without taking these additional uncertainties into account should be considered to be too optimistic, leading to an artificially high precision in the determination of $$\lambda _{\text {hhh}}$$ λ hhh . Such results could therefore be misleading in the quest to precisely identify the underlying physics of electroweak symmetry breaking.

title: Metabolic–epigenetic coupling links glycolysis to macrophage–mediated myelin clearance after peripheral nerve injury
abstract: Abstract Macrophages are essential for myelin clearance following peripheral nerve injury, yet the mechanisms linking their functional heterogeneity to metabolic regulation remain unclear. Single-cell RNA sequencing was combined with functional assays to characterize macrophage heterogeneity and investigate the relationship between metabolic reprogramming and myelin clearance after peripheral nerve injury. A distinct macrophage subset enriched was identified after injury that exhibited elevated expression of glycolysis-related and phagocytosis-associated genes. Functional analyses demonstrated that glycolytic activity was positively associated with macrophage-mediated myelin clearance. Among candidate regulators, solute carrier family 2 member 6 was highly expressed in this subset, and its knockdown impaired glycolysis, lactate production, histone lactylation and myelin clearance capacity, effects that were partially rescued by metabolic intervention or lactate supplementation. In vivo , lactate administration was associated with enhanced myelin clearance and improved nerve structural and functional recovery. These findings provide new insights into the interplay between metabolic reprogramming and immune function in nerve injury. These results provide a mechanistic foundation for the development of metabolism-targeted therapeutic strategies to enhance peripheral nerve regenera…

title: Synergistic Enhancement of Creep Performance in Al 19 Co 21 Fe 20 Ni 40 Eutectic High‐Entropy Alloy by Coupling Heterostructure Design With Boron‐Assisted Interfacial Optimization
abstract: ABSTRACT This study systematically investigates the creep behavior of an Al 19 Co 21 Fe 20 Ni 40 eutectic high‐entropy alloy (EHEA) at 500°C, focusing on the synergistic effects of heterostructure design and trace boron doping. Thermomechanical processing was employed to produce a heterostructure consisting of alternating lamellar and equiaxed regions. Creep tests reveal that this heterostructured alloy achieves a remarkable 320% increase in creep life compared to the as‐cast baseline. This enhancement originates from hetero‐deformation induced (HDI) strengthening, which drives the hard B2 phase to actively participate in co‐deformation alongside the FCC phase, effectively dispersing localized stress concentrations. Building on this heterostructure, the addition of 0.1 wt% boron further optimizes the FCC/B2 interfaces, yielding an additional 42% improvement in creep life. Geometric phase analysis demonstrates that boron strengthens the FCC/B2 interface, significantly reducing localized shear strain and stress concentration. This optimized interfacial state effectively suppresses the nucleation and growth of creep voids, delaying overall damage accumulation. These findings provide a practical strategy for developing advanced heat‐resistant EHEAs.

title: Development and characterization of starch–gelatin edible films reinforced with lemon peel and pomegranate peel powders
abstract: The development of sustainable alternatives to petroleum-based food packaging has increased interest in biodegradable edible films derived from renewable resources. In this study, powdered lemon ( Citrus limon ) and pomegranate ( Punica granatum ) peels were directly incorporated into starch gelatin matrices to produce edible films through a simple waste valorization approach. The effects of peel type on the morphology, water holding capacity, and mechanical behavior of the films were comparatively investigated. The pomegranate peel-reinforced films exhibited higher load-bearing capacity, whereas the lemon peel-reinforced films showed higher water holding capacity and greater flexibility. Scanning electron microscopy revealed distinct morphological differences between the two formulations, with the lemon peel-reinforced film exhibiting a relatively rougher and more heterogeneous surface, while the pomegranate peel-reinforced film displayed a comparatively smoother and more continuous morphology. These morphological differences were consistent with the observed differences in hydration and mechanical behavior. Overall, the findings demonstrate the potential of whole fruit peel powders as sustainable bio-based reinforcements for starch–gelatin edible films and highlight their potential for biodegradable food-packaging applications.

title: Ether-Based Ionic Gel Electrolytes with High Ionic Conductivity and High Thermal Stability for Energy Storage Device Applications
abstract: Abstract The current ionic gel electrolyte (IGE) materials cannot simultaneously achieve high ionic conductivity and high thermal stability. The regulatory mechanism of the ether functional groups on the interaction between ions still needs further investigation. Based on the above research status, this work relied on the σ-profile curve of the conductor-like screening model for real solvents (COSMO-RS) to compare the interface characteristics of different ionic liquids (IL). N-methyl-N-methoxyethyl pyrrolidine bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt ([C1OC2Pyr][TFSI]) was screened as the ionic conductive source. Poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) was chosen as the polymer substrate. A series of IGEs were successfully prepared by adjusting the mass ratio of the IL to the substrate material. IGE-3 sample (with an IL to PVDF-HFP mass ratio of 1:3) exhibited excellent comprehensive performance. This ionic gel presented a continuous, uniform, and loose network structure without obvious agglomeration. The thermal stability temperature was up to 380 oC, the electrochemical stability window reached 5.3 V, and the ionic conductivity was 4.25 × 10–3 S·cm–1. IGE-3 was assembled into a supercapacitor (cell-3). The coulombic efficiency of the device reached 97.9% at 1 A·g–1. Based on density functional theory (DFT) calculations, the intermolecular interactions of I…

title: Verbal Energy as Value-Oriented Discourse: Shakarim Qudaiberdiuly’s Poetic Language and Its Educational Significance
abstract: This study reconceptualizes verbal energy as a discourse-pragmatic effect produced when linguistic form, evaluative positioning, and culturally shared values converge in a literary or public utterance. It examines how Shakarim Qudaiberdiuly (1858-1931), a Kazakh poet and moral philosopher, uses language to orient readers toward reflection, knowledge, civic responsibility, and ethical action. The study addresses three questions: which linguistic resources generate verbal energy; how those resources encode cultural and moral values; and what educational implications follow from their interaction. A purposive micro-corpus of five passages – three poetic excerpts and two historically documented public-address episodes – was analyzed qualitatively. The coding framework combined addressivity, speech-act force, appraisal, conceptual metaphor, repetition, parallelism, and directive positioning. The findings identify four mutually reinforcing mechanisms: direct address constructs an accountable audience; evaluative contrasts organize moral choice; journey, elevation, illness-remedy, and inexhaustible-resource metaphors convert abstract values into actionable images; and rhythmic parallelism increases memorability and collective resonance. Verbal energy is therefore not treated as a measurable physical property of isolated words, but as an interpretive effect arising from patterned langu…

NaPF6-Based Battery Electrolytes near a Sodium Metal Electrode: Role of Organic Solvents on Solid Electrolyte Interphase Formation
abstract: Abstract The choice of electrolytes for improved sodium-metal batteries (SMBs) presents a major challenge owing to the complexity of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) between the electrode and electrolyte. Herein, we systematically examine and compare the dissociation mechanism of electrolytes consisting of sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF6) in three different organic solvents with varying polarity (tetrahydrofuran (THF), propylene carbonate (PC), and a mixture of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate (EC:DEC)) on the sodium metal surface using density functional theory (DFT) and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. For the NaPF6-THF and NaPF6-PC electrolyte systems, the study reveals the strong reducing nature of the PF6– anion, which readily dissociates and dominates over the solvent molecules present in the system. Our analysis reveals that the solvent molecules, THF and PC, are relatively stable against reductive dissociation over sodium metal in their respective electrolyte solutions. Conversely, in the EC:DEC-based electrolyte, SEI formation is derived from both the anion and EC, and DEC molecules remain undissociated within the simulation timescale. Further, the induced charge (electron) density difference approach captures the charge depletion and accumulation on the sodium electrode and electrolyte species, respectively.
