Mineral Particle Suspensions in Carbonate Electrolyte Enable LiF‐Rich Interphases for Durable Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The solid electrolyte interphase in lithium metal batteries determines cycling stability but often suffers from the incomplete decomposition of fluorinated components. Herein, we demonstrate that suspending LiF and Li 2 O particles in a carbonate‐based electrolyte promotes the defluorination of fluoroethylene carbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate. These particles preferentially adsorb fluorinated electrolyte species and induce electronic polarization, thereby modulating their redox reactivity and facilitating interfacial decomposition toward LiF. The generated LiF, together with the trace dissolution and interfacial reprecipitation of suspended LiF particles, continuously enriches the electrode surface with LiF‐rich inorganic species. This process results in the formation of a bilayer interphase on both the lithium metal anode and LiNi 0.6 Co 0.2 Mn 0.2 O 2 cathode, featuring a flexible inner layer and a dense LiF‐rich outer layer. The resulting interphase suppresses lithium dendrites, mitigates parasitic reactions, and enables 2400 h of stable cycling in symmetric cells and 85.6% capacity retention after 400 cycles in full cells. By introducing suspended LiF/Li 2 O particles to regulate the interfacial decomposition of fluorinated electrolyte species, this work provides an effective electrolyte‐design strategy for constructing robust interphases in lithium metal b…

title: Gate-to-Gate Life Cycle Assessment of Solidified Natural Gas Production via Clathrate Hydrate Formation: Environmental Trade-Offs of Thermodynamic Promoter Selection
abstract: Abstract Solidified natural gas (SNG) is a potential alternative to liquefied and compressed natural gas for natural gas storage, but its environmental performance has not been quantified. This study presents the first life cycle assessment of SNG production via clathrate hydrate formation, comparing unpromoted methane hydrate (sI), methane–tetrahydrofuran (THF) hydrate (sII), and methane–1,3-dioxolane hydrate (sII). A gate-to-gate assessment was performed using ReCiPe 2016 (H) with a functional unit of 1 MJ of natural gas stored as methane hydrate. Since unconverted methane is recycled, all configurations consume the same net quantity of methane, and the higher conversion of the promoted systems (42.0% versus 10.0%) instead reduces electricity demand from 0.116 to approximately 0.030 kW h MJ–1. The unpromoted process had the lowest impact in all 18 midpoint categories, including the lowest global warming potential (0.070 kg CO2-eq MJ–1) and end point single score (1.83 mPt). The global warming potentials of the 1,3-dioxolane- and THF-promoted processes were 3.0 and 4.7 times higher, with promoter production contributing 83% and 89%, respectively. Paired Monte Carlo analysis confirmed these rankings, with 1,3-dioxolane outperforming THF in 87–100% of iterations depending on the category. The ranking was unchanged under a 20-year characterization horizon and would be reversed on…

High-Speed Energy-Efficient Resonant Modulator on a Graphene-Organic Hybrid Platform
abstract: Abstract Resonant electro-optic modulators are of interest for encoding electrical signals to the optical domain with an option to perform simultaneous wavelength-division multiplexing while reducing the modulation energy consumption. Here, we demonstrate a compact, high-speed, and energy-efficient resonant modulator exploiting the ultrafast characteristics of graphene and organic materials, enabling efficient electro-optic modulation on the silicon platform. Graphene, with its extraordinary electronic and optical properties, is used as a transparent electrode material that brings the radio frequency field close to the photonic mode with minimal extra losses, while the organic material provides a high linear electro-optic coefficient. This arrangement provides both efficient light modulation in a compact device with an active length of 50 μm and a large modulation bandwidth of ∼35 GHz. High-speed data transmission experiments demonstrate a line rate of 320 Gbit/s, while a rate of 128 Gbit/s is achieved under CMOS-compatible voltages with energy consumption of ∼10.1 femtojoules per bit. The presented technology offers a practical and promising route toward integration of graphene into high-speed communication links.

title: Facilitating Charge Transport and Utilization in Mo-BiVO4 via FeCo-Metal–Organic Framework Dual-Function Modification for Efficient Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting
abstract: Abstract The photoelectrochemical water splitting performance of BiVO4 photoanodes has historically been constrained by poor charge transport and sluggish water oxidation kinetics. Here, we design a heterojunction photoanode by coupling Mo-doped BiVO4 with a bimetallic FeCo-metal–organic framework (MOF) constructed using an extended π-conjugated linker (4,4′-biphenyldicarboxylic acid). The bimetallic FeCo-MOF based on the elongated backbone simultaneously serves as a hole-extraction layer that facilitates interfacial charge separation and an excellent oxygen evolution cocatalyst. It not only establishes an efficient charge transport channel but also plays a crucial role in improving the surface reaction kinetics. The optimized Mo-BiVO4/FeCo-MOF photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 4.18 mA cm−2 at 1.23 V vs RHE and maintains stable operation for over 20 h, substantially outperforming pristine BiVO4. This work highlights the synergistic benefits of linker-engineered bimetallic MOF for high-performance solar water oxidation.

title: Solvent‐Free Roll‐Pressed Sandwiched Li Anode With Dual‐Sided Cu Nanowire Networks for High‐Energy Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Li metal anodes are promising for next‐generation high‐energy batteries, but their practical use is hindered by dendritic Li growth, unstable interfaces, and large volume fluctuations. Herein, we report a bidirectional sandwich‐structured Li metal anode (SLA) fabricated through a solvent‐free rolling and pressing strategy. The SLA integrates an ultrathin Li layer with thermally stable 3D Cu nanowire networks on both sides, forming a lightweight, flexible, and mechanically robust electrode. The interconnected Cu nanowire framework provides continuous electron pathways, homogenizes current distribution, and accommodates Li volume changes, thereby guiding uniform Li deposition and stripping within the electrode interior. Benefiting from this design, the SLA achieves a high Coulombic efficiency of 98.73% over 250 cycles at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 , while symmetric cells operate stably for over 1350 h with low polarization. Full cells paired with high‐loading NCM811 cathodes deliver excellent cycling stability and rate capability. For a 4‐layer stacked pouch cell, the SLA‐based system delivers a gravimetric energy density of 279.11 Wh kg −1 and a volumetric energy density of 470.52 Wh L −1 , outperforming the PLA counterpart. This work provides a simple strategy for advancing stable Li metal anodes and high‐energy‐density Li metal batteries.

title: Energy, Exergy, and Economic Assessment of a Modified Double‐Slope Solar Still Using Low‐Cost Heat‐Storage Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT In many arid and water‐scarce regions, the need for new methods of desalination that are inexpensive and environmentally friendly remains high as access to drinking water continues to be insufficient. Solar stills offer a viable solution, but their widespread use is limited due to low freshwater production and poor thermal performance. The current research investigates a traditional single‐slope solar still (TSS), a double‐slope solar still, and four modified double‐slope solar stills (with iron scraps, black Kanchey, shaving blade fins, and pebbles as thermal energy storage, respectively) (MSS‐1, MSS‐2, MSS‐3, MSS‐4, MSS‐5). In the study, MSS‐1 was the unmodified double‐slope system. The daily water yield in mL/day for various stills was recorded as follows: TSS: 1330, MSS‐1: 1890, MSS‐2: 2370, MSS‐3: 2450, MSS‐4: 3150, and MSS‐5: 2250. The MSS‐4 system (shaving blades) outperforms TSS, presenting the highest yield, increasing productivity by 136%. The peak energy efficiency for different solar stills was as follows: TSS: 29%, MSS‐1: 36.6%, MSS‐2: 46.5%, MSS‐3: 49.5%, MSS‐4: 52.5%, and MSS‐5: 38.3%, with MSS‐4 achieving the highest value of 58.5%. The maximum exergy efficiency recorded was TSS: 10%, MSS‐1: 11.5%, MSS‐2: 15.5%, MSS‐3: 19.6%, MSS‐4: 23.7%, and MSS‐5: 17.4%. title: Rewriting the Divide: Child-Centred Participation and Theoretically Informed and Evidence-Based Intervention Design
abstract: Abstract This paper contributes to debates on problematic, dominant criminological narratives by foregrounding children’s own accounts of the support they need to thrive, informing ongoing efforts to support their individual and moral development. Drawing on community-based, participatory focus groups and individual and small-group interviews with 58 children aged 10–17 attending youth centres in Cambridge (UK), the study departs from deficit-oriented, adult-led explanations that frame children primarily through risk, mental disorders, or criminalisation. The findings rework prevailing criminological intervention approaches in two ways. First, using reflexive thematic analysis, the study centres children’s lived knowledge to identify trust, belonging, voice, agency, relational consistency of care, emotional support, and autonomy as central to what makes interventions trustworthy, accessible, engaging, and effective, whilst overly didactic, rigid, or authoritarian approaches were identified as key barriers to participation and effectiveness. These accounts move beyond adult assumptions about children’s needs, showing that effective support is grounded in relational, dialogic, autonomy-supportive environments rather than deficit-oriented models. Second, the paper argues that centring children’s perspectives is necessary but not sufficient: interventions must also be theoretically…

title: Assessment Strategies of Art and Design Curricula in Enhancing Employability Skills among University Students of Kyambogo University, Uganda
abstract: Purpose: This study examined the relationship between formative and summative assessment practices and employability skills among undergraduate Art and Design students at Kyambogo University. Methodology: A quantitative approach and correlational research design were used. Data were collected through a self-administered questionnaire from 378 students. Descriptive statistics, Pearson’s product-moment correlation, and multiple regression were used to analyse the data. Findings: Formative assessment (r = .329, p < .001) and summative assessment (r = .262, p < .001) were positively and significantly correlated with employability skills. The regression model was statistically significant, F = 28.921, p < .001, and explained 13.4% of the variance in employability skills (R² = .134; adjusted R² = .129). Formative assessment (β = .271, p < .001) and summative assessment (β = .170, p = .001) were both significant positive predictors, with formative assessment showing the stronger association. Conclusion: Both formative and summative assessment are associated with employability skills, particularly when formative assessment provides regular feedback, reflection, and opportunities for peer and self-assessment, and summative tasks require students to demonstrate competencies in authentic, professionally relevant contexts. title: Understanding the Instability Origin for Design of Robust Pure RuO2 Anode Catalyst in PEM Water Electrolysis
abstract: Abstract Ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) shows great promise as an acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalyst in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), yet its insufficient stability─often attributed to Ru overoxidation─actually has a hidden cause. Herein, we show that the true culprit is instead residual chloride impurities inherited from the most commonly used RuCl3 precursor. Owing to strong Ru–Cl coordination, substantial chlorine residues are trapped in the RuO2 lattice during conventional synthesis; during electrolysis, they gradually leach out, dramatically accelerating Ru dissolution and lattice oxygen loss and triggering structural collapse. Guided by this insight, we developed a small-molecule-assisted synthesis that yields Cl-free RuO2. The resulting catalyst preserves exceptional structural integrity, sustains its initial activity through 80,000 accelerated degradation cycles, and delivers stable PEMWE operation at 500 mA cm–2 for 500 h, outperforming all reported single RuO2 catalysts and rivaling even the best doped or composite Ru-based catalysts. Our findings resolve a long-standing paradox in RuO2 catalysis and establish chloride elimination as a critical design principle for durable oxide electrocatalysts.

abstract: Custard apple (Annona squamosa L.) breeding requires early evaluation of progenies to identify cross combinations with favourable germination and seedling growth. The present investigation evaluated 20 F₁ cross combinations involving Selection No. 11, Balanagar, Sindhan, Mammoth and GJCA-1 under shade-net nursery conditions at Junagadh Agricultural University, Gujarat, from February to May 2025. The experiment was conducted in a Randomised Block Design with three replications, using 20 seeds per cross combination in each replication. Germination percentage was assessed at 30 days after sowing, and plant height, stem diameter, leaf length and leaf width were recorded at 90 days after sowing. Significant differences were observed among the cross combinations for germination behaviour and early seedling growth. Balanagar × Sindhan (C₆) recorded the earliest emergence (22.66 days) and the highest germination percentage (86.92%). Selection 11 × GJCA-1 (C₄) produced the greatest plant height (30.65 cm) and stem diameter (3.70 mm), whereas GJCA-1 × Mammoth (C₂₀) recorded the greatest leaf length (8.72 cm) and leaf width (3.32 cm). Reciprocal combinations showed contrasting performance for several traits, although maternal, paternal and cytoplasmic effects were not separately evaluated. The observed trait-specific variation indicates that multiple cross combinations should be considere…

title: The point of disconnection: early-drought fine root shrinkage is driven by plant water use in Pinus radiata
abstract: Abstract Understanding the root-soil interface is essential for determining when plants become hydraulically isolated from their soil environment during drought. Emerging evidence suggests roots shrink substantially during dehydration, but the drivers and water-flow implications remain elusive, with few data linking shrinkage across soil and plant water status. Using Pinus radiata, a widespread isohydric conifer, we use synchrotron-based Micro-CT to scan intact roots < 2.5 mm in soil during mild plant drying (prior to embolism) to isolate relationships between shrinkage, soil (Ψsoil) and xylem (Ψplant) water potential. Fine roots in situ began shrinking during the earliest stages of Ψplant drying (-0.2 MPa to -0.88 MPa), losing 14.8 ± 10.3% initial transverse-sectional area (62% of observed shrinkage) prior to incipient soil drying (0-72 kPa Ψsoil). Ψplant was a significantly better predictor of shrinkage than Ψsoil, showing a linear shrinkage-Ψplant relationship across this early drying gradient when normalised to shrinkage at -1 MPa, accounting for variable initial Ψplant. Ψplant decline was linearly coordinated with cortical lacunae formation. This Ψplant-driven pattern identifies root shrinkage as an essential component of plant hydraulic function during commonly experienced water potential gradients, occurring long prior to stomatal closure and xylem embolism. title: Wireless Power Transfer and IoT Integration for Electric Vehicle Charging: A Critical Review of Technologies, Safety, Cybersecurity and Research Gaps
abstract: Wireless electric vehicle charging removes the plug from the charging process and, when combined with Internet of Things connectivity, promises automated, grid-aware and user-friendly charging. Research on the two subjects has, however, grown largely in parallel. This paper reviews ten recent and foundational studies drawn from IEEE, Elsevier and MDPI journals and from conference proceedings, using a recent topical review in IEEE Access as the starting point. The studies are grouped into three themes: wireless power transfer technology and roadway deployment, exposure safety and standards, and IoT communication and cybersecurity. They are compared in terms of scope, type of evidence and stated limitations, and the reported performance ranges of the main power transfer techniques are examined. The synthesis shows that inductive and resonant systems dominate practical deployment, that safety work has concentrated on field exposure limits and foreign object detection, and that cybersecurity analyses have mostly addressed conductive chargers and their back end protocols. Little work examines how communication faults or attacks interact with the power electronics of a wireless charger. Seven research gaps are identified, including cross layer threat models, field validation under realistic misalignment, common evaluation practice and harmonised standards, and a staged agenda for fut…

title: Global DNA cytosine methylation is associated with phenotypic differences between spring- and autumn-germinated Erodium oxyrhinchum
abstract: Abstract Many desert ephemeral plants germinate in both spring and autumn, forming distinct cohorts with different phenotypes, yet the epigenetic basis of this variation remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate natural variation in global DNA cytosine methylation and its associations with phenotypes in the typical ephemeral plant Erodium oxyrhinchum. Here, we quantified global DNA cytosine methylation in E. oxyrhinchum at different growth periods. We also integrated ecological and physiological traits to construct plant trait networks (PTNs) for each cohort. DNA methylation in AG increased significantly before winter and decreased afterwards. In contrast, the SG cohort showed elevated methylation in early summer, exceeding AG levels. Notably, global methylation variation was associated with most size- and fecundity-related traits. PTN analysis revealed that plant height and DNA methylation were highly connected in the SG network, while leaf number and soluble sugar were highly connected in the AG network. Moreover, the SG network was more densely connected than the AG network, suggesting tighter trait coordination in SG. These results indicate that the two cohorts differ in methylation patterns and trait association structures. Plant Oxidative Stress Mediates the Synergistic Transformation of Benzotriazole Ultraviolet Stabilizers in Rhizosphere Soil: Insights from Dual Exposure Pathways
abstract: Abstract Benzotriazole ultraviolet stabilizers (BUVs) are widespread emerging contaminants in soil. However, their transformation in the rhizosphere and the regulatory effects of plant oxidative stress on rhizosphere remediation remain unclear. The objective of this study was to investigate these effects using molecular simulations and rhizosphere and foliar exposure experiments. The removal efficiency of the four BUVs was 15–46% higher in the rhizosphere of Helianthus annuus than under natural soil degradation. The plant rhizosphere promoted BUV desorption from soil and induced hydroxylation as a specific transformation pathway. Direct rhizosphere exposure triggered oxidative stress and accelerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in soil. Rhizosphere ROS contributed approximately 31.2%–42.7% to BUV transformation. Foliar exposure experiments suggested that plant oxidative stress is an important contributor to rhizosphere ROS generation. Under BUV stress, plant oxidative stress regulated the composition of dissolved organic matter (DOM) and the selective enrichment of bacteria, including Acidobacteriota, Actinomycota, and Bacteroidota. Multivariate correlation network analysis suggested that foliar exposure resulted in more complex interactions among rhizosphere microenvironmental characteristics than did direct rhizosphere exposure. This study provides insights into…

title: Plant Nutrient Homeostasis In A Rising CO2 World
abstract: Abstract The rapid rise in atmospheric CO2 concentration presents a critical paradox for global agriculture: while it stimulates photosynthesis and plant productivity, it simultaneously compromises crop nutritional quality. This decline in quality is linked to a lower concentration of essential macro- and micronutrients in crop edible parts, involving complex regulatory shifts that go beyond the simple growth dilution effect caused by the decoupling between growth and nutrient uptake. In this review, we summarize the current knowledge regarding the impact of elevated CO2 (eCO2) on nitrogen (N) nutrition, among other aspects, discussing how the availability of nitrate (NO3-) or ammonium (NH4+) affects plant growth and N status under eCO2, a long-standing debate in the field. We outline recent advances in the signalling mechanisms regulating NO3- uptake under eCO2 and discuss the interaction between photorespiration and the assimilation of both N sources. Likewise, we address the main effects and regulatory mechanisms associated with eCO2 and the homeostasis of sulphur (S), phosphorus (P) and the micronutrients iron (Fe) and zinc (Zn). Collectively, we intend to provide a comprehensive framework to guide future crop breeding and climate-resilient agronomic management.

Effect of Six Fertilization Treatments on the Agronomic Performance of Amaranth Under Morning and Evening Irrigation Conditions in Burkina Faso
abstract: Background: Leafy vegetables, particularly amaranth, are important in Burkina Faso for food security, nutrition, income generation, and livelihoods. However, their production is limited by poor soil fertility and nutrient deficiencies, highlighting the need for improved soil management and fertilisation strategies. Aims: The general objective of this study was to contribute to improving and maintaining amaranth productivity in Burkina Faso. Specifically, the aim was to assess the effects of fertiliser treatments on the growth and agromorphological development of amaranth, and to identify the effects of fertiliser treatments on amaranth productivity. Methodology: Six treatments were evaluated: T0: no fertiliser; T1: organic fertiliser; T2: organic fertiliser + NPK; T3: NPK; T4: organic fertiliser + composite fertiliser; T5: composite fertiliser. The plant material consisted of the Amaranthus hybridus variety known as FOTETE. The composite fertiliser consisted of urea, triple superphosphate and calcined Burkina phosphate. The design was a Fisher block with three replicates. Growth, development and harvesting parameters were evaluated. Results: Analysis of variance and comparison of means showed that the composite fertiliser performed best in terms of growth, development and productivity. In addition, the results showed that the composite fertiliser (Urea+TSP+CBKca) produced a tot…

title: The interplay of landscape connectivity, composition and configuration in alien plant invasions across an ecological network
abstract: Abstract Context Biological invasions are deemed to be the second most important global driver of biodiversity loss showing strong interactions with the aftermaths of land use change and landscape fragmentation. The role of landscape composition and configuration in biological invasions is widely considered while its interplay with landscape connectivity is less understood. However, ecological connectivity can be equally crucial for both native and alien species, constituting the backbone of ecological network initiatives. Objectives We aim to assess how landscape composition, configuration and connectivity (in the ecological network) influence α- and β-diversity (floristic uniqueness) of both alien and native plant species, and to determine whether these effects differ according to habitat type. Methods The study was conducted in a 298 km 2 ecological network in the lowlands of Friuli Venezia Giulia, northeastern Italy, encompassing a mosaic of agricultural, natural, and semi-natural habitats. A hierarchical sampling design was applied to 87 terrestrial habitat nodes, where plant species composition and abundance were recorded in 219 plots. Landscape composition, configuration and connectivity were quantified to examine their influence on native and alien plant α- and β-diversity across different habitat types. Results We found contrasting effects of landscape connectivity, co…

title: Successful Experiences of Virtual Enterprises in Social E-Commerce: The Cases of Facebook–Instagram and Amazon
abstract: This study clarifies the fundamental distinctions between traditional e-commerce, social media marketing, and social e-commerce, establishing a conceptual framework that explains their convergence and divergence in theory and practice. It examines international experiences where social e-commerce has been successfully implemented, highlighting Facebook and Amazon as representative models of virtual enterprises operating in this domain. Using a descriptive–analytical methodology, data were collected from books, academic articles, reports, websites, electronic platforms, and personal observations. The findings indicate that social e-commerce represents an advanced form of e-commerce that enhances transactions through social interaction, trust building, and user engagement. Virtual enterprises within this environment create global markets unconstrained by time and place, while promoting digital awareness and adaptation to rapid technological change. The results demonstrate that social e-commerce strengthens national economies by encouraging diversification, improving market efficiency, and supporting sustainable development. The study concludes that it offers a practical model for developing countries, particularly Algeria, to advance digital commerce.

title: The Influence of Peer Group Interaction on the IPAS Learning Outcomes of Elementary School Students
abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine whether there is an influence between peer interaction (Peer Group) and the results of students' science learning at SDN Pakis I Surabaya. This research method is, this research is a quantitative study that uses the ex post facto method, namely research used to find the causes of changes in behavior, symptoms or phenomena that occur and data collection using questionnaires on 5th grade students of SDN Pakis I Surabaya. The data processing will be done using SPSS 26. Conclusion: The results shiwed that peer interaction did not significantly outcomes (t = -0.628, p = 0.532). the regression model was also not statistically significant (F =0.394, p = 0.532), with an R2 VALUE OF 0.004, indicating that peer interaction explained only 0.4% of the variance in students IPAS learning outcomes. Therefore, it can be concluded that peer group interaction does not significantly influence the science learning outcomes of SDN Pakis students. Other factors can contribute to high and low learning outcomes, including parenting styles, socio-cultural conditions, or cultural factors.

title: The Ghost of the Native Speaker and the Dark Energy Shadowing the Learner: A Posthumanist Inquiry into Human– AI Relationships in Second Language Writing
abstract: Abstract While existing research indicates the utility of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assisting language learners, how human–AI relationships may condition learners' being and becoming remains underexplored. In this article, we draw on Barad's agential realism to discuss findings of a posthumanist phenomenological study on 110 Chinese students' experiences with GenAI in a L2 writing workshop. Five forms of human–AI relationships are identified from the metaphors that the student participants employed to describe their experiences: user–tool, king–minister, friend–partner, student–teacher, and slave–tyrant. Across these entangled relationships, human and GenAI agents are differentiated in ways that foreground the figure of a ghostly GenAI native speaker, experienced as competent, efficient, and self(‐)less. By contrast, learners' weaknesses are brought forth as deficient, slow, and unreliable. As our analysis reveals, the ghostly GenAI native speaker is rendered possible and intelligible through a range of existing apparatuses, whose enactment has summoned a dark energy, reconfiguring the way in which native‐speakerism exerts influence upon language learners—it reinforces a technical view of L2 writing and excludes learners not from native‐speaker communities but potentially from the sociality of L2 writing as a whole, with foreclosed possibilities for imaginin…

Triboelectric Nanogenerators for Human‐Robot Motion Energy Harvesting and Sensing: Structures, Embodied Artificial Intelligence, and Self‐Powered Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid development of humanoid robots and embodied artificial intelligence (EAI) is accelerating the transformation of elderly care and rehabilitation toward interactive, adaptive, and personalized human–robot collaboration. In this context, motion sensing technology is of critical importance. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), which convert biomechanical motions into electrical signals, offer a promising route toward self‐powered motion perception in embodied healthcare. This review summarizes recent advances in TENG‐based multimodal motion sensing for human–robot interaction, covering inertial vibration sensing, tactile sensing, non‐contact sensing, continuous trajectory sensing, and joint rotation sensing. The influences of structural configuration, motion mode, sensing direction, detection range, sensitivity, resolution, electrical output, and channel number on sensing performance under specific application scenarios are analyzed. Particular attention is paid to how TENG design strategies influence sensing universality, signal effectiveness, and the reliability of health monitoring and rehabilitation evaluation. Furthermore, the integration of TENGs with artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, including multimodal fusion, network architectures, edge computing, transfer learning, and large language models, is reviewed. AI and Intelligent Building Analytics for Energy Efficiency in Large Healthcare Campuses
abstract: Large healthcare campuses contain dissimilar clinical and non-clinical buildings, central thermal plants and increasingly connected building-control systems. Their energy demand is unusually difficult to optimise because continuity of care, infection prevention, thermal conditions and equipment reliability constrain operational flexibility. This critical narrative review evaluates whether artificial intelligence and intelligent building analytics offer credible improvements in energy efficiency at the campus scale, and under what technical and governance conditions. Peer-reviewed hospital-specific investigations, building-energy prediction and fault-detection studies, field evaluations of predictive control, and research on digital twins and clinical indoor environments were critically synthesised. Evidence available through 12 August 2026 was considered. The literature supports a clear distinction between accurate energy forecasting, detection of actionable faults, and measured energy savings attributable to closed-loop interventions. Hospital data studies demonstrate promising predictive performance, whereas direct, prolonged, independently evaluated deployments across entire healthcare campuses remain uncommon. Model predictive control has a stronger real-building implementation record than autonomous reinforcement learning, but aggregate benefits from ordinary commercial bu…

Effective Porosity and Pore–Ligament Architecture in Mg‐Based Solid‐State Hydrogen Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnesium (Mg)‐based hydrides offer high gravimetric capacity, high volumetric hydrogen density, elemental abundance, and low material cost, but their practical performance is constrained by coupled hydrogen transport, interfacial reaction, heat transfer, and structural evolution during repeated magnesium/magnesium hydride conversion. This mini‐review reframes porosity as a functional rather than purely morphological attribute. We critically synthesize representative precursor‐derived, scaffold‐free, and layered porous Mg architectures, and organize the available structural, transport, conversion, thermal, and cycling evidence around an operational definition of effective porosity: the gas‐accessible pore fraction that, at a specified structural and reaction state, satisfies a stated molecular‐hydrogen transport criterion within a specified timescale and is spatially coupled to internally converting regions of a percolating Mg‐rich solid domain. Strict three‐dimensional determination is distinguished from intermediate spatial validation and routine laboratory proxies to clarify what can and cannot be inferred experimentally. The analysis shows that high initial porosity, high surface area, or rapid powder kinetics alone do not establish storage‐relevant functionality. Secondary phases must be assigned process‐specific roles rather than inferred from coexistence, and ap…

title: GOVERNANCE MECHANISMS AND LOCAL TAX REVENUE: EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE FROM REGENCY AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS IN EASTERN INDONESIA
abstract: Differences in the capacity of local governments to generate tax revenue remain a major challenge in Eastern Indonesia. Although numerous studies have examined the relationship between governance and local tax revenue, empirical evidence identifying which governance mechanisms play the most critical role in enhancing tax revenue while accounting for disparities in regional economic capacity remains limited. This study aims to examine the effects of the capability of the Government Internal Supervisory Apparatus (APIP), the maturity of the Government Internal Control System (SPIP), and the Corruption Control Effectiveness Index (IEPK) on local tax revenue while controlling for the influence of Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP). A quantitative approach was employed using panel data from 150 regency and municipal governments in Eastern Indonesia over the 2022–2024 period, yielding a total of 450 observations. The data were analyzed using the Fixed Effects Model (FEM). The findings indicate that APIP capability and corruption control effectiveness have a positive and statistically significant effect on local tax revenue, whereas SPIP maturity does not have a statistically significant effect. These results suggest that, after controlling for differences in regional economic capacity, improvements in local tax revenue are driven more by the effectiveness of internal oversight an…

title: Assessment of Water Quality among Various Domestic Water Storage Tanks in Urban Area, Belagavi—A Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Background: Unhygienic household water storage is a significant contributor to the deterioration of water quality from source to consumption, elevating the risk of waterborne diseases in urbanizing areas of India. The physical condition and maintenance of domestic water storage tanks are critical yet frequently overlooked factors in public health. Objectives: To assess water quality among various domestic water storage tanks in urban areas. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted from March to August 2025, involving 207 households selected through a proportionate-to-size sampling method. Water samples were analyzed for physical, chemical, and microbiological parameters. The physical condition of the tanks was evaluated using a risk assessment score, while overall water quality was summarized using the water quality index (WQI). Results: Microbiological analysis revealed significant fecal contamination, with E. coli present in 16.43% of samples and total coliforms in 23.67%. While 74.88% of tanks were in the low-risk category, 7.25% were classified as critical. Poor physical conditions such as the absence of a lid, cracks, and infrequent cleaning were significantly associated with poor WQI ( P < 0.0001). A moderate positive correlation (ρ = 0.48, P < 0.0001) was found between the physical risk score and WQI. This correlation confirms that tanks with greater physi…

EFFECT OF CONFLICT MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES ON EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE IN NIGERIA REVENUE SERVICE (NRS)
abstract: Conflict is an inherent feature of large, rule-intensive tax administrations, where interdependent units must interpret complex regulations under strict accountability frameworks. Within the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS), poorly managed disagreements can extend case cycle times, increase rework, and reduce operational throughput. This study investigates how three distinct conflict management strategies—negotiation, collaboration, and compromising—relate to employee efficiency, evaluated through turnaround time, rework, throughput, and deadline adherence. Grounded in contingency and organizational information-processing theories, and integrating concepts of psychological safety, team learning, hierarchy, and cultural tightness–looseness, the study utilizes a cross-sectional survey of 371 NRS employees. Data were gathered using five-point Likert scales and analyzed via multiple regression models with efficiency as the primary outcome. The findings reveal that all three strategies significantly predict efficiency: Collaboration demonstrates the strongest positive association; Negotiation exhibits a moderate positive effect while Compromising yields a smaller yet positive effect. The overall model accounts for approximately 42% of the variance in efficiency while successfully meeting standard statistical diagnostic criteria. In terms of contributions and implications, conceptually,…

title: Electrification, Lightweighting, and Materials Supply: A Dynamic Life Cycle Assessment of the U.S. Light-Duty Vehicle Fleet
abstract: Abstract Electrification and lightweighting are reshaping vehicle designs and materials demand, with uncertain net effects on life cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Most existing fleet studies treat material choices, materials markets, and vehicle adoption separately, without capturing feedbacks between design, supply chains, and consumer behavior. This study develops an integrated system dynamics–life cycle assessment (SD–LCA) framework to explore these interactions for the U.S. light-duty vehicle fleet from 2000 to 2060. The model extends an established powertrain diffusion framework by endogenizing vehicle body material selection, battery capacity evolution, and materials market responses, linking these dynamics to a bottom-up life cycle assessment of fleet GHG emissions. Scenario analysis shows that increasing aluminum use in lightweight gasoline vehicles improves their utility and market share, largely offsetting use-phase GHG savings and yielding only modest reductions in total fleet emissions. In contrast, faster battery electric vehicle adoption raises cradle-to-gate emissions but more than compensates through lower use-phase emissions, reducing total fleet GHGs. Shifts in vehicle material demand also generate transient imbalances in steel and aluminum markets, temporarily lowering recycled fraction and increasing cradle-to-gate emissions. title: Effect of Electric Field, Hydrostatic, and Uniaxial Pressures on Physical Properties of NH 4 HSO 4 Ferroelectric Within the Framework of a Pseudospin Model
abstract: The static longitudinal dielectric, elastic, and thermal characteristics of the NH 4 HSO 4 crystal under the influence of a longitudinal electric field, as well as hydrostatic and uniaxial pressures, were calculated using a two‐sublattice pseudospin model of this ferroelectric. A linear dependence of the upper and lower Curie temperatures on the applied pressures has been demonstrated, as well as a linearly decreasing dependence of the lower Curie temperature on the electric field. The electrocaloric, barocaloric, and piezocaloric effects in this crystal have been investigated. The model predicts a negative electrocaloric temperature change near the lower Curie temperature, which can exceed 5 K.

title: Smart Waste Collection Based on Vehicle Routing for Municipal Solid Waste Using Genric Algorithms
abstract: Waste collection is a important activity for maintaining clean and healthy communities. Traditional waste collection systems generally depend on fixed collection schedules and predetermined routes such an approaches may not always be suitable, when waste generation, collection requirements or available resources change. Recent studies have explored dynamic routing and suitable waste-bin location planning to improve the efficiency of waste collection systems. This review paper focuses on two important areas: dynamic routing for waste collection and optimal planning of waste-bin locations. Dynamic routing help in the modifying collection routes according to changing requirements, while proper waste-bin location planning can make waste collection more accessible and organized. The paper reviewing exists studies related to dynamic routing and web-based approaches. A compare analysis is present to identify difference in objectives, technologies and practical applications of the reviewed studies. The review also identifies research gaps and possible directions for developing the simple and practical waste collection application.

title: A style-aware belief-based game model for automated-vehicle discretionary lane-changing decisions in mixed traffic
abstract: Discretionary lane changing in mixed traffic requires automated vehicles to account for uncertain responses from surrounding human-driven vehicles, particularly the target-lane rear vehicle. This study proposes SADP-QRE, a vehicle-level style-aware belief-based game model for automated-vehicle lane-changing decisions, integrating style-conditioned behavioral learning, online opponent-type belief updating, TTC-based risk assessment, and quantal response equilibrium. Naturalistic NGSIM trajectories are used to learn style-conditioned lane-changing and rear-vehicle response tendencies. During decision making, observed rear-vehicle motion updates the belief over latent opponent types, and the belief-aware payoff matrix generates probabilistic lane-changing decisions. The model is validated on held-out NGSIM LC/LK samples and evaluated in SUMO against expected-utility and leader–follower benchmark models. The trajectory-level validation yields ROC-AUC values of 0.764–0.782 and PR-AUC values of 0.713–0.749. In simulation, SADP-QRE reduces mean time loss by 3.71%–7.78% in a straight-freeway scenario and by 11.32%–22.24% in a merge–weave scenario, without reducing throughput.

title: In Situ Electric Tuning―An Emerging STM Tactic for Probing Exotic Quantum Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT In situ electric tuning (ISET) integrated with scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy (STM/STS) has established itself as a highly effective methodology for controlling quantum electronic states in low‐dimensional materials. This approach combines the sub‐atomic spatial resolution and meV‐resolved spectroscopic capability of STM with the reversible and continuously tunable carrier modulation of field‐effect device architectures. To date, this approach has been applied to numerous systems, including graphene‐based van der Waals heterostructures, correlated electron systems, and moiré superlattice systems hosting emergent quantum phases. Herein, we systematically summarize the state‐of‐the‐art experimental implementations, including global electrostatic gating, tip‐induced local gating, tip‐induced voltage pulse, and in‐plane electric tuning, accompanied with distinct physics under each configuration. We then highlight key representative advances in resolving gate‐dependent band renormalization, correlated insulating states, charge ordering, symmetry breaking, and electrically driven metastable phases at the nanoscale. We discuss practical limitations, such as restricted carrier‐density ranges, tip‐induced perturbations, dielectric reliability, and challenges in decoupling electric effects from current injection and Joule heating. Looking forward, we outline futu…

title: Social network based fuzzy decision-analytic model for hydrogen vehicle selection toward sustainable transportation systems
abstract: Abstract The selection of an effective hydrogen vehicle technology is a multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) problem with conflicting evaluation criteria and uncertainty in experts’ judgments. To tackle this challenge, this study presents an integrated social network analysis based fuzzy MCDM approach to hydrogen vehicle selection. First, in the present work, Social Network Analysis (SNA) is used to calculate the relative influence of experts using degree centrality. Second, the uncertainty and imprecision in experts’ linguistic assessments are captured in terms of Interval-Valued Fuzzy Sets (IVFS). Third, the Entropy method is used as an objective weighting method to give relative importance of the evaluation criteria. Finally, the Evaluation based on Distance from Average Solution (EDAS) technique is used to evaluate and rank the alternatives. The suggested methodology is used in four hydrogen vehicle alternatives, with the evaluation criteria of eight. The results indicate that $$O_1$$ (FCEV) is the most suitable option, with an EDAS appraisal score of 0.9992 followed by $$O_3$$ (H2Hybrid), $$O_4$$ (H2REEV) and $$O_2$$ (H2ICE). The proposed approach is further tested the effectiveness by comparing four existing hybrid MCDM approaches, and O1 is consistently determined as the best alternative. title: Vehicle-Based Methane Detection, Source Attribution, and Quantification in the Upstream Oil and Gas Sector: Method Overview and Controlled Release Validation
abstract: Abstract Vehicle-based measurement systems occupy an important niche in the multiscale methane measurement landscape between component-level technologies and aerial-based methods. Performance evaluations are often limited to one dimension (e.g., quantification), while methodological opacity limits interpretation and intercomparisons between technologies. Here, we develop a vehicle-based measurement unit employing repeated site-perimeter transects and a processing framework featuring a novel weighted-likelihood algorithm for automated source attribution. Using controlled release experiments at two dedicated testing facilities, we characterize system performance across three dimensions─detection, attribution, and quantification. The system achieved a 94.5% true-positive detection rate with no false positives and a 90% detection limit as low as 0.078 kg/h with five repeat transects. Attribution accuracy was high at the source-group level, reaching 99.7% in single-source releases and 86% in multisource scenarios. Quantification was unbiased for low-to-moderate complexity releases (2 source groups; slope = 0.99, R2 = 0.81) but overestimated under highly complex conditions (5 source groups; slope = 1.45, R2 = 0.91). These results provide a transparent performance benchmark, demonstrating that these systems are well-suited to survey the large populations of low-to-moderate-complexity …

DBSCAN-Based Spatial Hotspot Detection of Motorcycle and Three-Wheeled Vehicle Crashes
abstract: Because of the lack of physical protection and the often-complex interaction between motorcycles and 3-wheelers and the other components of urban transportation systems, motorcycles and 3-wheelers are among the most vulnerable road users. Therefore, it is important to determine spatial crash hotspots to enable evidence-based road safety management and targeted interventions. The purpose of this study is to detect crash hotspot areas of motorcycles and three-wheel vehicles for the Rusafa district in Baghdad using the density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) algorithm and the Haversine distance measure. There were 802 crash records that were georeferenced and analyzed to identify areas that have been more prone to crashes. We used a Ball Tree nearest-neighbor search algorithm to implement DBSCAN and preprocessed the geographic coordinates before we applied DBSCAN, converting them to radians. We did a sensitivity analysis and selected the optimal clustering parameters (eps = 0.5 km, min_samples = 5). Three spatial indicators (Zone_Label, Zone_Count, Hotspot_Flag) were then calculated to describe the identified hotspot regions. The framework recommended 37 spatial clusters, with 656 (81.8%) of these crashes being identified as a hotspot and 146 crashes (18.2%) as spatial noise. CHARGE HUB: A Comprehensive Review of Smart Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure, Booking Systems, and Intelligent Charging Services
abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has created a need for reliable charging infrastructure, convenient booking services, efficient energy management, and intelligent charging solutions. However, EV users may face problems such as limited charger availability, waiting time, uncertain charging costs, and difficulty identifying suitable charging stations. This review examines four published review papers covering EV charging station planning, smart charging, machine learning-based charging services, and charging technologies and standards. The reviewed literature indicates that effective EV charging requires coordination between charging infrastructure, digital platforms, energy management, and user requirements. Smart charging can improve energy utilization, while artificial intelligence and machine learning can support demand prediction, station recommendation, scheduling, and pricing. This paper compares the main contributions and limitations of the four reviews and identifies opportunities for integrating these functions into a unified charging management platform. The review also discusses how a system such as CHARGE HUB can connect users, charging stations, booking services, backend APIs, and databases. title: Green product development and pricing strategy considering consumer reference behavior
abstract: Abstract In the context of the green economy, green transition has emerged as a critical pathway for industries to achieve sustainable development. Green product development and pricing strategies serve as core components of firms’ green transition. This paper investigates how consumers’ environmental awareness and price–quality reference behavior influence consumer selection strategies, focusing on product line development and pricing decisions. Based on the multinomial logit model, this paper establishes a product line pricing model to analyze two development strategies: exclusive upgrading and development of green product and simultaneous development of traditional and green products. For each strategy, this paper derives optimal solutions for product price, market share, and firm profit. Our findings indicate that factors such as the green product perception sensitivity coefficient and product greenness exert differing influence trends on the optimal solution. Furthermore, a firm's green product development strategy depends on the market acceptance of green products and the price–quality reference behavior among customers. Additionally, accounting for uncertainties in platform environments, we address robust product line pricing problem, demonstrating that firms can achieve superior profits based on this approach.

title: TREINAMENTO RESISTIDO COMO ESTRATÉGIA DE PREVENÇÃO E TRATAMENTO DA SARCOPENIA EM IDOSOS: REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA
abstract: This study aimed to analyze the effects of resistance training on the prevention and treatment of sarcopenia in older adults. The study selection process resulted in 11 publications included in the review. The analyzed data indicate positive results regarding the use of resistance training as a method for the prevention and treatment of sarcopenia in older adults. The f indings highlight protocols combining moderate-to-high intensity with load progression, which lead to significant improvements in gait speed, balance, and muscle strength. Resistance training (RT) is an important strategy for the management of sarcopenia, being capable not only of contributing to the prevention of muscle mass loss, but also to the recovery of functionality in movements performed during daily routines and activities. In addition, it promotes functional independence and overall well-being, preserving autonomy, and promoting active aging.

title: Boron-doped mesoporous bioactive glass nanoparticles as a dual-delivery platform for tetracycline and phytochemicals: A synergistic strategy against multidrug-resistant bacteria
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and biofilm-associated tolerance substantially limit the effectiveness of conventional antibiotic therapy. This study investigated boron-doped mesoporous bioactive glass (B-MBG) nanoparticles as a dual-payload delivery system for the combined administration of tetracycline and selected hydrophobic phytochemical adjuvants, including berberine, curcumin, and resveratrol. The platform was designed to improve antibacterial and antibiofilm activity while facilitating the delivery of poorly soluble natural compounds. B-MBG nanoparticles were synthesized using a sol-gel method. Tetracycline and each phytochemical were nominal 2:1 input mass ratio. Particle morphology and structure were characterized by SEM, SEM-EDS, DLS, N2 adsorption–desorption analysis, and XRD. Biological activity was examined by planktonic microdilution at 24 and 48 h, disk diffusion, and a 72-h crystal violet biofilm assay. Cytocompatibility was evaluated in HaCaT keratinocytes at 24, 48, and 72 h. The resulting datasets were analyzed using multiparametric statistical methods and principal component analysis. B-MBG nanoparticles exhibited a predominantly uniform spherical morphology with particle sizes of approximately 100-150 nm. abstract: ABSTRACT Limited teacher readiness before conducting learning activities is one of the challenges in developing teacher quality in pesantren settings. This condition indicates the need for internal development programs that provide teachers with subject knowledge, mentoring, and practical experience before they undertake teaching responsibilities. This study aims to describe the implementation of the Ta’hil Program at Fadlillah Islamic Boarding School, the forms of teacher development provided, supporting and inhibiting factors, and its role in teacher quality development. This study employed a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation and analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings show that the Ta’hil Program serves as a preparatory stage for teachers before teaching for one semester through material provision and deepening, guidance, mentoring, and knowledge and experience transfer from senior teachers. Supporting factors include clear objectives, prepared materials, senior teacher involvement, experience transfer, and preparation time, while inhibiting factors include limited teachers with expertise in Science, Mathematics, and Islamic Astronomy. Enhanced Membrane Preference in APEX2 Proximity Labeling via an iEDDA Strategy With Built‐In Background Correction
abstract: ABSTRACT Proximity‐labeling techniques, such as engineered ascorbate peroxidase (APEX2), have revolutionized the mapping of spatially organized proteomes. However, achieving high spatial resolution and specificity remains challenging due to the diffusible nature of labeling intermediates and the difficulty in establishing robust negative controls. Here, we present a chemical strategy that addresses both challenges by engineering the labeling reporter itself. We developed a lipophilic APEX2 reporter, phenol‐ trans ‐cyclooctene (phenol‐TCO), designed to partition into membrane microenvironments. This reporter leverages inverse electron‐demand Diels–Alder (iEDDA) chemistry for subsequent detection. Crucially, we repurpose the inherent, non‐specific reactivity of the tetrazine–biotin conjugate to establish a powerful and practical built‐in negative control. When applied to profile the Lamin A‐associated proteome, the phenol‐TCO reporter enriches nuclear envelope and endoplasmic reticulum membrane proteins with high confidence, yielding a focused dataset. In sharp contrast, conventional phenol‐biotin labeled a diffuse set of proteins lacking lamina specificity. We demonstrate that the tetrazine‐biotin‐treated lysate control effectively removes non‐specific background while preserving genuine proximal interactors, supporting it as a practical alternative to traditional controls. A Novel Application of the Volumetric Absorptive Micro Sampling Strategy to Quantify Dexmedetomidine in Capillary Blood Using an LC – MS / MS Method
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Pain control in neonates is crucial as inadequate management may impair neuronal development. Dexmedetomidine (DEX), an alpha2 agonist, is approved for intravenous use in ventilated neonates. While intranasal DEX is off‐label in neonates and children, studies show its efficacy for magnetic resonance imaging sedation. Limited pharmacokinetic data exist for intranasal DEX in pre‐term infants and neonates. This study aimed to develop an analytical method for DEX quantification in blood samples (20 μL) of complex patients collected with microsampling technique to enable future pharmacokinetic studies. Methods A liquid–liquid extraction from blood absorbed in microsampling devices (MITRA) and an LC–MS/MS method were developed and validated following EMA/FDA guidelines. The method's suitability was verified by comparing results from nine paediatric blood samples collected in EDTA tubes or using MITRA devices. Results All results obtained for selectivity (no interference at R T of DEX), sensitivity (DEX LLOQ = 0.025 ng/mL), linearity (R 2 > 0.99), intra and inter‐day repeatability (CV % 1.8–11.8), stability, and hematocrit effect met the acceptance criteria for bioanalytical method validation. title: Disrupting Interfacial Hydrogen-Bonding Networks via Dynamic Reconstruction Strategy for Enhanced CO2-to-C2+ Electrocatalysis
abstract: Abstract The morphology and microenvironment of ion-conducting polymers (ionomers) on the catalyst electrode surface critically govern the CO2 electrocatalytic performance. Herein, we report a dual-reconstruction strategy that synergistically tailors the surface structure of the Nafion ionomer using positively charged molecules and solvent effect. By combining a low-dielectric-constant solvent (isopropanol) with arginine cations, the optimized electrode achieves an 83.6% Faradaic efficiency for multicarbon (C2+) products at a high current density of –500 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH. Based on experimental characterization and MD simulations, we propose a structural model in which the Nafion side chains are oriented away from both the catalyst surface and the electrolyte phase. In situ spectroscopic analyses, theoretical calculation, and experimental evidence suggest that this structural reorganization disrupts the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network, suppresses the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, improves effective gaseous CO2 accessibility, and facilitates C–C coupling along an energetically favorable *OC–COH pathway. This work provides valuable insights into microenvironment engineering of ionomer–catalyst interfaces for efficient CO2 electrolysis.

abstract: ABSTRACT This research was motivated by the fact that the instilling of moral values ​​has not yet proceeded optimally. A qualitative approach with a descriptive research design was employed. The research informants consisted of the school principal, one PPKn teacher, and three students from SMP Negeri 2 Hiliduho. Data collection techniques included observation, interviews, and documentation. Data analysis involved data collection, data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The results indicate that: (1) the PPKn teacher plays a role in instilling moral values ​​by providing understanding, advice, role modeling, habituation, guidance, and reprimands to students. abstract: Since the advent of Artificial Intelligence tools, translation researchers endeavored to examine how human translations are in comparison to those generated by AI tools, using corpora from various genres. Many genres have been investigated, yet self-help remains underexplored. title: Laser Power Transmission in Space: Plasma-Based Power Cell
abstract: Abstract Laser power beaming offers a route to space energy delivery, but semiconductor laser photovoltaic receivers face thermalization, Joule heating, and radiative recombination losses at the solid-state junction. Here, we propose a gas-phase plasma power cell that converts incident vacuum-ultraviolet photons directly into electrical output through xenon photoionization, magnetically guided electron transport, and collection at a biased electrode surface, replacing the fixed semiconductor junction with an optically tunable, all-gas-phase energy-conversion medium. The model includes secondary electron emission at the electrode surfaces as a possible interfacial energy recycling pathway. Particle-in-cell Monte Carlo simulations of a low-pressure xenon chamber driven by a 58.4 nm pulsed laser predict a steady-state laser-to-electrical conversion efficiency of 82.25% at an average incident power of 2000 W/m. Energy accounting is close to 1%, with 7.52% photon escape, 8.95% boundary loss, and 1.29% chamber-stored energy. Parameter scans over bias voltage, magnetic field, and gas pressure identify photon absorption, electron confinement, and plasma-electrode charge collection as the controlling design factors. title: Analisis Peran Film a Fantastic Woman sebagai Instrumen Soft Power Chile dalam Diplomasi Budaya Internasional
abstract: Kekuatan soft power dapat dibangun dari karya budaya yang diciptakan suatu negara. Salah satu contoh negara yang memanfaatkan film sebagai sarana soft power adalah Chile. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis peran film A Fantastic Woman melalui diplomasi budaya Chile dalam membangun citra positif di mata internasional. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kualitatif, yaitu teknik pengumpulan data melalui studi kepustakaan, studi dokumentasi, dan analisis film A Fantastic Woman (2017). Data dianalisis ini menggunakan konsep soft power Joseph S. Nye. Hasil pada penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa film A Fantastic Woman menunjukkan nilai hak asasi manusia, keberagaman, dan perlindungan terhadap kelompok rentan diskriminasi yang berpotensi untuk mendukung diplomasi budaya Chile. Pengakuan internasional terhadap film tersebut melalui penghargaan Academy Awards menunjukkan jangkauan pengakuan terhadap karya perfilman Chile. Namun, penelitian ini belum mengukur perubahan persepsi audiens internasional secara langsung.

title: Architecting Resilient Offline-First Transaction Platforms for Mission-Critical Retail Commerce: Integrating Secure Payment Orchestration, Conflict-Resilient Synchronisation, and Distributed State Recovery
abstract: Retail transaction platforms increasingly operate where network connectivity is a variable rather than a guarantee. A store may lose backend connectivity while its payment terminal stays locally responsive, or a kiosk application may restart mid-transaction while a payment authorisation is still in flight. Systems built on the assumption of continuous connectivity treat these conditions as failures to be logged rather than states to be recovered from, and checkout disruption, duplicate charges, or silent data loss follow at exactly the moment a retailer can least afford them. This article proposes an architecture for offline-first retail transaction platforms that treats payment safety, transaction durability, and inventory consistency as one integrated design problem rather than three separate concerns handled independently. Three elements are combined: a payment orchestration model that persists attempt identifiers and checks authoritative outcomes before any retry, a durable transaction journal recording every state transition so an application restart can resume, reverse, or reconcile an in-progress transaction rather than discard it, and a conflict-resilient synchronisation layer that classifies pending operations, detects conflicting state changes, and resolves them through a policy suited to the data type involved. Video Analytics as a Quality and Risk Management Tool in Retail
abstract: In this paper implemented in recent years of using risk management, digitalization, and video surveillance tools in quality management at enterprises ensure the quality and safety of products and services. A comparative analysis of video surveillance systems at two food retailers is presented. A problem with video surveillance usue is identified: the lack of a methodology for using accumulated video data to make management decisions minimize quality and safety risks. Directions for improving risk management using additional video surveillance functions are identified. The scientific novelty of this study lies in its refinement of the methodological approach to using video surveillance in quality management to minimize risks in the food retail industry.

title: Retail Theft and Consumer Protection in Indonesia: Coercive Recovery and Public Exposure under the 2026 Criminal Law Framework
abstract: Retail theft presents a legal problem that extends beyond the loss of merchandise. A retailer may have a legitimate property claim while its response to suspected theft creates a separate violation of a customer's liberty, dignity, or personal data rights. This article examines the boundary between lawful loss prevention and private punishment in Indonesia after the criminal law reforms effective in 2026. It uses doctrinal legal research, combining statutory interpretation, a targeted literature review, and expressly hypothetical retail scenarios. The analysis connects the Criminal Code, the Criminal Procedure Code, consumer protection legislation, civil liability, and personal data protection. It finds that proof of theft does not itself authorize compulsory monetary penalties, prolonged confinement, or unrestricted publication of identifying footage. Consumer status requires a separate examination of the transaction, while general criminal and data protection safeguards remain relevant even when that status is disputed. The article proposes a sequential assessment of the evidence, the authority for each intervention, the freedom of any agreement, and the continuing necessity of information use. It also identifies a consequential tension between the five-year eligibility and exclusion provisions governing restorative justice. The proposed framework preserves legitimate recover…

title: A cross-contextual meta-analysis of agentic AI in retail and supply chain operations: efficacy and implementation insights
abstract: Abstract Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in retail and supply chain operations, yet the empirical evidence for their efficacy has never been systematically quantified. This meta-analysis synthesizes 19 studies (total $$N = 5{,}292$$ ) to quantify the impact of agentic AI on operational performance and examine how contextual factors shape outcomes. Using a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation and the Hartung-Knapp (HK) adjustment for confidence intervals, we found near-total heterogeneity across the included studies ( $$I^2 = 99.5\%$$ , $$\tau ^2 = 7.18$$ ), with a 95% prediction interval $$[-4.20,\ 7.36]$$ indicating that the true effect in any new setting could range from substantial harm to exceptional benefit. Against this backdrop of extreme variability, the pooled Hedges’ $$g = 1.58$$ (95% CI $$[0.26,\ 2.89]$$ , $$p = 0.022$$ ) should not be read as a general implementation expectation but rather as an average masking fundamentally divergent context-specific effects. Enantioseparation on Helical Poly(diphenylacetylene) Derivatives Obtained by Helicity Induction and Memory Strategy Using Bio-Based Chiral Oils
abstract: Abstract Optically inactive poly(diphenylacetylene) bearing heptyl ester groups (poly-1) formed a preferred-handed helical conformation upon thermal annealing in various bio-based chiral oils, mainly chiral hydrocarbons, as a chiral source through intermolecular noncovalent interactions. Following the removal of the chiral oils, the induced macromolecular helicity of poly-1 remained stable in solution at room temperature, successfully demonstrating helicity memory (h-poly-1). The left-handed helix of h-poly-1 induced by (S)-limonene underwent complete inversion to a right-handed helix upon thermal annealing in (R)-limonene, and this helicity switching process was reversible and repeatable. When used as a chiral stationary phase (CSP) for high-performance liquid chromatography, h-poly-1 exhibited excellent chiral recognition ability comparable to those of commercially available polysaccharide-based CSPs toward biaryl derivatives with multiple hydrogen-bond donor groups, based solely on the macromolecular helicity induced by bio-based chiral hydrocarbons.

abstract: This study presents an evaluation of the Family Health Strategy (FHS) in Brazil, considering its historical development, advances, setbacks, weaknesses, and challenges from the perspective of a multidisciplinary team. The FHS constitutes an important strategy for reorganizing Primary Health Care and is grounded in the principles of the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), particularly universality, comprehensiveness, equity, territorialization, and social participation. The analysis shows that, since its implementation in the 1990s, the FHS has contributed to expanding access to health services, strengthening health promotion and disease prevention initiatives, bringing health teams closer to communities, and consolidating multidisciplinary work. The importance of community health workers in building relationships with families and understanding the needs of local territories is also highlighted. However, the policy presents weaknesses related to funding, infrastructure, professional turnover and staffing, inequalities among municipalities, and difficulties in coordinating the different levels of care. The changes introduced by the 2017 National Primary Health Care Policy also generated debate regarding greater flexibility in team composition and the possible weakening of the strategy’s community-based dimension. title: The Support Conditions for Successful Implementation of Indigenization Processes within a Municipal-Level Poverty Elimination Strategy
abstract: This research examines the support conditions necessary for the successful implementation of Indigenization processes as a strategy for poverty elimination. Conducted in collaboration with End Poverty Edmonton (EPE), a municipal-level nonprofit focused on poverty elimination, the study employed qualitative methods, including surveys, one-on-one interviews, focus groups, and Indigenous approaches such as conversations and sharing circles. Findings indicate that successful Indigenization requires four key conditions: reciprocal relationships, collective advocacy, space for reflection and learning, and time for adaptive and incremental change. These factors emerged as essential for fostering trust, shifting power dynamics, and embedding Indigenous ways of knowing within systems. The research underscores that Indigenization is a collective effort requiring both Indigenous and non-Indigenous collaboration, strategic learning, and sustained commitment to systemic transformation. The findings contribute to broader discussions on decolonization, reconciliation, and policy change in municipal and organizational contexts.

title: Vendi information gain for active learning and its application to ecology
abstract: Abstract While monitoring biodiversity through camera traps has become an important endeavour for ecological research, identifying species in the captured image data remains a major bottleneck due to limited labelling resources. Active learning—a machine learning paradigm that selects the most informative data to label and train a predictive model—offers a promising solution, but typically focuses on uncertainty in the individual predictions without considering uncertainty across the entire dataset. We study Vendi information gain (VIG) as an active learning policy that selects images based on their impact on dataset‐wide prediction uncertainty, capturing both informativeness and diversity. We applied VIG to two representative datasets in ecological image classification, the Kenya Camera Trap Dataset and the Missouri Camera Trap dataset, and compared VIG against common active learning methods. On both datasets, VIG achieves higher accuracy with fewer labelled examples. We further conducted extensive ablation studies to investigate the effects of the predictive model, batch sizes and other hyperparameters to find relatively robust performance from VIG. VIG has broad applicability beyond ecology, and our results highlight its value for biodiversity monitoring in data‐limited environments.

title: Comparative Performance of Mamdani and Sugeno Fuzzy Inference Systems with Gaussian Membership Functions for Mathematics Learning Assessment
abstract: Fuzzy inference systems (FISs) provide a framework for modelling the gradual and uncertain nature of student learning achievement. This study presents a controlled comparison of Mamdani and Sugeno fuzzy inference systems using Gaussian membership functions for mathematics learning assessment. The comparison retains the same dataset, input variables, Gaussian membership functions, and expert-defined rule base while changing only the inference mechanism. The dataset comprises 360 secondary school students, with examination score, assignment completion, and class participation used as input variables and teacher evaluation used as the benchmark for learning achievement. Both systems employ three Gaussian linguistic terms for each input and the same 27-rule knowledge base, while a zeroth-order Sugeno formulation is used for the Sugeno model. Model performance is evaluated using Pearson correlation coefficient, root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute error (MAE). Under the present dataset and model configuration, the Sugeno-Gaussian FIS achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.98996, RMSE of 2.7651, and MAE of 2.4279, compared with 0.9623, 7.2630, and 6.5607, respectively, for the Mamdani-Gaussian FIS. title: SCREENING OF COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT BIOMARKERS BASED ON MACHINE LEARNING AND SHAP INTERPRETABILITY ANALYSIS
abstract: This study aims to develop a cognitive impairment screening model based on the Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) using the XGBoost and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) framework, with the goal of improving predictive performance while enhancing clinical interpretability. The Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS)-1 cross-sectional dataset was used, containing multimodal clinical and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) data. After rigorous data cleaning, 235 subjects were included. Seven features with clear neurobiological significance were selected as input: Age, education, socioeconomic status, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), estimated Total Intracranial Volume (eTIV), normalized Whole Brain Volume (nWBV), and Atlas Scaling Factor (ASF). The model was evaluated using a test set from OASIS-1 and further validated on an additional OASIS-2 cohort. The proposed model achieved high performance on the OASIS-1 test set (Accuracy=0.851, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]=0.943) and demonstrated good generalization on OASIS-2 (Accuracy=0.867, AUC=0.938). SHAP analysis revealed that MMSE, nWBV, and age are the most influential features, with directionality consistent with established understanding of cognitive decline and neurodegeneration. title: Digital Twin-Driven Optimization of Mechanical Manufacturing Systems Using Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Industry 4.0 integrates cyber–physical systems, industrial Internet of Things technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and real-time analytics to improve manufacturing performance. However, small- and medium-scale manufacturing facilities frequently face fragmented automation, reactive maintenance, and limited integration between production data and operational decision-making. This study developed and experimentally evaluated an AI-enabled Digital Twin (DT) framework for optimizing a multi-station mechanical manufacturing system in Bangladesh. The manufacturing cell comprised six interconnected stations: raw-material inspection and sorting, automated loading and orientation, CNC machining, drilling and cutting, AI-assisted quality inspection, and automated storage and dispatch. A synchronized DT represented machine states, production flow, queue formation, operating parameters, energy consumption, tool condition, vibration, temperature, and quality outcomes. An AI layer supported anomaly detection and cycle-time prediction, while a multi-objective optimization mechanism balanced throughput and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) against cycle time, energy consumption, defect rate, and unplanned downtime. title: Comparing Elitist Genetic Refinement and Reference-Point-Based Multi-Objective Optimization for Deep Q-Network Cloud Task Scheduling
abstract: Cloud task scheduling must balance conflicting objectives: deadline compliance, energy consumption, makespan, and resource utilization. A common design pairs a forecasting module and a reinforcement-learning placement agent with a periodic evolutionary refinement stage, usually a single-objective genetic algorithm that merges the four objectives into one weighted score. This paper studies whether replacing that stage with the reference-point-based multi-objective Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) changes the scheduling results when forecasting and placement remain unchanged. Both strategies were evaluated on simulated five-machine clusters with workload-prediction signals from real monitoring traces over ten random seeds at 50,000 tasks (NSGA-III also at 100,000). The elitist genetic algorithm produced a mean of 0.495 percent of tasks violating their service-level agreement (SLA), against 0.178 percent for NSGA-III; a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test confirmed the difference (p = 0.0039, r = 0.854). Doubling the workload left NSGA-III’s violation rate stable (paired p = 0.426). NSGA-III needed far more time per run (48.56 versus 9.05 minutes) and slightly more energy (30,582,411 versus 30,034,047 simulation units; p = 0.0020, r = 0.886).
