Reusable and Robust Hydrogel With Dynamic Sacrificial S─S Bonds: In Situ Construction of an Integrated SEI/Hydrogel Interface for Highly Stable Zn–I 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The trade‐off among mechanical strength, ionic conductivity, and interfacial stability remains a core challenge for high‐performance hydrogel interfacial layers. Herein, an integrated SEI/polyurea–polyurethane hydrogel (PUMA) interface was constructed on the Zn anode via in situ gelation coupled with interfacial electrochemical reduction. Polyurea–polyurethane hard segments containing octuple H‐bonds, Zn 2+ coordination bonds, and dynamic S─S bonds reinforce PUMA through multi‐level energy dissipation and suppress side reactions by regulating interfacial water. Polyanionic soft segments rich in carboxyl and sulfonic acid groups construct low‐barrier, ion‐selective pathways, optimizing Zn 2+ transport and deposition by solvation regulation and mitigation of concentration polarization. Crucially, interfacial sacrificial S─S bonds undergo cleavage during electrochemical reduction, generating an integrated SEI/PUMA interface with enhanced interfacial stability. The dynamic polyanionic network also blocks polyiodide shuttling and enables thermal reprocessing. Consequently, PUMA@Zn achieves a Zn 2+ transference number of 0.79 and symmetric cell cycling for 5080 h (1 mA cm −2 and 0.5 mAh cm −2 ). title: The Effect of Leadership and Work Motivation on Employee Performance at the Department of Investment and One-Stop Integrated Services (DPMPTSP) of Palembang City
abstract: This inquiry utilizied a quantitatve design, applying multiple linear regression techniques for analisys. Information was gathered from a sample of 91 staff members as respondents. Outcome from the t-test demonstrated that leadership (X1) exerted favorable and meaningful influence on employe performance, as evidenced by a significance levek of 0,019 (0,019 < 0,05). Conversely, work motivation (X2) also yielded a substantial impac, yet it exhibited an inverse correlation with employee performance, marked by a significance level of 0,003 (0,003 < 0,05) and a t-value of -3,064. Concurrently, the F-test indicated that leadership combined with work motivation collectively and substantially influenced employe performance. Yielding a significance level of 0,000. Additionally, the coefficient of determination (R2) revealed that the independent variables accounted for 16.6% of the variance in employee performance, whereas the remaining 83,4% was attributable to alternative factors not axamined in this research. These findings imply that while work motivation lacking proper oversight can detrimentally impact employee performance within the studied organization. Keywords: Leadership, Work Motivation, Employee Performance

title: Quality of Life of Inmates in Correctional Centres in Rivers State, Nigeria: A Multi-facility Cross-sectional Study using the WHOQOL-BREF
abstract: Background: Incarceration exposes people to overcrowding, restricted contact with family and limited health care, all of which can erode quality of life (QoL). Evidence on inmates’ QoL in Nigeria is limited and mostly single-site. This study assessed QoL among inmates in three correctional centres in Rivers State, Nigeria. Methods: A descriptive, facility-based cross-sectional study was conducted between 13 May and 30 June 2026 among adult awaiting-trial and convicted inmates in the Port Harcourt, Ahoada and Degema correctional centres. Participants were selected by proportionate stratified systematic random sampling and completed a structured questionnaire that included the 26-item WHOQOL-BREF (0–100 scale). An overall QoL score below 50 was classified as poor QoL, following Galgam et al. (2025), who dichotomised the scale into good and poor quality of life because the WHOQOL-BREF has no validated cut-off. Data were analysed descriptively with SPSS version 25. Results: Of 423 questionnaires distributed, 407 were completed (response rate 96.2%). The mean age was 37.3 ± 11.4 years, and 80.8% were male. The mean overall QoL score was 40.3 ± 11.4, and 72.2% of inmates had poor QoL. The environment (32.1 ± 10.8) and social relationships (38.7 ± 15.2) domains had the lowest scores, followed by the psychological (41.5 ± 13.5) and physical health (44.2 ± 12.1) domains. title: Digital Transformation of HR Operations in Small, Field-Force-Driven Cosmeceutical Firms: A Conceptual Framework and Research Propositions Based on Secondary Evidence
abstract: Purpose: Digital human resource management (e-HRM) has been studied mostly in large and multinational organisations. This paper examines how HR digitalisation can be understood in a different setting: a small, field-force-driven firm in India's cosmeceutical and therapeutic-aesthetics segment, where a compact HR team supports employees who spend most of their time outside the office. Design/approach: The paper is conceptual. It combines published market estimates, the recent Indian regulatory changes that affect HR data and employment practice, and established technology-adoption theory (the Technology Acceptance Model, Diffusion of Innovations and socio-technical systems theory). The authors' internship context in an HR department of one such firm motivates the questions asked, but no primary survey or interview data are reported. Findings: Market sources agree on direction but not on size: estimates of India's HRMS and HR-technology market in 2024–25 range from about USD 0.87 billion to USD 1.2 billion, with projected growth rates from 7.56% to 17.34% a year. At the same time, the Labour Codes (effective 21 November 2025) and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 are turning HR systems from an administrative convenience into compliance infrastructure. title: Pengaruh Pelatihan Kerja dan Kompetensi Kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan dengan Kompensasi Sebagai Variabel Intervening pada Momo Jaya Aluminium
abstract: Penelitian ini menguji pengaruh pelatihan kerja dan kompetensi kerja terhadap kinerja karyawan dengan kompensasi sebagai variabel intervening di Momo Jaya Aluminium, Dlanggu, Mojokerto. Dengan metode kuantitatif eksplanatori, seluruh 105 karyawan dijadikan sampel melalui sampling jenuh, dan data kuesioner Likert dianalisis menggunakan PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4.0). Hasilnya, pelatihan kerja dan kompetensi kerja berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja karyawan maupun kompensasi. Kompensasi juga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kinerja serta memediasi secara parsial pengaruh pelatihan dan kompetensi (R² kompensasi = 0,814; R² kinerja = 0,673). Pengaruh langsung terbukti lebih besar daripada pengaruh tidak langsung, sementara kompensasi memiliki skor rata-rata terendah (3,98) sehingga perlu dibenahi. Perusahaan disarankan mengelola pelatihan, pengembangan kompetensi, dan sistem kompensasi secara terpadu untuk meningkatkan kinerja karyawan secara berkelanjutan.

DISASTER MANAGEMENT AND INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS IN INDIA: CHALLENGES AND REFORMS
abstract: Disaster management is an essential component of public administration, governance, and sustainable development. Its efficacy depends on a well-defined institutional framework, clear administrative responsibilities, adequate financial and human resources, effective interdepartmental coordination, and community participation. In India, the Disaster Management Act, 2005, established the legal framework for disaster management at national, state, and district levels. However, the existence of formal institutions does not automatically ensure effective implementation. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), through its reports on civil disaster preparedness and disaster management in Karnataka, has examined institutional weaknesses relating to preparedness, planning, coordination, capacity building, and early warning systems. International research has also emphasised the importance of strengthening local-government authority and capacity for disaster risk reduction. This article analyses the institutional arrangements for disaster management in India, examines documented administrative challenges, and proposes measures to improve institutional performance. It argues that disaster governance must move beyond a predominantly relief-oriented approach towards an integrated, accountable, participatory, and risk-informed system.

title: Beyond Conventional VV-ECMO: The Role of Veno-Pulmonary Support in Trauma-Associated ARDS With Right Ventricular Dysfunction
abstract: Severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) after trauma can require extracorporeal support, however, the usual approach to ARDS is often complicated by associated injuries. Prone positioning may be limited by unstable fractures or other injuries, while traumatic intracranial hemorrhage and recent bleeding can make systemic anticoagulation difficult. At the same time, severe ARDS can substantially increase right ventricular afterload and lead to right ventricular dysfunction. Conventional venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) improves gas exchange and may reduce right ventricular afterload indirectly, but it still relies on native right ventricular forward flow. Veno-pulmonary (V-P) ECMO offers an alternative by combining extracorporeal gas exchange with direct right ventricular unloading. Most published experience, however, has involved conversion to V-P support after refractory right ventricular failure has already developed. This review examines the role of V-P ECMO in severe trauma-associated ARDS, focusing on right ventricular dysfunction, selection of the initial extracorporeal configuration, and anticoagulation when traumatic bleeding limits standard management. We also describe an illustrative multiply injured patient with severe ARDS, evolving right ventricular dysfunction, and traumatic subdural hemorrhage who received V-P ECMO as the initial …

title: Aorta-to-Right Ventricle Tunnel Successfully Treated by Transcatheter Dual Konar MFO Closure: A Rare Case Report
abstract: An aortoventricular tunnel is a congenital structural defect characterized by an anomalous extracardiac channel that bypasses the normal valvular apparatus and connects the ascending aorta – at a level above the sinotubular junction – directly to a ventricular cavity. While communication with the left ventricle is the predominant form, the right ventricle (RV) may also serve as the terminal chamber, producing a hemodynamically distinct and clinically challenging variant. This RV form is a recognized – though uncommon – cause of high-output cardiac failure in pediatric patients. We present the diagnostic workup and successful transcatheter closure in a 12-year-old girl with an aorta-to-RV tunnel, demonstrating that percutaneous intervention using the Konar MFO (multifunctional occluder) device is a feasible and effective minimally invasive treatment strategy for this rare malformation.

title: Diversification Strategies, Corporate Governance Disclosure and Financial Performance of Agricultural Firms Listed at the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya
abstract: Agricultural firms listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) have recorded uneven financial performance, and evidence on whether diversification improves performance remains inconsistent. Little is known about whether corporate governance disclosure (CGD) lies on the path between diversification and performance. This study examined the association of horizontal, concentric, and conglomerate diversification with financial performance, measured by Return on Assets (ROA), and whether CGD mediated each association. The study was anchored on the Resource-Based View, supported by agency and signalling perspectives. An explanatory, longitudinal design was used with secondary data from the audited annual reports of the six agricultural firms listed at the NSE, studied as a census over 2019 to 2024 (36 firm-years). CGD was scored with a 50-item index adapted from Varshney et al. (2015) and Shrivastav and Kalsie (2017). Data were analysed using hierarchical regression, the Sobel test and bootstrap confidence intervals, followed by sensitivity checks. None of the three diversification types was associated with ROA at the 5% level, but adding CGD raised R² by .140 (B = 0.176, p = .022). CGD showed a statistically supported indirect association for horizontal diversification (indirect effect = 0.677, 95% CI [0.260, 1.124]) and concentric diversification (0.229, 95% CI [0.088, 0.383]),…

title: Who lives where? Compositional roots of the rural–urban divide in far-right populist support across Western Europe
abstract: Abstract The rise of far-right populism across Western democracies has sparked academic and public interest in its spatial dimension. Many seminal theories on the causes of far-right populism identify the rural–urban dimension as a crucial line of conflict in contemporary Western societies. However, we have surprisingly little comparative, cross-country evidence about its overlap with other social grievances. Specifically, this paper asks to what extent descriptive rural–urban differences reflect other social divides due to the unequal distribution of social groups along spatial lines. In an analysis of recent European Social Survey data from 15 Western European countries, I find significant rural–urban differences in twelve of them. A decomposition analysis using the KHB-method reveals that the estimated rural–urban difference is nearly halved once individual socio-demographic characteristics are controlled for. The compositional effects are mainly driven by differences in education, social class and—to a smaller extent—ethnic origin, but not by individual economic hardship, gender and age. I conclude that the rural–urban dimension of far-right populism is indeed evident across Western Europe and it’s also a reflection of the conflict between the ‘new’ high-educated, post-industrial middle class and the ‘old’ manual middle class.

title: Version-Bounded Filing Question Answering: A Controlled Study of Source Labels, as-of Filtering, and Model Heterogeneity
abstract: Financial question answering must distinguish a source that contains a relevant disclosure from a source eligible at the question’s cutoff. Evaluation also has to distinguish successful source selection from failures that prevent a narrow error from being counted. We examine these issues in a deterministic synthetic study of 32 original–amendment conflicts crossed with three cutoff regimes. Three prompt interfaces, four attested local model builds, and two fixed repetitions yield 2,304 retained responses. The original internally frozen cross-model hypothesis was unsupported: the mean filtered-minus-mixed wrong-version risk difference was −0.091796875, and only two of eight strata improved. A retrospective descriptive decomposition separates response-contract failure, valid abstention, correct answering, competing-version adoption, and other responses without changing frozen scores. Two builds produced no correct conflict answers in any arm while recording zero competing-version events. Their zeros therefore cannot establish successful version selection. For qwen3:8b, correct conflict answers increased from 48/128 under mixed context to 117/128 under filtering, while counted competing-version events fell from 47 to zero. Twenty-five years of progress in Parkinson’s disease research: from dopamine replacement to biological definition and regenerative therapy
abstract: Abstract The first quarter of the twenty-first century has transformed Parkinson’s disease (PD) from a predominantly motor, dopamine-deficiency syndrome into a heterogeneous multisystem disorder defined across clinical, genetic and molecular dimensions. This overview follows the trajectory of these advances from the historical foundations established prior 2000 to present concepts of prodromal disease, progression, biological classification and precision medicine. Epidemiological work has established PD as the fastest-growing major neurological disorder, while systematic characterization of non-motor symptoms has shifted diagnosis and attention beyond the nigrostriatal system in PD research. Imaging has progressed from exclusionary structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to quantitative susceptibility, diffusion and molecular approaches, although no single imaging biomarker yet provides a stand-alone diagnosis of PD. The discovery of α-synuclein gene mutations and its presence as protein in Lewy bodies and neurites connected genetics, protein aggregation and selective neuronal vulnerability. Seed amplification assays (SAA) now enable robust detection of pathological α-synuclein in cerebrospinal fluid and have catalysed biologically anchored staging proposals. At the same time, negative phase 2 antibody against α-synuclein trials illustrate the challenges of target engagemen…

title: Práticas ESG e Desempenho Financeiro: Evidências da B3
abstract: Esta pesquisa objetiva investigar a relação entre indicadores Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) e o desempenho financeiro corporativo. Com base em uma amostra de 60 empresas listadas na B3 no período de 2012 a 2019 — correspondente ao cenário pré-pandêmico —, foram estimados sete modelos econométricos por meio de regressão com dados em painel. As variáveis do estudo foram classificadas em: métricas ESG, indicadores financeiros e variáveis de controle. Os dados referentes ao desempenho socioambiental foram coletados na base CSRHub Consensus ESG Ratings, enquanto as informações financeiras foram extraídas de balanços patrimoniais e demonstrações de resultados disponíveis na Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM). Os resultados evidenciaram que a dimensão ambiental impacta negativamente o desempenho financeiro, mensurado pelo Lucro por Ação (LPA), possivelmente devido ao caráter não imediato do retorno financeiro desses investimentos. Em contrapartida, a governança apresentou relação positiva com o LPA, sugerindo que boas práticas corporativas contribuem para o resultado das organizações. Adicionalmente, observou-se um efeito significativo e negativo das variáveis de desempenho financeiro sobre o indicador geral ESG. Perceived problems in movement control at the piano among Japanese conservatory-trained classical pianists: a cross-sectional questionnaire survey screening for musician's dystonia
abstract: Abstract Musician's dystonia is a devastating task-specific movement disorder that robs performers of voluntary motor control during playing and, in progressive cases, extends to daily life, severely impacting mental health and career continuity. While research on musician's dystonia is extensive, studies specifically targeting professionally trained pianists are limited, and its etiology and optimal treatment remain unclear. This study investigated the characteristics and risk factors of focal dystonia among pianists who have received specialized piano training. An anonymous questionnaire was distributed to 2,863 individuals, including members of a professional musicians’ association in Japan (Japan Federation of Musicians), as well as students, piano teachers, and performers at music universities. Individuals reporting involuntary finger or wrist movements occurring exclusively during piano performance were operationally classified as suspected dystonia, a self-reported category that does not constitute a clinical diagnosis, and underwent secondary screening. Comparative statistical analysis was performed between the suspected dystonia group and a non-dystonia group. Among 241 valid respondents, 28 (11.6%) met this criterion. title: Quantification of Magnetic Interactions in van der Waals Heterostructures Using Lorentz Transmission Electron Microscopy and Off‐Axis Electron Holography
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic van der Waals (vdW) materials are promising for memory and logic applications because of their tunable magnetic properties and compatibility with vdW heterostructure devices. However, coupling between magnetic textures in stacked layers is difficult to resolve in conventional plan‐view measurements because the magnetic signal is integrated over the sample thickness. Here, these interactions are quantified in Fe 3 GeTe 2 (FGT)/graphite/FGT heterostructures using cross‐sectional Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and off‐axis electron holography, enabling reconstruction of the local projected magnetic induction within and between the layers. Domain alignment weakens with increasing FGT separation, yielding a stray‐field coupling length scale of nm for the cross‐sectional geometry studied here, corresponding to the average separation at which domain misalignment first emerges. This length scale corresponds to an approximately 23% reduction in the interlayer magnetic induction relative to bulk FGT. The magnetic induction is reduced relative to bulk FGT up to 100 nm from a surface. Comparisons with model‐based iterative reconstructions of the magnetization and micromagnetic simulations show that this near‐surface reduction is due to demagnetizing and stray fields. title: Role of LSG in realizing the right to education in North India
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the extent to which rural local self-governance realises the right to education through a comparative study of Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh, and examines the implementation of the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) as the principal instrument by which that right is delivered. The study adopts the Respect–Protect–Fulfil–Promote (RPFP) framework for evaluating the performance of the Gram Panchayat and the implementation of the SSA. The primary data were gathered through a mixed-method research design from 1,050 respondents, which comprised 150 Panchayat members and 900 beneficiaries, together with an institutional checklist of 29 government schools across fifteen purposively selected Gram Panchayats. The study found that awareness of the legal right and the provision of physical access are high, but the monitoring of enrolment, retention and dropout, the enforcement of protective duties, and community mobilisation are weak. Punjab lags most on monitoring and awareness, whereas Himachal Pradesh integrates governance most fully. Furthermore, the School Management Committees are universally constituted yet operate formally as it coexists with low beneficiary awareness. The article argues that decentralisation bridges rights-based legislation and educational outcomes only where local capacity, financial autonomy and outcome-based monitoring are prese…

title: Improving the clinical trial landscape for Parkinson syndromes in Germany
abstract: Abstract Germany has a longstanding tradition of excellence in neuroscience and Parkinson’s research, supported by outstanding academic institutions, specialized clinical centers, and a strong scientific community. Building on this strong foundation, the country now has the opportunity to transform its clinical research landscape into a more integrated ecosystem for Parkinson syndromes. Despite major advances in molecular understanding, biomarker development, and therapeutic innovation, important structural, regulatory, financial, and organizational barriers continue to limit the full translational potential of German Parkinson research. Participants in an expert workshop identified identify recurring challenges, including fragmented trial infrastructures, slow and bureaucratic regulatory procedures, insufficient funding for investigator-initiated clinical research, limited integration of patient organizations, and suboptimal patient recruitment pathways. This workshop-derived perspective outlines a strategic framework to elevate Germany from a country with excellent individual centers to a globally competitive and integrated hub for innovative Parkinson clinical research. title: PREVIDÊNCIA SOCIAL E AUTOPREVIDÊNCIA: DESAFIOS DA INFORMALIDADE E A URGÊNCIA DA EDUCAÇÃO FINANCEIRA NO BRASIL
abstract: Este artigo analisa o cenário previdenciário brasileiro contemporâneo, com foco na Previdência Social e na autoprevidência, diante do envelhecimento populacional, das mudanças introduzidas pela Emenda Constitucional nº 103/2019 e da persistência da informalidade em patamares elevados. O objetivo é descrever como os participantes de uma pesquisa nacional se organizam para a aposentadoria e discutir o papel da educação financeira nesse processo. Trata-se de estudo exploratório e descritivo, de abordagem quantitativa, baseado nos resultados da pesquisa realizada pela Associação Brasileira de Educadores Financeiros (ABEFIN) em setembro de 2025, com 600 entrevistados, apoiado por revisão bibliográfica e documental (2021-2026) e contextualizado com indicadores do IBGE, da OCDE, do Banco Central do Brasil, do Banco Mundial e do Ipea. Entre os participantes, 62% declararam não possuir reserva financeira para a aposentadoria, 95% afirmaram nunca ter recebido instrução formal sobre o tema e 80% manteriam o padrão de vida por no máximo seis meses em caso de perda de renda. Os resultados, de natureza descritiva e restritos à amostra, indicam coexistência entre baixa instrução previdenciária e baixa formação de reservas, sem permitir inferência causal. Microbiologically Influenced Corrosion‐Resistant Alloys: Mechanisms and Design Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) is a widespread degradation challenge threatening metallic infrastructure in marine and industrial environments. Conventional materials‐based mitigation approaches act primarily as external barriers and do not directly control the coupled microbial, electrochemical, and microstructural processes that govern long‐term damage. Unlike previous reviews organized primarily by microbial taxa or protection technologies, this review establishes a mechanism‐oriented framework that maps distinct MIC pathways to guide the rational design of MIC‐resistant alloys. The fundamental MIC mechanisms, including metabolite‐induced corrosion, oxygen concentration cells, and extracellular electron transfer, are outlined to establish the basis for bespoke materials design. Three interrelated design strategies are proposed: (i) microbial‐level inhibition through antibacterial alloying; (ii) interfacial regulation through passive film engineering to regulate charge transfer; and (iii) microstructure‐integrated design, including nanoprecipitates, multiphase structures, and multicomponent alloys, to achieve synergistic antibacterial, mechanical and corrosion‐resistant performance. Finally, key challenges and future directions toward durable and adaptive MIC‐resistant materials are discussed, providing guidance for bridging mechanistic understanding an…

Design, Synthesis, and In Silico Assessment of Phthalazine Derivatives using DFT, Molecular Docking, and ADMET Analysis
abstract: A series of phthalazine derivatives was synthesized, starting from 2-(1-oxo-4-phenylphthalazin-2(1H)-yl)acetohydrazide (1), which was efficiently converted into the oxadiazole phthalazine derivative (2) in excellent yield through a reaction with carbon disulfide under reflux. Subsequently, compound (2) served as a key intermediate to prepare a diverse range of new phthalazine derivatives (3–6) by reacting it with various alkyl halides and ethyl chloroacetate. All synthesized compounds were characterized using IR, NMR, and mass spectrometry. In addition, the molecular geometries of compounds (3–6) were optimized using density functional theory (DFT). For the in-silico evaluation, molecular docking studies were conducted against two bacterial target proteins (PDB IDs: 6TLS and 4OD9) for the synthesized derivatives. All ligands exhibited significant binding affinity values, ranging from -6.24 to -7.92 kcal/mol. Finally, drug-likeness and ADME properties were predicted using SwissADME. These findings highlight the newly synthesized phthalazine derivatives as promising antibacterial candidates for further biological investigation.

BOPPPS Instructional Framework Embedding Case‐ and Problem‐ Based Strategies in Oral Pathology Education: A Teaching Reform Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective : Oral pathology education requires students to master both foundational theoretical knowledge and clinical diagnostic reasoning, yet conventional lecture‐based instruction provides limited opportunities for structured participatory learning that actively engages both dimensions. This study evaluated the pedagogical effectiveness of the BOPPPS instructional framework—a six phase teaching model comprising bridge‐in, objective, pre‐assessment, participatory learning, post‐assessment, and summary—within an oral pathology curriculum. Within this framework, case‐based learning (CBL) and problem‐based learning (PBL) were integrated as complementary and overlapping pedagogical strategies and incorporated into phases of the BOPPPS framework, forming a unified, discipline‐adapted teaching approach. Methods : A total of 206 undergraduate oral medicine students were randomly assigned to the reform group (the BOPPPS instructional framework integrating case‐ and problem‐based strategies) or a traditional lecture‐based control group. Outcomes and learning experience were assessed through theoretical examination scores, experimental diagnostic image‐recognition performance, and student satisfaction questionnaire respectively. title: Leadership Development as an Essential Component of University-Based School Principal Preparation Programs: A Comparison of Programs in Kansas and Texas
abstract: School principals, in their role as leaders, play a critical part in overall school success. For this reason, leadership development must be considered as a central component of university-based principal preparation programs. With the variations in approaches to these programs throughout the United States in mind, this descriptive, qualitative study seeks to expand practical wisdom through a comparison of the leadership development components of two university-based principal preparation programs in Kansas and Texas. The study provides discussions on the challenge of transforming school principals into effective educational leaders and presents practical recommendations for future work on this critical domain.

title: The Influence of Market Ratio and Profitability Ratio on Stock Prices of Energy Subsector Companies on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2022–2024 Period
abstract: The objective is to determine whether liquidity and activity partially or This study was conducted to examine the effect of Price to Book Value (PBV), Return on Assets (ROA), and Net Profit Margin (NPM) on the stock prices of companies in the energy subsector on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2022-2024 period. The research sample consisted of 13 companies selected using purposive sampling. Data analysis was done using multiple linear regression with SPSS 26. The results showed that, individually, Price to Book Value (PBV) does not have a significant effect on stock prices (Sig. 0.187 > 0.05). Similarly, Net Profit Margin (NPM) also does not have a significant effect on stock prices (Sig. 0.256 > 0.05). On the other hand, Return on Assets (ROA) was proven to have a positive and significant effect on stock prices (Sig. 0.000 < 0.05). Simultaneously, the variables PBV, ROA and NPM significantly affect the stock prices of energy subsector companies on the IDX during the 2022-2024 period (Sig. 0.000 < 0.05). Keywords: Price to Book Value (PBV), Return On Assets (ROA), Net Profit Margin (NPM), Stock Price.

title: Wind Power Forecasting Under Complex Weather: Error Mechanisms, Technical Advances and Challenges
abstract: Wind power forecast errors grow markedly under complex weather and constrain secure grid integration. Earlier reviews are organised by method lineage, ramp events, uncertainties or systems, not by the error chain. This review follows the error through four steps, from the meteorological driver field and the station wind field to the conversion relationship and the turbine operating state, and separates meteorological errors from power forecast errors. Along this chain, cold fronts, deep convection, low-level jets and tropical cyclones give the error four distinct temporal forms. A timing shift, a random large deviation, a systematic diurnal bias, and a step change in operating state require different techniques. Where samples are scarce and the statistical relationship is unstable, physical constraints and data-driven methods must be fused. The error that remains divides into a part that technical means can reduce and a part set by a predictability ceiling, which does not fall with better resolution or data. Beyond the error itself, the power ramp follows the weather process rather than the forecast error, and its warning reaches dispatch separately. The gaps lie in the availability of observations and paired samples, and dispatch risk metrics cannot yet be converted into accuracy metrics.

title: Security and reliability constrained power management of virtual power plant considering ancillary services and energy markets models in smart grid
abstract: This study investigates the operation of a flexible renewable virtual power plant (VPP) with inverter-based system in a smart distribution network while considering the technical and economic objectives of the distribution system operator and maximizing the VPP’s participation in energy, reactive power, and reserve markets. A bi-level optimization framework is proposed in which the upper level minimizes a weighted combination of voltage security, power loss, and expected energy not supplied by incorporating AC optimal power flow and network security constraints. The lower level maximizes the VPP’s profit subject to inverter capabilities and operational and reserve constraints. The bi-level problem is transformed into a single-level formulation using the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions. To address uncertainties in load, renewable generation, mobile storage characteristics, market prices, and equipment availability, a hybrid stochastic-robust optimization framework is employed. Equipment availability is modeled stochastically to accurately assess reliability, whereas the remaining uncertainties are handled through robust optimization to improve resilience against forecasting errors. The proposed approach is distinguished by its inverter-based VPP model, integration of multiple technical performance indices, hybrid uncertainty modeling, and coordinated use of flexible resources for …

title: Rolling optimal dispatch method for virtual power plants integrating secondary and tertiary frequency regulation
abstract: The demand side of modern power systems contains abundant flexible resources that, when aggregated via virtual power plants (VPPs), can help alleviate the grid’s frequency regulation (FR) burden. In this paper, we propose a rolling optimal dispatch method for VPPs integrating secondary and tertiary frequency regulation. First, the adjustable capacity of various distributed energy resources (DERs) is quantified by accounting for their operational characteristics and the effects of uncertainty. Secondly, the technical characteristics and market mechanisms of secondary and tertiary frequency regulation are analyzed to formulate objective functions for DERs to jointly participate in these services, as well as the response strategy. Finally, based on the proposed strategy and optimization model, a two-stage day-ahead and intra-day rolling optimal dispatch is implemented, and the NSGA-II algorithm is employed to achieve Pareto frontier solutions. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed response strategy and multi-objective optimization model can fully exploit the regulatory potential of DERs, enabling rolling optimal dispatch for FR and dynamic adjustments to strategy parameters.

A deep learning algorithm for black hole spin estimation using hot spot secondary images
abstract: Sagittarius A* exhibits frequent flaring activity across the electromagnetic spectrum that is often associated with a localized region of strong emission known as a hot spot. Our study is aimed at training a deep learning model to provide a link between key parameters of this phenomenon (hot spot emission radius and the black hole inclination and spin) to the observed angle difference between the primary and secondary image (Δ PA) that could potentially be resolved by present and future interferometric arrays. Using the general relativistic radiative transfer code we generated a library of sim100000 models with varying system parameters and computed the position angle difference on the image plane between the primary and secondary images of the hot spot. We explored the equatorial and non-equatorial circular orbits and evaluate our models against approximate observational constraints, including partial-orbit visibility and observational errors. Our algorithm ̊amiland shows remarkable accuracy in calculating spin and inclination from the majority of the observational tests we perform (σ_ α_* ̧irc ), even in extreme conditions where only half of the orbit is visible. The off-equatorial estimation provides softer constraints in the absence of prior information. Our results demonstrate the importance of hot spot observations for spacetime estimations. Power system emulation for rapid exploration of water-energy policies
abstract: Abstract Resource systems like energy and water enable human development and economic growth. The strong linkages between river basins and electricity grids motivate adopting an integrated multi-objective approach to their planning and management to increase service levels, seek economic efficiency, and promote wider societal goals. Connecting multi-sector infrastructure system computer simulators to multi-objective search algorithms offers a practical tool for identifying synergies in these interdependent systems. However, this approach is constrained by the computational resources required to run joint energy-water simulation models many times to explore the multi-objective search space. In this study, we proposed a framework that links a fast power system model emulator to a river system simulator, then connects that integrated model to a multi-objective design process. The emulator in our case is an artificial neural network and the search algorithm is a multi-objective evolutionary optimizer. We compare optimized designs that use emulation with those from a conventional process-based simulator to check the emulators’ ability to guide a computer-aided multi-objective design process. title: Compatibility Ratio as a Guideline for Hardware/DNN Co-Design of Embedded Accelerators
abstract: Increasingly large deep neural networks (DNNs) pose a significant challenge regarding required compute capabilities and energy consumption, especially at the edge. This challenge generally necessitates dedicated inference hardware accelerators. Hardware/software co-design can improve overall system performance by jointly optimizing the hardware micro-architecture and DNN workload mapping. It is however not easy to quantify how well such an accelerator generalizes to workloads not considered during hardware/software co-design. In response to this, we introduce the Compatibility Ratio (CR) as a simple guideline for evaluating performance tradeoffs between optimal hardware micro-architecture configurations across different workloads. CR allows us to quantify the performance tradeoffs of deploying a workload on an accelerator optimized for a different workload. We demonstrate CR through two case studies on a systolic array-based accelerator. First, we apply CR to explore the design space of the accelerator across 13 DNN workloads. In this case study, CR analysis showed that the choice of representative workload during co-design can implicitly increase the normalized area-latency cost of unconsidered workloads by more than 30% in the evaluated design space. Furthermore, we use CR to analyze how well our systolic array-based accelerator template can generalize beyond a single DNN wor…

title: Compact scalable phase modulator with zero static power consumption for visible integrated photonics
abstract: Optical modulators in the visible regime have far-reaching applications from biophotonics to quantum science. Implementations of such optical phase modulators on a silicon-on-insulator waveguide platform have been mainly limited to utilization of the thermo-optic effect, liquid crystal technology, as well as piezo-optomechanical effects which are limited in modulation speed and modulation efficiency. Here, we report, to our knowledge, the demonstration of the first highly scalable compact phase modulator in the visible regime based on altering the refractive index of an indium-tin oxide capacitive stack over a Si 3 N 4 waveguide through the charge accumulation effect. The phase modulator architecture achieves a modulation efficiency, V π L, of 0.5V⋅cm at a zero static power consumption. Bandwidth and V π scale inversely, with the minimum V π value being 12.4±0.4V for a 400 µm long modulator and a corresponding phase modulator loss of 2.5 dB, and the highest −3dB bandwidth being 150 MHz for a 10 µm long modulator with a corresponding phase modulator loss of 0.06 dB. By enhancing the energy efficiency and bandwidth of phase modulators in the visible regime, this work enables implementation of large-scale and high-speed integrated photonic systems with applications from biotechnology to quantum sensing and computing.

title: Labor Mobility As An Institutional And Economic Mechanism Of Regional Labor Market Transformation
abstract: The article develops a conceptual interpretation of labor mobility as an institutional and economic mechanism of regional labor market transformation. Labor mobility is considered not only as spatial migration, but as an integrated system of territorial, sectoral, occupational, status and digital transitions of workers. The study reveals the relationship between mobility, structural unemployment, skills mismatch, informal employment, information asymmetry and transaction costs. A multi-level mechanism is proposed that connects human capital, labor market infrastructure, employers and public institutions. The author argues that the effectiveness of mobility should be assessed by the reduction of mismatches, improvement of employment quality, growth of labor income and strengthening of regional adaptability. Policy priorities for Uzbekistan include differentiated regional regulation, targeted training, digital matching services and support for the transition from informal to formal employment.

title: Heterogeneous stock market reactions to a sustainability reporting mandate: insights from the European Union
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how capital markets respond to the implementation of the EU’s Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). Both instruments are key components of the European Green Deal, designed to provide the standardized sustainability information needed to channel capital toward sustainable activities and strengthen corporate accountability. Design/methodology/approach The authors conduct an event study on five regulatory milestones – three CSRD-related and two ESRS-related events – using a matched sample of EU- and US-listed firms. In cross-sectional analyses, the authors further examine the moderating role of voluntary disclosure and environmental performance. Findings The event study results reveal heterogeneous stock market reactions. Reactions to CSRD events are significantly negative, indicating that investors view the new mandate as a cost burden. In contrast, ESRS-related events elicit positive reactions, suggesting that investors value the expected improvements in standardization and information quality. In addition, the cross-sectional analysis shows that voluntary sustainability reporting mitigates negative reactions to CSRD events, while strong environmental performance is associated with more favorable reactions to ESRS events. Research limitations/implications The finding…

title: Beyond food safety: environmental and sensory drivers of organic food purchase intention in an emerging market
abstract: Background/objectives Food perception encompasses a multidimensional evaluation of sensory, nutritional, safety, and sustainability attributes, yet the relative contribution of each dimension to attitude formation and subsequent purchase intention remains understudied in emerging market contexts. This study examines the relationships between five perceptual dimensions (food safety, naturalness, nutritional value, environmental concern, and sensory appeal) and attitudes toward organic food and purchase intention. Methods Data were collected via an online survey from 255 consumers using a non-probabilistic convenience and snowball sampling approach. Partial least squares structural equation modeling with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples was employed to test six hypothesized relationships. Results Five of the six hypothesized relationships were supported. Environmental concern, natural content, sensory appeal, and nutritional content were significantly associated with attitude, while food safety concern showed no significant association. The five perception dimensions jointly explained 64.5% of the variance in attitude. Attitude was strongly associated with purchase intention, supporting its central role within the proposed model. Conclusion Food perception operates through an integrated, multidimensional assessment rather than single attributes. The findings highlight the relevance of …

title: Health complexity, metabolic health and service use in a high need primary care population in Aotearoa New Zealand: a cross-sectional study
abstract: aim: The aim of this study was to understand the characteristics, health complexity and intensity of service provision for patients aged 16 years or older enrolled in a high-need practice. methods: This cross-sectional study used routinely collected data from an urban Very Low Cost Access practice serving a high-need population in Cannons Creek, Porirua, Aotearoa New Zealand. All patients aged ≥16 years enrolled for a 12-month period were included. Demographic, clinical, biological, medication and service use variables were extracted, and individuals were categorised into normoglycaemia, prediabetes and diabetes groups. Analyses used descriptive statistics, age-standardised rates and comparative assessments of health complexity and service utilisation. results: The population (n=4,715) was predominantly Pacific, with most living in areas of high socio-economic deprivation and 25% classified with prediabetes or diabetes. Younger adults with diabetes had disproportionately high HbA1c and elevated albuminuria. Long-term conditions (LTCs), particularly obesity-related conditions, increased progressively across the glycaemic spectrum, with twofold to fourfold higher rates in dysglycaemia. Prediabetes and diabetes groups had similar LTC profiles. Service use increased with worsening dysglycaemia, with individuals with diabetes having nearly double the consultation rates, triple the p…

title: How Australian fire and rescue service personnel would like to improve their decision-making learning and training programs
abstract: Effective management of the response to an incident or emergency event is critically dependent on the decision-making skills of incident and emergency management (IEM) personnel. In a series of workshops conducted in 2022 by Natural Hazards Research Australia, priorities were identified that specified future needs for the practice and training of IEM decision-making. The research in this paper contributes to the understanding of how to address these priorities by considering the views of a sample of fire and rescue service personnel about their agency’s current decision-making training program and aspects to improve. This paper provides findings from 34 semi-structured interviews with fire and rescue services personnel in Australia. The sample comprised 29 men and 5 women. Participants worked in rural fire services (n=17), urban fire services (n=9) and State Emergency Services (n=8). The findings suggest that there is need for greater training focus on emergency management decision-making, greater use of exercise-based training activities, a formal approach to mentoring and coaching staff development programs and mandatory refresher courses and review exercises to maintain incident management skills. Australian fire and rescue services agencies need to ensure they are taking a strategic and holistic approach to emergency management learning and development programs.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and drivers of forest ecosystem service value in China based on the equivalent factor method
abstract: Introduction To assess forest ecosystem service value (FESV) in China and support ecological conservation and high-quality forest ecosystem development, this study examined FESV from 2000 to 2023 from a geographical perspective. Methods The equivalent factor method was applied with coefficient adjustments at the provincial and county levels. County-level FESV estimates were aggregated to obtain provincial and national estimates for each year, and the center-of-gravity model, standard deviational ellipse, and Geodetector were used for analysis. Results The results showed that: (1) FESV in China followed an overall upward trend with fluctuations, increasing by 12% from 2000 to 2023. Regulating services accounted for the largest share, exceeding 66% in every year. (2) Total FESV was highest in western China, which accounted for more than 46% of the national total on average over the study period. Central and northeastern China occupied intermediate positions, while eastern China had the lowest total FESV. FESV per unit forest ecosystem area was highest in eastern China, while central China generally ranked second, with relatively lower values in northeastern and western China. Provinces in the highest FESV class (Level 5) were mainly located in western and northeastern China, and their number increased from two to four. The distribution of low-value provinces remained relatively s…

title: Live communication between doctor and patient as a core value of medical service: ideology of professional culture against depersonalization in the artificial intelligence era
abstract: Modern concept of the medicine's digital future, as a rule, links the patient's satisfaction with the visit to the medical institution with the level of its technical capacity, but the patient's assessment of the medical service provided is determined first of all by the live human contacts. However implementation of the artificial intelligence creates the risks of depersonalization of such contacts.

title: Ubuntu education as a decolonial praxis in pre-service teacher education
abstract: Ubuntu is widely referenced in African educational discourse, yet its integration into pre-service teacher education remains limited and largely superficial. It is frequently reduced to mission-statement rhetoric or simplified phrases such as ‘I am because we are’, with little engagement with its deeper epistemological, pedagogical or philosophical dimensions. This study examines how Ubuntu can be translated from philosophy to pedagogy to praxis within South African pre-service teacher education, exploring how it might more substantively inform teacher formation than its current symbolic usage. A conceptual, qualitative-exploratory design is employed to generate theoretical insight. The study integrates appreciative inquiry with dialogical literary analysis, drawing on a range of texts to construct a comprehensive account of Ubuntu education. Ubuntu philosophy and Ubuntugogy serve as interconnected conceptual frameworks informing the development of an Ubuntu praxis model for curriculum design, pedagogical strategies and teacher preparation. The research identifies a tension between the aspirational discourse surrounding Ubuntu and its limited practical implementation in teacher education. It argues for a deliberate, decolonial integration of Ubuntu that moves beyond symbolic acknowledgement towards meaningful educational praxis. Positioned within a decolonial philosophical and …

title: Service-oriented transformation breeds digital catering: variation by ownership
abstract: Purpose The literature has attributed enterprise digital catering to corporate finance and corporate governance factors, including operational pressure and individual or organizational characteristics; however, the role played by enterprise strategy in this context has been overlooked. From the perspective of enterprise ownership, this study examines the heterogeneous effects of service-oriented transformation on digital catering and identifies the moderating roles played by public attention, equity incentives, and information transparency in this context. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a propensity score matching difference-in-differences method to examine how service-oriented transformation influences digital catering and explores the underlying mechanisms from the perspective of ownership. The study uses panel data obtained from Chinese listed manufacturing enterprises between 2010 and 2023. Findings The effect of service-oriented transformation on digital catering varies across different ownership structures. Service-oriented transformation stimulates digital catering among state-owned enterprises (SOEs) but has no statistically significant effect on non-SOEs. These findings indicate that SOEs have strong incentives to engage in digital catering because of their affiliation with the government administrative system. Further analysis reveals that, in the cont…

title: Optimizing the Implementation of a Tiered Nursing Supervision System to Improve Service Quality in the Hospital Emergency Department
abstract: Nursing supervision is an essential directing and controlling function in maintaining nursing care quality, yet it had never been implemented in the Emergency Department (ED) of Rumah Sakit Ketergantungan Obat (RSKO) Jakarta, a national referral hospital for substance use disorders. This activity aimed to optimize the implementation of a tiered nursing supervision system in the unit. It was conducted from 24 August to 15 September 2026. The implementation method followed the planning stage (developing clinical and managerial supervision instruments), organizing (role allocation), staffing (socialization with pre-test and post-test), actuating (real supervision trials), and controlling (documentation and evaluation), targeting the Head Nurse, 1 Team Leader, and 8 staff nurses. Evaluation used the four-level Kirkpatrick model. Results showed an increase in participants’ understanding after socialization, from an average of 64% to 84.8% (post-test score range 72.7% to 90.9%). The managerial supervision trial achieved 100% (Very Good category) in a single observation, while clinical supervision of 8 staff nurses averaged 89% (Good category), with gaps in withdrawal scale assessment, crisis management skills, the 6 Rights of medication administration (50%), and infection prevention, occupational safety, and documentation. This activity indicates that a tiered supervision system can …

Academic self-condemnation, maladaptive emotion regulation, and NSSI-related risk cognition in chinese adolescents: a three-wave cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Academic pressure is a salient developmental context in Chinese adolescence, but longitudinal evidence is limited on how academic difficulty is internalized as shame-based self-evaluation and linked to later non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) risk cognition. Methods The study involved 3,734 secondary school students from Zhejiang Province, China, of whom 2,915 completed assessments at baseline (T1), 6 months (T2), and 12 months (T3). The primary complete-case analysis included 2,854 adolescents across 134 classes. We examined the prospective relationships from T1 shame and guilt proneness to T2 academic self-evaluative burden and cognitive emotion regulation, as well as from these T2 variables to T3 future likelihood of NSSI, conceptualized as NSSI-related risk cognition. Results T1 Shame-NSE was associated with higher T2 academic self-evaluative burden (β = 0.102, 95% CI [0.066, 0.138]). Academic burden was contemporaneously associated with catastrophizing (β = 0.176, 95% CI [0.133, 0.220]) and self-blame (β = 0.234, 95% CI [0.191, 0.277]), and all three T2 constructs were independently associated with higher T3 self-reported future NSSI likelihood (ORs = 1.19–1.22). Shame-Withdraw, the guilt facets, and rumination showed no independent T3 associations in simultaneous models. In the exploratory behavioral analysis, academic burden was also associated with newl…

Precarbonization Structural Regulation in CMS Membranes via Volatile Small Molecules for Enhanced Gas Separation
abstract: Abstract Carbon molecular sieve (CMS) membranes hold substantial promise for energy-efficient gas separation. A novel membrane formation regulation strategy was developed by introducing ammonium acetate (AA) into a 6FDA-TMPD polyimide (PI) precursor to tailor precursor chain packing and carbon microstructure evolution in CMS membranes. During membrane formation and thermal treatment, the volatilization and removal of AA loosened PI chain packing (d-spacing from 5.66 to 5.87 Å) and optimized free-volume distribution, which further promoted favorable carbon layer stacking, as well as abundant micropore and ultramicropore formation. By optimizing AA content and carbonization temperature, the optimal CMS membrane with 10 wt % AA at 550 °C (PI-10AA-550) delivered significantly enhanced gas permeabilities (H2 = 11580.1 ± 363.4 Barrer, CO2 = 7065.6 ± 103.7 Barrer) and selectivities (H2/CH4 = 102.9 ± 4.1, CO2/CH4 = 62.8 ± 2.1), surpassing the state-of-the-art upper bounds. Moreover, the membrane showed excellent anti-aging property and long-term stability over 28 days of operation, demonstrating considerable potential for efficient H2 and CO2 separation.

Frequency-dependent time delays in Sgr A* from a broadband VLA observation
abstract: Frequency-dependent radio time delays have been measured in Sgr A* light curves, with higher-frequency emission generally leading lower-frequency emission. These frequency-dependent lags have been interpreted in terms of an organized jet-like outflow, expanding plasma components, or magnetic-flux eruptions, although their origin and recurrence remain uncertain. We aim to search for and quantify frequency-dependent radio time delays in a new high-cadence Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) observation of Sgr A*. Using the improved broad 12--37 GHz frequency coverage on the VLA, we measured the timing of the dominant variability feature and compared the resulting lag--wavelength slope with previous measurements. Sgr A* was observed with the VLA on 28 May 2022 in the Ku, K, and Ka bands over an sim6 hour track. We extracted both band-averaged and 2 GHz subband light curves and measured the delays using a peak-time method and a locally normalized cross-correlation function. The light curves show one broad variability feature across the observed frequency range, with the maximum occurring progressively later at lower observing frequencies. Both timing methods recover a positive lag--wavelength relation, with a slope of order 40 . This value agrees with time lag results reported over more than 15 years from the first VLA observations at 22--43 GHz to later multifrequency VLA and AL…

Markov-Switching Multifractal Models for High-Frequency Trade Counts
abstract: Abstract This study extends the Markov-switching multifractal Poisson model for counts by incorporating zero inflation and adopting a generalized Poisson distribution. The zero-inflation component enables explicitly setting the probability of zeros, while the more general distribution provides control over the degree of conditional overdispersion and greater overall flexibility. Within this setting, we develop several analytical results to provide insight into the sources of count variation. The new models are applied to high-frequency trade count data for ten NYSE-listed stocks. The results suggest that the generalized Poisson distribution can account for part of the volatility generated by the intensity process in the basic model. This extension also performs best in-sample, with the lowest Bayesian information criterion for eight out of ten stocks. Out-of-sample, the zero-inflated specification appears to perform best overall, with the highest predictive likelihoods for six stocks. For point forecasting, other models are preferred, whereas for zero-event prediction it outperforms the alternatives for all but one stock. Taken together, the extensions can provide substantial improvements in the log likelihood, both in- and out-of-sample.

title: Resolvin D1 engages FPR2–ARRB2 signaling and chromatin–microRNA regulation to restrain inflammatory activation in bovine mammary epithelial cells
abstract: Introduction Mammary epithelial cells are active participants in local innate immunity, mounting NF-κB-dependent cytokine responses to inflammatory stimuli. Excessive or persistent activation of this pathway, however, can sustain inflammation. Resolvin D1 (RvD1) is a lipid mediator with pro-resolving activity, but the specific mechanism by which RvD1 regulates inflammation in bovine mammary epithelial cells remains to be elucidated. Methods Using an LPS-induced inflammatory model in MAC-T bovine mammary epithelial cells, with selected responses confirmed at predefined time points in primary bovine mammary epithelial cells, this study investigated how RvD1 pretreatment attenuates subsequent LPS-induced inflammatory activation. Results The results showed that RvD1 significantly inhibited LPS-induced mammary epithelial inflammation, and that its early anti-inflammatory effect involved FPR2/ARRB2-associated suppression of NF-κB signaling. Further investigation showed that ARRB2 contributed to the RvD1-mediated reduction in p65 and HDAC1 enrichment at the MEG3 promoter-proximal region and the restoration of H3K27ac at this region. Meanwhile, RvD1 increased CREB phosphorylation in an FPR2-sensitive manner and increased CREB enrichment at this region; CREB1 knockdown attenuated the RvD1-associated increases in MEG3 and DLK1–DIO3 locus-associated miRNAs. Among these miRNAs, bta-miR-380…

Carbon price distortion and energy resource misallocation: evidence from China’s emissions trading scheme
abstract: Abstract The Coase Theorem suggests that carbon markets should primarily perform two functions: price discovery and resource allocation. However, carbon price distortions may weaken both functions, raising concerns over resource misallocation and a possible “distortion superposition” effect. This study constructs a generalized cost function incorporating factor price distortions and carbon emission constraints to measure the degree of carbon price distortion. Using panel data for 30 Chinese provinces from 2000 to 2022 and a difference-in-differences approach, we examine how carbon price distortion affects energy resource misallocation in emissions trading scheme (ETS) pilot regions. The results show that energy misallocation is widespread across provinces and exhibits substantial regional heterogeneity. More importantly, the implementation of the ETS significantly aggravates energy misallocation in pilot areas, indicating that the policy, at its current stage, has not effectively directed energy resources toward high-efficiency and low-carbon sectors. Carbon price distortion further amplifies this adverse effect: the larger the deviation of carbon prices from their reasonable level, the stronger the ETS-induced deterioration in energy allocation. Mechanism analysis shows that carbon price distortion exacerbates energy misallocation mainly by constraining energy input and inhibi…

title: Role of Cardiogenic Shock Centres and Regionalised Networks for Acute MI-related Cardiogenic Shock: State-of-the-art Review on Behalf of the British Cardiovascular Interventional Society Focus Group
abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) complicating acute MI (AMI-CS) remains associated with high mortality and morbidity, despite advances in coronary revascularisation and mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Outcomes are determined not only by individual therapies, but also by the organisation of care, with current guidelines emphasising multidisciplinary, system-level approaches to enable rapid diagnosis, triage and treatment. This review examines how CS centres function within regional networks of care. We review definitions of AMI-CS, including haemodynamic, clinical and biochemical markers and their application to early identification and triage. We summarise key components of centre-based management, including revascularisation, invasive haemodynamic assessment, selective MCS use and post-percutaneous coronary intervention critical care. Contemporary data from dedicated CS centres and regionalised network models are compared, highlighting variations in transfer criteria and hub–spoke organisation alongside limitations in current evidence. The distinct phenotypic nuances of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest-associated CS are discussed and gaps in evidence with future perspectives are highlighted.

title: Sentiment-Driven Forecasting of Fractional Trading Activity Using LSTM Networks
abstract: Abstract Fractional trading has emerged as an opportunity for investors to invest in fractions of shares, enabling access to high-priced stocks even with small budgets, and thus reaching a bigger investment community. Aside from the inventory risk faced by all market makers, providers of fractional trading are unable to perfectly hedge their positions and therefore need to forecast retail investors’ order flow over short time horizons to manage their market risk. We develop machine learning models to predict trading activity in fractional trading using time series data on investor holdings of a large set of securities across different sectors combined with daily news sentiment indicators. Our approach proceeds in two stages. First, securities are grouped into clusters with similar trading patterns, and representative firms are selected from each cluster. Second, trading activity is modeled using long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks augmented with sentiment features. The results show that fractional trading activity can be modeled with meaningful predictive accuracy and that incorporating news sentiment improves LSTM performance in most cases. In two stylised examples, we demonstrate approaches to hedging and market risk management using the LSTM predictions. Feature importance analysis using methods from explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) identifies the primary …

title: Physics-guided non-crossing probabilistic forecasting for distributed photovoltaic clusters using dynamic graph attention
abstract: Accurate probabilistic forecasting of geographically distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation is challenged by incomplete measurements, weather-dependent cross-site correlations, and quantile crossing. This study proposes a physics-guided framework that integrates a physics-informed Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (PIL-WGAN-GP), a dual-exploration spatiotemporal graph neural network (DEST-GNN), and an arbitrary-quantile recurrent decoder (AQ-RNN). The imputation module combines self-supervised masking, solar geometry, a clear-sky-based power envelope, and deterministic projection. The forecasting module fuses a static spatial prior with a time-varying dependency graph, while the decoder predicts aggregate PV quantiles directly through bounded positive spacings and monotone interpolation. The framework was evaluated in a retrospective case study using hourly PV generation records from 11 Belgian regional PV zones and matched meteorological records in 2025. For 3-, 6-, and 12-h consecutive gaps, PIL-WGAN-GP reduced normalized mean absolute error from 1.450%, 2.473%, and 5.252% for linear interpolation to 0.869%, 1.027%, and 1.300%, respectively. Hard projection eliminated nighttime leakage and upper-envelope violations. Across 1-, 6-, 12-, and 24-h horizons, DEST-GNN-AQ reduced the average daylight nMAE from 3.689% for the no-graph AQ-RNN to 3.509…

title: AI-driven forecasting and portfolio optimization under ESG and uncertainty regimes: evidence from global equity indices
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how advanced machine learning (ML) and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models can enhance forecasting accuracy and portfolio decision-making under environmental, social, and governance (ESG)-driven and uncertainty-sensitive market conditions. The objective is to compare the predictive efficiency of state-of-the-art ML architectures with policy-based portfolio strategies to uncover the role of sustainability indicators in shaping market dynamics. Design/methodology/approach We analyze daily data for major ESG and conventional market indices across the USA, Europe, and China, integrating the Standard Statistics Company and Poor's Publishing Company (S&P) Green Bond Index, Geopolitical Risk (GPR), the US Financial Stress Index (FSI), Physical Risk Index (PRI), and Transition Risk Index (TRI). The forecasting stage combines a 20-day long short-term memory (LSTM) temporal representation with Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) under a strict 70/15/15 chronological train-validation-test design and train-only scaling. The portfolio stage compares Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) in a weekly self-financing environment with long-only weights, a 40% position cap, and proportional tra…

title: AI-Enabled ATC Decision Support Systems: A Systematic Review Of Trajectory Prediction, Conflict Detection, And Human-AI Teaming In The Loop
abstract: This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesises recent evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled Air Traffic Control (ATC) decision-support systems and examines how AI is used to improve operational performance, safety, and resilience in increasingly complex airspace. Research on machine learning, optimisation, and automation has expanded rapidly, but evidence remains fragmented across application areas and validation settings. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020-guided protocol was used to search Scopus and IEEE Xplore for English-language journal articles published from 2021 to 2025. Following screening, full-text eligibility assessment, and final reconciliation of study type, scope, and duplicate records, 30 eligible primary studies (n = 30) were included in the qualitative synthesis. The abstract level reporting completeness appraisal yielded a mean score of 80.28% and a median of 83.33%; 16 of 30 studies (53.33%) scored at least 80%, including six studies (20.00%) that scored at least 90%. These percentages describe reporting completeness rather than algorithmic performance. Blood–Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction by Integrating Deep Learning Representations with Chemical Compound Knowledge
abstract: Abstract Predicting blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability is essential for central nervous system drug discovery, but traditional descriptor-based methods of predicting BBB permeability lack structural context, and deep learning-based methods struggle with overfitting. We introduce a multimodel framework that integrates both transformer-derived molecular embeddings with physicochemical descriptors using a late-stage ensemble fusion strategy. Trained on both the B3DB and NeuTox data sets and evaluated on the benchmark BBBP, our model showed strong predictive performance, with data set-dependent performance. Feature fusion improved performance relative to embedding-only models in several settings, whereas descriptor-based models achieved comparable or higher performance in some settings. These results suggest that combining learned structural embeddings with chemical descriptors provides complementary predictive information, while the benefit of their integration may depend on the data distribution or classifier used.

title: Prognostic prediction of pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma using a transformer-based artificial intelligence model: a two-center retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas (pNECs) are a rare and heterogeneous group of malignancies, ranging from low-grade carcinoids to high-grade small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) and large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC). Prognostic tools for these tumors are scarce and have rarely been validated in external cohorts. Objectives This study aimed to develop a Transformer-based prognostic prediction model for pNEC and validate it in an independent external cohort, to improve survival estimation and support individualized treatment decisions. Methods This retrospective two-center cohort study included 823 patients with surgically resected pNEC (2001-2023). Models were developed in Center 1 (n=374; randomly split 8:2 into training and internal test sets) and externally validated in an independent Center 2 cohort (n=449). Three algorithms—logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), and the Transformer-based tabular foundation model TabPFN—were compared for estimating overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) at 1-, 3-, and 5-year landmarks, with evaluation by receiver operating characteristic, calibration, and decision curve analyses, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis for interpretability. Results TabPFN achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) in most tasks in both test sets, with task-dependent exceptions: in the internal test set…

title: Machine Learning Prediction of Transport Properties in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural Descriptors
abstract: Abstract Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries. They offer improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging. Ionic conductivity and diffusivity depend on complex, coupled interactions between polymer structure, chemistry, and ion dynamics. This work leverages machine learning to predict four key transport properties in amorphous polymer electrolytes using a molecular dynamics data set of more than 6,000 polymer electrolyte systems. These are ionic conductivity, bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TFSI) diffusivity, lithium-ion diffusivity, and polymer diffusivity. To enhance predictive capability and preserve mechanistic interpretability, we engineered chemically and structurally meaningful features from Simplified Molecular-Input Line-Entry System (SMILES) representations. Selected features include elemental composition, functional group densities, polarity descriptors, and polymer flexibility metrics. Three modeling frameworks were trained and evaluated under 5-fold cross-validation, including random forest, gradient boosting, and neural networks. Improving public transport prediction accuracy through multi-source data integration
abstract: This study proposes a data acquisition, preprocessing and machine learning pipeline to enhance the accuracy of travel time estimates for the public bus network in Ljubljana, Slovenia. Existing prediction services often rely on vehicle location and may insufficiently capture dynamic congestion and contextual conditions. Using data from five Ljubljana Passenger Transport (LPP) routes, we evaluate LPP and Google Routes estimates against observed travel times. We develop a multisource model combining real-time variables with contextual predictors, including bus line, time of day, day type, and weather. The approach demonstrates how multisource integration of local transit feeds, external routing, and environmental indicators can improve prediction accuracy, reliability, and overall performance.

Deciphering the Mechanisms of Cassava Response to Continuous Cropping and Drought Stress via Multi-Omics Integration
abstract: Abstract Continuous cropping (CC) and drought are major constraints on cassava production in China, though their individual and combined stress mechanisms remain unclear. A pot experiment employing a 2 × 2 × 3 factorial design was established to evaluate cassava performance under continuous cropping and drought stress. Compared to drought, CC more severely increased rhizosphere soil organic acid content, reduced pH, and diminished bacterial diversity and richness, thereby inducing negative allelopathic effects on cassava. The relative abundance of Chloroflexi and norank_c__AD3 was increased under CC treatment, a shift that potentially exacerbates soil microecological imbalance. CC-induced soil stress triggers jasmonic acid and salicylic acid accumulation, as well as MAPK-mediated defense pathways in cassava roots. Yet, this sustained immune activation incurs a heavy metabolic cost, ultimately compromising plant growth and yield. These findings offer novel insights into the mechanisms underlying cassava CC obstacles and identify potential targets for enhancing stress resilience.

title: Tissue-resolved transcriptomic and proteomic profiling reveals organ-specific molecular signatures associated with inter-animal variation in glycemic response to metformin in obese diabetic Mongolian gerbils
abstract: Background Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) affects hundreds of millions of people worldwide. Metformin remains first-line therapy for obese T2DM; yet, 30–40% of patients fail to achieve adequate glycemic control with monotherapy, the magnitude of HbA1c reduction varies two- to threefold between individuals, and the multi-organ coordination underlying this inter-animal variation in glycemic response remains unclear. Methods Obese diabetic Mongolian gerbils were administered metformin (100 mg/kg/day, oral gavage; n = 4) or vehicle (n = 3) for 5 weeks. We performed matched transcriptomic (RNA-seq) and data-independent acquisition proteomic profiling of liver, skeletal muscle, and inguinal white adipose tissue. Cross-omics analyses were anchored to glycemic parameters, and key hepatic findings were validated by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR). Gut microbiota were profiled via metagenomic sequencing. Results Metformin lowered 2-hour post-load glucose (2hPG) and ameliorated hepatic steatosis. In the liver, integrated transcriptomic–proteomic analysis revealed concordant downregulation of mitochondrial substrate carriers (Slc25a47, Slc25a29, Slc25a30) and lipid-handling factors (e.g. Apoa5, Apoc2), correlating with systemic glycemic burden among treated animals. In skeletal muscle, pathway-level integration supported the activation of metabolic remodeling pr…
