Mechanical Response and Motion-Mode Dependence of Phonon-Mediated Energy Dissipation in Si–MoS2–Si Sandwich Structure
abstract: Abstract Building on previous studies of monolayer MoS2, this work constructs an atomistic Si–MoS2–Si sandwich structure and investigates its mechanical response and phonon-mediated energy dissipation under interfacial confinement. The tensile results show that the mechanical strength of the sandwich structure gradually decreases as the Si–MoS2 interfacial spacing decreases within the range examined. During fatigue loading, the constraining effect of the Si atomic layers suppresses the out-of-plane deformation of the MoS2 nanosheet and dissipates part of the input energy through lattice vibrations, thereby improving the mechanical stability and fatigue performance of the sandwich structure. However, when fatigue resonance is induced by the external cyclic loading, the central MoS2 nanosheet still fails rapidly. Regarding frictional behavior, two relative motion modes between the upper and lower Si atomic layers and the central MoS2 nanosheet are examined: linear motion and reciprocating motion. Compared with linear motion, reciprocating motion produces a higher degree of phonon-mode matching between the Si atomic layers and the MoS2 nanosheet, facilitating the formation of efficient energy-dissipation pathways and resulting in greater frictional energy dissipation. In addition, owing to the resonance effect, the frictional energy dissipation exhibits a pronounced peak character…

title: Conditioned media derived from HepG2 cells treated with phosphoeleganin synthetic-derived compound PE/2 improve cytokine balance and metabolic response in 3T3-L1 adipocytes
abstract: Background The liver–adipose axis regulates insulin sensitivity and lipid metabolism, and its dysregulation contributes to metabolic disorders. PE/2, a semisynthetic derivative of the marine natural product phosphoeleganin, reduces IL-6 expression and secretion, enhancing insulin sensitivity in liver cells (HepG2). However, its role in liver–adipose communication is unclear. Methods To clarify the impact of PE/2 on liver–adipose tissue crosstalk, the conditioned media approach was used. Protein and mRNA levels were analyzed by Western blot and Real-Time RT-PCR, respectively. Lipid and glucose metabolism were evaluated by Oil Red O staining and glucose consumption assays, respectively. Results Our results indicate that in 3T3-L1 adipocytes, conditioned media derived from PE/2-treated HepG2 cells (CM PE/2 ) increased adiponectin expression by 1.85-fold and reduced interleukin-8 and interleukin-1β mRNA levels by 43% and 52%, respectively, compared with conditioned media alone (CM). The protective adipokine phenotype induced by CM PE/2 was accompanied by 1.75-fold lipid accumulation and increased expression of adipogenic markers, including PPARγ , C/EBPα , GLUT4 , and FABP4 . To examine whether this profile translates into enhanced insulin sensitivity, we evaluated the insulin pathway. Cyclic response characteristics of RC interior beam–column joints with unintended variations in material properties
abstract: Beam–column joints are critical components of reinforced concrete (RC) moment-resisting frames, where seismic performance depends on strength, stiffness degradation, energy dissipation, damping and ductility. In this study, the influence of unintended material-property variations on three full-scale RC interior beam–column joints subjected to quasi-static reversed cyclic loading under constant axial compression was investigated. The specimens tested were one control joint with a higher concrete compressive strength (fc = 28 MPa) (BCJ-28) and two joints with lower concrete strength (fc = 21 MPa) (BCJ-21 and BCJ-1.5). BCJ-1.5 had a higher column longitudinal reinforcement ratio of 1.5%. Material testing revealed lower than specified fc and higher than anticipated reinforcement yield strength, reducing the intended strong-column–weak-beam and joint shear strength ratios. All specimens exhibited stable hysteretic behaviour up to drift ratios of 2.4–2.9%, followed by progressive deterioration governed by joint shear cracking, bond deterioration, reinforcement slip and concrete crushing. The stiffness decreased by 30–45% after cracking, while the residual stiffness converged to approximately 19% of the initial value. Higher fc improved stiffness retention, lateral resistance and energy dissipation, whereas increased column reinforcement provided modest benefits. Existing damping–duct…

Citrullinated histone H3 and elevated polyamine metabolism gene expression in peripheral blood polymorphonuclear leukocytes as biomarkers for poor immunotherapy response in cancer patients
abstract: Abstract There is a critical need to identify validated biomarkers that can predict cancer patient outcomes. This study evaluated biomarkers of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and polyamine gene expression in peripheral blood that may correlate with greater risk for poor response to immunotherapy. Peripheral blood collected from cancer patients being treated with chemo/immunotherapy and from healthy volunteers was analyzed for levels of citrullinated histone H3 (Cit H3, a NETosis marker), inflammatory cytokines, and circulating tissue factor positive microparticles (TF + MPs). Elevated levels of plasma TF + MPs, Cit H3, IL-8, and IL-6 each significantly correlated with poor response to immunotherapy. Since in vitro stimulation of both human and mouse neutrophils to form NETs was blocked with addition of an inhibitor of polyamine uptake (Trimer44NMe), RNA expression of polyamine/glutamine metabolism genes was evaluated in both peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMN). Elevated expression of glutamine-associated genes in PBMCs and decreased expression of polyamine-associated genes in PMN correlated with favorable patient response to immunotherapy. Although not reaching significant levels, a high overall polyamine score in peripheral PMNs as well as increased plasma Cit H3 levels correlated well with poor response to immunotherapies i…

title: Assessment of mechanical response and damage mechanisms in fly ash and basalt fiber beams strengthened with different FRP wrap configurations
abstract: Abstract Sustainable materials and effective strengthening methods can contribute to the significant improvement of the structural performance and durability of reinforced concrete (RC) beams. 40% cement-fly ash replacement offers better sustainability and workability, whereas fibre reinforcement and external fibre reinforced polymer (FRP) wrapping are able to offer better strength and ductility. This paper is an experimental study where thirteen RC beams were studied, one of them being a conventional control beam, basalt fibre reinforced beam (BFRB) fibre contents of 0.5%, 1%, 1.5%, 2% and beams strengthened by applying E-glass fibre reinforced polymer (EGFRP) wraps, and glass fibre reinforced polymer (GFRP) wraps at 50, 75, 100, and 150 mm. In all mixes of concrete, fly ash was used as a partial replacement of cement (12.5%). The beams were tested to assess the load–deflection response, stiffness, ductility, cracking and failure modes. The mid-span deflections were determined analytically and the deflection was determined by the double integration method, which was compared to the experimental results. Basalt fibre content was found to result in much higher load-carrying capacity, stiffness, ductility and crack control than in the control beam, and a 1.5% of basalt fibre gave the best balance between strength and deformation capacity. A higher fibre dosage of 2.0% resulted in…

Concomitant Fibromyalgia in Patients With Other Rheumatic Diseases: Pain Level and Treatment Response
abstract: Introduction: Fibromyalgia commonly coexists with rheumatic diseases and may complicate disease assessment and management. This study evaluated whether patients with rheumatic diseases and concomitant fibromyalgia differed in pain severity and patient-perceived treatment response compared with those without fibromyalgia. Methods: Four patient groups were evaluated in a historical, cross-sectional study: (1) fibromyalgia alone, diagnosed using the 2016 American College of Rheumatology criteria; (2) another rheumatic disease and concomitant fibromyalgia, requiring a fibromyalgia Polysymptomatic Distress Scale (PDS) score of >11 points; (3) another rheumatic disease and a PDS score of 10 or 11 indicating “borderline” fibromyalgia; (4) a control group consisting of patients with nonfibromyalgia rheumatic disease and a PDS score <10. Pain level (0=no pain, 10=worst pain possible) and treatment response (0=no response, 10=positive response) were assessed with visual analog scales. Results: Among 503 patients, 108 were diagnosed with fibromyalgia alone; 83 with concomitant FMS; 39 with borderline FMS; and 273 with nonfibromyalgia rheumatic disease. The worst pain was reported by patients with concomitant fibromyalgia (mean, 6.7), followed by those with fibromyalgia alone (6.3) and borderline concomitant fibromyalgia (6.2). title: Assessment of the dynamic response of Croatian cultural heritage buildings to microseismic noise measurements
abstract: Purpose The 2020 Zagreb and Petrinja earthquakes caused damage to cultural heritage buildings in Croatia, motivating an investigation of their seismic response using non-invasive methods. This study focuses on two monuments: Trakošćan Castle and the Cathedral of St James in Šibenik. Design/methodology/approach Non-invasive ambient noise measurements are diagnostic tool for the preliminary assessment of post-earthquake effects. Ambient vibration measurements were conducted at Trakošćan Castle after the 2020 earthquakes and compared with pre-earthquake data to identify changes in dynamic properties. For the Cathedral of St James, pre-earthquake ambient vibration measurements of the structure were integrated with a microzonation study of predominant ground frequencies in its surroundings to assess potential soil-structure interaction effects. Findings For Trakošćan Castle, the comparison of pre- and post-earthquake data indicates a decrease in the natural frequencies of the tower and the second floor, suggesting an overall reduction in stiffness. The relationship between the frequencies of the Castle’s structures and the site frequencies may indicate possible soil-structure resonance and topographic amplification effects inferred from peak proximity. In the case of the Cathedral of St James, the combined analysis of free-field and in-structure measurements highlights critical stru…

title: Assessment of teachers’ knowledge, awareness, and response to students with asthma in Greater Cairo schools
abstract: Abstract Bronchial asthma remains a significant public health challenge, especially among school-aged children. Schoolteachers are often the initial responders to asthma attacks, making their role vital for early symptom recognition and first aid provision. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the knowledge, awareness, and response of schoolteachers to students with asthma. Between March 2024 and October 2024, a self-administered questionnaire was created on Google Forms and distributed to schoolteachers through WhatsApp groups of private and public schools across different districts in Greater Cairo. The questionnaire consisted of three sections assessing: (1) teachers’ experience and demographics, (2) basic knowledge of asthma, and (3) knowledge related to first aid response in an asthma attack. A total of 634 schoolteachers participated in the study. Of these, 361 (57%) reported having previously taught students with bronchial asthma, whereas only 176 (27.8%) had witnessed a student having an acute asthma attack before. A majority of participants (445/634, 70.2%) correctly identified the short-acting beta agonist (SABA) inhaler or nebulizer as appropriate first aid for an acute asthma attack. However, only 187/634 (29.5%) reported knowing the correct technique for using SABA inhalers or nebulizers during an asthma attack. More than half of the participants, 362/634 (57.1%)…

title: Combined heat and salinity stress accelerates oxidative injury and ABA-mediated stress response in cucumber seedlings
abstract: Introduction Cucumber is a heat- and salt-stress-sensitive vegetable crop, whose productivity and marketability are endangered by increasing temperatures and soil salinization driven by climate change. Combined stresses are becoming frequent, yet their interactive effects remain poorly understood. Methodology The current study evaluated the negative impacts of high temperature (HT, 40 °C) and salinity (75 and 150 mM NaCl) alone and in combination on cucumber seedlings, under a triplicated completely randomized design. Standard plant growth parameters, micro- and macronutrients, phytohormones, photosynthetic pigment concentrations, oxidative stress biomarkers, osmo-protectants, and antioxidant enzymes were recorded. Results Combined HT and 150 mM salt stress caused greater damage to photosynthetic pigments (49-68%), and >98% reduction in growth-promoting hormones, resulting in reduced plant growth (67-93%). Combined stress drastically depleted essential nutrients (94-99.6%) despite lower Na + and Cl - ion concentrations compared to 150 mM NaCl stress alone. Reduced plant growth under combined heat–salinity stress was associated with pronounced disturbances in mineral nutrition and ion homeostasis, although the relative contributions of nutrient imbalance and ionic toxicity could not be distinguished based on tissue mineral concentrations alone. title: Cholinergic input origins and current response properties in rat interstitial nucleus of Cajal neurons
abstract: The interstitial nucleus of Cajal (INC) and the prepositus hypoglossi nucleus (PHN) function as the neural integrators for vertical and horizontal gaze holding, respectively. Previous studies have suggested that cholinergic inputs from the mesopontine tegmentum modulate the function of the horizontal integrator; however, the modulation properties and origins of cholinergic inputs in the vertical integrator remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the cholinergic responses of INC neurons and the anatomical origin of the cholinergic inputs in rats. Whole-cell recordings in brainstem slices revealed that local application of acetylcholine (ACh) induced inward currents in INC neurons mediated by both nicotinic and muscarinic ACh receptors (nAChRs and mAChRs). Although current responses were predominantly mediated by nAChRs in PHN neurons, the participation of nAChRs and mAChRs differed depending on the INC neuron type. Retrograde tracing using an adeno-associated virus (AAV) in choline acetyltransferase (ChAT)-tdTomato transgenic rats demonstrated that the primary origin of cholinergic inputs to the INC was the caudal magnocellular region of the medial vestibular nucleus (MVeMC). Furthermore, the primary cholinergic inputs to the PHN originated from both the caudal MVeMC and the caudal PHN itself. These results indicate that the vertical neural integrator shares a common chol…

title: Pathological complete response and long-term outcomes after neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer: a multicenter retrospective cohort study with exploratory subtype analyses
abstract: Background To examine differences in pathological complete response (pCR) rates across immunohistochemistry (IHC)-defined breast cancer surrogate subtypes and the association of pCR with recurrence-free survival (RFS) and breast cancer-specific survival (BCSS). Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 3,803 patients from the Shanghai Jiao Tong University Breast Cancer Database who received neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery. Total pCR was defined as ypT0/is ypN0. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression assessed factors associated with pCR and its association with survival, respectively. Exploratory global subtype-by-pCR interaction tests were restricted to the remaining four subtypes with estimable within-subtype pCR contrasts. Sensitivity analyses included exploratory covariate-balancing analyses based on propensity score matching and overlap weighting, calendar-year adjustment, and subtype-stratified Cox models. Results Overall, 908 patients achieved pCR (23.88%), with rates differing across IHC-defined surrogate subtypes (P < 0.001). During a median follow-up of 46 months, pCR was associated with favorable RFS (adjusted HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.24–0.57) and BCSS (adjusted HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.18–0.50; both P < 0.001). title: Liposomal bupivacaine utilization in the pain management of postoperative selective dorsal rhizotomy patients
abstract: OBJECTIVE Selective dorsal rhizotomy (SDR) is a procedure commonly utilized to treat spasticity in children with cerebral palsy. Limited studies have evaluated postoperative pain management with the objective of opiate dosage reduction. This retrospective cohort study examined the role of liposomal bupivacaine (LB) in postoperative pain management and the outcomes of SDR patients. METHODS This retrospective study used the Pediatric Movement Disorders Center’s prospective database to query electronic medical records for demographic, surgical, and postoperative data for all patients who underwent SDR from 2023 through 2025. Patients were divided into two groups: those treated with 0.25% bupivacaine HCl (comparison group) or a mixture of LB and bupivacaine HCl (LB group). Both modalities were administered via local infusion during closure of the SDR incision. All patients also received our previously developed protocol that includes infusion of dexmedetomidine during SDR surgery combined with perioperative gabapentin and scheduled acetaminophen and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs postoperatively, henceforth referred to as the dexmedetomidine infusion (INF) protocol. RESULTS Operative duration, postoperative opioid and nonopioid medication administration, and therapy notes were collected for 41 patients. Patients who underwent SDR between May 2023 and July 2024 received our IN…

title: Analyzing the role of business digitization interface in the humanitarian services supply chain for community well-being
abstract: Purpose This study aims to reduce the hurdles in the humanitarian services supply chain (HSSC) deliverance with digitization. This will help reduce the communication and execution gap between the participating organization, suppliers and ground-level welfare service vendors. Design/methodology/approach The hybrid Plan-Do-Check-Act–fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution approach was adapted to strategize, address and prioritize the key strategic benefits (KSBs) of using business digitization interface (BDIs) with an interactive dashboard for data visualization and efficient monitoring. Findings The HSSCs typically depend on the availability of funds, procurement of relief materials, allocation of projects, engagement of service vendors and project execution. A unique approach was adapted to visualize the HSSC using BDIs to reduce inefficiencies in conventional tender-based welfare systems and international aid for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3, SDG7 and SDG11. Research limitations/implications The study reflects the use of data visualization in non-profit community development activities with the Technology–Organization–Environment–Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology approach. This replaces the old conventional methods of favored/non-transparent tender allotments. Non-profit organizations often lack access to funds to implement…

title: Hydrogeochemical Characterization and Geothermometric Assessment of the Gunung Kapur Geothermal System and Surrounding Thermal Waters, Jambi, Indonesia
abstract: The Gunung Kapur area in Jambi is part of a geothermal region characterized by volcanic, plutonic, and hydrothermal alteration features. This study evaluates the hydrogeochemical characteristics, fluid types, equilibrium conditions, and inferred reservoir temperatures of the Gunung Kapur geothermal system and surrounding thermal waters using pH, major-ion chemistry, Cl–SO₄–HCO₃ classification, silica and cation geothermometers, and the Na–K–Mg geoindicator. The dataset includes thermal waters from Idung Mancung, Sapan Melolong, Semurup 1, and Semurup 2, together with Kerinci cold water as a reference. The hydrochemical data indicate contrasting fluid characteristics. Idung Mancung is strongly acidic and sulfate-rich, consistent with shallow steam-heated water, whereas Sapan Melolong and Semurup 1 exhibit chloride-bearing characteristics and lower Mg concentrations, suggesting greater interaction with deeper geothermal fluids. Semurup 2 shows a more mixed and immature signature, while Kerinci cold water is dominated by bicarbonate and represents a shallow meteoric or peripheral component. Geothermometric estimates vary according to fluid maturity and water type. title: Integration of Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) and Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) In Fleet Traffic Accident Risk Analysis At PT Semen Indonesia Logistik
abstract: Traffic accidents involving distribution fleets are a safety concern that can be influenced by human factors, environmental conditions, supervision, and organizational factors. This study aims to identify the factors contributing to traffic accidents and determine risk priorities as a basis for developing recommendations to improve fleet safety at PT Semen Indonesia Logistik. The methods used are the Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) and Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA). HFACS is used to classify factors contributing to accidents, while FMEA is used to prioritize risks based on the Risk Priority Number (RPN). The integration of these methods enables the study not only to identify accident causation factors but also to determine which risks require the most immediate attention. The HFACS analysis shows that Adverse Mental States is the most dominant category, with 35 occurrences (18.92%), followed by Decision Errors with 33 occurrences (17.84%) and Perceptual Errors with 28 occurrences (15.14%). Meanwhile, the FMEA results indicate that driver fatigue has the highest RPN of 504, followed by failure to maintain a safe following distance with an RPN of 378 and failure to detect objects in blind spots with an RPN of 324. Based on these findings, the recommended improvements include implementing fatigue management, regulating working hours and rest per…

title: The management of patients with positive non-tuberculous mycobacterium cultures at a local centre in New Zealand—a retrospective study
abstract: aim: We aimed to assess whether management of patients with positive non-tuberculous mycobacterium (NTM) cultures at Palmerston North Hospital aligns with international guidelines. method: We conducted a retrospective study of adult patients with positive mycobacterial cultures between 1 December 2020 and 1 December 2022 in the MidCentral Region. Electronic records were reviewed for microbiological sampling, radiological assessment, treatment decisions, monitoring and outcomes. Management was compared with the 2017 British Thoracic Society and 2020 American Thoracic Society/Infectious Diseases Society of America guidelines. results: Fifty-four adult patients were included. Thirty-two (59%) met microbiological criteria for NTM pulmonary disease, and 22 (41%) met full diagnostic criteria. Fifty (93%) had at least two sputum samples sent, with 43 (80%) of these sent on separate days. The median number of days from sputum positivity to computed tomography (CT) was 63 days. Of those that met diagnostic criteria, 13 patients were offered treatment, 11 commenced therapy and five achieved culture conversion. Ten patients discontinued therapy. Reasons for treatment cessation were multifactorial and included persistent culture positivity, medication intolerance, medication interactions and radiographic improvement. Surveillance sputum monitoring during treatment was documented in 64% of …

title: The Influence of Digital Systems on Public Asset Management Practices in Tanzania: A Case of Selected Public Higher Learning Institutions
abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies and systems has fundamentally reshaped how public sector organizations operate and deliver services, although the influence of digital systems on public asset management practice is yet to be explored. The study assessed the influence of digital systems on public asset management practice in selected public higher learning institutions such as the College of Business Education and Dar es Salaam Institute of Technology. Specifically, it examined the influence of e-procurement system on public asset management practice. The study adopted a pragmatist research philosophy and a mixed methods approach, operationalized through a convergent mixed methods design. A sample size of 63 respondents was selected using purposive (10) and random sampling techniques (53). Respondents were administered with questionnaires and in-depth interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data were analysed using content analysis. The results reveal that e-procurement systems positively influence public asset management practice in Tanzanian higher learning institutions. This positive influence heavily dependents on overcoming significant infrastructure, capacity and system reliability challenges. title: Waste management efficiency in Europe: evidence from low-efficiency countries
abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate the dynamic efficiency of municipal waste management systems across 28 European countries during the period 2010–2022 and to identify the structural determinants of efficiency differences to support evidence-based environmental policy and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach The study employs DEA Window analysis (CCR framework) to assess the dynamic efficiency of municipal waste-management systems across 28 European countries during 2010–2022. The evaluation is based on one input and four output indicators derived from the European Circular Economy Monitoring Framework. Additional BCC sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulations are conducted to assess the robustness of the efficiency rankings. In the second stage, a panel fractional logit model is used to identify the structural determinants of efficiency in a group of structurally comparable low-efficiency countries. Findings The results reveal pronounced and persistent cross-country disparities in waste management efficiency across Europe. Countries with stronger institutional and infrastructural capacity consistently operate closer to the efficiency frontier, whereas structurally constrained countries exhibit persistent inefficiencies, particularly in recycling and material recovery. Although gradual improvements are observed over time, the convergence toward best-practice ben…

title: A Stability-Preserving Staggered Finite Difference Approximation for a Hybrid Wave System with Conditional Exponential Stability
abstract: We analyze a staggered finite difference approximation for a hybrid PDE-ODE transmission system consisting of two one-dimensional wave equations coupled through a dynamic interior mass. The continuous model is considered in an interface-damped regime in which the right boundary is conservative and the only dissipation acts through the transmission condition. In this regime, exponential stability is conditional and is governed by an arithmetic nonresonance condition on the geometry and physical coefficients. The main question addressed in this paper is whether this conditional stability mechanism is preserved at the semi-discrete level. We construct a finite difference scheme adapted to the dynamic transmission law and prove that it preserves the discrete energy dissipation identity. We then derive a mesh-dependent spectral nonresonance condition characterizing the absence of purely imaginary eigenvalues of the semi-discrete generator. For each fixed mesh, this condition yields exponential stability of the semi-discrete semigroup. Our main result concerns the decay rate under mesh refinement: it shows that, when the travel-time ratio of the two strings is a rational number satisfying the arithmetic condition and the meshes are matched so that the numerical travel time per cell is the same on both strings, the semi-discrete generators satisfy a mesh-uniform resolvent estimate on …

title: Construction of Halogen-/Phosphorus-Free and Carbon/Metal-Based Flame-Retardant System for Silicone Rubber
abstract: Abstract Aiming at extending its functional application, the critical environmental and efficiency issue of flame-retardant silicone rubber (SR) must be urgently addressed. Except for replacing the toxic/contaminated halogen-/phosphorus-containing compounds, the reduction of the loading filler became an effective strategy in improving the flame-retardant efficiency of SR. Inspired by the native charring ability of transition-metal elements, a carbon/metal-based flame-retardant system was fabricated by combining hydrophobic zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (H-ZIF-8) and expandable graphite (EG). This combination was conducive to avoiding the adverse effects of halogen- and phosphorus-containing flame retardants on environmental pollution and personal safety. Compared with the single component, when a mixture of H-ZIF-8/EG (mass ratio: 3:8) was introduced at a total loading of 11 phr, a limiting oxygen index (LOI) of 43.1% and a UL-94 V-0 rating were achieved for SR composites. Additionally, both the peak heat release rate (PHRR) and total heat rate (THR) of SR composites were reduced by 25.8% and 35.9%, highlighting the enhanced fire safety via good charring ability and a heat barrier effect. Despite the improved flame retardancy, the flame-retardant durability of SR composites was maintained when exposed to harsh environments (acid solution, alkali solution, hot water, and seaw…

title: Educational Management and Entrepreneurship at Pesantren Property in Indonesia (Contemporary Living Hadith Epistemology Study)
abstract: Pesantren (Islamic Boarding School) increasingly combine religious education with entrepreneurship, but studies of their management seldom ask which sources of knowledge shape managerial decisions, and living hadith research has mostly examined ritual and community practice. This article analyzes how the managerial functions of Pesantren Property, a pesantren in Sentolo, Kulonprogo, Yogyakarta, that teaches property entrepreneurship, are grounded in the living hadith framework. It uses a qualitative single-case design. Data came from semi-structured interviews with six informants (the founder, an operations director, two deputy directors, a senior lecturer, and an alumnus), non-participant observation from January to March 2025, and institutional documents. The study used inductive thematic analysis, supported by source and method triangulation, member checking, and an audit trail. The findings show that planning, organizing, actuating, and controlling each rest on a distinct cluster of prophetic traditions that are practiced, not only quoted. Planning begins with the question of benefit to others and with the balance (tawazun) of worldly and religious aims. Organizing follows amanah (trust), shura (consultation), and itqan (professional excellence). Actuating builds motivation on meaning, ongoing charity, and social responsibility. Controlling operates through weekly muhasabah…

title: Education Management in Islamic-Based Holistic Learning Challenges for Madrasa
abstract: This study explores the development and implementation of Islamic‑based holistic learning management in madrasas, focusing on Jambi Province. Its purpose is to examine how Islamic education can integrate academic achievement with moral and spiritual values, preparing students to face global challenges while preserving their Islamic identity. Using a qualitative case study approach, data were collected through interviews, classroom observations, and curriculum analysis, with triangulation applied to ensure validity. Findings reveal the need for curriculum reform that balances intellectual growth with character and spiritual development. However, challenges include limited infrastructure and resistance to change among educators. The study recommends investment in modern technology, continuous teacher training, and collaboration with local communities and international institutions to bridge resource gaps. Its originality lies in offering a comprehensive model of holistic Islamic learning management tailored to Jambi’s private madrasas. The contribution of this research is providing a framework that integrates Islamic principles with contemporary educational demands, ensuring relevance and quality in today’s globalized era

title: Case Report: Diagnostic pitfalls and individualized surgical management of borderline and malignant phyllodes tumors: a three-case series
abstract: Phyllodes tumors (PTs) can overlap with fibroadenomas clinically and radiologically, and incomplete preoperative characterization can alter surgical planning. We describe three women with borderline or malignant PTs who declined preoperative core needle biopsy; clinical underestimation of malignancy also contributed to proceeding directly to excision. Case 1, a 36-year-old woman with long-standing bilateral masses, had a 63-mm malignant PT with heterologous chondroid and osseous differentiation and osteoclast-like giant cells; two contralateral lesions were fibroadenomas. An involved margin prompted re-excision, with no residual tumor and a final closest histological margin of 20 mm, permitting breast conservation. Case 2, a 68-year-old woman with a 75-mm malignant PT, had mildly prominent ipsilateral axillary nodes on mammography but no abnormal enlargement on axillary ultrasonography. Following malignant PT interpretation on frozen section, wide local excision was converted to total mastectomy; sentinel lymph node biopsy was negative (0/3), and the closest margin was the deep margin at 20 mm. The patient declined postoperative radiotherapy. Case 3, a 53-year-old woman with previous right breast fibroadenoma excision, had a right borderline PT involving the inked margin and contralateral pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia. Re-excision approximately 2 cm beyond the previous …

title: Resilience in the face of disruption: how supply chain innovation drives operational performance in a resource-constrained environment
abstract: Purpose The article examines the relationship between supply chain innovation (SCI) and operational performance (OP), focusing on resilience in response to varying levels of supply chain disruptions within resource-constrained contexts. In the context of the dynamic capability theory, this study has sought to fill a very important gap in the literature on the SCI–OP relationship. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 697 manufacturing and service firms in Ghana using a two-phase survey. Data were analyzed using the Hayes conditional PROCESS analysis. Findings The results showed that supply chain resilience strongly mediates the relationship between innovation and OP. Furthermore, innovative practices perform significantly better in high-disruption contexts than in low-disruption contexts, thereby improving OP. Research limitations/implications Although the study employed a two-phase time-lagged survey design, the observational nature of the data limits strong causal inference, limiting the generalizability of the findings to other economies. Future research should adopt longitudinal designs and explore additional contextual variables to deepen understanding of how dynamic capabilities evolve and interact to influence OP in resource-constrained and unstable environments. Originality/value This study advances the dynamic capability perspective by positioning supply…
venue: The International Journal of Logistics Management

title: Configurational pathways and spatio-temporal evolution of value co-creation in smart eldercare services: a regional innovation ecosystem perspective
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how configurations of regional innovation ecosystem conditions support value co-creation in smart eldercare services, examining both configurational patterns and their spatio-temporal evolution across diverse regional contexts. Design/methodology/approach Integrating Service-Dominant Logic (SDL) with innovation ecosystem theory, the research employs Panel Qualitative Comparative Analysis (Panel-QCA) on panel data from 30 Chinese provinces spanning 2013–2023. Findings Three configurational patterns achieve high-level value co-creation: an actor-environment-resource multi-driven pattern, an actor-resource dual-driven pattern under constrained market openness, and an environment-driven pattern enabled by industry-university-research collaboration. These patterns exhibit a gradient spatial evolution from eastern multi-driven models to central dual-driven models and western environment-driven models. Temporally, they transition from holistic factor accumulation during the formation stage to core condition differentiation with peripheral condition complementarity during the expansion stage. Practical implications It provides policy insights for regions with diverse resource endowments and developmental stages to formulate differentiated smart eldercare service strategies. Originality/value This study extends SDL and innovation ecosystem theory by opera…

title: Health-system preparedness for early detection of mild cognitive impairment: primary-care evidence from a national study among general practitioners in Romania
abstract: Background Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a growing public health concern in aging populations. In Romania, adults aged 65 years and over comprise about one fifth of the population, and estimated MCI prevalence in this age group is among the highest in Europe (28.5%), yet no organised national programme for systematic early detection exists. General practitioners (GPs) are well positioned to contribute to population-level detection, but their knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding MCI have not been evaluated nationally. This study assessed these domains as primary-care indicators of health-system preparedness for early MCI detection. Methods We conducted a national cross-sectional study among GPs practicing in Romania between June 2025 and January 2026, using an online self-administered questionnaire adapted from a published knowledge, attitudes and practices instrument. Analyses included descriptive statistics, Spearman correlations, group comparisons and multiple linear regression. Results A total of 547 eligible GPs were included; 365–416 completed the questionnaire sections. The mean knowledge score was 33.20 (SD = 16.37): only 6.5% identified the Petersen diagnostic criteria, 10.8% recognized the most used cognitive screening instrument and 20.7% identified modifiable risk factors. Attitudes towards MCI detection were favorable (mean = 73.26, SD = 6.96). Nearly a…

title: Terrain-induced aerodynamic disturbances and wind sector management of a wind turbine in complex terrain: a SCADA–CFD cross-validation study at the Tetouan wind farm
Biased by sustainability? How cognitive biases shape procurement decisions under information equivocality
abstract: Purpose Climate change introduces new informational asymmetries across supply chains, increasing managers' need to process sustainability-related information in procurement decisions. Such information is equivocal, making its interpretation challenging and increasing decision-makers’ susceptibility to cognitive biases. Building on organizational information-processing theory and behavioral decision-making research, this study examines how cognitive biases shape procurement decisions involving sustainability information. Design/methodology/approach We developed hypotheses on cognitive biases emerging from three characteristics of sustainability information: structural properties (risky choice framing, attribute framing, numeracy and anchoring), inferential dynamics (halo effect) and social influences (herd effect). We tested these hypotheses through between-subject vignette-based experiments depicting individual, one-shot procurement decisions. The experiments were conducted in person with 475 participants, including managers and students. Findings We found that sustainability-oriented procurement decisions are vulnerable to cognitive biases. In particular, biases induced by the structural properties of information produced the strongest effects across both managers and students, followed by distortions emerging from inferential dynamics. In contrast, socially driven distortions…
venue: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

title: Patch Management or Public Law? A Critical Comment on the Five Eyes Guidance for the Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services
abstract: On 1 May 2026, six Five Eyes cybersecurity agencies jointly issued Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services, the first coordinated Anglophone statement on the governance of LLM-based autonomous agents. This Comment argues that, although the Guidance offers competent cybersecurity risk management within its stated remit, its institutional weight invites a broader governance reading that the document cannot bear, and that five structural limitations then come into view. First, the cybersecurity doctrines on which it relies are necessary but insufficient for agentic systems, whose delegated authority, underspecified goals, and long-horizon autonomy strain the assumptions of conventional controls. Second, it privatises systemic risk by imposing duties on deployers without specifying public-law obligations, redress, or liability across the agentic value chain. Third, it prescribes human oversight without specifying the conditions of effective control, so that responsibility risks being assigned to reviewers who lack the information, authority, or time to exercise it. Fourth, it reduces accountability to auditability, confusing a technical property with a legal relation between duty-holders and affected parties. Fifth, the security-defined mandates of its six authoring agencies, and the intelligence-oversight structures within which most of them sit, raise questions of institutional v…

title: Effects of Financial Distress, Managerial Ownership, Institutional Ownership, and Firm Size on Earnings Management
abstract: This study examines the effects of financial distress, managerial ownership, institutional ownership, and firm size on earnings management in the hotels, resorts, and cruise lines subsector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2022–2024. The research is motivated by discrepancies between operating activity and earnings growth during post-pandemic economic fluctuations, including rising profits despite declining operating revenue at PT Eastparc Hotel Tbk. A quantitative approach was employed, using purposive sampling to select 18 companies from a population of 30, yielding 54 company-year observations. Earnings management was measured using the Modified Jones Model, financial distress using the modified Altman Z-score, ownership variables using shareholding proportions, and firm size using the natural logarithm of total sales. Panel data regression was performed in EViews, with the Chow and Hausman tests supporting a fixed effects specification. The reported results indicate a positive and statistically significant coefficient for financial distress, whereas managerial ownership, institutional ownership, and firm size have no statistically significant individual effects on earnings management. The model has an adjusted R-squared of 0.530608. The study interprets the financial distress finding through the debt covenant hypothesis and highlights the limited explanatory ro…

title: Research and development of effective methods for restoring the load-bearing capacity of metal span structures, span structures damaged by missile strikes
abstract: The article considers a set of design solutions for the restoration of metal span structures of bridge structures of various structural schemes that are part of a highway bridge crossing and were damaged as a result of missile strikes. The restoration of road communication is of strategic importance, since bridge structures are key elements of the transport infrastructure of Ukraine. Their damage leads to disruption of logistical routes, especially in territories close to the combat zone. The purpose of the work is to develop effective engineering solutions for the prompt restoration of bridge structures damaged as a result of military operations and to ensure their safe operation. The study was carried out based on the results of a technical inspection of the bridge crossing, an analysis of the nature and extent of damage to metal span structures, as well as engineering development of options for their restoration. The cantilever parts of orthotropic plates of metal span structures suffered the greatest damage from missile strikes. As a result of direct hits, individual sections of the cantilevers were completely destroyed. Other elements also suffered serious damage. The span structures are in an unusable condition and require urgent restoration. To ensure safe operation, the technical condition of the structures is constantly monitored, and temporary restrictions on vehicle …

title: Baseline mucosal transcriptomic endotypes stratify healing capacity and biologic therapy outcomes in ulcerative colitis: an integrative multi-cohort study
abstract: Background Numerous baseline mucosal transcriptomic signatures have been proposed to stratify therapeutic outcomes in ulcerative colitis (UC), but cross-cohort transferability is frequently undermined by platform heterogeneity, endpoint/timepoint differences, and drug-specific biases. The resulting lack of a biologic-agnostic molecular baseline has limited clinical translation and prospective trial design. Methods We integratively re-analyzed endpoint-linked baseline mucosal transcriptomes from seven public UC GEO series (778 unique baseline samples), with three additional public accessions used for disease-activity and contextual analyses. The primary response/healing synthesis used five study slices spanning anti-TNF, anti-integrin, and etrolizumab-treated cohorts. Unsupervised decomposition identified baseline endotypes, and endotype-outcome associations were estimated within each cohort (OR per 1-SD increase) and summarized by random-effects cross-cohort pooling with heterogeneity reporting, rank/seed sensitivity analyses, endpoint-restricted summaries, and negative controls. Results Across five primary response/healing study slices, an epithelial barrier endotype (EPITHELIAL_BARRIER/NMF_C3) was associated with higher odds of response/healing (random-effects cross-cohort pooling OR = 3.171, 95% CI 1.491–6.744), whereas macrophage-inflammation and lymphoid/complement-stromal…

title: Comparison and spatial heterogeneity of eco-efficiency in two major river basins of China: nonlinear mechanism analysis based on spatial machine learning
abstract: Achieving a synergy between economic expansion and environmental conservation across major watersheds is vital for China’s sustainable trajectory. This study proposes a unified cross-basin framework, using a three-stage super-efficiency Slack-Based Measure (SE-SBM) and Global Malmquist-Luenberger (GML) index to assess the static and dynamic eco-efficiency (EE) of the Yellow River Basin (YRB) and the Yangtze River Economic Belt (YREB). For the analysis of spatiotemporal evolution, kernel density estimation (KDE) and the Dagum Gini coefficient (DGC) are implemented. A Geographically Weighted Random Forest (GWRF) model is introduced to characterize nonlinear associations and spatial heterogeneity among the factors associated with EE. Results reveal that: (1) The adjusted EE of the YRB declined, but it remained superior overall compared to the slightly rising YREB. In terms of space, the YRB shows a stepwise decline, while the YREB presents a concave shape with a lower center. (2) The technical progress (TC) is the primary contributor to GML-based EE growth in the two major river basins. The GWRF model uncovers significant nonlinear threshold effects (e.g., urbanization and environmental regulations) and U-shaped evolutionary characteristics (e.g., industrial structure and financial development). Local feature-importance patterns further indicate distinct spatial structures: a regu…

title: Advancing Precision UDP-Glycosyltransferase Engineering: A Multilevel Strategy from Mechanism to Design
abstract: Abstract Natural glycosides are widely used in food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic sectors. This is because glycosides exhibit crucially enhanced solubility, bioavailability, and application potential compared to their aglycones. This reaction is primarily catalyzed by uridine-diphosphate-dependent glycosyltransferases (UGTs). However, native UGTs are mainly limited by insufficient activity, narrow substrate scope, poor regioselectivity, and poor stability. Therefore, engineering efficient and robust UGT biocatalysts is essential to advancing the sustainable production of valuable glycosides. This review elaborates a systematic multilevel strategy for UGT engineering from discovery to precision design. It critically assesses these diverse engineering strategies and emerging trends while discussing their applicability and limitations for the development of advanced UGT biocatalysts.
venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: Timing of the anthropogenic carbon invasion in the Southern California Current
abstract: The Eastern Boundary Upwelling Systems (EBUS), such as the Southern California Current System (CCS), are well-known high-productivity regions driven by alongshore winds, although their role as oceanic sources and sinks of atmospheric CO 2 in the global carbon cycle is poorly understood. In the southern CCS, off Baja California, wind-driven vertical mixing upwells nutrient and carbon-rich waters from late winter to early summer, while weaker winds during the rest of the year allow the intrusion of nutrients and carbon-depleted subtropical surface waters. Here, we interpret the isotopic composition of organic carbon and calcitic records spanning ∼ 160 years from high-resolution sediment cores collected off Baja California, showing a clear trend toward lighter carbon isotopic compositions of the organic and inorganic carbon for the past seven decades. These trends are similar to the atmospheric records associated with the 13 C Suess effect, suggesting an atmospheric carbon invasion into the surface waters of the California Current. Nevertheless, the slope of the atmospheric carbon isotopic records is steeper than our marine record, most likely related to the upward mixing of subsurface waters with a relatively heavier carbon isotopic signature and advection processes inherent to the strong seasonality of the CCS southern boundary. These results will allow a better characterization…

title: Direct Evidence for Carbon Monoxide-to-Dioxin Conversion via Fly-Ash-Catalyzed Sequential Reactions in Incineration Flue Gas
abstract: Abstract The formation of polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs) in industrial thermal processes is traditionally attributed to solid carbon precursors via de novo synthesis. Carbon monoxide (CO), despite serving as an operational indicator of incomplete combustion, has not been directly implicated as a molecular carbon source for dioxin generation. Here, we provide definitive experimental and mechanistic evidence that CO can be catalytically converted into dioxins and dioxin-like compounds through a sequential reaction network mediated by fly ash. Using fixed-bed reactors packed with real fly ash, we isolate CO, H2O, and HCl as minimal reactants to reconstruct flue-gas chemistry. Transition metal species (Cu, Fe) in fly ash catalyze CO conversion via a coupled water–gas shift and Fischer–Tropsch-type process, generating a wide spectrum of aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbons. Concurrently, fly ash mediates HCl oxidation to active Cl2, enabling chlorination of these intermediates into chlorobenzenes and chlorophenols, which subsequently evolve into polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), polychlorinated naphthalenes (PCNs), and ultimately PCDD/Fs. Notably, Cl4–8DD/F congeners account for >90% of the formed PCDD/Fs, consistent with de novo synthesis signatures. This work establishes a new mechanistic paradigm for dioxin generation and highlights CO emission co…

title: Making blue carbon governable in China: standardisation, local experimentation and policy implications
Cooperative Dual-Template Assembly of Bimodal Interconnected Mesoporous Carbon Nanospheres with Boosted Charge Transport
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous materials have attracted great research attention since their first advent in 1990s; however, the self-assembly of soft micelles can generate only unary periodicity. A feasible strategy capable of building multinary pore structures remains scarcely explored due to huge synthetic difficulty. Herein, we explore a cooperative dual-template assembly route, which allows for compatible interaction of Pluronic P123 and L64 in solution, to successfully construct a type of mesoporous carbon nanospheres with bimodal mesopores. The key to such construction of hierarchical mesopores from a pure soft-template process without recruitment of a hard template mainly relies on the formation of composite micelles with both suitable mutual interactions and individually stabilized condensed states. The resultant mesoporous carbon spheres possess good uniformity in morphology and mesoporosity, including a mean particle size at ∼200 nm, a high surface area of 537 m2 g–1, and an interconnected bimodal mesopore size centered at 11.1 and 4.2 nm along with a massive amount of micropores. Moreover, this dual-template assembly strategy allows for precise structural regulation over the pore curvature and pore size through tailoring the reaction conditions. As a proof of concept, the fabricated bimodal mesoporous carbon, as an ammonium-ion battery anode, showcases excellent electrochemica…

title: The Effect of Institutional Ownership and Sustainability Committees on Carbon Emission Disclosure with the Proportion of Female Directors as a Moderating Variable
abstract: This study examines the effects of institutional ownership and sustainability committees on carbon emission disclosure, with female director representation as a moderating variable, in energy and manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) from 2021 to 2024. Motivated by low carbon emission disclosure in Indonesia, this study draws on Stakeholder Theory and Legitimacy Theory. Using purposive sampling, 40 companies were selected, yielding 160 observations. Data were analyzed using panel data regression and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) with the Random Effects Model (REM) and clustered-robust standard errors to address heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation. The results indicate that institutional ownership and sustainability committees positively and significantly affect carbon emission disclosure. However, female director representation does not moderate either relationship. These findings suggest that numerical female representation alone may be insufficient to strengthen corporate governance in promoting carbon transparency, particularly when substantive influence in strategic decision-making is not captured by the measurement. This study contributes to carbon accounting literature by highlighting the importance of institutional ownership and sustainability committees in enhancing carbon emission disclosure. The findings offer insights for compa…
