title: Component-specific effects of black carbon on oxytetracycline adsorption by HDPE microplastics: synergistic and antagonistic interactions and site-energy analysis
abstract: Environmental context Microplastics, antibiotics and black carbon can occur together in aquatic environments, but different forms of black carbon may change where antibiotics remain. We found that solid black carbon increased oxytetracycline retention in systems containing polyethylene microplastics, whereas dissolved black carbon decreased it. Distinguishing solid and dissolved black carbon may improve assessments of antibiotic transport and exposure in contaminated waters.

title: Carbon Dioxide Flushing and Zero-Valent Iron Addition during Anaerobic Digestion: Biogas Upgrading Does Not Necessarily Indicate Enhanced Biodegradation
abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide (CO2) supplementation and zero-valent iron (ZVI) addition have been proposed as strategies for enhancing methane production during anaerobic digestion. In this study, eight semibatch anaerobic digesters (four treatments operated in duplicate) treating piggery waste were operated for 100 days to evaluate the combined effects of CO2 flushing strategy and ZVI addition on methane production, process stability, and organic matter conversion. ZVI-amended reactors achieved substantially higher methane contents, reaching up to 98% CH4 under single CO2 flushing and approximately 90% CH4 under periodic CO2 flushing. Periodic CO2 supplementation promoted sustained methane generation, resulting in the highest cumulative methane production when combined with ZVI. Preliminary experiments further showed that CO2 flushing can effectively reduce pH under alkaline conditions, whereas ZVI addition enhances hydrogen generation and counteracts excessive acidification. Despite their superior methane production and methane contents, the ZVI-amended reactors exhibited lower organic matter conversion than the corresponding reactors without ZVI. The ZVI + CO2 once-flushed reactors showed the highest residual TOC and soluble COD concentrations (approximately 2104 mg L–1 and 5129 mg L–1, respectively) due to the high pH, whereas the greatest organic matter removal was achieved in t…

title: Short-term spatial variability in intertidal primary production and respiration during the tidal cycle, and resulting carbon budgets in the Authie estuary (France)
Effect of Carbon Dioxide Absorption on the Dynamics of Polyethyleneimine under Dry Conditions
abstract: Abstract The chemical transformations associated with carbon dioxide absorption in polyethyleneimine (PEI) have been extensively characterized. However, how these transformations impact the dynamics of PEI remains poorly understood. Through a combination of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), broadband dielectric spectroscopy (BDS), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), we systematically investigate the influence of CO2 chemisorption under dry conditions at room temperature on the dynamics of PEI. PEI films containing 1.1–2.7 mmol CO2/g PEI (corresponding to [CO2]:[N] = 0.05:1 to 0.13:1) were characterized across wide time scales from ∼10–10 to 102 s, where [CO2] and [N] represent the absorbed molar numbers of CO2 and the molar numbers of amines in PEI. Spectroscopic measurements, including NMR and FT-IR, confirm ammonium carbamate formation upon CO2 sorption. Furthermore, the CO2 chemisorption induces pronounced dynamical changes, including a near-linear increase in glass transition temperature, Tg, upto 11–19 K with [CO2]:[N] = 0.05:1 to 0.13:1, and a significant broadening of the glass transition step in DSC measurements. Accordingly, BDS reveals substantial slowing down in segmental dynamics, along with the emergence of two new types of secondary relaxations associated with carbamate and ammonium ion motions. Solid-state…

title: Inflammation, Scar, or Both? Interpreting Positron Emission Tomography Patterns in Cardiac Sarcoidosis
Hierarchical Assembly of Gold Nanoclusters Mediated by Kinetic Aggregation of Amphiphilic Amino Acid for Generation of Enhanced Emission and Tunable CPL-Activity
abstract: Abstract Hierarchical assembly of coinage-metal nanoclusters constitutes an important strategy for constructing optical materials with advanced luminescent performance and chiroptical activities. However, it remains intractable to rationally design and direct the hierarchical assembly process that leads to the desired functionalities. Herein, hierarchical assemblies of 6-aza-2-thiothymine-protected gold nanoclusters (ATT-AuNCs) are constructed by coassembling with an amphiphilic amino acid (Fmoc-Arg) whose aggregates serve as reservoirs to control the assembly kinetics. In the presence of a proper amount of Fmoc-Arg higher than its critical aggregation concentration, dynamic coassembly can be observed, which gives rise to tassel-like and hydrangea-like aggregates. Thermodynamic and kinetic spectral analyses verify that the controlled release of Fmoc-Arg and subsequent association with ATT-AuNCs are involved in the hierarchical assembly mechanism. Moreover, the obtained tassel-like and hydrangea-like aggregates exhibit enhanced emission and chiroptical activity. By introducing rhodamine B to construct a FRET system, the emission color as well as CPL can be bathochromically shifted. The tunable optical properties endow ATT-AuNCs/Fmoc-Arg systems with potential applications in anticounterfeiting. The dynamic assembly of nanoclusters described herein controlled by the reservoir of …

title: Ocean carbon sequestration during glacial climates due to combined Antarctic sea ice expansion and ocean circulation change
abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth’s Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. In contrast, changes in sea ice and circulation individually result in ocean carbon dioxide outgassing. When sea ice expansion and circulation changes act together, they enhance biological carbon storage by reducing ocean-atmosphere fluxes in the Southern Ocean, without invoking external drivers of the biological pump. This reduction inhibits the outgassing of upwelled remineralized carbon and promotes its resubduction into the abyss. Together, these results reveal a reinforcing feedback linking atmospheric cooling, Antarctic sea ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes to enhanced biological carbon storage and atmospheric carbon dioxide drawdown.
venue_publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science

title: Radical–Electrochemical Coupling Enables Amination of Methane
abstract: Abstract The selective functionalization of methane under ambient conditions is widely regarded as a holy grail in chemistry, yet remains fundamentally limited not only by the inertness of the C–H bond but also by the transient nature of highly reactive intermediates. Short-lived species are often difficult to preserve and utilize prior to productive coupling, constraining accessible reaction pathways and product selectivity. Here, we establish a reaction framework based on in situ interfacial interception of reactive radicals, enabling the temporal coordination between radical lifetime and subsequent reaction processes. Plasma generates short-lived methyl radicals in immediate proximity to a gas–electrode interface, allowing their direct delivery and capture at the catalytic surface, while the electrochemical interface independently converts ammonia into surface-bound amino intermediates. Their coupling enables selective C–N bond formation. This spatially and temporally coordinated process allows highly reactive radical species to be synchronized with interfacial reaction steps, facilitating their productive utilization. Guided by density functional theory, we identify a nickel–cobalt layered double hydroxide catalyst that promotes interfacial coupling between *CH3 and *NH2 intermediates. The optimized system achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 54% for methylamine at 10 mA cm–2,…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: HFIP-Promoted Bis-Phosphorylation via Dual C–P Coupling of Unprotected sec -Propargylic Alcohols and Phosphites: Access to Substituted (Prop-2-ene-1,2-diyl)( E )-Bisphosphonates
abstract: Abstract A first HFIP-promoted, direct coupling of unprotected secondary propargyl alcohols and phosphites has been developed, providing efficient access to substituted (prop-2-ene-1,2-diyl)(E)-bisphosphonates through the concurrent formation of P–C(sp2) and P–C(sp3) bonds. This transition-metal-free reaction proceeds rapidly at room temperature, featuring operational simplicity and scalability to gram quantities. Moreover, HFIP was recycled for further use by distillation, which makes this protocol a greener and more sustainable choice.

title: Ripples in Two-Dimensional Supports Direct Charge–Curvature Coupling in Donor–Acceptor Interfacial Chemistry
abstract: Abstract Ripples, wrinkles, and bubbles are common out-of-plane distortion motifs in deformable two-dimensional (2D) materials. By reshaping electronic structure, these distortions introduce a design dimension for functional materials under external bias. Here, we establish the relationship between out-of-plane-distortion-induced curvature and external-bias-induced charge and show that variable curvature can generate chemically distinct donor–acceptor interfacial chemistry on a single surface. Using corrugated graphene-supported M–N4 single-atom sites, representative of transition-metal–nitrogen–carbon (M–N–C) materials used in heterogeneous and electrochemical catalysis, we examine how negative curvature (mountain) and positive curvature (valley) regions respond to electron- and hole-rich conditions relevant to external bias. We identify a metal-dependent charge–curvature relationship in which donor and acceptor binding exhibit complementary mountain–valley asymmetry, arising from the interplay between localized and delocalized electronic states. The same asymmetry extends to coadsorption, where donor and acceptor species preferentially occupy complementary curvature regions of the shared corrugated support, resulting in long-range charge redistribution across the coupled donor–support–acceptor interface. Overall, these results establish ripples as chemically active motifs for…
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C

title: On Ammonia-Blended Coke Oven Gas (COG) in Coaxial-Flow Nonpremixed Flame for Decarbonization
abstract: Abstract Coke oven gas (COG) is a promising byproduct gas generated in steelmaking processes because of its high heating value and large production volume. The large amount of hydrogen in COG contributes to combustion reactivity, flame stability, and decarbonization. Recently, a strategy for recycling COG cofired with other fuels has been proposed to support continued utilization. Ammonia is an attractive carbon-free fuel, a suitable candidate for cofiring with COG. In this study, the combustion and emission characteristics of ammonia-blended COG were investigated using a coaxial-flow nonpremixed combustor. Experiments evaluated the flame length, blow-off limit, and OH radical and NOx emissions. 2D simulation using ANSYS Fluent analyzed flame temperature and NO mole fraction. As a result, it was found that the flame length decreased with increasing ammonia blending ratio because of the reduced heat release rate and fuel reactivity. The normalized correlation based on Roper’s equation accurately predicts the flame length of COG, implying that COG can subsequently be interpreted as a general-purpose fuel. In addition, despite decreased blow-off limit of the ammonia-blended COG, it still maintained a significantly higher stability limit than methane due to the high hydrogen content of COG. OH-PLIF measurements revealed that the flame structure and reaction intensity were only slig…

title: Architectural and structural solutions for the integration of photovoltaic systems into buildings considering energy efficiency and insolation conditions
abstract: Post-war reconstruction and the decentralization of Ukraine’s energy system necessitate the large-scale implementation of photovoltaic (PV) systems in residential, public, and industrial buildings. However, solar panels are often mounted on completed buildings as add-on equipment without regard to architectural composition, structural compatibility, or insolation conditions, which reduces energy performance, degrades the visual quality of the environment, and creates additional structural risks. Integrating photovoltaic elements directly into building envelopes (roof, facade, glazing) requires a systematic architectural and structural approach aligned with current building codes and local climatic conditions. The research objective is to develop methodological principles for selecting architectural and structural solutions for integrating photovoltaic systems into buildings, taking into account energy efficiency indicators and the insolation conditions of Ukraine’s territory. A systematic and comparative analysis of domestic and international experience in the architectural integration of building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) was applied, together with a multifactor assessment of insolation conditions, modelling of the influence of orientation and tilt angle of building envelopes on energy output, and expert evaluation of the structural compatibility of photovoltaic elements…

title: Хараа-хөдөлгөөний интеграци ба суралцахуйд тулгарч буй бэрхшээл хоорондын хамаарал (Бага ангийн ялгаатай хэрэгцээтэй суралцагчдынжишээн дээр)
abstract: It is essential to identify students’ diverse needs and provide timely, appropriate support. Visual–motor integration plays an important role in children’s learning, and weaknesses in this ability may contribute to learning difficulties. This study examined visual–motor integration among primary school students with diverse needs in relation to cognitive indicators and emotional states. For a small number of students, the findings were also compared with information from parents, caregivers, and teachers using an ICF-based questionnaire.Recall drawing performance was significantly and positively associated with attention and short-term visual memory, suggesting the importance of attending to, retaining, and recalling visual information. In contrast, copy drawing performance was not significantly associated with these cognitive indicators. Recall drawing performance also differed according to emotional state. Parent and teacher observations were consistent with children’s cognitive assessment results on some indicators but differed on others. These findings highlight the importance of using multiple sources of information, rather than a single assessment, to identify children’s learning needs.

title: Local Wisdom Integration and Community-Based Environmental Conservation in Bali Starling Conservation for The Development of Tengkudak Tourism Village
abstract: The development of tourism villages is no longer solely oriented toward increasing tourist arrivals but is also expected to maintain environmental sustainability, strengthen local identity, and provide tangible benefits to local communities. Tengkudak Village, Penebel District, Tabanan Regency, Bali, possesses unique potential through the presence of the Bali Starling (Leucopsar rothschildi), agricultural landscapes, rural community life, culture, and local wisdom that has developed within the community's social life. The existence of Kampoeng Jalak Bali in Tingkihkerep Hamlet represents an important asset for developing conservation-based tourism while strengthening the position of Tengkudak Village as a tourism village with distinct ecological and cultural characteristics. This study aims to analyze forms of local wisdom that support environmental conservation, identify the roles and participation of the community in Bali Starling conservation, and formulate an integration of community-based conservation with tourism village development. The research employs a descriptive qualitative approach using a case study method. Data are obtained through observation, in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, documentation, and literature reviews involving village stakeholders, traditional village institutions, Pokdarwis, conservation groups, farmers, MSME actors, youth, women's gro…

title: Digital transformation in work integration social enterprises: institutional pressures, dynamic capabilities and divergent trajectories
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how institutional pressures and organisational capabilities jointly shape digital transformation (DT) trajectories in work integration social enterprises (WISEs). While digitalisation promises efficiency gains and expanded social impact, it may also deepen digital exclusion and trigger mission drift in organisations designed to support vulnerable workers. Design/methodology/approach This study integrates institutional theory and the resource-based view (RBV) to analyse how external legitimacy pressures and internal dynamic capabilities influence DT processes in WISEs. Empirically, this study draws on five national focus groups and one transnational focus group involving 35 managers and practitioners across Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain and Romania. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings The findings reveal three distinct DT trajectories in WISEs: proactive transformation, where strong dynamic capabilities enable strategic and inclusive innovation; adaptive alignment, where moderate capabilities support gradual integration of digital tools while preserving organisational mission; and symbolic compliance, where limited capabilities result in superficial or project-driven digital adoption aimed primarily at maintaining legitimacy. This study demonstrates that DT in hybrid organisations is not a linear technological proce…

title: From E20 Ambition to Sustainable Implementation: Prospects, Structural Challenges and Strategic Pathways for Sugarcane-Based Bioethanol Development in Indonesia
abstract: Indonesia's ambition to introduce gasoline containing 20% bioethanol (E20) by approximately 2028 represents an important opportunity to diversify transportation fuels, strengthen domestic energy security, and accelerate agricultural industrialisation. Nevertheless, the feasibility and sustainability of this initiative depend on interconnected agricultural, technological, economic, environmental, and institutional conditions. This article critically examines the prospects and challenges of E20 implementation through a qualitative literature review of contemporary scientific publications from 2020–2026, supplemented by Indonesian policy documents. The analysis integrates energy-transition theory, sustainable bioeconomy perspectives, supply-chain management, lifecycle assessment, and institutional governance. Eight thematic dimensions are identified: energy security, feedstock availability, industrial readiness, automotive compatibility, economic viability, environmental sustainability, social inclusion, and policy coordination. The synthesis suggests that sugarcane-based ethanol could support gasoline substitution and rural value creation, but extensive feedstock requirements, competition with food production, industrial financing, land-use impacts, water consumption, and vehicle compatibility present substantial implementation challenges. International experience demonstrates th…
venue: Journal of Environmental Sustainability and Renewable Systems

title: Education in the era of artificial intelligence from a cross-border perspective regarding student perceptions, meta-competences and institutional integration
abstract: Purpose The accelerated transformations of the digital economy require a profound rethinking of higher education, especially in terms of preparing human capital for a future shaped by artificial intelligence (AI). The use of AI is no longer a peripheral technological option. Still, it has become a central vector in defining the skills required in the labour market, streamlining educational processes, and reshaping the relationship between learning and performance. Design/methodology/approach This paper aims to analyse, from a cross-border perspective, how AI is integrated into higher education in Romania, the Republic of Moldova and Ukraine. The investigation examines the relationships among available educational resources, AI use, AI-related skills, meta-competencies, self-reported perceived academic performance and career intentions in an emerging digital context. Findings The study uses a convergent mixed-methods design, combining survey data from 678 students with 76 semi-structured interviews with university teachers. The findings show that AI adoption is shaped by the interaction between institutional resources, actual use, AI-related skills, meta-competencies and national context. Students from Romania and the Republic of Moldova reported more frequent and varied AI use than students from Ukraine, while the Ukrainian profile reflected a more cautious pattern shaped by ri…

title: A narrative review of the decade-long integration of professional postgraduate education with standardized residency training in China
abstract: Since 2014, China has comprehensively implemented the Standardized Residency Training (SRT) program nationwide, and the integration of professional postgraduate education with SRT has operated for over a decade. This narrative review, based on searches of Wanfang Data and PubMed from January 2015 to December 2025, examines the achievements, persistent challenges, and reform options of this integration system. While the system has shortened medical training from six to three years and enriched clinical exposure, a fundamental structural contradiction persists: the dual identity of professional postgraduates as both “students” and “residents” creates an inherent conflict between clinical practice and academic training. Within the fixed three-year period, postgraduates bear the combined burden of 33 months of clinical rotations, coursework, and thesis research, leaving insufficient protected time for scientific research, compounded by misaligned training objectives, welfare inequity, delayed licensure, and elevated mental health burdens. Enrollment expansion has further strained training capacity and produced crowding-out effects on the broader medical talent pipeline. Implementation-level adjustments can partially alleviate these issues but cannot resolve the core contradiction. Reform should prioritize addressing the dual-identity tension through either flexible decoupling or co…

title: A High-Brightness, Low-Energy-Spread Au Needle Point Electron Source Nanocold-Cathode Adapted to Low-Power Photoelectric Coexcitation
abstract: Abstract To address the requirements of vacuum electronic and optoelectronic device applications for next-generation low-power-consumption, high-brightness, low-energy-spread, and tunable electron sources, the pursuit of high-efficiency metal nanocold-cathodes with plasmon-enhanced properties in specific waveband emerges as one of potent solutions. In this study, by screening and comparing the cathode materials and structures, we propose a high-brightness, low-energy-spread Au needle nanocold-cathode point electron source adapted to low-intensity photoelectric coexcitation. The experimental results demonstrate sensitivity to excitation light and outstanding electron emission performance of this point electron source: under the coexcitation of an electrostatic field below ∼1.25 V μm–1 and a supercontinuum-spectrum laser with average intensity of ∼24 W cm–2, the source achieved an emission current of 130 nA, improving by one order of magnitude when compared to the field emission current (∼13 nA) under pure electrostatic field excitation. As the laser excitation intensity increased, its effective work function decreased from 5.1 to 2.7 eV, resulting in a significant reduction of the excitation threshold for electron emission. Benefiting from the plasmon-enhanced light-harvesting effect, the cathode exhibits high sensitivity and selectivity to the wavelength and polarization of the…

title: A systems-level energetic framework for conscious processing: energetic organization as a constraint on large-scale neural integration
abstract: Conscious processing is associated with coordinated interactions among distributed neural systems, yet the biological constraints that enable and sustain large-scale neural integration remain incompletely understood. Contemporary theories emphasize computational, informational, and network mechanisms, while the potential contribution of systems-level energetic organization has received comparatively less explicit theoretical attention. This Hypothesis & Theory article proposes that systems-level energetic organization may represent an additional biological constraint influencing the neural conditions under which large-scale neural integration associated with conscious processing can emerge and be sustained. Systems-level energetic organization is defined as the dynamic coordination of energy production, distribution, allocation, and utilization across interacting neural systems. The framework integrates established principles of brain energetics, metabolic regulation, and distributed neural organization, while the proposed relationship between their systems-level coordination and conscious neural integration remains hypothetical. It is intended to complement rather than replace existing theories of consciousness and does not propose that energy generates consciousness, determines conscious content, or explains subjective experience. The framework generates experimentally te…

title: Digital-real industrial technology integration, knowledge interfaces, and firms’ export sophistication
abstract: Purpose Manufacturing export upgrading is shifting from scale expansion to a quality-driven stage centered on complex knowledge recombination and the improvement of product technical content. This paper aims to explore whether digital-real industrial technology integration enables firms to access more sophisticated export portfolios, with a view to understanding how the digital economy supports high-quality foreign trade. Design/methodology/approach This paper measures digital-real industrial technology integration using the co-occurrence of digital technology knowledge and industrial technology knowledge within firm patents and examines its effect on firms’ export sophistication. Findings Digital-real industrial technology integration raises firms’ export sophistication. Digital-real industrial technology integration improves export sophistication by promoting external knowledge transactions, strengthening internal digital knowledge stock and facilitating cross-domain knowledge recombination. The effect is more pronounced for state-owned firms, less financially constrained firms, high-tech firms and firms with stronger export bases. Originality/value From the perspective of knowledge integration, this paper shifts the research focus on digitalization and export upgrading toward the impact of the integration of firms’ internal digital technology knowledge and industrial technol…

title: Water-Locking and Its Release Effects in Argillaceous Silt Hydrate-Bearing Sediments by NMR Technology
abstract: Abstract During natural gas hydrate production in the Shenhu area of the South China Sea, water released from hydrate dissociation coupled with formation water, may induce water-locking, which blocks gas flow pathways and restricts productivity. To elucidate the mechanisms and potential remediation strategies, this study employed low-field NMR to systematically investigate the spatiotemporal evolution of water-locking in argillaceous silt hydrate reservoirs at initial water saturations of 50%, 70%, 90%, and 100%, and evaluated three antiwaterblocking agents (fluorocarbon types I and II, and nonionic surfactant III). Results show that water-locking predominantly occurs in micropores (T2 < 10 ms, pore size < 1 μm), with intensity increasing exponentially with saturation through four stages (end-face, mid-end combined, wide-area, and full-domain water-locking) identifying 70% saturation as the critical range for the tested material. Agents I and II perform effectively at low to moderate saturations, but their efficacy is severely limited at saturations ≥90% and under fully saturated conditions. Displacement pressure synergistically enhances agent performance, yet pressure alone is insufficient. This study clarifies the evolution mechanisms and application boundaries of chemical remediation, offering theoretical guidance for water-locking prevention and efficient hydrate deve…

title: A conceptual co-design framework for structuring bankable climate interventions: design and illustrative instantiation
abstract: Urban and regional authorities across Europe must design climate-resilient interventions under constrained budgets, while coordinating more closely with private investors and insurance companies. Participatory governance, multi-criteria decision analysis and climate-investment planning are rarely combined in a single, transparent workflow. This is mainly because cities lack conceptual frameworks linking these elements across policy, technical design and finance. Here we report how the Horizon Europe BLOSSOM project used a design science research methodology in which an ArchiMate-based enterprise-architecture framework, structured around the analytic hierarchy process, developed the Co-design Framework for Bankable Climate Interventions (CFBCI), proposed as a reference architecture for participatory co-design of climate-resilient interventions. CFBCI is illustrated through a single instantiation in the River Cole urban-reforestation intervention in Birmingham, United Kingdom, one of seven BLOSSOM pilot sites across Europe; this instantiation demonstrates the framework’s structure and is not presented as a validated case. Representational completeness was examined through the Bunge–Wand–Weber ontological model and a co-creation session with BLOSSOM stakeholders. This formative evaluation, rather than a test of bankability or decision effectiveness, revealed three incompleteness g…

title: Comprehensive immunoinformatics analysis and chimeric multi-epitope vaccine design targeting VP1 capsid protein of poliovirus type 3
Hansen Solubility-Guided Design Optimization of Biopolymer–Drug Compatibility for Photodynamically Antimicrobial Biomaterials
abstract: Abstract Designing polymeric nanocarriers for hydrophobic therapeutics requires an understanding of polymer–drug interactions and their dependence on polymer molecular weight. Herein, poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) oligomers (αPBS) with tunable molecular weights were prepared via controlled microwave-assisted alcoholysis to investigate the relationships among molecular weight, solubility behavior, and curcumin encapsulation. Experimental solubility mapping revealed substantial deviations between experimentally determined and conventionally predicted Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) in the oligomeric regime, highlighting the limitations of group-contribution methods for low-molecular-weight polyesters. The PBS oligomer with a M̅n of approximately 2,000 g/mol (αPBS6) exhibited experimental HSP values of δD = 17.0, δP = 7.3, and δH = 7.1 MPa½. Despite borderline-to-unfavorable HSP-derived compatibility with curcumin (RED ≈ 1.04 and χ ≈ 1.21), αPBS6 exhibited high curcumin encapsulation, demonstrating that HSP-derived parameters alone do not directly predict encapsulation efficiency. Curcumin-loaded αPBS nanoparticles (Cur@PBS6) had an average diameter of 232 ± 1.5 nm, a high loading capacity (8.54–9.10%), and good colloidal stability. Their loading capacity exceeded those of commercial PBS (6.36%), PBSA (6.64%), and PLA (2.75%) systems, indicating that molecular-weight modifica…

title: Methodological principles of economic justification of design decisions on land-use territory organization
abstract: The purpose of the study is to improve the methodological principles for the economic justification of design decisions concerning land-use territory organization and to develop a sequence for comparing alternatives with due regard to spatial characteristics, costs, expected economic results, the time value of money and risk. The methodological basis combines systems, comparative, calculation-and-constructive and scenario approaches, together with analysis, synthesis, structuring and discounted cash-flow analysis. Seven components of economic justification were systematized, including the initial spatial and economic state, changes in spatial organization, one-time and current expenditures, direct economic result, avoided losses, and the time component with consideration of risk. Six successive stages for comparing alternative design decisions were proposed. To demonstrate the methodology, three variants of organizing a conditional land-use territory were assessed over a seven-year horizon. With a baseline discount rate of 10 %, the net present values of the variants were UAH 0.439 million, UAH 0.892 million and UAH 0.972 million, while the profitability indices were 1.244, 1.288 and 1.174 respectively. Sensitivity analysis at discount rates of 7 %, 10 % and 15 % confirmed positive net present values for all alternatives within the assumed range and showed that the capital-inte…

title: From external green cues to action: how green packaging design, eco-labels and consumer characteristics build trust to drive purchase intention
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how green packaging design and eco-labels, as external cues of green products, influence consumers' purchase intentions through green trust, and tests the moderating role of green product knowledge on the effects of green packaging design and eco-labels on green trust, as well as the moderating effect of perceived environmental responsibility on the effect of green trust on purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach The model proposed in this study was validated using partial least squares structural equation modeling, with survey data from 388 respondents in the Chinese market. Findings Results indicate that green packaging design, eco-labels, and green trust each have a significant positive effect on purchase intention. Green trust mediates the relationships between green packaging design and purchase intention and between eco-labels and purchase intention. Green product knowledge positively moderates the effects of green packaging design and eco-labels on green trust. Perceived environmental responsibility positively moderates the relationship between green trust and purchase intention. Originality/value This study incorporates external green-product cues into a green trust mediated model of purchase intention and examines the moderating roles of consumers' green product knowledge and perceived environmental responsibility. The results…
venue: Asia Pacific Journal of Marketing and Logistics

title: Data-driven characterisation of variable source light curves with multimodal representation learning
abstract: Large-scale photometric surveys such as the Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) are producing light curves for hundreds of millions of variable sources. Characterising these sources has traditionally relied on supervised classifiers trained with hand-crafted features and curated label sets, limiting their applicability to predefined taxonomies and individual surveys. Zwicky Vera C. Rubin We present a general, survey-agnostic framework for the characterisation of variable sources from photometric time series that operates entirely without labelled training data and produces low-dimensional representations capturing light curve properties such as amplitude, periodicity, and asymmetry directly from the observations. Our method combines two complementary views of each light curve in a multimodal architecture. Raw time-domain observations are processed by a Transformer encoder, and a generalised Lomb--Scargle (GLS) periodogram is processed by a convolutional neural network. Training uses a split-half augmentation strategy, where each light curve is randomly divided into two temporal halves that serve as independent views of the same underlying variability. The two branches are trained jointly using the Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularisation (VICReg) objective to produce embeddings that are invariant across the two halves while m…

title: DESIGN THINKING SEBAGAI KERANGKA INOVASI PEMBELAJARAN MATEMATIKA BERORIENTASI PADA KEMAMPUAN PEMECAHAN MASALAH SISWA SMA
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang solusi inovatif dalam meningkatkan motivasi, keterlibatan, dan kemampuan pemecahan masalah siswa dalam pembelajaran matematika melalui pendekatan Design Thinking. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara, observasi, dan angket yang divalidasi ahli terhadap 61 siswa dan 5 guru dari lima SMA di Kota Semarang, untuk memetakan kebutuhan belajar siswa dan guru. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa pembelajaran matematika masih kurang interaktif, menyebabkan keterlibatan siswa rendah, serta banyak siswa kesulitan mengingat rumus, memahami konsep abstrak, dan menyelesaikan soal cerita. Kondisi ini berdampak pada rendahnya motivasi dan capaian belajar. Sebagai solusi, penelitian ini mengusulkan pengembangan media pembelajaran digital dengan elemen Gamifikasi seperti poin, lencana, tantangan, dan papan peringkat. Integrasi elemen tersebut diharapkan menciptakan pengalaman belajar yang menarik, mendorong partisipasi aktif, memberi umpan balik instan, dan menumbuhkan rasa pencapaian siswa. Desain media juga memperhatikan kebutuhan guru akan sumber belajar yang variatif dan mudah diterapkan pada pembelajaran berbasis masalah. Proses pengembangan difokuskan pada tahap empathize, define, dan ideate dalam Design Thinking, menghasilkan konsep solusi yang relevan dengan kebutuhan pengguna. Namun, karena belum sampai pada tahap prototype dan test, produk yang dihas…

title: Sustainable bio-based concrete: material innovations, durability challenges and life cycle perspectives
abstract: Purpose This review presents a critical evaluation of bio-based and bio-enabled cementitious systems as solutions for lowering resource use and climate change impact without compromising performance. This study aims to review their components based on the processing of the components, their interaction with the matrix, the mechanical properties, durability performance and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). Design/methodology/approach This research uses a structured narrative review methodology based on peer-reviewed sources from the Scopus database, which includes peer-reviewed English-language literature from the years 2005 to 2025. Data were categorized in terms of material type, manufacturing process, density and test age, mechanical and durability performance and LCA functional unit, system boundary, biogenic carbon handling, energy and water metrics. Findings What emerges is an inherent performance-functional property balance, rather than a universally superior material per se. Low-density materials made from hemp, straw, wood and cork possess excellent insulating capabilities, yet generally do not have structural properties. Surface-treated fibers, biochar and Microbial-Induced Carbonate Precipitation (MICP) improve crack prevention, transport resistance and self-healing after cracking; however, some environmental gains might be compromised due to the use of increased chemicals…
venue: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology

title: Aspects of design and main parameters of motor roads with the one-sided transverse profile of a carriageway
abstract: In Ukraine today, the requirements of norms and regulations for the public motor roads design set crown transverse profile for the carriageway beside elements where the one-sided transverse profile is stated by the definition. In Europe, a one-sided (unidirectional) transverse profile of the carriageway has been established as a mandatory one for international motor roads with separate carriageways, with appropriate provisions included into regulations regarding main international traffic arteries and TEM (Trans-European Motorway) Technical regulation. In this article, by using motor roads with separate carriageways as an example, the analysis of the conceptual aspects of the design of motor roads with one-sided transverse profile of the carriageways is performed. The special attention is paid to the conceptual design approaches for the carriageway with unidirectional transverse profile that provide its advantages over crowned one when motor road with separate carriageways is to be designed with minimal cross-sectional sizes ensuring most economically effective formation. The peculiarities of design of horizontal curves, superelevations, additional lanes, and the most critical problems of a surface drainage and also exclusive points of crown cross-section designing for junction of carriageways for various elements of a motor road are analyzed. Some aspects of deceleration and a…

title: From dialogue to design: a Bakhtinian perspective on young children’s emerging understandings of robots
venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education

title: Long-term salinity is associated with deteriorated soil properties, rhizosphere microbiome restructuring, and elevated wheat crown rot: evidence from a 19-year gradient experiment and a 3-year remediation verification
abstract: Soil salinization threatens global agricultural sustainability and may elevate soil-borne disease risk through coordinated changes in soil conditions and the rhizosphere microbiome, yet long-term field evidence remains limited. Here, a 19-year controlled field experiment with an artificial salinity gradient (non-saline, moderate, and severe) was conducted to characterise salinity-associated responses of soil physicochemical properties, wheat crown rot (WCR), and the rhizosphere microbiome. A 3-year field remediation demonstration was implemented to test whether replacing saline irrigation with non-saline water could reverse soil deterioration and reduce disease severity. The results showed that severe salinity increased soil pH from 7.64 to 8.38 and reduced available phosphorus, total nitrogen, and available potassium by 54.11%, 14.63%, and 37.69%, respectively, while the WCR disease index increased from 10.51 to 32.88. It also reduced microbial richness and diversity, altered rhizosphere community composition, with taxon-specific abundance shifts among halophilic taxa, and redistributed community functional potential, with greater representation of genes associated with compatible-solute metabolism and ion homeostasis alongside changes in carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur metabolism. Remediation reduced soil salinity and pH, improved nutrient availability, and decreased the WCR dis…

title: Enhancement of plant growth and soil stabilization by seaweed polysaccharides in the red soil region of Southern China
abstract: Red soil is the second most extensively eroded soil type in China, predominantly distributed in the southern regions. Vegetative measures are widely recognized as an effective approach for controlling soil erosion in red soil areas, as they enhance slope stability and substantially reduce soil loss. However, during the early growth stages, the short and fine roots of plants are unable to extend beyond the shear failure surface, which constrains their capacity to stabilize the surface soil. To address this limitation, researchers have introduced seaweed polysaccharides as a soil ameliorant. Nevertheless, the specific mechanisms by which seaweed polysaccharides influence plant growth, root-soil complex mechanics, and the erosion resistance of red soil remain poorly understood. Accordingly, an experimental study was conducted to investigate the enhancement of plant growth and soil stabilization by seaweed polysaccharides in red soil. The results indicate that (1) seaweed polysaccharides exhibited an optimal concentration range for improving red soil. At concentrations below 2%, seed germination, plant height, and stem growth were promoted, whereas concentrations exceeding 2% exerted inhibitory effects. (2) In terms of mechanical properties, seaweed polysaccharides significantly enhanced the shear strength of the soil. Compared with the control group, application of seaweed polysac…

title: Influence of lignoacids, a by-product of oxidation of plant raw materials into vanillin and cellulose, on radish seed germination
abstract: Обоснование. Лигнокислоты (ЛК) – побочный продукт каталитического окисления растительного сырья в ванилин и целлюлозу. По составу они схожи с гуминовыми кислотами и могут обладать ростостимулирующей активностью. Поэтому изучение ростостимулирующих свойств ЛК для сельскохозяйственных растений представляется актуальным. Цель. Изучение влияния условий окисления растительного сырья различных видов и условий проращивания редиса на ростостимулирующие свойства выделенных ЛК. Материалы и методы. Оценивалась ростостимулирующая активность ЛК, выделенных из различных субстратов, на семенах редиса Raphanus sativus var radicula в лабораторных условиях при проращивании на фильтровальной бумаге. Оценивались энергия прорастания, всхожесть, длины корней и гипокотиля редиса, усреднённый и максимальный ростостимулирующий эффект (РСЭ). Результаты. Все выделенные ЛК обладают значительным ростостимулирующим эффектом (РСЭ): отношение длины корней, выросших на седьмые-восьмые сутки под действием ЛК и в контроле имеет значение РСЭ = 1,3-2,0. Ростостимулирующий эффект возрастает в ряду РСЭ(ЛК Осины) << РСЭ(ЛК Костры льна) ≈ РСЭ(ЛК Соломы пшеницы) ≈ РСЭ(ЛК Сосны). Ростостимулирующий эффект оптимальных концентраций ЛК частично маскируется ингибирующим эффектом их высоких концентраций.

title: Virtual education and artificial intelligence in public health and health professions training: a scoping review
abstract: Abstract Introduction: In recent decades, information and communication technology (ICT) has significantly impacted the health sector, necessitating constant evolution in the way knowledge is taught and imparted through these platforms. This implementation includes virtual simulations, virtual campuses, and chatbots, among others. However, there is uncertainty about how public health is being taught using technology. Objective: To map and describe the available evidence on virtual education and artificial intelligence-enabled tools in public health and health professions, with emphasis on their educational uses, reported benefits, implementation challenges, and implications for public health workforce development. Methods: A scoping review was conducted following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were performed in PubMed/Medline, Scopus, and the Virtual Health Library (BIREME) for studies published between 2015 and 2025. Studies addressing virtual education and/or artificial intelligence–enabled technologies relevant to public health or health professions training were included using a Population–Concept–Context framework. Results: A total of 1,266 records were identified, and 34 sources met inclusion criteria. The included evidence was geographically diverse and methodologically heterogeneous. Findings were synthesized into three ove…

title: Plastid tRNA-derived small RNAs associate with AGO1 and accumulate upon sulfur deprivation in Chlamydomonas
abstract: Abstract Transfer RNA-derived small RNAs (tDRs) represent a diverse class of noncoding RNAs with emerging regulatory roles across all domains of life. In the green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, next-generation sequencing revealed abundant, specific tDRs, with a predominance of those derived from plastid-encoded tRNAs. Most of these tDRs map to the 5’ ends of mature tRNAs and are 29-33 nucleotides in length, suggesting that they arise from cleavage at the anticodon loop or stem. We confirmed the plastid origin of some tDRs by engineering the chloroplast genome to replace the plastid-encoded tRNAAsn(GTT) gene with a nuclear counterpart. As reported in land plants, DICER-LIKE endonucleases play a limited role in tDR biogenesis in Chlamydomonas. However, a distinct subset of abundant tDRs, originating from both nucleus- and chloroplast-encoded tRNAs, associates with ARGONAUTE1 (AGO1). Using Gaussia luciferase reporter assays, we demonstrated that AGO1-associated tDRs can mediate RNAi-like gene silencing, and that tDRs originating from plastid-encoded tRNAs can function outside the chloroplast. Additionally, the tDR population in Chlamydomonas undergoes dynamic changes in response to nutrient availability. While nitrogen starvation causes a general decrease in both mature tRNA and tDR levels, sulfur deprivation specifically induces the accumulation of certain tDRs. Furthermore, st…

title: Editorial: Impact of plant bioactive compounds on human nutrition and health
Differential physiological responses to sodium and potassium chloride in Salicornia europaea, a model euhalophyte
abstract: Sodium (Na) and potassium (K) have comparable crustal abundances and similar physicochemical properties. However, due to the predominance of NaCl over KCl in natural salinity, most studies on plant salt responses have focused on NaCl, leaving responses to KCl salinity largely unexplored. To compare plant responses to Na and K salts, the euhalophyte Salicornia europaea was grown under equimolar (100 mM) NaCl and KCl treatments. NaCl salinity enhanced plant dry biomass, succulence, water relations, and the accumulation of organic osmolytes, whereas KCl salinity induced defence responses, lignin deposition, and caused complete plant mortality within 7 weeks. The levels of signalling molecules (H2O2, NO, and H2S) showed distinct patterns between NaCl and KCl treatments. Genes involved in ion compartmentation (HKT1, NHX1, SOS1, and VHA-A) were upregulated only under NaCl salinity. Moreover, NaCl reduced cellular ammonium levels, whereas KCl led to its accumulation, accompanied by declines in amino acid and protein contents, suggesting a disruption of ammonium assimilation under KCl stress. Comparative studies involving two glycophytes and four halophytes revealed that whereas glycophytes exhibited similar or less growth inhibition under KCl than NaCl, halophyte growth was severely inhibited by KCl but stimulated by NaCl. Notably, ammonium accumulation patterns differed between the t…

title: LhMYB93–LhEAT1 module modulated by LhBRG3 regulates tapetum degradation and pollen fertility in lily ( Lilium Asiatica. hybrida)
abstract: Abstract Male sterility is crucial for solving pollen contamination and promoting inter-varietal hybridization. As the innermost layer of the anther, the tapetum directly contacts microspores, and tapetal abnormalities typically lead directly to male sterility. However, the regulatory mechanisms of tapetal degradation and its transport of substances to microspores remain poorly understood. This study identified LhMYB93 as a key positive regulator of tapetum degradation and microspore development in lilies. Specifically, transcriptomic analysis combined with transcriptomic and functional analyses revealed that LhMYB93 is expressed at lower levels in male-sterile lilies, and LhMYB93 can partially restore pollen fertility in male-sterile lilies. Additionally, LhMYB93 interacts with LhEAT1 to effectively activate the transcription of LhABCG26, a gene essential for tapetum degradation and microspore development. Additionally, in vitro and in vivo ubiquitination experiments have demonstrated that the LhEAT1–LhMYB93 module is ubiquitinated by the E3 ubiquitin ligase LhBRG3 during the late stages of anther development (S9–10) and subsequently degraded by the 26S proteasome. This process ensures the normal development and timely degradation of the tapetum, promoting the normal development of pollen. These findings provide novel insights into the regulatory mechanisms governing microspor…

title: A comprehensive checklist of North American gypsophile plants: insights into their distribution and state of knowledge
abstract: Background and aims – We present the first comprehensive checklist of North American gypsophiles (plants restricted or nearly restricted to gypsum soils) to encourage the further exploration of gypsum exposures, promote systematic studies, and raise awareness about the potential need of conservation measures for these ecologically and evolutionary unique species. Material and methods – The checklist was based on a historical literature search, herbarium specimens, and fieldwork. We estimated an Aridity Index for the gypsum localities of all occurrences, taxa description over time, growth form, generic diversity within families as compared to global patterns, and conservation status. Key results – We recognize 287 taxa as gypsophiles, which occur from Montana, USA to southern Mexico, including 282 angiosperm taxa, 3 ferns, one gymnosperm, and one lycophyte. Herbaria and literature review retrieved 3,528 records for gypsophile taxa. The gypsum localities from these records were classified from arid to humid, with most being arid or semi-arid. The most diverse families were Asteraceae (77 taxa), Brassicaceae (14), Loasaceae/Nyctaginaceae (13), and Cactaceae/Namaceae (11). The most diverse genera were Mentzelia / Nama / Nerisyrenia (11), Phacelia / Pinguicula (9), and Drymaria / Gaillardia (8). Most gypsophile taxa were classified as perennial herbs (207) or shrubs (38), but annual…

title: BnaA8.RAP2.1 negatively regulates cuticular wax accumulation and drought tolerance in Brassica napus
abstract: Abstract Cuticular wax is an important component of the plant surface barrier that contributes to water retention and drought adaptation. However, the transcriptional mechanisms that negatively regulate wax accumulation remain poorly understood. Here, we identify BnaA8.RAP2.1, an AP2/ERF transcriptional repressor, as a negative regulator of cuticular wax accumulation and drought tolerance in Brassica napus. Loss- and gain-of-function analyses revealed reciprocal effects of BnaA8.RAP2.1 on wax deposition, cuticle permeability, water loss, and drought tolerance. BnaA8.RAP2.1-overexpressing plants exhibited reduced wax accumulation, increased cuticle permeability and water loss, and greater drought sensitivity, whereas knockout plants showed the opposite phenotypes. Stomatal aperture measurements further revealed genotype-dependent responses under drought, suggesting that altered stomatal responses may also contributes to BnaA8.RAP2.1-mediated drought phenotypes. Mechanistically, BnaA8.RAP2.1 directly bound to and repressed the promoters of BnCER1-2 and BnGCN5, as demonstrated by ChIP–qPCR, EMSA, and dual-luciferase assays. Genetic rescue analysis showed that BnCER1-2 overexpression partially restored wax accumulation, water retention, and drought tolerance in RAP2.1-overexpression plants, supporting BnCER1-2 as a functional downstream target. Moreover, constitutive expression of …

title: Species composition, distribution, and pathogenicity of Botryosphaeriaceae species associated with canker, twig dieback, and fruit rot of walnut in Central Anatolia, Türkiye
abstract: Abstract Background Botryosphaeriaceae species are associated with important diseases such as canker, dieback, and fruit rot in walnut ( Juglans regia L.) trees. In this study, the prevalence, species composition, associations with symptoms and geographical distribution, pathogenicity, and temperature-dependent mycelial growth of the walnut disease complex associated with Botryosphaeriaceae were investigated in an integrated manner across eight provinces in the Central Anatolia Region of Türkiye (Aksaray, Kayseri, Kırıkkale, Kırşehir, Nevşehir, Niğde, Sivas, and Yozgat). Results Within the scope of the survey, 30,501 trees in 265 walnut orchards were examined; the prevalence of orchards containing at least one symptomatic tree was 87.9%, and the pooled overall incidence of symptomatic trees was 16.0%. The incidence of symptomatic trees varied significantly among provinces. Out of 1283 tissue samples taken from perennial canker, twig dieback, and fruit rot symptoms, 666 Botryosphaeriaceae isolates were obtained (51.9%); Diplodia seriata De Not. (37.4%), Neofusicoccum parvum (Pennycook & Samuels) Crous, Slippers & A.J.L. Phillips (29.0%), Botryosphaeria dothidea (Moug.) Ces. & De Not. (17.4%), Lasiodiplodia theobromae (Pat.) Griffon & Maubl. (8.6%), and Lasiodiplodia pseudotheobromae A.J.L. Phillips, A. Alves & Crous (7.7%) were identified. Isolate-level species composition showe…

title: Virtual reality-based intervention in forensic mental health services: a feasibility study of implementation, acceptability, and clinical outcomes
abstract: Objective This study evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary clinical outcomes of an immersive virtual reality (VR)-based relaxation program implemented as part of routine care in adult and juvenile forensic mental healthcare settings. Methods A feasibility study was conducted in two forensic mental healthcare services: an adult prison-based rehabilitation unit (UHRPI; n = 21) and a juvenile justice treatment unit (UTJJ; n = 8). The 12-week study comprised a four-week pre-intervention phase, a four-week intervention phase including eight VR sessions, and a four-week post-intervention phase. Feasibility, comprising service-user acceptability and professional usability, was the primary outcome. Secondary exploratory outcomes included physiological measures (blood pressure and heart rate), state anxiety (STAI-State), and subjective emotional states assessed immediately before and after each VR session using visual analog scales (VAS). Participant-level behavioral indicators extracted from institutional clinical records were summarized descriptively. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze repeated physiological and VAS measures, whereas state anxiety was analyzed using paired-samples t -tests. Results Acceptability and usability were high in both settings, and the intervention was generally well tolerated. In the UHRPI, significant reductions were observ…

title: Analisis Fenomenologi pada Pemain Melalui Hubungannya dengan Karakter Virtual dalam Game Online Genshin Impact
abstract: Open-world online games such as Genshin Impact offer players freedom to explore virtual environments, interact with digital surroundings, and communicate with individuals from diverse cultural backgrounds. Thus, online gaming serves not only as entertainment but also as a digital space for social interaction, emotional experiences, moral negotiation, and identity development. This study aims to explore how Genshin Impact players understand their relationships with virtual characters, particularly regarding emotional attachment, moral values, and identity exploration and formation. A qualitative phenomenological approach was employed to examine players’ subjective experiences through in-depth interviews with five active Genshin Impact players. Data were analyzed interpretively by relating participants’ lived experiences to phenomenological perspectives on gaming, emotional attachment theories, Erikson’s identity versus role confusion framework, Bandura’s moral disengagement concept, and perspectives on gamer communities and virtual communication. The findings reveal that emotional attachment to virtual characters enables players to express idealized aspects of themselves, explore personal aspirations, and regulate emotions while distinguishing virtual experiences from reality. Players also negotiate moral values through automatic, reflective, and habitual moral disengagement pro…

title: SWEET uniporters – a 2026 update
abstract: Abstract SWEETs are a family of ancient sugar transporters found in Archaea, Eubacteria, oomycetes, fungi, plants and metazoa. In plants, SWEETs play central roles in carbon allocation from source to sink tissues, as well as reproductive development, response to changes in environmental conditions, and biotic interactions. Recent studies have provided deeper mechanistic insights into SWEET-mediated transport, including substrate specificity, transport selectivity, structural dynamics, and the physiological diversification of family members across species. Emerging evidence highlights roles of SWEETs in symbiotic interactions and microbiome-associated carbon exchange. Given the growing number of recent reviews on SWEET physiology, this update focuses on current challenges and emerging perspectives on SWEET-mediated transport processes, cell-type specificity, functional diversification, the interpretation of overexpression phenotypes, and functions in symbiotic interactions. We also discuss how these insights may be leveraged to optimize carbon partitioning, improve resilience, and enhance crop productivity and biofuel production.

title: The Crisis of the Dictatorships: 50 Years Later
abstract: Abstract Fifty years after the publication of The Crisis of the Dictatorships – in which Nicos Poulantzas analyzes the processes of political crisis and transition in Portugal, Greece and Spain – this article revisits the book to underscore its enduring analytical relevance. It examines three key dimensions: the specificity of dependency in these social formations; the role of geopolitics and inter-imperialist contradictions in both sustaining and undermining dictatorships; and the limits of post-dictatorship democratization, marked by state continuities and the persistence of bourgeois hegemony. Challenging economistic and formalist interpretations, Poulantzas offers a framework that situates states within the imperialist chain, insisting that, in the context of increasingly internationalized capitalism, separating internal from external dynamics leads to a distorted analysis. The article contends that Poulantzas’s insights anticipate contemporary debates on authoritarianism by revealing how exceptional forms of domination can persist within formally democratic regimes.

title: A novel Phytophthora -specific putative lipid-binding protein triggers plant immunity
abstract: Abstract Plants recognize conserved pathogen-derived molecules to activate pattern-triggered immunity (PTI), yet many secreted proteins from oomycete pathogens remain functionally uncharacterized. Here, we identified PcCF16, a previously uncharacterized secreted protein from Phytophthora capsici, through activity-guided fractionation of the pathogen secretome. PcCF16 induced cell death and PTI-associated gene expression in Nicotiana benthamiana, and purified recombinant PcCF16 triggered reactive oxygen species production across multiple plant species. PcCF16-induced cell death was independent of the co-receptors BAK1 and SOBIR1, while defense gene activation remained SOBIR1-independent but was partially dependent on BAK1. Recombinant PcCF16 pretreatment enhanced resistance to P. capsici, while P. capsici lines constitutively expressing PcCF16 exhibited reduced virulence. Structure-function analysis identified residues 202-291 as the shortest fragment tested that was sufficient for cell death induction, whereas N-glycosylation enhanced PcCF16 accumulation and activity but was not strictly required. Structural analyses revealed similarity between PcCF16 and members of the tubular lipid-binding protein (TULIP) superfamily and predicted internal hydrophobic cavities. Consistent with these features, PcCF16 preferentially associated with phosphatidic acid in vitro. Despite substantia…

Monitoring Parameter Kelistrikan Panel Penerangan Gedung Parkir Berbasis PLTS–PLN dan IoT (Monitoring Electrical Parameters of a Parking Building Lighting Panel Based on PV–Grid Power Supply and IoT)
abstract: This study develops an Internet of Things (IoT)-based monitoring system for a parking-building lighting control panel supplied by a 1.65 kWp photovoltaic system with a hybrid PV-grid source. The system integrates an ESP32, PZEM-004T for AC measurement, PZEM-017 for battery-side DC measurement, a 20×4 LCD, Wi-Fi, MQTT, and a web dashboard. Field testing was conducted for five days by comparing voltage and current readings with an AVO meter and clamp meter and by observing battery operation and source transfer. The reported average errors were 0.18% for AC voltage, 0.02% for AC current, 0.09% for DC voltage, and 0.045% for DC current. The measured data were displayed on the LCD and dashboard, and a transfer from the battery to the PLN grid was observed at the end of the discharge scenario. Network latency and packet loss, ATS transfer time, SOC validation, and independent power-meter validation were not measured. The results support the use of the ESP32-PZEM-MQTT architecture as a functional monitoring layer for a PV-powered lighting panel, while the conclusions remain limited to the tested operating conditions.

title: The Relationship Between Stakeholders’ Participation in Glass Bottle Reverse Logistics and Supply Chain Performance: A Case of SBC Tanzania Limited
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the relationship between stakeholders’ participation in glass-bottle reverse logistics and supply-chain performance at SBC Tanzania Limited in Arusha. A descriptive research design was adopted, using questionnaires and interviews with 152 participants comprising consumers, retailers, distributors, and company staff. Stratified random sampling was applied for quantitative data collection and purposive sampling for qualitative interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics through IBM SPSS 27, while qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis. The findings revealed a strong positive correlation between stakeholder participation and supply-chain performance (r = 0.784, p < 0.01). Despite this, 68.1% of respondents reported that SBC Tanzania primarily reuses rather than recycles bottles, leading to customer dissatisfaction regarding packaging quality. Additionally, 65.9% expressed dissatisfaction with the current financial incentives for bottle returns. The study concludes that improving transparency, revising incentive structures, and strengthening communication can enhance stakeholder engagement and supply-chain sustainability. The findings contribute to the growing body of literature on circular-economy practices in developing economies by contextualizing stakeholder theory within reverse-logist…

title: Thyroid involvement in lysosomal storage diseases: current evidence and clinical perspectives
abstract: Abstract Lysosomal storage diseases are inherited multisystem disorders caused by defects in lysosomal enzymes, transporters, or associated proteins, leading to intracellular substrate accumulation and progressive organ dysfunction. The thyroid gland may be particularly vulnerable because hormone release depends on thyroglobulin endocytosis, endosomal trafficking, lysosomal proteolysis, iodide recycling, and cellular proteostasis. This review summarizes current evidence on thyroid involvement in lysosomal storage diseases, with emphasis on clinical manifestations, pathophysiological mechanisms, diagnostic evaluation, and management. A literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar from database inception through August 31, 2026. Eligible clinical, review, and experimental studies addressing thyroid function, morphology, autoimmunity, treatment effects, or bidirectional thyroid–lysosomal mechanisms were descriptively synthesized. The strongest association is observed in nephropathic cystinosis, in which progressive primary hypothyroidism is frequent and may be delayed by early cysteamine therapy. Thyroid abnormalities have also been reported in Fabry disease, Gaucher disease, Hurler syndrome, and Pompe disease, although evidence is less consistent and often based on small cohorts, isolated reports, or animal models. Proposed mechani…

title: Mechanistic Insights into Sodium Storage in N-Doped Graphene/MoS2 Heterostructures Revealed by Operando Raman Spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offer tunable interlayer spacing and accessible surfaces that can overcome key limitations of conventional sodium-ion battery (SIBs) anodes. Here, we investigate Na+ storage mechanisms in three-layer 2D heterostructures composed of horizontally stacked graphene (G), nitrogen-doped graphene (NG), and MoS2 (M) by combining cyclic voltammetry with operando spectroelectrochemical Raman spectroscopy. Restricting the active thickness to three atomic layers enables direct spectroscopic access to interfacial charge transfer and strain during cycling. Electrochemical analysis reveals that Na+ storage is governed by two coupled factors: the permeability of the electrolyte-facing outer layer, and the electronic–mechanical interactions within the interlayer space. NG outer layers facilitate ion access and deliver up to 40-fold higher capacities than pristine graphene stacks, whereas MoS2 top layers suppress ion infiltration. Operando Raman correlates faradaic features with reversible structural changes, allowing separation of charge-doping and strain effects during cycling. The results demonstrate that Na+ storage proceeds predominantly via reversible accumulation in confined interlayer and blister-like reservoirs formed during solvent cointercalation. Incorporating MoS2 as a middle layer redistributes charge and buffers mechanical strain, enh…

title: Analysis of the influence of electric battery location on the static stability indicators of an electric bus
abstract: The development of electric public transport is accompanied by the use of heavy traction batteries whose installation position changes the vehicle centre of mass and affects the transverse static stability of an electric bus. The purpose of the study is to evaluate the influence of traction battery installation height and centre-of-mass height on limiting static-stability indicators. A calculation model of transverse stability on a side slope was applied, taking into account sprung and unsprung masses as well as suspension and tyre compliance. The critical side-slope angle, critical adhesion coefficient, transverse stability coefficient, and variation in centre-of-mass height for different battery layouts were determined. For the T70117 electric bus, the limiting side-slope angle decreases as the centre-of-mass height increases. When the centre-of-mass height exceeds 1.4 m, the calculated angle becomes lower than 28°. For a 500 kg battery, roof installation at 3.4 m raises the centre of mass to 1.43 m, whereas floor installation at 0.43 m results in a centre-of-mass height of 1.32 m. The results confirm that lower battery placement increases the transverse static-stability margin. The practical value of the study is the possibility of using the obtained relationships during preliminary electric-bus layout design and selection of traction-battery installation positions.

title: Distributed electric propulsion redundancy for high endurance fixed-wing UAVs: engine-Out survivability of twin, trimotor and quad configurations
abstract: Purpose High endurance fixed-wing UAVs powered by solar arrays or hydrogen fuel cells carry energy systems that cost more than the airframe itself and a single motor failure can end a multi-hour mission. This study aims to compare twin, trimotor and quad propulsion on measured data to find where the engine-out redundancy of each end. Design/methodology/approach Static thrust stand data for a 6.5 kg, 3.3 m airframe are transferred to flight with advance ratio dependent propeller coefficients. On a 1000 Wh budget, engine-out cases are scored against a two-level criterion of stopped propeller drag, trim drag and rudder authority. Findings All three configurations cruise at 18 m.s-1 on 211–233 W and hold that airspeed after a motor loss with the tested motor and propeller combinations. What separates them is directional control. The quad and trimotor need under 12° of rudder and the trimotor loses its centerline motor with no yaw. The twin needs 73% of the rudder travel and cannot be trimmed below 12.8 m.s-1, marginal against the 12 m.s-1 minimum sustainable flight level. Originality/value For the tested components on this airframe, the twin-engine redundancy assumption inherited from manned practice does not carry over: the fin, sized for cruise stability, sets the redundancy of the twin and a minimum control speed after a motor loss belongs in the design case of such a layout.

title: Engineering Water as a Foaming Agent for Polyolefin Foams: A Green and Continuous Strategy
abstract: Abstract Polymer foams have attracted increasing attention due to their distinctive porous structure and promising application prospects, whereas there remains a challenge in continuously fabricating polyolefin foams by a facile, low-cost, and green strategy. “Puffed corn sticks” are a typical example of Chinese traditional food with a porous structure, which is visually attractive and incredibly delicious. In this study, borrowing the idea from continuously fabricating puffed corn sticks, HDPE has been successfully water-foamed into well-defined internal porous extrudates with different cross-sectional shapes through an extrusion molding method. Herein, water acts as a green foaming agent and the extrusion molding method provides suitable foaming conditions. Under such conditions, polyolefin foams are continuously fabricated by this green strategy. Of note, the current widely used polyolefins can be water-foamed by this strategy, and they can be further extruded into different cross-sectional shapes; therefore, such a water-foaming strategy is of excellent universality. This study proposes a new methodological guidance for the continuous fabrication of polyolefin foams by a green strategy, which will widen the application of polyolefins.

title: Environmental, social, governance and sales in South Korean distribution industry
abstract: Purpose This study examines how environmental, social, and governance (ESG) activities influence sales performance in the South Korean distribution industry, focusing on the moderating roles of advertising intensity and firm type (wholesale vs. retail). Design/methodology/approach Using panel data from 50 publicly listed wholesale and retail firms from 2012 to 2021, fixed-effects regression models were estimated. ESG performance was measured using annual evaluation scores from the Korea Institute of Corporate Governance and Sustainability (KCGS). Findings The direct effect of ESG activities on sales was not statistically significant. However, advertising intensity strengthened the relationship between overall ESG performance and sales. When ESG dimensions were analyzed separately, only the interaction involving the social dimension showed a significant positive relationship with sales. ESG effects were also stronger for retailers than for wholesalers, suggesting that consumer-facing contexts enhance ESG effectiveness. Originality/value This study extends ESG research by focusing on short-term sales outcomes and highlighting the roles of ESG heterogeneity, communication, and firm type in shaping ESG effectiveness.

The Medieval Text and the Modern Question: AI for Multilingual Semantic Retrieval across Centuries
abstract: Multilingual access to medieval literature requires retrieval systems to bridge historical and cross-lingual semantic variation. This article introduces HistRAG, a language-aware framework combining lexical retrieval, multilingual dense representations, historical adaptation, hybrid fusion, and cross-encoder reranking. HistRAG separates the effects of document modernization, query adaptation, and retrieval architecture within a unified experimental setting. The framework is evaluated on a heterogeneous collection of Medieval Catalan literature using equivalent queries in three contemporary languages. Results show that lexical retrieval is highly sensitive to query language, while multilingual dense representations provide more robust cross-lingual access. Fixed hybrid fusion offers no systematic advantage over dense retrieval, and historical adaptations produce heterogeneous, non-additive effects. Cross-encoder reranking achieves the strongest average effectiveness, although its contribution varies across languages and evaluation subsets. These findings support an architecture- and language-sensitive approach to semantic retrieval from historically distant collections and provide a reproducible basis for extending AI-enabled access to other medieval textual traditions.

title: Designing a Hybrid CNN-Transformer Architecture for Robust Medical Image Diagnosis
abstract: Medical image diagnosis increasingly relies on deep learning against a background where convolutional neural networks capture local texture well but miss long-range spatial relationships, while transformer models need large labeled datasets and heavy computation that clinical settings rarely have. This study pursues the objective of designing a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture that fuses convolutional feature extraction with self-attention to raise diagnostic accuracy on X-rays, MRI scans, and histopathology slides without exceeding the computational budget of real-world deployment. The proposed method pairs a lightweight convolutional backbone, which extracts local texture and edge features, with a transformer encoder that models global relationships across image regions, merging the two branches through a cross-attention fusion module before a classification head outputs the diagnosis. Training the architecture on publicly available medical imaging datasets and evaluating it against standalone CNN and transformer baselines using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score, the result reveals that the hybrid architecture beats both baselines, raising accuracy and sensitivity on cases with subtle abnormalities that need local texture recognition and broader spatial reasoning together, while inference time stays within a practical range for clinical workflows.
