title: Organic Compound Hunters: An Educational Game Supporting the Learning of Organic Compound Formulas and Nomenclature
abstract: Abstract The educational game titled “Organic Compound Hunters” was designed to reinforce preservice teachers’ learning regarding the naming and formula determination of organic compounds within the scope of chemistry education. The game is based on matching the chemical names of organic compounds─including alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, aromatics, and those containing functional groups (alcohols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, amines, and amides)─with their structural, bond-line, and molecular formulas; it aims to teach a total of 104 different organic compounds. The game set consists of 104 task cards, nine fixed cards, and a checklist. Five to eight students can play, with one student checking the accuracy of the matches in each round. The study found that the Organic Compound Hunters game offers an interactive learning environment that can help preservice teachers to understand the relationships between organic compound nomenclature and their structural, bond-line, and molecular formulas.

Differential diagnosis of pulmonary Talaromyces marneffei infection and pulmonary tuberculosis in HIV/AIDS patients using a CT-based multimodal 2.5D deep learning approach
abstract: Background To investigate the diagnostic value of a computed tomography (CT)-based multimodal 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) deep learning model for differentiating Talaromyces marneffei (TSM) from pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) in patients with human immunodeficiency virus infection/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (HIV/AIDS). Methods A total of 380 HIV/AIDS patients with pulmonary infections who were admitted to the Fourth People’s Hospital of Nanning from January 2018 to August 2025 were retrospectively enrolled, including 203 patients with PTB, 177 with TSM. The cohort was randomly divided into a training set and a test set at a ratio of 7:3. A clinical model, a radiomics model, and a 2.5D deep learning model were constructed separately. Results In the clinical feature model, Random Forest achieved the optimal performance, with a test set AUC of 0.856. In the radiomics model, XGBoost attained the highest AUC of 0.866. In the 2.5D deep learning model, ResNet18 performed best at the slice level with an AUC of 0.865, and the patient-level support vector machine (SVM) model based on MIL achieved an AUC of 0.885. The multimodal combined model integrating clinical, radiomics, and deep learning features achieved the highest AUC of 0.931 and a specificity of 0.981. title: Association of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Radiographic Findings Identified by Machine Learning and Outcomes of Patients Receiving Invasive Mechanical Ventilation
abstract: Objectives: To determine whether predictions from a deep learning model that identifies acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) findings on chest radiographs (CXRs) can also predict clinical outcomes beyond traditional indicators of hypoxemia and illness severity. Design: Retrospective cohort study. Setting: Single academic medical center. Intervention: None. Patients: Adult patients with CXRs performed at the time of invasive mechanical ventilation initiation. Methods and Main Results: We applied a deep learning model that was previously trained to identify bilateral airspace opacities consistent with ARDS to CXRs of 6591 patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. The resulting ARDS-CXR scores were evaluated for their ability to discriminate risk of 28-day mortality and their association with 28-day mortality and time to extubation after adjusting for a patient’s Pa o 2 /F io 2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV. The median ARDS-CXR score was –2.09, corresponding to an ARDS probability of 15%, and 1089 (17%) patients had a positive score, corresponding to an ARDS probability above 50%. Twenty-eight-day mortality was 35.1% among patients with a positive score and 13.5% among patients with a negative score. abstract: This study was motivated by the need to improve students’ mathematical representation ability and the importance of self-regulated learning in mathematics learning. It aimed to examine the implementation of the FERA learning model assisted by the Baamboozle application, determine whether students’ mathematical representation ability improved better than through conventional learning, and describe students’ self-regulated learning in the implementation of the FERA learning model. This study employed a quasi-experimental method with a Nonequivalent Control Group Design. The research was conducted at a senior high school in Sukabumi using purposive sampling, involving 30 students in the experimental class X-2 and 30 students in the control class X-1. The study was conducted on the Statistics topic over three meetings. Data were collected using a mathematical representation test, a self-regulated learning questionnaire, and observation sheets, and analyzed using the Ngain test, normality test, homogeneity test, and an independent-samples t-test. The results showed average implementation scores of 90.93% for the teacher and 87.50% for the students, the experimental class obtained a higher mean Ngain 0.756 than the control class 0.556, with a significant difference t(58) = 4.95, p <0,001 and a large effect size Cohen’s d = 1.278 and students’ self-regulated learning obtained a mean s…

title: Deep learning-based differentiation of FLASH ultrasound windows
abstract: Abstract Background Equine colic emergencies present highly stressful, time-critical scenarios for both clinicians and patients, thus rapid and accurate diagnostic triage is paramount. To support veterinarians under these high-pressure conditions, deep learning tools can be leveraged for automated image recognition to assist in localizing abdominal organs and interpreting FLASH (Fast Localized Abdominal Sonography of Horses) ultrasound windows. Objectives A software tool was developed to identify FLASH-specific ultrasound windows on the equine abdomen and to recognize ultrasonographic organ patterns. Study design Retrospective-prospective comparison of software and clinical examination, model development. Methods A deep learning approach for image classification was used to train software to assign ultrasound images to FLASH windows. Results Strongest software performance was observed for the duodenal window, with all test images correctly classified, corresponding to a recall of 1.00. Nephrosplenic window demonstrated high classification accuracy, but 23% of images were misclassified as gastric window. While 84% of ventral images were correctly classified, 16% were predicted as duodenal window. Most pronounced confusion was observed between ventral and thoracic windows, with only 55% of thoracic images correctly identified. Left and right middle third FLASH windows 4 and 6 wer…

title: The Lived Experience of Professional Learning of Teachers in the North of Scotland
abstract: In Scotland, as elsewhere, it is widely recognised that the quality of teaching is the most important factor in children’s learning, and therefore on education system outcomes. The quality of teaching can be improved through high-quality teacher professional learning. However, there is a lack of empirical research on how teachers experience professional learning. This paper describes the experiences of professional learning of twelve physics teachers in secondary schools across the north of Scotland. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews and by teachers completing professional learning career roadmaps and year-long reflective diary-logs. These experiences are compared with their contractual requirements and analysed against a theoretical framework based on Timperley’s principles of effective of professional learning, and Kennedy’s models professional learning. This aims to achieve an understanding of professional learning practices for teachers in Scotland. The study finds that most of the teacher professional learning is transmissive rather than transformative with little evidence of enquiry as stance or collaborative enquiry-based approaches. This neither serves the macro-level desire for transformative change nor the micro-level and nano-level desire for improved instruction and is unlikely to result in improvements in pupil outcomes or system performance.

title: Implementasi Model Pembelajaran Problem Based Learning Berbasis E-Newspaper Terhadap Pemahaman Konsep Struktur Atom Kelas X
abstract: Pemahaman konsep struktur atom yang masih rendah akibat sifatnya yang abstrak menuntut adanya inovasi model dan media pembelajaran. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh yang signifikan dari implementasi model Problem Based Learning (PBL) berbasis E-Newspaper terhadap pemahaman konsep struktur atom peserta didik kelas X SMA YP HKBP 1 Pematangsiantar. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode kuasi eksperimen dan desain Nonequivalent Control Group Design. Sampel ditentukan dengan teknik purposive sampling, yaitu kelas X-3 (31 peserta didik) sebagai kelas eksperimen yang belajar menggunakan model PBL berbasis E-Newspaper dan kelas X-4 (29 peserta didik) sebagai kelas kontrol yang belajar menggunakan pembelajaran konvensional. Data pemahaman konsep dikumpulkan melalui pretest dan posttest berupa 20 soal pilihan ganda yang valid, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas Shapiro-Wilk, uji homogenitas Levene, uji Mann-Whitney U, dan uji N-Gain. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata posttest kelas eksperimen (90,48) lebih tinggi daripada kelas kontrol (83,97), dengan N-Gain sebesar 0,81 (kategori tinggi) dibandingkan 0,68 (kategori sedang). title: Robust Deep Long-Term Correlation Filter Tracking
abstract: Long-term object tracking is an essential task for developing robust vision ability for intelligent robots and vehicles. To cope with various challenges in the dynamic driving environment, existing methods usually maintain a target appearance model and update it in an online manner. However, the errors may accumulate during the updating process when the target suffers from the problems caused by such issues as long-term occlusion and out-of-view, thus resulting in tracking failures. This work proposes a Robust Deep Long-term Tracking (RDLT) method, which can alleviate the impact of erroneous updates by incorporating an offline learned deep Siamese network into a unified correlation filter tracking framework. Specifically, it learns a deep correlation filter model that models target temporal variations to locate the target. To avoid tracking failures caused by the challenges like long-term occlusion, a pre-trained deep Siamese network is activated to search for the target on an enlarged searching region when the correlation filter outputs low response values, by which several target candidate windows can be obtained. To correctly select the optimal target window, this work further proposes a novel multi-expert evaluation schema. It evaluates the target candidate windows by using a pair of “experts”, i.e., Correlation filter-based expert (C-expert) and Deep similarity-based exper…

title: Selective extraction of phenolic compounds from barley waste using deep eutectic solvents
abstract: In this study, the development of an ultrasound method for extraction of phenolic compounds from barley waste using acidic deep eutectic solvents (UAE-DES) was investigated. Optimization of the extraction parameters, which include extraction time, temperature, and ultrasound power (UP), was performed using the One-Factor-at-a-Time (OFAT) experimental design, followed by HPLC-PDA for determination of total quantified phenolic content (TQPC). In addition, the influence of water addition on TQPC was evaluated. The Maximum TQPC obtained was 5.78 mg/g using ChCl: formic acid at a molar ratio (1:2) and optimal conditions of (70 °C, 30 min, 80% UP, 10% water), and 4.67 mg/g, using ChCl: tartaric acid at a molar ratio (1:2) and optimal conditions of (70 °C, 25 min, 100% UP, and 20% water). The obtained TQPC was 5- and 4-fold higher in comparison with 70% methanol and 70% ethanol extraction. LC–MS-qTOF analysis of DES extracts revealed diverse phenolic compounds, while the concentration range of compounds obtained was as follows: ferulic acid (0.86–2.47 mg/g), catechin (0.12–2.16 mg/g), p -coumaric acid (0.12–0.32 mg/g), naringenin (0.54–0.86 mg/g), and apigenin (0.15–0.91 mg/g). SEM analysis confirmed enhanced accessibility of lignocellulose in DES-treated samples. The sustainability of UAE-DES extraction was assessed using AGREE, AGREEprep, CACI, BAGI, and CaFRI green tools. The grade…

title: Optimization of transport and logistics systems in deoccupied territories in the conditions of post-war reconstruction
abstract: The functioning of transport and logistics systems in the deoccupied territories occurs in conditions of critical uncertainty, security risks and significant destruction of the basic infrastructure, which makes it impossible to apply classical market models of routing and management. The purpose of the article is to formalize destructive factors and develop scientifically based approaches to the adaptation and optimization of freight and passenger transport and logistics systems in the deoccupied territories in the conditions of post-war recovery. The paper uses the apparatus of set theory (to systematize and formalize risk factors), systemic and comparative analysis (to assess challenges in the freight and passenger sectors), as well as elements of mathematical modeling and vector optimization (to formulate prospects for further research). The general set of destructive factors is formalized. A three-level model of adaptation of the transport and logistics system of the deoccupied territories of Ukraine is substantiated. It is proven that its optimization requires a transition from single-criteria methods to multi-criteria trade-off optimization.

abstract: Background Prostate cancer (PCa) is responsible for a substantial proportion of male cancer cases worldwide. Biochemical recurrence (BCR) representing a critical challenge in its disease management. Formononetin, a natural isoflavone derived from traditional Chinese medicine, has demonstrated potential anticancer properties. We sought to determine the translational potential of Formononetin-targeted molecules in PCa. Methods A list of putative targets of Formononetin were identified through five public databases. Overlapping candidates underwent further refinement using an ensemble of bioinformatics tools, encompassing differential expression profiling, co-expression network construction, and multiple machine-learning classifiers. Docked complexes and complementary analyses were subjected to evaluate the binding stability. To functionally validate GSTM2, we assessed its functional role on PCa cell growth, motility, and invasiveness in vitro , as well as the expression of CXCL10 and CCL22 chemokines. Results Integrative analysis identified 413 Formononetin targets, with overlapped 335 PCa-associated genes. Through weighted gene co-expression network analysis and differential expression analysis, 22 candidate genes were identified as Formononetin-related genes in PCa. Machine learning algorithms and survival analysis further suggested GSTM2 as the most important target. GSTM2 was…

title: Proposal of an integrated structural-interactionist model of psychological harassment at work: beyond the harasser–victim dynamic
abstract: Purpose This paper introduces and proposes an integrated structural-interactionist model of psychological harassment at work to better identify the mechanisms to prevent and counter this relational dysfunction. Design/methodology/approach Based on a narrative review methodology of the literature, the conceptual model incorporates the perspectives of both the psycho-individual and socio-organizational paradigms. The model allows for an extension of understanding within a structuro-interactionist perspective on psychological harassment at work. A synthesis of existing literature is undertaken to identify the multiple dimensions of the dynamics of harassment at work. Findings The integrated structuro-interactionist model is based on five propositions specifying the role of (1) environmental factors, (2) organizational factors, (3) managerial factors, and (4) personal and dispositional factors in the dynamics of workplace harassment. An additional proposition (5) concerns the nature of individual and organizational consequences of psychological workplace harassment. Originality/value Building on the contributions of several previous models of psychological harassment at work, this integrated structural–interactionist model synthesizes earlier paradigms. It aims to enhance the ability to identify organizational levers that can prevent and counter occurrences of workplace harassment.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analysis of gene expression changes in brown adipose tissue during cold acclimatization in rats
abstract: Abstract Objective This study aims to conduct a combined analysis of differentially expressed genes in the transcriptome and proteome of brown adipose tissue in cold-tolerant rats, exploring potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for cold acclimatization. Methods Male SD rats underwent intermittent cold exposure. Blood and brown/white adipose tissue samples were collected after 21 days. Differentially expressed genes and proteins in brown adipose tissue were identified through high-throughput mRNA transcriptome sequencing and tandem mass tag (TMT) mass spectrometry analysis, combined with detection of glucometabolic markers in blood samples. Results Transcriptome analysis identified 2031 differentially expressed genes, comprising 344 upregulated and 1687 downregulated genes. Proteomic mass spectrometry analysis identified 376 differentially expressed proteins, comprising 217 upregulated and 159 downregulated proteins. Integrated analysis revealed 13 synergistically upregulated genes and 11 synergistically downregulated genes. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses indicated that upregulated genes predominantly clustered in fatty acid metabolism processes and PPAR signaling pathways, while downregulated genes were enriched in adipocyte lipolysis regulation pathways. abstract: Introduction Teacher turnover undermines instructional continuity and organizational stability in education systems worldwide. Despite extensive research, limited attention has been given to how multiple forms of capital jointly predict turnover intention in expatriate-dominated, non-Western contexts. This study applies the Four-Capital Framework to examine associations between human, social, structural, and psychological capital and teacher turnover intention in Qatar. Methods Data from a weighted cross-sectional survey of 1,010 teachers in public and private schools were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). More than 90% of participants were non-Qatari. The analysis examined direct associations and indirect pathways through psychological capital. Results Structural capital had the strongest positive association with psychological capital, while psychological capital was negatively associated with turnover intention. Social capital had a significant indirect association with turnover intention through psychological capital, whereas its direct association was not statistically significant. Human capital had a positive direct association with turnover intention. The model explained 61.1% of the variance in psychological capital and 28.5% of the variance in turnover intention. Acute exacerbation of systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease-associated interstitial lung disease: integrated pathophysiology and respiratory care
abstract: Abstract Acute exacerbation of systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease-associated interstitial lung disease (AE-SARD-ILD) is an uncommon but severe cause of acute respiratory failure, frequently requiring intensive care. Although commonly managed according to paradigms derived from acute exacerbation of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis or acute respiratory distress syndrome, AE-SARD-ILD encompasses heterogeneous pathological processes with distinct respiratory mechanics, pulmonary vascular involvement, reversibility, and treatment response. Management based solely on the underlying rheumatic disease or radiological pattern may therefore be inadequate. This Perspective reviews current evidence on the diagnosis and critical care management of AE-SARD-ILD and proposes an integrated clinical–radiological–mechanical framework for physiology-guided decision-making. Moving beyond conventional disease- and imaging-based fibrotic classifications, the framework identifies four dominant, potentially overlapping physiological phenotypes arising from the interaction between the chronic pulmonary substrate and the superimposed acute insult: fibrotic/UIP-like, inflammatory/ARDS-like, pulmonary hypertension-dominant, and diffuse alveolar haemorrhage-dominant. title: Architecting Co-continuous PVDF Composites via Multi-material 3D Parallel Printing for Enhanced Piezoelectricity and Wearable Sensing
abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoelectric composites have attracted considerable attention for self-powered sensing; however, achieving efficient electromechanical response while maintaining structural integrity under repeated deformation remains challenging. Herein, a structure-driven multi-material 3D parallel printing strategy is developed to construct polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based piezoelectric composites with a co-continuous dual-phase architecture. In this design, ionic liquid (IL)-modified PVDF serves as the piezoelectric phase, where the IL promotes β-phase formation and dipole orientation, while carbon nanotubes (CNTs)-reinforced PVDF provides a conductive phase for electrical signal collection. Unlike conventional stacked configurations, the parallel-printed architecture enables continuous integration of the piezoelectric and conductive phases, providing intimate interfacial contact and a mechanically interconnected structure. The resulting structural continuity facilitates stress transfer during mechanical deformation and contributes to a stable electromechanical response. Kelvin probe force microscopy measurements further reveal an interfacial potential difference of 85.6 mV, indicating distinct interfacial electrical characteristics between the two phases. When more is not better: how business model portfolios drive performance in multi-business model entrepreneurial firms
abstract: Purpose Drawing on configuration theory, this study examines how different combinations of business model (BM) design themes shape the financial performance of entrepreneurial firms that simultaneously adopt multiple business models. We thus depart from typical BM research that investigates design themes in isolation to focus on how configurations of design themes differentially influence the performance of firms that operate BM portfolios. Design/methodology/approach We employ fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to test whether specific configurations of BM design themes relate to high financial performance. fsQCA aligns well with the main objectives of this study because it captures equifinality and causal complexity, allowing for the empirical examination of multiple configurations that can lead to high performance. The final sample consists of 107 UK software firms characterized by rapid innovation adoption and frequent use of BM portfolios. Findings The results indicate three distinct configurations that relate to high financial performance: (1) novelty combined with the absence of customer lock-in and product/service complementarities; (2) novelty combined with efficiency and the absence of product/service complementarities; and (3) novelty combined with customer lock-in and product/service complementarities in the absence of efficiency. Process-based upgrades to the WRF multi-layer green-roof scheme (WRF-MLGR v2.0) and evaluation against field observations
abstract: Green roofs can moderate urban heat by increasing latent heat flux and reducing sensible heat flux. However, capturing these effects in models depends on accurate representation of key green-roof processes, including substrate heat and moisture transport, soil-vegetation-atmosphere energy and moisture exchanges, interactions with the underlying roof, and drainage. Here we introduce targeted, process-based updates to the green-roof scheme (hereafter, MLGR) within the multi-layer urban canopy model (BEP-BEM) in the WRF mesoscale model to address key limitations in the original formulation. The updates include a non-linear dependence of soil thermal conductivity on moisture, vegetation-modulated surface thermal conductivity, explicit soil-surface evaporation, multi-layer root water uptake for transpiration, and canopy interception with evaporation and dew formation. We evaluate the original and modified MLGR schemes using hourly observations from an extensive sedum roof in London, Canada, for “summer” (1 July–31 August 2014) and “fall” (1 September–31 October 2014) periods. We also analyze 11–18 October 2025, when green roof modules were placed directly on the roof deck – which corresponds to the model's lower boundary assumption. title: Preparing to lead in polycrisis: a multi-method process evaluation of HR-driven psychosocial resilience training for leaders
abstract: In crises and fluctuating organizational contexts, resilience is increasingly recognized as a critical HRM strategy for sustaining organizational functioning and human capacity. This multi-method study evaluates an HRM-driven psychosocial resilience training program, including emotional training elements, for public and private leaders operating under polycrisis conditions. The study examines how leaders engage with resilience-oriented training and perceive its contribution to their capacity to anticipate, cope with, and learn from adversity. Participants´ evaluation of cyclic “resilience sprints,” the mechanisms of impact, and contextual influences were analyzed using descriptive and statistical methods. Findings show that structured resilience sprints support implementation, although the number, intervals, and duration of sprints were less suitable during polycrisis. Leaders achieved measurable effective training (Kirkpatrick reaction/learning levels), though training effectiveness (behavior/results levels) was more limited. Key facilitators included being gathered in a psychologically safe learning environment with committed trainers and supportive colleagues, while the main barrier was prioritizing training alongside work demands. Training-timing and motivation shifted dynamically throughout the period. The study contributes to HRM, Management, and Applied Resilience schola…

Professionalism: the Australian Emergency Management Uniform Minimum Dataset
abstract: The professionalisation of emergency management in Australia is ongoing. Supporting that process is the development of a body of knowledge to support the new profession. The body of knowledge for emergency management requires that emergency events are recorded in a manner and format that supports ongoing learning and research. There is currently no agreed format or standard for the recording of emergency events in Australia. Emerging from research into the human capacities of an emergency manager in Australia is the concept of a minimum dataset that supports building the body of knowledge and supports future research. The Australian Emergency Management Uniform Minimum Dataset is proposed as a means of standardising the collection of data related to emergency events that occur in Australia. A standardised collection of data will allow for practitioners and researchers to identify and learn from past events and will support the professionalisation of emergency management practice.

title: FINANCIAL PLANNING MEDIATES FINANCIAL LITERACY AND CAPITAL ACCESS IN ENTERPRISE INVESTMENT DECISIONS
abstract: This study examines the influence of financial literacy and access to capital on investment decisions, with financial planning as a mediating variable among food and beverage Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in West Java, Indonesia. This research employed a quantitative approach using a descriptive and verificative design. Data were collected from 135 MSME owners selected through stratified random sampling using a Likert-scale questionnaire. The results indicate that financial literacy and access to capital have positive and significant effects on financial planning. Financial literacy and access to capital also have positive and significant direct effects on investment decisions. Furthermore, financial planning has a positive and significant effect on investment decisions and significantly mediates the relationship between financial literacy, access to capital, and investment decisions. The study highlights that improving MSME investment decisions requires strengthening financial literacy, expanding access to capital, and encouraging effective financial planning practices simultaneously. These factors contribute to better resource allocation and support the long-term sustainability of food and beverage MSMEs.

title: STRUCTURAL ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL-ECONOMIC TERMS: SIMPLE, DERIVED, COMPOUND, AND TERMINOLOGICAL UNITS
abstract: This article examines the structural organization of contemporary English financial-economic terminology, with particular attention to simple terms, derived terms, compounds, and multi-word terminological units. The study aims to identify the principal structural patterns used to name financial and economic concepts, describe their morphological and semantic characteristics, and determine how structural organization affects translation into Uzbek. A descriptive comparative approach is employed. The analyzed terminology is grouped according to the number and type of lexical components and the degree of semantic and terminological unity. The analysis shows that simple terms form the basic lexical layer of the system, while derived terms expand this layer through productive affixes expressing processes, states, qualities, agents, and relations. Compound and multi-word units are especially prominent because economic concepts frequently involve relationships between institutions, processes, instruments, policies, and measurable variables. In the analyzed distribution, simple terms account for 13 percent and derived terms for 24 percent, whereas compound and terminological units together account for 63 percent. The findings also indicate a close relationship between structural type and translation strategy. Simple terms generally have direct Uzbek equivalents; derived terms often all…

abstract: A growing number of Generation Z individuals are entering Indonesia's stock market, yet whether financial literacy meaningfully shapes their investment interest is still an open question, and few studies have tested attitude, perceived behavioral control, and financial literacy together within a single model built around Management students. This paper examines how these three factors jointly and individually relate to stock investment interest among Generation Z Management students. The sample comprised 323 active Management students, selected through purposive sampling from a population of 1,430 students who had completed a Financial Management course, with data gathered via a Likert-scale questionnaire and processed through multiple linear regression. The findings indicate that attitude, perceived behavioral control, and financial literacy each exert a positive and statistically significant partial effect on stock investment interest, and together account for 71.7 percent of its variance, with financial literacy emerging as the strongest predictor results that support all four proposed hypotheses. These outcomes align with earlier work linking financial literacy to investment interest, yet depart from findings among mutual fund investors where perceived behavioral control and financial literacy showed no significant effect, pointing to the possibility that such influences va…

UNDERSTANDING FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT BEHAVIOR: THE ROLES OF FINANCIAL LITERACY, FINANCIAL ATTITUDE, AND FINANCIAL SELF-EFFICACY
abstract: This study examines the direct effects of financial literacy and financial attitude on financial management behavior and their indirect effects through financial self-efficacy among students in the Management Study Program, Universitas Muhammadiyah Yogyakarta. A quantitative explanatory design was employed using questionnaire data from 150 respondents selected through non-probability sampling. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that financial literacy and financial attitude have positive and significant effects on financial management behavior and financial self-efficacy. Financial self-efficacy also has a positive and significant effect on financial management behavior. Furthermore, financial self-efficacy significantly mediates the relationships of financial literacy and financial attitude with financial management behavior. These findings highlight the role of financial knowledge, financial attitudes, and confidence in managing financial matters in explaining students’ financial management behavior.

title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
abstract: Abstract Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

Scentronic: An artificial intelligence–assisted olfactory interface for remote odor sharing and transmission
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the surge of human–machine interfaces (HMIs) for various applications. Olfaction is a fundamental chemical sense crucial to perception, memory, and emotion. Current limitations arise from the difficulty of accurately capturing, transmitting, and reproducing odor signals, and the lack of standardized, network-enabled platforms. This work presents an internet of things (IoT)–enabled olfactory interface for remote odor sensing and stimulation. The system integrates an artificial intelligence-assisted odor sensing platform with a wearable piezoelectric olfactory actuation system. We demonstrate the design, characterization, and application of this framework, which integrates devices, circuit architecture, and software algorithms. Applications in medical contexts include psychophysical testing to study olfactory pathways and evaluate sensory loss. We further showcase multisensory stimulation through integrated olfactory and gustatory interfaces for enhanced immersion. This study establishes a scalable framework for IoT-based olfactory interaction, advancing HMIs toward a future that includes the long-overlooked chemical senses.

title: Detection of Financial Statement Fraud Using Fraud Hexagon Theory
abstract: This study examines indications of financial statement fraud in Indonesian banking companies using the fraud hexagon framework. The framework comprises pressure, capability, collusion, opportunity, rationalization, and ego, operationalized through financial targets, financial stability, external pressure, chief executive officer education, political connections, ineffective monitoring, the nature of the industry, total accruals, and the frequency of chief executive officer photographs. A quantitative approach was applied to banking companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2019–2022. Purposive sampling identified 39 companies, providing 156 initial company-year observations; 50 observations were excluded as outliers, leaving 106 for analysis. Multiple linear regression was used, supported by descriptive analysis and classical assumption tests. The results indicate that pressure, when represented by financial targets and external pressure, is significantly associated with the detection of financial statement fraud. Financial stability and the proxies for capability, collusion, opportunity, rationalization, and ego show no statistically significant individual effects. The adjusted R-squared is 0.017, indicating limited explanatory power. title: Assessment Design Needs: A Preliminary Study on Using Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools for Educators
abstract: Assessment is considered as a key feature and central pillar in the teaching and learning process, particularly in making of judgement and measurement of student achievement and mastery of learning outcomes. The traditional methods of designing assessments items face several challenges, such as the need and requirement to design the assessment items manually, the time-consuming nature of the design process and the required cognitive skills through formal training provided by various institutions. As the result, the assessment items may lack on the detailed and context specific to validity and reliability, lack of standardized rubric and inconsistent scoring in performance based. A preliminary study was conducted at the analysis phase to explore fundamental understanding of Outcome-Based Education (OBE), Assessment Literacy, and Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) literacy among educators. Forty-six educators were involved in this study. Findings have shown that most of the respondents have lower level of using GAI tools and prompt engineering skills, 43.5% use GAI for teaching and learning, searching information (34.8%), idea collection process (6.5%), reflection/journal (4.3%), writing programming code (4.3%), generate image (4.3%) and other tasks (2.2%). title: Environmental impact assessment in the design and restoration of bridge crossings
abstract: The restoration of bridge crossings under conditions of large-scale wartime destruction of Ukraine’s transport infrastructure raises pressing questions about the quality of environmental management in design — in particular, the completeness and effectiveness of the environmental impact assessment procedure. At the same time, the regulatory framework governing EIA for bridge crossings, as transport infrastructure objects with significant potential environmental impacts, has not previously been the subject of systematic comparative analysis. To fill this gap, 14 elements of the EIA procedure under Directive 2011/92/EU (as amended by 2014/52/EU) were compared with the corresponding provisions of Ukrainian Law No. 2059-VIII of 23.05.2017 (as amended on 15.11.2024). Compliance was established for 6 procedural elements and partial compliance for 8; no element was found to be entirely absent from Ukrainian law. The most significant regulatory gaps concern the screening of bridge crossings as a distinct object category, the analysis of alternatives, post-decision monitoring, and the legal regulation of EIA under conditions of accelerated wartime restoration. title: Perancangan Ruang Wudhu Berbasis Green Design pada Masjid Daarut Tauhiid Bandung
abstract: Area wudhu menjadi ruang utama dalam aktivitas umat muslim, seringkali terabaikan dari aspek perancangan sehingga memunculkan isu kelembaban ruangan, pencahayaan, dan penggunaan material yang kurang ramah lingkungan dan tidak mudah dalam perawatan. Dalam kegiatan pengabdian masyarakat ini bertujuan merancang ulang salah satu area wudhu di Daarut Tauhiid Bandung dengan pendekatan green design berdasarkan indikator Greenship dari Green Building Council Indonesia (GBCI). Solusi yang ditawarkan meliputi pemilihan material ramah lingkungan, optimalisasi pencahayaan alami, peningkatan kenyamanan dan aksesibilitas pengguna, serta integrasi tanman indoor di area wudhu. Metode pelaksanaan dalam pengabdian masyarakat ini dilakukan melalui tiga tahap, yakni observasi lapangan, proses desain, dan presentasi karya. Observasi lapangan dilakukan pengukuran dan dokumentasi ruang eksisting dan diskusi bersama masyarakat sasar untuk menemukan temuan permasalahan dan harapan yang di inginkan masyarakat. Selanjutnya perancangan desain ruang wudhu yang didasari oleh tahap awal dan diperkuat dengan teori hasil dari studi literatur. Terakhir presentasi karya dan diseminasi sosialisasi ruang wudhu yang dihadiri oleh pengurus Daarut Tauhiid sekitar 10 orang untuk melakukan evaluasi desain. Hasil program ini menghadirkan model perancangan 2D dan 3D area wudhu berbasis green desain untuk Masjid Daarut Ta…

title: Serial Changes in Multimodal Imaging and Electroretinographic Findings in Acute Unilateral Outer Retinopathy Presenting With Blind Spot Enlargement
Defending the NRR from Chung’s ‘When to Limit the Market’
abstract: Victor Chung (2026) thoughtfully challenges my 2023 argument for the “Normative Representativeness Requirement” (NRR). According to the NRR, a successful moral objection to a system of political economy (e.g., shareholder capitalism, stakeholder capitalism) must both address a representative sample of firms and show that the sample is unethical overall. These conditions are difficult to meet for objections to highly complex socioeconomic systems, and critics often ignore them. In this Response, I describe the NRR and show why Chung’s argument, though interesting, relies on both a mischaracterization and questionable focal cases.

title: EMPLOYMENT SECURITY AND LABOR-MARKET RESILIENCE UNDER ECONOMIC SHOCKS: EVIDENCE FROM EMERGING ECONOMIES
abstract: Economic shocks can cause problems with job stability. Reduce money that families earn. This makes labor markets more unstable. Employment security and the ability of labor markets to recover after times are very important parts of economic security - especially in countries that are developing. This study looks at how jobs have changed in Uzbekistan from 2020 to 2025 using job and unemployment data. It also looks at Germany’s Kurzarbeit program as an example of a policy that helps protect jobs during economic times. The research uses existing statistics and a case study method to understand how job security is connected to the ability of labor markets to handle shocks. The results show that better job numbers don’t always mean job security or good social protection. They don’t always mean that workers are safe from problems either. This can help the economy recover faster when things start to get better. The study says that protecting jobs should go together with training for workers, strong social protection systems and policies that help economies change. It ends by saying that making labor markets stronger means looking at both the number of jobs and the quality of those jobs. It also means having support ready, for workers and businesses when economic shocks happen.

title: Proofing the concept of a segmented biophotovoltaic process to produce electricity from marine cyanobacteria: an indoor and outdoor approach
abstract: Abstract This study presents an innovative biophotovoltaic (BPV) process with three components: a cyanobacteria reservoir that serves as the biological engine; an electron-capture reactor that redirects transmembrane electrons; and a radiation-harvesting tower designed to maximize energy input and enhance system scalability. For the indoor (LED) and outdoor (solar radiation) tests, the most suitable resistances to yield the maximum current density were 164 Ω and 220 Ω, respectively. Indoor electricity generation peaked at 227 mW m − 2 , with an average of 175 ± 47 mW m − 2 , while outdoor tests peaked at 215 mW m − 2 , with an average of 166 ± 26 mW m − 2 , indicating similar efficiency under both conditions. To explain these efficiencies, the 5% loss in performance is most likely related to the increase in temperature from 20 °C to 32 °C and the resistivity of electrode materials. To confirm this, complementary experiments (in triplicate) demonstrated that an increase in incubator temperature to 32 °C also resulted in lower electricity generation (125 ± 25 mW m − 2 ). The heat conduction to the cyanobacteria medium led to harsher environmental conditions for Synechocystis pevalekii , and the increased resistivity caused voltage drops. Overall, the proof of concept of our BPV process demonstrated that it is technically possible to run in the system in an external laboratory env…

title: THE INTERNATIONAL MARKET FOR MARITIME TRANSPORT SERVICES: CURRENT TRENDS AND TRANSFORMATION FACTORS
abstract: The article examines current trends in the international market for maritime transport services and identifies the factors driving its transformation. The purpose of the study is to clarify the role of maritime transport services in international trade, systematise the main directions of market change, and determine how economic, trade policy, geopolitical, technological, environmental, and infrastructure and logistics factors affect its operation. The market is defined as a system of relations between service providers and users within which demand for and supply of shipping capacity, freight rates, routes, and conditions of carriage are formed. Its principal components comprise demand, supply, pricing, transport and logistics infrastructure, institutional regulation, technological support, and related services. The findings show that current market development is characterised by slower growth in the physical volume of seaborne trade, route reorientation, rising transport activity, freight rate volatility, digitalisation, decarbonisation, the increasing importance of port connectivity, and stronger requirements for supply chain resilience. The author’s contribution lies in distinguishing trends as observable directions of market change from factors as the forces producing such change, and in classifying the factors into six groups. The factors are additionally divided into cy…

Baby Stocks: A Market-Based Model for Paying Reparations
abstract: This article addresses the concept of paying reparations for slavery and systemic racism in the United States by using individually-owned investment accounts granted at birth (i.e., “baby stocks”) in order to redress racially unequal ownership of the U.S. stock market. Thus far, most of the literature on reparations has focused on making the moral case that reparations are due and calculating the total amount that should be paid. Building upon this background, this article proceeds to consider the prospective question of how should reparations be paid? Based on evidence from long-term investing, the author argues that a portion of reparations should be paid with an index fund of the U.S. stock market, because stocks accumulate wealth better over time than other major asset classes. The philosophical and practical complexities of paying reparations with baby stocks are addressed, especially the issue of limiting autonomy to manage assets in order to reduce market risks and maximize long-term gains. Finally, potential avenues for developing baby stocks within the context of current political and financial realities are discussed.

title: Geopolitical conflicts and the global pharmaceutical economy: A conceptual analysis of supply chain disruptions and market resilience
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine how geopolitical conflicts impact the global pharmaceutical economy through disruptions in pharmaceutical supply chains and pharmaceutical markets. Specifically, it aims to explore how current geopolitical conflicts impact pharmaceutical markets and supply chains in terms of pharmaceutical availability and production costs. Approach This study used a conceptual approach in its analysis of how geopolitical conflicts impact pharmaceutical markets and supply chains. It synthesized literature and insights from various sources and global pharmaceutical supply chain analyses to create a conceptual framework that explains how pharmaceutical supply chains and markets are impacted by geopolitical conflicts. Findings From the analysis of literature and the pharmaceutical supply chain on a global level, it has been observed that geopolitical conflicts impact pharmaceutical supply chains through trade sanctions, variations in energy prices, transportation problems, and shortages of raw materials and APIs. In such cases, the cost of production is affected, and supply chain stability is impacted. To mitigate such effects, supply chain diversification and strategic medicine reserves are recommended. Originality This paper aims to contribute to the literature with a conceptual perspective on the relationship between geopolitical conflicts and pha…

title: Finding the Sweet Spot: Isomerization Strategy Enables Balanced Energy Dissipation of NIR-II AIEgens for “One-for-All” Tumor Phototheranostics
abstract: Abstract “One-for-all” phototheranostics with the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) emission have garnered great enthusiasm for seamlessly integrating superb imaging and high-efficiency therapy into a single formula. However, it is still a nontrivial conundrum to achieve balanced excited-state energy dissipation to guarantee high NIR-II brightness, photothermal conversion, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. As a powerful tool for balancing radiative and nonradiative decays, aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) are emerging as a promising frontier in developing “one-for-all” phototheranostic agents, while their phototheranostic performance needs to be further improved. In this contribution, we designed and synthesized two positional isomers, 5BT-PBPT and 6BT-PBPT, by attaching donors at the 5- and 6-positions of the benzo[b]thiophene (BT) segment, respectively, to investigate the effect of positional isomerism on the phototheranostic performance of NIR-II AIEgens. Interestingly, both experimental and computational results demonstrate that the isomerization affords great strength in tuning energy levels, structural conformations, aggregation behaviors, and excited-state energy dissipation. Consequently, a sweet spot for fully utilizing excitation energy was achieved in 5BT-PBPT nanoparticles (NPs), which exhibited not only strong NIR absorption but also…

title: Financial Leverage and Stock-Price Volatility in an Emerging Market: Evidence from Indonesian Consumer Non-Cyclicals
abstract: Consumer non-cyclicals are often considered defensive investments; however, differences in capital structure may expose their stocks to substantial price volatility. This study examined the relationships between profitability, financial leverage, firm size, and stock-price volatility among Indonesian consumer non-cyclical firms from 2022 to 2024. A quantitative observational research design was employed using a balanced panel of 30 firms, comprising 90 firm-year observations. Stock-price volatility was measured using the natural logarithm of Parkinson's range-based variance estimator, calculated from annual high and low stock prices. A random-effects panel regression model incorporated year fixed effects and firm-clustered standard errors, supplemented by robustness checks involving a logarithmic transformation of leverage, a price-source subsample analysis, and the exclusion of highly leveraged observations. Financial leverage was positively and significantly associated with stock-price volatility (coefficient = 0.2427; p = 0.002), whereas profitability exhibited no statistically significant association (p = 0.499). Firm size demonstrated a negative association that was marginally significant at the 10% significance level (p = 0.062). The positive association between financial leverage and stock-price volatility remained robust following the logarithmic transformation and with…

Control of Dollar Spot with Fungicides on a Creeping Bentgrass Green in New Brunswick, NJ, 2024 and 2025
abstract: Dollar spot, caused by the fungal pathogen Clarireedia jacksonii , is one of the most destructive diseases on cool-season turfgrass, infecting a wide range of turfgrass species, and has the largest economic impact on turfgrass facilities. Symptoms of dollar spot initially start as small, circular, sunken spots that generally do not exceed 5-cm in diameter. The infected leaves show up as bleached and show a light straw color. Under favorable conditions, the disease progresses, and the spots can coalesce into irregularly shaped large patches. This report evaluates the efficacy of synthetic fungicides for managing creeping bentgrass dollar spot. Results from this trial will help turfgrass managers develop effective management programs for dollar spot.

title: Chasing US financial instability: spillovers between financial conditions and the AI market
abstract: Purpose This article examines spillovers between US financial conditions and artificial intelligence (AI)-related equity performance, amid debate over AI-driven financial fragility reminiscent of the 2000 dot-com bubble. Design/methodology/approach The analysis combines the three subcomponents of the Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index (credit, leverage and risk) with the S&P Kensho Artificial Intelligence Enablers & Adopters Index, used as a proxy for US AI market performance, over the period from June 1, 2018 to December 12, 2025. It applies the quantile-on-quantile connectedness framework of Gabauer and Stenfors (2024), with a time-varying extension and bootstrap inference. Findings The results show that connectedness between the AI market and financial conditions is state-dependent and becomes intense when the receiving side of the system is in an extreme regime. Credit and leverage conditions affect the AI market asymmetrically and dominate transmission when AI valuations themselves move into tail states. The risk component emerges as the most persistent transmitter across quantile combinations, indicating that changes in volatility, uncertainty and risk appetite are the main drivers of the AI-finance nexus. Feedback spillovers from the AI market appear episodic and arise mainly in cross-tail configurations, when financial conditions are sharply tightening or e…

title: Electricity Generation Assessment of Photovoltaic Window System Using Data-Driven Modeling
abstract: Photovoltaic window systems have emerged as a promising building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) technology by enabling electricity generation while maintaining facade transparency. However, accurately estimating their electricity generation potential at early design stages remains challenging due to the complex influence of architectural geometry on solar exposure. In this study, a data-driven regression framework is developed to predict the total annual electricity generation of photovoltaic window systems using a parametric simulation dataset provided by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL). The proposed framework employs four architectural and geometric input parameters window-to-wall ratio, number of stories, floor height, and north–south to east–west aspect ratio which are typically available during the early stages of building design. Three regression models, namely Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosted Regression Trees, are systematically evaluated using a five-fold cross-validation strategy. Model performance is assessed using normalized error metrics, including root mean square error, mean absolute error, and the Pearson correlation coefficient. The results indicate that Gradient Boosted Regression Trees achieved the best predictive performance, with a normalized RMSE of 0.265, normalized MAE of 0.235, and Pearson correlation coefficient of …

title: ASSESSMENT OF HOUSING FINANCE ACCESSIBILITY AND MORTGAGE MARKET PERFORMANCE IN NIGERIA
abstract: Housing finance enables households to convert future income into present access to housing, yet the capacity of Nigeria's formal mortgage system to perform this role remains contested. This study assesses the structure, performance, accessibility and affordability of housing finance in Nigeria using exclusively secondary data. A documentary and ex-post facto design was adopted, drawing on Central Bank of Nigeria reports, publications of the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria, National Pension Commission, Nigeria Mortgage Refinance Company and World Bank, together with peer-reviewed studies. Trend, ratio, percentage-change and documentary analyses were applied. Results show that Primary Mortgage Bank assets increased from ₦451.95 billion in 2018 to ₦624.06 billion in 2024, while deposits rose by 79.5 per cent. Net loans grew more slowly from ₦229.60 billion to ₦307.51 billion, and the loan-to-asset ratio fell to 49.3 per cent in 2024. Prudential indicators improved after 2021, although the 2024 non-performing loan ratio remained high at 21.86 per cent. NHF lending, mortgage refinancing and Retirement Savings Account equity access widened formal financing channels, but low incomes, financing costs, land-title constraints, documentation requirements, construction costs and limited long-term funding continue to weaken effective access. The study concludes that institutional capacity …

title: Short-Term Impact of China's Reverse Repo Operations on the Overnight Shibor: Evidence from the Money Market
abstract: Based on daily data from China's money market between March and April 2025, this study investigates the short-term effects of the People's Bank of China's (PBC) reverse repo operations on the overnight interbank rate (O/N Shibor). Using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression and an event-study approach, the analysis explores both the quantity-based and price-based transmission mechanisms of monetary policy. Empirical results indicate that an increase in the reverse repo amount significantly reduces the overnight rate at the 5% level, confirming the liquidity-supply channel of quantitative policy and demonstrating that liquidity injections effectively ease short-term funding costs. The reverse repo rate exerts a positive but statistically insignificant influence, suggesting that while its price signal aligns with theoretical expectations, its short-term transmission remains limited. The one-week Shibor has a strong and significant positive impact on the overnight rate, highlighting the dominant role of market expectations. Overall, the findings suggest a three-stage transmission chain-liquidity adjustment, market expectations, and rate response-where reverse repo operations mainly function as a liquidity-relief mechanism shaped by expectation dynamics rather than a direct policy shock.

A Bibliometric and Systematic Analysis of the Most-Cited Studies on Pre-Service Physical Education Teachers
abstract: This study aimed to identify and analyze the most cited articles on PETE (Physical Education Teacher Education) students through a systematic review and bibliometric analysis, revealing research trends and contributing to the teacher education literature. Studies indexed in the Web of Science database were examined to determine the most productive authors, journals, countries, and keywords. Thematic orientations, methodological characteristics, and educational implications were systematically assessed. Results indicated a notable increase in PETE-related publications after 2010. Chiva-Bartoll, Dervent, and Block were identified as leading authors, while the Journal of Teaching in Physical Education was the most prominent journal. The United States, Spain, Australia, and the United Kingdom showed the highest country-level affiliation frequencies. Frequently used keywords include perceptions, beliefs, pedagogical content knowledge, attitudes, inclusion, and experiences; however, the themes of gender, diversity, and validity show relatively limited development within the thematic structure. The findings reveal an increase in publication frequency after 2010 among the 50 most-cited studies examined and emphasize the need for future research to focus more on issues of gender, diversity, and validity.

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on the Efficiency of Infrastructure Project Implementation: A Field Study of Service Agencies in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
abstract: Objective: The current study aimed to identify the impact of digital transformation on the efficiency of implementing infrastructure projects in Saudi service entities, by studying the dimensions of digital transformation, represented by the technical dimension, the organizational dimension, and the human dimension, and measuring their impact on improving the efficiency of project implementation in the city of Riyadh. Methodology: The study adopted a quantitative research design using the descriptive analytical approach. The study population consisted of all employees in service agencies related to the implementation and management of infrastructure projects in the city of Riyadh in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The study followed the simple random sampling method, and it amounted to (398) individuals. The study tool was the electronic questionnaire, due to the large size of the study sample of employees in agencies related to the implementation of infrastructure projects in the city of Riyadh. Results: The results showed that the level of digital transformation implementation was very high with an overall average of (4.46), and the level of efficiency in implementing infrastructure projects was very high with an average of (4.32). The results confirmed the existence of a statistically significant effect of digital transformation in its various dimensions on improving the effici…

title: Analysing Enablers of Green Logistics Adoption in Indian Logistics Service Providers: A Multimethod Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental sustainability in logistics has become increasingly critical as firms experience growing pressure to reduce their emissions and improve their overall supply chain's ESP. The emissions associated with the transportation, warehousing, and distribution activities of their logistics service providers (LSPs) can significantly affect their ESP. In India, freight transportation is heavily dependent on road transportation, and road freights account for a substantial share in freight‐related greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. While Green Logistics Practices (GLPs), such as route optimisation, energy‐efficient warehousing, and cleaner transportation, can improve environmental outcomes, their adoption remains uneven, particularly in emerging economies. Existing research has largely examined individual drivers of GLP adoption or focused on manufacturing and broader supply chain contexts, with limited understanding of how these drivers are interrelated and their relative importance in influencing GLP adoption. The study addresses this gap by modelling the inter‐relationships among GLP drivers and weighting their relative importance for LSPs in an emerging economy context. This study analyses the drivers of adoption of GLPs and their relationship with the environmental sustainability performance (ESP) of LSPs using Institutional Theory and Stakeholder Theory. A multi‐meth…

title: Xizmatlar sohasida davlat-xususiy sheriklikning samarali mexanizmlari
abstract: В статье рассматриваются механизмы государственно-частного партнерства (ГЧП) в сфере услуг с акцентом на распределение ответственности, рисков и стимулов между публичной и частной сторонами. В отличие от общего описания форм ГЧП, исследование сосредоточено на том, какие элементы контрактной конструкции определяют качество услуги, устойчивость проекта и интерес инвестора. Обобщены подходы к государственным контрактам, аренде, концессиям, совместным предприятиям и моделям BOT, BOO, DBFO, LDO, O&M и Service Contract. На основе международных методических материалов предложен алгоритм выбора модели для проектов сферы услуг, включающий идентификацию рисков, оценку способности сторон ими управлять, определение показателей результата и механизмов мониторинга. Отдельно сформулированы предложения, применимые к практике государственно-частного партнерства в Узбекистане.

Pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence untuk Penguatan Branding Digital UMKM dalam Meningkatkan Daya Saing Produk Lokal
abstract: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the main pillars of the Indonesian economy, but most micro-scale business actors face limited resources in managing their businesses. The main problem faced by the service partners, namely Sahabat Genggam Teman Indonesia (GTI), which facilitates MSME administrators in Bekasi City, is low literacy. Branding is digital, with less-than-optimal brand identity elements, minimal use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), and limited resources to obtain professional assistance. This Community Service (PKM) activity aims to improve partners' literacy and skills in using AI technology, particularly ChatGPT as an AI branding assistant, to independently design brand names, slogans, brand positioning, product descriptions, and social media copy. The activity will be carried out independently in a hybrid format at the Grand Metropolitan Bekasi Ballroom and via Zoom Meeting on October 13, 2026. The implementation method includes surveys and problem identification, material/module preparation, educational training with lectures and interactive discussions, and evaluation. The outcome of this activity is increased knowledge and skills among partners, in this case MSMEs, enabling them to operate and use ChatGPT as an AI branding assistant to design brand names, slogans, brand positioning, product descriptions, and copywriting independently for social me…

Marangoni Effect-Mediated Interfacial Regulation of Oriented Laser-Induced Graphene–MOF Heterojunctions toward High-Performance Dual-Mode PEC-SERS Biosensor
abstract: Abstract Heterojunctions of graphene and MOFs are highly desired for optoelectronic sensing analysis, yet disordered MOF growth severely restricts interfacial charge transfer and sensing performance. Herein, we report a solution-phase synthesis by taking advantage of the Marangoni effect to achieve the oriented growth of a porphyrin-based MOF on laser-induced graphene (LIG), yielding a LIG–MOF heterojunction with vertically aligned spike arrays. The intimate heterointerface enables ordered 3D electron transport and generates an interfacial electric field (IEF) to boost photoelectrochemical (PEC) properties, offering an enlarged carrier density by 3.0 × 105-fold compared with LIG. For surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS), a selectively enhanced Raman signal of the MOF by methylene blue (MB) is observed on LIG–MOF, uncovering a competitive charge transfer mechanism. In LIG–MOF, IEF properly directs electrons from LIG to the MOF while blocking electron injection into MB; photoexcited electrons from MB transfer stepwise to the MOF, enhancing its Raman signal. Consequently, a PEC-SERS biosensing chip is developed with LIG–MOF via aptamer-gated controlled MB absorption. The biosensing chip can simultaneously generate in situ PEC and SERS responses under 532 nm laser excitation via the LIG–MOF heterojunction for accurate and sensitive detection of patulin. title: Effect of Low-Pressure Radio Frequency (RF) Plasma Exposure Time on the Profile of Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.): GC-MS Based Chemometric Evaluation
abstract: This study investigated the effects of low-pressure radio frequency plasma (LPRFP) treatment applied at different durations (90 s, 3, 5, 9, and 15 min) on the volatile component profile of powdered turmeric using GC–MS combined with chemometric analysis. A total of 49 volatile compounds were identified, among which artemisia ketone was the most dominant and stable component, accounting for an average of 39.12%. Ten major constituents, including ar-curcumene, α-zingiberene, β-sesquiphellandrene, β-bisabolene, β-caryophyllene, ar-turmerol, himachalene, farnesene, humulene, and turmerol isomers, collectively represented more than 80% of the total volatile profile and exhibited significant variations. Short plasma exposures (90 s and 3 min) preserved the relative proportions of the dominant sesquiterpenes, maintaining chemical stability close to the control samples. In contrast, prolonged treatments (9 and 15 min) caused a marked reduction in the concentrations and peak areas of these compounds, attributed to non-thermal oxidative degradation. Monoterpenes were identified as the most plasma-sensitive group, whereas oxygenated compounds increased significantly with extended treatment, indicating plasma-induced oxidative transformation. Statistical analyses confirmed that plasma duration significantly influenced volatile composition (p < 0.05). A treatment time of 5 min was determ…

Tailoring Methane Pyrolysis and Carbon Products through Bubble Dynamics Regulation via Inlet Design in Molten Copper
abstract: Abstract Molten metal-catalyzed methane pyrolysis represents a promising route for low-carbon hydrogen production coupled with valuable carbon materials. However, the influence of methane bubble dynamics on interfacial reactions and carbon evolution remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that bubble dynamics engineering can effectively regulate methane conversion and carbon structure formation in molten copper. By integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations with experimental investigations, we reveal that the gas inlet configuration significantly alters bubble detachment, rising behavior, and residence time. The conventional straight inlet (I-type) generates relatively large bubbles that interact strongly with the nearby quartz wall, resulting in wall-guided bubble transport and a shorter rising path. In contrast, the curved inlet structure (U-type) promotes bubble detachment into the bulk molten Cu, leading to less wall-constrained and more tortuous bubble trajectories with longer residence times. The optimized bubble dynamics increase methane conversion to 12.11% and the carbon production rate to 0.74 g/h, while simultaneously improving the structural quality of the carbon products. These findings establish bubble dynamics as a key process parameter governing interfacial carbon supply and growth pathways, providing a scalable strategy for enhancing hyd…

title: Low-frequency fiber Bragg grating accelerometer based on an elliptical flexure hinge lever amplification mechanism
abstract: To address the demand for low-frequency vibration monitoring in transportation infrastructure, an FBG accelerometer incorporating an elliptical flexure hinge lever amplification mechanism was developed. A theoretical model was constructed to calculate the sensor’s sensitivity and resonant frequency, while a genetic algorithm was used to optimize the sensor’s structural parameters. Furthermore, a finite element model was constructed for modal analysis, followed by experimental verification conducted on a low-frequency vibration platform. The findings show that the sensor has a resonance frequency of 81 Hz, a sensitivity of 256.25 pm/g within the 1–45 Hz operating range, and a linearity greater than 0.996. The transverse interference remains below 5.74%, indicating a strong transverse anti-interference capability. Featuring simple fabrication and ease of packaging, the proposed sensor is highly suitable for vibration monitoring in complex environments.

title: Effect of Low-Frequency Modulation on the Penetration Profile and Microstructure in Double-Pulsed GMAW of AA6061 Aluminum Alloy
abstract: Double-pulsed gas metal arc welding (DP-GMAW), in which strong and weak pulse groups alternate periodically at a low frequency, is promising for improving the weld quality of aluminum alloys. However, how the low-frequency modulation shapes the bead profile and microstructure remains unclear. Bead-on-plate DP-GMAW of AA6061 aluminum alloy was therefore performed, in which the numbers of pulses in the strong and weak groups were varied from 1:1 to 30:30 (low frequency 41.67–1.39 Hz). Fish-scale ripples appeared on the bead surface at all tested frequencies, whereas the penetration fluctuated periodically only when the number of pulses per group reached 7 or more, so that the onset of the periodic fluctuation is bracketed between 8.33 Hz and 5.95 Hz. Both the penetration and the reinforcement peak/valley differences increased as the low frequency decreased; the largest penetration peak/valley difference reached 664.33 μm at 2.78 Hz, and the ratio of the penetration to the reinforcement peak/valley difference was largest at 3.79 Hz, where the penetration difference (627.83 μm) amounted to 532.06% of the reinforcement difference, suggesting that the droplet-impingement-driven flow affects the pool bottom far more strongly than the bead surface. At 3.79 Hz, the valley and peak angles reached 91.52° and 158.33°, respectively. It is proposed that the droplet-driven melt erodes the sol…

FSF-RTDETR: a frequency–spatial feature fusion network for eggplant fruit disease and pest detection in complex agricultural scenes
abstract: Detecting fruit diseases and pests in complex agricultural scenes remains challenging due to large target-scale variation, weak lesion features, leaf and branch occlusion, and severe background interference. To address these problems, this study focuses on eggplant fruit disease and pest detection and proposes FSF-RTDETR, a frequency–spatial fusion model. The proposed model builds a dual-branch frequency–spatial enhanced backbone to improve disease and pest feature representation from both frequency details and spatial structures. In the frequency branch, AFDC and MFFWBlock enhance high-frequency responses such as fruit borer edges, rot lesion textures, and thrips bite marks through attention-guided frequency-domain convolution and multiscale wavelet feature modeling. This design improves the perception of small targets with weak boundaries and fine textures. In the spatial branch, VisionClueMerge and G6MambaLayer preserve local spatial cues and introduce six directional scanning paths covering horizontal, vertical, and diagonal interactions. This helps the model better describe occluded targets, complex backgrounds, and irregular lesion distributions. Furthermore, EGMuF adaptively integrates edge-texture information from the frequency branch and structural semantic information from the spatial branch through channel, spatial, and pixel-level gated attention. title: ESCOLHA TEMÁTICA EM TRABALHOS DE CONCLUSÃO DE CURSO DE ARQUITETURA E URBANISMO, 2021-2026, E SUA RELAÇÃO COM A DEMANDA HABITACIONAL DO OESTE PARANAENSE
abstract: O estudo analisa a distribuição temática de 154 trabalhos de conclusão de curso em Arquitetura e Urbanismo produzidos entre 2021 e 2026 em uma instituição privada de ensino superior de cidade média do Oeste do Paraná, com atenção à participação da habitação de interesse social. A pesquisa adota abordagem documental, descritiva e quantitativa, com classificação por função programática predominante e por município de implantação, além da leitura das ementas das disciplinas de projeto e de planejamento urbano. A habitação de interesse social serve de parâmetro de análise porque tem três atributos ausentes nas demais categorias. São eles previsão legal que vincula a atuação profissional, demanda mensurada e publicada por município e menção explícita em ementa de disciplina obrigatória. Os resultados indicam que 10,4% dos trabalhos tratam de habitação e que 3,9% abordam habitação de interesse social, enquanto equipamentos de saúde, cultura e assistência social concentram as maiores participações. O confronto com os dados oficiais de necessidades habitacionais do Paraná mostra distância entre a demanda registrada nos municípios de implantação e a pauta temática da formação. O texto discute implicações curriculares e limites do trabalho de conclusão como indicador formativo.

title: Tunable Chiral Terahertz Radiation With Colossal Circular Nonlinear Optical Response From Two‐Dimensional Perovskites
abstract: ABSTRACT Chirality is a fundamental geometric property endowing materials with distinct optical behaviors, pivotal in the frontier of nonlinear optics and photonics. Chiral two‐dimensional (2D) hybrid organic‐inorganic perovskites (HOIPs) integrate intrinsically broken inversion symmetry with molecular chirality, offering exceptional potential for tailoring nonlinear optical responses. Here we report the generation of tunable chiral terahertz (THz) radiation from the prototypical chiral 2D HOIPs single crystals (R/S‐(BrBA) 2 PbBr 4 ), exhibiting giant and broadband circular nonlinear optical response with asymmetry factor that approaches the theoretical upper limit of 1, corresponding to near‐complete discrimination between opposite circular polarizations. By directly resolving the helicity‐dependent components of the emitted THz fields, we show that the helicity‐dependent response originates at the emission stage, rather than arising from propagation or post‐emission polarization filtering. Beyond polarization modulation, oscillatory features associated with chiral phonon modes were observed in the emitted THz signals, suggesting a coupling between THz chirality and collective lattice dynamics. These results establish the THz domain as a fertile regime for chiral light–matter interaction and open new pathways for ultrafast chiral spectroscopy, polarization control, and coheren…
