Preconception Systemic Inflammation Response Index and Time‐to‐Pregnancy
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Systemic inflammation may affect female reproductive function, but there is relatively little epidemiological evidence regarding the association between pre‐pregnancy inflammatory status and fertility. We explore the association between the pre‐pregnancy Systemic Inflammation Response Index (SIRI) and the time to pregnancy (TTP) in couples trying to conceive. Method This study included 1739 couples from the National Free Preconception Check‐up Project (NFPCP) in Guangzhou. SIRI was calculated as neutrophil count × monocyte count/lymphocyte count from routine complete blood count (CBC) at baseline. Quartile and continuous variable analysis of SIRI was performed, and restricted cubic spline functions were used to evaluate the dose–response relationship. The associations were adjusted for demographic, behavioural, and lifestyle factors. Results In the NFPCP preconception couple cohort, 1182 pregnancy events were observed. In categorical analyses, women in the highest quartile of SIRI (Q4: 0.99, 5.58) had lower fecundability than those in Q2 (FR, 0.79; 95% CI 0.63, 0.98), indicating a longer TTP. The inverse association became more apparent at SIRI levels above approximately 0.89 in spline‐based analyses. Sensitivity analyses yielded comparable effect estimates after restricting the analysis to live birth outcomes and excluding women with chronic inflammatory co…

title: Preparedness and Response: Law Enforcement Strategies for Post-Disaster Crime Management
abstract: This study examined perceived law enforcement preparedness and problems encountered in managing post-disaster property crimes and public-order concerns in the Second District of Bohol during academic year 2024–2025. A cross-sectional descriptive, comparative, and correlational survey involved a reported 251 personnel from the Philippine National Police, Bureau of Fire Protection, and Philippine Coast Guard. The researcher-made instrument used five-point agreement responses. The supplied summary tables reported preparedness means of 4.42 for property crimes and 4.33 for public-order concerns, with an overall mean of 4.37. Reported problem means were 2.29 and 2.20, respectively, with an overall mean of 2.25. The reported correlation was weak and not statistically significant (r = −.065, p = .307). Aggregate group-comparison results suggested variation by agency and, for problems encountered, length of service, but these results require verification of agency coding, scoring, assumptions, and original statistical output. The findings describe personnel perceptions rather than observed crime-control performance. Proposed actions prioritize communication continuity, resource assessment, joint exercises, and community reporting, supporting SDG 11 through integrated disaster-risk planning. Their effectiveness has not been evaluated.

title: Millimeter-Wave Seed Priming Alters the Rice Root Proteomic Response to Salt Stress
abstract: Salt stress is a major constraint on rice production because it inhibits plant growth and reduces yield. Although millimeter-wave (MMW) seed priming was reported to improve plant performance under environmental stress, the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects remain largely unknown. This study examined whether MMW seed priming improves early rice performance under salt stress and characterized associated changes in the root proteome. Rice seeds were irradiated with MMW, and morphological traits were evaluated under 150 mM NaCl as salt stress for 2 days. Based on morphological results, rice seeds were irradiated with 20 mW for 20 min. Root proteins were analyzed based on the growth responses. Among 6307 proteins analyzed with label-free proteomics, selected proteomic observations were further examined by immunoblotting, gene-expression analysis, and starch measurements. MMW irradiation improved seed germination and alleviated salt-induced inhibition of root growth. Proteomic analysis showed that proteins associated with carbohydrate metabolism and endoplasmic-reticulum function were markedly affected by MMW irradiation. Glutathione reductase and ascorbate peroxidase accumulated under salt stress and further increased following MMW irradiation. Calreticulin and calcium-dependent protein kinase were also increased in abundance by MMW irradiation under salt stress. In additi…

title: Determinants of response to CAR T cell therapy in a multicenter, multi-trial cohort analysis of patients with lymphoma
abstract: Abstract In patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) treated with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, factors associated with efficacy overlap with prognostic biomarkers. Currently, there is no consensus on optimal product characteristics. We analyzed the phenotypic attributes of the anti-CD19 CAR T therapy axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) from 580 patients with NHL across multiple clinical trials with long-term follow-up (median, 41.9 months). A high proportion of naive-like (CCR7 + CD45RA + ) T cells was the most significant feature associated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.31−0.68, P = 9.8 × 10 −5 , high versus low naive-like T cell groups) without impacting safety. The relationship between naive-like T cells and efficacy was independent of tumor microenvironment characteristics (assessed in 112 patients). In multivariate models, the naive-like phenotype outperformed clinicopathologic features such as inflammatory markers and tumor burden, remaining significant after adjusting for product expansion. An inverse correlation was observed between prior lines of therapy and the proportion of naive-like T cells in both product and matched apheresis samples, suggesting a benefit of earlier intervention. The key findings were validated in an independent cohort of 203 patients treated with axi-cel-based ther…

title: Forecasting İstanbul Airport’s Passenger Volume: A Comparative Analysis of Time Series and Machine Learning Models
abstract: The volume of air transportation has increased dramatically thanks to globalization. In this perspective, accurate passenger demand forecasting gained importance for proactive capacity planning, resource allocation, and operational efficiency in the global aviation industry. This study aims to forecast passenger numbers in İstanbul Airport (IST), which is the biggest airport of Türkiye and one of the busiest airports in Europe. To achieve this, two methods, namely SARIMA, which is one of the traditional time series methods and the Prophet, which is a machine learning method, were utilized in a comparative analysis, and forecasts for passenger numbers were made with both methods. The study dataset consists of 89 months of passenger data of İstanbul Airport (from January 2019 to May 2026) and data used by dividing as a training and a test set. Methods’ performances were evaluated using standard error metrics, MAPE and RMSE. The empirical findings reveal that SARIMA outperformed the Prophet model in terms of errors. Although the Prophet performed similarly to SARIMA in regular periods, in irregular periods SARIMA performed much better. For the future, both methods are expecting the continuation of the growth trend of İstanbul Airport’s passenger volume.

title: Data-driven forecasting of Flu, RSV, and COVID-19 related outcomes in the United States and Canada via Hankel dynamic mode decomposition
abstract: The (large) season-to-season variability and limited dynamical history make the forecasting of infectious diseases a challenging problem. Here, we examine the extent to which advances in data-driven dynamical modeling can provide accurate predictions by benchmarking the performance of one such method, Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), on the 2024−2025 influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 seasons in the United States and Canada. Using Hankel-DMD, we generated weekly forecasts that were submitted to the Center for Disease Control and Prevention’s (CDC) FluSight Forecast Hub and the University of Guelph’s AI4CastingHub. Across both Hubs, we find that Hankel-DMD can provide high quality forecasts at the beginning and end of the season, but forecasts in the middle of the season suffer from significant overestimation of the season peak. This leads to worse than baseline performance on FluSight Forecast Hub, when submissions are evaluated across the entire season. Hankel-DMD is found to be the best among a small number of models that submitted enough forecasts against which to compare for forecasting influenza, RSV, and COVID-19 in Canada. As this was the first active year of AI4CastingHub, this suggests that Hankel-DMD may be especially useful when expertise is lacking for predicting infectious dynamics in new regions. To study how Hankel-DMD can be bette…

title: Evaluating machine learning and econometric models for inflation forecasting: evidence from a Sub-Saharan African panel
abstract: Abstract Policymakers in Sub-Saharan Africa increasingly face decisions regarding the adoption of machine learning methods for inflation forecasting, yet these approaches are rarely benchmarked against simple persistence models. This study constructs a reproducible, annual panel of macroeconomic indicators for eight Sub-Saharan African economies (1972–2024, N = 424) to compare eight forecasting approaches: a naive random-walk benchmark, two linear econometric models (pooled OLS and country fixed effects), three machine learning models (Elastic Net, Random Forest, and XGBoost), and a recurrent neural network (LSTM) evaluated with and without early stopping. Using a chronological train/validation/test split and pairwise Diebold–Mariano tests, we evaluate out-of-sample predictive accuracy. The empirical results indicate that no estimated model statistically outperforms the naive persistence baseline. While Random Forest, XGBoost, Elastic Net, and the early-stopped LSTM show no statistically significant difference from the random walk, traditional linear models and the uncorrected LSTM are significantly dominated by it. Although implementing early stopping substantially improves LSTM performance, it does not yield a competitive advantage over simpler tree-based ensembles. These findings align with the well-documented random-walk puzzle in global inflation forecasting, suggesting th…

Temporal trends and comparative forecasting of echinococcosis in endemic Xinjiang (2010–2024): changes during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Abstract Objective To analyze temporal trends of reported echinococcosis cases in Xinjiang from 2010 to 2024 and evaluate the long-horizon out-of-sample forecasting performance of different time series models during the COVID-19 period and subsequent years. Methods Data were sourced from the China Infectious Disease Surveillance and Reporting System. Annual trends were analyzed using Joinpoint regression to calculate Annual Percentage Change (APC) and Average Annual Percentage Change (AAPC). Monthly data were summarized descriptively to characterize monthly reporting patterns. Five forecasting approaches—Naive, Seasonal Naive, SARIMA, Prophet, and LSTM—were trained using 2010–2019 data and evaluated on 2020–2024 data under a common fixed-origin framework, without updating or refitting using observed test-period values. Performance was assessed using root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and symmetric mean absolute percentage error (sMAPE). Expanding-window rolling-origin one-month-ahead forecasting was additionally conducted as a sensitivity analysis. Results A total of 20,302 cases were reported, peaking in 2017 and reaching a low in 2022. title: Short-Term Solar Irradiance Forecasting Using a Dual Gaussian Process Regression-Particle Filter Framework with Limited Meteorological Measurements
abstract: Accurate solar irradiance forecasting can effectively reduce the impact of power fluctuations on the power grid and provide guidance for the control and optimal scheduling of the power system. To address the difficulty of solar irradiance forecasting at sites with limited meteorological measurements, this study proposes a dual Gaussian process regression–particle filter (DGPR-PF) framework. Firstly, a multi-layer correlation analysis method is designed to screen meteorological features while fully considering the coupling relationship between meteorological factors. Secondly, the proposed framework contains two complementary GPR models: a state-transition model that learns the temporal evolution of irradiance from historical irradiance sequences, and an observation model that establishes the nonlinear relationship between irradiance and a small number of available meteorological variables. Temperature and maximum wind speed are selected through multi-layer correlation analysis and used as real-time observations, and a particle filter (PF) recursively fuses the temporal prior generated by the state model with meteorological information from the observation model, thereby correcting irradiance forecasts and reducing the influence of forecasting uncertainty. Finally, the proposed method is validated using the dataset collected by the Yulara Solar System in Australia, and the resul…

title: Through the Looking-Glass of Prices: The Effects of Price Transparency Achieved Through Transition to a Unified Price Indicator
abstract: Price is a universal tool for transmitting information among a great many consumers and producers performing economic calculations. Market prices provide signals that aggregate numerical information about the individual plans of a multitude of strangers acting on tacit and dispersed knowledge. Attempts to replace such spontaneously emerging social self-organization with centralized planning are untenable, as Austrian economists proved during the early twentieth century economic calculation debate. Nevertheless, enthusiasm for regulatory control over pricing is being revived by optimism about modern IT. This article defends the theses that using different sources of price information for a single market is advisable and that the effects of price transparency on competition are ambivalent. Such transparency is misleading because it does not incorporate all the knowledge relevant and necessary for making business decisions. A regulator has illusory control over pricing only by ignoring the heterogeneity of demand for price information while in fact increasing transaction costs for market participants. This article’s methodology is based on Austrian Economics, New Institutional Economics, and Industrial Organization theory. A product differentiation model has been adapted to demonstrate the effects of heterogeneity in demand for price information. Due to differences in the “contrac…

title: CNN–LSTM-Based Spatio-Temporal Forecasting of MNDWI-Derived Coastal States: A Multi-Temporal Landsat Study in Northeastern Brazil
abstract: Abstract Accurate forecasting of shoreline evolution is important for coastal monitoring and management, particularly in dynamic and data-scarce environments. This study investigates a modular framework, applied to Icapuí, northeastern Brazil, that integrates multi-temporal Landsat imagery, remote-sensing-based shoreline extraction, linear regression, and a hybrid convolutional neural network–long short-term memory (CNN–LSTM) architecture. Two distinct Landsat temporal datasets were used for the statistical and deep-learning experiments, and no regression-generated imagery was incorporated into CNN–LSTM training or evaluation. Water–land boundaries were derived from observed Landsat imagery using the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI) followed by binary classification. For spatio-temporal modelling, the CNN–LSTM operated directly on sequences of observed MNDWI rasters to predict the raster corresponding to the subsequent time step. Model performance was evaluated using MAE and RMSE in normalized MNDWI raster-value units, which quantify raster reconstruction error rather than shoreline-position error in physical units. Predicted MNDWI rasters were subsequently converted into binary water–land representations from which vector shorelines were derived for spatial interpretation. Integration of Fuzzy C-Means and Deep Learning for Local Solar Prediction to Optimize Substation Operations in Jakarta
abstract: The increasing integration of Solar Power Plants (SPPs) into urban power grids requires reliable solar resource information and appropriate identification of substations with similar regional characteristics. However, conventional solar irradiance forecasting studies often focus on temporal prediction accuracy without considering substation spatial heterogeneity, which may limit their application to SPP integration planning. This study proposes an integrated spatial-temporal framework that combines Fuzzy C-Means (FCM)-based substation clustering with solar irradiance forecasting to support SPP integration in Jakarta. 62 substations in Jakarta were clustered using FCM based on transformer count, transformer capacity, solar irradiation, temperature, and PV output. The clustering results were evaluated using the Partition Coefficient (PC), Partition Entropy (PE), Davies-Bouldin Index (DBI), and Calinski-Harabasz Index (CHI). Four clusters were identified, with Cluster 2, represented by the Jatiwaringin area, selected as the most stable cluster for further forecasting analysis. Solar irradiance data from Jatiwaringin were subsequently modeled using Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) and a hybrid SARIMA-Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) approach. SARIMA achieved an RMSE of 0.16706, MAE of 0.09932, and MAPE of 1.87%, while the hybrid SARIMA-RNN further improved a…

title: Symptom‐Based Machine Learning Framework for Early Syndrome Coronavirus 2 ( SARS ‐ CoV ‐2) Infection Prediction
abstract: ABSTRACT Early and accurate identification of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection remains a critical challenge, especially in limited‐infrastructure healthcare settings where access to molecular diagnostics is restricted. This study presents a symptom‐based machine learning framework for rapid prediction of COVID‐19 infection using routinely collected clinical indicators. The dataset used in this work is openly accessible at https://redivis.com/datasets/rxta‐4v35cgyz , enabling full transparency and reproducibility. After comprehensive preprocessing, recursive feature elimination with a random forest estimator identified nine key predictors, including SpO 2 , fever, loss of smell/taste, shortness of breath, dry cough, fatigue, age, diabetes status, and respiratory rate. Multiple supervised learning algorithms—logistic regression, SVM, k‐NN, decision tree, random forest, and a stacked ensemble—were trained and evaluated using 10‐fold cross‐validation. The stacked ensemble model outperformed all baseline classifiers, achieving an accuracy of 0.87, balanced sensitivity (0.88) and specificity (0.86), and the lowest error rate (0.12), demonstrating strong robustness and generalization by leveraging complementary strengths of the base learners. The proposed framework is computationally lightweight, delivers prediction times under 50 ms, and is suitable for deployment in real‐time clinical decision‐…

title: DPMF: Dual-Path Multi-timescale Fusion with Phenology-Gated Prediction for Tomato State and Daily Water-Nutrient Flux Estimation
abstract: Full-cycle management of greenhouse tomato requires continuous information on crop state together with estimates of daily water and nutrient use, yet destructive biomass measurements are sparse, and a single fixed model shared across resources is prone to stage-dependent negative transfer. This study proposes Dual-Path Multi-timescale Fusion (DPMF), a development-aware framework for reconstructing crop state from sparse observations and estimating daily resource fluxes. The state path combines a process-based dry-matter prior with a gated recurrent unit trained on three kinds of supervision: point states, biomass increments between adjacent samples, and cumulative harvested-fruit dry matter. The resource path uses smooth phenology gating to weight task-specific and shared ExtraTrees predictions across six crop-development stages, so that information is shared between resources only where sharing does not degrade accuracy. On 64 destructive samples from seven light-temperature treatments, DPMF achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of $132.821\,\mathrm{g\,m^{-2}}$ and a mean absolute error (MAE) of $65.246\,\mathrm{g\,m^{-2}}$, 6.09% and 5.31% lower in RMSE than interpolation-based and point-only supervision, respectively. Machine Learning Prediction of Treatment Failure After Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization for Subdural Hematoma
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) is effective for chronic subdural hematoma (SDH), but failure rates vary and risk prediction tools are lacking. This study developed and validated a machine learning (ML) model to predict MMAE treatment failure for SDH. METHODS: We conducted an international, multi-institutional retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent MMAE for SDH between 2019 and 2025. The cohort was split into training and test sets, stratified by treatment failure, with all hematomas from each patient assigned to a single cohort to prevent data leakage. Multiple ML algorithms were evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation, with gradient boosting selected as the final model. The primary outcome was treatment failure, defined as rescue surgical evacuation or persistent/recurrent SDH requiring retreatment. Model performance was assessed using area under the curve-receiver operating characteristic. Patients were stratified into low-risk (<5%), medium-risk (5%-15%), and high-risk (>15%) groups using a priori clinically defined thresholds. RESULTS: Among 692 treated hematomas in the test cohort, 64 (9.2%) experienced treatment failure. The gradient boosting model achieved an area under the curve-receiver operating characteristic of 0.856 (95% CI, 0.803-0.902) before calibration and 0.832 (95% CI, 0.766-0.889) after isotonic calibrati…

Crime, Causes of Crime, and Criminal Investigation in NigeriaA Critical Narrative Review of Investigative Capacity and Institutional Coordination
abstract: Crime prevention and criminal investigation involve related but distinct problems: explaining offending does not establish how an allegation becomes reliable evidence. This critical narrative review examines that relationship in Nigeria through Social Disorganization Theory and Routine Activity Theory. The synthesis draws on a purposively selected corpus of 16 sources comprising two theoretical works, five contemporary empirical studies, two statutes, six official institutional documents or webpages, and one official survey summary. A targeted supplementary search undertaken on October 19, 2026, prioritised research published from 2020 to 2026 and authoritative materials relevant to institutional responsibilities. Five themes organise the analysis: structural vulnerability, changing evidence requirements, investigative capacity, forensic and digital capability, and governance and coordination. The evidence supports attention to training, information integrity, and organisational arrangements, while its geographical and methodological limitations prevent nationwide estimates of investigative performance or causal claims about reform effectiveness. The article proposes an evidence continuity framework connecting reporting, preservation, analysis, inter-agency transfer, and prosecutorial review. title: Вопросы выбора критериев оценки современных крупнотоннажных судов ледового плавания на стадии концептуального проектирования
abstract: Создание крупнотоннажных судов ледового плавания, способных круглогодично работать в Арктике, является приоритетным направлением развития транспорта РФ и эффективным средством решения проблемы увеличения грузопотока по трассам Северного морского пути. На стадии концептуального проектирования таких судов в качестве критерия оценки их эффективности при эксплуатации во льдах очень часто прибегают к использованию ледового класса. На основе выбора ледового класса формулируют требования к ледопроходимости, пропульсивной мощности, форме обводов корпуса, типу движительно-рулевого комплекса, а также устанавливают необходимость привлечения ледоколов для организации проводки. В работе показано, что такой подход к определению облика проектируемого крупнотоннажного судна на стадии формулирования технических требований имеет ряд существенных недостатков, которые приводят либо к удорожанию постройки судна ввиду применения значительных ледовых подкреплений корпуса и мощного движительно-рулевого комплекса при завышении класса, либо к увеличению стоимости его эксплуатации в связи с необходимостью обеспечения безопасности плавания за счёт привлечения ледоколов для организации проводки на протяжённых участках трасс Северного морского пути. Подробно рассмотрены основные аспекты аналитической работы, результаты которой могут быть использованы для определения технических требований к проектированию с…

INSTITUTIONAL CAPITAL AND FISCAL CAPACITY IN OVERCOMING DISBALANCES: EVIDENCE FROM ESTIMATED EQUATIONS
abstract: This article investigates the role of institutional capital and fiscal capacity in overcoming macroeconomic disbalances during post-conflict recovery in Ukraine. We evaluate the impact of institutional and fiscal effectors on macroeconomic stabilisation and derive policy proposals from our dynamic models. Literature treats institutional quality as an endogenous variable, difficult to operationalise for medium-term policy. We extract institutional capital as a latent principal component from observable indicators, introducing it into a nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag model with an error correction term. The novelty lies in quantifying the delay between institutional changes and macroeconomic responses. Factor analysis reveals that institutional capital quality (PC5) explains 6.9 % of the variance, whereas state fiscal capacity (PC2) explains 14.6 %. Despite its smaller share, PC5 emerges as a central driver of real GDP growth. Our estimation demonstrates that PC5 at a two-year lag has a significant positive coefficient on real GDP growth (+5.7799). This lets us claim that institutional reforms yield macroeconomic dividends with a two-year delay. The marginal return of the GDP growth circuit to PC5 is +2.64, second only to structural modernisation. The model reveals a tradeoff, since institutional capital enters the trade balance and inflation circuits negatively. Conver…

title: Inspiratory muscle strength and skeletal muscle mass are associated with postoperative functional exercise capacity after lung cancer surgery
abstract: Although surgical resection is the cornerstone of curative treatment for early-stage lung cancer, patients often experience postoperative declines in physical fitness and skeletal muscle mass, resulting in reduced exercise capacity, which is associated with prognosis. This study aimed to identify clinical factors associated with postoperative functional exercise capacity, as measured by the incremental shuttle walk test, in patients undergoing lung cancer surgery. This retrospective study included 62 subjects (mean age, 67 ± 8.7 years; 24 women and 38 men) who underwent lung cancer surgery and completed a postoperative assessment at 3 months. Functional exercise capacity was assessed using the incremental shuttle walking distance (ISWD) as the primary outcome. Correlation and regression analyses were conducted to examine the associations between ISWD and concurrent measures of forced expiratory volume in 1 second, forced vital capacity, maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP), maximal expiratory pressure, and skeletal muscle index (SMI). At 3 months postoperatively, ISWD was negatively correlated with age ( r = −0.354, P = .005) and positively correlated with SMI ( r = 0.253, P = .048) and predicted MIP (%; r = 0.293, P = .02), whereas other pulmonary function parameters were not significantly associated with ISWD. title: Bearing capacity attenuation and energy response of end-anchored bodies under dynamic disturbance with different frequencies
abstract: Dynamic disturbances significantly impact the stability of end-anchored systems, yet their bearing capacity attenuation and energy response evolution remain poorly understood. This study investigated sandstone end-anchored specimens with anchorage lengths of 300 mm and 600 mm. By conducting comparative static pull-out tests and pull-out tests following sinusoidal cyclic disturbances via a custom-designed apparatus, coupled with Particle Flow Code 2D (PFC 2D ) numerical simulations, the capacity attenuation, energy dissipation, and internal damage evolution were analyzed. Results reveal a negative correlation between bearing capacity and disturbance frequency. Low-frequency (10 Hz) disturbances cause severe damage, triggering extensive interfacial debonding, whereas 50–200 Hz disturbances induce highly localized damage. The failure process involves elastic, slip, debonding-slip, and complete detachment stages, governed by a tensile-shear mode. This is characterized by axial debonding along the cable-anchoring agent interface and radial or oblique tensile micro-cracking within the anchoring agent. Low-frequency energy propagates efficiently over long distances and continuously accumulates, whereas high-frequency energy dissipates rapidly. Furthermore, extending the anchorage length to 600 mm effectively enhances system rigidity and dynamic resistance. Numerical simulations confir…

title: Coexisting nickel ions enhance tungstate removal by calcium-aluminum layered double hydroxide: Characteristics and synergistic mechanism
abstract: Tungsten (W) and nickel (Ni) have divergent chemical properties and coexist in some industrial wastewater, making their simultaneous removal a significant challenge. In this study, a nitrate-intercalated CaAl-layered double hydroxide (CaAl-LDH) with high purity and crystallinity was synthesized using the microwave-assisted method for the removal of tungstate (WO 4 2− ) and nickel (Ni 2+ ) ions in single and/or binary systems. In single systems, low concentrations of WO 4 2− (20–100 mg W/L) resulted in low removal efficiency and rapid dissolution of the LDH, forming CaWO 4 colloids, while high concentrations of WO 4 2− (1000 mg/L) led to the formation of large and easily filterable CaWO 4 precipitates. Such a dissolution-precipitation process is responsible for the high removal amount of ∼1000 mg/g. In binary systems, the presence of Ni 2+ significantly enhanced the removal of WO 4 2− ; for instance, 100 mg/L Ni 2+ enabled the complete removal of WO 4 2− , increasing the amount of W removed from 40 to ∼210 mg/g. Similarly, WO 4 2− promoted Ni 2+ removal (increasing the removal capacity from 350 to 406 mg/g), though this effect was itself concentration-dependent. Oxyanions inhibited WO 4 2− removal by competing for Ca 2+ ; however, in ternary systems containing Ni 2+ , they unexpectedly promoted WO 4 2− removal. Solid characterization confirmed that WO 4 2− was mainly removed by …

Etching mechanism of β -Ga2O3 in BCl3/Ar inductively coupled plasma reactive ion etching
abstract: We report on the study of the etching mechanism of beta gallium oxide (β-Ga2O3) through the inductively coupled plasma reactive-ion etching (ICP RIE) mechanism using chloride (BCl3/Ar) based plasma. We primarily focus on the mechanism of etching of β-Ga2O3 using BCl3/Ar plasma. The samples were etched for different ICP and RF powers. The obtained results help understand the different mechanisms that are responsible for etching gallium oxide. We found different limiting mechanisms under various RF and ICP powers. We also report on the mechanism of an intermediate heterogeneous complex formation that helps in the etching of gallium oxide. Furthermore, a 4 μm deep trench was etched to show the efficacy of the recipe. The study presented in this report will help better understand the etching mechanism in β-Ga2O3, which is still at a very nascent stage, and help in fabricating power devices with high aspect ratio trenches.

title: Cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic syndrome: novel molecular mechanism and glucagon-like peptide-1-targeting therapy
abstract: Cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents a systemic disease continuum arising from the progressive and reciprocal interactions among metabolic dysfunction, kidney injury, and cardiovascular disease. Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are major metabolic drivers of early CKM progression and contribute to cardiac and kidney injury through insulin resistance, glucotoxicity and lipotoxicity, chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and ectopic lipid deposition, thereby establishing a self-reinforcing vicious cycle across the metabolic, cardiovascular, and renal systems. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and its receptor (GLP-1R) not only participate in the regulation of glucose homeostasis and energy metabolism but also represent an important regulatory nexus linking metabolic dysfunction to cardiorenal injury. GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) improve metabolic homeostasis by enhancing glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppressing glucagon release, reducing appetite and body weight, and decreasing visceral and ectopic fat accumulation. In parallel, they may exert renal and cardiovascular protective effects by improving endothelial function and microcirculation, suppressing inflammation and oxidative stress, maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis, and attenuating fibrosis. In recent years, large-scale clinical studies have furthe…

abstract: Purpose: Loss of digital leverage can severely disrupt inverted pendulum mechanics and alter how mechanical work is distributed during walking. The biomechanical efficacy of prosthetic footwear in individuals with bilateral toe amputation remains poorly understood. This exploratory single-case study quantified the effects of custom prosthetic footwear on pendular recovery, mechanical work distribution, and functional mobility in a 52-year-old male with complete bilateral digital amputation (metatarsals preserved), while evaluating intervention effects relative to concurrent walking speed changes. Methods: Three-dimensional kinematic data were collected during barefoot and prosthetic footwear walking across 13 consecutive stride cycles (7 barefoot, 6 shod). Functional speed restoration was evaluated via the Locomotor Rehabilitation Index (LRI). Unadjusted condition differences were evaluated using Hedges’ g with bootstrap confidence intervals. To isolate intervention effects from walking velocity, a single-case multiple linear regression model incorporating a first-order autoregressive error structure [AR(1)] evaluated speed-adjusted intervention effects (β1) centered at grand mean speed (1.14 m/s). Results: Walking speed increased substantially from 0.88 ± 0.08 m/s barefoot (range: 0.76–0.98 m/s) to 1.45 ± 0.05 m/s with footwear (range: 1.38–1.52 m/s; Hedges’ g = 7.78), restori…

Shell-resolved causal mechanism of K-point bandgap: first-order valley-Hall opening and higher-order shell dominance in rotating photonic crystals
abstract: The rotational robustness of valley photonic crystal bandgaps is conventionally attributed to C 3 symmetry persistence, yet the microscopic mechanism linking rotation to gap evolution remains unclear. We perform a shell-resolved causal analysis of K-point bandgap formation in rotating triangular-hole valley Hall photonic crystals. By selectively freezing individual Fourier shells in the plane-wave expansion and measuring the resulting gap change, we identify that the fourth Fourier shell (shell 4, | G | a /2 π = 3.46) dominates the gap’s rotational variation, with causal efficacy 16 times larger than the first shell. Perturbation analysis reveals that the K-point gap opens through a first-order valley-Hall mechanism driven by inversion-symmetry breaking, with its first-order origin set by the first-shell Fourier component, whereas across the rotation scan the gap is strongly anticorrelated with the first-shell amplitude (r 2 = 0.999), pointing to higher-order shells as the source of its angular variation. The gap’s angular variation is causally dominated by shell 4 ( R 4 = 3.43), with intermediate shells collectively dominating. A Löwdin perturbation framework qualitatively explains this intermediate-shell dominance through the competition between the squared matrix element | ε ( G s )| 2 and the energy denominator G s 2 . Single- and multi-shell intervention reveals a sub-addi…

title: CO 2 emission and microbial community dynamics in soybean farmland under different organic material returning
abstract: Abstract Fertilization not only influences crop productivity but also plays a pivotal role in regulating soil CO 2 emissions within agricultural ecosystems. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanisms governing soil CO 2 emissions under different fertilization regimes in the Northeast China Black Soil Region. Field experiments were conducted using four treatments: mineral fertilizer (NPK), and NPK combined with biochar (NPK + BC), organic fertilizer (NPK + OF) or straw (NPK + SF). A comprehensive assessment was performed, including measurements of soil CO 2 flux, physicochemical properties, microbial community composition, plant physiological traits and crop yield. The results showed that, compared with the CK, soybean yields significantly increased by 10.00%, 8.15% and 3.70% under NPK + BC, NPK + OF and NPK + SF, respectively. Regarding mature stage soil properties, NPK + BC, NPK + OF and NPK + SF significantly elevated soil organic matter (SOM) by 16.30%, 23.86% and 1.39%, meanwhile available phosphorus (AP) by 19.76%, 24.00% and 6.78%, respectively. CO 2 flux was reduced by 24.66% in NPK + BC but increased by 41.34% in NPK + OF. Furthermore, fertilization significantly altered microbial diversity; the ACE index increased by 7.82% under NPK + BC in the mature stage. abstract: Silica–carbon briquettes enable the incorporation of fine-grained silica-bearing materials and carbonaceous reductants into the charge used for ferrosilicon smelting. This study examines the composition of the composite disclosed in Patent of the Republic of Kazakh-stan No. 38264, the results of X-ray diffraction analysis of the briquette, and the chemical composition of ferrosilicon samples sequentially collected during the experimental smelting campaign. According to the patent data, the composite contained 41.41% fixed carbon, while the ash content was 39.38% on a dry basis, and the SiO2 content in the mineral fraction was 90–92%. The first addition of briquettes was recorded at tapping No. 17. However, the exact timing of the corresponding metal sample collection relative to briquette charging is unknown; therefore, this sample was excluded from the comparison between the two operating periods. In samples Nos. 10–16, the Si content ranged from 74.75 to 76.21 wt.%, whereas in samples Nos. 18–24, it ranged from 75.49 to 76.47 wt.%. title: Carbon nanodots as modulators of growth, physiological and biochemical responses in forage pea (Pisum sativum L.)
abstract: Forage pea (Pisum sativum L.) is an important cool-season legume forage crop, and improving its early vegetative performance is of practical interest. In this study, we investigated the dose-dependent effects of carbon nanodots (CDs) on growth, photosynthetic pigments, and oxidative stress-related biomarkers in forage pea seedlings. We grew seedlings in soil and applied CDs exogenously via foliar spray (20 mL per pot) at 100, 200, and 300 ppm three times at 3-day intervals, with measurements made 14 days after the first application. Each treatment consisted of three pots, with four seedlings per pot. Root and leaf lengths, chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, total chlorophyll, proline, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and malondialdehyde (MDA) contents were determined. CDs treatment resulted in statistically significant differences in root and leaf length. Root length increased from 5.14 cm in the control to 8.50 cm at 300 ppm, whereas leaf length showed the highest numerical value at 100 ppm (1.80 cm) compared with 1.34 cm in the control. Root H2O2 content increased relative to the control (1.555 µmol g⁻¹ FW), with the highest level observed at 200 ppm, while leaf H2O2 decreased with increasing CD concentration from the control value of 1.810 µmol g-1 FW. MDA responses were tissue- and concentration-dependent, with the highest root MDA content recorded at 300 ppm (0.275 nmol g⁻¹ FW) and th…

title: Regio‐Selective Electrocatalysis in Single‐Wall Carbon Nanotubes: Platinum Inside for Hydrogen Evolution Reaction/Hydrogen Oxidation Reaction and Ruthenium Outside for Oxygen Evolution Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing selective and durable electrocatalysts remains a key challenge for the development of electrolyzers and unitized regenerative fuel cells (URFCs). Herein, we explore a novel approach toward specific reactions in water splitting, where one of the catalysts (Pt) is confined inside single‐wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) for specific hydrogen evolution/oxidation reaction (HER/HOR), while the second catalyst (Ru/RuO x ) is located outside the SWCNTs for specific oxygen evolution reaction (OER), yielding a Pt@SWCNT@Ru catalyst with spatially separated inner and outer active sites. Encapsulation within SWCNTs also enhances Fe 3+ tolerance compared to Pt/C. Long‐term chronoamperometry reveals stable HER currents over 84 h and distinct Ru activation/decay kinetics over 72 h under acidic OER, while inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy shows no detectable Pt or Ru dissolution, indicating that spatial separation of Pt is likely to be preserved. These findings establish Pt@SWCNT@Ru as a proof‐of‐concept platform for spatially resolved, multifunctional electrodes relevant to next‑generation URFC architectures.

title: Microbially mediated interactions between enhanced weathering and carbon inputs shift soil organic carbon dynamics
abstract: Abstract Enhanced weathering, adding crushed silicate minerals to soils, is being explored as a way to draw down atmospheric carbon dioxide, but its effects on soil organic carbon remain uncertain. We show that olivine amendments change soil carbon cycling depending on time and on labile carbon availability. In a 55-week soil microcosm experiment, adding olivine alone reduces total soil organic carbon. Adding olivine with glucose initially suppresses microbial carbon uptake, but by week 55 instead boosts microbial biomass and mineral-associated organic matter more than glucose alone, while lowering respiratory carbon loss. These late-stage gains grow stronger alongside geochemical signs of mineral weathering. Nanoscale imaging shows that newly formed soil organic carbon accumulates within pre-existing organic and mineral microsites rather than directly on olivine or newly formed clay surfaces. Our findings suggest that when labile carbon is available, enhanced weathering can increase soil carbon storage primarily through microbial processing, rather than by creating new mineral surfaces for carbon to bind to.

title: Integration of sociomathematical norms in problem-based learning on social arithmetic material for junior high school based on economic sustainable development goals
abstract: Purpose – This study explored junior high school mathematics teachers’ experiences and pedagogical readiness in integrating Problem-Based Learning (PBL), sociomathematical norms (SMN), and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into Social Arithmetic instruction, addressing limited understanding of their role in mathematical discourse and sustainable economic literacy. Methodology – A qualitative phenomenological study involved 12 purposively selected mathematics teachers in Kuningan Regency, Indonesia. Data were collected through in-depth interviews and analyzed using Bogdan and Biklen’s procedures, including data reduction, categorization, thematic interpretation, and verification. Findings – Teachers demonstrated limited understanding of SMN, particularly in distinguishing mathematical justification, explanation, and solution efficiency from general classroom behavior. Although PBL was reportedly implemented, instruction remained predominantly procedural, with insufficient opportunities for mathematical discussion, negotiation, and solution evaluation. Social Arithmetic teaching emphasized technical calculations rather than authentic economic decision-making and sustainability contexts. abstract: ABSTRACT Nanofluidic systems hold great promise for water treatment and blue energy harvesting. However, fabricating natural‐based nanofluidic materials that simultaneously deliver tunable channel orientation, high charge density, and robust mechanical at scale remains challenging. Herein, we demonstrate a wood nanofluidic platform enabled by ionic nano‐engineering of the wood cell wall, involving ionized cell‐wall scaffold reconstruction and in situ nanopolymer polymerization. Periodate oxidation followed by Schiff‐base coupling grafts positively charged ─NH 2 functionalities onto the cellulose skeleton, converting oxidized wood from negatively charged (ζ = −16.5 mV) to positively charged (ζ = +33.5 mV). Subsequent in situ nano‐polymerization rebuilds a 3D gel network within the cell wall, enriching charge density while creating additional nanochannels and interconnecting previously isolated pores. This strategy of structure regulation, interface modification, and functional assembly that overcomes the intrinsic “fiber‐aligned transport” limitation of wood. As a result, the obtained cationic wood membrane (C‐WM) and anionic wood membrane (A‐WM) deliver tensile strengths of 11.7 and 13.1 MPa, respectively, and exhibit high ionic conductivities of 2.24 × 10 −3 and 1.65 × 10 −3 S cm −1 in dilute electrolytes. title: Trade Costs, Regional Integration, and Bilateral Exports in Asian Landlocked Developing Countries: A PPML Gravity Analysis
abstract: Landlocked developing countries (LLDCs) face persistent trade-cost disadvantages arising from distance, transit dependence, border frictions, and uneven logistics performance. This study reconstructs bilateral merchandise exports for 11 Asian LLDCs to a common set of 50 large importing markets over 2010–2024 and evaluates export correlates using Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood (PPML) gravity models. The trade-eligible sample comprises 6800 exporter–importer–year observations, including 993 source-validated constructed zeros; source-missing observations are not treated as zeros. Models progress from a conventional gravity benchmark with year fixed effects to pair-fixed-effects specifications and structural gravity with exporter–year, importer–year, and pair fixed effects; standard errors are clustered by dyad. The conventional benchmark finds positive exporter and importer gross domestic product (GDP) coefficients and a negative distance coefficient. Logistics Performance Index coefficients are not robustly significant after introducing pair fixed effects. Bilateral effectively applied tariff coefficients are generally negative but not significant at the 5% level. Normal-Mode-Based Nudged Band (NM-NEB) Method: Retrieving Potential Energy Surface Information from Local Hessians to Improve Transition State Search
abstract: Abstract Traditional nudged elastic band (NEB) methods often yield unphysical initial paths due to the lack of curvature information from the potential energy surface (PES). To overcome this limitation, we propose a Normal-Mode-based NEB (NM-NEB) method that only leverages Hessian matrices of reactant and product minima. Key PES information is extracted from the local Hessian matrices of reactants and products via frequency calculations, and dominant reaction modes are identified using a Franck–Condon factor-based vibrational mode matching strategy. By displacing reactants and products along these modes, we obtain two improved end points near the true transition state, from which a physically reasonable initial path is constructed. Validation on 20 diverse benchmark reactions at the B3LYP-D3/6–31G* level shows that NM-NEB achieves stable convergence where Cartesian- and internal coordinate-NEB fail, with geometric and energy errors within 0.1 Å and 1.0 kcal/mol, respectively. The mode-guided path also reduces optimization iterations and avoids unphysical artifacts inherent in traditional interpolation. By leveraging only local Hessian information at the end point minima, this strategy achieves robust and efficient transition state search and provides a promising approach for medium-to-large systems, with its reliability fully validated on 20 diverse small-molecule benchmark rea…

title: Charge‐State‐Controlled Surface Modifiers for High‐Voltage and Stable Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT For wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide perovskites, quasi‐two‐dimensional (quasi‐2D) surface reconstruction using bulky‐cation spacers is widely employed to passivate surface defects and disrupt halide migration pathways. Nevertheless, under operational stress, conventional ammonium‐based spacers can undergo deprotonation, destabilizing the low‐dimensional surface layer and weakening its function. Herein, we report an organic‐spacer charge‐state control strategy for the surface modification of Cs 0.2 FA 0.8 PbI 1.8 Br 1.2 wide‐bandgap perovskites. This strategy involves combining octylammonium (OA) with N ‐methylsulfanilic acid (NMSA) to form NMSAO, a charge‐neutralized ammonium–sulfonate modifier state. This configuration induces an associated Ruddlesden–Popper‐like quasi‐2D phase at the perovskite surface that suppresses trap‐mediated recombination, facilitates interfacial charge extraction, and disrupts halide‐ion migration pathways. As a result, the NMSAO‐treated perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.83% and an open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 1.326 V, compared with 17.30% and 1.197 V for the untreated control PSCs. Furthermore, the NMSAO‐treated PSCs retain 93.59% of their initial PCE after 500 h of continuous illumination under ISOS‐L‐1 conditions and more than 93% after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C. title: Mitigating electrical discharge damage in EV bearings: A critical review from inverter design to bio-based greases
abstract: Abstract Research on electric vehicles (EVs) has gained increasing attention due to the global transition toward cleaner and more sustainable transportation. However, ensuring the efficiency, reliability and long-term durability of EV drivetrains remains a major challenge. In EV bearings, inverter-induced shaft voltage and bearing currents can trigger electrical discharge across the lubricating film when the local electric field exceeds the dielectric strength of the grease. These discharge events can result in surface damage and lubricant degradation, leading to premature bearing failure and affecting the motor reliability. This review critically discusses the mechanisms of electrical discharge damage in EV bearings and reviews recent mitigation strategies including motor and inverter design optimisation, bearing materials and surface engineering, and specialised lubricant formulation. This review further discusses the development of bio-based greases for EV bearing applications, including formulation requirements, bio-based oil selection, thickener system design and additive strategies. The key challenge is to balance conductivity, dielectric stability, tribofilm formation, and grease durability under coupled mechanical, thermal, and electrical stresses. Overall, this review provides a framework for developing high-performance bio-based EV bearing greases that can mitigate el…

title: Immunoinformatics and reverse vaccinology design of self-amplifying RNA vaccine against marburg virus with structural dynamics and immune simulation analysis
abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD), a deadly zoonotic illness in humans, is caused by the Marburg virus (MARV), a single-stranded RNA virus belonging to the Orthomarburgvirus genus of the Filoviridae family. There are currently no approved vaccines or efficient antiviral therapies for MARV, despite high morbidity and fatality rates of the virus, particularly in Africa. Recognizing its epidemic potential and its inclusion on the WHO list of blueprint priority pathogens, an immunoinformatics approach was used to design novel multi-epitope saRNA vaccine candidates (MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII) targeting the viral GP, NP, VP40, and VP35 via CD8 + , CD4 + , and B cell epitopes. These epitopes were derived from target protein sequences and incorporated into MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII after validation for antigenicity, non-allergenicity, non-toxicity, and conservation. Additionally, the selected epitopes were conjugated to suitable adjuvants via various linkers, thereby enabling the design of a potentially stable vaccine. Additionally, the designed MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were incorporated into the standard saRNA model, in which ORF-2 encodes the target vaccine peptide. Moreover, biophysical analyses unveiled that the developed vaccines are basic (pI < 7), soluble (GRAVY < 0), and stable (aliphatic index < 80). title: Boron nutrition in horticultural crops for enhancing yield and fruit quality
abstract: Boron (B) is an essential micronutrient involved in reproductive development, fruit growth, yield formation, and quality of horticultural crops. It contributes to cell wall integrity, membrane function, carbohydrate transport, pollen germination and pollen tube growth, fruit set, and nutrient translocation. B availability influences reproductive development, yield, and fruit quality, with both deficiency and excess adversely affecting crop performance, while optimal B nutrition can promote fruit development and quality. However, B responses vary considerably with crop species and cultivar, initial B status, application rate and source, and environmental conditions. This review critically examines the physiological and biochemical roles of B and the proposed mechanisms underlying its effects in horticultural crops, with emphasis on reproductive development, yield, fruit quality, and postharvest performance. It evaluates variability and limitations in the available evidence, particularly dose- and crop-dependent responses, and critically assesses the emerging use of nano-boron, including concerns related to phytotoxicity, environmental safety, nanoparticle stability, economic feasibility, and limited field validation. Although nano-boron has shown promising potential, current evidence remains insufficient to establish its consistent superiority over conventional B sources across …

title: Woody root and shoot xylem anatomy reveal patterns of whole-plant axial variation and suggest structure-function tradeoffs
abstract: Abstract Plants must balance multiple functions across their large woody bodies, including water transport, biomechanical support, and storage. While vessel diameters within woody shoots have been intensively studied, woody roots compose a substantial portion of the plant body and remain comparatively understudied. Moreover, little is known about axial variation in xylem fibers and parenchyma. We excavated root systems of six Populus balsamifera L. spp. trichocarpa trees and examined xylem traits at 1-m increments from root tip to shoot tip. At each sampled location we measured several anatomical and functional traits. Anatomical traits included the percentage area of vessels, fibers, secondary wall area, and parenchyma; fiber diameter and wall thickness; vessel element diameter, wall thickness, and length; and inter-vessel pit area and density. Hydraulic functional traits included hydraulic conductivity and embolism resistance. Vessel diameter increased from organ apices toward the root-shoot junction in both roots and shoots, reaching maximum values in older root tissues. Model comparison strongly favored piecewise regressions over a single power-law relationship reflecting the inability of a single global scaling relationship to capture the pronounced structural transitions between root and shoot tissues. Axial trends for other traits differed between roots and shoots, resul…

title: Virtual Reality for Delirium Prevention in Intensive Care Unit Nurses and Mechanically Ventilated Patients: Descriptive Qualitative Study
abstract: Abstract Background Patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) who are on mechanical ventilation are at high risk of developing delirium. Virtual reality (VR) technology, as an emerging intervention method, shows promising application prospects in delirium prevention, but its specific experience in clinical practice still requires in-depth exploration. Objective This study aims to explore the real experiences of ICU nurses and mechanically ventilated patients in participating in VR delirium prevention, with the aim of providing practical evidence for the optimization and application of this technology in clinical practice. Methods A descriptive qualitative research design was adopted. From March to June 2025, using purposive sampling, participants were selected from the internal medicine, surgery, central, and respiratory ICU departments of a tertiary hospital in Zhengzhou. A total of 73 patients on mechanical ventilation were screened. Among them, 49 were excluded due to not meeting the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) or Barthel Index (BI) score criteria, 5 had delirium at the time of enrollment, 1 was excluded due to visual impairment, and 2 voluntarily withdrew during the study. Finally, 16 patients on mechanical ventilation and 16 nurses were included for semistructured interviews. Data analysis was conducted using the inductive content analysis method. Results Thro…

title: Better Late than Never: The Impact of Hatching Time on Heterodera schachtii Parasitism
abstract: Plant-parasitic nematodes are a diverse group collectively capable of infecting most major crops. Among the most damaging are the cyst nematodes, which can remain dormant in the soil for decades as infection-competent, developmentally arrested, second-stage juveniles in eggs. Hatching is stimulated by a variety of factors. However, the impact of hatching factor responsiveness on nematode morphology, physiology, gene expression, and infection biology has not been explored. We examined the impact of hatching time on the beet cyst nematode, Heterodera schachtii . We found that late hatchers invaded host roots and established feeding sites in greater numbers than early hatchers. We demonstrate variation in baseline parasitism gene expression and in responsiveness of genes to effectostimulins—small, plant-derived molecules that upregulate parasitism genes. Three quarters of effectostimulin-induced transcriptional changes were also modulated, either positively or negatively, by hatching time. Although there were no observable morphological differences between early- and late-hatching nematodes on their day of hatching, the late hatchers displayed signs of faster utilization of internal energy reserves after 7 days at 4°C, as evidenced by less body area attributed to fat, than early hatchers. Finally, we found no evidence of substantive genetic differences between early and late hatch…

title: Spatial variation in morphological traits of natural Haloxylon ammodendron populations on the eastern margin of the Badain Jaran Desert
abstract: Abstract Spatially explicit information on morphological variation within natural Haloxylon ammodendron populations remains limited. We examined size‐associated morphological and spatial variation in a natural population on the eastern margin of the Badain Jaran Desert. Plant height, crown diameter, and stem‐base diameter were measured for 1,151 individuals. Based on the lower and upper quartiles of stem‐base diameter, individuals were classified into small, intermediate, and large stem‐base diameter classes. Descriptive statistics and geostatistical analyses were used to characterize morphological variation and model spatial dependence. Mean plant height and crown diameter increased across the small, intermediate, and large stem‐base diameter classes. The interpolated maps showed spatial variation in all measured traits. Plant height and crown diameter exhibited partially similar spatial patterns, whereas stem‐base diameter showed a different spatial pattern. The fitted semivariogram parameters also differed among traits and diameter classes. The observed differences represent size‐associated morphological and spatial variation rather than independently validated age‐dependent changes. Because soil moisture, groundwater depth, local topography, wind fields, and plant interactions were not directly measured, the environmental mechanisms underlying the observed patterns remain u…

title: Nitrogen enrichment favors homeostatic plants whereas mowing benefits plastic plants: evidence from the elemental composition in a meadow steppe
abstract: Abstract Plant elemental composition and stoichiometry, central to ecological function, are strongly influenced by global change drivers like nitrogen (N) deposition and land-use practices such as mowing. However, a holistic understanding of how multi-elemental composition (i.e., biogeochemical niches) mediate species-specific responses to these drivers remains limited. We conducted a decade-long field experiment in a meadow steppe, subjecting two dominant species, Leymus chinensis (a grass) and Carex duriuscula (a sedge), to N addition and mowing treatment. We quantified foliar concentrations of nine elements (K, Ca, Na, Mg, Al, Fe, Mn, Cu, Zn) to characterize their biogeochemical niches and stoichiometric homeostasis. Our results revealed that the resource-conservative L. chinensis maintained high stoichiometric homeostasis and a stable biogeochemical niche size and hypervolume under N addition, correlating with increased biomass. In contrast, the resource acquisitive species C. duriuscula showed greater plasticity, and mowing induced a significant change in its foliar element biogeochemical niche size and hypervolume, which were positively correlated with its biomass. Random forest analysis identified biogeochemical niche characteristics as a key driver of biomass for C. duriuscula but not for L. chinensis, where N addition and light availability were more critical. This stu…

title: Resourcing Trust: How Power and Precarity Shape Nonprofit Funding Experiences
abstract: Abstract Nonprofits face challenges securing adequate and sustained funding, marked by resource constraints and power imbalances between funders and grantees. Using a constructivist grounded theory approach, we interviewed nonprofit leaders to examine funding relationships from grantees’ perspectives. Our study was situated in the Northern Canadian context, where nonprofits often operate in small, resource-constrained, and geographically dispersed communities. Drawing on Resource Dependency Theory, we interpreted how power and resource control shaped participants’ experiences. Four core themes emerged: community and relationship-centered practices, application and reporting make-work, transactional relationships and power, and operational and administrative support. We also explored the relevance of trust-based philanthropy (TBP), an emerging funding model with limited empirical attention. Our findings show alignment with and gaps in TBP practices, prompting development of an empirically grounded framework that extends understanding of nonprofit funding relationships and refines interpretations of TBP and resource dependence in constrained funding environments. From these findings, we offer practical guidance for more equitable funding systems.

title: Scarcity‐Weighted Virtual Water, Sustainable Economic Growth and Productivity: Evidence From 43 Countries
abstract: ABSTRACT Water scarcity constrains development, but its economy‐wide implications across global supply chains remain difficult to quantify. This study combines consumption‐based water footprints from EXIOBASE 3.8 with basin‐level water‐stress factors to construct a scarcity‐weighted virtual‐water intensity indicator. Two‐way fixed‐effects models covering 43 countries over 1995–2019 examine its associations with economic growth and productivity. Non‐agricultural specifications reveal no detectable effects, suggesting that macroeconomic constraints operate mainly through agricultural water use. Full‐sector estimates associate greater intensity with lower GDP per capita and total factor productivity growth. These associations persist (and strengthen for GDP) when the absolute scarcity‐weighted footprint replaces the GDP‐normalised indicator, suggesting that GDP normalisation does not explain the findings. Net scarcity transfer analysis links productivity losses primarily to domestic scarcity, while growth effects are consistent with transmission through trade. The findings position agricultural water governance, trade diversification, and water‐use efficiency monitoring as central levers for Sustainable Development Goal 6.4 and sustainable economic development. The evidence suggests that the macroeconomic association between scarcity‐weighted virtual‐water dependence and economic …

title: How do fertilized and unfertilized Fabaceae trees respond to seasonal variation in Amazonian reforestation?
abstract: Abstract Plants adjust traits such as stomatal conductance ( g s ) and leaf area (LA) to cope with resource fluctuations, and while species differ in their responses to water scarcity, fertilization can enhance resilience. This study assessed how seasonal variation, fertilization, and their interaction influence functional adjustments in tree legumes: three non-N-fixers ( Cenostigma tocantinum , Senna reticulata and Dipteryx odorata ), one N fixer ( Clitoria fairchildiana ), and two facultative N fixers ( Inga edulis and Acacia mangium ). The experiment included six species with nine replicates per treatment, monitored over a 25-month period. Gas exchange, nutrient and carbohydrate concentrations, and leaf area were measured on fertilized and unfertilized plants under both drought and wet conditions, enabling analysis of both physiological and biochemical responses across different environmental and nutritional scenarios. All species reduced their g s , photosynthetic performance, and transpiration rates during drought, and fertilization imposed little effect on these seasonal changes. However, fertilization increased LA in D. odorata and C. fairchildiana , but not in A. mangium . Seasonal changes and fertilization also influenced macro (P, K, Ca) and micronutrients (Fe, Zn), with responses differing significantly among species. Most species, particularly those that were fertil…

title: Differential Susceptibility and HR-Like Resistance Responses in Arabidopsis thaliana to Colletotrichum coccodes and Colletotrichum scovillei
abstract: Hemibiotrophic fungi of the genus Colletotrichum provide valuable systems for studying plant immunity and pathogen lifestyle transitions; however, compatible and incompatible interactions have rarely been compared within the same host species. Here, we show that Arabidopsis thaliana exhibits contrasting responses to two phylogenetically distinct hemibiotrophic fungi, Colletotrichum coccodes KACC40803 and Colletotrichum scovillei KC05. Multilocus phylogenetic analyses using ITS , ACT , GAPDH , and TUB2 sequences confirmed their taxonomic identities. The two fungi also differed morphologically, particularly in colony characteristics and appressorial structures. Inoculation of Arabidopsis leaves with C. coccodes caused progressive chlorosis, necrotic lesions, extensive fungal colonization, acervulus formation, and increasing fungal biomass, indicating a compatible susceptible interaction. Host defense-related genes associated with salicylic acid– and jasmonic acid–mediated pathways were suppressed during infection. By contrast, C . scovillei induced restricted lesion development, rapid accumulation of callose and reactive oxygen species, localized plasma membrane disruption, and strong induction of defense-related genes in Arabidopsis leaves, consistent with an incompatible hypersensitive response (HR)–like cell death. Fungal biomass remained low throughout infection, demonstratin…

Nonlinear regime of radially spreading extensional flows. Part 2. Power-law fluids
abstract: Radially spreading extensional flows can become unstable and develop tearing patterns consisting of rifts and tongues. Such patterns have been observed in laboratory experiments with strain-rate-softening (shear-thinning) polymer solutions and in spreading ice shelves. Linear stability analysis predicts that axisymmetric spreading of power-law fluids becomes unstable when the fluid is shear thinning. However, understanding the emergence and evolution of rifts requires analysis of the nonlinear flow regime. In Part 1 of this study we developed a numerical simulation of the full nonlinear equations and showed that Newtonian fluids remain globally stable, consistently with theoretical predictions and experimental observations. Here we extend that framework to explore power-law fluids. We demonstrate that purely viscous shear-thinning fluids can develop rifts, and evolve rift-tongue patterns consistently with theoretical and experimental findings. Starting from an axisymmetric base state, we examine the resulting flow under monochromatic perturbations over a range of amplitudes, wavenumbers, fluid properties, and boundary and initial conditions. We find that for shear-thinning fluids, rift formation depends strongly on perturbation amplitude, while being less sensitive to the perturbation wavenumber. title: The Explanatory Power of Space in History: Historical Narrative and Geographical Causality in Social Studies Textbooks
abstract: This study examines how historical events, facts, and processes in the Common Heritage learning domain of 5th-, 6th-, and 7th-grade social studies textbooks are presented in terms of geographical causality. Designed as a qualitative document analysis, the study analyzes the relevant sections of textbooks published by the Turkish Ministry of National Education using a Geographical Context Coding Scheme. The analysis focused on the geographical elements associated with historical content, levels of geographical explanation, and history-geography integration. Findings indicate that geographical causality is visible at all three grade levels but varies by theme. In Grade 5, it is strongest in early settlements, environment-life relations, production, and natural resources; in Grade 6, in Turkistan, nomadic life, military organization, migration, settlement, and trade routes; and in Grade 7, in the foundation and expansion of the Ottoman State, the conquest of Istanbul, geographical discoveries, and economic structure. Across grades, the explanatory role of space also shifts from environment-life relations toward more complex geopolitical and economic networks. Geography remains largely descriptive or supportive in cultural and intellectual topics. More systematic integration of geographical context into historical content could strengthen students’ historical and spatial thinking.

title: Power Quality Enhancement Using a Fuzzy Logic-Based Shunt Active Power Filter with Instantaneous Power Theory
abstract: The rapid growth of power electronic converters and other nonlinear loads has made current harmonics, poor power factor and reactive power burden the dominant power quality problems in modern distribution networks. This paper presents a three-phase shunt active power filter (SAPF) in which the reference compensating currents are extracted using the instantaneous reactive power (p-q) theory and the DC-link capacitor voltage is regulated by a Mamdani-type fuzzy logic controller (FLC) in place of the conventional proportional-integral (PI) controller. The fuzzy controller uses the DC-link voltage error and its change as inputs, with seven linguistic sets per variable and a 7 × 7 rule base of 49 rules. A hysteresis current controller generates the gating pulses of the IGBT-based voltage source inverter. The complete system, supplying a three-phase diode bridge rectifier load from a 50 Hz grid, is modelled in MATLAB/Simulink. The total harmonic distortion (THD) of the source current falls from 25.80% without compensation to 4.64% with the PI-controlled SAPF and to 1.45% with the fuzzy-controlled SAPF, well within the IEEE 519 limit of 5%. The fuzzy controller also settles the DC-link voltage at its 740 V reference without overshoot, whereas the PI controller leaves a steady offset of about 5 V.

title: National governance and corporate social responsibility performance in a conflict affected frontier market
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the linkage between the quality of governance at the national level and corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance in publicly traded firms in Palestine. Based on the frameworks of agency theory, stakeholder theory, and legitimacy theory, the study tests six hypotheses related to each dimension of the WGI framework by the World Bank: VC (voice and accountability), PS (political stability), GE (government effectiveness), RQ (regulatory quality), RL (rule of law), and CC (control of corruption). CSR performance is measured using corporate social responsibility expenditures, representing the real monetary investment of the firms in social and environmental operations. This study utilizes an unbalanced panel data set for 473 firm-year observations from 43 publicly traded companies on the Palestine Exchange during the period 2014–2024, using fixed-effect regression as the main approach and system GMM as the robustness test. As can be observed from the findings, voice and accountability, political stability and absence of violence, government effectiveness, and rule of law are found to positively and significantly impact CSR spending, whereas regulatory quality has a significant negative impact on CSR expenditure, supporting the theory of institutional substitution. Corruption control does not significantly impact CSR spending. The findings emp…

title: How Does Social Presence Affect Non-Interactive Teaching When the Audience Is a Familiar Peer?
abstract: This study investigated how different levels of social presence affect non-interactive teaching in the presence of a familiar audience. We compared three teaching conditions (video, online, and in-person) to examine whether higher levels of social presence can increase motivation and engagement, thereby improving learning outcomes. A restudy was used as the control condition. All students taught in front of a familiar peer. Results showed that social presence increased sequentially from the restudy condition to the video, online, and in-person teaching conditions. No significant differences in state anxiety or extraneous cognitive load were found among the three teaching conditions, although students in the video condition experienced significantly higher state anxiety than those in the restudy condition. Students in the in-person condition reported higher motivation, germane cognitive load, and intrinsic cognitive load than those in the restudy condition. Students in the in-person and online conditions also exhibited more happy expressions than those in the video condition. However, students in the video condition outperformed students in both the in-person and restudy conditions on the transfer test. Online teaching achieved comparable academic performance to video teaching. Social presence and motivation together mediated the positive effects of teaching activities on transf…

title: How Peer Working Hours Shape Individual Preferences: Experimental Evidence From Germany
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how colleagues' working hours influence individual working hours preferences. We conducted a representative survey experiment among German employees in 2024, in which participants received randomized information about colleagues' working hours. We combine the survey experiment with quantitative and LLM‐based text analysis of an open‐ended question. Colleagues' hours causally influence stated preferences, yet respondents' explanations focus on personal reasons. This shows that social factors influence working time preferences alongside the individual considerations that respondents most frequently identify. Our findings highlight the importance of collective action for working‐time policy and reveal methodological considerations for studying labor supply preferences.
