title: AC-NB: Ant colony-based secure routing and naive bayes detection of black hole attacks in VANETs
abstract: Abstract Vehicle Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) are fundamental to achieving zero-fatality intelligent transportation, yet their open nature exposes them to severe security threats, particularly blackhole attacks that disrupt routing and compromise safety. Existing countermeasures force a trade-off between security and efficiency: cryptographic methods impose excessive overhead, while machine learning detectors lack real-time adaptability. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes AC-NB, a closed-loop framework that integrates an enhanced Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) routing protocol with a lightweight Naïve Bayes classifier. In AC-NB, a continuous feedback cycle is established: the Bayesian detector computes node trust values from packet drop rate, forward rate, and RSSI mismatch, and these trust values directly update the ACO heuristic—which jointly considers link security, link quality, distance, and node trust—steering route selection away from malicious nodes. Extensive highway simulations under 20% blackhole attackers show that AC-NB achieves end-to-end delays of 13–48 ms (an order-of-magnitude reduction over baselines), packet delivery ratio between 80% and 98%, throughput between 78% and 98%, and detection rates above 90% with low false positives. These results confirm that tightly coupling probabilistic detection with adaptive multi-criteria routing can simultaneously deliver…

title: Temperature-dependent loss physics and thermal fatigue of GaN HEMTs and SiC MOSFETs under realistic energy-storage mission profiles
abstract: Abstract The temperature-dependent loss physics and thermal fatigue of two 650~V wide-bandgap power switches of equal rating, a GaN HEMT and a SiC power MOSFET---are compared under realistic energy-storage operation. Datasheet-calibrated models of the on-resistance, switching energies, and output capacitance energy $E_{\mathrm{oss}}=\int_0^{V}C_{\mathrm{oss}}(v)\,v\,\mathrm{d}v$ were traced to their physical origins---phonon-limited two-dimensional electron-gas transport in the GaN heterostructure; channel, JFET, and drift resistances in the SiC device---and embedded in a bidirectional buck--boost converter driven by three annual (8760~h) mission profiles built entirely from measured data: hourly satellite irradiance (PVGIS-SARAH3, 2023), the real hourly load of the Turkish transmission system (2023), and 10\,617 real electric-vehicle charging sessions (2019). The hourly junction-temperature trajectories were processed by rainflow counting, and a Coffin--Manson--Arrhenius fatigue model was calibrated to the published power-cycling data. Three results emerge. First, the efficiency-optimal switching frequency varies by more than a factor of four (20--93~kHz) for the same GaN device across the three duty cycles, while under near-idle grid duty, the efficiency gap between the technologies collapses to below 0.03 percentage points, leaving the ranking to secondary design constraints…

title: Exploring associations of perceived mental fatigue and perceived energy with gait characteristics during level and downhill walking in healthy young adults
abstract: Mental fatigue may influence locomotor control, but evidence in healthy young adults is limited. This study examined whether a 40-minute working-memory task was accompanied by changes in perceived fatigue and cognitive performance and whether subjective fatigue and energy states were associated with pre-to-post changes in gait during level and downhill treadmill walking. Forty healthy young adults were included in the analyses and randomly assigned to a low-load 0-back condition ( n = 21) or a high-load 2-back condition ( n = 19); questionnaire-based analyses used the 38 participants with complete data. We assessed mental and physical energy and fatigue immediately before and after the task using the Mental and Physical State and Trait Energy and Fatigue Scales. We recorded reaction time and accuracy across five task blocks. Gait was assessed with six inertial sensors before and after the task during level walking (0°) and downhill walking (9° decline) at 5 km/h. Associations between subjective fatigue and energy ratings and pre-to-post changes in gait parameters were examined using Pearson correlations. Perceived mental fatigue increased and perceived mental energy decreased after the cognitive task. Perceived physical fatigue also increased, whereas perceived physical energy did not change significantly. Reaction times improved across blocks in both conditions; accuracy decre…

title: Impact of Industrial Policy and Energy Transition on the Life Cycle of Coal Mining Enterprises
abstract: This study compares the impact of industrial policy and the energy transition on the life cycles of coal mining enterprises in 31 countries from 2017 to 2022 and takes into account differences in national coal industry development strategies by using panel data on enterprise entry and exit, climate policy, energy mix, and government support. Econometric techniques, such as fixed and random effects models, clarify nonlinear relationships between policy measures and coal enterprise dynamics. The findings show that these dynamics are shaped by three opposing forces: the global climate agenda, national energy security strategies, and institutional inertia. Three key paradoxes are identified: the expansion of nuclear power correlates with fewer coal mine closures; the Climate Change Performance Index is significant only in countries where coal is not a strategic resource; and green subsidies do not prevent the entry of new coal enterprises. Four country groups are identified: major exporters, major importers, domestically oriented coal producers, and green transition economies. Environmental goods exports accelerate mine closures, whereas coal rents and the share of coal in the energy mix slow this process. title: Longitudinal Associations Between Fruit and Vegetable Prescription Program Participation and Pediatric Blood Pressure and Weight Status
abstract: Background/Objectives: This study examined whether engagement in a pediatric fruit and vegetable prescription program (FVPP) offering one $15 prescription during office visits influenced health, hypothesizing that youth improve blood pressure (BP) and weight status after one year. Methods: This non-controlled longitudinal intervention trial included data from caregiver–child dyads at one pediatric clinic (child age 8–16 years). Correlated data models evaluated average longitudinal trends of study endpoints. Causal inference analyses for longitudinal data estimated time-varying effects of the FVPP on outcomes. Results: In total, 304 dyads enrolled. Youth reduced mean body mass index (BMI) percentile (p = 0.02), systolic BP (p < 0.001), and diastolic BP (p = 0.01). Youth also reduced the odds of elevated systolic BP (p < 0.001), diastolic BP (p = 0.004), and overall BP (p = 0.003). Children who redeemed ≥1 prescription reduced BMI percentile compared to counterparts who did not redeem (p = 0.02). Children who redeemed ≥1 prescription between baseline and 6 months reduced odds of obesity or elevated systolic BP at 12 months, with a relative odds ratio of 0.47 (p = 0.01) or 0.51 (p = 0.05), compared to peers who did not redeem. Conclusions: The results suggest that pediatric FVPP engagement may contribute to improvements in key health outcomes, underscoring the need for further inv…

Electron-Trapping Molecular Engineering in Cycloolefin Copolymer Dielectrics for High-Temperature Capacitive Energy Storage
abstract: Abstract High-temperature dielectric capacitors require polymer dielectrics with simultaneously high energy density, low dielectric loss, and excellent thermal reliability. However, conventional high-temperature polymers generally suffer from severe conduction losses, while cycloolefin copolymer (COC), despite its excellent thermal stability and low dielectric loss, exhibits limited breakdown strength (Eb) that restricts its energy storage capability. Herein, an all-organic molecular blending strategy is proposed by incorporating anthrone (AT) molecules into a COC matrix to regulate charge transport and enhance dielectric performance. The introduced AT molecules regulate carrier transport through their electron-accepting characteristics and favorable energy-level alignment, facilitating electron trapping and suppressing carrier migration. Consequently, the optimized AT1.0 composite achieves enhanced Eb of 654 MV m–1 and a discharge energy density (Ud) of 5.13 J cm–3 at 150 °C while maintaining an ultrahigh charge–discharge efficiency (η) above 95%. Furthermore, the composite film exhibits excellent high-power discharge capability, stable cycling performance over 5 × 104 cycles, and outstanding large-area uniformity. This work demonstrates a molecular blending strategy for enhancing the energy storage performance of COC-based polymer dielectrics by regulating charge transport, p…

title: Varietal Resistance of Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp.) to Attack by Callosobruchus maculatus (Fabricius, 1775) (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) During Post-Harvest Storage in Mali
abstract: Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata (L.) Walp.) is a tropical legume of major economic, nutritional and agronomic value, but its production is severely constrained by post-harvest losses, mainly caused by the cowpea weevil Callosobruchus maculatus. An experimental study was conducted at the Entomology-Parasitology Laboratory of FST/USTTB (November 2023–February 2024) to assess the susceptibility of forty cowpea varieties, grown under irrigated and water-stress conditions, to damage by C. maculatus during three months of storage. Sterilized seeds (30 g per 500-mL jar) were infested with three pairs of newly emerged (0-24 h) C. maculatus adults, using a completely randomised design with three replicates (360 jars in total). Varietal susceptibility was assessed through the median development period (MDP), damage rate, adult mortality, weight loss and susceptibility index (SI). Five varieties (KT2-23-5, CZ16-3-71, IT13K-1424-12, FAKSON, IT15K-2386-1) were resistant under water-stress conditions and five others (SIMBO, KVX78-6PLANT-1, CZ16-1-1-91, TILIGREPLANT-6, KVX61-1) under irrigated conditions. The combined analysis confirmed the resistance of three varieties: KT2-23-5, TILIGREPLANT-6 and KVX61-1. Damage was positively and significantly correlated with MDP, weight loss and SI, whereas adult mortality was not significantly associated with observed losses. These findings suggest that post-…

title: Programmable Organic Light‐Emitting Transistors Enabled by Floating‐Gate Charge Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Display technologies for high‐resolution smartphones, wearable screens and near‐eye VR/AR microdisplays increasingly require compact pixel architectures with high aperture ratios. Organic light‐emitting transistors (OLETs) improve functional integration by combining transistor switching and electroluminescence within a single device. However, conventional OLETs still define emission states through instantaneous electrical bias, leaving state storage separated from light emission. The absence of memory‐emission co‐location limits intrinsic state programmability in OLET‐based pixel devices. Here, we report programmable organic light‐emitting transistors (P‐OLETs) based on a floating‐gate architecture, in which charge storage enables reversible charge trapping and release, producing programmable switching behavior and tunable electroluminescence. The stored charge modulates channel transport and light emission, allowing electrical programming to define persistently retained optical states. Optimized P‐OLETs exhibit a large memory window of 27.07 V, stable luminance retention over 5000 s, and reliable endurance over 100 program/erase cycles. Floating‐gate charge storage shifts OLET operation from bias‐defined emission toward charge‐state defined emission and establishes a memory‐emission integrated device architecture. This work introduces programmable state‐retentive emis…

title: Lignin-Derived Nitrogen-Doped Carbon/SiO x Nanocomposites for Applications for Lithium Storage
abstract: Abstract To address the limitations of conventional graphite- and Si-based anodes, a facile in situ synthesis strategy was developed to construct lignin-derived nitrogen-doped porous carbon/SiOx (NLPC/SiOx) nanocomposites using sodium lignosulfonate as a renewable precursor. The influence of SiOx content on structural characteristics and lithium storage performance was systematically investigated. Structural analyses revealed that nanoscale SiOx particles were uniformly dispersed within the porous N-doped carbon framework, establishing intimate interfacial contact. This integrated architecture facilitates electron and Li+ transport while accommodating volume variations during repeated lithiation/delithiation. The optimized NLPC/SiOx-25 electrode delivered a reversible capacity of 879 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1, with 89.3% capacity retention after 100 cycles. Furthermore, it maintained a capacity of 260 mAh g−1 after 4000 cycles at 5 A g−1, demonstrating excellent long-term cycling stability. The enhanced electrochemical performance is attributed to the synergistic effects of nanoscale SiOx dispersion, the conductive N-doped carbon framework, and improved interfacial integration. This work presents a sustainable strategy for developing durable Si-based anodes while promoting the high-value utilization of lignin-derived industrial byproducts.

abstract: Air Sungai Musi memiliki permasalahan kualitas berupa kandungan besi (Fe), mangan (Mn), kekeruhan, padatan terlarut, dan kontaminasi mikrobiologi yang memerlukan pengolahan bertahap. Variasi laju alir yang digunakan adalah 6, 8, 10, 12, dan 14 L/menit dengan tekanan udara aerasi 4 bar. Parameter yang dianalisis meliputi pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), kekeruhan, Fe, Mn, Total Coliform, dan Escherichia coli. Data dianalisis secara deskriptif dengan membandingkan hasil pengukuran terhadap nilai acuan kualitas air berdasarkan Peraturan Menteri Kesehatan Republik Indonesia Nomor 2 Tahun 2023. Experimental Investigation of a Hybrid Thermal Management System for LFP Battery Packs Using Ag 2 O Nano Fluid–Cooled Serpentine Copper Tubes Embedded in Graphite‐Enhanced PCM
abstract: ABSTRACT Effective thermal management is critical to ensure the safety, reliability, and performance of lithium‐ion battery modules under high thermal loads. While hybrid phase change material (PCM)–liquid cooling systems have been widely explored, the present study introduces a novel material‐level enhancement through the use of an Ag 2 O–ethylene glycol Nano fluid, whose application in battery thermal management remains largely unexplored. A compact 4S5P battery module comprising 21 700‐type lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells (14 V, 22.5 Ah) is experimentally investigated under 1C, 1.5C, and 2C discharge rates, along with 1C charging conditions. The proposed hybrid BTMS integrates PCM with active liquid cooling using Ag 2 O Nano fluid at varying concentrations (1–5 wt.%), enabling a systematic evaluation of its thermo‐physical impact. The results demonstrate that, in the absence of thermal management, the module temperature rapidly increases to approximately 60°C at 2C, indicating severe thermal stress. In contrast, the proposed system significantly enhances heat dissipation, maintaining the maximum cell temperature within 30°C–32°C, thereby achieving a reduction of 5%. Furthermore, increasing nanoparticle concentration improves convective heat transfer, with optimal performance observed at 5 wt.%, reaching temperature to 29°C resulting in improved temperature uniformity acro…

Research on vehicle lateral active vibration reduction system based on centrifugal harmonic force generator under constrained information
abstract: Abstract Modern intelligent transportation and heavy-duty transport technologies increasingly operate under complex road conditions and high-load environments, making vehicle lateral vibration a critical concern for driving safety and ride comfort. Traditional passive suspension systems have inherent limitations in effectively addressing complex and time-varying disturbances. To overcome these challenges, this paper introduces centrifugal harmonic force generator technology and proposes a lateral active vibration reduction control scheme for information-constrained conditions. In practical engineering environments, lateral disturbance forces are difficult to measure directly, while often only the lateral acceleration of the vehicle body is available. A single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) lateral vibration dynamics model and an equivalent lateral control force model are established. A vehicle motion state reconstruction method relying on a single acceleration sensor is then designed using numerical integration and digital low-pass filtering. Building upon this, a PD feedback closed-loop control framework is constructed, and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is introduced to optimize the control gains under the physical constraints of the generator. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that the PSO-optimized active control strategy reduces the lateral vibration inde…

Evaluation Method of Surplus PV Potential Considering of EV Charging Behavior
abstract: ABSTRACT As the adoption of renewable energy accelerates, utilizing surplus photovoltaic (PV) power for electric vehicle (EV) charging has attracted growing attention. However, EV user charging behavior involves significant uncertainties—such as driving distance and plug‐in probability—that cannot be accurately captured by average‐based models, leading to potential misestimation of PV surplus absorption. This study constructs a probabilistic framework that models EV charging behavior using data and Monte Carlo simulations, evaluating the PV surplus mitigation rate as a probability density function (PDF). Furthermore, it analyzes how variations in charging timing and user behavior affect the stability of PV absorption, and derives indicators such as the required number of EVs and their standard deviation. These insights contribute to the strategic design of realistic and scalable solutions for social implementation.

Interfacial Copper Oxidation Under an Applied Alternating Electric Field and a Water‐Soluble Caramel Support Enable Clean, Low‐Defect Transfer of Large‐Area Graphene
abstract: ABSTRACT Graphene is a promising platform for next‐generation electronics, yet conventional transfer from catalytic metals often introduces cracks, wrinkles, polymer residues, and unintended doping that compromise device performance. Here, we report a synergistic transfer strategy combining interfacial Cu oxidation under an applied 50 Hz AC electric field with a water‐soluble caramel support. Under otherwise identical aqueous‐treatment conditions, the AC‐field‐treated graphene/Cu exhibits faster oxidation propagation and lower spatial heterogeneity than the water‐only control, producing a Cu 2 O‐rich interfacial state favorable for subsequent graphene delamination. The caramel support, prepared from sucrose and corn syrup, provides tunable thermomechanical compliance, conformal contact with diverse target substrates, weak interaction with graphene, and facile aqueous removal. Using this approach, graphene was successfully transferred at the 4‐inch scale onto SiO 2 /Si and other substrates, with a root‐mean‐square surface roughness of 0.73 nm. Compared with PMMA‐transferred controls, the resulting graphene exhibited reduced support‐derived contamination, fewer transfer‐induced structural perturbations, weaker p‐type doping, and improved carrier transport. This work provides a scalable route for clean, low‐damage, large‐area graphene transfer and device integration.

Pulsed electric field-mediated elimination of yeast [ PSI + ] prion is variant dependent and affects cell growth dynamics
abstract: Yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a widespread model system in which mechanisms of prion induction and elimination have been identified. New and safe substances and methods are being sought to eliminate prions from cells. In this research, we applied guanidinium hydrochloride (GuHCl) alone and in combination with pulsed electric field treatment against [ PSI + ] prion. The analysis of cell culture optical density and doubling time showed that the method of [ PSI + ] prion elimination increases cell doubling time, with combined treatment having a more severe impact on cell growth than GuHCl treatment alone. Additionally, we found that both elimination methods can impact the optical culture density achieved by [ psi − ] cells. However, the cells in which the [ PSI + ] prion has been eliminated by GuHCl alone are able to reach the same optical density as unaffected [ psi − ] cells and a higher optical density than the affected [ psi − ] cells by GuHCl alone. These findings suggest that the presence and subsequent removal of the [ PSI + ] prion influence early exponential growth, revealing lasting effects on cell growth dynamics that are distinct from previously reported effects on stationary phase survival. This work highlights how prion elimination strategies, including chemical and electric field treatments, can impact post-curing growth behavior in yeast cells.

title: Heavy-Duty Diesel Vehicle Deterioration: Impact of Vehicle Age and Emission Control Technology on NO x Emissions
abstract: Abstract This study examines the effect of aging and deterioration on NOx emissions from heavy-duty diesel trucks (HDDTs) with different emission control technologies, including Engine Control only, exhaust gas recirculation (EGR), and selective catalytic reduction (SCR). In-use tailpipe emissions were measured from 12,023 HDDTs from 13 roadside measurement campaigns conducted in California and Utah between 2008 and 2024. Vehicle registration records and the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) engine certification database were used to identify engine NOx control technology. At younger ages, SCR-equipped HDDTs generally emitted significantly less NOx than non-SCR-equipped HDDTs. However, after several years of aging, NOx emissions from SCR-equipped HDDTs were comparable to or exceeded those from non-SCR-equipped HDDTs across locations, engine manufacturers, and engine model years. Although cumulative lifetime emissions from SCR-equipped HDDTs remained lower than non-SCR HDDTs, the reduction in lifetime NOx emissions was substantially smaller than estimated by EPA’s MOtor Vehicle Emission Simulator (MOVES). MOVES predicts an 80% reduction in lifetime NOx emissions from SCR-equipped HDDTs, whereas our estimate is approximately 32%. These findings may indicate that the long-term benefits of SCR for reducing HDDT NOx emissions are smaller than expected and highlight the need fo…

STRATEGY FOR ENSURING ORGANIZATIONAL RESILIENCE: EVOLUTION FROM JUST-IN-TIME TO JUST-IN-CASE
abstract: The study is devoted to the systemic transformation of conceptual foundations of strategic management and the assurance of organizational resilience of business entities under conditions of extreme macroenvironmental turbulence, severe economic shocks, and ongoing military-political instability. The paper comprehensively highlights the evolutionary transition from the traditional lean production concept Just-in-Time (JIT), focused on total minimization of inventory, operational cost reduction, and maximum efficiency, to the preventive Just-in-Case (JIC) model, which prioritizes the formation of strategic buffers, operational safety, and long-term business continuity. It is proven that excessive optimization within the JIT paradigm creates critical vulnerability in global supply chains during unexpected force majeure circumstances. The concept of "dynamic buffering" is substantiated as an economically sound alternative to chaotic resource accumulation, based on ABC risk analysis and optimization of the Cost of Resilience. Strategic adaptation tools are analyzed, including multi-sourcing supplier diversification, nearshoring, friendshoring, as well as the transition to "glocalization" and ecosystem partnership models with deep inter-organizational process integration. Special attention is paid to digital transformation as a fundamental factor of resilience, specifically the imple…

Engineering a Dynamic Alloy–Fluoride Interface via a Co-Placement Gas-Phase Strategy for Stable Lithium Metal Anodes
abstract: Abstract Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) hold great promise for next-generation high-energy-density energy storage systems, but suffer from uneven Li nucleation and unstable interfaces. Here, a scalable coplacement gas-phase reaction strategy is developed to construct an adaptive alloy–fluoride interface on nickel mesh current collectors, enabling one-step in-situ formation of a uniform Ni3Sb/NiF2 layer. The lithiophilic Ni3Sb alloy effectively lowers the lithium nucleation barrier and guides uniform lithium deposition. Upon cycling, NiF2 is transformed into a LiF-rich interphase, which stabilizes the electrode/electrolyte interface and homogenizes Li+ flux. The combined interface enables durable and uniform Li plating/stripping under long-term cycling. Consequently, the Ni3Sb/NiF2-modified anode achieves stable cycling for over 2600 h in symmetric cells and delivers 83.1% capacity retention after 240 cycles in LiFePO4 full cells with a high areal capacity of 10 mAh cm–2. This work provides a facile and scalable strategy for engineering multifunctional interfaces toward practical LMBs.

title: Aurora Kinases Have the Potential to Serve as an Effective Therapeutic Strategy in the Treatment of Various Types of Cancer
abstract: Aurora kinases, encompassing Aurora A, Aurora B, and Aurora C, function as essential regulators of mitosis by controlling checkpoints, centrosome dynamics, and cytokinesis; their dysregulation is a primary driver of uncontrolled cell proliferation, a hallmark of cancer. Although previous reviews have comprehensively summarized these roles, the present study offers a distinct advancement by quantifying the original contribution—a novel Aurora kinase–substrate interaction, a unique resistance mechanism, and a new therapeutic vulnerability, clearly setting this work apart from foundational studies. Our findings show that inhibition of this target selectively impairs tumor growth without affecting normal cells, thereby providing direct evidence that targeting this specific axis constitutes a viable and previously unrecognized strategy for cancer therapy. Together, these results not only elucidate the mechanistic functions of Aurora kinases in tumorigenesis but also provide actionable insights for the design of next-generation kinase.

Unbearable time: Gender, power, and temporal governance in abortion policy and practice
abstract: Abstract In this article, I argue that state regulation of time in abortion policy, as well as its intended and unintended effects in practice, is a crucial site through which to understand the vexed relationships among time, gender, and state power. Anthropologists working in various global sites have demonstrated how state control over when abortion care can legally be provided operates as a form of reproductive governance that shapes if, when, and how pregnant people are able to access abortion care. Medically unjustified policies that regulate access to abortion care on the basis of time are stark examples of injurious forms of temporal governance —state mobilization of temporal strategies of control that result in harm, suffering, and even death. Anthropological attention to temporal governance contributes to public understanding of abortion by showing how policies of curtailing time and seizing time are employed as instruments of gendered constraint that produce deeply uneven possibilities for reproductive future‐making.

title: Evaluation of the Impact on Transformer Insulation by Lightning Surge Voltage Analysis on Wide‐Area Power Network
abstract: When lightning surges simultaneously enter three phases of the primary circuit of a transformer, specific frequency components within the lightning surge may match the resonance frequency of the transformer. This can lead to overvoltages at the neutral point of the transformer windings, potentially causing insulation breakdown. In this study, an analysis simulating the entry of the lightning surge into a transformer due to indirect lightning was conducted, and the insulation impact at the transformer neutral point was investigated. As a result of simulations modeling a wide‐area power network, voltages containing frequency components corresponding to the resonance frequency of the transformer neutral point in the range from several to several tens of kHz were confirmed. While it is self‐evident that a direct lightning strike to a transmission tower can lead to transformer failures, it has been suggested that lightning surges occurring in transformers as a result of indirect lightning may also cause transformer failures owing to overvoltages at the transformer neutral point. © 2026 Institute of Electrical Engineers of Japan and Wiley Periodicals LLC.

EVALUATION OF INTERNAL CONTROLS OVER THE REVENUE CYCLE: A CASE STUDY OF RETAIL COMPANY X
abstract: This study evaluates internal controls over the revenue cycle at Retail X, a modern convenience store chain operating a digital ordering application integrated with a Point of Sale (POS) system. The evaluation applies the COSO Internal Control–Integrated Framework/ICIF (COSO, 2013), focusing on two components: Risk Assessment and Control Activities. A descriptive case study approach was employed, with data collected through semi-structured interviews with three informants—the Store Manager, Cashier, and Service Crew—and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings identify four operational risks: transaction input errors, product preparation errors, order pickup errors, and disruptions in receiving digital orders. These risks stem from employee-customer-system interactions and limitations in human resources and digital infrastructure. Control activities implemented include order confirmation, preparation SOPs, order labeling, product remaking, and manual order verification. However, the evaluation reveals uneven control coverage, heavy reliance on human factors, and a predominance of corrective over preventive controls. By tracing risk from its source to the adequacy of existing controls, this study extends the application of COSO ICIF to digitally integrated retail settings in developing economies. The study concludes that strengthening internal control requires procedural i…

Does Corporate Water Performance Matter to Investors?
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates whether corporate water performance matters to investors, using water consumption, withdrawals, and discharge as three proxies of performance. Based on a sample of 2141 US firm‐year observations with available water data in the CDP annual surveys over 2014–2019, we find that poor corporate water performance is consistently associated with lower market value. This valuation penalty is weaker among firms that voluntarily disclose their water performance data to the CDP, but stronger among firms with a dedicated CSR committee on the board. Our results are robust to potential endogeneity issues. Overall, our findings suggest that investors reward sound water management and penalize weak practices more heavily when governance structures raise expectations for environmental stewardship. The study offers policy‐relevant insights by highlighting the financial benefits of transparent water reporting and contributes to the emerging literature by showing that water stewardship is a value‐relevant corporate strategy.

title: Visuospatial and Verbal Abilities in Poor Readers: Cognitive Differences and Strategy Use
abstract: ABSTRACT Developmental dyslexia is characterized by difficulties in reading and impairments in cognitive functions. It has also been linked to dysfunction of the brain regions involved in verbal and visuospatial processing. Although some research suggests individuals with dyslexia may rely on visuospatial strategies to compensate for their verbal difficulties, other studies have reported contradictory findings on visuospatial abilities. This study compared the cognitive performance of 11 poor readers and 15 typical readers across two verbal and four visuospatial tasks. Additionally, the strategies employed by each group to complete these cognitive tasks were explored. While poor readers showed worse performance across all verbal and visuospatial tasks than typical readers, there was no significant group difference in strategy use. Moreover, verbal cognitive inefficiencies were associated with reading difficulties. Poor readers' cognitive challenges, despite no difference in the strategies employed, highlight the importance of addressing both verbal and visuospatial difficulties in dyslexia.

Uncertainty estimation of incoming comet trajectories with a thermophysical non-gravitational force model for Comet Interceptor encounter planning
abstract: Abstract The European Space Agency Comet Interceptor mission is designed to fly-by an as-yet undetermined incoming long-period or dynamically-new comet, which will require an accurate prediction of its trajectory. Cometary orbits are perturbed from purely gravitational trajectories by non-gravitational accelerations (NGAs) stemming from their outgassing, however, and these must be taken into account in the navigation. We here test the ability of ground-based astrometry and standard NGA-fitting techniques to predict the position and velocity of incoming comets perturbed by a Monte Carlo sampled thermophysical acceleration model. We find that, due to the difficulties of predicting NGA evolution as well as the limitations of reasonably simulated astrometry, predicted accuracies are unlikely to meet the mission goals of 1000 km and 1 m s−1 in position and velocity, sixty days before intercept. We instead recommend expanded uncertainties of 10,000 km and several m s−1. Our NGA fits struggle to reproduce the reference accelerations and trajectories when outgassing is rising steeply at a few AU-incoming, but with more observations up until perihelion, do eventually converge, leading to good estimates of many of the underlying acceleration parameters even for half an orbital arc.

Uncertainty Quantification and Compensation of Positional Error for Collaborative Robots
abstract: Abstract The positional accuracy of collaborative robots is degraded by errors from multiple sources. Existing error compensation methods improve the positional accuracy, but they output deterministic predictions without uncertainty quantification (UQ), which introduces hidden risks in high-precision applications. Moreover, directly applying Bayesian approximation techniques, such as Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout, to raw joint variables is further hampered by the nonlinear coupling among joints, which yields uncertainty intervals too wide to be informative and limits point-estimation accuracy. To address these problems, this paper proposed a novel framework integrating Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) with an MC dropout neural network. KPCA extracts nonlinear features from the joint space and decouples the joint variables before they enter the network, which improves the accuracy of the learned mapping. MC dropout then generates a predictive distribution of the positional error, from which a 95% confidence interval is obtained for each target. The framework was validated on an Elite EC-63 collaborative robot. The proposed method predicts both the positional error and its uncertainty. It reduces the mean absolute positional error to 0.0546 mm after compensation. The proposed method establishes a lightweight, dual-capability framework that simultaneously provides high-precis…

Clinical prognostic risk model optimization based on vascular density in neuroblastoma
abstract: ABSTRACT Importance Elevated microvessel density (MVD) and lymphatic vessel density (LVD) have been linked to poor outcomes in several malignancies. However, their prognostic significance in neuroblastoma (NB) remains unclear. Objective To evaluate the prognostic value of MVD and LVD in NB and construct an optimized prognostic model. Methods Sixty patients with NB were included. MVD and LVD were quantified using immunohistochemical staining for CD31 and D2‐40, respectively. Cox regression‐based prognostic models combining these markers with the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) classification were compared with the standard INRG‐based model using receiver operating characteristic curves, the concordance index (C‐index), decision curve analysis (DCA), net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. Model robustness was assessed using bootstrap with 1000 resamples. Results The median MVD and LVD were 24.0/mm 2 and 7.16/mm 2 , respectively. High MVD (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.788) and high LVD (AUC = 0.693) were significantly associated with lower 5‐year event‐free survival (22.2% vs. 78.2% for MVD; 44.8% vs. 81.5% for LVD; both P < 0.05). In the multivariable Cox regression analysis, both LVD (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.088, P = 0.010) and INRG classification (HR = 5.594, P = 0.008) showed statistically significant associations with progno…

title: A geometric framework for stochastic iterations
abstract: This paper concerns models and convergence principles for dealing with stochasticity in a wide range of algorithms arising in nonlinear analysis and optimization in Hilbert spaces. It proposes a flexible geometric framework within which existing solution methods can be recast and improved, and new ones can be designed. Almost sure weak, strong, and linear convergence results are established in particular for stochastic fixed point iterations, the stochastic gradient descent method, and stochastic extrapolated parallel algorithms for feasibility problems. In these areas, the proposed algorithms exceed the features and convergence guarantees of the state of the art. Numerical applications to signal and image recovery are provided.

title: Stochastic dynamics simulation of the focused electron beam induced deposition process
abstract: This work presents a novel and general multiscale computational methodology for modeling the focused electron beam–induced deposition (FEBID) process. The approach is based on stochastic dynamics implemented using the MBN Explorer and MBN Studio software packages and provides a probabilistic description of the complex sequence of physical and chemical processes that govern FEBID, including precursor adsorption, diffusion, dissociation, and desorption. The developed framework enables simulations under experimentally realistic spatial and temporal conditions while retaining molecular-level resolution. An exemplary set of model parameters has been derived from atomistic simulations to demonstrate the methodology’s capabilities; however, the primary goal of this work is not parameter optimization, but rather the establishment of a general and transferable modeling framework applicable to a broad range of precursors, substrates, and irradiation conditions. As a representative case, the FEBID of W(CO) 6 precursors on a hydroxylated SiO 2 –H substrate is investigated, showing how the method reproduces key experimental trends and reveals the microscopic mechanisms of deposit formation. The developed multiscale approach provides a robust foundation for predictive simulations of irradiation-driven fabrication processes and their applications in 3D nanoprinting and nanoscale materials eng…

title: Stochastic template banks for GW searches using low-discrepancy sequences
abstract: Abstract Matched filtering remains the most sensitive method for detecting gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences. The efficiency of such searches depends on how well a discrete template bank covers the underlying parameter space. Conventional geometric, stochastic, and hybrid placement methods can lead to uneven coverage and redundant templates in higher dimensions. Hybrid methods are generally the most efficient among these, while stochastic methods are simpler to implement, particularly when the parameter-space metric is difficult to compute. In practice, both approaches rely on uniform random sampling, which often requires a large number of proposal points to achieve adequate coverage. We find that stochastic template banks constructed using low-discrepancy sequences achieve comparable recovery fractions while requiring 27.5% fewer proposal points in two dimensions, about 12% fewer in three dimensions and 17% fewer in a four-dimensional eccentric equal-spin toy bank. The final template count is much less sensitive to the proposal sampling, consistent with the metric-volume constraints of the covering problem. We introduce a slab-wise coarse prefilter to accelerate candidate rejection for strongly anisotropic metrics. Applied to the 4D toy bank, it gives a total bank-construction speed-up of about 1.28 × . The primary benefit of low-discrepancy sampling is ther…

title: An Integrated Risk‐Informed Optimization Framework for Disinformation Interdiction in Coupled Information‐Physical Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT The manner in which society consumes and responds to information has significantly evolved in recent years, increasing the potential risk of interacting with, reacting to, and spreading misinformation and disinformation. In this paper, we introduce a novel integrated optimization framework that simultaneously models the dynamics of an information layer (where correct information or false information spreads) and a physical layer (where users interact with a physical infrastructure system). We consider an over‐the‐horizon problem in which an adversary seeks to disrupt physical infrastructure by spreading false information about its operation and performance, prompting users to behave in ways that degrade system performance. Focusing on public transit, we study how disinformation about station closures alters user behavior and system efficiency, and develop an optimization model to identify effective interdiction strategies that mitigate these impacts. The information layer incorporates personality‐driven susceptibility and simulates dis/information diffusion, while the physical layer uses a multicommodity network flow model to capture user movements and expose the effects of disinformation on travel time. Our integrated approach enables the joint analysis of both layers, revealing complex interdependencies that are overlooked when studied separately. A case study of the…

title: The Effectiveness of Data Augmentation in Image Classification Using Whale Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Imbalanced datasets significantly degrade the performance of image classification systems, particularly in application domains where data collection is difficult, such as medical diagnosis and plant disease analysis. Data augmentation is a commonly used strategy to alleviate this problem by increasing the number of samples in minority classes. In this study, a novel image augmentation approach based on optimized edge detection, named Whale Optimization Algorithm–based Image Augmentation (WOA-IA), is proposed. Unlike conventional augmentation techniques, the proposed method generates synthetic samples by combining original images with optimally extracted edge representations. Edge detection is performed using a multi-layer filter structure whose parameters are optimized via the whale optimization algorithm by maximizing similarity with reference edge images. The resulting edge images are then integrated into an angular placement-based augmentation model. The effectiveness of the proposed WOA-IA method is evaluated on five widely used imbalanced datasets—Plant Leaves, Flowers102, Cassava, Plant Village, and HAM10000—using pre-trained CNN models including DenseNet201, MobileNet, and VGG16. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves classification performance compared to both imbalanced datasets and standard edge-based augmentation techniques, p…

From Optimization to the Pontryagin Maximum Principle
abstract: This article is a gentle stroll through the field of optimization and optimal control, aiming to acquaint the reader with the evolution of developments leading up to the Pontryagin maximum principle. The exposition adheres to simplicity without sacrificing integrity. The continuous versions of results are derived as limits of discrete versions, thus adopting a unified approach to finite-dimensional and function spaces, and wherever permissible, an intuitive connection to physics is established. Complete proofs are not provided; instead, the key geometric ideas in the proofs are presented.

title: Development of a Web-Based Expert System for the Diagnosis of Depressive Disorders
abstract: The diagnosis of depression is a critical task in modern clinical psychology. However, traditional methods using paper questionnaires and manual scoring are labor-intensive and do not provide immediate feedback to patients. Existing web platforms for psychological testing are primarily focused on data collection and do not offer formalized algorithms for the automated interpretation of results according to clinically validated methods. This paper presents the development of a web-oriented expert system for diagnosing depression based on the Beck Depression Inventory. A mathematical model is proposed that formalizes the structure of the knowledge base as a set of questions with diagnostic coefficients, a user response vector, and a classification function for unambiguously mapping results to a set of diagnostic conclusions. Based on this formal model, a three-component system architecture was developed using React.js, which includes a root state management component, a component containing the expert system logic, and a static knowledge base module. The solution is implemented as a web application with an intuitive interface built using HTML5 and CSS3, along with data validation mechanisms and automated calculation of the diagnostic conclusion based on the clinically validated Beck Scale threshold values. Experimental testing on four response scenarios corresponding to different…

title: The First World War and Japan’s cabinet system: how the conflict changed the perception and reception of foreign constitutional models by Japanese elites (1912–1920)
AI-Generated Fashion Imagery and Consumer Purchase Intention
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is widely adopted in fashion visual communication, yet imagery over-optimization causes product-image discrepancies and undermines consumer decisions. This study deconstructs three core characteristics of artificial intelligence-generated fashion imagery—visual realism, detail completeness, and style compatibility—and tests their impact on purchase intention via perceived authenticity and trust, with product price and consumer heterogeneity as moderators. Using a mixed-method approach (N = 845) and structural equation modeling, results confirm (1) the three characteristics positively influence purchase intention through direct risk reduction and indirect value identification, (2) trust plays dual mediating roles (direct and serial: artificial intelligence imagery → authenticity → trust → purchase intention), and (3) trust's mediation strengthens with higher prices (66.0% for high-price versus 39.6% for low-price products), and consumer segments differ in trust-building paths. This research enriches decision support system literature and offers actionable strategies for fashion brands.
venue: International Journal of Decision Support System Technology

title: Frozen-Bit Jammer Steering (FB-JS): Mitigating Multi-Band Channel Erasures in 5G Polar Codes
abstract: The mathematical properties of the polar coding make it a code capable of achieving capacity limits under Successive-Cancellation List (SCL) decoding, and, therefore, the polar coding schemes have been universally accustomed to the 5G New Radio (NR) specification for protecting the transmissions over the control channels. In today's environment, however, the wireless transceivers are subjected to multi-band deterministic jamming and narrow-band pulsed interference in hostiles or co-existence spectrum environments. The traditional channel-domain mitigation techniques are based on global scrambling or chaotic interleaving which randomize the burst erasures. This paper shows that classical uniform interleavers cause severe soft-value LLR contamination across recursive decoding trees. Classical interleavers achieve this by distributing erasures uniformly over the code structure, and so destroy the natural isolation of error-free sub-trees and contaminate the soft-value updates at recursive check-nodes, which makes path metric discrimination very difficult in the SCL engine. In order to mitigate this structural weakness in the context of strict hardware limitations, Frozen-Bit Jammer Steering (FB-JS) external interleaving framework is proposed, which operates as a 3GPP-compatible external permuter transparent to standardized silicon cores. Instead of being able to scramble bit seque…
venue: Muthanna Journal of Engineering and Technology

title: Coparenting and Mental Health: A Multi‐Country Analysis of Mother's and Father's Stress and Depressive Symptoms
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To examine the associations between coparenting quality and parental mental health (depressive symptoms and stress) among mothers and fathers across seven culturally diverse countries. Background Coparenting plays a critical role in shaping family dynamics and individual wellbeing. While prior research has linked coparenting to parental mental health, cross‐national comparisons remain limited. Methods This secondary analysis was conducted in a merged dataset from eight independently collected samples (2463 fathers and 2437 mothers) from seven countries (Belgium, Brazil, Italy, Japan, Portugal, Sweden, United States). Coparenting quality was assessed using the Coparenting Relationship Scale. Parental depressive symptoms and stress were measured using validated scales, with z‐score standardization applied across studies. Multigroup path analyses were conducted to examine associations between coparenting and parental mental health, controlling for parent and child age. Model comparisons explored cross‐country differences. Results Higher coparenting quality was mostly consistently associated with lower depressive symptoms among both fathers and mothers. Higher coparenting quality was associated with lower parenting stress for both mothers and fathers in the three countries studied (Brazil, Italy, United States). Model comparisons revealed limited cross‐national d…

title: Suv xo'jaligi infratuzilmasidan samarali foydalanish — iqtisodiy barqarorlikning muhim omili
abstract: В статье рассматривается экономическое значение эффективного использования водохозяйственной инфраструктуры и повышения экономического потенциала земель водного фонда. Анализируется влияние технического состояния водохозяйственных объектов, эксплуатационных затрат и потерь воды на экономические результаты. Разработаны научно-практические предложения по дифференцированной экономической оценке земель водного фонда, определению начальной арендной стоимости и формированию экономических паспортов земельных участков с учётом их местоположения, инфраструктурной обеспеченности, разрешённого использования и экологических ограничений.

title: Understanding Flood Risk Perceptions and Preparedness Gaps among Migrant and Mobile Populations in Chiang Mai, Thailand: Implications for Inclusive Flood Risk Management
abstract: Urban flood risk is increasingly shaped by population mobility, yet disaster preparedness research continues to often assume stable residence, secure housing, and equal access to official warning systems. This study examines flood risk perception and preparedness among migrant and mobile populations in Chiang Mai, Thailand. Using a mixed-methods design combining a multilingual survey (206 responses; 201 with valid mobility-status data), expert interviews (n = 16), and mapping of participant-reported flood locations, it compares hidden populations (undocumented and other precarious residents), international migrants, digital nomads, and tourists/short-term visitors. Findings show that flood risk is widely recognised but preparedness action remains limited. Prior flood experience is highest among hidden populations (76.5%) and international migrants (63.8%), yet only 6.3% of respondents report being very prepared, and 32.5% have taken no preparedness measures. Preparedness is concentrated in low-cost actions, such as saving emergency contacts, while measures requiring financial resources, stable housing, or longer-term planning are far less common. Logistic regression indicates that perceived flood likelihood and institutional trust are positively associated with undertaking at least one preparedness action. However, preparedness still centres on relatively low-cost behaviours, s…
venue: Journal of Hazards, Risk and Resilience

title: THE ROLE OF SIRI' CULTURE IN FRAUD PREVENTION: ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY IN VILLAGE FUND MANAGEMENT
abstract: The management of village funds requires effective governance mechanisms to prevent fraud, particularly through accountability and transparency. In addition to these formal mechanisms, local cultural values such as Siri’ culture, which emphasizes self-worth, honor, and moral responsibility, may potentially strengthen fraud prevention mechanisms. This study examines the effects of accountability and transparency on fraud prevention in village fund management and investigates the moderating role of Siri’ culture in these relationships. A quantitative approach was employed using questionnaires distributed to 121 respondents, including village officials, members of the Village Consultative Body (BPD), and hamlet heads from 11 villages in Karossa District, Central Mamuju Regency. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with WarpPLS 7.0. The results show that accountability and transparency have positive and significant effects on fraud prevention. However, Siri’ culture does not significantly moderate the relationship between accountability and fraud prevention or the relationship between transparency and fraud prevention. These findings indicate that accountability and transparency play important roles in fraud prevention in village fund management, while the effectiveness of these mechanisms does not significantly differ according to t…

title: NURSES' KNOWLEDGE AND ATTITUDES TOWARD CANCER PAIN MANAGEMENT: A LITERATURE REVIEW
Conservative Management of a Displaced Iliopsoas Avulsion in an Adolescent: A Case Report and Systematic Review
abstract: Objective: To report a case of traumatic iliopsoas tendon avulsion with displacement exceeding the commonly cited 2-cm surgical threshold, managed successfully without surgery, and to systematically review the literature on optimal treatment and return-to-sport outcomes. Design: Case report combined with a PRISMA-compliant systematic review of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase. Setting: Level I university trauma center; systematic review of published case reports and series. Participants: A 16-year-old male competitive soccer player (index case) and 58 additional patients from the literature, predominantly adolescent males with sports-related iliopsoas avulsion. Interventions: The index patient received conservative treatment with staged weight bearing and structured physiotherapy. Across the literature, 90% (52/58) were treated conservatively and 10% operatively. Main Outcome Measures: Clinical recovery, strength restoration, radiographic union on MRI, and return to sport. Results: Eighteen studies (58 patients; 59 including this case) were analyzed. A bony lesser-trochanter avulsion was present in 98% (57/58). Of at least 9 patients with displacement >2 cm, 5 recovered fully nonoperatively. The index patient was pain-free with full strength and unrestricted soccer return at 3 months; 6-month MRI showed radiographic nonunion despite complete functional recovery. Return to s…
