title: La bien-pensance ‘right-thinking’ as a discursive stigma: An analysis of contemporary media uses of a polarizing hetero-categorization
abstract: Depuis plusieurs années, les désignations « bien-pensants » et « bien-pensance » connaissent un regain de circulation dans les médias français, notamment dans les controverses liées au wokisme. Initialement porteur d’une valeur positive, le terme a subi un retournement axiologique et fonctionne désormais, dans certains discours médiatiques conservateurs ou réactionnaires, comme un stigmate polémique. Employé en hétéro-désignation, il assigne à l’adversaire une posture morale jugée dogmatique ou hypocrite, tout en permettant au locuteur de se construire un ethos dissident et lucide face à une pensée présentée comme dominante. Adossée à une analyse du discours énonciativiste, cette étude examine comment le lexique de la « bien-pensance » devient un outil de disqualification idéologique dans des éditoriaux et tribunes. L’analyse combine une approche sémantique et une approche pragma-énonciative attentive à la modalisation, aux phénomènes de dialogisme et à la construction des frontières symboliques entre nous et eux. L’hypothèse centrale est que bien-pensants agit comme un opérateur d’antidoxa produisant trois effets majeurs : disqualification morale de l’adversaire, auto-légitimation dissidente et polarisation du débat public. Ces formules apparaissent ainsi comme des marqueurs de rupture révélateurs des tensions axiologiques et idéologiques contemporaines dans l’espace médiatiqu…

title: Stablecoin Liquidity and U.S. Monetary Policy Transmission
Central bank tone and financial markets: evidence from the European central bank
Financial Performance Analysis of PT Indonesia Kendaraan Terminal Tbk Based on Liquidity, Solvency, Activity, and Profitability Ratios for the 2022–2025 Period
abstract: This study aims to analyze the financial performance of PT Indonesia Kendaraan Terminal Tbk based on liquidity, solvency, activity, and profitability ratios during the 2022–2025 period. The study employs a descriptive method with a quantitative approach using secondary data in the form of the company’s annual financial statements obtained from the Indonesia Stock Exchange. The results indicate that, overall, the company’s financial performance improved during the study period. The liquidity ratios, consisting of the Current Ratio (CR) and Cash Ratio (CaR), demonstrate a very strong ability to meet short-term obligations, while the solvency ratios, consisting of the Debt-to-Asset Ratio (DAR) and Debt-to-Equity Ratio (DER), reflect a sound capital structure with relatively low levels of debt. In terms of activity ratios, TATO and FATO increased, while WCTO showed a declining trend, indicating that working capital management efficiency still needs to be improved. The profitability ratios, consisting of NPM, ROA, and ROE, also showed an increasing trend, indicating that the company’s ability to generate profits improved. Overall, PT Indonesia Kendaraan Terminal Tbk demonstrated good financial performance throughout the study period.
venue: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research

title: Is There a Shift to the Right among Young People in Germany?
What are the roles of sex and gender in antimicrobial resistance? Evidence across infection, selection and transmission
abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance is shaped by biosocial and microbiological processes, yet sex and gender have not been systematically framed across the three domains (infection, antibiotic selection and transmission) that lead to drug-resistant infection. Synthesising available evidence, we find no consistent sex or gender bias in resistance prevalence; where differences are reported, prevalence is more often higher in men. Context-specific analyses are needed to determine how gendered interventions should be, if at all.

title: DETERMINANTS OF VILLAGE FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT EFFECTIVENESS: SISKEUDES UTILIZATION, APPARATUS COMPETENCY, AND INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEM IN SINDUE DISTRICT
abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of SISKEUDES utilization, apparatus competency, and internal control system on the effectiveness of village financial management in Sindue District, Donggala Regency. Effective village financial management plays an important role in supporting transparent, accountable, and responsible village governance. This study employed a quantitative approach using a survey design. Data were collected through structured questionnaires distributed to 104 village officials from 13 villages, consisting of village heads, village secretaries, finance officers, general affairs officers, planning officers, welfare officers, service officers, and government officers. The sampling technique used was saturated sampling. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS. The results indicate that SISKEUDES utilization has a positive and significant effect on village financial management effectiveness (p < 0.05), while apparatus competency also has a positive and significant effect (p < 0.05). Meanwhile, internal control system does not have a significant effect (p > 0.05). Simultaneously, SISKEUDES utilization, apparatus competency, and internal control system significantly affect village financial management effectiveness (p < 0.05). This study concludes that SISKEUDES utilization and apparatus competency are significant factors ass…

title: Bovine leukemia virus and dairy youngstock: a narrative review of early-life transmission and its consequences for whole-herd control
abstract: Bovine Leukemia Virus (BLV) is a retrovirus that causes a lifelong infection in cattle through the integration of proviral DNA into the host genome, creating immune dysfunction. Youngstock, females born and raised on dairy farms with the purpose of entering the milking herd, are exposed to BLV through both vertical and horizontal transmission risks. As youngstock progress through distinct management development periods (fetal and neonatal, preweaning, and post-weaning), each presents unique exposure risks that require different management strategies to aid in the mitigation of BLV. The failure to address BLV infection in youngstock allows infected replacement animals to enter the milking herd, undermining any mature cow-focused control strategies. The economic impacts may also be compounded by reduced return on investment in youngstock. Targeted interventions during the youngstock periods, informed by diagnostic screening for BLV and improved management strategies, are essential to disrupt the cycle of infected youngstock entering the milking herd. Incorporating BLV control measures with the entire herd offers a more sustainable approach to reducing BLV prevalence and limiting its long-term effects on animal health and profitability.

title: The Rise of Alternatives
abstract: Abstract Since the 2000s, U.S. public pension funds have actively shifted their risky investments away from public equities and toward alternative assets like private equity and hedge funds—some much more than others. We explore a range of possible explanations for these trends and argue that beliefs about the risk-adjusted return of alternatives have played a central role. Pension beliefs are shaped by investment consultants, peers, and experience in the 1990s. Other demand-side channels related to risk-seeking motives, spending needs, and fund governance have weaker empirical support. We also consider supply-side factors and agency interpretations of the data. (JEL G11, G23, G41, H75)

title: The Impact of Overall Financial Viability on Entrepreneurial Intention in South Africa
abstract: This study examined the relationship between overall financial viability (OFV) and entrepreneurial intention (EI) in South Africa by extending the entrepreneurial potential model created by Krueger and Brazeal (1994 , Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice , 18, 3, 91–104). OFV was derived from human-centric design as an antecedent of perceived feasibility. OFV was implemented as a second-order construct consisting of venture profitability, venture financing and personal financial well-being. Structural equation modelling was applied to data from 306 respondents recruited via snowball sampling. OFV positively and significantly predicted perceived feasibility ( β = 0.622, p < .001). Venture profitability ( β = 0.730) and venture financing ( β = 0.174) were significant antecedents of OFV, while personal financial well-being was non-significant ( β = −0.025, p = .443). This finding may reflect the necessity-driven entrepreneurial context of South Africa. The extended model achieved acceptable fit only under relaxed thresholds (comparative fit index = 0.906, Tucker–Lewis index = 0.894, root mean square error of approximation = 0.081), and the non-probability sample limits generalisation. The cross-sectional design rules out causal inference. These findings offer an empirical extension of EI theory with context-specific implications for entrepreneurship education and incubation progra…
venue: Journal of Entrepreneurship and Innovation in Emerging Economies

title: Contemporary elective right hemicolectomy in Scotland: a National Enhanced Recovery Colorectal Initiative (NERCI) study
abstract: Abstract Background This study describes the introduction of a Scottish nationwide implementation programme to establish Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) care following colorectal surgery. The National Enhanced Recovery Colorectal Initiative (NERCI) dataset is presented for right hemicolectomy, with Public Health Scotland records used to validate the results. Methods This was a national cross-sectional observational study of Scottish patients undergoing elective right hemicolectomy using two large orthogonal datasets: the NERCI database 2016–2024 and the Scottish Morbidity Records (SMR01) database coded from all inpatient episodes between 2010 and 2024. Results There were 12,853 elective right hemicolectomy operations recorded in the SMR01 database between 2010 and 2024. Prior to the introduction of NERCI (2010–2015) the median length of stay was 7 days compared with 5 days between 2016 and 2024. Between 2016 and 2024, there were 5342 right hemicolectomies recorded in the NERCI database compared with 7881 in the SMR01 database, indicating a 67.3% total case capture. Case capture was near complete for minimally invasive surgery procedures (considerably less so for open surgery ~28%), and annualised length of stay, mortality and 30-day readmission were strongly correlated between datasets. In the NERCI dataset, the majority of procedures were performed for cancer (87%) and …

title: The Clash between the Right to Privacy and the First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution during American Presidential Campaigns
abstract: Big Data analysis has fundamentally reshaped American presidential campaigns. At the heart of this shift is electoral microtargeting, which involves the meticulous profiling of citizens for highly customized political communications. Current study explores the complexities produced by such practices. The friction between First Amendment which protects the political expression and the right to everyone’s personal privacy. Although American courts consistently uphold broad safeguards for political discourse, the large-scale aggregating of sensitive psychographic information by campaign organizations and private data brokers operates largely outside the current disjointed and highly fragmented U.S. data privacy regime. Current research aims to highlight legal deficiencies and evaluate the degree to which the prevailing First Amendment paradigm might counterintuitively impair democratic processes trapping voters in asymmetric information bubbles. The findings underscore a pressing need for comprehensive federal statutory reforms that would reconcile the freedom to campaign with mandates for transparency and stronger data security.

title: Rational Design of Potent and Highly Selective FGFR1 Irreversible Inhibitors Guided by Molecular Dynamics Simulations
abstract: Abstract Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed distinct P-loop conformational differences in the ATP-binding domain between FGFR1 and other FGFR subtypes. A conformation-restricted linker optimization strategy was applied to identify a potent and selective irreversible FGFR1 inhibitor (compound 24). MD models demonstrated that the covalent warhead of compound 24 retained an optimal distance and orientation toward the P-loop cysteine of FGFR1, facilitating efficient Michael addition. After covalent conjugation, compound 24 interacted with the hinge region and precisely matched the unique FGFR1 conformation. Its robust antitumor activity was validated in cellular, CDX, and PDX models by suppressing FGFR1-dependent tumor growth, providing a novel strategy for subtype-selective FGFR1 inhibitor development.

title: AI-DRIVEN, EVIDENCE-BASED GENERATIVE DESIGN: A TEACHING FRAMEWORK FOR LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTONICS INTEGRATING RESEARCH FINDINGS, DESIGN PRECEDENTS, AND INTELLIGENT RECOGNITION AND JUDGMENT
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has entered design courses, but its use often stops at tool operation. Taking Landscape Architectonics, an undergraduate course in landscape architecture programs, as the vehicle, this paper builds a teaching framework for generative design that integrates four elements: research findings, design precedents, AI-based recognition and judgment, and AI generation. The core claim is simple. Teaching students to “use AI” means teaching them to run an evidence-constrained generative design chain. “AI-driven” therefore carries two meanings: at the tool level, AI executes generation; at the teaching level, evidence steers generation, and the work of teaching lies in leading students from the former toward the latter. Among the four elements, research findings and design precedents are static knowledge that travels across sites. Research findings supply criteria for what counts as good. Design precedents supply examples of what to do, distilled from 13 street design guidelines into 114 retrievable situation packages. AI-based recognition and AI generation produce dynamic outputs anchored to a specific site. Students mobilize these elements through three stages—reading the site, grounding the context, and giving form—and a chain of evidence disciplines each stage. The framework follows three design principles: complementary elements, partial embedding, and ex…

title: Generalized‐Udwadia–Kalaba‐Theory‐Based Robust Constraint Following Control Design for Wheeled Mobile Robot System With Equality and Inequality Constraints
abstract: ABSTRACT Ensuring high‐precision trajectory tracking for wheeled mobile robots operating under complex constraints and uncertainties remains a critical challenge. To address this, we propose a robust constraint‐following control framework based on Generalized Udwadia‐Kalaba theory, capable of simultaneously enforcing both equality and inequality constraints while handling system uncertainty. First, based on the diffeomorphism transformation, the constrained state variables are mapped into the unconstrained space. Second, an error dynamic model of the WMR is integrated with a GUK‐based robust controller to make the variable precisely follow both equality and inequality constraints. Through Lyapunov analysis, we prove the system achieves uniform boundedness and uniform ultimate boundedness. Finally, simulations on the WMR demonstrate that the controller ensures precise constraint following without violating safety boundaries and outperforms existing methods in some aspects, including convergence speed and error performance.
venue: International Journal of Robust and Nonlinear Control

title: A comprehensive review of advanced manufacturing techniques, ai-enabled design, and mechanical characterization of nature-inspired helicoidal hybrid composites for impact-resistant applications
abstract: Abstract Helicoidal structures mimic nature and are evident in plant cell walls, lamellar bone, and the shell structures of mantis shrimp and beetles. These nature-inspired helicoidal composites are widely used in impact-resistant applications. Traditional hand-layup methods for producing layered helicoidal composites can introduce defects such as gaps, overlaps, and wrinkles, which can be mitigated using Automated Fiber Placement (AFP). Optimizing AFP process parameters, including pressure, temperature, and layup speed, is crucial. While experimental optimization is costly and time-consuming, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based design offers a more efficient alternative. This narrative review explores the inspiration behind helicoidal structures and their application fields. It also covers advanced manufacturing of hybrid long-fiber layered composites using AFP + autoclave/hot press, ceramic filler-based nanocomposites using direct ink writing (DIW), and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-based nanocomposites using digital micromirror device (DMD). Furthermore, it discusses the roles of machine learning and deep learning, coupled with finite element modeling, in minimizing process-induced defects. Compared with conventional AFP inspection techniques such as laser profilometry and thermography, a defect-detection algorithm based on PointNet + + , a convolutional neural network…

title: Design and application research of outdoor microclimate improvement facilities
abstract: Abstract The rapid development of urban construction in China has caused many ecological problems in recent years. Meanwhile, fast-paced lifestyle brings great mental pressure to its population. Designing and creating suitable outdoor spaces and microclimate that can relax people's bodies and minds presents a potential means of addressing these challenges. Using human comfort as metric, this study discusses the relevant micro-factors that affect outdoor microclimate and proposes the landscape measures for improving it. Through case studies, it establishes the design-microclimate outcome relationship by identifying three types of facilities, landscape, sunshade, and atomization, that have the most significant impacts on outdoor microclimate and by demonstrating their applicability to specific sites.

title: Enhanced system dynamics in distributed generation based modern day hybrid power system
abstract: Abstract This research examines the frequency mitigation of a hybrid power system that incorporates with both distributed generation resources. The developed system is equipped with suitable system non-linearity for practicality. A novel fractional tilt based controller is proposed for this system. The efficacy of the proposed controlling strategy is assessed from existing controllers documented in the literature for similar power systems. Meta-heuristic methods have been used to optimise controller gains. The impact of solar and wind, on system dynamics is also explored. Further, the hybrid energy storage devices are included to evaluate its impact. Finally, a sensibility study is performed for variations in load demand.

title: Frameworks of Power: Redux
Tea exports from India: Growth patterns, market stability, transition dynamics and future outlook
abstract: This study analysed the growth performance, instability, changing export patterns of Indian tea over a last 20 years period and export projections for next five years. The secondary data sourced from the UN Comtrade was collected for the study purpose. The findings of the analysis revealed that the export of tea from India experienced a significant and positive growth trend at 1 per cent level of significance. The instability index for export value was lower than that of the export quantity suggesting that export earnings were relatively more stable compared to the fluctuations observed in export volumes. In terms of stability of export destinations, Iraq was identified as most stable country in importing tea from India with the highest retention of India’s tea export share followed by Russia, countries aggregated ‘others’ category, Iran and UAE. On the other hand, the USA was found to be the least stable country indicating poor retention of trade share and limited reliability for sustained tea exports. Indian tea export projections indicated positive trends in Russia, Iran and the countries pooled under the category ‘others’ reflecting strengthening market potential in these destinations.

title: Fixed Assets Management System (FAMS) with Rule- Based Predictive Forecasting for Asset Lifecycle Management
abstract: Effective management of fixed assets is important for organizations that depend on physical resources to sustain daily operations, comply with regulatory requirements, and maintain financial accountability. This study examined the current fixed asset management practices of an organization and proposed a Fixed Assets Management System (FAMS) that integrates Rule-Based Criteria Matching (RBCM) and rule-based predictive forecasting using asset lifecycle information. The study focused on identifying difficulties in the existing asset management process, determining the features considered necessary for the proposed system, and assessing its potential user acceptance through the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). This study employed a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design within a descriptive-developmental framework, involving thirty (30) purposively selected respondents consisting of strategic decision-makers, operational users, and technical evaluators. Quantitative data were collected through a structured questionnaire and summarized using frequency counts, percentages, and weighted means, while semi-structured interviews and open-ended responses provided explanatory qualitative insights. Results indicated that respondents considered the existing manual asset management process to have substantial operational difficulties, particularly in maintaining inventory accuracy, mo…
venue: Technologique: A Global Journal on Technological Developments and Scientific Innovations

title: Small-Scale Renewable Energy Market: Exploring Opportunities and Challenges Within a Selected African Electricity Distribution Company
abstract: The market for small-scale renewable energy has increased in Africa as a strategy for the diversification of electricity supply and mitigation of power cuts, thus promoting sustainable energy solutions. The market is however faced with many challenges despite its vast potential The study made an exploration of the small- scale renewable energy (SSRE) market for a selected electricity company in Africa. Specifically, the study identified opportunities and challenges that are associated with participating in this energy market. The Socio-Technical Transition Theory formed a key part of the study. The study adopted a qualitative research approach, with purposive sampling, and a sample size of 20 managers. Semi-structured interviews were conducted online, and data was analysed using thermatic analysis. The results show that the electricity company participation in the SSRE market is important in improving service delivery, enhances benefits amongst various stakeholder categories. However, the study found that participation in the SSRE market is constrained by grid infrastructural issues, high connection and compliance costs, regulatory complexities the low customer awareness and workforce incapacity. The study recommends that the electricity company should invest in the expansion and upgrading of distribution network, implement vigorous marketing campaigns and continued investment …

title: Do LLM-derived text features improve electricity price forecasts beyond document activity? Evidence from Australia's National Electricity Market
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can turn market notices and news into features for electricity price forecasting. Such features also record when documents arrive and whether their extraction failed, so a gain measured against a model without text can reflect document activity as well as content. We add the counts of the same documents and of their failed extractions to a no-text LightGBM model and measure each LLM representation against this activity reference, which needs no additional LLM requests. With gpt-6-luna as the extractor, we forecast Australian electricity prices from operator notices (5-30 minutes ahead) and WattClarity news (day-ahead) after the extractor's documented knowledge cutoff, averaging forecasts over three training seeds. For news, the counts alone lower mean absolute error (MAE) by 3.0%, most of the 3.6% reduction that the better LLM representation achieves relative to the no-text model; its increment beyond the counts is not significant. For notices, two of the three LLM representations lower MAE beyond the counts, by 0.14-0.21% and 0.45-0.52%, whether the counts are cumulative or cover recent windows, whereas the third shows no significant reduction. Time-shifted placebos give mixed evidence on whether these gains require text aligned with the target. Benchmarks using the operator's pre-dispatch forecasts (notices) or price history alone (news) are more …

title: Response-Tailored or Standard-Duration Antibiotic Treatment for Infective Endocarditis
Micro–Macro Synergistic Engineering of Metal-Organic Framework-Intercalated GO Membranes for Efficient Solar-DrivenWater-Electricity Cogeneration
abstract: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporation and thermoelectric cogeneration present sustainable pathways to address global water and energy scarcity. Among various photothermal materials, 2D graphene oxide (GO) membrane evaporators have attracted considerable attention. However, they suffer from restricted water transport and poor heat localization, leading to unsatisfactory evaporation performance. Herein, we report a micro–macro synergistic engineering strategy to construct ZIF-8-intercalated GO composite membranes with a central macroscopic perforation (GO-MOF30-1.5) for efficient solar water-electricity cogeneration. At the microscale, the intercalation of ZIF-8 nanoparticles expands the interlayer spacing, creates abundant light-trapping sites, and enhances both water transport and photothermal conversion. At the macroscale, the central hole eliminates the “evaporation dead zone”, improves thermal convection, and accelerates vapor escape. Benefiting from this hierarchical design, the optimized GO-MOF30-1.5 membrane achieves a broadband solar absorptance of 86.21% under one sun. Consequently, it delivers a high evaporation rate of 1.53 kg m–2 h–1 with an outstanding evaporation efficiency of 91.91%. The membrane also exhibits excellent salt tolerance and long-term cycling stability. When coupled with a thermoelectric module, the system produces a stable open-circuit volta…

title: Defining kratom: evidence-based policy guidelines for a rapidly evolving market
abstract: The leaves of Mitragyna speciosa, commonly called kratom, have been consumed for centuries in Southeast Asia for their energizing and analgesic properties. Over the last decade kratom has gained popularity in the United States, with an estimated 10–16 million consumers, and a wide variety of products have become available in the marketplace. Along with a plethora of product formulations that contain various concentrations of kratom alkaloids, new products have emerged, labelled as “kratom”, but comprised of highly concentrated synthetic alkaloids. Consumers and regulators alike struggle to differentiate the spectrum of products that range from those similar in composition to traditional kratom to those that are illegally marketed, unapproved novel drugs. With significant implications to public health policy and safety, there is a need to clearly define and differentiate kratom, kratom-derived, and synthetic products. Herein we offer guidance to support standardization of the terminology used in the manufacture and labelling of kratom and kratom-derived products in the United States. This is intended to be a reference tool for use by industry and federal, state, and other jurisdictions that oversee the kratom industry to encourage clear and consistent communication.

title: Preface: 5th International Conference on Financial Technology and Market Management (FTMM 2026)
abstract: The 2026 5th International Conference on Financial Technology and Market Management (FTMM 2026) have been conducted during September 26-27, 2026, in San Francisco, USA. This conference aims to bring together leading academic scientists, researchers, and scholars to exchange and share their experiences and research results on all aspects of economics, business, and marketing management. It also provides a premier interdisciplinary platform for researchers, practitioners, and educators to present and discuss the most recent innovations, trends, and concerns as well as practical challenges encountered and solutions adopted in the fields of economics, business, and marketing management. About 24 presentations including 3 plenary talks were presented. The presentations are grouped into 9 areas of particular interest: (1): Economic and monetary crisis, (2): Taxes and regulation, (3): Emerging markets issues, (4): Corporate finance and governance, (5): Asset pricing, investment, and portfolio management, (6): Financial markets, (7): Risk management and quantitative finance, (8) Econometric modeling and empirical issues, (9): Mathematical Finance. With best regards, Conference Organizing Chair San Francisco, USA
venue: Highlights in Business, Economics and Management

title: The Market Power Effect of Uniform Delivered Pricing and Platform Competition
Double-edged sword of market-political orientation ambidexterity on firm growth in transition economies: an institutional logics perspective
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the double-edged effects of market-political orientation ambidexterity (MPOA) on firm growth in transition economies. From the view of institutional logics, we examine the contradictory mechanisms of MPOA on firm growth, opportunity identification versus opportunity exploitation, and explore the moderating roles of internal coordination capability and stakeholder engagement capability. Design/methodology/approach We used on-site survey data from 238 Chinese firms to test our hypotheses via hierarchical regression analysis. Survey data are appropriate for measuring strategic orientations, which are the strategic philosophies or logics guiding strategic attention and resource allocation for superior performance. Findings MPOA enhances policy opportunity identification but reduces business model efficiency. Policy opportunity identification and business model efficiency positively contribute to firm growth. The positive effect of MPOA on policy opportunity identification is strengthened by internal coordination capability but weakened by stakeholder engagement capability. The negative effect of MPOA on business model efficiency is weakened by stakeholder engagement capability. Originality/value Firms with MPOA are characterized as multifunctional organizations that incorporate elements from both state logic and market logic. From different views …

title: Different houses, different channels: Monetary policy, macroprudential regulation, and bank liquidity in Indonesia’s housing market
abstract: Existing studies typically assume that monetary and macroprudential policies are transmitted uniformly across housing markets, despite substantial differences in financing structures and buyer characteristics across housing segments. This study addresses this gap by examining whether the effects of monetary policy, macroprudential regulation, and bank liquidity differ across small, medium, and large housing markets in Indonesia. Using quarterly panel data from 17 provinces covering 2012Q1–2024Q4, we employ a fixed-effects framework to estimate the effects of interest rates, Loan-to-Value (LTV) regulation, bank liquidity, and their interaction on segment-specific housing prices. The results provide strong evidence of heterogeneous policy transmission. LTV policy significantly affects housing prices across all segments, whereas monetary policy significantly affects small and medium house prices but not large house prices. Moreover, the interaction between LTV policy and bank liquidity is significant only in the large-house segment, indicating that the transmission of macroprudential policy varies with housing market size and liquidity conditions. These findings demonstrate that aggregate housing price responses can mask important differences across market segments. The study contributes to the housing policy literature by providing segment-level evidence on the heterogeneous tran…

title: Integrating labor-market data and sustainability competencies: a framework demonstrated through the sustainable systems science major at Virginia Tech
abstract: Purpose Sustainability-focused education is essential for preparing students to address the complex, interdisciplinary challenges of global environmental and social change. Yet, fast-evolving labor-market demands and technological change can create misalignment between academic sustainability programs and the workforce competencies expected in sustainability-related careers. This paper aims to present a case study of the sustainable systems science major at Virginia Tech; a newly developed undergraduate program created in tandem with a broader curriculum redesign in the Department of Sustainable Biomaterials. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on program documentation, sustainability education literature and occupational data, this study examines the design and implementation processes undertaken in 2021–2022. The curriculum development process integrated two evidence-based design tools: (1) a validated sustainability competency framework and; (2) national labor-market intelligence, specifically knowledge, skills and abilities (KSAs) from the US Department of Labor’s occupational information network (O*NET) system. This dual integration guided curriculum structure, course development and learning outcomes to support both academic rigor and workforce relevance. Findings The case demonstrates how embedding sustainability competencies alongside occupational data can strengthen al…
venue: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education

title: TRANSFORMASI UMKM MENUJU INTERNATIONAL MARKET: IMPLEMENTASI PROGRAM EDUKASI DI KELURAHAN DUKUH SUTOREJO KOTA SURABAYA
abstract: Kegiatan pengabdian masyarakat melalui program Kuliah Kerja Nyata (KKN) di Kelurahan Dukuh Sutorejo, Surabaya, bertujuan untuk mendorong Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) agar siap bersaing di pasar internasional. Melalui seminar “UMKM Go International Market”, program ini memberikan edukasi seputar strategi ekspor, pemasaran digital, dan penguatan branding produk lokal. Pendekatan yang digunakan meliputi observasi kebutuhan, pelaksanaan seminar interaktif, serta evaluasi berbasis kuesioner. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan adanya peningkatan pemahaman pelaku UMKM terhadap potensi pasar global, pentingnya inovasi produk, dan penggunaan teknologi dalam pemasaran. Antusiasme peserta serta kesadaran akan peluang ekspor menjadi indikator keberhasilan program ini. Diharapkan kegiatan serupa dapat terus diadakan secara berkala untuk memperkuat kesiapan UMKM dalam menghadapi tantangan pasar internasional yang terus berkembang.

title: Vehicle Response-based Mode Shape Extraction of Damped Bridges Using an Enhanced Three-step Approach
Unamortized black-box variational inference for joint response and response time models
abstract: Abstract An important aspect of psychometric model application is the choice of a suitable algorithm for parameter estimation. Particularly in the case of large datasets and high dimensional models, conventional algorithms may be inapplicable or relatively slow. As a remedy, variational inference was suggested in machine learning. While amortized variational inference algorithms are already established for several psychometric models, there has been little research on unamortized variational inference algorithms. In this article, we investigate the accuracy of this estimation method for a multidimensional variation of the joint model for responses and response times proposed by Van der Linden (Psychometrika 72: 287-308, 2007). Our results indicate that the proposed algorithm can be used for accurate item parameter estimation of these models even in relatively small datasets. In addition it is computationally fast in large datasets. We applied the method to a multidimensional empirical dataset in clinical psychology.

title: Assessment of PI controller parameters for transient response optimization of DFIG-based WECS
When volunteer mobilization outpaces coordination: workflow repair in disaster response
abstract: Purpose This study examines what happens when rapid volunteer mobilization expands faster than the capacity to organize heterogeneous people, information, resources and tasks during disaster response. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a single embedded qualitative process design centered on a rapidly scaled, messaging-mediated volunteer response following a September 2025 barrier-lake flood in eastern Taiwan. The primary process evidence consists of contemporaneous records from the focal coordination group, supplemented by targeted traces from task-specific subgroups, two public forums, nine semi-structured interviews, five fieldnote-based observations and open-ended volunteer accounts. Findings Mobilization-generated coordination strain became visible through repeated verification, misrouting, uneven task allocation, stale or ambiguous requests and situations in which volunteers or resources accumulated in some locations while remaining needed elsewhere. The analysis identifies three recurrent forms of workflow repair: functional differentiation, boundary regulation and intermediary translation. These practices were observably enacted and reused, but repair remained partial, uneven and subject to changing task demand, participant learning, formal intervention and safety constraints. Originality/value The study distinguishes the capacity to mobilize help from the capac…
venue: Disaster Prevention and Management: An International Journal

title: Soil–plant transfer of Mn, Mo, and Zn and tea quality response to microelement fertilization in yellow-gleyic pseudopodzolic soils of Lankaran, Azerbaijan
Resistance-gene minority variation and delayed microbiological response in rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis
abstract: Introduction Routine whole-genome sequencing (WGS) interpretation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistance focuses mainly on consensus-level mutations. Minority variants, quantified by allele frequency (AF), may indicate resistant subpopulations under drug pressure, but their association with treatment response in rifampicin-resistant or multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (RR/MDR-TB) remains unclear. Methods We retrospectively analysed RR/MDR-TB patients treated in Ningbo, China, from 2021 to 2025, integrating clinical, phenotypic, treatment, microbiological, and WGS data. Minority resistance-associated variants (RAVs) were defined as low-frequency variants matching WHO V2 mutation catalogue entries at AF ≥ 3%, with AF ≥ 5% defining the primary higher-frequency subset. Per-drug analyses excluded patients whose target genes had median depth <200×. Associations with microbiological response were assessed using covariate-adjusted logistic regression, with higher-frequency and treatment-matched variants examined secondarily. Results We analysed 229 RR/MDR-TB patients with linked WGS, treatment, and microbiological follow-up data. Fixed RAVs (WHO V2 catalogue-annotated) were carried by 220/229 patients (median 3, IQR 2–5). Minority RAVs at AF ≥ 3% were detected in 13 patients. Overall minority-RAV burden was not clearly associated with microbiological response after adjustment. The…
venue: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

title: Decolonising borders and reimagining African solidarity: A theological response to xenophobia in South Africa through Ubuntu, Black Theology of Liberation and the Azanian imagination
abstract: Xenophobia in post-apartheid South Africa remains a persistent socio-political and ethical challenge that exposes deep contradictions within African solidarity and the unfinished project of liberation. This article argues that xenophobia is not an episodic or spontaneous social malfunction but a historically produced manifestation of coloniality, which continues to structure identity, citizenship and belonging in contemporary South Africa. Although apartheid formally ended, violence directed at African migrants reveals the persistence of colonial border regimes, nationalist imaginaries and socio-economic inequalities that continue to produce exclusionary forms of belonging. Drawing on Ubuntu philosophy, Black Theology of Liberation, liberation theology and decolonial thought, the article develops a theological framework for interpreting xenophobia as a structurally embedded condition of modern colonial formation. It further proposes Azania as a decolonial theological imagination through which African identity and solidarity may be rethought beyond inherited colonial cartographies of territory and nationhood. Within this framework, belonging is reimagined as relational, ethical and grounded in shared humanity rather than legal or territorial classification. The article ultimately advances a theology of African solidarity rooted in hospitality, justice and relational personhood. …

title: Subjective alcohol response across drinking contexts: a systematic review with bayesian meta-analysis
Optimization of external tilt-control setpoints for a superconducting gravimeter based on internal displacement voltage response
abstract: Abstract The external tilt control state is one of the important factors affecting the long-term stable observation of superconducting gravimeters. Influenced by factors such as mechanical assembly errors of the instrument and relative position deviations between internal and external structures, the horizontal zero position of the external tilt control system is not necessarily equivalent to the optimal response state of the internal superconducting magnetic levitation sensing system. To address this issue, this paper proposes an optimization method for the external tilt setpoint based on the internal displacement voltage response, establishing a local response model among external tilt, magnetic levitation force balance, and displacement voltage under small tilt angle and locally quasi-static conditions. A local quadratic relationship is established using the mean tilt angle and mean displacement voltage within the plateau segment, and verified through the original local scanning and supplementary experiments adopting a fixed tilt step size and a unified recording duration. The supplementary experiments yield average extreme positions of -4309.75 μrad and -3997.92 μrad for the X-axis and Y-axis, respectively, with inter-test sample standard deviations of 6.89 μrad and 7.16 μrad, respectively. The average extreme positions of the two axes differ from the original experimental …

title: Rapid response characterization of 2025 FA22 in support of the IAWN campaign: Observations from Europe
abstract: The near-Earth asteroid 2025 FA22 was the focus of a coordinated international campaign by the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN) to stress-test planetary defense responses following its discovery in March 2025. We provide a multi-technique physical characterization using European assets in the framework of the European NEOPOPS project. The primary goals were to determine the asteroid's rotation period, surface composition, and size in order to assess crucial aspects for planetary defense and support the broader IAWN campaign. Characterization involved coordinated photometry, visible spectroscopy, and bistatic radar observations. The asteroid has a synodic rotation period of 13.084 ± 0.007 h, a potentially homogeneous surface composition consistent with X- or Sx-type, and an estimated mean effective diameter of 162 ± 21 m. Radar measurements established lower bounds consistent with an elongated shape inferred from the light curve, but the size interpretation remains dependent on geometry. We obtained multi-technique characterization within weeks from the alert, demonstrating the effectiveness of rapid coordinated visible and radar observations for potential impactors within the tight operational windows required for planetary defense.

title: Joint production and demand planning in reverse logistics with blockchain influences
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to formulate a joint production and pricing model within a blockchain-enabled reverse logistics system. The authors’ analysis reveals that the optimal production quantity follows a benchmark-type policy: it decreases with the inventory level, while the optimal planned mean demand increases with inventory. These structural results are derived through theoretical analysis and further validated through numerical simulations. Design/methodology/approach This paper develops a joint production and pricing model in a blockchain-enabled reverse logistics system. The analysis reveals that the optimal production quantity follows a benchmark-style policy – decreasing with inventory – while the optimal planned mean demand increases with inventory. The authors examine how three blockchain-influenced factors – demand multiplier, demand variability and reverse logistics cost – affect firm decisions and expected profit. Findings Numerical results show that a higher demand multiplier enhances profitability and justifies greater production. In contrast, increased demand variability, as may arise from blockchain-induced uncertainty, reduces expected profit but leads to higher production as a hedge. Higher reverse logistics costs prompt the firm to reduce production, lowering profits. Research limitations/implications Notably, the planned mean demand exhibits nonmonotonic b…

title: Transient response of a cylindrical cavity in three-dimensional elastic space under impact loading: an analytical solution
Free Vibration Response of Laminated Composite and Sandwich Microplates with Soft Porous Core Using a Non-Polynomial Zig-Zag Theory in the Refined Couple Stress Framework
Tourism demand forecasting in the artificial intelligence era using large language models
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether large language models (LLMs) can improve tourism demand forecasting accuracy compared to established statistical and machine learning approaches. Design/methodology/approach A systematic out-of-sample comparison is conducted using monthly tourism arrival data from Eurostat for eight European source markets. Benchmarks include optimized seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIMA), exponential smoothing (ETS), Prophet, Random Forest and seasonal naive models. Three LLM families are evaluated as zero-shot forecasters. Robustness is assessed across a pre-COVID stable period, a future period beyond LLM training cutoffs and an older model test. Findings LLM-based forecasts demonstrate consistent performance advantages over all benchmark models across countries and evaluation periods. In the main post-COVID period, LLMs achieve mean MASE values of 0.67–0.85 compared to 1.56 for ETS, 2.67 for SARIMA, 3.04 for Prophet and 4.32 for Random Forest. The LLM advantage persists in the pre-COVID stable period (LLM MASE 0.85–0.90 vs SARIMA 1.71 and ETS 1.31), indicating that the benefit extends beyond structural-break contexts. Robustness tests using an older LLM model and forecasts for a future period beyond LLM training data indicate that data contamination does not explain the observed performance patterns. Prompt ablation analysis re…

title: Sukuk and green bonds in the context of sustainable finance: an empirical analysis
abstract: Purpose As the climate crisis intensifies, the transition toward a sustainable economy has become increasingly urgent. This study investigates the dynamic interconnections between Islamic financial instruments, specifically sukuk differentiated by credit ratings, and sustainable finance assets, namely green bonds and clean energy indices. It aims to assess the degree of convergence between Islamic finance and sustainable finance frameworks and to evaluate whether sukuk can contribute to environmental objectives while offering diversification benefits to investors. Design/methodology/approach This study uses an empirical framework based on daily data covering the period from April 30, 2015, to May 1, 2025. The Quantile-on-Quantile (QonQ) methodology is used to capture heterogeneous dependence structures across different market conditions, allowing for the identification of nonlinear and asymmetric relationships across the entire conditional distribution. Sukuk are classified according to credit ratings (AAA, AA, A and BBB) to examine heterogeneous linkages with green bonds and clean energy markets. The results are further illustrated using three-dimensional surface plots. Findings The empirical results show that highly rated sukuk (AAA and AA) exhibit weak and nonlinear dependence with green bonds, indicating limited integration across market conditions. In contrast, lower-rated…

title: A multi-epoch search for distant Solar System bodies in the Catalina Sky Survey
abstract: Wide-field astronomical surveys have significantly expanded the population of known trans-Neptunian objects. However, detecting very distant bodies remains challenging due to their extremely slow apparent motion and faint magnitudes. Multi-epoch transient surveys provide an opportunity to identify such objects by exploiting the positional consistency in observations obtained on different nights. We developed and validated an automated detection pipeline to search archival multi-epoch survey data for faint, slow-moving bodies in the outer Solar System, and we assessed its potential for discovering previously unknown distant objects. We applied our pipeline to observations from the Catalina Sky Survey (CSS), analysing repeated images of the same sky regions obtained over multiple nights. The algorithm identifies candidate objects based on positional consistency and motion across epochs. Its performance was evaluated through recovery tests using catalogued objects and synthetic sources injected into the images, allowing us to quantify the detection efficiency as a function of apparent magnitude. The pipeline successfully recovered the distant trans-Neptunian objects Sedna and Eris in blind tests where prior catalogue information was disabled. The recovery fraction of catalogued objects approaches 100$%$ for objects brighter than 19.5 mag in the V band, while the synthetic-source r…

title: Attitudes towards pain relief and wound management, and their on-farm use during cattle dehorning in northern Australia
abstract: Context Dehorning remains a common procedure across the northern Australian beef industry due to the widespread use of horned breeds and management constraints in extensive operations. Amputation dehorning has cattle welfare and production implications, including haemorrhage, infection, flystrike, weight loss and mortality. The use of and producer attitudes towards pain relief and wound treatments are not well documented. Aims This study aimed to document cattle dehorning practices in northern Australia and identify producer-defined priorities for effective wound management treatments in extensive beef systems. Methods An online survey targeting Australian beef cattle producers was conducted between February and August 2023. Four online focus groups involving producers and industry stakeholders from northern Australia were conducted to explore attitudes, practices, experiences, and priorities related to pain relief and wound management for dehorning of cattle. Quantitative data were analysed using Fisher’s exact test and qualitative data were analysed thematically. Key results Dehorning was performed by 92.5% of northern Australian survey respondents, most commonly using surgical methods. Pain relief was used by 75% of producers, most commonly Tri Solfen® (65%) and meloxicam (28%). Multimodal analgesia was used by only a minority (15%). Relief from pain (91%) and improved wound…

title: Short- and Mid-Term Clinical, Functional, and Radiographic Outcomes of the 5C® MEDic Knee System Following Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty
abstract: Background Medial pivot total knee arthroplasty (TKA) has been developed to better reproduce native knee kinematics and improve patient satisfaction compared with conventional implant designs. This study evaluated the short- and mid-term clinical, functional, radiographic, and survivorship outcomes of the 5C® MEDic medial pivot knee system following primary TKA. Methods A retrospective cohort study included 419 primary TKAs performed in 372 patients between 2022 and 2025, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS-12), Oxford Knee Score (OKS), Forgotten Joint Score (FJS-12), visual analogue scale (VAS) satisfaction, and range of motion. Radiographic evaluation included hip–knee–ankle angle, arithmetic HKA, joint line obliquity, lateral distal femoral angle, medial proximal tibial angle, and Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee (CPAK) classification. Implant survivorship was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis. Results Significant improvements were observed in all patient-reported outcome measures at 1 year . Mean OKS improved from 20.8 preoperatively to 41.2, while KOOS subscales demonstrated substantial gains in pain, symptoms, function, sports, and quality of life. Knee flexion increased from 111.1° to 123.2°, and extension improved from −5.6° to −0.7°. Kaplan–Meier survivorship was 99.8%…

title: Kualitas Pelayanan, Fasilitas, dan Kompetensi Petugas sebagai Prediktor Kepuasan Masyarakat pada Layanan e-KTP di Kota Samarinda
abstract: Kepuasan masyarakat merupakan indikator utama kinerja pelayanan publik, tetapi belum jelas apakah fasilitas fisik berkontribusi terhadap kepuasan di luar proses layanan dan petugas ketika warga tidak dapat memilih penyedia layanan lain. Penelitian ini menguji apakah kualitas pelayanan, fasilitas pelayanan, dan kompetensi petugas berasosiasi dengan kepuasan masyarakat pada layanan Kartu Tanda Penduduk elektronik (e-KTP) di Dinas Kependudukan dan Pencatatan Sipil Kota Samarinda, Indonesia, serta apakah fasilitas masih berkontribusi secara unik setelah kedua variabel lainnya dikendalikan. Survei potong lintang yang bersifat eksplanatori-prediktif dilakukan pada Juli 2026 terhadap 100 pengguna layanan yang dipilih melalui accidental sampling. Instrumen berupa kuesioner 17 butir berskala Likert lima tingkat, dengan korelasi butir-total terkoreksi 0,321–0,615 dan koefisien Cronbach’s alpha 0,680–0,693. Data dianalisis dengan regresi linear berganda menggunakan IBM SPSS 25 setelah uji asumsi klasik. Kualitas pelayanan (β = 0,215; p = 0,025) dan kompetensi petugas (β = 0,300; p = 0,009) berasosiasi positif dan signifikan dengan kepuasan, sedangkan fasilitas tidak (β = 0,020; p = 0,861). Secara simultan, ketiga variabel berasosiasi signifikan dengan kepuasan (F = 5,626; p = 0,001) dan menjelaskan 15,0% variasinya (R² terkoreksi = 0,123). Fasilitas berkorelasi kuat dengan kompetensi petu…

title: Development and usability evaluation of a web-based inventory system for small retail enterprises
abstract: Purpose: to develop a web-based inventory system for Toko Hardi Grosir Manisan and evaluate its functional performance and usability using black-box testing and the system usability scale (SUS). Method: this study employed a user-centered design approach within the human–computer interaction (HCI) framework, involving user requirements analysis, interface design, system development, functional testing using black-box testing, and usability evaluation using the system usability scale (SUS). The collected data were analyzed descriptively to assess system functionality and usability. Findings: showed that all 13 black-box testing scenarios passed, achieving a 100% pass rate. The SUS evaluation yielded an average score of 77.0, exceeding the benchmark of 68 and indicating above-average perceived usability based on the illustrative dataset. Implications: a practical solution for improving inventory management in small retail businesses by reducing reliance on manual records, facilitating stock monitoring, and improving inventory reporting. Originality: lies in integrating web-based inventory system development, black-box testing, and SUS-based usability evaluation within the specific operational context of a confectionery wholesale business, Toko Hardi Grosir Manisan.

title: Community Participation in Project Planning and Performance of County-Funded Road Infrastructure Projects in Baringo County, Kenya
abstract: County funded road infrastructure projects in Baringo County, Kenya, continue to experience delays, stalling and incomplete delivery despite policy commitments under the County Integrated Development Plan (2023–2027) to expand and upgrade the road network. This manuscript examines the relationship between community participation in project planning and the performance of these projects. Using a correlational research design, data were collected from 88 stakeholders drawn from county government officials, project management staff, engineers, contractors, finance and procurement officers, ward administrators, and monitoring and evaluation officers, sampled from a target population of 137 through stratified random sampling. Descriptive findings showed that community participation in project planning was moderate (M = 3.47, SD = 1.19), with identification of priority needs rated highest and committee representation lowest. Performance of road infrastructure projects was similarly moderate (M = 3.47, SD = 1.19), supported by strong perceived improvements in accessibility and travel time but constrained by weak timeliness and budget adherence. Pearson correlation revealed a positive and statistically significant relationship between planning participation and project performance (r = .525, p < .001). Simple linear regression further confirmed that planning participation significantly…

title: PROSPECTS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF INFORMATION SYSTEMS (TECHNOLOGIES) IN THE SPHERE OF ECOLOGY AND NATURE MANAGEMENT ON THE BASIS OF MODEL LEGISLATION OF THE COMMONWEALTH OF INDEPENDENT STATES COUNTRIES
abstract: This article examines the process of harmonizing the legislation of CIS countries on information systems in the field of ecology and natural resource management based on the CIS Model Law “On State Information Systems in the Field of Environmental Protection, Natural Resource Management, and Environmental Safety”. The article defines the nature of the CIS model legislation as advisory acts. It also identifies the actual state of legal regulation of public relations in this area in Russia and some CIS countries. It concludes that a promising area for harmonizing the legislation of these countries is the development of unified approaches to the digitalization of information on the state of the environment and its components. Relations in the field of natural resource management and their digital development are a national issue, and harmonization is inappropriate given the national characteristics of each state.

title: Detailed study of HD 219134: A benchmark K dwarf with a compact planetary system
abstract: Space-based missions such as CoRoT, , and TESS have revolutionised asteroseismology and strengthened its synergies with exoplanet science. With PLATO and ARIEL on the horizon, these synergies will play an even more central role. Kepler We revisit the characterisation of the nearby K dwarf HD 219134 using advanced seismic diagnostics. Our goals are to investigate the reported tension between asteroseismic and interferometric radii, update the fundamental parameters of the star, refine the properties of its planetary system, and investigate the coupled rotational, magnetic, and star–planet evolution of the system, including the atmospheric mass‑loss histories of its planets. The stellar characterisation is based on detailed asteroseismic forward modelling complemented by seismic inversions to quantify systematic uncertainties associated with non‑seismic constraints, assess the compatibility of radius measurements, and evaluate the impact of surface modelling on seismic inferences. The revised stellar properties were used as inputs for rotational evolution investigations, stellar wind modelling, and high‑energy irradiation histories. Seismic inversions rule out the most recent interferometric radius determination, whereas asteroseismic and spectroscopic results are compatible with the previous interferometric measurement from 2019. We derive revised stellar mass, radius, and age o…

title: Steering sustainability: the configurational role of FinTech in governance-driven emission reduction goals in Islamic and conventional banks
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how corporate governance influences banks’ emission reduction goals (ERG), focusing on the configurational role of FinTech disclosure. Design/methodology/approach The study examines 20 banks listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange over 2020–2023 (80 bank-year observations), covering both Islamic and conventional banks. It applies fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to identify configurations of governance attributes, FinTech disclosure and bank characteristics that are sufficient for ERG. Findings The results show that no single governance attribute is sufficient to ensure ERG; instead, ERG emerge from specific configurations of governance features, FinTech disclosure and financial characteristics. Smaller boards, higher proportions of independent and female directors and strong Shariah board presence contribute to ERG when combined with high FinTech disclosure and favorable bank-level conditions. Practical implications The findings provide actionable guidance for regulators and bank boards. Strengthening governance structures (e.g. independent and diverse boards) and encouraging transparent FinTech disclosure can help integrate environmental objectives into governance and digital strategies, especially in emerging markets. Originality/value This study makes three original contributions to the Islamic and conventional banking …

title: Correction: Educational change in times of crisis: the case for system leadership
Physician admission preferences under the Diagnosis-Intervention Packet payment system: a discrete choice experiment in a Chinese tertiary hospital
abstract: Background Payment reforms seek to contain costs while maintaining quality, but their effects depend on how frontline physicians respond to financial and regulatory signals. China’s Diagnosis-Intervention Packet (DIP) reform is a case-based, point-based payment model implemented within a regional global budget. Objective To examine physicians’ admission preferences and trade-offs across clinical, financial, operational, and regulatory attributes within a tertiary hospital operating under the DIP payment system. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional discrete choice experiment among 339 physicians in a tertiary hospital in central China. Six attributes captured clinical complexity, length of stay, treatment technology, service revenue, expected DIP margin, and compliance risk. Physicians’ choice preferences and opt-out choices were analyzed using mixed logit models, and preference heterogeneity was further examined using latent class logit models. Results Expected DIP loss was strongly negatively associated with admission preference ( β = −1.81, p < 0.001), whereas expected profit was associated with a smaller positive preference ( β = 0.45, p < 0.001). A Wald test confirmed a significantly stronger response to losses than gains ( p < 0.001), consistent with loss aversion. Expected DIP margin accounted for 41.94% of relative attribute importance, followed by clinical co…

title: Glymphatic system dysfunction in stroke: the relationship between clearance failure and neuroinflammation
abstract: Abstract Stroke triggers a complex secondary injury cascade, in which neuroinflammation plays a central role. The glymphatic system is a perivascular clearance network that facilitates cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and interstitial fluid (ISF) exchange and removes metabolic waste from the brain. Recent studies suggest that glymphatic dysfunction is not simply a consequence of stroke, but also contributes to disease progression. Impaired glymphatic clearance promotes the accumulation of damage-associated molecular patterns, inflammatory mediators, and toxic metabolites within the brain parenchyma, sustaining both innate and adaptive immune responses. At the same time, inflammatory signaling, immune cell infiltration, and vascular injury progressively disrupt perivascular architecture and aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarization, leading to further impairment of glymphatic transport. As a result, glymphatic dysfunction and neuroinflammation reinforce each other, contributing to cerebral edema, persistent inflammation, and neurological deterioration after stroke. In this review, we summarize current evidence linking glymphatic dysfunction to neuroinflammation in both ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke. We discuss the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying this interaction and preclinical therapeutic approaches that may help preserve or restore glymphatic function after stroke. A better unde…

title: Pengaruh Pesonal Branding Media Sosial dan Kecerdasan Emosional Terhadap Kesiapan Kerja Mahasiswa di Kabupaten Tasikmalaya
abstract: Kesenjangan antara kompetensi akademik dan kesiapan memasuki dunia kerja masih dihadapi lulusan perguruan tinggi di Indonesia, sedangkan bukti empiris tentang peran personal branding media sosial dan kecerdasan emosional belum konsisten. Penelitian ini menganalisis asosiasi kedua variabel tersebut dengan kesiapan kerja mahasiswa di Kabupaten Tasikmalaya, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif asosiatif kausal dengan pengumpulan data cross-sectional. Sampel berjumlah 98 mahasiswa dari 14 perguruan tinggi yang dipilih secara purposif dan didominasi mahasiswa perempuan. Data dikumpulkan pada tahun 2026 melalui kuesioner tertutup berskala Likert 1–5 yang memuat 26 item adaptasi. Seluruh item dinyatakan valid dan ketiga instrumen reliabel (Cronbach's alpha ,800–,838). Data dianalisis dengan regresi linier berganda setelah uji asumsi klasik. Personal branding media sosial dan kecerdasan emosional berasosiasi positif dan signifikan dengan kesiapan kerja pada taraf signifikansi 5%, baik secara parsial maupun simultan, dan model menjelaskan 64,4% variasi kesiapan kerja. Koefisien terstandar kecerdasan emosional (β = ,577) lebih besar daripada personal branding media sosial (β = ,276), tetapi selisih ini belum diuji secara formal dan kedua prediktor berkorelasi cukup tinggi. Temuan hanya berlaku pada sampel purposif ini dan menunjukkan asosiasi…

title: Enabling fire-safe gardens: a case study from Greater Hobart
abstract: Garden management plays a crucial role in reducing bushfire risk at the wildland-urban interface, yet implementation of fire-safe practices remains challenging. An analysis of garden assessments and in-depth interviews with 23 property owners in Greater Hobart, Tasmania, examined how technical, social and emotional factors influence garden bushfire adaptation decisions. Using the Cynefin framework and complexity theory, this study demonstrates that successful adaptation addresses multiple domains of complexity, from straightforward vegetation management to complex socio-emotional attachments to garden spaces. Findings reveal that while personalised garden assessment reports can motivate change, their success depends on a broader set of conditions. Barriers include practical constraints (e.g. green waste management), emotional attachments to garden elements and difficulties obtaining context-specific guidance. By applying the As Low As Reasonably Practicable (ALARP) principle, this study identified cost-effective interventions across the 4 avenues of institutional support and resource management, individual garden bushfire adaptation, personalised technical guidance and community support networks. This research suggests that creating fire-adapted gardens requires coordinated support systems that address both practical implementation challenges and emotional connections to garden…

title: The GAPS Programme at TNG. LXXX. Characterisation of the 400 Myr old multi-planet system K2-233
abstract: Studying the physical properties of the exoplanets is crucial for retrieving the characteristics of their atmospheres and their inner composition. Precise measurements of exoplanetary masses are crucial to constrain their bulk densities and infer their inner composition. For young systems hosting planets within or near the radius valley, accurate physical parameters are required to distinguish between different evolutionary scenarios and to understand the impact of atmospheric mass-loss mechanisms, such as photoevaporation driven by stellar activity. In this work we perform a revision of the masses of the three transiting exoplanets hosted by K2-233, a young (∼ 400 Myr old) K-type active star. Through dedicated simulations, we get insights into the evolution of planets' atmospheres over time being affected by photoevaporation, and into the modelling of the planets' interiors. We collected 70 HARPS-N observations within the GAPS/ArMS Large Programme and performed a joint analysis combining 124 HARPS literature observations, the available K2 light curves, and TESS data obtained simultaneously with our radial velocity monitoring. After obtaining the planetary information, we reconstructed the atmospheric evolution of the planet K2-233 d by using our photoevaporation code. Due to the strong stellar activity of K2-233, we explored several Multi-GP configurations and demonstrated tha…

title: Environmental risk, natural disasters, and economic growth management in Indonesia: A satellite-based analysis
abstract: This study examines how environmental risk and natural disasters affect economic performance in a disaster-prone emerging economy. It focuses on the short-run and long-run impacts of flood exposure, forest loss, and spatial economic expansion on Indonesia’s economic growth, with implications for investment stability and growth management. The study integrates satellite-based indicators of flood exposure, forest loss, and night-time light intensity with national time-series macroeconomic data for Indonesia over the period 1960–2024. These variables are analyzed using a dynamic time-series framework to capture both short-run adjustments and long-run equilibrium relationships between environmental risk and economic performance. The results show that environmental factors affect economic performance in differentiated ways. Forest loss exhibits a statistically significant long-run association with economic growth, reflecting the continued role of land conversion and resource utilization in Indonesia’s development process. In contrast, disaster-related indicators do not display robust long-run negative effects at the aggregate level, suggesting that adaptive mechanisms such as reconstruction activity and economic diversification mitigate their macroeconomic impact. Short-run effects of environmental variables are generally limited. This study contributes to the business and managemen…

title: UNIFORM RULES IN THE FIELD OF CONSUMER RIGHTS PROTECTION: ON THEIR PLACE IN THE SYSTEM OF RUSSIAN LEGISLATION AND KEY NOVELTIES. PART 2
abstract: The article analyzes the innovations in the field of consumer protection legislation that arose in connection with the approval, by Decree of the Supreme State Council of the Union State, of the Uniform Rules in the Field of Consumer Protection, which came into force on December 6, 2024, on the territory of the Russian Federation and the Republic of Belarus. The article analyzes the main changes introduced by this act into Russian legislation, noting the focus of the Uniform Rules on raising the level of guarantees of consumer rights and interests, imposing additional obligations on business entities, expanding the scope of application to relations arising from the acquisition of goods, works, and services on a gratuitous basis, as well as the involvement of persons who do not have the status of individual entrepreneurs and sell their products to consumers.

title: Mechanisms of Secondary Peaks and Flood Recession in Urban Levee-Breach Events under Tributary–Mainstream Interactions
The triple nature of the PSR J0435+3233 system
abstract: The recent pulsar timing ephemeris of PSR J0435+3233 indicates that this millisecond pulsar (MSP) has a spin-down rate that is much higher than observed in other MSPs and challenges our understanding of the formation and evolution of MSPs. We propose that this system is a hierarchical triple, and that the high spin-down rate is caused by varying acceleration due to a tertiary in a wide orbit. We use pulsar timing methods with radio and γ-ray observations of PSR,J0435+3233 to determine the system properties. We find that a hierarchical triple timing model describes the timing observations of PSR,J0435+3233 and that this results in the detection of γ-ray pulsations back to the beginning of the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) data in 2008. The intrinsic spin-down rate remains uncertain, as it correlates with the parameters of the outer orbit, but large spin-down rates are excluded, and the intrinsic rate is at least two orders of magnitude lower than the observed rate, in line with other Galactic MSPs. We identified a star located 11 mas from the pulsar position as the optical counterpart to the tertiary companion. From the 1.5-2.5,kpc distance and colours, we infer that the tertiary is a 1.2,M_⊙ F-type main-sequence star. Along with the pulsar binary, it orbits the common centre of mass with an eccentric (e ≈ 0.6) wide (≈ 70 yr) orbit that is likely seen at a low orbital inclina…

title: Transforming The Doctoral Program in Geological Engineering Toward Excellent Accreditation: An Integrative Model of Academic Quality, Research Output, and Internationalization
abstract: The Doctoral Program in Geological Engineering at Universitas Pembangunan Nasional “Veteran” Yogyakarta is currently accredited “Very Good” by LAM Teknik. It faces increasing demands to achieve Excellent accreditation while strengthening its international competitiveness. This study aims to develop an integrative model and strategic roadmap to transform the program by improving academic quality, research performance, scholarly output, and internationalization. The study used a qualitative descriptive–analytical approach through document review, benchmarking with leading doctoral programs, gap analysis, SWOT analysis, stakeholder consultations, and conceptual modeling. The analysis identified six strategic priorities, including internationalization; leadership and networking; student recruitment and support; faculty capacity; research productivity; and scholarly publication. Key challenges include high faculty workloads, limited institutionalized international collaboration, low participation of doctoral students in international publications, and no international student enrollment. Based on these findings, the Academic–Research–Output–Internationalization (AROI) Model was developed as an integrative framework linking academic quality, research capacity, scholarly productivity, and global engagement. The model is supported by a five-year strategic roadmap comprising five phases…
