title: Carbon finance and forest conservation in Sumatra: a moderated–mediation approach involving community empowerment and institutional–technical barriers
abstract: Purpose This study examines how carbon finance is associated with perceived forest conservation outcomes in Sumatra, Indonesia, focusing on community economic empowerment and institutional and technical conditions. Design/methodology/approach The study used a single cross-sectional survey of 250 stakeholders across four Sumatran provinces who assessed carbon-finance programme implementation during 2020–2024. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to examine direct, mediating, moderating, and conditional indirect relationships. Findings Carbon finance is modestly associated with perceived forest conservation outcomes. Community economic empowerment provides a significant partial transmission pathway, while institutional and technical barriers are negatively associated with perceived conservation outcomes and attenuate the carbon finance-conservation relationship. Collectively, the results indicate that carbon finance functions as a conditional incentive mechanism embedded in community and institutional processes. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design and reliance on perceived outcomes limit causal and ecological interpretation. The findings provide context-specific evidence of associations among financial incentives, socioeconomic processes, and institutional conditions. Practical implications National regulators should clarify govern…

title: The science-policy gap on invasive species management: a review of research capacity, regulations, and data availability for an intergovernmental framework in the gulf cooperation council
Acute heart failure in emergency settings
abstract: Abstract Acute heart failure (AHF) represents a major cause of emergency medical care worldwide and continues to carry a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality despite advances in chronic heart failure management. Most patients with AHF present to emergency departments (EDs), where the first hours of care are critical to determine prognosis. Of these, some have been previously evaluated and treated by prehospital emergency medical services before ED arrival. This consensus document summarizes the current evidence and provides practical advice to emergency physicians for the diagnosis, treatment, and disposition of patients with AHF in these emergency settings (emergency medical services and ED). It emphasizes the importance of a rapid phenotypic classification into acute decompensated heart failure, acute pulmonary oedema, isolated right ventricular failure, or cardiogenic shock, as a key tool to guide early management and triage decisions. It reviews evidence on prehospital and ED management, including the use of biomarkers, imaging, ventilatory support, diuretic and vasodilator strategies, and early initiation or continuation of guideline-directed medical therapy. It also discusses risk stratification and disposition decisions supported by validated tools. Finally, it identifies major knowledge gaps and future research priorities, including pragmatic trials to assess p…

title: A Hybrid CNN–LSTM Framework for Accurate Load Forecasting in Virtual Power Plants
abstract: Accurate load forecasting plays a critical role in ensuring the secure operation and efficient energy scheduling of virtual power plants (VPPs). However, the increasing integration of renewable generation, energy storage devices, and flexible demand resources brings substantial uncertainties and complex nonlinear characteristics to VPP load profiles. Conventional forecasting methods often face challenges in simultaneously learning short-term variations and capturing long-term dependencies in dynamic load sequences. To overcome these limitations, this paper develops a hybrid convolutional neural network and long short-term memory (CNN–LSTM) based forecasting framework for VPP load prediction. Specifically, the one-dimensional convolutional neural network is employed to extract hierarchical local temporal features from historical load data, while the LSTM module is designed to characterize long-term temporal correlations by exploiting its memory and gating mechanisms. A unified end-to-end training strategy is further introduced to optimize the feature extraction and sequence learning processes jointly. Extensive experiments are performed from multiple perspectives, including comparisons with state-of-the-art forecasting approaches, performance evaluations under diverse load fluctuation scenarios, robustness assessments with varying prediction horizons and input disturbances, and …

title: Global commodity price shocks and Indonesia’s exchange rate dynamics during the Russia-Ukraine conflict: A VECM analysis
abstract: The Russia–Ukraine conflict has disrupted global commodity markets, particularly crude oil, natural gas, wheat, and corn, leading to increased price volatility and affecting exchange rate dynamics. This study aims to analyze the Granger-causal relationship between global commodity prices and the USD/IDR exchange rate using the Vector Error Correction Model (VECM). Monthly data from November 2013 to September 2023 are employed to examine both short-run dynamics and long-run equilibrium relationships. The results show that, in the long run, crude oil prices have a negative relationship with the USD/IDR exchange rate, indicating an appreciation of the Indonesian Rupiah, while natural gas, wheat, and corn prices have positive effects, contributing to currency depreciation. In the short run, only crude oil prices significantly influence the exchange rate. The Granger causality test reveals a unidirectional relationship from crude oil prices to the exchange rate. Furthermore, the model demonstrates high predictive accuracy, with MAPE values of 1.54% (exchange rate), 6.91% (crude oil), 10.54% (natural gas), 6.92% (wheat), and 4.50% (corn). These findings highlight the dominant role of energy commodities and confirm that global commodity shocks significantly influence exchange rate movements, providing important insights for policymakers in managing economic stability.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Financial Volatility Forecasting and Portfolio Risk Management: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Framework
The Influence of Live Streaming, Marketing Communication Strategies, and Price Discounts on Purchase Decisions for Glad2Glow Skincare Products on Shopee
abstract: The development of e-commerce and the Shopee Live feature increases opportunities for interactive skincare product marketing, while brand competition encourages companies to use marketing communications and price discounts to influence purchasing decisions. This study aims to analyze the influence of live streaming, marketing communication strategies, and price discounts on purchasing decisions for Glad2Glow skincare products on Shopee. The study used a quantitative approach with a causal associative method. The study population was Glad2Glow consumers in Sidoarjo Regency who had watched and purchased products through Shopee Live, with a sample of 100 respondents selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected through a Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The results showed that all three variables partially and simultaneously had a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions. Price discounts were the most dominant variable. In conclusion, the integration of the three marketing strategies can strengthen consumer purchasing decisions

title: Severe Rotisserie Tilt of Scleral-Fixated CT Lucia 602 Intraocular Lenses: A Multicenter Case Series
abstract: This multicenter case series describes severe rotisserie tilt of scleral-fixed CT Lucia 602 intraocular lenses (IOL) observed across multiple surgeons and centers between 2021 to 2023. The study reviewed 1,408 intrascleral haptic fixation (ISHF) surgeries performed by 20 surgeons from 18 centers, including both retina and anterior segment specialists, at both academic and private practice settings, and identified 45 tilted IOL cases with the CT Lucia requiring surgical intervention. There was a wide variation in instrumentation, tunnel construction approaches, and lens insertion techniques. The average estimated tilt was 74.8º ± 40.1º. Abnormalities in the haptic-optic junction were found in 34 of 45 (76%) cases. Management included replacing the IOL, placing an anterior chamber IOL, refixating the IOL, or leaving the patient aphakic. Of those receiving another CT Lucia lens, seven of 16 (44%) cases experienced repeat tilt, representing a meaningful risk of recurrence. Given the heterogeneity of surgeon technique, our findings may represent a concerning reproducible failure phenotype.

title: Towards Reliable Strength Prediction of Crystalline Rock Using an Image-Based Framework
Multimodal Prediction in Robotic Surgery: The Incremental Value of Task-Level Kinematic Data
abstract: Objective: To determine whether multimodal predictive models incorporating task-level objective performance indicators (OPIs) alongside preoperative clinical variables improve prediction of surgeon experience, case complexity, and outcomes in robotic cholecystectomy. Background: OPIs from robotic platforms enable automated assessment of intraoperative performance, but prior multimodal analyses have suggested limited incremental value beyond clinical variables. Whether this conclusion holds when OPIs are computed at task level and target specifically curated endpoints remains untested. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 234 Calot’s triangle dissections, 198 by attending surgeons and 36 by trainees. Three feature sets per target—clinical-only (10 preoperative variables), OPI-only (10 target-specific kinematic features), and combined—were evaluated using nested 5-seed×5-fold cross-validation across 5 algorithms (logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM). Discriminative performance was compared by paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on fold-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Feature contributions were quantified with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. Results: For surgeon experience and case complexity, OPIs alone matched the combined model (AUROC: 0.967 vs. 0.964; 0.791 vs. 0.792; both P >0.05) and…

title: Clinical Trial Prediction Markets — Information, at What Cost?
Causal Discovery in Photospheric Magnetic Field Time Series for Interpretable Solar Flare Prediction
abstract: Abstract Deep learning has proven to be a vital advancement in many fields that present difficult classification and prediction tasks. This includes astrophysics, particularly space weather prediction, where accurate modeling has become essential for protecting satellite and ground infrastructure from the impacts of solar flares and solar energetic particle events. Despite their strong predictive ability, one issue with deep learning as a method for space weather prediction is the poor interpretability of these “black box” methods. A possible solution to this comes in the form of a structured deep learning framework named Amortized Causal Discovery (ACD), which aims to enforce an easily interpretable layer in the neural network that represents the causal summary graph. We apply this method to the Space Weather Analytics for Solar Flares dataset, a rich source of multivariate time series (MVTS) data of solar active regions, to demonstrate that high-intensity solar flares can be detected ahead of time by comparing their causal summary graphs with those of other flare events. In this work, we use graph metric statistics as well as objective performance tests against state-of-the-art classifiers to demonstrate the depth of insight that ACD can produce into differences between MVTS samples in the context of solar flare prediction.

title: A unified ensemble learning framework for electric motor fault diagnosis, thermal state prediction, and remaining useful life estimation
abstract: Electric motors are critical components of modern industrial and transportation systems, making accurate fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance essential for operational reliability. This study proposes a unified machine learning framework for motor fault classification, temperature prediction, and remaining useful life (RUL) estimation using three publicly available electric motor datasets. The proposed pipeline integrates sliding-window segmentation, multi-domain feature extraction, consensus-based feature selection, and physically motivated descriptors derived from electrical and thermal measurements. Five machine learning algorithms, namely Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, LightGBM, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), were systematically evaluated. For fault diagnosis on the Ottawa UOEMD-VAFCVS dataset, evaluated with a file-level train–test split in which all segments of a recording are kept in the same partition, LightGBM achieved the highest performance on the held-out recordings (Accuracy = 1.0000, F1-score = 1.0000, ROC-AUC = 1.0000). Sliding-window segmentation increased the number of trainable observations from 128 to 2,432 and improved the macro F1-score from 0.569 to above 0.994 across all models. For thermal prediction on the PMSM dataset, LightGBM obtained R² values of 0.993, 0.991, 0.989, and 0.987 for rotor, stator winding, stator tooth,…

Application of machine learning prediction models for in-hospital mortality in diabetic sepsis patients: a study based on the MIMIC IV database
abstract: Abstract Background Sepsis complicated by diabetes mellitus represents a significant clinical challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Accurate prognostication of in-hospital mortality in this complex patient population is crucial for optimizing clinical decision making, resource allocation, and patient management strategies. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study utilizing data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database. The study focused on adult ICU patients with concurrent diagnoses of sepsis and diabetes mellitus. Six machine learning algorithms were evaluated for their predictive performance: Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), XGBoost and LightGBM. Additionally, we assessed the prognostic capability of the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score. Model discrimination was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). To enhance model interpretability, we employed SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values to elucidate the relative importance of predictor variables. Results The study cohort comprised 7716 patients, with 1357 (17.6%) experiencing in-hospital mortality. Among the machine learning models evaluated, GBDT exhibited superior predictive performance…

title: A Gradient Boosting-Based Machine Learning Model for the Prediction of the Hardness of Thermoplastic Polymers
abstract: Abstract Modern experimental techniques can measure the hardness of thin films and structural features on the nanometer scale. These techniques can be applied to many types of materials, but as the hardness of the material decreases, more specialized and precise equipment is needed. For polymers, this analysis can be relatively expensive and time-consuming, so here we demonstrate a gradient-boosting-based machine-learning model that can provide a fast and reliable prediction of the hardness of thermoplastic polymers. This model is based on the XGBoost algorithm and shows reasonably good performance with an R2 value of 0.46–0.69. The features used in this study include experimental (mechanical and thermal properties) and molecular descriptors obtained using RDKit. The model is robust, with reasonable performance obtained when key experimental features are removed and/or when the selection of polymers is reduced. This suggests that this approach will be useful in “bottom-up” strategies for polymeric materials development.

title: Application of interpretable deep learning in brain age prediction: a comprehensive review
abstract: Abstract Brain age prediction has emerged as a promising approach for characterizing interindividual differences in brain aging. However, the increasing complexity of deep learning models has created a substantial gap between predictive performance and interpretability. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has, therefore, become increasingly important for identifying the neuroanatomical features underlying brain age predictions. This review systematically examines interpretable deep learning approaches for brain age prediction. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect identified 32 eligible studies, which were organized into post-hoc explanation methods and intrinsically interpretable models. We further propose a four-dimensional operational framework encompassing Algorithm Reliability, Robustness and Reproducibility, Biological Validation, and Clinical Utility. The reviewed literature indicates a transition from localized feature attribution toward generative, disentangled, attention-based, and anatomically meaningful representations. However, interpretation remains sensitive to methodological and imaging-related factors, while brain age gap (BAG) is also influenced by age dependency, calibration, reference-population composition, and site heterogeneity. Future research should emphasize standardized evaluation and prospective clinical validation to…

Bioprocessing of Talaromyces purpurogenus for production of dihydromonascorubrin with a powerful antioxidant and antimicrobial activities integrated with the network-guided target prediction and molecular docking analyses
abstract: Abstract The antibiotic resistance of pathogenic microorganisms due to the irresponsible use in healthcare and agricultural practices is one of the global threats for the human, especially immune-compromised patients. Thus, searching for a novel compounds from fungi with unique affinity to combat the drug-resistant microorganisms was the objective. Talaromyces purpurogenus # PZ292970.1, an endophyte of palm tree Elaeis guineensis , has the highest productivity of azaphilone pigment (25.5 AU410/ml), with a strong activity against E. coli (MIC value 6.8 µg/ml), S. aureus and C. albicans (MIC value 12.5 µg/ml). The extracted pigment of T. purpurogenus has a strong antibiofilm activity for S. aureus (86.2%), C. albicans (85.8%) and E. coli (79.7%), compared to the control. The TLC purified-pigment of T. purpurogenus had a maximum absorbance at λ 410 nm, with a small one at λ 510 nm, revealing the identity of the major peak as orange azaphilone pigment. The purified pigment gave a distinct single peak by HPLC, ensures their structural homogeneity. From the FT-IR analyses, the absorption and stretching vibration of the target compound functional groups ensures their spectral identity as polyketide azaphilone. The 1HNMR and 13CNMR spectra revealed characteristic proton signals for the aromatic polyketide related to dihydromonascorubrin derivatives. From LC–MS/MS, the purified compound…

title: Viewpoint: understanding consumer vulnerability across service ecosystem configurations
abstract: Purpose This viewpoint aims to advance understanding of consumer vulnerability by examining how different configurations of structural, institutional and relational conditions shape vulnerability across service ecosystems. Country context, regulation and customer-to-customer (C2C) interaction provide complementary perspectives for examining these conditions. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a conceptual, integrative approach, synthesising literature from transformative service research, service ecosystem theory and marketing to develop an analytical framework that integrates country context, regulation and C2C interaction. Findings Consumer vulnerability varies according to the configuration and interdependence of structural conditions, institutional arrangements and relational processes. Together, these conditions may create, reinforce, negotiate or alleviate vulnerability across different service ecosystems. Research limitations/implications The framework encourages comparative, multi-level and longitudinal research examining how structural, institutional and relational conditions combine and change across service ecosystem configurations. Practical implications The framework encourages service providers and policymakers to adopt ecosystem-oriented strategies that consider structural, institutional and relational conditions together when addressing sources of vul…

title: Analyzing the Effect of Service Quality Dimensions on Student Satisfaction and Retention at ITTR English Course
abstract: Background: English proficiency has become increasingly important in globalization. ITTR English Course, a prominent language school in Riau, experienced enrollment growth from 300 to 554 students (2020-2025), yet revenue targets were not achieved, indicating potential service quality issues affecting student retention. Objectives: This study investigates service quality gaps at ITTR English Course using SERVQUAL model dimensions to identify improvement priorities for enhancing student satisfaction and retention. Methods: Sequential explanatory mixed-methods design involving quantitative questionnaire surveys (n=200), qualitative NVivo analysis, Current Reality Tree root cause analysis, and Analytic Hierarchy Process prioritization. Focus group discussions with five internal divisions were conducted. Results: Reliability emerged as the most critical dimension for student satisfaction, with operational consistency as the primary concern (42 codings). System digitalization received the highest prioritization score (0.56) among improvement alternatives. Conclusions: Service quality improvements, particularly through system digitalization, process standardization, and accountability mechanisms, can enhance student satisfaction, retention, and institutional financial sustainability.

title: Remote monitoring in patients awaiting elective cardiac surgery is associated with improved clinical outcomes: a prospective service evaluation
abstract: Abstract Background Rising elective cardiac surgery waiting times are associated with increased risk of clinical deterioration and unscheduled admissions. Remote patient monitoring (RPM) may offer earlier detection of deterioration, but its role during the pre-operative waiting period is not well established. Methods We conducted a prospective single centre service evaluation of a digital RPM pathway for adults listed for elective cardiac surgery between September 2022 and September 2023. Patients submitting at least one digital symptom questionnaire (activated group) were compared with those who did not (non-activated). Primary outcomes were preoperative mortality and unscheduled admissions requiring non elective intervention. Secondary outcomes included resternotomy, 1 year postoperative mortality, and length of stay. Results Of 1,164 patients, 799 (68.6%) were activated. Baseline characteristics were similar aside from higher hypertension and diabetes prevalence in the non-activated group. Pre-operative mortality was significantly lower in activated patients (0.6% vs 2.2%; RR 0.29, 95% CI 0.09–0.87; p=0.018). Unscheduled admissions were also reduced (2.1% vs 4.3%; RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.25–0.95; p=0.031). Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated early and sustained separation (log-rank p=0.012). Secondary outcomes were similar between groups. In the propensity-matched cohort, activatio…

title: Sustainable service scenes: formation mechanism of consumers’ premium purchase of specialty agricultural and livestock products in short-video live streaming
abstract: Advancing the market realization of premium pricing for high-quality agricultural and livestock products is essential to facilitating the transition of traditional agriculture toward a sustainable, resource-efficient, and quality-driven development paradigm. However, Information asymmetry in the agricultural and livestock products market gives rise to the “lemons problem,” impeding the sustainable consumption of high-quality, differentiated products and undermining their ability to command premium pricing. With the development of the digital economy, short-video live streaming has emerged as a new driver for promoting the sustainable consumption of such products at premium prices. Drawing on servicescape theory, this study uses Inner Mongolia mutton as a representative case and constructs a structural equation model based on 402 valid questionnaires to examine the formation mechanism of consumers’ premium purchase intentions for specialty agricultural and livestock products in short-video live streaming. In addition, multi-group analysis is conducted to examine whether these mechanisms differ across consumers with different demographic characteristics. The results indicate that short-video live streaming effectively encourages consumers to purchase specialty agricultural and livestock products at premium prices through the dual pathways of “scene reconstruction–value upgrading”…

title: The Role of Digital Banking, Service Quality, and Religiosity on Islamic Bank Customer Loyalty with Customer Satisfaction as a Moderating Variable
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of digital banking, service quality, and religiosity on Islamic bank customer loyalty with customer satisfaction as a moderating variable. The research method uses a systematic literature review (SLR) by analyzing relevant journals. The results show that digital banking, service quality, and religiosity have a positive effect on customer loyalty. Furthermore, customer satisfaction strengthens the relationship between these variables and customer loyalty in Islamic banks.
venue: Neo Journal of economy and social humanities

title: Policy crisis in service ecosystems
abstract: Purpose This research introduces the concept of policy crises. Using a service ecosystem lens, it tests how meso-level responses to macro-level political change impact micro-level brand perceptions and intentions, showing downstream implications of public policy. This research aims to answer a call for empirical work that integrates public policy and services marketing. Design/methodology/approach In two online experiments, this research tests whether organizational responses of supporting, stalling or a mixed approach to a policy crisis, as well as actor political affiliation, impact individual brand perceptions and behavioral intentions. Findings Supportive actions, compared to mixed and stalling actions, negatively impact individual perceptions of a service brand’s authenticity, brand trust and behavioral intentions. However, this pattern is reversed for individuals who share a political affiliation with the policy source (e.g. executive branch). These results hold when individual and regional differences are accounted for. Practical implications Based on our findings, we present a tool for service organizations to use in efficient and data-driven decision-making in times of policy change. Recommendations are based on whether a given policy change is a crisis, what types of actions are legally justifiable, and whether a majority of the micro-level members of the service ecos…

title: FAKTOR YANG BERHUBUNGAN DENGAN PERILAKU TIDAK AMAN PADA PEKERJA CLEANING SERVICE DI LINGKUNGAN PERGURUAN TINGGI: STUDI PADA UNIVERSITAS HASANUDDIN
abstract: Latar Belakang: Kecelakaan kerja merupakan kejadian yang tidak diharapkan dan dapat menimbulkan kerugian bagi perusahaan maupun pekerja. Salah satu faktor utama penyebab kecelakaan kerja adalah perilaku tidak aman (unsafe action). Cleaning service merupakan salah satu profesi yang rentan terhadap kecelakaan kerja akibat tugas yang dilakukan secara berulang dan paparan bahaya ergonomis. Tujuan: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis faktor-faktor yang berhubungan dengan unsafe action pada pekerja cleaning service di Universitas Hasanuddin. Metode: Penelitian ini merupakan studi analitik observasional dengan desain cross sectional yang melibatkan 112 pekerja cleaning service. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner yang telah diuji validitas dan reliabilitasnya. Analisis bivariat dilakukan menggunakan uji Chi-square dengan tingkat signifikansi 5%. Hasil: Sebanyak 49 responden (43,7%) memiliki perilaku tidak aman dengan kategori risiko tinggi. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa tidak terdapat hubungan yang signifikan antara jenis kelamin dengan unsafe action (p = 0,708). Sebaliknya, terdapat hubungan yang signifikan antara pengetahuan (p = 0,011), ketersediaan alat pelindung diri (APD) (p = 0,020), masa kerja (p = 0,046), dan pengawasan (p = 0,015) dengan unsafe action. LEGAL REGULATION OF CUSTOMS VALUATION OF EXPORTED GOODS
abstract: Taking into account the raw material orientation of exported goods subject to export customs duties, close attention to filling the federal budget of the Russian Federation at the expense of this type of payment seems to be very relevant. Based on the systematic analysis of the norms of current legislation, it was established that there are different approaches to determining the customs value of imported and exported goods, which does not fully meet the general principles of forming the price of a transaction with goods, which is the basic element of the determined customs value of goods. The authors of the study formulated editorial amendments to regulatory legal acts specifying the procedure for determining the customs value of exported goods.

title: Low-frequency spectra and scattering of pulsars towards the Gum Nebula with the MWA
abstract: The Gum Nebula is a nearby ionised complex with sight-line-dependent pulsar propagation. We test whether a smooth ionised structure can explain spectral turnovers and pulse broadening towards the Gum Nebula, or whether smaller-scale material is required. We analysed Murchison Widefield Array Voltage Capture System observations of six pulsars over 80--240,MHz, measuring source-dependent sub-band flux densities and combining them with literature data. We fitted power-law, free--free absorption (FFA), and turnover-constrained broken-power-law (BPL) spectra using propagated uncertainties and fractional-error-floor tests. title: Fuzzy logic and frequency ratio based landslide susceptibility mapping using geo environmental and hydro meteorological factors in pithoragarh, uttarakhand
abstract: Mass movement events leads to severe infrastructural and socioeconomic damage across the Himalayan belt, particularly in Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand, India, where over nearly 1,000 events have been recorded in the last two decades. Modelling landslide susceptibility in such highly several, monsoon dominated terrains requires frameworks capable of handling significant spatial and lithological uncertainty. This study assesses and map out regional landslide vulnerability using a Multi Criteria Decision Analysis methodology based on fuzzy logic and frequency ratio. A spatial database comprising fourteen geo spatial and hydro meteorological conditioning factors was integrated to capture the region’s complex topographical and climatic changes. The analytical performances of the models were mathematically validated against a historical landslide inventory using the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve. For this uncertain terrain, the Fuzzy Logic model produced a realistic and reliable susceptibility standard with an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.686, in the other hand the frequency ratio model provides an AUC of 0.876. In this region, the middle and southern part, which are dominated by unconsolidated soils and heavy monsoon precipitation, are major hazard zones, while the northern side crystalline rock formations are still mostly stable, according to the spatial distribution …

title: Biosynthesis, enzymatic basis, and transcriptional regulation of benzylisoquinoline alkaloids in medicinal plants
abstract: Abstract Benzylisoquinoline alkaloids (BIAs) are a class of structurally diverse secondary metabolites, with over 2,500 identified variants classified into seven major categories based on their core skeletons. These compounds exhibit significant pharmacological activities – including antitumor, antibacterial, and anti-inflammatory effects – and serve as important sources of clinical drugs such as morphine, berberine, and magnoflorine. Currently, BIAs are primarily obtained through plant cultivation and extraction. However, factors such as low in-planta content, seasonal constraints, and environmental variability contribute to vulnerabilities in the supply chain. In light of these challenges, microbial biosynthesis using engineered strains (e.g., yeast) has emerged as a promising alternative, though it requires complete elucidation and functional expression of all pathway enzymes. Enhancing BIAs production in crops through transcriptional regulation – targeting key enzymes, transcription factors (such as WRKY, bHLH, and AP2/ERF families), and phytohormone signaling – represents a feasible interim strategy. Advanced approaches, including coexpression of enzyme genes and transcription factors, hold promise for accelerating the development of industrial-scale alkaloid-producing cell factories and crop improvement, thereby enabling sustainable drug supply.

title: The pendular regulation model: a transdiagnostic approach to emotional regulation
abstract: Contemporary psychiatric classification systems face persistent concerns regarding diagnostic heterogeneity, comorbidity, and limited mechanistic precision. Although dimensional and transdiagnostic initiatives—including HiTOP, RDoC, and network models—have advanced the field, a unifying regulatory architecture integrating nonlinear dynamics, hierarchical predictive processing, stress physiology, and identity stabilization remains underdeveloped. The present article introduces the Pendular Regulation Model (PRM), a neurodynamic transdiagnostic framework conceptualizing psychological functioning as bounded oscillatory regulation within hierarchical predictive systems embedded in neurovisceral and stress-responsive networks. Within this model, psychopathology reflects maladaptive stabilization patterns characterized by regulatory constriction or destabilization. Identity coherence is proposed as an emergent property of repeated regulatory trajectories over time. The manuscript outlines a structured empirical agenda designed to evaluate the model’s longitudinal predictive capacity using established quantitative methods. Explicit falsifiability criteria are specified. If empirically supported, the PRM may offer an integrative regulatory framework capable of clarifying cross-diagnostic variability and informing treatment responsiveness.

title: Calycosin alleviates myocardial injury in diabetic mice by enhancing lipophagy in cardiomyocytes via Rab7a regulation
abstract: Background Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major life-threatening cardiovascular complication of diabetes mellitus, characterized by myocardial lipid deposition, lipotoxicity and progressive cardiac dysfunction. Impaired lipophagy—the selective autophagic clearance of lipid droplets (LDs)—is a key driver of DCM progression, and Rab7a, a small GTPase, is essential for autophagosome–lysosome fusion, the rate-limiting step of efficient lipophagic degradation. Calycosin (CA), a natural isoflavone derived from Astragalus membranaceus , exerts antidiabetic and cardioprotective effects. However, whether CA regulates lipophagy via Ras-related protein Rab-7a (Rab7a) to ameliorate DCM remains largely unknown. The present study investigated whether CA alleviates DCM by promoting lipophagy through Rab7a-dependent mechanisms. Methods In vivo , DCM was induced in male C57BL/6J mice by a high-fat diet combined with low-dose streptozotocin (STZ), followed by daily CA administration. In vitro , neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes (NMCMs) were isolated and exposed to high glucose and high lipid (HGHL) conditions to mimic the DCM microenvironment. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography. Myocardial lipid accumulation was evaluated by Oi-Red O staining, Bodipy staining and triglyceride (TG) quantification assay. Lipophagy was monitored using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), LC3-LD co…

title: TARGETED ADVERTISING AS AN OBJECT OF LEGAL REGULATION: PROBLEMS OF DEFINITION AND THE CONFLICT OF PUBLIC AND PRIVATE INTERESTS
abstract: The article is devoted to the analysis of legal problems of targeted advertising as an object of regulation in the digital economy. The author formulates the definition of targeted advertising and highlights its qualifying features. Three critical gaps in the legislation on personal data are identified. The conflict between the economic interests of platforms and the constitutional right to privacy is substantiated. Specific directions for improving legislation are proposed, including the consolidation of the concept of profiling, the introduction of granular consent, and the extension of the special categories regime to deduced data.

title: High-frequency subsurface-penetrating radar investigation of the shallow subsurface at the Zhurong landing site
abstract: The shallow subsurface at the Zhurong rover landing site records recent geological processes under Late Amazonian conditions. The Rover-mounted Subsurface Penetrating Radar (RoSPR) on board the Zhurong rover provides a unique opportunity to investigate the fine-scale geological structures of the shallow Martian subsurface in southern Utopia Planitia. Our objectives are to constrain the fine-scale structure and electromagnetic properties of the shallow subsurface from both global and local perspectives and to infer the dominant modification processes at the landing site. We processed and analyzed the RoSPR high-frequency channel data using a workflow that included microwave tomographic imaging and loss tangent estimation based on energy attenuation. To identify subsurface scattering characteristics, we applied full-polarimetric Freeman decomposition to the radar data. The average loss tangent of the shallow subsurface is 0.0071 ± 0.0018, highlighting significant spatial heterogeneity in electromagnetic properties. At the global scale, radar reflection intensity shows a systematic attenuation trend consistent with the north-to-south topographic gradient along the traverse and correlates with local topographic undulations in most segments. This pattern likely reflects variations in weathered layer thickness controlled by topography-driven aeolian erosion and deposition. At the loc…

title: Cultural heritage recognition and rural sustainability in China: Community capacity and tourism workforce participation as pathways to SDGs 8 and 11
abstract: Cultural heritage recognition is often expected to support rural development, but the mechanisms linking recognition with sustainability remain uncertain. This study examines the association between a tourism-resource-weighted cultural heritage recognition exposure index and rural sustainability in China, with tourism-supporting community capacity and tourism workforce participation evaluated as distinct pathways. The UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity and the China Tourism Resilience Dataset were combined to form a balanced panel of 31 provincial-level regions from 2011 to 2020 (310 province-year observations). Composite indices were constructed from z-standardized indicators. Associations were estimated using pooled ordinary least squares with province-clustered standard errors, a 2000-resample cluster-bootstrap pathway decomposition, variance inflation factors, an unweighted heritage-count specification, municipality exclusion, alternative index scaling, and two-way fixed effects. The adjusted recognition-exposure-sustainability association was positive but not statistically significant. Recognition exposure was positively associated with tourism-supporting community capacity, and the indirect association through this pathway was significant (0.330; 95 % CI [0.114, 0.499]). The workforce-participation indirect association was small …

title: Unwilling to leave, unable to stay: mechanism of plasticity in site fidelity as a rewarding tactic in changing environments
abstract: Abstract Context Home-ranging is common among animal species, as site fidelity facilitates cognitive map development and promotes efficient habitat use. The adaptive value of site fidelity, however, should decline as habitat conditions change, yet empirical evidence remains limited, especially for wide-ranging species. Objectives We investigated how fire and forest harvesting affect home-range stability in boreal caribou, a species typically exhibiting strong site fidelity. We then identified conditions where fidelity increases mortality and when shifting home ranges becomes advantageous. Methods We monitored 331 GPS-collared caribou across 667,000 km 2 of boreal forest. Forest harvesting and fire disturbance levels were related to indices of home-range fidelity derived from the spatial proximity of locations across successive years. Survival was then evaluated in relation to habitat conditions following home-range adjustment. Results Recent forest disturbances reduced fidelity, indicating behavioral plasticity. However, the fitness consequences of fidelity were strongly context‑dependent. High fidelity reduced mortality level when individuals occupied or selected low‑disturbance home ranges, but increased mortality when individuals remained faithful to highly disturbed ranges, particularly those dominated by regenerating cuts. Conclusions The study provides empirical evidence …

The Rapid Release Process and Mechanism of Nutrients in Biomimetic Weathered Granite Rock Powder
abstract: Ecological restoration of waste slag sites is often constrained by topsoil scarcity and nutrient deficiency. Therefore, this study investigated organic acid-matured granite rock powder (M-GRP) to evaluate its mineral nutrient-release behavior and structural evolution, with the aim of developing it as a compost mineral additive. The results showed that 0.2 mol/L malonic acid, a solid-to-liquid ratio of 1:75, and maturation at room temperature for 8 h provided effective nutrient release from granite rock powder. Characterization analysis showed that protons and organic groups in malonic acid promoted the dissolution of feldspar and illite in granite rock powder, accompanied by the substantial dissolution of clinochlore and calcite. Feldspar and illite exhibited severe dissolution at edges and protrusions, forming pits and pores. Malonic acid treatment decreased the unit-cell volume and interplanar spacing of the surviving mineral phases and interplanar spacing, and increased surface roughness, lattice defects, and surface disorder. Quartz remained comparatively stable, with its morphology and crystal structure preserved. In addition, the specific surface area of M-GRP increased, accompanied by changes in its pore structure and pore-size distribution. These results provide a theoretical basis and technical support for the resource utilization of rock powder.

title: Spectroscopic monitoring of long secondary period variables. The case of J-type carbon stars
abstract: Long-secondary-period (LSP) variables are a subclass of long-period variables whose origin is a matter of debate. The current leading hypotheses involve binarity or non-radial pulsations. We aim to investigate the spectroscopic signatures associated with the LSP variability by targeting two J-type carbon stars exhibiting an LSP - VZ Per and UV Cam - and further constrain its origin. Decade-long spectroscopic monitoring was used to obtain a long-term radial-velocity (RV) curve for the two stars. From a frequency analysis, we isolated an LSP signal. The retrieved periodicity was then compared with changes in spectral profiles and available light-curve variability to further constrain the origin of the modulation. For VZ Per, the LSP derived from the RV curve (∼,960 days) is correlated with the light-curve dimming event and a variation in the Balmer absorption line profile. These results translate into changes in the gas and dust column densities with the phase of the LSP, with the maximum gas column density occurring ahead of the dust. For UV Cam, the RV monitoring yields a period of ∼,1178 d, with an amplitude of about 1,km/s. When interpreting the RV modulation as a Keplerian signal for both stars, a low-mass ($<0.1, ̊m M_⊙$) close companion is found. In this scenario, variations in gas and dust column densities with (orbital) phase trace the material in the expanding comet-lik…

title: Characterizing Lyman alpha emission from high-redshift galaxies
abstract: The Lyman α (Lyα) line from high-redshift galaxies is a powerful probe of the epoch of reionization (EoR). Neutral hydrogen in the intergalactic medium (IGM) can significantly attenuate the emergent Lyα line, even in the damping wing of the cross section. However, interpreting this damping wing imprint relies on prior knowledge of the spectrum that escapes from the galaxy and its environs into the IGM. This emergent spectrum is highly sensitive to the composition and geometry of the interstellar and circumgalactic media and therefore exhibits a large galaxy-to-galaxy scatter. Characterizing this scatter is further complicated by nontrivial selection effects introduced by observational surveys. Here we build a flexible, empirical model for the emergent Lyα spectra. Our model characterizes the emergent Lyα luminosity, the velocity offset of the Lyα line with respect to the systemic redshift, and the Hα luminosity using multivariate probability distributions conditioned on the UV magnitude. We constrained these distributions using observations of z NIRCam, and we forward-modeled the observational selection functions together with the galaxy parameters. Our model yields Lyα equivalent-width distributions that better match independent Subaru observations than previous empirical models. The extended distributions of Lyα equivalent widths and velocity offsets that we obtain could faci…

title: 100% Waste-Derived Carbon-Sequestering Binder via Low-Temperature Sintering Enabled by Waste Glass
abstract: Abstract Traditional cement production contributes substantial CO2 emissions, prompting a need to develop alternative binders. This work aims to report the development of a fully waste-derived carbon-sequestering binder produced by sintering at a lower temperature. A C2S-based binder was successfully produced using 55% carbide slag and 45% waste glass powder, yielding 34.3 wt % β-C2S and 24.2 wt % γ-C2S at 1100 °C. The incorporation of waste glass provided a fluxing effect due to its Na2O content, enabling C2S formation at reduced temperature. The synthesized binder achieved a compressive strength of 58.6 MPa after carbonation curing for 5 h, accompanied by a CO2 uptake of 14.6%. Mineralogical and microstructural analyses revealed calcite as the dominant carbonation product with a refined pore structure and low porosity, both of which contributed to early strength development. Moreover, it was found that an excessive raw meal Ca/Si ratio (>2.2) can significantly deteriorate the microstructure and strength of a carbonated paste. Finally, the preliminary carbon footprint assessment indicated that the synthesized binder offers a potential CO2 emissions reduction of up to 60% compared to conventional Ordinary Portland Cement production. This work establishes the feasibility of producing a 100% waste-derived, low-temperature binder that actively sequesters CO2, offering an altern…

title: Multiscale damage characteristics and energy evolution patterns of coal treated with supercritical carbon dioxide
abstract: Abstract Coalbed methane (CBM) reservoirs in China are typically characterized by low permeability, requiring stimulation techniques to improve gas recovery. Supercritical carbon dioxide (SC-CO 2 ) fracturing has emerged as a promising waterless stimulation method, offering advantages such as improved reservoir integrity, the enhancement of complex fracture networks, and potential for CO 2 geological sequestration. As a sedimentary rock, coal exhibits a distinct bedding structure formed during diagenesis, critically affecting permeability enhancement and CBM extractability. To evaluate the effects of SC-CO 2 exposure on coal containing bedding planes with different orientations, a series of experiments is conducted using coal samples with bedding dip angles of 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, and 90°. A multi-technique approach, including Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), ultrasonic testing, and acoustic emission (AE) monitoring, is employed to characterize changes in functional groups, pore structure, mechanical properties, and acoustic properties before and after SC-CO 2 treatment. Results show that SC-CO 2 significantly reduces the intensity of infrared spectral peaks and alters the abundance of functional groups in coal samples, thereby facilitating the desorption of coalbed methane. Pore structure analysis reveals that SC-CO 2 modifies por…

title: Infrared spectroscopy of gas-phase hydrogenated and methylated pyrenes: From laboratory spectra to the simulated 3.4 μm emission band
abstract: Observations of the aromatic infrared (IR) emission band at 3.3 μm often reveal satellite emission features in the 3.4 -- 3.6 μm range. While the 3.3 μm band is attributed to the CH stretching vibration of polycylic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the satellite bands, particularly its prominent 3.4 μm component, is assigned to aliphatic CH stretching vibrations in hydrogenated and methylated PAH-like species. We derive state-of-the-art IR emission spectra for aliphatic-containing pyrene derivatives and compare them with astronomical observations. This will help us to refine our understanding of the contribution of these species to the 3.4 μm emission band. Infrared spectra (1.4--25 μm) of gas-phase hydrogenated pyrenes (dihydropyrene, tetrahydropyrene, and hexahydropyrene), methylated pyrene, and pyrene were recorded at temperatures ranging from 373 to 673 K, depending on the species. The band profiles were analysed using a multi-component fitting tool, and empirical anharmonicity laws were derived to quantify the evolution of the band positions and widths with temperature. The obtained spectral data were combined with the results of a Monte Carlo emission model to simulate the emission spectra following UV-photon absorption, up to the dissociation limit (łesssim6 eV). The resulting synthetic spectra were then compared with astronomical spectra including James Webb Space Telescop…

title: Revisiting the Einstein Cross with X-shooter spectra: New estimates of accretion disk parameters and broad emission line profiles from microlensing
abstract: We present a spectroscopic study of the lensed quasar Q2237+0305, the Einstein Cross, assessing the best wavelength coverage to date with the X-shooter instrument (from 3000 to 20000 Å), and thus improving the available spectroscopic data for this system. Using as a reference the characteristic emission lines for each quasar macro-image, we estimate the chromatic microlensing effect between pairs of images and calculate the extinction curve, confirming no significant differences between spectra C and A caused by extinction in the lens galaxy. In addition, we model the accretion disk characterized by a temperature profile with logarithmic slope 1/p and size r_s, assuming a thin-disk model with a power-law function of the form r_s ∝ łambdaup^p. To do this, we calculated a set of three chromatic microlensing measurements compiling previous estimates from the literature to test the wavelength dependence. This temperature profile was also compared to the canonical thin-disk model with p=4/3. Finally, we estimated the likelihood between the disk model and the observed data collected from multiple epochs through mock microlensing magnification maps and determined the probability density functions of each parameter from a Bayesian analysis. As a result, our estimated values for the accretion disk size and its exponential index are s =4.9^ +2.3 _ -2.6 (lt-day) and p=0.77^ +0.47 _ -0.28 …

title: Direct high-speed rail substitution for Chinese Super League team travel: a directional carbon dioxide scenario assessment
abstract: Introduction Professional football team travel provides a setting for evaluating transport substitution under explicit organizational rules. Methods We modeled operating-stage CO 2 emissions for all 240 away-team round trips in the 2025 Chinese Super League using a reference railway travel date of 20 September 2026. The analysis combines 2025 fixture geography with a 2026 transport snapshot; it does not reconstruct historical club travel. An air-intensive reference (S0) assigns coach travel to directional road distances of 300 km or less and air travel otherwise. S1 and S2 replace eligible reference air legs with no-transfer G/D/C-series rail services within six and eight scheduled hours, respectively. Outbound and return services and road access are evaluated separately, permitting mixed rail-air round trips. Results For the 480 modeled legs, each with 40 travelers, S0 emissions total 2,100.06 t CO 2 . S1 assigns 196 legs to rail and reduces the reference total by 478.99 t (22.81%). S2 assigns 232 rail legs, comprising 115 all-rail and two mixed round trips, and reduces the reference total by 620.34 t (29.54%). The five largest club savings account for 47.57% of S2 savings. Factorial scenarios yield 22.35% –23.79% for S1 and 29.11%–30.76% for S2; these ranges are not confidence intervals. Uniform 50% uptake reduces expected savings to 11.40% and 14.77%. Subsurface volumetric estimates of ultramafic and mafic rocks in the Livengood Terrane, Central Alaska: implications for carbon mineralization
abstract: Abstract Mafic and ultramafic rocks are sources of critical minerals and also provide a medium to securely store CO 2 . The objective of this study is to delineate the geometry and assess the volumes of ultramafic rocks in the Livengood Terrane in central Alaska using high-resolution aeromagnetic, petrophysical, and borehole datasets. We analyzed magnetic anomalies using 3D inversion using constraints from previous outcrop and petrophysical data. The high-resolution aeromagnetic anomaly map reveals elongated high-magnetic signatures extending from northeast corner to southwest corner of the study area, which are associated with the Cambrian Cascade ophiolite assemblage of the Livengood Terrane. 3D magnetic inversion results show three high-susceptibility bodies (HS-1 to HS-3) with magnetic susceptibility values ranging from 0.03 to 0.055 SI, and a combined estimated volume of ~ 12 km 3 . Estimates of in situ carbon mineralization based on laboratory experiments and stoichiometric calculations indicate a plausible CO 2 storage capacity of approximately 250 Mt to 1 Gt CO 2 . These findings highlight first-order target areas in the Livengood Terrane for initial assessment of carbon mineralization potential. Furthermore, this study demonstrates that geophysical inversion of magnetic data can help guide site selection and development for carbon mineralization.

title: Carbon Insertion into Electron-Deficient (Aza)indoles via a Radical-Polar Crossover Strategy
abstract: Abstract Despite a surge of progress in both strategic approaches and reagent design, carbon insertion into indoles remains limited to electron-rich substrates, notwithstanding the prevalence of electron-poor (aza)indoles in medicinal chemistry. We report herein a radical-polar crossover strategy that overcomes this limitation through a photocatalytic, iodomethyl-radical-mediated cyclopropanation/autoxidation approach. The method enables access to a range of highly substituted, electron-poor quinolines, naphthyridines, and triazanaphthalenes, many of which are challenging to prepare by traditional syntheses. We demonstrate the modification of medicinally relevant (aza)indoles, and preliminary mechanistic observations support autoxidation via an anionic cyclopropane ring opening pathway.

Industrialisation, Renewable Energy Consumption, and Carbon Dioxide Emissions in Indonesia: A Time Series Analysis of 1992–2021
abstract: This study examines the relationship between industrialization, renewable energy consumption, and carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions in Indonesia. Industrialization is proxied by industrial value added, and renewable energy consumption by its share of total energy consumption. Using a quantitative inferential approach, World Bank time series data for 1992–2021 were analyzed with multiple linear regression, with a logarithmic transformation of the dependent variable. Industrial value added has a positive and significant relationship with CO₂ emissions, whereas renewable energy consumption has a negative and significant relationship. Simultaneously, both variables are significantly related to emissions (F-statistic probability = 0.0000), and the coefficient of determination of 0.9895 shows that the model explains 98.95% of the variation in CO₂ emissions. Classical assumption tests indicate normality and no multicollinearity, autocorrelation, or heteroskedasticity, and the data satisfy stationarity. These findings suggest that rising industrial activity may increase carbon emissions, while renewable energy use can serve as a viable solution to mitigate them in Indonesia.

Enhancing efficiency and emission characteristics of a dual-fuel engine using spirulina biodiesel–ethanol blends with nanoparticles and hydrogen infusion
abstract: Abstract The present study aims to investigate the effect of ethanol and Titanium Dioxide (TiO₂) nanoparticles (NPs) as additives in Spirulina platensis oil methyl ester (SPOME)-diesel blends as pilot fuel, along with Hydrogen (H₂) as a secondary fuel, to determine the performance, combustion, and emission characteristics of a dual-fuel Compression Ignition (CI) diesel engine. Biodiesel was synthesized from Spirulina platensis oil via transesterification at a 1:6 oil-to-methanol molar ratio, yielding 97.2%. A B20 blend (20% SPOME + 80% diesel) was initially prepared, followed by B20E20 (20% vol. of Ethanol + B20). Further, TiO₂ NPs (50 mg/L) were dispersed in the B20E20 sample. These additive-enhanced blends were tested in a dual-fuel CI engine, with and without H₂ induction, at varying loads. The stability and homogeneity of the NP-dispersed blends were confirmed through FESEM, HRTEM, FTIR, SAED, and XRD analyses. Performance parameters such as Brake Thermal Efficiency (BTE) increased by 10.4%, and Brake Specific Fuel Consumption (BSFC) decreased by 13.3% significantly for the B20E20 + TiO₂50 + 6H₂ blend at higher load. Emissions of CO, CO₂, and HC reduced by 36.3%, 6.68%, and 8.36%, respectively. Although NOx emissions slightly increased with H₂ induction, the B20E20 blend exhibited reduced NOx at higher load. title: Biodiversity and Carbon Stock Management Strategy in Industrial Areas Based on the Focus-Diversify-Maintain (FDM) Framework: A Case Study of PT TMMIN Karawang Plant 3
abstract: Management of biodiversity in industrial areas requires a strategic approach to balance manufacturing activities with ecosystem conservation. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of applying the Focus-Diversify-Maintain (FDM) framework in optimizing biodiversity management and carbon storage at PT Toyota Motor Manufacturing Indonesia (TMMIN) Karawang Plant 3. Flora data collection was conducted via census in 8 built-up land blocks and sampling in undeveloped land. Avifauna data were gathered using a combination of point count, vantage point, species list methods, and drone-based aerial monitoring. Calculations of above-ground carbon stocks were performed based on biomass formulas and standard carbon conversion equations. The results identified 24 plant species from 13 families, totaling 1,302 tree and non-tree individuals in built-up areas, alongside 44 bird species from 24 families. The Shannon-Wiener diversity index ( ) for birds reached 2.227, dominated by Nycticorax nycticorax, Egretta garzetta, and Lonchura punctulata. The descriptively formulated FDM framework has the potential to guide priority avifauna conservation zoning (Focus), plan the enrichment of local food flora (Diversify), and recommend maintaining carbon sink functions (Maintain) within industrial areas.

abstract: Investigating the characteristics and formation mechanisms of plasma upflows at the edges of active regions (ARs) is essential for understanding the coupling between different layers of the solar atmosphere and the origin of the slow solar wind. Air-Compatible Indole-Based NHC–Copper Catalysts for A3 Coupling Reaction
abstract: Abstract A series of indole-based N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) copper complexes has been developed as air-compatible catalysts for A3 coupling reactions. The optimized catalytic system efficiently promotes the three-component coupling of aldehydes, amines, and alkynes under aerobic conditions with catalyst loadings as low as 0.1 mol %. Systematic evaluation of ligand structure reveals that both electronic and steric features of the indole-derived NHC framework play key roles in modulating catalytic activity and stability under air. Notably, differences in time-dependent catalytic behavior are correlated with the air stability of the Cu–NHC complexes, providing insight into catalyst deactivation pathways. These results demonstrate the potential of indole-based NHC–copper complexes as efficient catalysts for A3 coupling reactions under operationally simple conditions.

title: Transition Metal Phosphide/Carbon Nanocomposites for Supercapacitors: Structure-Property Relationships, Performance Limitations, and Design Principles
Review sustainable energy from livestock waste: a review of biogas production pathways
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable energy and the environmental challenges of livestock waste management have intensified interest in biogas as a renewable and circular bioenergy solution. This review critically evaluates biogas production from key livestock wastes such as chicken manure, piggery waste, and cow dung focusing on how feedstock composition, anaerobic digestion pathways, pretreatment methods, and co-digestion strategies influence methane yield and process stability. These substrates differ markedly in biochemical characteristics: chicken manure is nitrogen-rich and prone to ammonia inhibition, piggery waste exhibits high biodegradability and methane potential, and cow dung provides stable digestion but is constrained by lignocellulosic hydrolysis limitations. Comparative analysis of experimental studies reveals wide variability in reported methane yields, driven by differences in operating conditions, reactor design, microbial adaptation, and scale. Persistent gaps between theoretical biomethane potential and experimental performance are discussed, highlighting the roles of ammonia toxicity, hydrolysis-limited kinetics, and scale-dependent losses. Co-digestion and pretreatment consistently enhance methane production by improving nutrient balance and substrate accessibility, yet challenges remain in methodological standardization, process scalability, and long-term …

title: PENERAPAN PJU DENGAN SOLAR PANEL SEBAGAI IMPLEMENTASI ENERGI TERBARUKAN (RENEWABLE ENERGY) DI LINGKUNGAN TECHNO PARK UPNVJT
abstract: Kebutuhan energi terbarukan yang ramah lingkungan meningkat sebagai akibat dari krisis energi dan kerusakan yang disebabkan oleh penggunaan energi fosil. Indonesia memiliki potensi besar untuk memanfaatkan energi matahari karena negaranya tropis. Dapat dicapai melalui penggunaan panel surya untuk Penerangan Jalan Umum (PJU). Tujuan dari pengabdian ini yaitu untuk menerapkan sistem PJU berbasis tenaga surya di lingkungan Techno Park UPN “Veteran” Jawa Timur, sebagai bentuk pengabdian kepada masyarakat dan upaya untuk mendukung green campus. Metode pelaksanaannya melibatkan mahasiswa KKN melalui observasi, diskusi, perencanaan, pemasangan dan evaluasi. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa instalasi PJU berbasis tenaga surya berhasil memberikan pencahayaan yang terang, hemat energi, dan tahan terhadap kondisi lingkungan. Survei kepuasan pengguna menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar responden sangat puas dengan kualitas pencahayaan, kenyamanan, dan kontribusi program terhadap estetika lingkungan. PJU berbasis tenaga surya merupakan solusi penerangan yang berkelanjutan berdampak positif pada pengembangan energi terbarukan di lingkungan kampus. Kata Kunci : Panel surya PJU, energi terbarukan, kampus hijau , pengabdian masyarakat

title: Cycle Integration: Copy Number, the Closure Vesicle, and the Band of the Genome
abstract: The pore, the lipid supply, the replication schedule, the division rule and the codon-gated loop of the preceding articles are joined here into one cycle and asked a question none of them asked: whether every vessel keeps one strand. Replication runs once per period and division only at dusk, so one strand per vessel holds exactly when every vessel divides at every dusk. Three statements follow under named hypotheses. One period's lipids close exactly one minimal enclosure of the anchored strand, the closure vesicle, of radius 13.04 nm at 200 units. When every vessel divides at every dusk the mean birth size halves its distance to that vesicle each period, whatever the division rule, so the population comes to consist of closure vesicles dividing symmetrically; large founders persist only as a vanishing share, budding one closure vesicle per period. And the symmetric orbit exists if and only if a single number $g$, the per-period osmolyte gain in units of the closure vesicle's content, does not exceed one. Below one the vessels are flaccid at birth with reduced volume $g$; at one the orbit is taut and marginal; above one the closure vesicle is lost at its first dusk, and so is every other founder tried. Condensation raises the admissible input for an established lineage, but a founder without remnant gains less, and survives only if $g \leq 1/(2 - e^{-\kappa})$. Computed: for $…

title: Research on “Three Entries” Ideological and Political Curriculum Integration: A Case Study of English Writing Course
abstract: This study carried out a one semester comparative teaching experiment of curriculum ideological political education for second year English teacher majors in ZW University of China. Guided by the Production Oriented Approach (POA), the experiment integrated socialist core values into the whole process blended teaching of English Writing. The experimental group adopted an integrated online offline teaching design embedded with curriculum ideological political elements, while the control group received conventional writing instruction without special ideological political interventions. Multiple data sources including unified final examination papers, standardized questionnaires and semi structured individual & group interviews were adopted. Three core dimensions, namely learning motivation, value cognition improvement, and overall writing academic performance, were measured for effect evaluation. The experimental results demonstrated that the experimental group achieved statistically significant improvements across all three dimensions. Students’ comprehension of Chinese discourse, cross cultural critical thinking competence, and mission awareness to tell Chinese stories in English were notably enhanced. In contrast, no statistically significant changes were observed among the control group regarding learning initiative, value cognition or writing achievements. This experiment v…

title: Effectiveness of digital health interventions for care integration in coronary artery disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Structured Abstract Aim To assess the effectiveness of digital health interventions (DHIs) supporting care integration for coronary artery disease (CAD) in improving health outcomes compared to usual care. Methods For this systematic review, we searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, EBSCO Psychology and Behavioural Sciences Collection, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1 January 1995 to 5 November 2025. We included studies reporting primary data on DHIs supporting care integration for patients with CAD. Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and readmissions, and CVD events. Secondary endpoints were the control of cardiovascular risk factors. We conducted random-effects meta-analyses in RevMan and assessed risk of bias with Cochrane’s RoB tools. Results We included 72 studies (23,111 participants), assessing 45 in the meta-analysis. All DHIs supported person-centred care integration (n=72) while few DHIs addressed clinical care integration (n=22), professional integration (n=12) and functional integration (n=22). Compared to usual care, DHIs supporting care integration had significant reductions in the odds of CVD events (OR: 0.74 [0.59, 0.92], df=5, p=0.02), but not in all-cause mortality or readmissions. Conclusions Although this review shows that DHIs supporting care integration were associated with reduced CVD events compared to usual care, the current evidence remains concentrated pr…

title: A Low-Energy Vision-Language Pattern Recognition Method for Design Style Analysis and Generative Evaluation in Art Design Education
abstract: To address the problems that style recognition of student works in art design education relies heavily on teachers’ experience, generative evaluation feedback tends to be generalized, and multimodal models usually involve high inference energy consumption, this paper proposes a low-energy vision-language pattern recognition method, namely LE-VLPR. The proposed method takes design images, work descriptions, task requirements, and teacher rubrics as inputs, constructs a design style prompt graph, and achieves alignment between image features and style semantics through vision-language contrastive learning. A lightweight adapter, dynamic visual Token selection, and 8-bit quantized inference are further introduced to reduce deployment cost. Meanwhile, rubric-constrained evaluation and triple consistency verification are incorporated to reduce feedback hallucinations. Experiments on ArtEdu-Style show that LE-VLPR achieves 90.28% Accuracy and 89.69% Macro-F1. For generative evaluation, the Pearson correlation reaches 0.846, the MAE is reduced to 4.37, and the hallucination rate decreases to 4.21%. The per-sample energy consumption is 1.83 J, and the EEP reaches 49.01. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method can achieve accurate style recognition and reliable instructional feedback under low-energy conditions.

Implementation of self-declare policy in halal certification in Indonesia: challenges, policy model, and integration of maqāṣid al-sharīʿa
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the implementation of Indonesia’s self-declared halal certification policy for micro and small enterprises (MSE), identifies its challenges and proposes a policy framework that integrates maqāṣid al-sharīʿa principles to improve its effectiveness, equity and compliance. Design/methodology/approach This qualitative study was conducted among halal certification institutions (LP3H) in Java: State Islamic University (UIN) Walisongo Semarang, State Islamic University (UIN) Sunan Kalijaga Yogyakarta, Institute of Islamic Studies (IAI) Ngawi and State Islamic University (UIN) Raden Mas Said Surakarta. This study included LP3H managers, three halal product process assistants (PPH) who mentored more than 500 MSEs and seven MSE owners from Ponorogo in food production. MSE participants were identified through field outreach and the 3rd National Coordination Meeting of LP3H in Jakarta on June 7, 2024, which revealed 20 cases of administrative and substantive errors in self-declare. Data collection involved interviews, focus group discussions and field observations, including the socialization of Sertifikasi Halal Gratis (SEHATI; Free Halal Certification) services conducted by the Ponorogo Halal Center. Findings The implementation faces structural and operational bottlenecks, including inadequate coordination among LP3H, PPH and MSE actors, a disconnect be…

title: Energy-Sensitive Learnable Directional Prior-Fused Residual Clique Network for Seismic Data Denoising
abstract: Accurate reservoir prediction is essential for oil and gas exploration, yet strong random noise under complex geological conditions often obscures weak seismic reflections and limits the reliable characterization of dolomite reservoir sweet spots. To address this issue, we propose an Energy-Sensitive Learnable Directional Prior-Fused Residual Clique Network (ELDP-RCNet) for seismic denoising. The method combines a learnable directional high-frequency prior, residual Clique feature learning, and energy-sensitive amplification (ESA) to jointly enhance structural representation and weak-signal preservation. A non-subsampled multi-scale decomposition with learnable directional filtering is employed to capture anisotropic structural information, while ESA preferentially strengthens low-energy directional responses before prior aggregation. The resulting prior is progressively injected into cascaded residual Clique blocks, which promote hierarchical feature interaction and reuse. ESA is further incorporated into local residual learning to enhance weak seismic responses during deep feature extraction. Multi-level features are finally fused through global residual reconstruction. Experiments on synthetic seismic data demonstrate that ELDP-RCNet effectively suppresses random noise while improving signal-to-noise ratio, reflection-event continuity, spectral fidelity, and weak-signal pres…
