title: The Effect of Profitability, Capital Structure, and ESG on Firm Value with Dividend Policy as a Moderating Variable: Evidence from the Energy Sector
abstract: Background: Firm value in the energy sector reflects financial fundamentals and investors’ assessment of sustainability-related risks. Previous studies show mixed findings regarding the effects of profitability, capital structure, ESG performance, and dividend policy on market valuation. Objective: This study examines the effects of profitability, capital structure, and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance on firm value, with dividend policy as a moderating variable. Methods: Using purposive sampling, 15 of 89 energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2024 were selected. A quantitative approach with panel data regression was employed using combined time-series and cross-sectional data. Results: ROA, DER, ESG, DPR, and their interaction terms jointly affect firm value. Partially, ROA, ESG, and DPR significantly affect firm value, whereas DER does not. DPR moderates the relationships between ROA and firm value and between ESG and firm value but does not moderate the relationship between DER and firm value. Conclusion: Profitability, ESG performance, and dividend policy are significantly associated with firm value, while capital structure is not. Dividend policy moderates the profitability–firm value and ESG–firm value relationships. The negative ESG × DPR coefficient indicates that dividend policy weakens the association between…

title: Investigating the Combo correlation of gamma-ray bursts as a tracer of dynamical dark energy
abstract: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) collaboration recently presented results indicating that dark energy (DE) may exhibit dynamical behavior. Calibrated gamma-ray burst (GRB) correlations can be employed to verify or reject a time evolution of the DE equation of state (EoS), ω(z), up to redshifts of z∼ 9. We used the most updated catalog of GRBs fulfilling the Combo correlation; we improved its calibration by employing three catalogs of type Ia supernovae at redshifts of złeq0.075 and the Bézier interpolation of the Hubble rate as an alternative to the cosmographic series that cannot be constrained at high redshifts. To test the evolution of ω(z), we adopted a model-independent, redshift-binned DE parameterization. In both the calibration and the DE reconstruction analyses, the impact of the spatial curvature on the results was explored. The calibrated Combo correlation yields a Hubble constant of H_0 km/s/Mpc, which alleviates the existing Hubble tension and is broadly consistent with current measurements, although the uncertainties prevent a high-precision measurement. Regarding the reconstruction of ω(z), at złesssim0.55 we find a clear (gtrsim2 sigma) departure towards ω<-1 from the cosmological constant value. However, the shortage of GRBs in this redshift interval, together with possible population and selection effects, prevents us from drawing a robust concl…

title: PI-STGNN model-driven risk assessment method for leapfrog tripping in photovoltaic power plants
abstract: Unintended fault propagation in photovoltaic plants stems primarily from collector-line leapfrog tripping, a hazard characterized by multi-factor coupling, time-varying dynamics and hidden causal links that remain difficult to fully characterize under complex operating conditions. To tackle this challenge, this work presents a physics-informed spatio-temporal graph neural network (PI-STGNN) tailored for leapfrog tripping risk assessment: a hierarchical indicator set is constructed through systematic analysis of tripping mechanisms and protection coordination rules, a conditional diffusion model is deployed to generate multi-scenario augmented samples to alleviate real-world fault data scarcity, and physical constraints including protection time grading and electrical distance are explicitly embedded into the learning pipeline to strengthen the model’s capacity to capture risk evolution patterns and support accurate identification. For high-risk detection, the proposed approach achieves a precision of 0.92 and a recall of 0.91, delivering a notable reduction in missed detection of high-risk events.

title: Aerodynamic optimisation of HGVs trailers to minimise drag
abstract: In recent years, increasing efforts have been seen to reduce the output of greenhouse gas emissions. Rising fuel prices and legislative pressure by the UK government has pushed the drive to reducing emission production within the transport industry and, as a result, it has quickly become one of its primary goals. This has prompted the development of drag reduction methods to minimise the fuel consumption within vehicles. While sectors like automotives and aviation have advanced in this area, heavy goods vehicles have lagged behind despite their major contribution to UK freight and greenhouse gas emissions. Research shows that aerodynamic drag accounts for a major portion of HGV fuel consumption, which adds to their operational costs. This study focuses on this field, where boattails of varying slant angles and a teardrop trailer design were investigated, and their effectiveness in reducing drag was evaluated. This investigation was conducted through the use of Computational fluid dynamics where various meshing and modelling procedures were reviewed leading to high fidelity within the simulations. Following the investigation, it was found that the Teardrop trailer showed the best performance where it was able to achieve a 20.34% reduction in drag without any compromise on cargo space. This was attributed with its ability to reduce the size of the trailer base wake, reduce the fr…

title: Brain Tumor Diagnosis Using Vision Transformer and Optimized ViT with Hybrid Optimizers, and XAI Integration
abstract: Brain tumors critically affect human life and mostly fall into glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor categories. Detection in early stages and precise categorization lead efficiently to successful diagnosis and lowered healthcare expenditure. A classification system based on deep learning applying the ViT architecture to discriminate brain MRI images among these three types of tumors is introduced in this work. The initial brain tumor dataset in the .mat file format was resized to the .jpg file type and from 512–512 pixels to 224–224 pixels for suitable compatibility for processing using deep learning models. The dataset consisted of 3064 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI images, and the model had a classification accuracy of 93.8%. To improve the models performance and in this research, we used the RAdam and LookAhead optimizers and assessed the model’s performance using the 5-Fold cross-validation technique. In this study, the proposed model’s accuracy was obtained at 96.75%, 98.73%, 98.01%, 97.47%, and 98.37% through the use of the ViT, thus deriving a cross-validation accuracy of 97.87%, the suggested framework is supported by evidence that confirms its robustness and ability to generalize. To facilitate benchmarking, ViT was compared with various CNN models, such as VGG16 with Random Forest (VGG16-RF), VGG19, EfficientNet-B3, and MobileNet-Large, and these reached accura…

title: ANALYTICAL STUDY OF HEAT TRANSFER BY RAYLEIGH–BÉNARD CONVECTION IN VARIABLE VISCOSITY NEWTONIAN LIQUIDS: A WEAK NONLINEAR THEORY
abstract: Chaotic convection finds extensive application across diverse physical and mechanical phenomena, weather prediction, crystal production, satellite motion within our solar system, and ecological dynamics. Its widespread utility underscores its significance in understanding and analyzing complex systems in numerous fields. The study deals with the dynamics of regular and chaotic convection within a Newtonian fluid with variable viscosity confined between two infinitely extended horizontal layers with temperature gradient (Rayleigh–Bénard convection problem). Employing the Galerkin technique and using minimal representation of Fourier series, a three-dimensional generalized Lorenz nonlinear model is derived. The generalized Lorenz model derived is numerically solved and phase portraits are utilized to analyze the system’s qualitative dynamics. The onset of chaos in conventional fluid configurations occurs at a scaled Rayleigh number [Formula: see text] of 24.7368. Additionally, a weakly nonlinear analysis is performed to comprehend the heat transport within the fluid layer concerning the variation of the scaled Rayleigh number and thermorheological parameter. It is demonstrated that the onset of convection occurs at significantly lower Rayleigh numbers in fluids with exponentially decreasing viscosity compared with fluids of constant viscosity. Furthermore, an increase in the ther…

title: Pulsatile flows for simplified smart fluids with variable exponent power-law: Analysis and numerics
abstract: In this paper, we study the fully-developed, time-periodic motion of a shear-dependent non-Newtonian fluid with variable exponent rheology through an infinite pipe [Formula: see text], [Formula: see text], of arbitrary cross-section [Formula: see text]. The focus is on a generalized [Formula: see text]-fluid model, where the power-law index is position-dependent (with respect to [Formula: see text]), i.e. a function [Formula: see text]. We prove the existence of time-periodic solutions with either assigned time-periodic flow-rate or pressure-drop, generalizing known results for the Navier–Stokes and for [Formula: see text]-fluid equations. In addition, we identify explicit solutions, relevant as benchmark cases, especially for electro-rheological fluids or, more generally, “smart fluids”. To support practical applications, we present a fully-constructive existence proof for variational solutions by means of a fully-discrete finite-difference/-element discretization, consistent with our numerical experiments. Our approach, which unifies the treatment of all values of [Formula: see text], [Formula: see text], without requiring an auxiliary Newtonian term, provides new insights even in the constant exponent case. The theoretical findings are illustrated by means of numerical experiments.

title: Measurement method of entrance pupil baseline for Dual-mode Variable-array Imaging Interferometer Testbed
abstract: In 2018, China proposed the Multiple spacecraft Exoplanet Aperture sYnthetic INterferometer (MEAYIN) project to explore habitable planets near other solar systems. We have established a Dual-mode Variable-array Imaging Interferometer Testbed (DVIIT) in the laboratory to develop some key technologies for the MEAYIN. The precise measurement method of the entrance pupil baselines for each sub-aperture is one of the key technologies to be developed. A measurement method of entrance pupil baselines based on dual-comb femtosecond laser absolute ranging technology has been proposed. It uses independently developed ranging optical ruler and a reference aperture to measure the distance from the system optical axis of the DVIIT to each sub-aperture. Measure the motion errors of each sub-aperture and then correct the distance based on the measurement results to obtain more accurate entrance pupil baselines. Theoretical analysis and test result indicated that the method can achieve micrometer level measurement accuracy for the entrance pupil baselines of the DVIIT. In addition, the method has the feasibility of being extended to the MEAYIN project with longer baselines.

Detection thresholds are established through peak signal-to-noise-ratio statistics and analysis of inverted maps. In this paper, we focus on the ALMA-accessible CANDELS fields (COSMOS, GOODS-S, and UDS), covering ∼130,000 optical/NIR-selected galaxies spanning 0.0<z<15.0. We identify an ALMA data mining project. title: Role of Rock Mechanics and Rock Engineering in Energy Transition: A Perspective from ARMA 2025
Formation dynamics of a rotating solar spicule-like event and associated energy-mass transport
abstract: Vortical structures and elongated chromospheric spicule-like features are ubiquitous small-scale dynamic phenomena in the lower solar atmosphere. Both are important channels for transporting mass and energy from the solar surface to the corona. However, the physical connection between vortical motions and the formation of spicule-like structures, as well as their role in mass and energy transport, remains incompletely understood. We aim to investigate the connection between the vortex motion and the formation of a spicule-like event and the associated mass and energy transport. We performed three-dimensional radiative magnetohydrodynamic (3D RMHD) simulations in an upward-directed (positive-polarity) open magnetic field with an initial background strength of 10 G. We identified vortex-associated spicule-like events and carried out a detailed analysis of one representative event. Prior to the formation of this spicule-like event, a photospheric vortex appears and twists the magnetic field lines, then develops upwards into higher atmospheric layers, forming a magnetic tornado system. This event is generated during this process. At the periphery of this magnetic tornado, twisted magnetic field lines with negative vertical components reconnect with both external positive-polarity background fields and central positive-polarity fields. The magnetic reconnection sites rise and rotate…

title: Drought severity determines the effectiveness of straw mulching in alleviating water stress during early maize growth
abstract: Introduction Drought is a major constraint on the early growth and photosynthetic productivity of maize (Zea mays L.), yet whether the physiological benefits of straw mulching depend on drought severity remains unclear. Methods A two-year experiment was conducted in 2025 and 2026 using straw removal and straw mulching under three irrigation levels (135, 105, and 75 mm), representing well-watered, moderate-drought, and severe-drought conditions, respectively. Plant growth, photosynthetic performance, carbon-assimilation enzyme activities, osmotic adjustment, and antioxidant responses were evaluated. Results Increasing drought severity generally reduced leaf area index (LAI), plant height (PH), dry matter accumulation (DW), photosynthetic performance, and carbon-assimilation capacity, while increasing the accumulation of proline, soluble sugars, betaine, malondialdehyde (MDA), and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), together with antioxidant responses. The physiological effects of straw mulching varied markedly with drought severity. Under moderate drought, mulching more consistently maintained plant growth and photosynthetic performance, preserved carbon-assimilation enzyme activities, and reduced MDA and H₂O₂ accumulation. In contrast, these beneficial responses were substantially weaker and less consistent under severe drought. Across physiological traits, better growth and carbon-a…

title: Elapsed irrigation time improves morpho-kinematic classification of lettuce irrigation-stress histories
abstract: Plant movement carries information on water status, but its predictive value may depend on the recent irrigation context in which movement is expressed. Previous lettuce morpho-kinematic (MK) analyses suggested that integrating a precise measurement of elapsed irrigation time ( Δt , defined as the interval from the last irrigation preceding the observation day to the start of imaging, excluding any same-day irrigation) may improve classification, but its contribution was not formally separated from nominal irrigation schedule (which represents a protocol-derived low-resolution Δt proxy). We reanalysed 140 plant-day observations from 24 plants in two controlled-environment experiments using, to isolate the predictive value of Δt , a schedule-balanced binary contrast obtained by grouping well irrigated (FC) and chronic stress (SC) against moderate and severe acute stresses (SM and SS respectively). Penalised logistic models were evaluated with plant-level balanced validation and plant-class balanced log-loss. Adding Δt reduced held-out log-loss from 0.5250 to 0.4836 (ΔLL = 0.0414; 95% CI = [0.0034, 0.0807]), whereas adding nominal schedule did not (ΔLL = −0.0039; 95% CI = [−0.0342, 0.0273]). The estimated Δt benefit remained predominantly positive under stricter validation, while schedule-preserving permutations and redundancy analysis supported an observation-specific contributi…

title: Hetero-grafting affects sugar and flavonoid accumulation in ‘Misty’ blueberry (Vaccinium corymbosum)
abstract: Introduction Grafting can be used in blueberry cultivation to improve soil adaptability and scion fruit quality. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Methods We investigated the effects of rabbiteye blueberry ( Vaccinium virgatum ) ‘Climax’ and ‘Brightwell’ rootstocks on fruit quality, biochemical characteristics, and related gene expression in ‘Misty’ blueberry ( Vaccinium corymbosum ). Results The fruit quality of ‘Climax’-grafted ‘Misty’ (CM) was superior to that of ‘Brightwell’-grafted ‘Misty’ (BM). CM showed greater scion stem diameter and fruit size, as well as the net photosynthetic rate, and chlorophyll contents in leaves. Notably, LC-MS/MS analysis detected significant increases in specific sugars and flavonoids in CM fruit, with glucose and fructose contents 10.2% and 11.4% higher than BM, respectively. Twenty-four out of the 31 quantified flavonoids were more abundant in CM. In contrast, 26 of the 28 detected amino acids accumulated at higher levels in BM, as did most organic acids. A total of 1,411 differentially expressed genes, including 830 upregulated and 581 downregulated genes, were detected between CM and BM fruit, in which the genes associated with sugar ( VcSWEET12 and VcINV1 ) and flavonoids ( VcF3′H and VcUFGT ) were upregulated in CM fruit. An integrated analysis pinpointed nine transcription factors, including VcWRKY75 …

A consistent, physical, and analytical model for cosmic microwave background observables of reionisation. I. Derivation, constraining power, and detectability of the auto spectra
abstract: The epoch of reionisation imprints its history and morphology on the cosmic microwave background temperature and polarisation anisotropies through two effects: the kinetic Sunyaev Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect and Thomson scattering. To perform joint analyses of these observables and put tight constraints on the reionisation history and morphology, a common reionisation model is required. We present a quick, physically accurate analytical approach to consistently deriving the angular power spectra of the three main resulting imprints: the spatial fluctuations of the Thomson optical depth, patchy kSZ effect, and scattering and screening B-modes. The approach differs from existing analytical models, as it is calibrated on high-resolution hydrodynamical simulations and depends on the physical parameters of reionisation. Our predicted power spectra are consistent with the ones derived from cosmological simulations, whilst including more physical information, such as the typical size of ionised bubbles and the duration of reionisation. We provide an updated detectability assessment and show that both C_ and C_ Python package. could be measured by experiments similar to CMB Stage 4 and CMB-HD, respectively. We demonstrate the complementarity of the three observables in constraining reionisation history and morphology, and we also illustrate the potential of their joint analysis to get a gl…

title: Salicylic Acid-Induced MdTGA9-MdERF138- MdHCT Module Is Associated with Lignin Deposition and Improved Anthracnose Resistance in Autotetraploid Apple
abstract: Summary Apple anthracnose, caused by Colletotrichum gloeosporioides, severely threatens global apple production. Autotetraploid ‘Hanfu’ apples show stronger anthracnose resistance than diploids, but the underlying molecular mechanism remains unclear. This study identified a novel salicylic acid (SA)-regulated lignin biosynthesis signaling pathway that is closely associated with the enhanced resistance in autotetraploid ‘Hanfu’ apples. Autotetraploid apples accumulated higher endogenous SA levels, and the SA-responsive transcription factor MdTGA9 was markedly induced by both SA treatment and C. gloeosporioides infection. Mechanistically, MdTGA9 acts as a nuclear transcriptional activator to directly bind to the MdERF138 promoter and activate its expression. MdERF138 then transactivates the lignin biosynthetic gene MdHCT, thereby promoting lignin accumulation. Functional verification showed that MdTGA9 overexpression in apple calli, fruits and leaves significantly enhanced anthracnose resistance, and MdERF138 and MdHCT were confirmed as positive regulators of this resistance. Collectively, this study reveals a previously uncharacterized MdTGA9-MdERF138-MdHCT regulatory cascade that integrates SA signaling and lignin-based physical defense, which accounts for the enhanced disease resistance of autotetraploid apple. These findings provide valuable gene resources and a new molecular…

title: Combined application of Azospirillum brasilense and humic acid improves growth, physiology and yield of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) under tillering-stage drought stress
abstract: Abstract Drought at the tillering stage is one of the most damaging abiotic constraints to wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) production in arid and semi-arid cropping systems. A field experiment was conducted to evaluate whether the plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium Azospirillum brasilense and the organic soil amendment humic acid, applied singly or in combination, could mitigate the adverse effects of drought stress imposed at the tillering stage. The experiment was laid out in a randomized complete block design with eight treatments and three replications: an untreated control, sole A. brasilense , sole humic acid, and their combination, each evaluated under well-watered and drought-stressed conditions. Drought stress was initiated at tillering (25 days after sowing) by withholding the first irrigation and was maintained for 21 days, after which normal irrigation resumed. Drought stress significantly ( p < 0.01) reduced all measured growth, physiological and yield attributes relative to the well-watered control. Sole application of A. brasilense or humic acid partially alleviated these reductions, but the combined treatment consistently produced the most favorable outcome under both water regimes. Under well-watered conditions, the combined treatment increased plant height, spike length, spikelets per spike, 1000-grain weight, grain yield and biological yield by 13.2, 25.4, 9…

title: Analyzing one’s own and others’ errors in 360° video-based virtual reality: an exploratory pilot study in swiss vocational healthcare training
abstract: Abstract Video-based reflection can help learners recognize procedural errors and develop prevention strategies. 360° video-based virtual reality (360°VR) is increasingly used for error analysis, especially in tertiary education, because it can depict authentic professional situations with a high degree of physical realism. However, little is known about whether analyzing one’s own errors differs from analyzing a peer’s errors in 360°VR and about how vocational learners respond to this task. Using a two-condition between-groups design, this pilot study compared two approaches to error analysis in 360°VR: healthcare assistant apprentices analyzed either their own venipuncture procedure (SELF; n = 16) or a peer’s procedure (PEER; n = 17). Outcomes included error-analysis performance, sense of presence, epistemic emotions, motivation, and perceived cognitive demand. Between-group differences were analyzed using Mann–Whitney U tests. SELF participants reported a higher sense of presence and perceived usefulness, but also greater anxiety. Although SELF participants rated the error-analysis task as easier than PEER participants did, performance did not differ detectably and was low in both conditions, suggesting that the task may have been difficult for apprentices. The substantially greater effort required to produce individualized SELF recordings was therefore not matched by any de…

abstract: Compensating for atmospheric turbulence through the use of adaptive optics (AO) has now become commonplace for VLT and ELT class telescopes in order to retrieve a resolution close to their diffraction limit. Accompanying this trend is a greater need for simulations that can be used to understand and predict performance when facing different observing conditions, namely the evolution of the atmospheric turbulence or the diversity of the AO guide source. The so-called power spectral density (PSD)-based methods are well adapted to this demand thanks to their simplicity and speed. Moreover, they provide a comprehensive breakdown error budget and impact on the focal plane, which is of especially high interest in the case of extreme AO. The drawback of these methods is the challenge to describe non-linear wavefront sensors (WFSs), such as the pyramid WFS or the Zernike WFS. Thus, there is a need for the development of fast yet accurate methods to describe the behaviour of AO systems including sensitive WFSs. AO systems We have developed a method to compute the AO system response (electromagnetic phase power spectral density and point spread function) based on the accuracy of the convolutive formalism. Our method allows for the inclusion of the non-linear behaviour of the WFS within PSD-based numerical tools. We compared the numerical implementation of the method with end-to-end simul…

title: Best practices for patient authorship and involvement in pharmaceutical industry peer-reviewed publications: systematic literature review and qualitative evidence synthesis
abstract: Abstract Background Patient authorship and involvement in peer-reviewed publications is an increasing and evolving practice across the pharmaceutical industry, however implementation remains inconsistent and there is a need for specific and comprehensive guidelines. Methods This practice-informed systematic literature review and qualitative evidence synthesis searched the peer-reviewed and grey literature (1 Jan 2018–1 June 2025) for meta-research, thought leadership, or commentaries about patient involvement in publications. Qualitative extractions were split into three datasets of best practices, gaps, and recommendations. Best practice codes were then categorised and synthesised into evidence-based best practices using meta-aggregative pragmatic inquiry and mapped to the stages of the publication lifecycle. As secondary, a priori analyses, a subset of codes relating to conflicting topics from the codebook generated using the best practice dataset were then deductively applied to the gaps and recommendations datasets and analysed for interpretation and expansion of concepts using reflexive thematic analysis. Results A total of 166 peer-reviewed literature and grey literature records were included in the reviewed, resulting in a synthesis of 66 best practices for patient involvement in peer-reviewed publications across and beyond the publication lifecycle. Two conflicting best…

title: Promoting mental health and social inclusion among refugees and asylum seekers in Greece: a practice-based pilot evaluation of a peer-delivered PM+ and case management intervention
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to present a practice-based pilot evaluation of a peer-delivered multicomponent psychosocial intervention for refugees and asylum seekers in Greece. The intervention combined Problem Management Plus (PM+), addressing the mental health dimension of distress through structured psychological strategies, with peer case management (PCM), addressing the social inclusion-oriented dimension through service navigation, practical support and linkage to community resources. Design/methodology/approach This study used a non-randomised pre–post design. Adult Arabic-, Farsi- and French-speaking refugees and asylum seekers receiving community-based psychosocial support in Athens were enrolled during the 2023 implementation year. Of 61 eligible participants, 47 completed the full programme, including five PM+ sessions, needs-led PCM and both baseline and post-intervention assessments. Outcomes were assessed using the GAD-7, PHQ-9 and PSYCHLOPS. Findings Participants showed statistically significant reductions in anxiety symptoms, depressive symptoms and person-generated psychological distress from baseline to post-intervention, with large within-group effect sizes. Exploratory analyses suggested that the degree of change varied across some participant characteristics. Research limitations/implications The absence of a control group, completer-analysis design, small samp…

title: The Impact of Greenfield Investment in Renewables on Energy Poverty
abstract: In the context of the global energy transition and the continuous advancement of sustainable development goals, how Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments can improve energy accessibility, reduce energy use costs and alleviate energy poverty has become an important issue in energy economics research.This study investigates the impact of Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments on energy poverty using panel data from 153 countries from 2003 to 2023.This study employs a two-way fixed effects model and further conducts endogeneity tests and a series of robustness checks. The results provide the following observations. First, Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments significantly reduces energy poverty. Second, its mitigating effect varies across countries and regions. Third, the effect shows greater strength in non-high-income countries. Moreover, the mechanism analysis based on the interaction between Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments and electricity consumption indicates that Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments plays a stronger role in alleviating energy poverty in countries with lower electricity consumption levels.Hence, this research provides stronger support for the role of Renewable Energy Greenfield Investments in mitigating energy poverty. This paper further delves into the policy implications arising from the findings.

title: Depth-Dependent CO2 Storage Efficiency: A Numerical Simulation Study of Saline Aquifers
abstract: Abstract Estimation of CO2 storage efficiency with depth is important for assessing the feasibility, scalability, and long-term performance of carbon capture and storage (CCS) projects. Previous studies have reported inconsistent observations regarding the variation of storage efficiency with depth, including a nonlinear trend in which structural storage efficiency declines to zero near 2400 m, nonzero simulated storage efficiencies by the DOE-NETL, and claims of completely leak-free storage at greater depths due to phase-density reversal. A consistent and validated understanding of depth-dependent storage efficiency based on exhaustive reservoir fluid dynamics and reactive phase equilibrium is unavailable. This study presents a comprehensive numerical investigation of CO2 storage efficiency in saline aquifers as a function of depth using 2-D CMG-GEM simulations conducted over 1000 years, with all key flow dynamics and thermodynamic parameters defined as depth-dependent. Results show that total CO2 storage efficiency decreases from ∼0.92 at 800 m and 0.99 at 1200 m to ∼0.76 at 2500 m and remains within a narrow band at greater depths. Total CO2 leakage efficiency increases from ∼0.02 at 800 m to a maximum of ∼0.35 at 4000 m, and then declines to ∼0.22 at 11,000 m. The CO2 storage capacity per unit pore volume increases continuously with depth, reaching ∼980 kg/m3 at approximate…

title: Gen-EBM: An energy balance model for terrestrial planets. Climate multistability from snowball to post-runaway greenhouse climates
abstract: Climate multistability and tipping points are fundamental properties of planetary climates that strongly depend on the underlying climate feedbacks. We present the Geneva energy balance model (Gen-EBM), a new 1D latitudinal EBM designed for the rapid exploration of terrestrial planet climates, and use it to investigate how planetary rotation, eccentricity, and thermal inertia shape climate attractors and multistability. Gen-EBM was implemented in Rust and builds upon previous exoplanet EBMs by incorporating a temperature-dependent, outgoing longwave radiation prescription spanning Earth-like, runaway-onset, and post-runaway greenhouse regimes. We constructed bifurcation diagrams from ensembles of simulations and explored the effects of rotation rate, orbital eccentricity under the mean-flux approximation, and surface thermal inertia. The inclusion of post-runaway greenhouse states substantially enlarges the region of parameter space over which multiple climate states coexist. Within our model framework, slow rotators approach the spatially homogeneous limit and maintain broader temperate stability ranges, whereas fast rotators develop strong equator-to-pole temperature gradients that narrow the temperate branch. Under the mean-flux approximation, increasing eccentricity enhances climate variability and can modify the attractor structure itself. The critical eccentricity at whic…

title: Comparative analysis of bioethanol production in Ghana and West Africa: capabilities, challenges, and transferable practices—a systematic review
abstract: Ghana’s bioethanol industry holds significant renewable energy potential in West Africa; it is characterized by abundant agricultural resources but constrained by structural and policy challenges. This systematic review examines Ghana’s bioethanol production capabilities relative to eight regional countries (Nigeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, and South Africa), analyzing feedstock availability, policy frameworks, technological adoption, and socioeconomic impacts through a defined literature search and screening strategy, comparative policy analysis, and thematic synthesis (see Methodology). Ghana demonstrates diversified feedstock potential with cassava yields of 22–38 tons/hectare and ethanol production potential of 280–320 L/ton from cassava peels. Agricultural residues could theoretically produce 200 million liters annually, sufficient for five million households. However, only 5% of this potential is currently utilized due to collection and processing constraints. Policy analysis reveals that while Ghana established a 10% biofuel integration target by 2020 (extended to 20% by 2030), implementation lacks enforcement mechanisms, unlike successful regional models such as Malawi’s E10 blending mandate, which has been in place since 1982. Ghana possesses exceptional feedstock diversification potential, particularly through non-competitive food crop…

title: Hesitancy fuzzy Zagreb energy for hesitancy fuzzy graphs with application to optimal business location selection
abstract: In a fuzzy graph (FG), A membership value ranging from 0 to 1 is allocated to every vertex and edge, indicating the extent to which they participate in the graph. This idea is elaborated upon in an intuitionistic fuzzy graph (IFG), offering a more sophisticated method of addressing uncertainty through providing vertices and edges membership, non-membership, and hesitation values. Hesitancy fuzzy graphs (HFGs), which show the degrees of truthfulness, falsehood, and abstention, extend the idea of the IFG. The Zagreb indices (ZIs) are topological descriptors in graph theory (GT) defining the structural aspects of a graph utilizing vertex degrees. This study enhances the notion of fuzzy ZIs in FGs to hesitancy fuzzy Zagreb indices (HFZIs) in the context of HFGs. This study demonstrates the hesitancy fuzzy Zagreb matrix (HFZM) and the hesitancy fuzzy Zagreb energy (HFZE) of HFGs with the aid of illustrated examples. The lower and upper limits of the HFZM and HFZE have been established. To demonstrate their relevance, these HFGs were used to solve a decision-making (DM) problem, specifically identifying the ideal location for launching a Zagreb energy (ZE) based firm. Along with that, the ZE of the spherical fuzzy Zagreb matrix (SFZM) and the HFZM are compared.

Lepto-hadronic modeling of blazars associated with well-reconstructed high-energy neutrino events
abstract: The association of active galactic nuclei (AGN) with high-energy neutrinos has been investigated in both population studies and individual source analyses. However, whether individual associations are driven by physical processes or arise from chance coincidences remains an open question. A sample of blazars, AGN with relativistic jets closely aligned with the line of sight, spatially consistent with IceCube high-energy events, provides a natural framework to address this question. By combining multifrequency observations with physically motivated emission models, it is possible to assess whether these sources can plausibly account for the detected neutrinos. We studied six blazars with single gamma-ray counterparts to well-reconstructed IceCAT-1 high-energy events, accounting for the improved localization expected from IceCAT-2, and compiled their multifrequency spectral energy distributions. We modeled these sources within a lepto-hadronic framework, exploring their parameter space in order to reproduce the observed emission while preferentially selecting solutions that maximize neutrino production. We find that the spectral energy distributions can be reproduced with compact emission regions close to the broad-line region with moderately high Doppler factors. The overall emission is generally dominated by leptonic processes with subdominant contributions from hadronic cascad…

title: Beneath the flames: season of burning effects on growth in native grassland plants with underground storage organs
abstract: Underground storage organs (USOs) allow many perennial herbaceous plants to survive disturbance and seasonal stress by storing resources that support resprouting. However, the cost of disturbance may depend strongly on when it occurs relative to plant phenology and resource allocation cycles. In temperate grasslands, prescribed fire has historically been applied during summer or autumn when many herbaceous species are dormant. Increasing use of spring burns means fire can coincide with active growth and reproduction; yet, the implications for USO-dependent species remains poorly understood. We tested how burn season influences growth and belowground resource dynamics in four perennial species common to temperate native grasslands. Plants were subjected to simulated fire treatments in either spring (during active growth) or summer (after the main growth season). USO dry mass was measured as a proxy for stored resources, and post-fire phenological responses were monitored to assess the effects of subsequent growth and reproduction. Responses varied among species. Eryngium ovinum (Apiaceae) and Arthropodium strictum (Asparagaceae) rapidly resprouted after spring burning, and in some cases, reproduced within the same growing season. Summer burning coincided more closely with their vegetative dormancy. Both species generally had lower USO biomass following spring burns than summer b…

Association Between Health Promotion Program Participation and Health Knowledge and Health-Promoting Behavior Among Adolescents in Pati Regency, Central Java: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Introduction: This study aimed to examine the association between participation in adolescent health-promotion programs and health knowledge and health-promoting behaviors among adolescents in Pati Regency, Central Java. Methods: A quantitative analytic cross-sectional study was conducted from February to April 2025 across three sub-districts: Kecamatan Pati, Juwana, and Gabus. A total of 207 adolescents aged 13–19 years from six public junior and senior high schools were selected using multistage stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a structured self-administered questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, participation in Posyandu Remaja or Pelayanan Kesehatan Peduli Remaja (PKPR), health knowledge, and health-promoting behaviors. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, and multivariable binary logistic regression. Results: Participation in Posyandu Remaja or PKPR was independently associated with adequate health knowledge after adjustment for sociodemographic factors (adjusted OR = 2.89; 95% CI: 1.68–4.97; p < 0.001). Participation was also associated with good health-promoting behavior in bivariate analysis (crude OR = 2.74; 95% CI: 1.63–4.60; p < 0.001). Reproductive health had the lowest proportion of adequate knowledge (43.0%), whereas physical activity had the highest (73.4%). Female sex was independently associa…

abstract: Purpose: This study analyzes the procedure for eliminating Rural and Urban Land and Building Tax (Pajak Bumi dan Bangunan Perdesaan dan Perkotaan/PBB-P2) receivables based on proof of payment at the Regional Revenue Agency (Badan Pendapatan Daerah/Bapenda) of Palembang City and evaluates its conformity with applicable Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).Methodology: A qualitative descriptive approach was used. Data were collected through observation, interviews with Bapenda staff, and documentation of administrative processes during a practical work program. The data were analyzed by comparing implementation practices with existing SOP provisions.Results: The findings show that the elimination procedure is generally implemented in accordance with administrative rules, including application submission, document verification, evidence examination, preparation of the elimination decree, official review, and final approval by the Head of Bapenda. However, implementation still refers to the objection SOP because a specific SOP for elimination based on proof of payment has not yet been established.Conclusions: The procedure is administratively orderly and largely consistent with current SOPs, while the integrated tax information system enhances data accuracy and verification effectiveness.Limitations: This study is limited to the implementation of PBB-P2 receivable elimination proce…

Accuracy of electric current inference assuming three-dimensional hydrostatic equilibrium
abstract: The chromospheric and coronal heating problem is among the major open questions in solar physics. There are many possible mechanisms that can explain the rise in temperature that is required to reproduce the observations, many of which are related to the presence of magnetic fields. However, their observational confirmation and relative contributions are far from being fully established. Studying some of the heating processes in the solar atmosphere requires the estimation of electric currents. Since these depend on the spatial derivatives of the magnetic field components, it is necessary to obtain the full magnetic field vector from observational data in a 3D geometrical grid. We developed a new method to obtain the 3D geometrical configuration of the atmosphere using the approximation of hydrostatic equilibrium in three dimensions to determine the gas pressure and density as a function of optical depth, column mass, or geometrical distance. This development has been designed as an extension for any inversion code that outputs a stratification of temperature and gas pressure or density to enable the estimation of electric current densities from observations. We investigated our approach using a snapshot from a sunspot MHD simulation. The difference between the solver output and the simulation, taken as the ground truth, is mostly between 30 and 45 %. It does show a similar pat…

title: Electric charge modifies the far-infrared and millimetre opacity of cosmic dust grains
abstract: Electrically charged dust grains are ubiquitous in astrophysical environments, yet their extinction properties at far-infrared (FIR) and millimetre wavelengths have not been studied. Using the modified Lorenz--Mie formalism with charge-induced surface conductivity, we compute the column-density-normalised extinction of four grain materials representative of interstellar medium dust, over a range of size distributions and surface electric potentials. For electrically neutral grains the results reproduce conventional Mie extinction behaviour. When a surface potential of only a few volts is imposed, new extinction features emerge at łambda ≳ 50,μm that are entirely absent in neutral grains. The amplitude depends strongly on grain material. For amorphous silica the enhancement reaches several orders of magnitude at łambda > 50,μm, while astronomical silicate develops a broad new bump at łambda > 100,μm. The physical origin is resonant excitation of surface plasmon-like modes by excess charge carriers. These results show that the opacity of cosmic dust in the submillimetre and millimetre domain depends on the grain charge state, a factor not considered in current interstellar medium dust models or cosmic microwave background foreground analyses.

title: Practical Tools for Fire Risk Assessment in Mediterranean Open Woodlands Using Handheld Laser Scanning and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Photogrammetry
abstract: Abstract Mediterranean forests are becoming increasingly vulnerable to wildfires. Given this, there is an urgent need for accurate, high-resolution data on canopy fuel characteristics to facilitate fire behavior modeling and guide risk mitigation efforts. This study assesses the performance of handheld mobile laser scanning (HMLS) and low-cost unmanned aerial vehicle digital aerial photogrammetry (UAV-DAP) in estimating key canopy fuel parameters and stand structural attributes, including canopy base height, stand height, canopy fuel load, canopy bulk density, and canopy cover. Field data were collected from 12 circular plots in open woodlands ( dehesas ) dominated by Quercus suber or Quercus ilex in the southwest of the Iberian Peninsula. Each plot was surveyed using traditional forest inventory, HMLS with a GeoSLAM ZEB Horizon scanner, and UAV DAP with RGB imagery processed using structure-from-motion techniques. In both cases, the resulting point clouds were processed using LiDAR360 software to extract canopy fuel parameters. HMLS yielded the most accurate estimates for most variables, with relative root mean square error (RMSE%) values ranging from 4% for canopy fuel load to 23.3% for canopy base height. UAV DAP showed a wider range of RMSE% values, from 5.9% for stand height to 41.2% for canopy bulk density, and was notably less effective for variables that require the cha…

title: A sustainable Fermatean fuzzy bi-objective four-dimensional transportation model for automated electric vehicle logistics planning using a Fermatean fuzzy game-theoretic method
abstract: The transportation problem is a significant optimization model in supply chain management and logistics that aims to determine the most effective allocation of goods from multiple sources to various destinations. In a logistics plan, shipments are frequently transported through different routes using automated electric vehicles (AEVs) instead of regular vehicles, which offers a sustainable alternative by reducing transportation-related emissions, improving air quality, eliminating noise pollution, supporting green logistics, and reducing dependence on fossil fuels. The simultaneous consideration of objectives and parameters, such as origins, destinations, routes, and vehicles, extends the classical transportation problem to a bi-objective four-dimensional transportation problem, providing a realistic framework for complex logistics networks. However, in a real-world scenario, parameters are often uncertain due to dynamic traffic conditions, fluctuating energy prices, varying road conditions, and adverse weather conditions. The triangular Fermatean fuzzy environment effectively captures uncertainty associated with the parameters by allowing greater flexibility, thereby providing more reliable decision-making under uncertain conditions. For these reasons, this study develops a bi-objective four-dimensional transportation model under a triangular Fermatean fuzzy environment for AE…

title: On-sky dark-hole digging with implicit electric field conjugation on MagAO-X
abstract: Direct spectroscopy is a very promising approach to characterizing the atmospheres of nearby rocky exoplanets, but non-common path aberrations (NCPA), which are differential aberrations between the science optical path and the adaptive optics optical path, can leak through the coronagraph and create speckles that mimic exoplanet signals. This limits the sensitivity of high-contrast imaging instruments at close angular separations - exactly the separations where we want to search for rocky exoplanets with current and future telescopes and instruments. We aim to actively remove the NCPA on-sky during observations by using focal-plane wavefront sensing and control with the newly upgraded MagAO-X instrument. MagAO-X is equipped with a unique second-stage adaptive optics (AO) system containing a dedicated deformable mirror (DM) for coronagraphic focal-plane wavefront control. Because this DM is placed after the science and AO beam splitter, it is not seen by the main AO loop. The DM has been recently upgraded from an ALPAO-97 to a Boston Micromachine Kilo-DM, which enables focal-plane wavefront control with the implicit electric field conjugation (iEFC) algorithm. We developed the necessary procedures to run iEFC with MagAO-X on-sky. We demonstrate the successful removal of NCPA on-sky with an iEFC interaction matrix that was calibrated on the MagAO-X internal source; this demonstra…

title: Resilience dynamics in family SMEs of the Kivu: a longitudinal analysis of responses to black swan and risk events in a VUCA context
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how family-owned small and medium-sized family enterprises (SMEs) in the Kivu region develop and adopt resilient behaviours in response to both predictable disruptions and highly unpredictable events. It further examines how these resilience responses evolve over time. Design/methodology/approach A longitudinal qualitative multiple-case study design was adopted. Data were collected from six family-owned SMEs through repeated interviews to examine the disruptive events they experienced and the responses implemented before, during and after each disruption. The data were analysed using thematic analysis to identify and classify the resilience mechanisms mobilised throughout the disruption process. Findings The findings reveal that Kivu family-owned SMEs deploy multiple resilience responses simultaneously rather than sequentially. Organisational agility and market-oriented strategies are mobilised in complementary ways across different types of disruptions. The analysis also highlights a strong temporal dimension, showing that resilience practices evolve before, during and after crises through continuous learning, adaptation and strategic reconfiguration. Together, these processes produce distinct yet convergent resilience trajectories over time. Originality/value This study advances resilience theory by proposing an integrated analytical fra…

title: Trans-sinus fracture as the gatekeeper: a two-step clinical strategy to guide venous imaging in mild-to-moderate traumatic brain injury
abstract: Background Traumatic cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (tCVST) is an underrecognized complication of traumatic brain injury (TBI). Despite its potential for serious neurological sequelae, no consensus exists regarding indications for CT venography (CTV) or MR venography (MRV) in patients with mild-to-moderate TBI. Trans-sinus fracture has been identified as a risk factor for tCVST, yet its predictive value alone remains insufficient to guide clinical decision-making. Objective To propose a two-step clinical decision strategy for guiding venous imaging selection in mild-to-moderate TBI, using trans-sinus fracture as a gatekeeper followed by D-dimer and headache visual analog scale (VAS) score stratification. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included 528 patients with mild-to-moderate TBI (Glasgow Coma Scale score > 8) who underwent CTV, MRV, or digital subtraction angiography between January 2024 and January 2026. Firth penalized logistic regression was employed to identify tCVST predictors. A two-step strategy was derived: Step 1 screened for trans-sinus fracture; Step 2 applied D-dimer threshold ≥ 3.95 mg/L or headache VAS score ≥ 3 in trans-sinus fracture-positive patients. Results Traumatic cerebral venous sinus thrombosis was diagnosed in 41 patients (7.8%). Trans-sinus fracture was independently associated with tCVST (odds ratio 8.44, 95% confidence …

title: Linking digital transformation strategy, digital circular supply chains and sustainable supply chain performance: the moderating role of environmental dynamism
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how digital transformation strategy (DTS) influences sustainable supply chain performance (SSCP) through digital circular supply chains (DCSC) in manufacturing SMEs in an emerging market economy such as Vietnam. It also investigates whether environmental dynamism (ED) moderates the relationships between DTS and DCSC, and between DCSC and SSCP. Design/methodology/approach Primary data were captured using a tailored questionnaire, a quantitative methodology was employed. The model incorporated moderated mediation and tested using survey data from 468 managers/directors in Vietnam’s manufacturing SME. It employs partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) technique to evaluate the proposed hypotheses. Findings The results show that DTS positively affects SSCP both directly and indirectly. DCSC has a significant positive impact on SSCP and partially mediates the relationship between DTS and SSCP. Furthermore, ED moderated the relationships between DTS and DCSC as well as between DCSC and SSCP. Originality/value This study yields novel insights into how DTS drives SSCP through DCSC in manufacturing SMEs operating in emerging economies. It extends the literature by identifying ED as a critical boundary condition shaping the effectiveness of digital transformation. The findings yield valuable implications for managers seeking to leverag…

Strategy Sets the Scene: Genetic architecture of linalool resistance in Botrytis cinerea
abstract: Abstract Botrytis cinerea is a necrotrophic fungal pathogen that infects thousands of plant species. During infection, these diverse plant hosts produce different specialized metabolites that can inhibit pathogen growth and shape pathogen fitness. However, the genetic architecture of pathogen resistance toward individual host defense metabolites remains poorly understood. To address this question, we exposed 83 B. cinerea isolates to the metabolite linalool and quantified physiological and structural responses. Exposure revealed extensive phenotypic diversity across isolates. Population structure analysis using genome-wide SNP data showed little genetic subdivision despite diverse hosts and geographic location. Genome-wide association identified 98 genes of interest associated with membrane transport and stress response regulation. Genetic associations were stronger for morphological traits than for physiological traits, suggesting that hyphal architecture may have a complex genetic architecture contributing to linalool resistance. Together, these results establish natural variation in linalool response and provide candidate loci for understanding how generalist pathogens respond to host-derived chemical defenses.

title: The loudest voice in a room: a program for ecosystem strategy and coordination through rationality
abstract: Purpose This article considers how organizations can become central coordinating stakeholders in innovation ecosystems without relying on direct control over key resources, technologies or partners. Drawing on Niklas Luhmann's systems theory, attention is shifted from ecosystem-level control mechanisms to a decision program of expectation management internal to organizations that allows them to cultivate rationality and legitimacy in becoming central to an ecosystem while preserving other stakeholders' autonomy. Design/methodology/approach Secondary analysis is applied to an established qualitative case study of Carlsberg's development of the Green Fiber Bottle using Luhmannian systems theory, causally relating expectations, complexity, rationality, legitimacy and coordination, and developing a causal loop diagram. This causal loop diagram is applied to the case and illustrates how Luhmann's concepts can be traced through concrete organizational decisions and interactions. Findings The analysis suggests that a decision program for expectation management can serve as the internal engine that increases rationality for organizations. When combined, rationality and legitimacy reinforce one another and enable organizations to coordinate with autonomous stakeholders, while establishing them as reference points within an innovation ecosystem, allowing them to attain keystone-member ce…

title: EFEKTIVITAS PENGGUNAAN GAME BASED LEARNING BERBANTU GOOGLE SLIDE TERHADAP PEMAHAMAN KONSEP MATERI HIMPUNAN
abstract: Masih kurangnya pemahaman siswa terhadap konsep-konsep matematika, terutama dalam materi himpunan menuntut adanya inovasi dalam pembelajaran. Tujuan dari penelitian ini adalah untuk mengetahui efektivitas penggunaan metode Game Based Learning (GBL) berbantu Google Slide terhadap peningkatan pemahaman konsep siswa. Penelitian ini menerapkan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain pre-experimental jenis one group pretest-posttest. Subjek penelitian merupakan siswa kelas VII.6 SMP Negeri 1 Tarumajaya yang berjumlah 34 orang, yang dipilih melalui Teknik cluster random sampling. Instrumen yang digunakan berupa tes pemahaman konsep yang telah diuji validitas dan reliabilitasnya. Data analisis melalui uji prasyarat dan uji hipotesis dengan bantuan Microsoft Excel.Temuan penelitian menunjukan adanya peningkatan skor rata-rata dari pretest sebesar 37,65 menjadi 75,09 pada posttest. Uji normalitas Shapiro-Wilk menunjukan bahwa data berdistribusi normal. Selanjutnya, uji paired sample t-test menghasilkan nilai t-hitung sebesar 15,13 yang lebih besar dari t-tabel (2,03) dengan p-value < 0,005, yang mengindikasikan adanya perbedaan signifikan antara hasil pretest dan posttest. Selain itu, nilai rata-rata N-Gain sebesar 0,60 tergolong dalam kategori sedang. title: ANALISIS PERAN GURU DALAM MENANAMKAN SIKAP EMPATI KEPADA PESERTA DIDIK MELALUI PEMBELAJARAN PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA DI KELAS V SD
abstract: ABSTRACT Cultivating empathy in elementary schools requires learning practices that not only convey moral values but also provide opportunities for students to apply them in their daily interactions. This study aims to describe teachers’ efforts, school support, and the challenges encountered in cultivating empathy through Pancasila Education in Grade V at UPTD SD Negeri 077272 Lolofaoso Tabaloho. The study employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive method. The informants consisted of the school principal, the Grade V teacher, and three students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, then analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. Data trustworthiness was examined using source and technique triangulation. The findings identified five teacher strategies: role modeling, positive behavioral habituation, collaborative learning, advice and reinforcement, and the creation of a supportive learning environment. These practices were reinforced by school culture and cooperation with parents. Students demonstrated empathetic behaviors through caring, mutual respect, willingness to help, and cooperation, although differences in individual characteristics, environmental influences, and limited instructional time remained challenges. The study concludes that empathy cultivation is implem…

title: Machine learning detection of small Strombolian eruptions in noisy multi-temporal infrared images: Toward continuous monitoring
abstract: Abstract We show that a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on denoised multi-temporal infrared images (single images whose red, green, and blue channels hold three consecutive frames so that change between them appears as color) can detect small Strombolian eruptions that previously fell below the detection limits of conventional automated methods. Strombolian eruptions at Mount Erebus, Antarctica, range from large eruptions that eject lava throughout the crater to small eruptions that are mostly contained within the lake. We built these images from thermal imagery of the Ray lava lake and trained a CNN to classify them into three categories: “no eruption”, “small eruption”, and “large eruption”. A training and verification dataset of more than 54,000 images was built through a three-stage process, Clean → Expanded → Denoised, starting from a curated set of eruptions. We applied confident learning (Cleanlab) with five iterations of five-fold Stratified Group K-Fold cross-validation. On the held-out test set, the denoised model achieved a macro F1 of 0.9782, Matthews Correlation Coefficient = 0.9397, and macro AUC = 0.9981. To test temporal generalization, we applied the model to all December 2015 images, recorded over 10 months after the latest training images, during which the lake’s morphology changed. The network detected 49 large and 420 small eruptions. Manual veri…

title: MORAL AWARENESS-BASED PSYCHOSOCIAL RESILIENCE AMONG STUDENTS WITH SPECIAL NEEDS FOLLOWING FLOODS: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR LOCAL WISDOM-BASED TRAUMA-INFORMED LEARNING
abstract: This article aims to develop a conceptual framework for local wisdom–based trauma-informed learning to support psychosocial resilience recovery and strengthen moral awareness among students with special needs following floods. The study adopts a conceptual approach through a narrative literature review of trauma-informed education, play as a medium for psychosocial recovery, post-disaster recovery experiences in Indonesia, traditional games in inclusive education, and children's moral development. The analysis identifies key ideas, compares findings and limitations of previous studies, and synthesizes them contextually into a learning design responsive to students' needs. The findings comprise five core conceptual propositions, a mapping of six trauma-informed principles into activity design guidelines, and a five-phase session sequence integrating traditional games, a sense of safety, moral reflection, and academic support. The framework also incorporates ethical considerations, activity adaptations for diverse student needs, and an evaluation design addressing psychosocial indicators, participation, and moral awareness. However, available empirical evidence remains limited, particularly concerning students with special needs after floods. As no field data were collected, the proposed framework cannot yet be considered effective and requires further empirical validation.

title: A hybrid framework for Turner Syndrome facial detection: integrating deep feature learning and geometric prior knowledge under data scarcity
abstract: Abstract Turner Syndrome (TS) is a chromosomal disorder characterized by growth retardation and congenital ovarian dysgenesis. Given the considerable morbidity and mortality, early diagnosis and timely intervention are crucial to improving outcomes. However, the gold standard diagnostic method, karyotype analysis, is time-consuming and requires specialized laboratory expertise. Since TS patients often present distinct facial features, AI-based facial recognition could help identify patients with characteristic appearance as a screening tool. Inspired by the value-of-information principle, we propose a hybrid framework integrating deep feature learning and geometric prior knowledge under data scarcity. We retrospectively constructed this AI facial recognition model for TS detection and validated it in a prospective cohort. The proposed framework achieved 95.41% accuracy, 96.55% sensitivity, and 95.24% specificity, substantially simplifying the diagnostic process. When training was performed only on the hard subset obtained after difficulty-based stratification into three equal groups, the sensitivity reached 100.00%, indicating that all patients were correctly identified. Grad-CAM visualization of key facial regions improved model interpretability and aligned predictions with clinical insights. Our method offers a low-cost and easily accessible approach to TS screening. By allow…

title: PENERAPAN PROBLEM BASED LEARNING BERBANTUAN GEOGEBRA UNTUK MENINGKATKAN MOTIVASI BELAJAR DILATASI PESERTA DIDIK SMA
abstract: Tujuan dari riset ini ialah untuk meningkatkan motivasi belajar peserta didik dengan menerapkan pendekatan problem based learning (PBL) berbantuan GeoGebra pada bahan ajar Dilatasi di kelas XI C SMA Negeri 4 Palu. Mekanisme pembelajaran amat penting, terutama dalam matematika, yang sering dianggap rumit dan abstrak. pendekatan PBL dipilih karena menunjang peserta didik untuk aktif mencari solusi masalah kontekstual. Selain itu, GeoGebra merupakan alat bantu visual yang membantu peserta didik memahami konsep transformasi geometri, khususnya dilatasi. Penelitian tindakan kelas (PTK) digunakan dalam riset ini, yang dikerjakan dalam dua siklus. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan observasi, dokumentasi kegiatan pembelajaran, dan angket motivasi belajar. Analisis data menggunakan deskriptif kualitatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penerapan pendekatan PBL berbantuan GeoGebra menumbuhkan motivasi peserta didik untuk belajar matematika. Peserta didik menjadi lebih antusias, lebih aktif dalam diskusi, dan lebih mampu mengaitkan konsep matematika dengan situasi dunia nyata. Oleh karena itu, penerapan pendekatan PBL dengan bantuan GeoGebra bisa menjadi alternatif strategi pembelajaran yang efektif untuk menumbuhkan motivasi belajar matematika peserta didik.

title: The impact of gamification on language learning: a Quasi-experimental study in higher education
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the role of gamification, conceptualized as a reflective lesson improvement cycle in the areas of engagement, motivation and language proficiency at the higher education level. Design/methodology/approach A quasi-experimental design spanning 14 weeks was conducted with 300 undergraduate university students as part of a collaborative lesson study process consisting of a cyclical process of: plan, teach, reflect. Statistical analysis was conducted with the use of ANOVA, Cohen’s d and Kruskal–Wallis tests. Findings The findings showed significant improvement in all language skill areas, with a large effect size (d = 1.37) suggesting gamification made a considerable contribution to engagement and learning outcomes for the students. Research limitations/implications This study was conducted at one university, and involved a 14-week intervention. These factors may limit the generalization of findings. Although we employed appropriate statistical analyses (ANOVA, Cohen’s d, Kruskal–Wallis), more extensive longitudinal studies are necessary to confirm the meaning of sustained findings. Qualitative understanding related to teachers’ reflections could add depth to contextual understandings. abstract: Modern wide-field astronomical surveys are substantially increasing the volume of observational data and the discovery rate of near-Earth asteroids (NEAs), placing growing demands on efficient and automated initial orbit determination (IOD). The physics-informed extreme-learning machine (PIELM) is an artificial intelligence (AI)-based algorithm for IOD that reconstructs orbital trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. However, optical survey observations often span arcs that are too short to provide sufficient geometric constraints, making it difficult for the standard PIELM to determine a reliable initial orbit. New IOD methods capable of handling too-short arcs (TSAs) are therefore increasingly needed. We develop a new AI-based method for determining the initial orbits of NEAs from TSAs. It yields reliable initial estimates for subsequent least-squares refinement. We propose a metaheuristic PIELM method, termed MH-PIELM. An artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm explores candidate solutions defined by a single line-of-sight range, with PIELM embedded directly within the search to reconstruct the corresponding trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. The resulting PIELM loss serves as the fitness function, guiding the ABC algorithm toward promising candidate solutions. The method was tested on the initial optical observations reported for s…

title: Data representation matters: Optimising machine learning for X-ray source classification by leveraging spatio-spectral information
abstract: Distinguishing between faint extended X-ray sources, such as galaxy clusters, and point-like sources, primarily active galactic nuclei (AGNs), is a fundamental yet challenging task in X-ray surveys, which are crucial to cosmological studies and astrophysical source population analyses. This paper presents a benchmark comparison of convolutional neural network models for classifying simulated observations of AGNs and galaxy clusters, focussing on the impact of data representation and interpretability of those data. XMM-Newton We systematically evaluated 1D, 2D, 2D+1D, and 3D CNNs trained on distinct data representations derived from simulated observations of AGNs and clusters: 1D (spectral), 2D (imaging), and 3D (event cube) data. Our experimental design leverages the physical constraints of the apparent size–redshift relation to ensure realistic source populations at fixed flux limits. We further applied 3D-GradCAM to interpret the learned features and assess the physical basis for the model's decision making to move beyond black-box classification. XMM-Newton Our results demonstrate that increased spectral resolution enhances classifier performance using 1D data and 2D spatial information provides a strong morphological baseline, the integration of both domains yields significant diagnostic gains. We find that a 3D CNN architecture applied directly to spatio-spectral event cub…

abstract: This article examines the relationship between the modern psychological concept of metacognition and the teachings found in the Satipatthana Sutta within the Buddhist tradition. Metacognition refers to awareness and regulation of one’s own thinking processes, including the ability to observe, evaluate, and guide cognitive activities. The study explores how similar ideas appear in early Buddhist teachings, particularly through the practice of mindfulness described in the Satipatthana Sutta. Using a qualitative and interpretive approach, the discussion analyses primary Buddhist texts together with relevant secondary sources. The analysis shows that the mindfulness practices explained in the Satipatthana framework encourage continuous awareness of mental states, actions, and experiences, which closely parallels the functions of metacognitive awareness described in educational psychology. The article argues that these Buddhist insights can contribute meaningfully to contemporary discussions of learning, self-regulation, and reflective thinking. By comparing these two perspectives, the study highlights the relevance of classical Buddhist teachings for understanding and developing metacognitive skills in modern educational contexts.

title: LIGHTS: Limitations of far-infrared tracers for Galactic cirrus mitigation in the era of ultra-deep imaging
abstract: Current and forthcoming deep optical imaging surveys reach surface brightness levels fainter than 30 mag/arcsec2$, where Galactic cirrus emission becomes a significant contaminant. This poses a major challenge for the study of extremely low-surface-brightness extragalactic structures. We investigated the relationship between far-infrared emission, as traced by the Herschel 250 μm band, and optical surface brightness in the Sloan and bands. We find that, for Galactic cirrus with μ_g≳ 27 mag/arcsec^2, a linear relation is consistent with the data, assuming optically thin dust, with optical cirrus emission amounting to ∼0.1% of the far-infrared flux. Using Herschel far-infrared data to trace Galactic cirrus enables its identification over wide areas but at the cost of significantly reducing spatial resolution. This limitation introduces source confusion and restricts the effective surface brightness depth that can be robustly probed in optical data. We show that, when cirrus emission is modeled using Herschel 250 μm data, the limiting surface brightness is μ_V∼ 28 mag/arcsec^2. This is substantially shallower than the nominal depth of surveys such as LIGHTS or the 10-year co-added LSST (μ_V∼ 30.5 mag/arcsec$^2). These results highlight a fundamental limitation in the use of currently available far-infrared data for cirrus mitigation in ultra-deep optical imaging and emphasize the …

title: Jet-streak forcing and deep moisture transport during the 7 March 2025 record rainfall in Bahía Blanca, Argentina
abstract: Bahía Blanca (38.7°S, 62.2°W) experienced an unprecedented rainfall event on 7 March 2025, officially documented by the Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN) as a historical record with an estimated return period exceeding 100 years. This study provides an observationally based diagnosis of the event, testing the hypothesis that record precipitation resulted from the coupling between upper-level jet-streak-associated divergence, deep ascent and exceptional moisture transport. We combine integrated multi-satellite retrievals for global precipitation measurement (IMERG) satellite precipitation with ERA5 (fifth generation ECMWF (European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts) atmospheric reanalysis) reanalysis fields and adopt event-consistent daily metrics (24-h windows) to characterise the dynamical and thermodynamical environment. IMERG reveals a spatially organised precipitation footprint co-located with a persistent corridor of enhanced integrated vapour transport (IVT) toward south-eastern Buenos Aires Province. Over the upstream region of Bahía Blanca, upper-level diagnostics show an anomalous jet-streak configuration at 200 hPa (along-flow acceleration percentile 99.3%) concurrent with extremely rare divergence at 200 hPa (percentile 99.8%) and exceptionally strong deep ascent (minimum ω daily metric, percentile 99.9%). Vertical diagnostics indicate that moisture trans…

title: Is it time for anti-CD20 discontinuation in multiple sclerosis? Cumulative risk or cumulative uncertainty
abstract: The widespread adoption of anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies (anti-CD20 mAbs) in multiple sclerosis (MS) has prompted increasing interest in treatment discontinuation and de-escalation strategies. In this perspective, we critically examine current data on outcomes following anti-CD20 discontinuation, including evidence from registries, prospective cohorts, and real-world studies. Available findings suggest that disease control achieved under anti-CD20 therapy is pharmacologically maintained rather than biologically resolved, and that B-cell repopulation following treatment cessation is heterogeneous and not reliably predictive of clinical stability. Reports of disease reactivation after discontinuation and the absence of validated biomarkers to identify patients who may safely stop therapy highlight substantial uncertainty. Current evidence therefore remains insufficient to support routine anti-CD20 discontinuation in MS, while a cautious, individualized approach—potentially incorporating dose-spacing strategies—may better reflect the current state of knowledge.

title: Development and Optimization of an Aqueous Method for Carotenoid Extraction from Sticks of Ilex paraguariensis
abstract: Abstract Ilex paraguariensis sticks are agroindustrial by-products rich in bioactive compounds, especially carotenoids such as lutein. In this study, an aqueous method was developed and optimized for the extraction of total carotenoids and lutein, using water and a food-grade surfactant as the extraction solution. Extraction conditions were optimized using a full 2 3 central composite design. The optimized parameters (0.5% polysorbate in the extracting solution and 5 min of agitation in a water bath at 58 °C) resulted in the extraction of 2.91 mg of lutein per 100 g of sticks, together with high antioxidant activity. Compared with a conventional exhaustive extraction method described in the literature, based on the use of acetone and petroleum ether, the proposed aqueous process yielded a 1.32-fold higher total carotenoids content under the reported experimental conditions. This result indicates a higher carotenoids recovery relative to the conventional method, although differences in extraction procedures and potential matrix effects should be considered when comparing the results. In addition, chlorogenic acids were efficiently extracted under the optimized conditions. abstract: Introduction Sugarcane bagasse is an abundant agro-industrial residue with significant potential for sustainable bioethanol production; however, its minimally processed aqueous extract has limited nutritional suitability for efficient microbial fermentation. This study demonstrate a simple, low-severity approach for producing bioethanol from aqueous sugarcane bagasse extract without chemical or enzymatic pretreatment, while identifying nutrient supplementation strategies to improve fermentation performance using Saccharomyces cerevisiae MTCC 180. Methods An aqueous extract of sugarcane bagasse was prepared using a mild extraction process without chemical or enzymatic pretreatment and characterized by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. Carbon, nitrogen, and mineral supplements were initially screened and optimized using a one-variable-at-a-time approach. The most influential nutrients were subsequently optimized through response surface methodology employing a central composite design. Ethanol production was quantified under previously optimized fermentation conditions. Results The aqueous bagasse extract contained fermentable carbohydrate-associated functional groups but supported only limited ethanol production in its untreated form.
