Machine learning–driven structural optimization of zigzag silk fibroin ionic conductors for spatially resolved wearable motion detection
abstract: Abstract Flexible ionic conductors that maintain stable electrical performance under large deformation are critical for wearable sensing. However, their geometric design space couples topology, manufacturability, and deformability in a high–dimensional parameter space that trial–and–error approaches cannot navigate efficiently. Here, we present a data–driven structural design workflow for zigzag–patterned silk fibroin ionic conductors. Zigzag unit cells parameterized by four control points yield 3000 mirror–tiled variants whose biaxial unfoldability, quantified as the mean stretch ratio $${\lambda }_{{mean}}$$ λ m e a n , is labeled by quasi–static simulations. An XGBoost surrogate trained on 15 structural descriptors predicts $${\lambda }_{{mean}}$$ λ m e a n with $${R}^{2}$$ R 2 = 0.97. A continuous–action A2C reinforcement learning agent then uses the surrogate to search for high–unfoldability configurations under manufacturability constraints. Three optimized configurations at $${\lambda }_{{pred}}$$ λ p r e d = 1.27, 1.77, and 2.04 are fabricated as direct–write–printed silk fibroin ionic conductors with ten–channel resistance readout. title: Digital Twins in Irrigation Optimization: Advantages, Opportunities, and Challenges
abstract: Efficient irrigation management is important to increase agriculture water use efficiency and achieve sustainable crop production under increasing water scarcity and climatic variability. Based on advanced devices and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, the irrigation system can be digitalized and transformed from experience-driven decision-making toward data-driven, predictive, and adaptive control. Digital Twins (DTs) enable smart irrigation management through continuous bi-directional data flows, dynamic model updating, intelligent prediction, and closed-loop execution. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the applications of DTs in irrigation management and optimization, covering Internet of Things (IoT), Remote Sensing (RS), and advanced simulation-inspired irrigation systems. Furthermore, we discuss the opportunities and challenges in DTs for irrigation optimization with the development of new techniques, and identify the major technological trends, existing bottlenecks, and future research directions for DT-enabled irrigation.

Strengthening the diagnosis of death due to lightning: an integrated forensic approach – a literature review
abstract: Abstract The diagnosis of “death by lightning strike” is typically confirmed through an external postmortem examination. The principle pathological findings are typically located on the external aspects of the body and clothing, while internal examination typically reveals few, if any, specific or diagnostic pathological changes. Following a fatal lightning strike, the victim may have only subtle or no typical findings on the body’s surface. Misdiagnoses have occurred repeatedly in the past. Therefore, this literature review investigated whether autopsies of lightning strike victims can lead to or support the correct diagnosis. From a total of 120 case reports on lightning strike accidents with autopsy findings, 34 cases exhibited characteristic injuries that the authors attributed to the lightning strike. The head, heart, lungs, and skeletal system were the most commonly affected areas. Since there is currently no pathognomonic finding for internal injuries after a lightning strike incident, the authors propose at least one additional piece of evidence in addition to a characteristic finding to establish the correct diagnosis. The diagnostic certainty of a lightning-related death may be increased by corroborative evidence, which may include reliable witness accounts, additional trace evidence indicative of a lightning strike at the location where the body was found, or confirm…

title: An eight-gene prognostic signature and its immune associations in gastric cancer: integrated transcriptomic and clinical analyses
abstract: Background Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) is a major etiological factor in gastric carcinogenesis and has been associated with alterations in the tumor immune microenvironment. However, how H. pylori -related transcriptional features intersect with the broader molecular and immune heterogeneity of established gastric cancer remains incompletely characterized. Methods Single-cell RNA-sequencing data (GSE234129) were used for exploratory comparison according to H. pylori status and to define an initial candidate gene set. An eight-gene prognostic signature was subsequently developed in TCGA-STAD and evaluated in independent gastric cancer cohorts. Model-development optimism was assessed using 1, 000 full-pipeline bootstrap resamples. Immune features were evaluated using CIBERSORT, ESTIMATE, TIDE, and immunophenoscore, while observed anti-PD-1 response was explored in the disease-matched PRJEB25780 cohort. RGS1 was further assessed in an independent immunohistochemical cohort. Results Exploratory single-cell analyses suggested differences in immune-cell composition, T-cell states, and antigen-presentation-related pathways according to H. pylori status. The eight-gene prognostic signature stratified overall survival in the TCGA-STAD cohort and two independent GEO cohorts. After full-pipeline bootstr…

title: An integrated GIS and remote-sensing framework for district-level dengue risk assessment in northern India: development of a spatial Dengue Risk Index and assessment of its spatial concordance with reported incidence
abstract: Abstract Background Dengue is an increasingly important vector-borne disease driven by climate variability, urbanization, environmental change, and population growth. Despite its rising burden in northern India, district-level spatial epidemiological frameworks integrating environmental suitability, transmission hazard, and population vulnerability remain limited. This study developed an integrated geographic information system (GIS)- and remote-sensing (RS)-based Dengue Risk Index (DRI) describing long-term spatial susceptibility to dengue in Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh, and assessed its spatial concordance with reported dengue incidence. Relative humidity and the Normalized Difference Moisture Index were excluded after redundancy screening. Rainfall was derived from India Meteorological Department (IMD) 0.25° daily gridded data for 2025, elevation from the Copernicus 30 m DEM, and population density from WorldPop 2025 constrained estimates. abstract: Introduction Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), defined as colorectal cancer diagnosed before 50 years of age, represents an emerging global health challenge with rapidly increasing incidence. Although EOCRC exhibits distinct clinical and molecular characteristics, the cellular ecosystem and mechanisms underlying its aggressive behavior remain incompletely understood. Methods Here, we integrated seven independent single-cell RNA sequencing cohorts comprising 473,939 high-quality cells from 174 colorectal cancer (CRC) patients (39 EOCRC and 135 average-onset CRC [AOCRC]) to construct a comprehensive cellular landscape across age groups. After Harmony-based integration, nine major cellular lineages were identified, and malignant epithelial cells were characterized using chromosome-level copy number variation inference. We systematically compared malignant and stromal compartments, followed by malignant-state characterization, trajectory analysis, and cell -cell communication modeling using Slingshot, CellChat, and NicheNet. Results EOCRC displayed extensive remodeling of the tumor ecosystem rather than isolated epithelial alterations. Professional development, lifestyle behaviors, and job satisfaction: the mediating role of work-life balance in a multi-sector sample
abstract: Background Modern organizations face increasing pressure to enhance employee satisfaction and productivity. Although prior research has examined individual antecedents of job satisfaction, less is known about whether professional-development, behavioral, and lifestyle-related resources are associated with job satisfaction through work–life balance. Objective This study examines the associations of social media engagement (SME; hereafter used to denote social media engagement), employee training (ET), healthy dietary habits (HDH), online learning participation (OLP), and physical activity (PA) with job satisfaction (JS), with work–life balance (WLB) evaluated as a model-based indirect pathway. Methods A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was administered to 437 working professionals across multiple industries. Structural equation modeling (SEM) and bootstrapped indirect-effect analysis were used to assess the measurement model, structural relationships, and indirect associations. Results The measurement model demonstrated strong reliability and validity. All five antecedent variables were significantly and positively associated with WLB, with OLP showing the strongest path coefficient (β = 0.379). Multi-omics profiling identifies a putative Akkermansia–HK3–lactate immunometabolic link associated with JPZS treatment in lupus nephritis
abstract: Background Lupus nephritis (LN) is associated with aberrant glycolytic reprogramming in renal immune cells, yet its relationship with gut microbial alterations remains poorly defined. Hexokinase 3 (HK3) has emerged as a candidate metabolic node in myeloid activation, while the relationship between gut Akkermansia abundance and renal HK3-associated metabolic changes in LN remains unclear. We used Qihuang Jianpi Zishen decoction (JPZS), an herbal formula used as an adjunct in clinical practice, as an experimental probe to investigate this putative gut–immunometabolic connection through integrated multi-omics. Renal function, autoantibodies, histopathology, and glomerular IgG deposition were assessed across treatment groups. title: Comparative analysis of β-glucan content in single and multi-species medicinal mushroom powders with potential nutraceutical applications
abstract: Medicinal mushrooms are widely recognized for their bioactive compounds, particularly β-glucans, which are associated with immunomodulatory, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities. In recent years, blends of medicinal mushroom powders have attracted increasing attention due to their potential synergistic effects resulting from the combination of multiple fungal species and their diverse metabolite profiles. The present study evaluated the total glucan, α-glucan, and β-glucan content of four medicinal mushroom powders ( Ganoderma lucidum , Inonotus obliquus , Hericium erinaceus , and Pleurotus eryngii ) as well as four multi-species mixtures formulated from these fungi. Glucan quantification was performed using the validated enzymatic β-Glucan Assay, based on complete hydrolysis and enzymatic determination of released glucose. The results demonstrated a clear predominance of β-glucans over α-glucans in all samples analyzed. Pleurotus eryngii exhibited the highest β-glucan concentration among single-species powders (47.63% dry weight), while Inonotus obliquus showed the lowest value (8.99% dry weight). Multi-species blends displayed elevated β-glucan concentrations ranging from 42.73% to 47.42%, confirming the contribution of high-glucan species within the formulations. The low proportion of α-glucans in all samples suggests minimal contamination with reserve p…

title: Robust multi-weather UAV small object detection framework with complex entropy-aware and wavelet convolution
abstract: Abstract In adverse weather conditions such as fog, haze, rain, and snow, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) small object detection faces decreased accuracy due to reduced image quality and blurred object features, which seriously affects the reliability of low-altitude detection tasks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a robust multi-weather UAV small object detection framework based on unsupervised domain adaptation with a teacher-student self-training paradigm. The proposed framework introduces complex entropy-aware attention and wavelet convolution to enhance target representation under severe weather degradation. Aiming at the domain distribution differences in multi-weather scenarios, the framework alleviates such differences through more robust category-level prototype matching and global statistical characteristic learning based on DATR (domain adaptive detection transformer model). First, to alleviate feature uncertainty introduced by adverse weather noise, we design a complex entropy-aware attention mechanism that estimates channel-wise Shannon entropy and assigns adaptive weights according to feature information concentration. Instead of simply emphasizing uncertain responses, the proposed mechanism suppresses high-entropy ambiguous features while preserving low-entropy discriminative representations that remain more reliable under weather-induced degradation…

title: Tourism, inequality and health: rethinking sustainability
abstract: Purpose The goal is to analyze how tourism is associated with changes in population health, measured through the regional burden of disease. Although tourism is a strategic driver of economic growth, its implications for public health remain poorly investigated. The objective is to study whether and under what conditions tourist flows generate health benefits or risks. Design/methodology/approach Health is measured using Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) provided by the Global Burden of Disease project. Using panel data for 20 Italian regions from 2008 to 2021, we analyze tourism intensity, average length of stay and spatial concentration of arrivals. The application of a hybrid within-between model allows us to distinguish between short-term and long-term structural differences. Findings The results show a dual impact. In the short term, longer stays and concentrated arrivals are associated with an increase in DALYs, signaling pressure on health services and the local environment, while a greater number of arrivals is associated with a reduction in DALYs. In the long term, regions with structurally high tourism intensity tend to be associated with worse health outcomes; however, higher per capita income seems to mitigate these negative effects. Policies should focus on redistributing flows, reducing concentration and strengthening the resilience of local health systems. R…

title: Anesthetic Management of a Patient with Class III Obesity Undergoing Bariatric Surger per Laparoscopic
abstract:
Background : Class III obesity presents significant perioperative challenges due to altered respiratory physiology, increased risk of difficult airway, aspiration, and postoperative respiratory complications. Laparoscopic surgery further increases these challenges through pneumoperitoneum, which can impair respiratory mechanics and increase carbon dioxide load. Optimal airway management, positioning, ventilation, and postoperative respiratory support are therefore essential.

Case Illustration : A 31-year-old man with class III obesity (BMI 51.6 kg/m²) underwent laparoscopic esophagectomy and gastrectomy under general anesthesia. The patient was positioned in the ramp position and preoxygenated with 100% oxygen for 5 minutes. Anesthesia was induced with propofol 200 mg and fentanyl 200 μg. Following confirmation of adequate mask ventilation, atracurium 50 mg was administered. Tracheal intubation was successfully performed after induction according to the 2022 American Society of Anesthesiologists Difficult Airway Algorithm. Controlled mechanical ventilation was maintained at 12 breaths/min with PEEP of 6 cmH₂O and a minute ventilation of 6.4 L/min. Anesthesia was maintained with sevoflurane 2–3 vol% in an oxygen–air mixture with FiO₂ 50%. Postoperatively, the patient remained mechanically ventilated with stable hemodynamics and was tran…

title: Exploring the influence of track and field athletes' self-management on athletic performance: the chain mediating role of psychological resilience and competitive spirit
abstract: Objective Against the backdrop of increasingly intense competition in competitive sports, the mechanisms underlying the improvement of athletes' athletic performance have become an important research topic. Based on self-regulation theory and relevant perspectives in sport psychology, this study explores the relationship between self-management and athletic performance among track and field athletes, and examines the single mediating and chain mediating effects of psychological resilience and competitive spirit. Methods This study employed a cross-sectional quantitative survey design and used non-probability convenience sampling to recruit 772 Chinese track and field athletes. Established scales were used to assess self-management, psychological resilience, competitive spirit, and athletic performance. SPSS 31.0 and AMOS 31.0 were used for descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, common method bias testing, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling. Direct, individual indirect, and serial indirect effects were examined using 5,000 bootstrap samples. Results Self-management was positively associated with athletic performance. Psychological resilience and competitive spirit each significantly mediated the relationship between self-management and athletic performance. In addition, psychological resilience and competitive spirit formed a significant serial…

title: Complex Airway Management in Pierre Robin Sequence with Failed Intubation: Case Report and Lesson Learned
abstract:
Background : Pierre Robin Sequence (PRS) is a rare condition with a global prevalence of 1 in 8,500-14,000 live births, characterized by micrognatia, glossoptosis, and upper airway obstruction. Reporting this case is essential to enriching the literature on PRS management, especially in Indonesia, where case data is still limited.

Case Illustration : A 1 year ten months old child with PRS, palatoschizis, laryngomalacia, secondary hypothyroidism, and mandibular hypoplasia. The patient will undergo mandibular osteodistraction to address airway obstruction and improve facial structure. Since birth, the patient has shown feeding difficulties and airway obstruction. At five months of age, an echocardiography examination revealed a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). The patient was fasted for 6 hours before surgery, intravenous access was established, and premedication with midazolam 0.05mg/kgBB. Preoxygenation, induction with ketamine 1mg/kgBB, intubation with spiral ETT No. 3.5 and atracurium 0,5mg/kgBB were given, and maintenance anaesthesia using sevoflurane. Close monitoring was done to ensure the patient's stability. Postoperatively, the patient was transferred to the intensive care unit with intravenous paracetamol analgesic and close monitoring to prevent complications.

title: Navigating the digital paradox: AI-enabled collaboration and organizational resilience
abstract: Purpose Drawing on a unified resource-orchestration model, this study examines how artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled inter-firm cooperation influences organizational resilience in manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), through a mediated-moderated pathway involving digital service innovation strategy and leadership cognition. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was employed: exploratory qualitative construct refinement followed by a time-lagged quantitative survey of 269 SME managers in Viet Nam, analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and the Johnson–Neyman technique. Findings AI-enabled inter-firm cooperation is positively associated with organizational resilience, a relationship positively mediated by an AI-driven digital service innovation strategy. Crucially, the executive's digital paradox mindset negatively moderates this link, revealing a novel cognitive substitution effect. Practical implications SME managers should invest in interoperable AI platforms for automated boundary-spanning data sharing. Furthermore, leaders must recognize that internal paradoxical cognition and external AI networks can functionally substitute for one another in building resilience. Originality/value The study extends an established AI-enablement construct by demonstrating a novel integrative mechanism through …

High-resolution transmission spectroscopy of KELT-18b. Metastable helium detection at 1083 nm
abstract: Exoplanets orbiting near their host stars experience intense irradiation, which can drive the expansion and escape of their upper atmospheres. The near-infrared metastable helium triplet at 1083.3 nm has emerged as a powerful diagnostic to probe these mass-loss processes. We present the first high-resolution transmission spectroscopy of the ultrahot Jupiter KELT-18b, probing its escaping atmosphere by analyzing a single transit obtained with the CARMENES spectrograph. Transmission spectroscopy and Doppler tomography were utilized to isolate the planetary signal. To mitigate contamination from the strong telluric OH lines overlapping the region of interest, two distinct data analysis procedures were applied: a standard Molecfit and OH-masking approach, as well as a principal component analysis (PCA)-based method. By combining the two complementary approaches, we successfully detect a He,I triplet absorption feature of 1.10 ± 0.22% (5.1σ). The signal exhibits a velocity shift consistent with zero and is attributed to the exoplanetary atmosphere. An injection test reveals that the PCA-based method significantly suppresses the retrieved signal. Additionally, using the ATES and TPM codes, we modeled the atmospheric photoevaporation and the helium triplet profile for different He/H ratios and stellar extreme ultraviolet (XUV) fluxes, accounting for instrument and planetary rotational…

abstract: Purpose This paper investigates the associations of ex-bureaucrats and ex-politicians serving on bank boards with financial reporting quality using a sample of Turkish banks over the period 2007–2022. Design/methodology/approach We mainly perform ordinary least squares and logistic regressions to test our hypothesis and address the research question. To mitigate selection bias and endogeneity problems, we perform the Heckman two-stage selection model and system GMM procedures. To mitigate the omitted variable bias, we use a fixed effects estimator. Additionally, we constructed an alternative sample by excluding ex-bureaucrats without professional experience in accounting, finance, taxation, or other relevant fields. Finally, we created interaction terms using the ex-bureaucrat and ex-politician variables. Findings The findings indicate that ex-bureaucrat directors are associated with higher financial reporting quality, particularly through lower discretionary loan loss provisions, whereas ex-politician directors exhibit no consistent association with financial reporting quality. Additional analyses provide robust support for the discretionary loan loss provision results. However, the evidence for small-profit reporting is less robust, particularly in the bank fixed-effects estimations. abstract: Purpose: This study aims to analyze the influence of organizational culture and the utilization of the Village Financial System (Sistem Keuangan Desa/SISKEUDES) on the accountability of village fund management in Merawang District, Bangka Regency.Methodology: This research employs a quantitative approach using primary data collected through questionnaires distributed to village financial managers. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), and ordinal data were transformed into interval scale using the Method of Successive Intervals (MSI).Results: The results indicate that organizational culture has a positive and significant effect on village fund management accountability. Beyond Flooded Homes: Household Financial Resilience, Healthcare Access, and Economic Recovery After Disasters—Lessons from the 2025 Hat Yai Flood
abstract: Flood disasters can affect household welfare through simultaneous losses of income and assets, disruption of healthcare, and increased expenditure required for recovery. These pressures are commonly examined in separate literatures on disaster economics, household coping, financial protection, and health-system resilience. This paper brings them together around a household-level problem: competing claims on limited resources after a disaster. We propose a conceptual framework in which disaster-related economic losses and healthcare disruption converge on household financial-buffer capacity. When resources are insufficient, households may continue to obtain healthcare and experience financial hardship, delay or forgo care and experience unmet need, or move between these responses as disruption persists. Continuity-dependent healthcare can amplify this constraint by reducing the flexibility to postpone healthcare use or expenditure. The 2025 Hat Yai flood in Southern Thailand illustrates the upstream conditions represented in the framework. Available evidence documents widespread livelihood and productive-asset losses alongside disruption of essential healthcare services, including dialysis. Household-level evidence is not yet available to determine the extent of catastrophic health expenditure, forgone care, or longer-term welfare loss following the flood. The framework suggests…

title: The Effect of Profitability and Leverage on Financial Distress
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to examine the effect of profitability and leverage on financial distress among manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The study focuses on identifying whether internal financial characteristics represented by profitability and leverage can explain variations in companies' financial distress conditions.Methodology: This research employs a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from annual reports and financial statements of manufacturing companies listed on the IDX. The sample selection was conducted using purposive sampling based on predetermined criteria. Data analysis was performed using multiple linear regression to examine the relationship between profitability, leverage, and financial distress.Results: The findings indicate that profitability and leverage have significant effects on financial distress. Companies with stronger profitability tend to have lower risks of experiencing financial distress due to their ability to generate earnings and maintain financial stability. Meanwhile, higher leverage increases financial pressure because greater dependence on debt may reduce the company's ability to fulfill financial obligations.Conclusions: The study concludes that profitability and leverage are important financial indicators in predicting financial distress among manufacturing companies. Analyzing Nitrogen Fertilizer Markets in the Context of Agricultural Sustainability: Informed Target Market Selection with Multi-Criteria Decision-Making
abstract: Nitrogen fertilization is essential for balancing yield stability and supporting agricultural intensification, particularly in nations where cropland expansion is constrained. The pivotal role of nitrogen fertilizers in sustainable agriculture also renders them a strategically traded commodity. Consequently, trade-oriented analyses of fertilizer markets represent a vital dimension of sustainability research, as they influence input accessibility, production stability, and global food security. This study aims to develop an integrated and structured multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework to identify emerging markets for nitrogen fertilizer exporters, accounting for the multi-dimensional impacts of global change. The analysis focuses on AMIS countries, which constitute the core of global agricultural production and trade. The decision model incorporates a diverse set of agricultural, demographic, and trade-related criteria, including import value, trade balance, agricultural nitrogen use, fertilizer use per unit of cropland, cropland availability, food vulnerability, and urbanization rate. Criterion weights are established using the CRITIC method—accounting for both contrast intensity and inter-criteria correlations—while alternative markets are ranked via the Fuzzy TOPSIS method. abstract: Stock markets play an important role in global economic development. The Nairobi Securities Exchange, like other developing markets, has shown fluctuating performance. The literature reviewed revealed inconsistent findings on macroeconomic factors and stock market returns in Kenya and other emerging markets, highlighting the need for the current study. This study examined the relationship between selected macroeconomic variables and stock returns at the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE). Specifically, the effects of changes in the inflation rate, the short-term 91-day Treasury bill interest rate, and the KES/US dollar exchange rate on stock returns, measured using monthly logarithmic returns of the Nairobi Securities Exchange All Share Index (NASI). The study targeted all monthly observations of the selected variables from January 2016 to December 2025, using the December 2015 NASI value to obtain January 2016 log NASI returns only. The study employed a census approach for comprehensive coverage of the data. title: A Study of Market Survey, Retailer Engagement and Brand Awareness Activities in the Indian Dairy Industry: A Case Study of Govind Milk and Milk Products, Pune
abstract: Retail availability and brand recognition shape the fortunes of regional dairy brands in India, yet few studies document how routine field activities contribute to both. This paper examines the market survey, retailer engagement and brand awareness work carried out for Govind Milk and Milk Products in Pune during an On-the-Job Training (OJT) assignment from 15 May to 15 July 2026. The four objectives were to document product availability and visibility, examine retailer requirements, complaints and lead-generation opportunities, assess consumer responses during society-based activities, and identify practical challenges and improvements. A descriptive and exploratory design was used. Primary data came from field observations, retailer and consumer interactions, Google Forms entries and GPS-tagged photographs, supported by peer-reviewed literature and official sources. A practical field-coverage approach, not probability sampling, was followed. The field team visited 460 outlets (200 grocery shops, 120 medical shops and 140 bakeries), reported 200+ leads and 90 complaints, and interacted with 550+ consumers in two residential societies; a separate analytical base of 220 was used for selected indicators. Ghee, chaas, basundi, curd and buttermilk were commonly observed as available, curd attracted notable consumer interest, and shoppers frequently compared Govind with Amul. Retail…

title: Professional Networks and the Labour Market Assimilation of Immigrants
abstract: Abstract We examine how professional networks shape immigrants’ job search and labour market assimilation. Analysing displaced workers in Sweden, we show that connections to firms through conationals are especially important for immigrants’ job finding. As networks expand to include more natives, the value of such connections rises towards that seen for displaced natives. Origin homophily also predicts whether a connection provides a referral—increasing earnings and lowering turnover—rather than vacancy information. Networks account for 20 per cent of the growth in immigrants’ re-employment over their first decade after arrival; immigrants’ networks are as productive as natives’ after fifteen years.

abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkaji secara kualitatif melalui studi literatur penerapan strategi pembelajaran Market Place Learning (MPL) berbasis kearifan lokal jajanan Sunda dalam menumbuhkan pemahaman peserta didik mengenai kedudukan Pancasila sebagai ideologi terbuka. Sebanyak 10 artikel utama dipilih dan dianalisis secara mendalam berdasarkan relevansi dengan fokus kajian. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa MPL dapat mendukung terciptanya pengalaman belajar yang aktif, dialogis, dan bermakna melalui kegiatan bertukar informasi, berdiskusi, bekerja sama, dan mempresentasikan hasil belajar. Kajian ini juga menemukan adanya celah penelitian karena sebagian besar studi masih membahas MPL atau kearifan lokal secara terpisah. Oleh karena itu, hasil kajian ini menunjukkan adanya peluang untuk mengintegrasikan MPL dengan kearifan lokal jajanan Sunda sebagai alternatif pembelajaran Pendidikan Pancasila yang lebih re…

title: THE MARKET PROSPECTS OF THE GUANGXI ZHUANG EMBROIDERED BALL AND CONSUMERS' PURCHASE INTENTION
abstract: This study examines embroidered balls (xiuqiu), a Guangxi Zhuang craft listed as intangible cultural heritage, and draws on 481 valid responses from an online and offline questionnaire. Using logistic regression and cluster analysis, it answers two questions: which factors shape a consumer's willingness to buy an embroidered ball, and how consumer segments differ in that willingness, which together indicate where the market for this craft is heading. The core buyer is a female undergraduate aged 19 to 23. Women and residents of central and western Guangxi show significantly stronger purchase intentions than other groups. Cluster analysis sorts consumers into three groups: price-sensitive (35%), quality-oriented (45%) and culturally committed (20%). The industry also faces an ageing pool of inheritors and weak demand. The paper proposes strategies along four lines: production, policy, transmission of the craft, and promotion.

title: Distribution Network Reconfiguration in Active Distribution Systems Using a Discrete Adaptive Hybrid Seagull Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Distribution network reconfiguration requires connected radial operation to be maintained while searching a large discrete space, a challenge intensified by distributed generation. This paper proposes the Discrete Adaptive Hybrid Seagull Optimization Algorithm, which reformulates the continuous migration and attack operators of the Seagull Optimization Algorithm on Fundamental Loop decision sets. Rather than chaining migration and attack in every iteration as in the original continuous update, an iteration-dependent stochastic schedule selects exactly one discrete operator for the entire population. A decaying control factor regulates migration intensity, and every candidate is evaluated through steady-state alternating-current power flow using OpenDSS. Across 100 independent runs, the proposed method reaches the 33-bus best-known loss of 139.55 kW in every run and yields a mean loss of 279.91 kW on the 135-bus system. A seven-variant ablation identifies migration as the principal performance driver and shows an additional robustness contribution from attack and stochastic phase selection on the larger network, while not supporting a claim that the fixed attack step is uniquely optimal. On the Molecular Basis of Shrinkage in Hydrophobic Tissue Clearing
abstract: Abstract Tissue clearing enables the optical imaging of intact tissues and facilitates 3D visualization of complex biological systems and cellular structures. However, tissue clearing using benzyl alcohol-benzyl benzoate (BABB) leads to tissue shrinkage, potentially compromising advanced analysis and applications. The molecular and physical origins of this phenomenon have not been completely understood. To study the molecular aspects of tissue shrinkage, we systematically studied the effects of shrinkage across a range of tissues and process steps. After characterizing the water, lipid, and protein content of these tissues, we found that although tissue clearing does remove lipids, the amount of shrinkage correlates instead with the protein content. Comparative magic-angle spinning solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (MAS-ssNMR) spectroscopy on tissue undergoing BABB treatment revealed changes in protein conformational dynamics and protein hydration. Combined with analysis of changes in the dielectric constant during the tissue-clearing process, our results indicate that changes in the electrostatic forces between charged molecules (proteins) are more important than lipid extraction for the shrinkage, contrary to what has been hypothesized for shrinkage in tissue clearing.

abstract: The article provides the market mechanisms for ensuring the competitiveness of the dairy products subsector of Ukraine under conditions of transformation of the economic environment, intensification of competition, resource constraints and changes in domestic and international market conditions. The competitiveness of the dairy products subsector is considered as a complex economic characteristic reflecting the ability of its participants to use resources efficiently, form sustainable competitive advantages and maintain stable market positions. The study substantiates that the formation of competitiveness is determined by a system of interconnected market factors covering milk production, procurement and supply of raw milk, processing, distribution and sale of dairy products. Particular attention is paid to the role of market supply and demand in determining the conditions for the functioning of dairy enterprises. The production volume of raw milk, cattle population, cow productivity and technological development are identified as important factors affecting the stability of the raw material base and the economic efficiency of subsequent stages of the dairy value chain. The influence of raw milk prices on the profitability of agricultural producers and the cost parameters of processing enterprises is substantiated. title: Gas or electricity + thermal storage? operating cost and emission modelling for industrial heat in Alberta
abstract: Abstract Industrial heat generation, which is responsible for over 18% of total global emissions, is largely derived from fossil fuel combustion. As a key driver of many industrial processes, decarbonization of industrial heat is a critical lever for emission reduction. We investigate one pathway to decarbonize industrial heat, using an electrically powered thermal storage unit, and evaluate the cost and associated emissions reductions for the province of Alberta, Canada. Alberta’s historically carbon intensive electricity grid is beginning to experience an abundance of intermittent supply surplus resulting from its growing capacity of wind and solar generation, lack of interties, and significant inflexible cogeneration requirements. This results in low-cost and low-carbon hours that were found to soon be frequent enough to reliably supply industrial heat at lower operating costs and emission intensity than existing natural gas alternatives and continuous electric boilers. However, this is not reflected in scope 1 emission accounting when electricity for industrial heat is sourced directly from behind-the-fence cogeneration—a likely configuration. As such, we recommend policy initiatives be adopted that ensure environmental benefits can be attributed and claimed directly by the industrial plant.

title: The Performance of Passively Managed Index Portfolios Versus Complementary Non-Index Portfolios: Evidence from the H-Share Market
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index against value-weighted and equal-weighted non-index portfolios from October 2001 to December 2017. Using complete H-share data from Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited, we evaluate risk-adjusted performance, tracking efficiencies, and return distributions. Empirical findings demonstrate that a passively managed index portfolio dominates complementary non-index portfolios, confirming that rigorous index inclusion and maintenance criteria function as a structural quality assurance mechanism. Market capitalization and turnover ratios significantly dictate return behaviors, validating index-tracking strategies over alternative non-index equity groupings.

title: The Contribution of Interns to Strengthening a Positive Work Culture: A Case Study in a Tourism and Event Service Company
abstract: This study aims to examine the role of interns in supporting the development of a positive organizational work culture through initiative, responsibility, professionalism, and the processes of adaptation and competency development during the internship period. A qualitative descriptive approach was employed, with data collected through in-depth interviews, participatory observation, and documentation. Informants included the Chief Business Officer (CBO) as the main supervisor and several supervisors from various operational divisions. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis with methodological triangulation and member checking to ensure validity. Findings indicate that interns not only assist in operational tasks but also contribute to strengthening discipline, responsibility, and teamwork within the organization. Their interaction and communication with employees and supervisors facilitate learning and professional attitude development. Interns also introduce new perspectives that add value to organizational processes. Challenges such as initial guidance needs, inconsistent discipline, and adaptation to professional work culture were noted. Structured mentoring and effective communication are essential to optimize interns’ contributions.

title: The Power of Trust: Examining the Mediating Role of Customer Trust in the Link Between Service Quality and Purchase Intention Among Airline Passengers
abstract: Saudi Arabia's aviation sector has accomplished great progress within the context of its Vision 2030 program. However, there is a critical gap in the research concerning the impact of service quality on consumer purchase intentions and the underlying mechanisms driving this relationship. The current study plans to fill this gap by testing both the direct and indirect impacts of perceived service quality on purchase intentions in the framework of the Saudi airline sector, using customer trust as a mediator.The study employed survey method and the sample consisted of 400 airline passengers. The questionnaires were completed online and were previously tested for reliability and validity. The Service Quality (SERVQUAL) Scale, the Brand Trust Scale, and the Purchase Intention Scales were used.Exploratory factor analysis was practiced to the measurement tools, the factor structures were checked and validated, and the reliability analyses demonstrated consistency. Correlation and regression analyses revealed the following findings: Perceived service quality increases both customer trust and purchase intention. Perception of trust partially mediates the relationship between service quality and purchase intention. Accordingly, providing high-quality service and fostering trust are both crucial for influencing airline consumers' purchase intentions.This article examines service quality, …

title: The Paradigm of Spiritual Service (Sewa) in Brahma Kumaris’ Avyakt Murlis: Core Principles, Psychological Impediments, and Behavioral Attributes
abstract: Within the philosophy of the Brahma Kumaris World Spiritual University (BKWSU), spiritual service (sewa) is understood not merely as an act of social altruism or external engagement, but as an integral path to self-transformation (swa-unnati) and global well-being (vishwa-unnati). Drawing on the spiritual teachings in the Avyakt Murlis, this paper examines the conceptual foundations of sewa, its guiding principles, the psychological challenges spiritual volunteers (sewa-dharis) face, and the qualities that characterise effective spiritual service. The analysis highlights the importance of maintaining a balance between meditative remembrance (Yad) and practical service (Sewa), supported by an attitude of instrumental consciousness (Nimitt Bhav), purity of intention, and selfless love. It also explores common psychological obstacles, including ego, the desire for recognition, and spiritual exhaustion, which may undermine the quality and purpose of service. To encourage greater self-awareness and reflective practice, the paper proposes a ten-point introspective diagnostic framework for spiritual practitioners to evaluate their attitudes, motivations, and conduct in service. The paper argues that, within the Brahma Kumaris framework, authentic sewa functions both as a means of personal purification and as a pathway toward collective and universal welfare.

Digital Readiness, Psychological Empowerment, and Public Service Motivation as Determinants of Public Service Quality: The Mediating Role of Employee Work Engagement
abstract: This study aimed to examine the effects of frontline digital readiness, psychological empowerment, and public service motivation on public service quality, with employee work engagement serving as a mediating variable. A quantitative approach with an explanatory research design was using a dataset representing 240 respondents from 12 public service organizations, comprising 120 frontline employees and 120 service users. The sampling framework combined purposive sampling for employees and service users with matched service evaluations. Measurement instruments consisted of structured questionnaires adapted from established scales assessing digital readiness, psychological empowerment, public service motivation, work engagement, and public service quality. The data were designed for analysis using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicated that digital readiness, psychological empowerment, and public service motivation positively influenced work engagement. Digital readiness and psychological empowerment also demonstrated positive direct relationships with public service quality, whereas public service motivation showed no significant direct relationship. Work engagement positively influenced public service quality and mediated the relationships between all three independent variables and service quality. The model explained 57% of the vari…

title: Application of the Natural Resources Conservation Service Technical Release 55 Method in Stormwater Management for Land Development Projects: A Practitioner Case Study
abstract: The Natural Resources Conservation Service Technical Release 55 (TR-55) method remains one of the most widely used tools for estimating runoff on small land development sites in the United States, and in many Pennsylvania municipalities it is effectively the default method required for stormwater submissions. Most published work on the method concerns its theoretical basis, particularly the curve number and the initial abstraction ratio, while comparatively little describes how practicing engineers actually apply it and defend it in review. This paper documents that practice from the perspective of a civil engineer preparing site design and stormwater management plans for land development projects in Bucks County, Pennsylvania. It describes when the runoff calculation takes place in a typical project, how the principal inputs are selected (curve number from mapped hydrologic soil groups, time of concentration from segmented flow paths with a 100-foot sheet-flow limit, and rainfall depths from NOAA Atlas 14 checked against municipal ordinances), and how pre-development conditions are established on previously disturbed sites. These choices are then illustrated through one example from current practice: a townhouse development of approximately 3.5 acres, where the calculations led to two infiltration basins and a vegetated swale. The example shows how the hydrologic result meets …

title: Mapping TPACK self-efficacy beliefs in pre-service Chinese language teachers: a mixed-methods study
abstract: Introduction Digital education places distinctive psychological pressure on pre-service Teachers of Chinese as a Foreign Language (TCFL). This study reinterprets the seven-dimensional Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) scale as a measure of self-perceived TPACK competence, read as an indicator of technology-integration self-efficacy beliefs. Methods An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was used. A total of 202 pre-service TCFL teachers completed questionnaires; eight were interviewed, and six lessons were video-coded (inter-coder κ = 0.83). Results Self-perceived competence was unevenly distributed: Technological Knowledge was lowest (M = 3.68), and Technological Content Knowledge was highest (M = 3.83), the latter associated with short-term extrinsic online-teaching demands. Pedagogical Content Knowledge ( r = 0.784) and Technological Pedagogical Knowledge ( r = 0.835) showed the strongest associations with overall TPACK. Teaching practice, technology training, and competition experience each showed distinct associations, whereas gender and academic level did not. Interviews further surfaced two exploratory themes: employment pressure and cross-cultural online-teaching stress. Discussion Self-Determination Theory is used only as an interpretive lens; basic psychological needs were not measured, so no claim about need satisfaction is tested. The findi…

title: Stars and Squares: Mapping the Strengths and Challenges of Disability Service Provision in International Higher Education
abstract: Professionals from 13 universities representing eight countries participated in a journey mapping activity that requested participants map a student with a disability’s journey at their institution from initial interaction to progress toward graduation. Following the activity, participants reflected on their visual representation of the perceived student journey through questions provided in a reflection document. These documents were analyzed to identify strengths and challenges in disability service office practices. Strengths include student-centered services delivered utilizing clear accommodation processes informed by a caring culture within a supportive institution. Challenges within the disability service office include disability service staff capacity and unclear policies, and challenges across the institution include both a lack of resources and inclusive policies. The knowledge and resistance toward inclusion by professors and professional staff is a foundational challenge in supporting the student population. Implications for practice, policy and research are identified with the goal of expanding global efforts to improve access and success in higher education for students with disabilities.

title: Resveratroloside alleviates senescence-associated phenotypes in vitro through the coordinated regulation of mitochondrial function and chromatin structure
How do different forms of environmental regulation affect high-quality economic development?
abstract: Environmental regulation is increasingly important for coordinating ecological protection and economic transformation, yet its influence on high-quality economic development (HQED) may differ across regulatory forms. Drawing on institutional theory, this study examines formal and informal environmental regulation across 31 Chinese provinces from 2005 to 2022. Province and year fixed effects are employed together with nonlinear, robustness, heterogeneity, and mechanism analyses. The findings show that formal environmental regulation significantly restrains HQED, whereas informal regulation promotes it. Formal regulation displays a U-shaped effect, while informal regulation follows an inverted U-shaped pattern, with both nonlinear relationships mainly evident in eastern China. Mechanism tests further show that technological innovation and industrial agglomeration help transmit the effects of environmental regulation to HQED. These findings demonstrate that the economic consequences of environmental governance depend on regulatory form and provide evidence for designing differentiated environmental policies that support sustainable economic transformation.

title: Architectural Regulation of T‐Lymphocyte Function in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Current Evidence and Translational Opportunities
abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a chronically injured liver in which anti‐tumor immunity is governed not only by immune‐cell abundance and checkpoint signaling, but also by the spatial, mechanical, and multicellular organization of T lymphocytes. This review reframes T‐cell architecture as a regulatory layer operating across molecular, cellular, and tissue scales. Cytoskeletal remodeling, immunological synapse geometry, mechanotransduction, vascular positioning, stromal exclusion, and tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) organization collectively influence T‐cell activation thresholds, effector competence, exhaustion trajectories, and therapeutic responsiveness. We synthesize HCC‐specific evidence from spatial transcriptomics, multiplex imaging, digital pathology, and clinical cohorts, while clearly distinguishing direct HCC observations from mechanisms extrapolated from other solid tumors or foundational T‐cell biology. Current evidence supports the prognostic relevance of intratumoral CD8+ localisation, perivascular immune rims, fibrotic exclusion niches, and mature intratumoral TLS, but causal links between architecture and T‐cell fate remain incompletely defined. We propose an architecture‐guided framework in which spatial immune states serve as both biomarkers and modifiable therapeutic targets. Spatially informed checkpoint blockade, engineered T‐cell…

title: Coordination‐Based Regulation of Integrated Photoanodes for Boosted Water Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting for hydrogen evolution has been deemed a promising approach for solving the world's sustainable energy‐related and environmental challenges. However, poor charge separation in semiconductor photoelectrodes is the major challenge to overall solar energy conversion efficiencies. Moreover, n‐type semiconductors as photoanodes exhibit sluggish water oxidation kinetics. Coordination‐based regulation between semiconductors and cocatalysts as a form of interface optimization in integrated photoanodes has been proved an effective strategy to optimize charge transfer and water oxidation processes. Herein, recent critical headway on improving the efficiency of semiconductor‐based photoanodes for water oxidation via coordination‐based regulation is reviewed. In particular, this review aims to clarify how coordination‐based regulation achieves performance enhancement through the joint modulation of surface states and spin‐electronic states. The mechanism of coordination‐based regulation in integrated photoanodes on charge transfer and water oxidation kinetics prioritization scheme is demonstrated in detail. These benefits of coordination‐based regulation for efficient and stable water splitting devices will show huge advantages in the future.

title: A lightweight frequency-domain enhanced framework for small object detection in remote sensing
abstract: Abstract Remote sensing small-object detection remains challenging: weak target details are attenuated by repeated downsampling, sparse object responses are difficult to separate from background clutter, and objects vary widely in scale and aspect ratio. We propose FD-YOLO, a compact detector with three complementary components. The feature enhancement cascaded architecture reorganizes the neck so that each detection scale is reached through paths of different depth, and implements its fusion nodes with a cascaded unit that keeps a shallow localization anchor together with every refinement state and re-weights them through an input-conditioned depth router. Size-Aware Frequency Convolution derives a radial energy descriptor from the complex Fourier spectrum, predicts per-image gains over learnable Gaussian frequency bands, and modulates spectral amplitude while preserving phase, so that the emphasized bands follow the scale composition of the current scene instead of a fixed partition; a parallel position-dependent spatial branch retains localization cues. Multi-scale expansion attention mixes multi-dilated local-attention responses along an explicit scale axis, adds horizontal and vertical strip attention for elongated structures, and applies input-adaptive multi-kernel refinement. On the SIMD dataset, FD-YOLO achieved an mAP@50 of 83.97%, which was 8.84% higher than the YOLOv…

title: Allobaculum stercoricanis and Its Postbiotics Alleviate Dextran Sulfate Sodium (DSS)-Induced Colitis through the Regulation of theTLR4/NF-κB Signaling Pathway
abstract: Abstract Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal disorder that has become a global public health concern. Postbiotics offer advantages in biosafety and reproducibility over probiotics. Here, we demonstrated that live Allobaculum stercoricanis (A. stercoricanis) and its two postbiotic preparations─inactivated bacterial cells (POST) and cell-free fermentation supernatant (CFS)─effectively alleviated dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice. Integrated gut microbiome and serum metabolomics analyses indicated that these interventions may act through modulating bile acid metabolism and Toll-like receptor signaling pathways. Further investigations combining postbiotic metabolomics, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations identified α-muricholic acid (α-MCA) as a candidate functional metabolite, with the farnesoid X receptor (FXR) as a potential target. We hypothesize that α-MCA may contribute to ameliorating intestinal inflammation through engagement of FXR and suppression of the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway. These findings provide new insights into postbiotic-based therapeutic strategies for IBD.
venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: Forecasting India’s Milk Production using Time-series Econometrics and Machine Learning Models: A Comparative Assessment
abstract: Background: Milk production is a major component of India’s agricultural economy, contributing significantly to food security, rural livelihoods and economic development. Reliable forecasts of future milk production are essential for effective policy formulation, strategic planning and sustainable growth of the dairy sector. This study evaluated the forecasting performance of time series econometric and machine learning models for predicting India’s milk production. Methods: Annual milk production data for the period 1961-2024 were obtained from the Food and Agriculture Organization Corporate Statistical Database. Time series properties were examined and forecasting models were developed using the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average, Exponential Smoothing and Neural Network Autoregression approaches. Model performance was evaluated using information criteria, diagnostic tests, forecast accuracy measures and predictive accuracy comparison tests. Result: Milk production increased steadily during the study period, recording a CAGR of 4.05%. The series became stationary after second differencing and the autoregressive integrated moving average (0,2,1) model provided the highest forecasting accuracy, with a root mean square error of 12,693.94, a mean absolute error of 10,407.38 and a mean absolute percentage error of 4.97%. Forecasts indicate that milk production of India will …

title: Athlete-AI: a multi-modal artificial intelligence framework for personalized athlete monitoring and injury risk forecasting
LLM-enhanced Graph Contrastive Learning for Technology Flow Forecasting
abstract: Technology flow (TF) forecasting aims to predict whether a technology will be utilized by another, which is significant for future cross-integration technology innovation. Although existing methods have made substantial progress in intra-domain TF forecasting, inter-domain TF forecasting remains underexplored and faces several fundamental challenges. Specifically, semantic gaps between technologies from different domains hinder effective representation learning; historical inter-domain TFs are highly sparse, limiting the ability to learn reliable structural dependencies; and intra-domain and inter-domain TFs exhibit distinct flow patterns, which are difficult to model within a unified framework. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose an LLM-enhanced Graph Contrastive Learning ( LGCL ) framework that supports both intra-domain and inter-domain TF forecasting. Specifically, we first leverage LLMs with bias-aware representation adjustment to generate semantically enriched and accurate technology representations to bridge gaps across multiple domains. Then, to mitigate the sparsity of inter-domain TF data, a technology co-occurrence view is incorporated to complement historical TF information. We further develop a non-negative contrastive learning module to integrate the TF and co-occurrence views, enabling effective representation alignment without relying on negat…

title: Metaheuristic Optimization and Artificial Intelligence in Wind Energy Systems for Sustainable Environment: Forecasting, Control, Design, and Diagnostics—A Critical Review
abstract: Wind power is the largest renewable energy source used at the sustainable utility scale. However, wind turbine design, siting, forecasting, control, and maintenance face real challenges, mainly because wind speed is variable and poorly predictable. Over the last ten years, researchers have applied both artificial intelligence (AI) models and metaheuristic optimization algorithms across all phases of the wind energy value chain. This review examines these two methodological approaches across four application fields, with particular attention to evaluation practice, validation level, and implications for sustainability. First, we review wind speed and power forecasting, from statistical baselines to machine learning and deep learning architectures, including models that rely on metaheuristics to tune their hyperparameters and decomposition stages. Second, we examine control applications, focusing on metaheuristic tuning of generator and converter controllers (mainly rotor-side control of doubly-fed induction generators), pitch and torque control, and maximum power point tracking (MPPT). Third, we discuss design-level optimization, covering blade aerodynamic design and wind farm layout under wake effects. Fourth, we examine machine-learning-based supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) monitoring and fault diagnosis, including normal-behavior modelling and anomaly detecti…

title: Comparative Analysis of Univariate and Multivariate Time Series Forecasting Models for Hard Token Inventory Planning in Banking
abstract: Background: Hard token availability is essential for secure transaction approval and service continuity in banking, yet quota-based stock planning may lead to stockouts, overstocking, and operational inefficiencies. This study compares univariate and multivariate time series forecasting models for branch-level hard token inventory planning. Methods: This study aims to develop a forecasting model for branch-level hard Using the CRISP-DM framework, historical operational data from 197 branches were processed into a forecasting-ready dataset. ARIMA and Prophet were developed as univariate models, while Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) incorporated operational, economic, and engineered temporal features. Model performance was evaluated using MAE, RMSE, MAPE, and R². Results: TFT achieved the lowest MAE (5.997) and MAPE (11.56%), as well as the highest R² (0.7403), indicating the strongest overall performance across three of the four evaluation metrics. Prophet recorded the lowest RMSE (10.721), while ARIMA showed the weakest overall performance. Conclusion: The results identify TFT as the preferred model for hard token demand forecasting, based on its lower absolute and percentage prediction errors and highest R² among the evaluated models. Although Prophet achieved a lower RMSE, TFT demonstrated stronger overall performance across the evaluation …

title: Debt price premia and controlling shareholder tunnelling
Kerosene Up, Petrol Down: Demand and Distribution after Madagascar’s Thirty-Month Fuel Price Freeze
abstract: Between July 2022 and December 2024, the administered retail prices of the three main petroleum products sold in Madagascar were held constant in ariary for 30 months. In January 2025, the government resumed monthly adjustment. The resulting price shocks went in opposite directions across products: by September 2025, petrol had fallen by 13.7 percent and diesel by 7.6 percent, while kerosene, the lighting fuel of poor households, had risen by 39.1 percent. We use this configuration to estimate the response of deliveries to relative prices on a monthly product panel that we construct from successive issues of the national statistical office’s economic bulletin, covering October 2021 to September 2025, and we are explicit about how far the design can carry a causal reading. The estimates are consistent in sign and order of magnitude across specifications: the own-price elasticity is −0.84 in first differences, −0.51 in levels with product-specific trends, and −1.52 for kerosene taken alone. We test each estimate against an exact randomization distribution built by displacing the price path in time, a device that never treats the three products as interchangeable. Two of the five estimates clear that test at its attainable floor of p = 0.021; the pooled levels estimate does not, at p = 0.38. With two price events, the design has limited power, and we report failures alongside succ…
