title: Forecasting the OR: How Prediction Markets Could Transform Perioperative Care

Pituitary volume as a permissive morphological threshold for hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis activation in children: a comprehensive diagnostic prediction study with relative importance decomposition
abstract: Objective The gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test, the reference standard for confirming hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis (HPGA) activation, is invasive and costly. Pituitary volume (PV) on MRI has been proposed as a non-invasive surrogate, yet whether PV constitutes a permissive morphological threshold or is redundant with clinical parameters remains undefined. We evaluated PV as a morphological threshold of HPGA activation and quantified its relative importance, unique information content, and clinical utility. Methods We retrospectively enrolled 896 children who underwent pituitary MRI and GnRH stimulation testing. PV was measured using the ellipsoid approximation. Out-of-fold cross-validated AUC was the primary performance metric. Predictor importance was quantified by Shapley value decomposition, permutation importance, and Lindeman–Merenda–Gold (LMG) variance partitioning. Morphological-threshold analyses examined HPGA activation across PV deciles. Statistical mediation tested whether insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) mediated the PV–HPGA association, with formal power analysis for incremental AUC detection. Results PV exhibited a threshold pattern: HPGA activation was 28.9% (95% CI 20.5–39.0) in the lowest PV decile (≤115 mm³) versus 92.2% (95% CI 84.8–96.2) in the highest (≥335 mm³; OR 4.38, 95% CI 2.60–7.36; per-IQR OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.59–2.62). …

title: Preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in small hepatocellular carcinoma (≤ 3 cm) by leveraging cross-phase variations of MRI contrast phases
Multi-step prediction of electronic expansion valve opening of a low-carbon air-conditioning system with condensation heat-recovery unit
abstract: Condensation heat recovery provides an energy-saving approach for air reheating in air-conditioning systems, but its dynamic performance depends strongly on the regulation of refrigerant distribution. The electronic expansion valve (EEV) controls the refrigerant flow entering the heat-recovery branch, and accurate short-horizon prediction of EEV opening can support predictive operation and supply-air state regulation. In this study, a VMD-GRU-Attention framework was proposed for direct multi-step prediction of EEV opening in an air-conditioning system with a condensation heat-recovery unit. Variational mode decomposition (VMD) was first used to decompose the original EEV opening sequence into modal components with different frequency characteristics. A gated recurrent unit (GRU) network was then used to extract temporal dependencies, and an attention mechanism was introduced to enhance the contribution of informative historical states. Experimental data collected from an actual system were used for model evaluation. Compared with RNN, TCN, LSTM and GRU, the proposed model achieved lower prediction errors and a more concentrated absolute percentage error distribution. At the 10th prediction step, MSE, RMSE, MAE and MAPE were reduced by 57.78%, 35.02%, 35.75% and 35.78%, respectively, compared with GRU. The results demonstrate the framework's effectiveness for EEV opening predict…

title: DeepOSSA: a deep learning framework for personalized survival prediction in osteosarcoma patients
abstract: Background Osteosarcoma, the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents, is marked by high invasiveness and heterogeneous outcomes due to inter-patient variability in tumor biology and treatment response. Accurate prognostic modeling is crucial for personalized risk stratification and clinical decision-making. Objective We developed and validated DeepOSSA, a deep learning framework for individualized survival prediction in osteosarcoma, leveraging high-dimensional, sparsely encoded clinical data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Methods Clinical data from 895 osteosarcoma patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2018 were extracted. Continuous variables were optimally discretized using X-tile, and categorical covariates were one-hot encoded. We compared DeepOSSA against seven representative models spanning classical machine learning (support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and gradient boosted decision trees (GBDT)), deep learning (multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and Transformer), and survival analysis (Cox proportional hazards (CoxPH) and DeepSurv). DeepOSSA integrates a Transformer-based representation tower for high-order sparse feature crossing with a Cox-style discrete-time survival head, enabling joint optimization of feature representation and time-to-event modeling. Performance was evaluated on a held-out t…
venue: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology

title: gTranslate: rapid and accurate translation table prediction for prokaryotic genomes
abstract: Background Bioinformatic tools often require the prediction of protein-coding genes to make inferences about prokaryotic genomes. Typically, the genetic code used for translating genes to proteins must be specified by the user based on the taxonomic classification of a genome assembly or, for some widely used tools, established using a heuristic rule based on gene coding densities. Manual specification is at best inconvenient, but more challenging is that many bioinformatic tools are applied before taxonomic classifications have been established making specifying the translation table impractical. Methods Here we provide a computationally efficient tool, gTranslate, that uses an ensemble of five machine learning methods to accurately predict translation tables for prokaryotic genomes. The feature vector used by gTranslate takes advantage of differences in gene coding densities when predicting genes under different translation tables along with features that consider the number and ratio of UGA stop codon reassignments to tryptophan or glycine. gTranslate is freely available at https://github.com/cmc-aau/gTranslate and archived on Zenodo. Results We demonstrate that gTranslate correctly predicts the translation table of prokaryotic genomes >99.99% of the time ( i.e. , <1 error per 10,000 genomes) and outperforms a more computationally expensive prediction method and a coding den…

title: From biomarker discovery to prediction models: clinical translation of multi-omics for early prediction of gestational diabetes mellitus
abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) affects roughly one in seven pregnancies worldwide, yet diagnosis by oral glucose tolerance testing at 24–28 weeks of gestation leaves only a narrow window for intervention. The demonstrated benefit of treating early-diagnosed GDM has intensified interest in first-trimester prediction. This narrative review synthesises recent advances in early-pregnancy biomarkers for GDM, shifting the emphasis from biomarker discovery to clinical translation. Conventional lipid indicators and composite indices provide moderate predictive power at minimal cost (odds ratios 1.4–1.7; AUCs 0.75–0.82). Metabolomic and lipidomic studies have identified recurrent signatures — phospholipid remodelling, glycerolipid accumulation, fatty acid and acylcarnitine excess, branched-chain amino acids and bile acids — that map onto insulin resistance, lipotoxicity and hepatic steatosis, and omics-enhanced models report derivation-stage AUCs of approximately 0.83–0.95 with apparent incremental value over clinical factors alone, although these estimates derive predominantly from small cohorts that have rarely undergone external validation. Gut-microbiome features, thyroid parameters and environmental exposures further widen the aetiological frame. Translation remains limited, however, by small derivation cohorts, scarce external validation, analytical heterogeneity and the abse…

title: The Dual Engine of Mindfulness: Forging Capacity in High-Stakes Leadership
abstract: Leaders across every sector face a common vulnerability: the involuntary collapse of developed capacity into reactive, survival-based instinct under pressure. Drawing on the Lenses of Leadership model, this paper argues that mindfulness is not a passive wellness practice but a rigorous training mechanism producing two complementary capacities: Illumination, the metacognitive awareness to detect unconscious threat narratives, and Jōriki, the trained cognitive strength to decouple from them. Together these capacities convert involuntary state collapse into deliberate choice, preserve cognitive bandwidth under pressure, and build the psychological resources required for sustained higher-order leadership. Eight practical strategies for daily application are provided.
venue: Journal of Leadership, Accountability and Ethics

title: Capacity-First Philosophy of Psychology
abstract: Abstract This paper aims to show that a neo-Aristotelian version of capacity-first philosophy of mind is fruitfully applied to a question which is specific to philosophy of psychology, namely: What counts as an adequate explanation in psychology? Drawing on Kenny, Glock and Schellenberg, the paper argues that the neo-Aristotelian capacity view is built around a set of criteria for the classification of capacities. All capacities are classified according to (1) possession-, (2) exercise-, (3) vehicle-, (4) opportunity-, (5) enablement- and (6) successful employment- criteria. These classification criteria are used to reconstruct the process of de-intellectualizing explanations of psychological phenomena. De-intellectualization targets theoretical assumptions about the circumstances in which the various criteria for classifying capacities are satisfied. The capacity approach offers a tool for regimenting the process of de-intellectualization. It also illustrates the contrast between de-intellectualization and Dennett’s homuncular functionalism. Rather than offering nothing more than conceptual clarity for debates about the metaphysics and epistemology of mind, the neo-Aristotelian capacity view explains why de-intellectualizing explanations is a feature of adequate explanations in psychology.

title: Surge capacity versus surge capability in nursing and health system preparedness: a scoping review
Reengineering Teacher Digital Capacity: An Adaptive EdTech Leadership Framework for Pedagogical Transformation through Readiness-Based Differentiated Technology Mentoring
abstract: This study examined changes in teacher digital capacity following readiness-based differentiated technology mentoring and developed an Adaptive EdTech Leadership Framework and Toolkit. Conducted at De La Salle Santiago Zobel School, Muntinlupa City, Philippines, during School Year 2025–2026, it employed a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design with a one-group pretest–posttest quantitative phase followed by explanatory interviews. Thirty-six probationary teachers completed matched Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) surveys; 33 had complete paired Technology Integration Matrix (TIM) observations. Baseline readiness combined perception-based and practice-based indicators to differentiate six weeks of mentoring. Core TAM remained high and statistically stable, increasing from 4.528 to 4.574, t(35) = 0.804, p = .427. Overall TIM increased from 1.664 to 2.470, t(32) = 6.016, p < .001, with a large paired effect size of 1.047. All five TIM dimensions improved significantly. Baseline readiness was associated with posttest outcomes but not significantly with change magnitude. Seven explanatory themes emphasized personalized support, purposeful technology selection, learning-centered enactment, guided practice, classroom feedback, contextual conditions, and continued professional support. Integrated findings indicate that acceptance and pedagogical integration followed distinct deve…
venue: QualiSearch Journal of Educational Research and Practice

title: Post-Earthquake Field Hospital Bed Capacity Allocation Problem Solving Two-Stage Stochastic Programming: A Case Study in Istanbul Avcılar
abstract: Field hospitals are temporary healthcare facilities deployed to provide medical services in scenarios where conventional healthcare infrastructure is disrupted due to natural or human-induced disasters, migration, armed conflicts, or similar crises. Depending on the anticipated needs, these facilities may be categorized into specialized types, such as orthopedic and traumatology field hospitals, surgical field hospitals, or general medical aid field hospitals. Bed capacity is a critical determinant of the scale of a field hospital, which in turn influences the spatial requirements for setup, personnel allocation, and associated costs. Typically established for short-term use, ranging from six months to two years, the operational duration, bed capacity, and structural configuration of field hospitals collectively define their functional capabilities. This study proposes a two-stage stochastic mathematical programming model to address the problem of calculating the optimal bed capacity for field hospitals delivering post-disaster healthcare services, with a focus on earthquake scenarios. Compared with two-stage stochastic models, the mathematical model proposed in this study exhibits distinct differences from existing models in the disaster and hospital bed capacity modeling literature. The model integrates uncertainties inherent in disaster contexts, such as fluctuating patient …

title: Associations Between Individual Differences in Cognitive Control Capacity and Multitasking Performance
abstract: Background/Objectives: Cognitive control capacity (CCC) describes the maximum volume of information an individual can reliably process per unit time, a key cognitive factor of multitasking performance. While sustained high-load multitasking is known to induce cumulative cognitive impairment, it remains untested whether CCC is associated with vulnerability to this decline across subjective, behavioral, and neural levels. This study systematically characterized how individual differences in CCC relate to multitasking processing ability and examined whether a higher CCC is associated with smaller cognitive fatigue during extended operations. Methods: CCC was assessed in 313 college students via the adaptive MFTA_A paradigm. Participants scoring in the upper and lower 27% of the CCC distribution formed the high-CCC group (n = 42, 3.65 ± 0.33 bps) and the low-CCC group (n = 41, 2.04 ± 0.28 bps). All participants completed a 1 h multitasking information-processing test comprising tracking, instrument monitoring, and listening subtasks. Alertness was measured with the Psychomotor Vigilance Task before and after the test, subjective workload was rated across four Visual Analogue Scale dimensions, and continuous task-state EEG was recorded to analyze spectral power and microstate dynamics. Results: Relative to low-CCC participants, the high-CCC group showed smaller post-test alertness d…

title: Quantum channel capacity of traversable wormholes
Cu-Based Versatile p-d Bimetallic Catalysts for Efficient CO2 Reduction Reaction via Orbital Matching Mechanism
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction reaction to high-value multicarbon products represents a highly promising strategy for achieving carbon neutrality goals. Among various electrocatalysts, copper-based materials occupy a central position due to their unique capability for *CO adsorption and dimerization; however, they still face severe challenges, including high overpotentials and limited product selectivity. Orbital engineering, particularly the construction of p-d bimetallic systems through the introduction of p-block metals, has emerged as a pivotal approach to surmounting the performance bottlenecks of Cu-based catalysts. This review systematically summarizes the recent research progress in copper-based p-d bimetallic catalysts designed via orbital engineering for efficient CO2 reduction reaction. We provide an in-depth discussion on the modulation mechanisms of p-block metals on the performance of Cu active centers from three key dimensions: electronic effects, geometric effects, and microenvironment regulation. Furthermore, we summarize the primary challenges currently facing the field of p-d orbital matching and offer perspectives on the rational design of future CO2 reduction catalytic systems that possess high activity, stability, and energy efficiency, aiming to provide theoretical guidance and practical insights for the large-scale application of gree…

title: The psychological effect of gamification mechanism in XR immersive environment on user willingness to behave
abstract: With the rapid landing of XR technology in the fields of architecture, education, medical and other fields, how to effectively guide user behavior through interaction design and content mechanism has become the core topic of human-computer interaction research. This paper examines how gamification mechanisms in an XR immersive environment influence users' behavioral intentions. Drawing on self-determination theory as the overarching framework and incorporating spatial narrative structure and the Octalysis framework, it systematically examines the mediating roles of the three basic psychological needs—autonomy, competence, and relatedness—in the immersive experience. The study uses a combination of literature review and theoretical analysis, and constructs a theoretical model of "gamification elements → psychological needs to meet → willingness to act" through the depth analysis of typical XR cases such as medical training, building space guide, safety education and other types of XR cases. The study suggests that XR's distinctive sense of presence and interactivity may amplify the psychological effects of gamification drivers, such as a sense of mission and progression, while excessive competition and manipulative design may undermine intrinsic motivation.

title: Based on Multi-Spectral Technology, the Interaction Mechanism of Xylitol, Stearic Acid and Gelatin Was Explored
abstract: To optimize the properties of gelatin-based films and expand their applications in the food industry, this study systematically investigated the interaction mechanisms between xylitol (Xyl), stearic acid (Ste), and gelatin (GA) using multispectral technology combined with thermodynamic analysis and molecular docking simulations. The results demonstrated that both Xyl and Ste formed stable non-covalent complexes with GA through static quenching, and the binding processes are spontaneous. The Xyl-GA complex acts on the amino acid residues of glycine GLY21, alanine ALA20, glutamine GLN19 and arginine ARG17, with a binding constant of 1.35 L/mol and a binding site number of 0.17, and elevated temperature can effectively promote its binding reaction. In contrast, stearic acid–gelatin forms stable complexes with alanine ALA20, valine VAL22, methionine MET23, phenylalanine PHE25 and arginine ARG17 through hydrogen bonds and van der Waals forces. The increase in temperature will weaken the binding force between Ste and GA. Synchronous fluorescence spectroscopy verified that the binding sites of xylitol and stearic acid were adjacent to the tryptophan residues of gelatin. Three-dimensional fluorescence spectroscopy further confirmed that the combination of the two additives can induce conformational changes in the gelatin polypeptide chain. This study characterized the binding sites, ch…

title: Constitutional Disobedience in the Practice of Concurrent Office-Holding by Deputy Ministers: Non-Compliance with Constitutional Court Decision No. 80/PUU-XVII/2019 and a Proposed Compliance Oversight Mechanism
abstract: Constitutional Court Decision No. 80/PUU-XVII/2019 established in its legal reasoning that the prohibition against concurrent office-holding applicable to ministers also extends to deputy ministers. Nevertheless, the government failed to implement this interpretation, relying on the position that the binding legal force of Constitutional Court decisions is confined to their operative provisions. Several years later, Constitutional Court Decision No. 128/PUU-XXIII/2025 expressly incorporated this prohibition into its operative provisions while reaffirming the binding legal force of the reasoning articulated in Decision No. 80/PUU-XVII/2019. This article examines the normative relationship between these two decisions, analyzes the government's non-compliance during the 2020–2025 period through the lens of constitutional disobedience, and proposes an oversight mechanism to strengthen compliance with Constitutional Court decisions. Employing normative juridical research, this study adopts statutory, case-based, and conceptual approaches. The findings reveal three principal conclusions. First, the legal reasoning underpinning Decision No. 80/PUU-XVII/2019 constitutes a binding ratio decidendi. Accordingly, Decision No. 128/PUU-XXIII/2025 primarily serves to reaffirm the existing constitutional norm and eliminate interpretive ambiguities rather than establish a new legal obligation. …

title: Integrated NMR, HPLC-Chemometrics, and Network Pharmacology Strategy for Quality Assessment and Mechanism Elucidation of Gelatinous Chinese Medicines
abstract: Gelatinous Chinese medicines (GCMs), such as Ejiao, are animal-derived solid preparations traditionally used for blood and qi deficiency. With growing market demand, adulteration has become a critical quality concern. This study established a multimodal quality assessment system for GCMs. Using 1H NMR, we characterized the acid hydrolysates of GCMs and identified 17 components, including 16 total hydrolysable amino acids and taurine, revealing compositional similarity across seven GCMs. Stability studies under acid hydrolysis were conducted on 19 amino acids, all of which remained stable except methionin, cystine, and tryptophan, leading to the selection of the remaining 16 amino acids as target analytes. A pre-column derivatization–HPLC method was validated for the quantification of 16 total hydrolysable amino acids, showing excellent linearity (r2 > 0.999), high precision (RSD < 2.71%), and satisfactory recoveries (90.74–109.3%). Content determination of 65 batches revealed batch-to-batch variations in total hydrolysable amino acid profiles. Combined with chemometrics, the method successfully discriminated dermal, horn, bone, and shell glues, and further enabled subcategory differentiation. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that these amino acid components may interact with key targets (e.g., GRM5, GABRA1, GABBR2) and pathways, primarily neuroactive ligand–receptor inte…

title: Structural Characterization and Hypoglycemic Mechanism of Pumpkin Seed Polysaccharides
abstract: This study investigated three pumpkin seed polysaccharide fractions (PSP-1-1, PSP-1-2, and PSP-1-3) with molecular weights of 29,797 Da, 11,209 Da, and 4346 Da, respectively, all containing both α- and β-glycosidic linkages. Structural analysis revealed arabinose, galactose, and glucose as predominant residues in PSP-1-1, while PSP-1-2 and PSP-1-3 additionally contained xylose, with all fractions sharing common structural units. All three fractions were associated with dose-dependent increases in GLP-1 secretion from L cells and with upregulation of genes in the sweet taste receptor pathway. The pooled fraction PSP-1s showed higher gene expression than individual fractions and was therefore selected for in vivo studies. In diabetic mice, PSP-1s intervention alleviated weight loss, reduced hyperphagia and polydipsia, lowered blood glucose, improved glucose tolerance and dyslipidemia, and decreased GSP, insulin, and HOMA-IR while increasing QUICKI. Qualitative histological observations suggested less pronounced pancreatic islet abnormalities following PSP-1s intervention. PSP-1s increased serum GLP-1 concentrations and colonic SCFA concentrations and altered gut microbiota composition. Collectively, the hypoglycemic effects of PSP-1s were accompanied by changes in serum GLP-1, colonic SCFAs, gut microbiota composition, and hypothalamic GLP-1R and appetite-related gene expression.…

title: A Data-Sharing Coordination Mechanism for Medical Consortia Under Government Incentives
abstract: Research on data-sharing behaviour within a medical consortium not only enriches the theoretical framework of medical data element circulation but also provides scientific decision-making support for governments, hospitals, and others, thus facilitating cross-institutional and cross-regional data sharing and value realisation. This paper focuses on the challenges of medical data sharing within a medical consortium, based on evolutionary game theory, deeply explores the strategic interaction logic between core and primary care hospitals and the government, and proposes data-sharing optimisation recommendations suitable for medical consortia. The following results were obtained: government subsidies are a key lever for initiating system evolution; the differences in the probability of data leakage brought about by regulatory intensity positively affect the willingness of two-level hospitals to share data; the level of trust between hospitals shows one-way dominance and two-way influence characteristics; the hospital-specific medical data loss coefficient imposes a rigid constraint on hospitals’ strategic choices; and the proportion of technology costs borne is sensitive to the strategies of core hospitals but stable for primary care hospitals. Finally, based on the findings of the study, corresponding recommendations are put forward, with the aim of contributing to medical data v…

title: Unraveling the Reaction Mechanism for FAAE Formation during Fast Pyrolysis of Mixed Food Waste
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the detailed reaction mechanism for the formation of biodiesel-range compounds, i.e., fatty acid alkyl esters (FAAE), via a novel route involving fast pyrolysis. Our recent studies have shown that large fractions of FAAE can be obtained in bio-oil if fast pyrolysis of extractive-rich biomass is conducted under a particular combination of operating conditions, following extensive experimental work. The extractives must contain large fractions of lipids, and operating conditions must have an optimal value for volatile residence time, temperature, and heating rate for FAAE to form. Together, these factors lead to FAAE formation reactions, which require detailed mechanistic investigation for the advancement of this novel route to biodiesel production. Therefore, this paper presents an unravelling of the detailed reaction mechanism involving various possible routes having several intermediate steps. Overall, the FAAE formation reaction can be summarized as the reaction between the free fatty acids (FFA) generated via decomposition of lipids in the biomass and in situ alcohols (IA) generated via decomposition of the lignocellulosic part of the biomass. Formation of these intermediates was confirmed by the corresponding experimental results. Moreover, fatty acids and alcohols are necessary for FAAE formation, thus involving intermediate steps for their for…

title: FORMATION OF AN ADAPTIVE MECHANISM FOR ENTERPRISE STAFFING UNDER STRUCTURAL LABOUR SHORTAGES
abstract: The article examines the theoretical and applied foundations for developing an adaptive mechanism for enterprise staffing under structural labour shortages. Labour shortage is interpreted as a persistent mismatch between enterprises’ demand for employees and the available labour supply in terms of quantity, qualifications, competencies, and territorial distribution. The current state of the Ukrainian labour market is analysed with regard to declining labour supply, demographic and migration changes, occupational and skills mismatches, technological transformation, and increasing competition among employers for workers. The study employs analysis and synthesis, comparison, systematisation, logical generalisation, a systems approach, and graphical representation. It is substantiated that, under persistent labour shortages, staffing cannot be limited to searching for candidates and filling current vacancies. It should combine external recruitment with the involvement of insufficiently represented population groups, employee development and retention, reskilling and upskilling, internal mobility, and the adaptation of work organisation and technological processes. The key factors causing structural labour shortages are systematised, while the external and internal opportunities available to enterprises for reducing staffing gaps are identified. An adaptive enterprise staffing mecha…

title: Smartphone-assisted colorimetric sensor based on Au/Fe3O4 nanozyme for total antioxidant capacity evaluation in fruits
Toward first-principles description of amorphous monolayer carbon growth
abstract: The synthesis and properties of amorphous monolayer carbon have attracted extensive attention, yet the computational simulation of its growth mechanism poses great challenges. In a recent study, Monte Carlo simulation based on a hybrid potential model has enabled the atomic-scale growth of amorphous monolayer carbon, revealing a novel chaining-branching-networking-filling (CBNF) mechanism. In this study, we further push forward the accuracy of the growth simulation by combining a MACE-based machine-learning force field with three-dimensional continuous-space Monte Carlo sampling. The simulations shed light on the atomistic origins of the CBNF mechanism on the Cu(100) substrate: restricted carbon mobility, out-of-plane buckling, and transient subsurface carbon excursions induce kinetic trapping near deposition sites, favoring local chain extension before compact island formation; meanwhile, enhanced chain-end extension suppresses side branching, leading to elongated carbon chains and delayed network formation. These near-first-principles descriptions provide a reliable foundation for our further understanding of the structure and growth process of amorphous carbon.

title: Crystal violet adsorption on a hierarchically porous FAU zeolite–carbon dots composite: steric constraints, energetic heterogeneity, and time-dependent mass transfer
Vacancy Configuration Effects on Oxygen–Carbon Bonding and Carbon Network Reconstruction in Fullerene Nanocages
abstract: ReaxFF molecular dynamics was used to examine oxygen–carbon bonding and carbon network reconstruction of pristine C60, monovacancy C59, and two specific C58 vacancy configurations at 1600-2800 K. Oxidation and oxygen-free conditions each used three independent trajectories and 200 ps production periods. At 2800 K and nominal oxygen loading of 0.5, the normalized C–O bond order sums were 0.04075 ± 0.03532 for V2-adj and 0.17501 ± 0.04520 for V2-sep. Their initial C–C retention fractions were 0.9617 ± 0.0397 and 0.6231 ± 0.1279, respectively. These late-stage differences persisted across bond order thresholds of 0.30–0.40. Matched oxygen-free controls showed substantial thermal reconstruction, especially for V1, demonstrating that connectivity replacement cannot generally be attributed to oxygen attack. The V2-sep mean was 7.85% below an additive two-V1 bonding benchmark, but the difference was smaller than its propagated sampling uncertainty. The results concern the selected configurations and parametrization, whose initial coordination environments differ; they do not establish universal vacancy separation effects or real soot oxidation kinetics.

title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
abstract: Abstract Heatwaves are becoming more frequent, intense and prolonged as the climate warms, placing stress on the electricity infrastructure underpinning modern societies. Yet how rising temperatures erode grid capacity remains under-quantified. Existing power-flow models either oversimplify thermal effects or become computationally intractable when resolving them in detail. Here we introduce a unified, computationally efficient framework that jointly captures temperature-dependent demand, generator derating and spatially resolved transmission-line thermal limits within an alternating-current optimal power-flow formulation. Applying it to the Western European system with open-access grid, high-resolution weather reanalysis and demand data, we simulate hundreds of projected heatwave scenarios for 2026–2030. Across these represented grid configurations, the analysis reveals substantial national disparities: the Spanish grid exhibits temperature-induced bottlenecks and load shedding, whereas the German grid remains comparatively resilient. Heatwave-aware power-flow analysis thus uncovers structural bottlenecks and should be integrated into grid planning and adaptation as heatwaves intensify under climate change.

title: The Uhlenbeck–Ford model in two dimensions: Reference system for fluid-phase free-energy calculations
abstract: We investigate the Uhlenbeck–Ford (UF) model as a reference system for free-energy calculations in two-dimensional (2D) fluids. The 2D virial coefficients are computed exactly up to the tenth order and combined with molecular simulation data to construct highly accurate numerical representations of the equation of state and the excess Helmholtz free energy. We then determine the phase diagram of the model in order to establish the thermodynamic stability limits of the fluid phase and thereby identify the range of applicability of the UF model as a fluid reference system. In the course of this analysis, we identify the solid, hexatic, and fluid phases and show that the fluid remains the only thermodynamically stable phase, independent of density, for scaling parameters up to p ≲ 70. Finally, we demonstrate the practical applicability of the 2D UF model as a reference system through thermodynamic integration calculations of the free energy of a two-dimensional Lennard-Jones fluid.

title: Photoinduced Amination of α-CF3 Alkyl Bromides with Oxime Carbonates by Merging Energy Transfer and Boryl Radical-Mediated Halogen-Atom Transfer
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a metal-free photoinduced amination of α-CF3 alkyl bromides with oxime carbonates, providing a broad scope of structurally diverse α-trifluoromethyl amines. Oxime carbonates function as bifunctional reagents that undergo homolysis to generate iminyl radicals as nitrogen sources and alkoxycarbonyloxyl radicals via an energy transfer (EnT) process. The alkoxycarbonyloxyl radicals abstract hydrogen atoms from ligated boranes via a hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) process, yielding reactive ligated boryl radicals (LBRs) that trigger halogen-atom transfer (XAT).

title: An integrated resource–demand–engineering framework for prioritizing bedrock geothermal exploration targets in the central-southern Hebei Plain, North China
abstract: Bedrock geothermal reservoirs in the central-southern Hebei Plain are important targets for geothermal development. However, spatial differences in resource conditions, development demand, and engineering accessibility make it difficult to determine exploration priority. This study evaluated the exploration priority of 38 previously identified bedrock geothermal potential areas with reservoir depths shallower than 4000 m. Seven indicators, including policy need, supply-demand matching, burial depth, reservoir temperature, resource modulus, drilling control, and heat-transmission distance, were organized under three criteria: development demand, resource conditions, and engineering feasibility. Indicator weights were determined using the analytic hierarchy process, and GIS-based spatial analysis and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation were applied to 4041 grid cells measuring 3 km × 3 km. Comprehensive scores ranged from 1.10 to 7.22 and showed marked spatial variation. Priority exploration zones occurred as discontinuous clusters across several predefined geothermal potential areas, with major concentrations in the Baoding–Xiong’an and Cangzhou–Hengshui sectors. Development demand has the largest criterion-layer weight (47.4%), followed by resource conditions (37.6%) and engineering feasibility (14.9%). In the sensitivity analysis, varying each indicator weight by ±20% yielded Spear…

title: Kirigami-Graded Metabeam for Broadband Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting: A Numerical Analytical and Finite-Element Study
abstract: Self-powered sensor nodes need vibration harvesters that work over a band of frequencies, but the arrays and graded metamaterials that provide such bandwidth need many separately clamped resonators. This numerical study presents a kirigami-graded metabeam in which U-shaped slits in one 250 × 16 × 0.5 mm aluminum sheet release four tabs of graded length (44–62 mm); the sheet is folded and clamped at both ends, and a PZT-5A patch straddling each root feeds its own resistive load. A distributed-parameter cell model is verified against a three-dimensional coupled-field finite-element model within 1% in frequency and 2% in power. In the finite-element model, each cell mode is confined to one tab (off-diagonal amplitudes ≤ 0.09) and the cells deliver 0.59–1.44 µW per (m s−2)2 at 130–274 Hz; their band-mean power is 3.6 times that of a single clamped tab and 0.9 times that of four separately clamped tabs, with two clamps instead of four. Interleaving the cells so that frequency-adjacent cells are not spatial neighbors keeps the modes localized on an 18 Hz grid and gives a continuous 212–284 Hz band with 1.1 times the four-tab power. One root-compliance parameter places 18 cell frequencies within 2–3%, and the sensitivity of the results to the assumed damping is quantified. No measurement is reported; the experimental characterization of the prototype is left to a separate study.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Radiofrequency Echographic Multi Spectrometry Compared with Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry: A Real-World Study
abstract: Background: Radiofrequency Echographic Multi-Spectrometry (REMS) is an ultrasound-based technique for the assessment of bone mineral density (BMD) that has been proposed as an alternative to dual-energy X ray absorptiometry (DXA) for the diagnosis of osteoporosis. Although previous studies have reported high diagnostic concordance between REMS and DXA, evidence from real-world settings remains limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance and agreement between REMS and DXA in a clinical population undergoing BMD assessment. Methods: In this retrospective observational study, 145 subjects undergoing BMD evaluation were assessed with both REMS and DXA. Complete paired examinations were available for 142 patients at the lumbar spine and 134 at the femoral neck. DXA was used as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance of REMS was evaluated by calculating sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV). Agreement between REMS and DXA diagnostic classifications was assessed using linearly weighted Cohen’s kappa. Mean REMS and DXA measurements were compared using paired Student’s t-tests, whereas agreement between continuous BMD measurements was assessed using Bland–Altman analysis. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to evaluate the discriminative performance of REMS T-scores. …

title: Insoluble π –d -Conjugated Small Molecules Featuring p -Type Ligands Enable All-Organic Dual-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Organic electrodes for secondary batteries are hindered by molecular dissolution and low operating voltages. Herein, we report a coordination-driven strategy to construct insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules (BTD-M, M = Cu, Ni, or Zn) featuring high-voltage p-type triphenylamine-derived ligands (N4′,N4′-diphenyl-[1,1′-biphenyl]-3,4,4′-triamine, BTD). By precisely tuning metal–ligand coordination, we thermodynamically lock discrete molecules against electrolyte dissolution while preserving unhindered access to active sites. The optimal BTD-Cu exhibits a narrow bandgap of 0.7 eV, enabling extensive electron delocalization for electronic conductivity. This electrode delivers a near-theoretical capacity of 134 mAh g–1 at 1C and still delivers 83 mAh g–1 at 10C. Leveraging bipolar redox chemistry of p-type ligands and metal centers, the symmetric all-organic dual-ion battery achieves an average voltage of 2.4 V and a cycle life exceeding 1000 cycles. This work establishes insoluble π–d conjugated small molecules as an accessible platform for organic battery design.

title: Peer-reviewed bioinformatic resources foster accessibility, transparency, reproducibility, and rigor in the microbial sciences
abstract: ABSTRACT The Databases, Software Tools, and Web-based Services special issue of Microbiology Resource Announcements features announcements that foster transparent, open, rigorous, and reproducible practices in the microbial sciences. These resources span the microbial sources and the three types of bioinformatic resources sought in the call for submissions. By publishing in Microbiology Resource Announcements , developers improve the discoverability and utility of their bioinformatic resources. Furthermore, it provides them with an opportunity to be credited for their work developing the resource. It also signals to the community that the resource is intended for broader use. The bioinformatic resources announced in this special issue fit alongside the other types of resources more commonly published in the journal and serve as useful companions to research articles published across ASM’s journals portfolio. Looking forward, the journal continues to seek submissions that continue the strong momentum created by the announcements included in this special issue.

title: Quantifying QX → QY Energy Relaxation in Chlorophyll a
abstract: Abstract Chlorophyll a is a prototypical porphyrinoid chromophore featuring complex electronic structure, which plays a central role in oxygenic photosynthesis. In particular, the properties of the lowest-energy Q-band govern light absorption, ultrafast energy transfer, and charge separation processes. However, the precise time scale of intramolecular energy relaxation between its two lowest electronic states, QX and QY, a key step in chlorophyll photophysics, eluded accurate quantification. Here we directly measure this relaxation time in chlorophyll a and determine a definitive time scale of 25 fs. We used sub-10 fs pulses and a specially developed polarization-control scheme for two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy to selectively isolate population-transfer pathways. This disentangles ultrafast energy relaxation from the spectral congestion, pulse overlap signals, and coherent artifacts. The measured time scale establishes that the vibronically-mixed QX state functions as a transient intermediate, rapidly funneling excitation into the lowest-energy QY state, consistent with the non-adiabatic vibronic coupling model. This result resolves a long-standing ambiguity in chlorophyll photophysics and provides an experimental benchmark for vibronic mixing models describing vibroelectronic properties of porphyrinoid chromophores and intramolecular energy relaxation. Furthermore, t…

title: Neural sensitivity to peer rejection predicts depressive symptoms and daily mood in adolescents
abstract: Abstract Understanding the role of peer feedback, particularly rejection, is critical for adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the neurophysiological markers core to peer feedback, especially those that may presage risk for depression, are unclear. Adolescents ( N = 179; ages 13–18; healthy controls n = 62, remitted MDD n = 80, current MDD n = 37) completed a baseline clinical assessment and a revised Chatroom Task during EEG recording, from which the P3 to peer acceptance and rejection feedback was quantified. Over 12 months, daily mood and keyboard inputs from adolescents’ smartphones were passively obtained. Linear models evaluated whether the P3 difference between rejection and acceptance (ΔP3) prospectively predicted depressive severity and average daily mood. Exploratory natural language processing examined whether friendship-focused social communication moderated the association between neural sensitivity to peer feedback and subsequent clinical outcomes. Group and feedback type interacted in predicting P3 amplitude (F(2176) = 4.84, p = 0.009): adolescents with current MDD showed larger P3 amplitudes to rejection than acceptance, whereas remitted MDD showed elevated amplitudes to both feedback types relative to controls. In a general linear model adjusting for age, sex, site, and baseline depression severity, the Grou p × ΔP3 interaction was significant i…

title: Optimization of Heat Transfer Process With Variable Specific Heat Working Fluids Through Phase Change Latent Heat Adjustment
abstract: ABSTRACT Heat exchange between circulating working fluid and thermal storage medium is an essential process in thermodynamic cycles of energy storage systems. Thermophysical properties of the working fluids therefore play an important role in such systems. Conventional heat‐transfer fluids, such as water and thermal oil, have relatively constant specific heat capacities, whereas high pressure CO 2 varies significantly with temperature near the critical region. Such a difference causes a specific heat capacity mismatch between these fluids, leading to temperature difference increase along the heat exchanger. The large temperature difference also increases entropy generation. Here we propose a new method to reduce the irreversibility through the adjustment of equivalent specific heat capacity based on phase‐change latent heat. To validate such an approach, a steady‐state model counterflow heat exchanger was used for high‐pressure CO 2 at 10–15 MPa. Eight paraffins with phase‐transition temperatures from 40°C to 58°C were combined to give a phase‐change material mixture. A genetic algorithm optimized the paraffin proportions, proportional coefficient, and temperature‐shift parameter. The optimized phase change mixture closely matched the temperature‐dependent specific heat capacity profile of CO 2 within the investigated range. The best agreement occurred at 11 MPa. Under the same…

title: Integration of Renewable Energy and Hybrid Power System for Sustainable Transportation: A Vessel-to-Grid Approach
abstract: Sustainable maritime transportation requires electrical systems that are reliable, energy-efficient, and capable of integrating cleaner energy sources. This study develops and evaluates a small-scale hybrid power prototype that combines a 50 Wp photovoltaic (PV) source as the renewable-energy component with a mini steam power source as a complementary generator, using an ESP32 microcontroller, INA219 sensors, MPPT control, a buck-boost converter, and relay-based automatic switching. The experimental program included static component verification and dynamic tests under changing solar irradiance, steam pressure, source-transfer conditions, smartphone monitoring, and 180-minute battery-charging cycles. The PV source produced 11.1–19.7 V and 0.8–2.6 A depending on weather conditions, while the mini steam source became stable from approximately 20 psi and produced 23.3–24.5 V and 2.2–2.5 A between 20 and 50 psi. Automatic source switching occurred in approximately 0.2 s in all five trials. Both charging paths raised battery voltage to 12.8 V at 90 min, after which charging was automatically disconnected. These results show that renewable-energy utilization can be strengthened by hybrid-source coordination, real-time monitoring, and energy storage to support continuity of power for maritime transportation. From a Vessel-to-Grid (V2G) perspective, the prototype demonstrates enabling …

title: Low‐Temperature Experimental Characterization of Magnetite‐Based Rock‐Bed Thermal Battery
abstract: ABSTRACT Rock bed thermal energy storage (RTES) systems are increasingly used as affordable and scalable solutions for low‐temperature heat storage. However, experimental investigations of magnetite packed beds under repeated charge–discharge cycles remain limited. This study experimentally evaluates the thermal performance of a horizontal cylindrical RTES system filled with magnetite and operated as a low‐temperature thermal battery for greenhouse applications. Two airflow strategies are compared over two successive cycles of charging and discharging: (i) unidirectional airflow during both charging and discharging (Model 1) and (ii) reversed airflow during discharge (Model 2). Thermal performance is analyzed through temperature stratification, heat transfer dynamics, energy recovery, and dimensionless performance indicators, including the Thermal Efficiency Index ( TEI ), Temperature Uniformity Index ( TUI ), Normalized Temperature Standard Deviation ( NTSD ), and Temperature Gradient Ratio ( TGR ). Results show that airflow reversal significantly enhances thermal propagation and heat extraction. Model 2 achieves a more pronounced thermal‐front response, generally higher TUI and TGR values, and higher energy recovery, delivering up to 30% more recovered heat during the first discharge period and approximately 15.79% more during the second discharge period compared with Model 1…

title: SLAFF: Shapley Local Attribution Feature Fusion with Bayesian-Optimized Ensemble Learning for Detecting Intrusions in Renewable Energy Power Systems
abstract: The incorporation of the internet into modern power systems has improved real-time communication, automation, and regulation but also heightened the risk of cyberattacks. Due to the continual generation of massive amounts of high-dimensional and heterogeneous data by these systems, it is difficult to differentiate between the many types of cyberattacks. Thus, this paper proposes a novel Shapley Local Attribution Feature Fusion (SLAFF) algorithm to select the subset of features based on Shapley values and the local attribution values. Initially, the training data are balanced using the oversampling technique. The SLAFF algorithm is implemented on the balanced dataset using only the training set to avoid data leakage. The different feature subsets are formed and trained using machine learning methods with the balanced and unbalanced datasets. The ensemble model is developed using the different ML algorithms and trained using the Bayesian optimization method. The highest accuracy is achieved by the ensemble model with 95.87% accuracy on the Kaggle Power System Intrusion dataset on 25 feature subsets and 95.36% accuracy on the Figshare Power System dataset on 40 feature subsets. Thus, implementing the proposed method will find discriminative features while preserving classification performance and offering an SLAFF method for power-system intrusion detection.

title: Digital Affordances and the Structuring of User Participation: A Case Study of LEGO’s Digital Platforms
abstract: Digital brand communication offers opportunities for action alongside information. This article examines how LEGO Ideas, LEGO Builder and BrickLink, including Studio, organise user participation. Drawing on relational affordance theory, it analyses eight official documents and a supplementary announcement on creator rewards, distinguishing platform features, documented action possibilities, and documented procedures and constraints. The comparison identifies three participation arrangements: submitting designs for company review, using digital guidance for physical assembly, and linking digital design with parts procurement and transaction feedback. These arrangements offer task-specific opportunities rather than a single progression towards deeper engagement. Action cues communicate these opportunities, task relevance explains their potential usefulness, and governance defines who can participate and who controls the results.

title: Social Belonging in Communication through Memes and Participation in Online Challenges
abstract: Abstract: This article presents a literature review on the topic of how social belonging is expressed, both in communication through memes and in participation in online challenges. The topic is highly relevant, given how prevalent memes and online challenges are in the digital sphere – particularly on social media. Furthermore, there is a lack of research on this issue, as well as scarcity of literature on them and a lack of comparative analysis regarding how social belonging manifests itself in each case. The methodology includes a desk study and analysis of selected memes. The aim of this literature review is to examine how social belonging manifests itself in communication via memes and in participation in online challenges, and whether it differs in any way. It is hypothesised that social belonging manifests itself differently in the two cases. The article presents examples of studies that examine how communication through memes and participation in online challenges serve as a means of satisfying this vital human need, and highlights the differences in how this need manifests in each case. The literature review reveals that both phenomena satisfy the need for social belonging, but do so in different ways. Through memes, belonging manifests itself through identification with a shared experience, whilst participation in online challenges builds it through joint activities. …

title: Physicochemical and Oxidative Quality Changes in Beef During Refrigerated Storage at 4 °C
abstract: The quality of raw meat is crucial for consumer acceptance, food safety, and nutritional value, yet it deteriorates rapidly even under refrigeration due to ongoing biochemical processes. This study aimed to evaluate the quality of beef stored at 4 °C by integrating conventional physicochemical parameters with oxidative stability indicators, in order to estimate the storage period during which refrigerated beef retains acceptable oxidative and physicochemical quality. pH, water activity (aw), colour parameters (CIE L*, a*, and b* of both inner and outer surfaces), thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), and protein carbonyl levels were monitored over a 20-day storage period. pH increased significantly throughout storage (p < 0.05), rising from 5.15 on day 0 to 6.52 on day 20. Although water activity values showed statistically significant variation (p < 0.05), the numerical range remained narrow (0.933–0.947), indicating no practically meaningful change in free water content. Among colour parameters, the outer surface a* value declined markedly, reaching its lowest point on day 10 (9.57 ± 1.47), while b* values increased progressively, reflecting concurrent pigment degradation and lipid oxidation. Lipid and protein oxidation remained relatively limited during the first three days for lipid oxidation and five days for protein oxidation but accelerated substantially…

title: Evaluation of the collection and storage of packed red blood cells in ferrets
abstract: Abstract Background Blood transfusion is lifesaving in anaemic ferrets, but species‐specific blood‐banking systems are lacking, and optimal storage conditions for packed red blood cells (pRBCs) have not been established. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the bacteriological, biochemical and haematological stability of pRBC stored in citrate‒phosphate‒dextrose‒adenine (CPDA) at 4°C over 28 days. Methods Blood samples (15 mL) were collected monthly from four healthy adult male ferrets over six months, yielding 24 samples. pRBCs were isolated by centrifugation and stored at 4°C in CPDA‐containing vacuum tubes. Weekly assessments included bacteriological cultures, pH, glucose, lactate, electrolytes, complete blood counts and erythrocyte morphology. Equivalence testing was used to assess changes over time. Results Most bacterial cultures yielded no growth. Serratia marcescens and Microbacterium spp. were considered to be post‐collection contaminants. pRBC stored at 4°C showed progressive deterioration, with decreases in glucose concentration and pH, increases in lactate and potassium concentrations, increased mean corpuscular volume, decreased mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration and marked echinocytosis by day 28. Plasma stored at −18°C remained stable. Limitations The small sample size, use of vacuum tubes and dilution for biochemical analysis may limit generalisability.…

title: Deciphering Crystal Structure‐Lithium Storage Behaviors in Niobium Tungsten Oxides Toward High‐Power Lithium‐Ion Capacitors
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion capacitors (LICs) bridge the gap between batteries and supercapacitors, offering high energy/power density and long cycle life. However, their practical performance is limited by the scarcity of battery‐type anodes combining fast lithium‐storage kinetics with structural robustness, and by the difficulty of matching such anodes with capacitive cathodes of comparable rate capability. Here, a family of niobium tungsten oxides with distinct crystal structures, Wadsley–Roth phases (Nb 12 WO 33 , Nb 14 W 3 O 44 , and Nb 16 W 5 O 55 ) and a tungsten‐bronze phase (Nb 18 W 16 O 93 ), are systematically evaluated as high‐rate anodes. Their open frameworks endow high lithium intercalation potentials (1.57–1.67 V vs. Li/Li + ) and excellent rate capability. Among these, Nb 16 W 5 O 55 exhibits the lowest lithium‐ion migration energy barrier (0.15 eV), reflecting superior lithium‐storage kinetics. Pairing Nb 16 W 5 O 55 with capacitive carbon cathodes yields high‐performance LICs in both aqueous and organic systems: the aqueous Nb 16 W 5 O 55 //APDC device delivers 62.8 Wh kg −1 at 3.3 kW kg −1 , while the optimized organic Nb 16 W 5 O 55 ‐CNT//GO device operates over 0.01–3.7 V, achieving an ultrahigh energy density of 300.6 Wh kg −1 and a maximum power density of 33.3 kW kg −1 , with excellent rate capability and cycling stability. This work elucidates the structure–k…

title: Changes in Major Aromatic Compounds of Roasted Coffee Bean Powder During Storage Using Colorimetric Sensor Array
abstract: Aroma is one of the most important factors in the quality of coffee. A colorimetric sensor array (CSA) that gives a pattern of responses to the coffee aroma was used to follow changes during storage. The response of the array to four major aroma compounds of coffee, furfuryl alcohol, dimethyl trisulfide, 2,3-butanedione and 2,3-pentanedione, was examined first, and the four compounds proved distinguishable by their response patterns in hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA). The changes in volatile constituents of coffee during storage at 4 and 25 °C were studied. The response patterns of the stored samples were examined by principal component analysis (PCA). The samples became less distinguishable from one another as the storage period lengthened, converging in the score plots from day 10 at 4 °C and from day 5 at 25 °C. This behavior is consistent with a loss of aroma freshness during storage. GC-MS was used to quantify individual aroma compounds in the stored samples. These results show that the colorimetric sensor array has potential as a rapid indication of the overall state of coffee aroma during storage, complementing the quantitative analysis of individual compounds by GC-MS.

title: Predicting Adoption Intention of Electric Vehicles: Mediating Effect of Attitude
abstract: Environmental pollution remains a global problem at present. One of the main sources of air pollution is toxic emissions from traditional vehicles powered by fossil fuels. Electric vehicles (EVs) are aggressively promoted globally to resolve environmental concerns, minimize the after-effects of emissions and reduce dependency on fossil fuels. Greenhouse emissions and fuel usage in transportation may be greatly reduced by EVs. Thus, the objective of this research is to identify the variables affecting Indian consumers’ intentions to adopt EVs by utilizing an enhanced version of the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology with an additional variable, trust. The mediating role of attitude was assessed to predict the adoption intentions of EVs. Data were gathered from 418 respondents using a standardized questionnaire. Variance-based structural equation modelling was employed to validate the suggested theoretical framework. The results revealed that trust is the second most significant construct that influences the adoption intentions of EVs after attitude, followed by performance expectancy and social influence. It is confirmed that attitude partially mediates the impact of trust, performance expectancy and social influence on EV adoption intention, whereas attitude is found to fully mediate the relation between facilitating conditions and EV adoption intention. Therefo…

title: Resistance hysteresis and pitch instability mechanisms of an air-cushion vehicle during unsteady acceleration
Star-like topologies enhance the charging power of quantum batteries
abstract: Abstract Quantum batteries are quantum systems that store energy and deliver it on demand, and their practical value hinges on how fast they can be charged. While collective charging protocols and global control are known to enhance charging power, it remains unclear how the battery’s internal interaction architecture itself constrains performance. Here we study interacting fermionic batteries whose internal couplings are encoded by a graph adjacency matrix and which are charged through a uniform interaction with an external fermionic device. We prove that the star topology uniquely maximizes the initial slope of the charging power at zero local field. At finite field, we derive an exact spectral criterion for outperforming the star and construct a star-like family that satisfies it. Based on numerically established correlation, we expect these findings to extend to the maximal average charging power as well. To confirm the dominance of the star architecture, we complement the analysis by an exhaustive sweep over all connected graphs with N ≤ 7 vertices, and by largerrandom-graph benchmarks.

title: Blackberry juice as a vehicle of potential probiotic bacteria isolated from aguamiel, blackberry, and pulque: consortium analysis and kinetic growth
abstract: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are widely recognized as probiotics, offering various health benefits. The hypothesis that the formation of bacterial consortia enhances these health benefits is based on the premise that synergistic interactions between strains increase viability and metabolic activity. The aim of this study was to examine the interactions between LAB strains isolated from aguamiel, blackberry, and pulque to assess their probiotic potential and incorporation into blackberry juice. Previously isolated LAB strains from three samples of aguamiel, blackberry, and pulque were used. The identification of these strains was facilitated by using an API kit. As a result, 16 distinct co-cultures were established, each composed of three unique strains. A total of four co-cultures exhibited growth of all strains through mutualistic interactions. These co-cultures (Co-1, Co-6, Co-11 and Co-13), were considered bacterial consortia and were selected for the evaluation of growth kinetics in MRS medium and blackberry juice fermentation. These strains showed a reduced exponential phase, allowing them to reach the stationary phase more quickly. This accelerated adaptation suggests that LAB consortia can adjust more effectively to new environmental conditions, suggesting their potential use as probiotics for functional beverage applications.

Sim-to-Real: A multi-stage transfer learning method for thermal error modeling of electric spindles
abstract: Thermal error is a major factor limiting the machining accuracy of electric spindle systems. Accurate thermal error modeling (TEM) is therefore essential for precision improvement. However, data-driven neural networks often suffer from performance degradation due to limited real-world training data and increasing model complexity. In practical machining scenarios, acquiring sufficient measured data is challenging because real-time tool tracking is difficult to achieve. To address this issue, this paper proposes a sim-to-real multi-stage transfer learning framework for thermal error prediction under limited-data conditions. First, a thermodynamic model of the electric spindle is constructed to generate large-scale simulation data that are physically consistent with real working conditions. Second, a multi-scale residual network (MSRN) is developed to extract hierarchical thermal features through parallel multi-scale convolutional layers and residual connections. Third, a multi-stage transfer strategy is designed to progressively bridge the gap between simulation and real-world data by sequential pretraining on simulated data, intermediate adaptation using historical measurements with partial layer freezing, and final fine-tuning using limited target-domain samples. The proposed method is evaluated on six transfer tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that it consistently outpe…

title: Cell-type dependence of effects from transcranial electric brain stimulation
abstract: There is an urgent need for better treatment options for many neurological conditions, including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, depression, and epilepsy. Transcranial electrical stimulation (tES) is a non-invasive, safe, inexpensive, and promising method that could address some of this unmet need. The therapeutic value of tES has been well demonstrated, but the effect is highly variable. To enable tES to reach its full potential requires a better understanding of how tES modulates neural activity so that tES treatments can be tailored to specific neurological conditions and individual patients. The neural response to tES is, however, highly complex, and the parameter space involved in optimizing tES treatments is daunting. This has made it difficult to obtain general insights into how tES modulates neural activity, and a central challenge lies in the cell-type-specific and frequency-dependent nature of these responses. In this study, we investigated cell-type-specific neuronal responses to tES over a broad frequency range, using a large database of biophysically detailed neuron models. We found that pyramidal cells respond strongly to low-frequency tES, but their responses drop sharply with frequency. In contrast, inhibitory neurons show a smaller reduction and, on average, become more responsive than pyramidal cells above ~ 60 Hz. By leveraging a reciprocity theorem…

title: A virtual reality simulator for electric wheelchair driving training
abstract: Driving an electric wheelchair requires motor coordination, spatial perception and quick reactions to obstacles, particularly challenging for people with mobility impairments. Traditional training methods have several limitations, including large physical spaces, constant supervision, equipment wear and the high cost of electric wheelchairs, which restricts their availability in rehabilitation contexts. This work presents the development of a Virtual Reality simulator for electric wheelchair driving training, providing a safe, immersive environment where users can practise without risk of injury and at their own pace. The project follows an Action Research methodology, in collaboration with the Associação de Paralisia Cerebral de Braga. It is developed in the Unity game engine and supports virtual reality headsets and desktop input devices. In contrast to existing solutions, the proposed simulator is natively developed in Portuguese, freely available to the partner rehabilitation institution and organised around a progressive curriculum of ten indoor and outdoor training levels, complemented by a freestyle mode and gamification mechanics to sustain motivation. The system has been integrated with the Meta Quest 3 headset, running at a stable frame rate for smooth, responsive interaction while avoiding factors that may induce cybersickness. The system also records each patient’s …

title: Schedule-Informed Empty-Vehicle Dispatching for OHT Systems in Semiconductor Manufacturing
abstract: Overhead hoist transport (OHT) performance affects the execution of semiconductor production schedules because transport delays postpone subsequent operations. This study develops the Scheduler and OHT Allocation Monitoring Simulator (SOMOS), an event-driven environment that integrates machine processing, transport request generation, OHT movement, and subsequent production execution. Based on SOMOS, we propose Schedule-informed Empty-Vehicle Dispatching (SEVD), which repositions idle OHT vehicles before pickup requests occur using immediate pickup demand, remaining processing information, and a schedule-derived spatial demand prior. SEVD retains the conventional HUNGARIAN assignment procedure for actual requests. Experiments compare SEVD with six benchmark dispatching methods over 20 paired seeds. Relative to HUNGARIAN assignment, SEVD reduces the mean post-assignment empty-approach travel from 96.82 s to 71.23 s and source wait p90 from 428.74 s to 399.34 s while maintaining production-level performance comparable to the strongest benchmarks. These gains are obtained by redistributing vehicle movement toward proactive repositioning, with total empty travel increasing by 17.8% and total travel distance by 6.8%. Fleet size and ablation experiments further show that the clearest benefit is associated with proactive spatial repositioning rather than precise temporal prediction. T…

title: In Situ Second Harmonic Generation (SHG) Studies of Surface Electric Field on Cobalt Oxide Electrodes
abstract: Cobalt oxide/hydroxide is considered to be an efficient electrochemical (EC) catalyst, and the surface electric field may partly explain this efficiency. The space-charge electric field influences the surface electric field due to electron/hole separation and accumulation in the space-charge layer; charge carriers may then participate in chemical reactions, or the surface electric field may polarize molecules for reactions. The surface electric field can be probed in situ by electric field-induced second harmonic generation (EFISH); however, the EFISH technique remains underdeveloped for catalyst systems beyond TiO 2 . This work focuses on developing the EFISH method to detect the surface electric field of Co-based electrocatalyst thin films. An optical electrochemical cell and a second harmonic generation (SHG) setup were built, and the EFISH response of Co/Co(hydr)oxide/electrolyte samples was measured. In situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), Raman spectroscopy, and chronoamperometry were also used to explain their electrochemical and physical properties. This work provides a method for calculating the surface electric field and helps to understand EFISH signal generation, which contributes to the further development of EFISH applied to electrocatalysis.

title: The myth of institutional neutrality: A dangerous climate obstruction strategy
abstract: Promoting the idea of institutional neutrality is a misleading and dangerous climate obstruction strategy. Within the financialised universities of the United States, institutional neutrality is a myth because it fails to acknowledge how research institutes and climate research agendas, have been - and continue to be, heavily influenced by corporate, military and political interests. This myth conceals how powerful interests have invested in universities to legitimate climate denial, delay fossil fuel phaseout, and distract away from climate concern. Corporate capture of universities has not only limited what kind of climate research is conducted and dampened societal responses to the climate crisis. It has also contributed to growing mistrust in scientific research and eroded the public good mission of higher education institutions. Instead of reinforcing the myth of institutional neutrality, higher education institutions need to reclaim their public good mission and recommit to engaging directly with urgent community needs to collectively prepare society for the turbulent times ahead.

title: Polylactic co-glycolic acid (PLGA)-based nanoparticles encapsulating Persea americana seed extract: A potential therapeutic strategy against oxidative stress and diabetes in rat model
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia arising from insulin resistance or impaired insulin secretion. Conventional and commercially available effective antidiabetic drugs are often associated with adverse effects and reduced efficacy over prolonged use, highlighting the need for safer and plant-based alternatives. Persea americana seed extract (PSE) has antidiabetic potential but suffers from non-specific distribution and poor bioavailability, thus limiting its clinical application. This study developed and evaluated the poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles encapsulating Persea americana seed extract (PSENP) to enhance therapeutic efficacy and delivery. Nanoparticles were characterized for zeta size, zeta potential, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), stability and their phytochemical composition, with HPLC confirming the presence of bioactive compounds including quercetin, syringic acid, and gallic acid. In-vivo , forty wistar rats were allocated into five groups: normal control, diabetic control, metformin-treated, PSE-treated, and PSENP-treated. Biochemical parameters were evaluated including fasting blood glucose, insulin (serum level), lipid profile, oxidative stress biomarkers (superoxide dismutase, catalase), and inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α). Histopathological examination of pancreatic tissue …

title: Electrical Surface Polarization as a Functionalization Strategy to Improve Bone Regeneration of Apatite‐Based Graft Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Apatite‐based bone graft materials are widely used for bone repair; however, their limited bioactivity and slow remodeling often hinder replacement by newly formed bone. Electrical surface polarization has emerged as a promising strategy for modifying the surface properties of apatite‐based biomaterials without altering their chemical composition. This study investigated whether different degrees of electrical polarization produce distinct biological responses in apatite‐based materials. Synthesized carbonate apatite (CA) was used for mechanistic in vitro evaluation, whereas a clinically relevant xenograft material was employed for in vivo validation. Material characterization confirmed the formation of B‐type CA with a bone‐like mineral composition. Thermally stimulated depolarization current measurements verified successful induction of surface charges, with polarization intensity dependent on treatment conditions. In vitro studies using human peripheral blood‐derived osteoclast precursors demonstrated that electrically polarized CA surfaces significantly enhanced osteoclast differentiation and resorptive activity compared with nonpolarized controls, with the strongest effects observed under higher polarization conditions. Increased resorption pit depth and volume further indicated enhanced osteoclast functionality. In vivo implantation of polarized xenograft materia…

title: Baveno VI criteria validation and development of a new non-invasive strategy for varices rule-out in patients with HCC (SAPHE-R: Stiffness, ALBI, Platelets, HEpatocellular carcinoma Rule)
abstract: Background and Aims: Accuracy of Baveno criteria for avoiding endoscopy in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is uncertain, and systematic upper gastrointestinal endoscopy (UGE) may not be necessary. We evaluated Baveno VI criteria performance in this population and developed an alternative non-invasive rule to exclude esophagogastric varices of any grade, rather than high-risk varices (HRV). Methods: Patients with BCLC 0-C HCC and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) from Italian Liver Cancer (ITA.LI.CA) database, with available liver stiffness measurement (LSM), UGE, and blood tests within six months of diagnosis, were included. Independent predictors of varices identified by logistic regression were combined through grid-search to derive a rule-out strategy (SAPHE-R), validated by bootstrap-resampling and in an independent cohort (Vienna). Results: The derivation cohort comprised 598 patients (age, 69 years; male sex, 75.3%; viral etiology, 69.3%; BCLC 0/A, 77.9%; ALBI 1, 54.2%; varices, 33.4%; HRV, 11.2%). Baveno VI criteria missed 8.5% of varices and 6.0% of HRV, sparing 31.1% of UGE. Independent predictors of varices were incorporated into SAPHE-R (LSM≤16 kPa, platelet count ≥160×10⁹/L, ALBI grade 1), which missed 4.0% of varices (HRV 3.0%, spared UGE 17.6%). Perumda Tirta Pakuan's Public Relations Communication Strategy Based on Wilson & Ogden's Model via Instagram to Enhance Public Transparency in Water Services
abstract: Public transparency is essential in water service management to maintain public trust. However, a communication gap remains between public information needs and institutional delivery through digital platforms. Although Instagram is increasingly used by public service organizations, studies that specifically examine the application of Wilson Ogden's communication strategy model in the context of regional water utility (PDAM) public relations remain limited, particularly in Indonesia. This study aims to analyze the communication strategy of the Public Relations of Perumda Tirta Pakuan Bogor City in utilizing Instagram to enhance public transparency, as well as to identify challenges and solutions. Data were collected during a four-month internship through direct observation, participant observation, in-depth interviews, and literature review. The findings reveal that the PR team systematically applied Wilson Ogden's four-phase framework. In the formative research phase, frequent public inquiries regarding water disruptions indicated an information gap, leading to a strategy focused on delivering clear and consistent updates. The tactics phase involved the use of Instagram features such as feeds, reels, and direct messages, with three specific content formats: Tirta Pakuan Content Update (real-time service conditions), SIGAP Content (visualization of complaint handling), and Tirt…
