title: Study on Power-Law Singularity Precursory Characteristics of Catastrophic Failure of Deep Coal–Rock Under Real-Time Unloading
abstract: Deep coal–rock excavation under high stress may induce dynamic disasters. This study conducted real-time unloading tests on coal and sandstone using DIC and power-law singularity modeling. The results indicate that the evolution of strain rate consists of three stages; pre-catastrophe strain rate accelerates in a power-law manner (β→–1). Strain localization is the physical origin of singularity. Sandstone exhibits larger strain-rate amplitudes than coal, with distinct spatial distributions of β. These findings provide quantitative, lithology-sensitive precursory criteria for early warning of catastrophic instability in deep rock engineering. Compared with previous studies that applied power-law singularity analysis and DIC separately, mostly under quasi-static compression, the novelty of this work lies in (i) investigating the real-time drilling-unloading path of excavation on intact coal and sandstone specimens under high-stress holding conditions, (ii) combining the temporal power-law singularity analysis with a full-field strip-based strain-localization analysis to quantify both the temporal and spatial evolution of the singularity exponent β, and (iii) providing lithology-dependent β ranges as quantitative precursors. In summary, the study reveals the unloading mechanism and precursor characteristics of catastrophic failure in deep coal and sandstone excavation, providing v…

title: Technological Voice: Technology as Power, Freedom, And Transformation in Christina Dalcher’s Master Class
abstract: Technology and gender are inextricably linked, and technology systems can serve as instruments of patriarchal control and as resources through which women express agency and resistance. This study focuses on Technofeminism to examine the relationship between gender and technology in Christina Dalcher’s Master Class. Technofeminism argues that technology is woven into social interactions and power systems, while also highlighting women’s ability to negotiate and appropriate technological resources. This study analyses the technofeminist dimensions of Master Class through three factors: Technology as Patriarchal, Technological Freedom, and Technological Transformation. The methodology employed is a qualitative textual analysis of the novel, examining the Q system as a form of technological classification, patriarchal power, and gendered control. It also explores how women utilise technological resources to access knowledge, agency, and resistance to institutional authority. This study investigates Elena’s experience in a technologically mediated culture, emphasising her experience with the Q system, prenatal Q testing, digital information, and institutional expectations. This study reveals that technology in Master Class is a medium of control and also a source of agency, and that women negotiate identity, power and resistance in technologically mediated social relations. title: Algorithmic Editorial Power: AI, Capital, and Journalistic Autonomy in Smart Newsrooms
Long term survival model with frailt terms based on the power variance function family
abstract: Abstract We present a new class of survival models that combine unobserved population heterogeneity and cured individuals by incorporating frailty terms from the Power Variance Function (PVF) family, referred to as PVF-Induced Defective (PVF-ID) models. This structure broadens classic frailty theory and defective lifetimes under a proportional-hazards lens, letting researchers flexibly track long-term survivors in mixed cohorts. Inference follows a full-Bayesian routine run via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, and key frequentist properties are cross-checked using simulation studies. When applied to HIV/AIDS records, the model reliably pinpoints important covariates and quantifies the fraction of cured patients. In this case study, among several baseline hazards, the simple exponential form wins by both leave-plus-one marginal likelihood (LPML) and raw marginal likelihood. Together, these findings position the PVF-ID framework as a robust, versatile toolbox for studying survival data with immune subpopulations.

title: Review of Insulation Ageing and Lifecycle Management for Oil‐Immersed Power Equipment: From Conventional Testing Analysis to Artificial Intelligence Method
abstract: ABSTRACT Oil‐immersed power equipment is a critical component for energy transmission and secure operation of modern power grids. The ageing of oil–paper insulation under combined electrical, thermal and mechanical stresses directly affects equipment lifetime and system reliability. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the ageing behaviour and full‐lifecycle management technologies of oil–paper insulation in oil‐immersed power equipment. First, the structural characteristics of oil–paper insulation and its microscopic ageing mechanisms under multi‐stress conditions are analysed. Subsequently, lifetime calculation models under electrical, thermal, and electro–thermal–mechanical coupled stresses, together with their recent application progress, are systematically summarised. Ageing condition assessment and remaining useful life prediction methods based on characteristic parameter testing and multiphysics techniques are then reviewed, followed by an overview of recent advances in ageing‐state visualisation and dynamic evolution analysis. Finally, this paper discusses artificial intelligence‐oriented intelligent operation and maintenance (O&M) systems, digital twin (DT) modelling and knowledge graph applications. Based on the review, this paper further discusses future research directions, including lifetime degradation mechanisms and dynamic prediction of oil–paper insula…

title: Achieving Sustainable Development Goals in Türkiye: Central Government Strategy Through a Cherry‐Picking Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Countries have differing priorities in the process of achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Examining how these priorities are reflected in national strategies facilitates the interpretation of future actions. The literature on SDGs achievement in Türkiye has largely been limited to municipalities, universities, and sectoral institutions. No study addresses the entire central administration, which is at the heart of national policy‐making. Aiming to address this gap, this study conducts a content analysis of the 2024–2028 strategic plans of 84 central administrations in Türkiye and evaluates the intended contribution, sustainability contexts, and performance measurement tools through a cherry‐picking approach. Across these forward‐looking plans, intended contribution is most prevalent for SDG 16 (98% of plans) and lowest for the ecological SDGs 6, 13, 14, and 15 (5%–29%), reflecting planned priorities rather than achieved outcomes. Central governments address sustainability as an institutional structure rather than a broad vision and measure success primarily through output‐level rather than outcome or impact indicators. The results indicate that the selective approach is also valid in the Turkish central government and that the biosphere aspect of sustainability is neglected. The study suggests making a roadmap for climate action mandatory in strategic p…

title: The Fragmentation of Material Flows: Mapping Barriers to Circular Economy Adoption in Bangladesh's Ready‐Made Garment Sector
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper provides an empirical diagnosis of the systemic challenges preventing the transition to a circular economy (CE) in Bangladesh's ready‐made garment (RMG) sector. Drawing on in‐depth interviews ( n = 13) with key industry stakeholders, the study characterises current waste flows and analyses the barriers to circularity. Findings reveal a predominantly linear material flow dominated by informal networks and constrained by a lack of traceability, limited recycling infrastructure and weak policy support. The study identifies power asymmetry between global brands and local manufacturers as one of four interacting ‘lock‐in’ mechanisms, alongside institutional voids, infrastructural and technological constraints and traceability failure, that together prevent the industry from moving beyond fragmented, linear practices. This structural governance failure actively inhibits progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 12, particularly Targets 12.5 and 12.6. Based on the multilevel perspective, supplemented by institutional theory and the resource‐based view, the analysis argues that the current linear production regime is maintained by institutional voids and internal resource constraints that must be addressed before prescriptive solutions can be operationalised. The empirical scope centres on postproduction and preconsumer waste governance; postconsumer textile wast…

title: A high-performance artificial lemming algorithm with multi-strategy synergetic search for complex engineering optimization
Reframing Stakeholder Roles in Multistakeholder Partnerships: A Role Theory Approach to Collaborative Action on Food Waste
abstract: ABSTRACT Multistakeholder partnerships (MSPs) are promoted as collaborative arrangements to address food waste, yet most research focuses on core stakeholders directly involved in food production and consumption, leaving the roles of supporting stakeholders underexplored. This study redirects attention to these vital actors, such as governmental bodies, financial institutions, and industry associations, whose engagement can be important to initiating, stabilizing, and sustaining collaboration. Drawing on role theory, we examine the case of Food Waste Free United in the Netherlands through interviews and secondary data. We identify four dynamic role orientations enacted by supporting stakeholders: mediator, facilitator, supporter, and influencer. Each role embodies distinct practices, ranging from building trust and establishing data sharing arrangements to mobilizing networks, shaping policy, and strengthening capabilities, which can contribute to the stability and effectiveness of MSPs. Our analysis further reveals that motivations to engage extend beyond external pressure, encompassing a search for embeddedness within the partnership ecosystem and opportunities for learning. By applying role theory, we advance understanding of how supporting stakeholders enable MSPs to move beyond fragile arrangements toward sustained, systemic impact. These insights offer theoretical contrib…

title: Digital Visibility Optimization: Seo Article Strategy And Impact On Website Traffic At PT. Tourezia Inspira Cakra
abstract: The post-pandemic recovery of the tourism and event industry has intensified competition among service providers, particularly in terms of digital visibility. This condition encourages companies to optimize search engine–based marketing strategies to reach potential customers effectively. This study aims to analyze the implementation of Search Engine Optimization (SEO) article strategies and examine their relationship with website traffic performance at PT Tourezia Cakra Inspira during the observation period from February to July 2025.This study adopts a qualitative descriptive approach using a case study design. Data were collected through direct observation, interviews with the SEO supervisor, and secondary data analysis obtained from Google Analytics and Google Search Console. The analysis focuses on the SEO article writing process, website traffic patterns, and internal factors influencing organic traffic performance. The findings indicate that PT Tourezia Cakra Inspira has implemented SEO article strategies through a systematic process, including keyword research, content planning, article writing, on-page optimization, and performance monitoring. SEO articles function as initial entry points that direct users to the company’s core service pages, particularly event services. title: Propagation of Uncertainty in Multi-Source Elevation Models into Hydrological Modelling and Sediment Connectivity in a Loess Catchment
abstract: The accuracy and resolution of digital elevation models (DEMs) determine the reliability of outputs used in hydrological modeling. However, an assessment of their suitability should not be limited to vertical accuracy alone. Particularly in small, highly fragmented catchments, uncertainty in elevation representation can propagate to subsequent derivatives depending on the local topographic structure and, consequently, influence the interpretation of runoff organization and sediment transport. The aim of this study is to determine how differences between multi-source elevation models propagate from the underlying elevation representation through slope and runoff organization to the drainage network and the spatial pattern of sediment connectivity. In the Stocki Creek catchment in the Lublin Uplands (SE Poland), ASTER GDEM, SRTM, EU-DEM, and a local TIN model were compared. Aerial laser scanning (ALS) data were used as a high-resolution reference for validating elevation and derived outputs. Vertical accuracy was assessed using RMSE and NMAD, and then the representation of relief, slope, hydrologic routing outputs, the drainage network, and the Sediment Connectivity Index (SCI) were compared. The smallest discrepancies relative to ALS were obtained for the TIN (RMSE 1.48 m; NMAD 0.41 m), and the largest for ASTER (6.78 m; 2.37 m). Errors were highest in forested areas. All models…

title: Calibrating clinical reasoning under uncertainty: a qualitative study of expert physiotherapists in musculoskeletal practice
“There’s more that we don’t know than we do know”: Unpacking uncertainty in bariatric surgery
abstract: Bariatric surgery remains the “gold standard” treatment for obesity, according to the American College of Surgeons in 2025; however, while evidence shows that surgery can improve health and increase lifespan for many, most available data focus on short-term outcomes, and high-quality long-term research remains limited. Furthermore, patients and providers seemingly experience uncertainty regarding postoperative outcomes, frequently attributing suboptimal results to each other. To explore these uncertainties alongside broader elements of the surgical experience, we conducted semi-structured qualitative interviews with Canadian women who had received surgery at least 1 year prior and registered dietitians who currently or previously worked in bariatric surgery in Canada, using reflexive thematic analysis and thinking with theory to analyze data. We constructed three themes: (1) Surgical uncertainty and “misplaced” optimism; (2) Promise of certainty through pathologization; and (3) (Dis)honesty: Nondisclosure as uncertainty management. We argue that bariatric professionals must engage more transparently with uncertainty and evidentiary gaps to mitigate medical bias and provide more meaningful support to patients considering or living with the outcomes of the procedure.

title: Determining Social License to Operate: Design of Experiments, Uncertainty Characterization and Historical Consistency Assessment of a Hybrid Simulation Model for a LatAm Green Hydrogen Project
abstract: Uruguay’s largest green-hydrogen initiative—an integrated e-fuels complex proposed for the Department of Paysandú—is approaching its final investment decision amid a public debate centered on water use, land occupation and community acceptance. Building on a peer-reviewed formulation in which social acceptance acts as an operational moderator of the local economy, this article reports the experimental, uncertainty and corroboration program of a hybrid System Dynamics and agent-based territorial impact model: a replicated factorial design, two global sensitivity campaigns, a 1000-replication Monte Carlo campaign, policy isolation studies, a feasibility assessment under editable thresholds, and a 2010–2022 historical backcast. In the simulations, capacity raises income only jointly with external demand (interaction: 21.2% of variance), while employment responds primarily to the public-investment rate (55.1%). Two behavioral parameters—the rates at which community trust builds and erodes—rank highest for every output (PRCC 0.74–0.96); as these are judgment parameters, the quantitative conclusions are conditional on their declared ranges, and their empirical calibration through a longitudinal design is identified as the priority. Acceptance declines monotonically across the sampled capacity range and the outcome distribution is bimodal, so policy is read as shifting the probability…

title: A novel software clustering approach-based on large-scale many-objective optimization for object-oriented systems
abstract: Abstract Large-scale many-objective optimization problems (LSMaOPs) present a significant challenge for conventional evolutionary algorithms when trying to find optimal solutions. To overcome the limitations of conventional evolutionary algorithms in handling LSMaOPs, various improved algorithms, known as large-scale many-objective optimization algorithms (LSMaOAs), have been introduced. However, real-world LSMaOPs, particularly Large-Scale Many-Objective Software Clustering Problems (LSMaSCPs), demand more effective optimization approach. This paper introduces an Information Feedback Model (IFM) based LSMaOA called Large-scale Many-Objective Harmony Search (LSMaHS) designed to tackle the LSMaSCPs. To evaluate the performance of different variants of LSMaHS, they are tested on five different LSMaSCP instances and compared with existing LSMaOAs. The experimental results demonstrate that the variants LSMaHS-F1 and LSMaHS-R1 significantly outperform existing approaches, especially on more than 12 and 8 test problems out of 20 test problems, respectively. Thus, the proposed approach can assist software engineers more effectively in improving the maintainability and modularity of large applications.

title: FedSTIP-Tuning: Federated Black-Box Prompt Tuning with Aggregate-Only Feedback and Common-Candidate Optimization
abstract: Federated black-box prompt tuning enables organizations to adapt a proprietary frozen language model without centralizing their labeled data, but local search-state aggregation does not directly define a shared pooled-data objective, and client-specific feedback can expose private signals. We propose FedSTIP-Tuning, which composes a three-party permutation-based protected forward propagation with a common-candidate population and pairwise-masked loss aggregation in a cross-silo setting. All participating clients evaluate the same prompt candidates, and the coordinator ranks their sample-weighted aggregate losses, thereby optimizing the empirical objective over the fixed union of client shards under full participation. Under the stated semi-honest and non-collusion assumptions, the aggregation layer hides each released loss vector’s client-level decomposition, while the aggregate values and execution metadata remain observable to their authorized parties. On RoBERTa-large, FedSTIP-Tuning exceeds the strongest evaluated FedBPT configuration by 6.40, 2.66, and 7.60 percentage points on AG News, SST-2, and DBpedia, respectively, under matched forward budgets. Its protected forward preserves all candidate rankings across 600 paired generations and is 861× and 957× faster than a generic interactive two-party computation reference on the RoBERTa-base warm and cold paths, and 694× and …

title: Constraint-Based Wing Planform Sizing of a Fixed-Wing UAV Using an AVL–ANN Surrogate and Artificial Bee Colony Optimization
abstract: Choosing a wing for a fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is seldom about maximizing one aerodynamic figure of merit alone. The planform also has to stay stable and live within the limits of the propulsion system. This paper sizes the wing at the conceptual stage from two variables, the span (b) and the chord (c), through a constraint-based workflow. Each candidate first passes a fast feasibility screen for the stall limit, stall speed, wing loading, and power demand under a fixed mass model, a 50 km/h cruise, the motor power ceiling, and standard atmospheric conditions, with a further Reynolds-based realism filter. Wings that survive are analyzed in AVL, a Vortex Lattice Method (VLM) solver. For each one an operating point that meets the required lift is selected, and the lift-to-drag ratio (L/D) and the directional-stability derivative (Cnβ) are read at that point. A single feed-forward artificial neural network (ANN), a machine-learning surrogate mapping [b, c, AR, S] to [L/D, Cnβ], accelerates the search, after which an artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm maximizes a multi-objective index built on that surrogate. The direct AVL trade-off and the ANN+ABC search point to the same wing, b = 1.90 m and c = 0.24 m (S = 0.456 m², AR = 7.92), giving L/D ≈ 16.61 and Cnβ ≈ 0.241 at α = 12°, with every feasibility constraint met. Under leave-one-out cross-validation the surrog…

title: Optimization and multi-modal mechanistic elucidation of a composite cryoprotectants system for freeze-drying of Staphylococcus saprophyticus HS-42 and Meyerozyma guilliermondii LS-76 isolated from Xuanwei ham
Sequential Low-Light Image Enhancement Using Eigenvalue-Based Gamma Correction and Laplacian Feature Map-Based Transmission Map
abstract: Low-light images are typically captured under adverse conditions, such as nighttime environments or low-contrast settings, which severely hinder visual understanding and object recognition. Although various deep learning and image signal processing techniques have been proposed to address this issue, low-light image enhancement remains a challenging task due to the lack of ground-truth reference images and the diverse range of real-world degradation phenomena. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel low-light image enhancement framework utilizing an eigenvalue-based gamma correction method based on the ratio of the 1st and 2nd eigenvalues, which effectively captures the inherent characteristics of the input image. Furthermore, because image enhancement processes inevitably amplify background noise, this paper incorporates a specialized denoising method inspired by dehazing theory to mitigate this side effect. A critical challenge in mathematical dehazing models is the accurate estimation of the transmission map, which is often distorted by strong light components in low-light scenes, leading to undesirable halo effects and color distortion. To solve this, this paper introduces a Laplacian feature map-based transmission map, leveraging the fact that Laplacian edge components remain independent of ambient illumination. Extensive experimental evaluations demonst…

title: A IMPORTÂNCIA DA CONTROLADORIA FINANCEIRA NO PROCESSO DE TOMADA DE DECISÃO ESTRATÉGICA
abstract: Este artigo discute a contribuição da Controladoria Financeira para o processo de tomada de decisão estratégica nas organizações. Seu objetivo é destacar o papel da Controladoria Financeira na análise e no fornecimento de informações relevantes aos gestores, visando fundamentar decisões estratégicas. A metodologia adotada consiste em uma revisão bibliográfica, baseada em artigos científicos, livros e relatórios especializados nas áreas de auditoria e controladoria financeira. O referencial teórico abrange conceitos relacionados à Controladoria Financeira, à tomada de decisão estratégica e ao papel dos sistemas de informações contábeis. Os principais resultados indicam que a Controladoria Financeira contribui para o monitoramento gerencial e o fornecimento de informações que permitem identificar oportunidades e riscos, além de fundamentar decisões estratégicas com maior precisão. A análise e a interpretação dos dados financeiros possibilitam avaliar a viabilidade de investimentos, a rentabilidade de projetos e a eficácia das estratégias adotadas. Conclui-se que a Controladoria Financeira exerce uma função estratégica na gestão organizacional, permitindo que os gestores fundamentem suas decisões em informações confiáveis e consistentes. Essa prática contribui para a maximização dos resultados financeiros e o alcance dos objetivos estratégicos. Nesse contexto, investir em uma estr…

title: THE RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN AND FORENSIC PERMANENCE: NAVI-GATING THE TENSION BETWEEN DIGITAL ERASURE AND CRIMINAL JUS-TICE IN INDIA
abstract: The right to be forgotten is a key aspect of privacy in the digital era. It has given people the right to request erasure or delinking of personal data. The DPDP Act in India adds to the con-stitutional privacy framework laid down by the Supreme Court in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India with the new concept of erasure rights. This article will explore the conflict between what is erased and what is preserved in a digital world in criminal investigations. It contrasts the developing framework in India with that of the First Amendment of the United States. Article 17 of GDPR outlines a framework for erasure, but India will have to weigh the privacy rights enshrined in Article 21 of the Constitution against free speech rights under Article 19. The arti-cle examines the tension and conflict between forensic permanence and erasure claims, espe-cially in the context of criminal justice. Based on comparative analysis and doctrinal scholar-ship, the following article sets out a model that maintains investigative integrity while respect-ing privacy rights that we term the CLEAR Framework (Contextual Lawful Erasure with Ac-countability and Retention). It states that the framework should include elements of statutory clarity and procedural safeguards, technical specifications for delisting and deletion processes, and judicial safeguards specific to the Indian constitutional structure.

title: A lightweight reversible and attack resilient hybrid framework for secure medical image transmission
abstract: Abstract The increasing use of telemedicine, cloud-based radiology, and electronic health record (EHR) systems has intensified the need for secure and reversible medical image transmission. This paper proposes LDAHF (Lightweight Reversible and Attack-Resilient Hybrid Framework), which integrates transform-domain watermarking, reversible host-image recovery, standardized key derivation, authenticated encryption, and replay protection within a unified architecture. A $$16\times 16$$ binary watermark is spatially pre-scrambled using the Arnold Cat Map (ACM) with $$k=5$$ and embedded into the $$\text{LL}_{2}$$ sub-band of a two-level Integer Wavelet Transform (IWT) using parity quantization with $$T=20$$ . Three mutually distinct, key-dependent embedding locations are assigned to each watermark bit, and majority voting is employed during extraction. Embedding-induced coefficient residuals are preserved within the protected payload and used to restore the original $$\text{LL}_{2}$$ coefficients before inverse IWT reconstruction. HKDF-SHA-256 derives domain-separated encryption and embedding subkeys from a 256-bit master secret, while AES-256-GCM provides authenticated encryption and an authenticated sequence number provides replay protection. Experimental evaluation on representative Brain MRI, Chest X-ray, Head CT, Knee X-ray, and Retinal Fundus images yielded an average PSNR of 31…

title: Analysis of Big Data-Based Financial Technology and AI on Financial Inclusion in Indonesia
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of implementing Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based financial technology on increasing financial inclusion in Indonesia during the period 2019–2024. The background of this study is based on the rapid increase in digital transformation in the financial sector triggered by the adoption of fintech, but there is still a gap in financial access, especially among low-income groups and disadvantaged regions. This study uses a quantitative approach with a panel data model, involving independent variables of Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP), education level, average internet access, fintech loan recipient entities, and the number of mobile banking users on the dependent variable of the Financial Inclusion Index. The data was obtained from official publications of the Financial Services Authority (OJK), Bank Indonesia (BI), and the Central Statistics Agency (BPS). The results of the analysis show that Big Data and AI have a positive and significant contribution to expanding financial inclusion through increased credit distribution efficiency, expanded access to digital services, and personalized financial products. However, their influence is still limited by gaps in digital literacy, infrastructure, and trust in data security. The findings of this study are expected to provide strategic input for regulators, fintech industry player…

The Effect of Women on the Board of Directors, Firm Size, and Profitability on Firm Value at PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk for the 2015–2024 Period
abstract: This study examines the associations of women’s representation on the board of directors (WOBD), firm size, and profitability with firm value at PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk during 2015–2024. Using ten annual observations, the study employs descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression. The results show that WOBD has a negative but insignificant coefficient (? = ?0.031; p = 0.146), firm size has a negative and significant coefficient (? = ?4.320; p = 0.002), and net profit margin (NPM) has a negative but insignificant coefficient (? = ?0.006; p = 0.773). The overall model is significant (F = 12.874; p = 0.005), with an R² of 0.866. Firm size is negatively associated with firm value, whereas WOBD and NPM show no significant partial associations. These findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the small sample and limited variation in WOBD.

title: Determinants of SDG7 Progress in E7 Economies: Financial Development, Tax Burden, Trade Openness, and Technological Innovation
abstract: ABSTRACT Low‐carbon energy consumption plays a critical role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions to combat climate change, while also being closely linked to macroeconomic dynamics such as financial development, technological innovation, trade openness, and economic growth. In this context, factors such as tax burden, the depth of the financial system, and the level of openness stand out as key determinants that either encourage or hinder the transition to low‐carbon energy. This study investigates the effects of financial development, tax burden, technological innovation, trade openness, and economic growth on low‐carbon energy consumption in E7 economies (Brazil, China, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Russia, and Türkiye) during the period 1995–2024. The analysis utilizes second‐generation panel data methods and applies the augmented mean group (AMG) and regularized common correlated effects (RCCE) estimators to identify long‐run relationships. The empirical findings reveal several strong country‐specific effects. Financial development positively impacts low‐carbon energy consumption in Mexico, while negatively impacting it in Indonesia and Russia. Economic growth is found to promote low‐carbon energy consumption in China, Indonesia, and Russia. Technological innovation negatively impacts low‐carbon energy consumption in Mexico. Trade openness positively impacts low‐carbon energy …

title: Toward the Rational Design of Tailored Ligands for Intrinsically Disordered Proteins through NMR
abstract: Abstract Understanding the driving forces governing the interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins and their potential ligands represents a key step toward the rational design of drugs targeting this type of proteins. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to achieve detailed atom-resolved information toward this ambitious goal. We present here a set of differently functionalized calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to target different regions of the well-characterized intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein. Dedicated NMR experiments extended the analysis from backbone to side-chain nuclear spins, thus enabling the atom-resolved identification of short-range contacts between the calixarene ligands and methyl or aromatic groups of the protein surface, and revealing how these interactions refine the electrostatically driven association within different lysine-rich motifs. This approach provides a comprehensive description of how the macrocycles recognize and bind the target protein, offering a basis for the rational design of ligands capable of modulating protein function.

title: Evaluating Fermented and Non‐Fermented Lettuce‐Based Biostimulants Through a Design of Experiments Approach to Address Agronomic and Microbial Impacts in Strawberry Soilless Cultivation
abstract: ABSTRACT Intensive agriculture relies heavily on synthetic fertilizers, which contribute to green‐house gas emissions and to the degradation of soil quality and microbial biodiversity. In line with circular‐economy principles, the conversion of organic biomass into biostimulants through fermentation has emerged as a sustainable strategy to support plant performance. This study evaluated the use of solid‐state fermentation with lactic acid bacteria (LAB) to produce an experimental biostimulant from retail lettuce waste and assessed its agronomic and microbial effects on soilless‐grown strawberry. A design of experiments approach, a statistical, multivariate method for systematically planning experiments and modelling the relationships between process factors and measured responses, was used to model the fermentation process and to identify the key factors driving microbial growth. Strain selection was the main determinant, and fermentation with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum at 25°C for 24 h was identified as the optimal condition, reaching 8.6 Log CFU g −1 . When applied to strawberries, the fermented biostimulant enhanced plant growth, root development and fruit production in a dose‐ and stage‐dependent manner, with the highest dose increasing fruit number by approximately 3.7‐fold and markedly raising fruit fresh weight and phenolic content relative to the untreated control. Our Father
abstract: Abstract The Lord’s Prayer occupies a central place in the Christian faith. Taking up the suggestions of Bram van de Beek, this article examines the extent to which the Lord’s Prayer can be correlated with an eschatological hope for Israel. This will be done by systematically working through the various petitions of the Lord’s Prayer, showing how each utterance of this prayer relates to God’s promises to the people of Israel. Consequently, Israel’s deliverance can be seen as a foreshadowing of God’s redemption of the whole of creation.

title: A Hybrid CNN–LSTM Framework for Accurate Load Forecasting in Virtual Power Plants
abstract: Accurate load forecasting plays a critical role in ensuring the secure operation and efficient energy scheduling of virtual power plants (VPPs). However, the increasing integration of renewable generation, energy storage devices, and flexible demand resources brings substantial uncertainties and complex nonlinear characteristics to VPP load profiles. Conventional forecasting methods often face challenges in simultaneously learning short-term variations and capturing long-term dependencies in dynamic load sequences. To overcome these limitations, this paper develops a hybrid convolutional neural network and long short-term memory (CNN–LSTM) based forecasting framework for VPP load prediction. Specifically, the one-dimensional convolutional neural network is employed to extract hierarchical local temporal features from historical load data, while the LSTM module is designed to characterize long-term temporal correlations by exploiting its memory and gating mechanisms. A unified end-to-end training strategy is further introduced to optimize the feature extraction and sequence learning processes jointly. Extensive experiments are performed from multiple perspectives, including comparisons with state-of-the-art forecasting approaches, performance evaluations under diverse load fluctuation scenarios, robustness assessments with varying prediction horizons and input disturbances, and …

The Influence of Islamic Capital Market Education and Literacy on Students’ Investment Activity in Digital Sharia Investment Platforms
abstract: Despite the growing number of students with sharia investment accounts, active participation in digital Islamic investment platforms remains limited indicating a gap between financial education and actual investment behavior. This study examines the influence of Islamic capital market education and literacy on students’ investment activity on digital sharia platforms. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, data were collected from 95 students in the fifth and seventh semesters of the Faculty of Islamic Economics and Business (FEBI) at UIN North Sumatra, selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS version 27. The results show that Islamic capital market education has a positive but statistically non-significant effect on investment activity (β = 0.415; t = 1.726; Sig = 0.088). In contrast, Islamic capital market literacy has a positive and significant effect (β = 0.717; t = 3.274; Sig = 0.001), making it the most dominant predictor (standardized β = 0.463). Simultaneously, both variables significantly explain 46.5% of the variation in investment activity (F = 39.997; Sig= 0.000). These findings suggest that improving applied literacy not merely theoretical education is essential to stimulate active investment behavior, with practical implications for curriculum design, investment gallery programs, and Islamic fintech pla…

Design of Power System Stabilizer Using Harris Hawk Optimizer for 150 kV Sulselrabar Electricity System
abstract: In this paper, design of the Power System Stabilizer (PSS) using Harris Hawk Optimizer (HHO) is proposed to improve stability of the 150 kV interconnected electricity system in South, Southeast, and West Sulawesi (Sulawesi Selatan, Tenggara, dan Barat – Sulselrabar), as one of the large-scaled electricity of Indonesia. The simulation and optimization are performed in Simulink/MATLAB software. HHO is used to find the optimal parameter of PSS based on the Critical Damping Index (CDI) calculation. For investigating the performance, load changes are subjected to the power system. Based on the results, HHO achieved the best stability improvement compared to the Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CSA). Based on the time domain simulation analyses, the HHO-based PSS design reduced overall oscillation by 83.81%, and reduced settling time by 57.9%. Based on the Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE) calculation, the HHO-based PSS design also reduced the average error by 67.34%.

title: Does Muscle Pay? Gender Difference In The Labor Market Returns To Body Composition
abstract: This paper studies whether muscle strength affects the labor market outcomes and whether any gender difference presents in the effect. Based on the data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2013 to 2014, this paper employs regression analysis methods to estimate how various body composition indicators are related to income and employment. Unlike previous studies that mainly relied on Body Mass Index (BMI) as a weight indicator, this paper introduces functional strength indicators such as muscle mass and grip strength to measure physical ability more comprehensively. The research results show that there is no significant correlation between traditional weight indicators and income and employment, while there is a relatively stable positive correlation between grip strength and the labor market outcomes. Meanwhile, the analysis found that the correlation was more significant among males, while the results among females were relatively weak.

title: Market data governance as knowledge management: managing temporality via rule versioning, provenance and auditability
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how organisations hold governance knowledge stable enough to execute reliably yet revisable as policies and conventions change. It develops a temporality-focused conceptual elaboration of knowledge management (KM) for executable governance, reading market data rules as boundary objects whose validity is bounded in time. Design/methodology/approach The study is a retrospective analysis of an existing design artefact – a Python repository for an equity trading ecosystem, built by the authors for an earlier project – from which design knowledge is abstracted using design science research principles, a documented coding protocol and analytic generalisation. Findings The artefact carries governance knowledge in effective-dated fee regimes resolved deterministically, explicit session and settlement conventions, schema exemplars and fixtures without a validation gate, and reporting treated as an audit output. It supports a lightweight provenance analogue, not formal provenance, answering “what rule applied when” through inspectable configuration and deterministic resolution. Five artefact-level validations pass and are independently reproducible. Research limitations/implications One artefact, analysed by those who built it, can support claims about how executable governance may be structured, not about adoption or effectiveness. Propositions are the…

title: The Depth of Problem Definition: Evaluating Pre-Service Mathematics Teachers’ Initial PCK through Post-Case Study Diagnosis
abstract: This qualitative embedded single-case study examined how pre-service mathematics teachers in Eastern Indonesia define pedagogical problems after school-based case studies and how the depth of those definitions differs across initial pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) categories. Six purposively selected sixth-semester students, two each in low, moderate, and high initial-PCK groups, were selected from 44 questionnaire respondents. Data comprised post-case-study reports, an initial-PCK questionnaire, and semi-structured interviews. The data were analyzed through a reflexive thematic procedure involving data condensation, coding, theme development, and cross-category comparison, with triangulation, peer debriefing, member checking, and an audit trail. All participants identified conceptual and procedural difficulties, prerequisite gaps, and modeling obstacles. However, low-PCK participants predominantly described surface symptoms; moderate-PCK participants mapped error patterns and prerequisite weaknesses using evidence; and high-PCK participants constructed precise, evidence-based, multidimensional diagnoses spanning cognitive, affective, and metacognitive dimensions. Topic complexity was treated as an analytic condition rather than a basis for causal inference by comparing the structure and evidential quality of definitions within each case and then across PCK categories. title: ​Service-Oriented HR Practices and Service Performance in Borobudur Tourism MSMEs: Employee Engagement as Mediator
abstract: This study examines the relationships between Service-Oriented Human Resource Management (SOHRM), employee engagement, and service performance among tourism MSMEs around Borobudur. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey provided 380 valid responses obtained through purposive sampling. The relationships were assessed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). SOHRM was positively associated with employee engagement (β = 0.527, p < 0.001) and service performance (β = 0.159, p = 0.001). Engagement was also associated with service performance (β = 0.525, p < 0.001). The indirect association through engagement was significant (β = 0.277, p < 0.001), consistent with partial mediation. The cross-sectional design, self-reported data, and non-probability sampling limit causal interpretation and generalization. SOHRM had an average variance extracted of 0.467, below the conventional convergent-validity threshold, and four initial indicators were excluded. Service-oriented Human Resources (HR) practices were related to service performance directly and through employee engagement. This study connects the ability–motivation–opportunity and job demands–resources perspectives with service provision in heritage-tourism MSMEs. This study identifies an engagement-related pathway in smaller tourism enterprises while showing the need for further validation of the reduced S…

title: THE EFFECT OF WELCOME DRINK AND FRONT OFFICE SERVICE QUALITY ON GUEST COMFORT DURING REGISTRATION
abstract: This study was motivated by guest waiting time during the registration (check-in) process, particularly during periods of high hotel occupancy, which may affect guest comfort. The Balcone Suites & Resort provides welcome drinks and Front Office services as part of its initial service while guests wait. This study aims to determine the effect of welcome drinks and Front Office service quality on guest comfort while waiting for the registration (check-in) process, both partially and simultaneously. This study employed a quantitative approach with a causal associative design. The sample consisted of 120 respondents selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive analysis, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression with SPSS. The results showed that all variables were in the good category. Partially, welcome drinks did not have a significant effect (sig. = 0.079), while Front Office service quality had a significant effect (sig. = 0.010). Simultaneously, both variables had a significant effect (sig. = 0.002), with an R² of 0.105.

title: The Effect of Perceived Usefulness of the Tring Application and Digital Service Quality on Customer Loyalty through Customer Satisfaction at PT Pegadaian, Mamuju Branch
abstract: Digital transformation in the financial services sector has encouraged PT Pegadaian to develop the TRING application as a digital service platform to enhance customer satisfaction and loyalty. This study aims to analyze the effects of perceived usefulness of the TRING application and digital service quality on customer loyalty through customer satisfaction at PT Pegadaian, Mamuju Branch. This study employed a quantitative approach using a survey of 100 respondents who use the TRING application. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with the assistance of SmartPLS software. The results indicate that: (1) perceived usefulness of the TRING application has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction; (2) digital service quality has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction; (3) perceived usefulness of the TRING application has a positive but insignificant effect on customer loyalty; (4) digital service quality has a positive and significant effect on customer loyalty; (5) customer satisfaction has a positive but insignificant effect on customer loyalty; (6) perceived usefulness of the TRING application does not have a significant effect on customer loyalty through customer satisfaction; and (7) digital service quality does not have a significant effect on customer loyalty through customer satisfaction. …

title: THE ANALYSIS OF EMPLOYEE RELATIONS ACTIVITIES AT PT BANK CENTRAL ASIA TBK, JUANDA BEKASI SUB-BRANCH OFFICE IN EMPOWERING CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE OFFICERS’ COMMUNICATION SERVICE COMPETENCE
abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of employee relations (ER) in empowering the communication competence of customer experience officers (CXO) at PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, Juanda Bekasi Sub-Branch Office. The main focus of this research is on how employee relations (ER) activities support the enhancement of interpersonal communication skills, which are essential in maintaining the quality of digital banking services. This research employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive method. Data were collected through participatory observation and in-depth interviews with employee relations (ER) supervisors, customer experience officers (CXO), and customers. Data analysis was conducted using an interactive model consisting of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings reveal that employee relations (ER) significantly contribute to improving the confidence, mental readiness, empathy, and communication skills of customer experience officers (CXO). The positive impact of these activities is not only experienced by employees internally but also perceived by customers through more friendly, humanistic, and professional services. Therefore, employee relations (ER) can be positioned as a strategic partner in supporting the success of digital banking services while simultaneously strengthening the company’s positive image in the public eye.

title: Examining the Effects of Digital Service and Customer Experience on Hotel Guest Satisfaction: A Quantitative Study at Whiz Prime Hotel Padang
abstract: This research is grounded in the importance of digital services and customer experience in enhancing hotel guest satisfaction. This study aims to determine the influence of digital services and customer experience on guest satisfaction at Whiz Prime Hotel Padang. This research used a quantitative approach with a causal associative method. The sample consisted of 150 respondents selected using purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics 27. The results showed that Digital Service had a positive and significant effect on Guest Stay Satisfaction, with a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05. Customer Experience also had a positive and significant effect on Guest Stay Satisfaction, with a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05. Simultaneously, Digital Service and Customer Experience had a positive and significant effect on Guest Stay Satisfaction. Based on the Standardized Beta value, Digital Service had a more dominant effect than Customer Experience. These findings indicate that improving the quality of digital services and providing positive guest experiences can support higher guest satisfaction during their stay.

title: Forging a Future-Ready Command Structure: Proposals for a More Robust Medical Administrative Framework within the Sri Lanka Medical Service
abstract: Sri Lanka’s health system is internationally acclaimed for delivering commendable health outcomes at a low cost. However, to sustain these achievements and navigate the complex challenges of a new era—characterized by a profound demographic transition, the escalating burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs), and the lessons learned from global health crises,the administrative and leadership framework of the Sri Lanka Medical Service must evolve. The existing structure, governed by the Medical Service Minute of 2014 with its subsequent amendments, has served its purpose but now requires signiﬁcant reform to enhance strategic oversight, empower provincial leadership, and create clearer, more specialized career pathways for medical administrators. This article puts forward a series of proposals for a restructured medical administrative service. The proposed framework advocates for an expanded and stratiﬁed senior executive hierarchy, mandates speciﬁc postgraduate qualiﬁcations for distinct leadership roles, and formalizes an administrative pathway from the grassroot level. It is argued that these reforms are essential for building a resilient, efﬁcient, and forward-looking health service capable of meeting the health needs of Sri Lankans for decades to come.

title: Teaching Performance and Self-Efficacy among PTRU-Oriented Pre-Service English Teachers during Teaching Practicum
abstract: The Professional Teacher of Rajabhat University (PTRU) Model provides a competency-oriented framework for teacher preparation at Rajabhat Universities in Thailand. Using a convergent mixed-methods design, this study examined teaching performance, teaching self-efficacy, and practicum experiences among 28 fourth-year pre-service English teachers during the second semester of their year-long school-based practicum within a PTRU-oriented teacher education program. Teaching performance was examined using practicum-based professional competency assessments covering Learning Management, Parent and Community Relations, and Teacher Duties and Professional Ethics, while teaching self-efficacy was measured using the Teachers’ Sense of Efficacy Scale (TSES). Semi-structured interviews were also conducted to explore participants’ teaching and professional experiences during practicum. Teaching performance scores were toward the upper end of the assessment scale and were higher across successive assessment periods, from 89.15% in the first period to 92.47% in the third. Teacher Duties and Professional Ethics showed the highest relative performance (94.12%), followed by Learning Management (91.45%) and Parent and Community Relations (89.88%). Teaching self-efficacy was also toward the upper end of the TSES scale (M = 7.54, SD = 0.38), with Classroom Management showing the highest…

title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
abstract: Abstract Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

Non-invasive adjunctive diagnostic models incorporating high-frequency ultrasound and shear wave elastography for pediatric Duchenne muscular dystrophy
abstract: Background This study aimed to comprehensively characterize skeletal muscle properties in pediatric patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) using high-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) and shear-wave elastography (SWE), and to construct and compare diagnostic models based on these modalities to evaluate their potential as non-invasive adjunctive tools for assessing muscular involvement. Methods A total of 53 genetically or pathologically confirmed pediatric DMD patients and 61 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were enrolled. The bilateral biceps brachii and quadriceps femoris muscles were examined using HFUS and SWE. Inter-observer reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to HFUS parameters for dimensionality reduction, followed by logistic regression to establish a standardized HFUS diagnostic model. A separate SWE model was constructed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to evaluate and compare the diagnostic performance of the individual and combined models. Results The HFUS model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.875 (95% CI: 0.807–0.943), with 88.9% sensitivity and 81.9% specificity. The SWE model showed an AUC of 0.846 (95% CI: 0.763–0.909), with 69.8% sensit…

PERAN MEDIA AUDIO VOICEMAKER DAN METODE TOTAL PHYSICAL RESPONSE (TPR) TERHADAP KETERAMPILAN MENYIMAK BAHASA ARAB: KAJIAN SISTEMATIS LITERATURE REVIEW
abstract: Listening skill (mahārah al-istimā') is an important component of Arabic language learning, yet its development continues to face challenges in providing consistent auditory input and engaging learners actively during instruction. The development of text-to-speech (TTS) technology, including VoiceMaker, provides an alternative for delivering flexible audio materials, while the Total Physical Response (TPR) method enables learners to respond to language stimuli through physical activities. This study aims to analyze research findings on the use of TTS-based audio media, particularly VoiceMaker, and the TPR method in supporting Arabic listening skills and to identify opportunities for integrating the two approaches in instruction. The study employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Relevant literature was identified through Google Scholar, SINTA, DOAJ, and other academic sources based on the criteria of publications from 2020 to 2026, full-text availability, relevance to language learning and listening skills, and clearly identifiable research objectives, methods, and findings. Of the 210 records initially identified, 25 articles were included in the final synthesis after duplicate removal, screening, eligibility assessment, and quality appraisal. The findings indicate that TTS/VoiceMaker provides flexible, repeatable, and adaptable audit…

title: Imaging tumor heterogeneity to predict response to transarterial chemoembolization in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based habitat imaging is a promising non-invasive approach for assessing intratumoral heterogeneity and predicting responses to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) in hepatocellular carcinoma. A recent multicenter study by Lv et al published in the World Journal of Gastroenterology combined MRI-derived habitat features with clinical data to develop a predictive model that achieved area under the curve values of 0.97, 0.91, and 0.93 across different cohorts, outperforming single-modality models. The ecological diversity index from Gaussian mixture model clustering offers a new measure of tumor ecosystem complexity. However, there are methodological concerns, including potential information leakage, confounding factors from mixed TACE methods, misclassification of modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors outcomes due to imaging variability, and limited inter-site radiomics harmonization. The low transportability of the standalone clinical model (area under the curve values = 0.54, accuracy = 0.41) underscores significant variability across centers. Future efforts should focus on prospective validation with standardized imaging, integration of multiparametric MRI, multi-lesion modeling, radiogenomic correlation studies, and decision-impact trials to assess whether model-guided patient selection can improve survival outcomes. Comprehensive Evaluation of Distance-Based MCDM Methods Using Response to Criteria Weighting: A Ranking Stability and Sensitivity Analysis
abstract: Selecting an appropriate new store location is a complex multi-criteria decision-making problem because potential locations must be evaluated using multiple criteria with different performance characteristics. This study proposes an integrated distance-based Multi-Criteria Decision-Making framework using RECA Weighting combined with TOPSIS, SPOTIS, and EDAS to determine objective criterion importance and evaluate the stability and robustness of alternative rankings. The dataset consists of eight potential store locations evaluated using six criteria: Rental Cost, Building Area, Accessibility, Consumer Traffic, Parking Availability, and Infrastructure. RECA Weighting is applied to determine objective criterion weights based on performance variation, while TOPSIS, SPOTIS, and EDAS are used to generate preference scores and rankings through different distance-based evaluation mechanisms. The results show that Consumer Traffic obtains the highest criterion weight of 0.1824, while Parking Availability receives the lowest weight of 0.1422. The ranking results identify LS5 as the best-performing alternative, followed by LS3, although several alternatives exhibit different ranking positions across the applied methods. Weight-variation analysis using Spearman rank correlation shows that SPOTIS achieves perfect ranking stability with a correlation of 1.0000, TOPSIS demonstrates very stro…

Study On IPO Underpricing And Long-Run Aftermarket Performance In Hong Kong
abstract: This study examines initial public offering (IPO) underpricing and long-run aftermarket performance in Hong Kong using a sample of 598 IPOs listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK) between 2006 and 2013. IPO performance is measured using initial returns, raw returns, and market-adjusted returns over holding periods of up to two years. The study further investigates whether IPO performance varies by listing year, subscription ratio, and the final offer price’s position within the indicative price range. The results indicate that IPO underpricing remains a significant feature of the Hong Kong market. The average first-day return is 16.2%, suggesting substantial initial gains for investors. However, these gains are not sustained, as IPOs generate an average two-year market-adjusted return of approximately −8%, indicating significant long-run underperformance. This pattern suggests that initial investor optimism leads to temporary overvaluation, followed by subsequent price corrections. Cross-sectional analyses show that IPOs issued during periods of high issuance activity, those with higher subscription ratios, and those priced closer to the upper bound of the filing price range generate stronger initial returns but weaker long-run performance. These findings support the asymmetric information, ex-ante uncertainty, investor sentiment, hot issue market, and partial adjustme…

title: Supervisi Humanistik sebagai Model Pembinaan Profesional Guru dalam Manajemen Sekolah
abstract: This article aims to construct a conceptual framework of humanistic supervision as a model for teachers’ professional development within school management by addressing the limitations of conventional supervision, which tends to emphasize administrative compliance and evaluative control. The study employs a qualitative approach through a literature review, critically examining relevant scholarly publications, educational policy documents, and theoretical references. Conceptual analysis is used to identify the fundamental principles, essential characteristics, implementation patterns, and managerial implications of humanistic supervision in educational settings. The findings indicate that humanistic supervision is characterized by dialogic, reflective, collaborative, and developmental interactions that prioritize teachers’ professional growth rather than merely assessing their performance. In contrast to traditional supervisory models, this approach positions teachers as active participants in professional learning and continuous improvement rather than as passive objects of evaluation. Its successful implementation requires integration into school policies, organizational culture, and transformational leadership practices that foster trust, empowerment, and shared responsibility among educational stakeholders. Furthermore, humanistic supervision contributes to creating a suppor…

title: Harnessing Neuroendocrine and Circadian Clocks in Beneficial Insects for Agricultural Chrono-Management
abstract: Abstract Pollinators and natural enemies provide essential agricultural ecosystem services that are regulated by circadian clocks, hormones, and biogenic amines. This review synthesizes research on the integration between neuroendocrine systems and circadian clocks across different taxa, identifying both conserved regulatory mechanisms and lineage-specific adaptive traits. These multilayered interactions coordinate insect behavior, life-history development, and the alignment of insect activities with available resources. We propose agricultural chrono-management, a framework to improve ecosystem services by using targeted environmental cues to align beneficial insect activity with farming schedules. However, most evidence so far comes from the laboratory and controlled studies, and field validation remains limited. We further evaluated the feasibility, ecological risks, and climate resilience of photoperiodic regulation, nutritional modulation, and synthetic ecological interventions. Key future research priorities include multiomics integration, large-scale field validation, and predictive modeling of ecosystem services. This synthesis links molecular-level regulatory mechanisms to ecological outcomes and establishes a foundational framework for climate-resilient management of beneficial insects.

Mapping Artificial Intelligence Research in Business and Management Higher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping business and management higher education, yet the field remains dispersed across educational, managerial, and technological conversations. This study maps that literature through a reproducible bibliometric review of Dimensions.ai records published from 2017 to 2025. The search and final export were completed on August 22, 2026. PRISMA 2020-guided screening retained 352 English-language open-access articles, chapters, and monographs. Descriptive indicators were combined with VOSviewer 1.6.20 analyses of co-authorship, contributor citations, cited-author co-citation, and title-and-abstract term co-occurrence. Annual output increased from 1 publication in 2017 to 191 in the complete 2025 publication year. Citation impact was concentrated in a small number of recent studies, while the co-authorship network remained fragmented into several small groups. Country results placed the United Kingdom first among records with affiliation metadata, although country information was missing for 182 of 352 records. After removing metadata artifacts, the most frequent title-and-abstract terms included intelligence, ChatGPT, business, opportunity, assessment, and engagement. The study contributes a transparent, multi-layer map of an emerging field and identifies priorities for curriculum design, assessment, responsible AI governance, and stronger cross-…

title: The Effectiveness of Learning Institution Management on Students’ Learning Interest and Satisfaction
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of the management effectiveness of a tutoring institution on students’ learning interest and learning satisfaction at Esensi Tutoring Center. The study employed a mixed-methods approach using an explanatory sequential design, which integrates quantitative and qualitative analyses sequentially. The research subjects consisted of 25 respondents, including one tutoring center manager, four tutors, and 20 students. Quantitative data were collected through questionnaires, while qualitative data were obtained through interviews and observations. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and simple linear regression, whereas qualitative data were analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The results indicate that the management effectiveness of the institution has a positive and significant effect on students’ learning interest, with a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.765 and a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.586, indicating a contribution of 58.6%. Management effectiveness also has a positive and significant effect on students’ learning satisfaction, with a correlation coefficient (R) of 0.835 and a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.698, indicating a contribution of 69.8%. The qualitative findings further support these results, demonstrating that systematic instructional planning, e…

title: Smart visitor management system for safety and security in high-rise commercial buildings in Sri Lanka: an analysis of implementation barriers
abstract: Purpose Smart visitor management systems (SVMS) are digital tools that control and monitor visitor access to enhance safety and security in complex, high-occupancy buildings. Despite increasing security demands in high-rise developments, SVMS remain underdeveloped in Sri Lanka. This study aims to investigate the key barriers to implementing SVMS in high-rise commercial buildings in Sri Lanka. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative approach was used using a multiple case study strategy. Six high-rise commercial buildings in Sri Lanka were purposively selected for in-depth investigation. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 experts, including in-house stakeholders and SVMS vendors. Data were analysed using the template analysis method to ensure reliability and credibility. Findings A total of 31 barriers were identified and categorised into five themes: technological, economical, organisational, regulatory and informational. Key barriers specific to Sri Lanka include legacy infrastructure, economic instability, limited skilled workforce, lack of regulatory environment and low awareness. These challenges reflect both global patterns and unique contextual limitations faced by the local industry. Practical implications The results assist stakeholders, building owners, property managers and policymakers in optimising visitor management, improving safety and efficiency…

title: An SEM-BBN approach for predicting construction payment delay via respondent-reported project-interaction factors under perceived power asymmetry
abstract: Purpose This study examines how perceived power asymmetries in client–contractor relationships contribute to construction payment delay and develops an early-warning model based on project-interaction information assessable by contractors. It addresses the limitation of existing payment-prediction models, which depend on client financial information that payment receivers cannot access. Design/methodology/approach A model was refined through a four-round Delphi study and tested using questionnaire data from 486 UK construction projects. Partial least-squares structural equation modelling was used to validate the behavioural pathways, and the supported structural and moderation pathways were converted into a Bayesian belief network for predicting payment-delay severity. Predictive performance was evaluated on a held-out test set and benchmarked against alternative classifiers. Findings Perceived coercive power asymmetry was the most consistent driver of client and contractor opportunistic financial strategies, whereas perceived reward and expert power asymmetries generally reduced opportunism. Perceived forced payment obligation moderated mediated-power pathways, while digital infrastructure establishment moderated selected non-mediated-power pathways. title: Digital Marketing, Fintech Literacy, Financial Management, and Income Growth among Student Entrepreneurs
abstract: Student entrepreneurship has become increasingly intertwined with digital platforms and technology-enabled financial services, making digital and financial capabilities potentially important for sustaining business income. This study examined the relationships between digital marketing, fintech literacy, financial management, and income growth among student entrepreneurs in Medan, Indonesia. A quantitative approach was employed using questionnaire data collected from 100 student entrepreneurs. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The results showed that digital marketing was positively and significantly associated with income growth (β = .344, p < .001), fintech literacy demonstrated a positive and significant relationship with income growth (β = .262, p = .009), and financial management was also positively and significantly associated with income growth (β = .403, p < .001). Among the three predictors, financial management showed the largest standardized path coefficient, indicating the strongest relative structural association with income growth. Collectively, digital marketing, fintech literacy, and financial management explained 79.4% of the variance in income growth (R² = .794). These findings indicate that income growth among student entrepreneurs is associated with complementary digital and financial…

title: ANFIS-Based Energy Management for a Grid-Connected PV-Battery Hybrid System at Renewable Energy Integration Demonstrator of Indonesia
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance evaluation of an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS)-based Energy Management System (EMS) for a grid-connected PV–battery hybrid system. The proposed EMS aims to coordinate the power exchange among the photovoltaic (PV) array, battery storage, and the utility grid to ensure reliable operation and optimal renewable utilization. The ANFIS controller receives three inputs PV power, load power, and battery state of charge (SOC) and generates the battery reference power () to regulate the charging and discharging processes. The system was trained using approximately 1600 data sets, with 30% used for testing and checking, achieving a final root-mean-square (RMS) error of 0.0589. The proposed control strategy was validated through three test scenarios: (1) constant load with variable irradiance, (2) variable load with constant irradiance, and (3) simultaneous variations of load and irradiance. Simulation results show that the ANFIS-based EMS effectively maintains power balance, prevents battery overcharge or deep discharge, and stabilizes SOC within the 30–80% range. In addition, the controller efficiently manages power sharing between the PV system, battery, and grid, ensuring optimal energy utilization and reduced grid dependency. Overall, the results confirm that the proposed EMS demonstrates adaptive, stable, and intelligent…

title: Financial Management, Accounting Training, and Financial Technology as Determinants of Microenterprise Financial Performance
abstract: Financial performance is central to the sustainability of microenterprises, yet their ability to achieve favorable financial outcomes may be associated with how effectively financial activities are managed, the accounting training received by business owners, and the utilization of financial technology. This study examined the relationships between financial management, accounting training, financial technology, and the financial performance of microenterprises in Medan Labuhan District, Medan, Indonesia. A quantitative explanatory cross-sectional design was employed involving 100 microenterprise owners selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The results showed that financial management was positively and significantly associated with financial performance (β = .308), accounting training demonstrated a positive and significant association with financial performance (β = .331), and financial technology was also positively and significantly associated with financial performance (β = .226). Among the three predictors, accounting training showed the largest path coefficient in the structural model. title: From flight shame to system change: developing the multi-level eco-emotion activation framework
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to develop the multi-level eco-emotion activation framework (MLEAF) to address the fragmented understanding of how ecological emotions, like “flygskam” (flight shame), shape travel decisions within tourism systems. Design/methodology/approach A scoping review was conducted following Joanna Briggs Institute and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines and analysed 67 peer-reviewed publications using descriptive quantitative techniques and inductive thematic synthesis. Findings The MLEAF sees the eco-emotions as operating simultaneously across individual, social and institutional levels, connected by feedback loops and resistance mechanisms. It explains why flygskam drives change in some tourism contexts but has no effect in others and shows that the value−action gap is a result of the system rather than individual failure. Practical implications The framework shows that “flygskam” does not have to be a choice between sustainability and tourism survival. When emotional awareness is backed by social norms that value sustainable travel and by infrastructure that offers real alternatives, tourism can be transformed instead of declining through mode switching, slow tourism and better accessibility. Originality/value The MLEAF is the first integrated conceptual framework that explains how eco-em…

title: Illuminating furniture e-retailing: an eye-tracking study on effects of image brightness and design complexity on visual attention and consumer perceptions through the AC-TER model
abstract: Purpose Grounded in the Attention Capture and Transfer by Elements of Advertisements (AC-TEA) model, this study examines atmospheric variables, image brightness and design complexity, in furniture e-retail by integrating visual attention with perceptions of pleasantness and order. Design/methodology/approach An eye-tracking experiment measured consumers' visual attention in images simulating furniture e-retail storefronts or catalogues. Metrics included pupil dilation as an index of emotional arousal and cognitive effort, and fixation-based measures to capture visual attention and information processing. The study used home-interior images varying in brightness and design complexity, integrating physiological data with post-test perceptions of pleasantness and order. Findings Results show greater pupil dilation when consumers view dark-filtered or highly complex images, indicating higher emotional arousal and cognitive effort. Brighter lighting conditions are associated with reduced pupil dilation. Scene complexity also affects attentional metrics, leading to longer fixation durations but fewer fixations in high-complexity images, suggesting a more focused visual information processing. Furthermore, these visual attention patterns translate into perceptual judgements, with attention to dark and moderately structured scenes positively predicting pleasantness and order, respectiv…
