title: Qualitative systematic literature reviews: methodological insights and theoretical contributions
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to address the methodological inconsistencies prevalent in qualitative-based systematic literature reviews (Q-SLRs) within hospitality and tourism (H&T) and proposes a comprehensive framework to enhance their rigor and replicability. Design/methodology/approach This paper presents a quality framework for Q-SLR methodology, outlining best practices for conducting Q-SLRs and a “theorizing from association” approach to guide the development of theoretical implications for Q-SLRs. Findings The framework presents four phases: planning, conducting, extracting and analyzing, providing a step-by-step approach to Q-SLR. The novel “theorizing from association” integrates H&T literature with related fields, including management, organizational behavior and marketing. Practical implications The proposed framework enhances methodological rigor and fosters theoretical advancement, ensuring that future reviews can more effectively contribute to the field. Originality/value This paper addresses a critical gap in the H&T literature by providing a comprehensive guide to conducting Q-SLRs and to theoretical development from Q-SLRs.

title: Integrated intelligent smoke management system: integrating electrostatic precipitation with PID-controlled air recirculation for charcoal-grill restaurant kitchens
abstract: Abstract Charcoal-grill restaurants can contribute to localized air pollution through emissions of particulate matter, including PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀, particularly in small kitchens with limited ventilation. This study developed and experimentally evaluated an intelligent smoke management system integrating a dual-stage electrostatic precipitator (ESP), PID-controlled multi-pass air recirculation, and a compact smoke-capture hood for small charcoal-grill restaurants. The prototype was tested in an enclosed kitchen with a volume of 25 m 3 under Single-pass and Recirculation operating modes at airflow velocities of 2 and 3 m/s using six paired experimental runs (n = 6). System performance was evaluated based on PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀ removal efficiency, particulate removal rate, Equivalent Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADRₑq), and electrical energy consumption. The results showed that the Recirculation mode at an airflow velocity of 3 m/s achieved the highest particulate-removal efficiencies, reaching 95.15% for PM₂.₅ and 95.50% for PM₁₀. These values were significantly higher than those obtained under the corresponding Single-pass condition (p < 0.001). Under this operating condition, the measured average system-level electrical power was 68.2 W, corresponding to an energy consumption of 11.4 Wh per 10-min experimental cycle. title: Genetic Management of Small Livestock Populations: From Inbreeding Control to Conservation of Animal Genetic Resources
abstract: Abstract Small animal populations are vulnerable to the erosion of genetic variability. When few breeding animals contribute genes to the next generation, relatedness increases, heterozygosity declines and harmful recessive alleles are more likely to be expressed. This case study uses simple quantitative genetics concepts to help students and practitioners understand how inbreeding can be monitored and managed in livestock populations. The case begins with the biological meaning of the inbreeding coefficient, F, and shows how inbreeding reduces heterozygosity from 2pq to 2pq(1 − F). It then introduces effective population size, N e , and demonstrates why the balance between breeding males and breeding females matters more than census size alone. A worked scenario shows that a population with 5 breeding males and 200 breeding females has an idealized N e of 19.5 and an expected ΔF of about 2.6% per generation under equal-contribution assumptions. Practical responses include increasing the number of breeding males, balancing sire use, rotating mating groups, monitoring family representation and securing semen, embryos, somatic cells or DNA in a gene bank. The case trains students and practitioners to move from population inventory to effective population size, risk classification, mating design and cryoconservation planning. title: Mega-event governance beyond the host city: social capital and rural inclusion during the Tokyo 2020 Olympics
abstract: Purpose Mega-events are frequently promoted as catalysts for regional development, yet communities located near event activities may remain peripheral to the governance processes through which opportunities and legacies are produced. This study examines how event governance structures and local relational capacity shaped the participation of two rural, venue-adjacent communities in the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, and how these relationships performed under COVID-19 disruption. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a comparative embedded case design of two rural hot-spring (onsen) towns in the Tohoku region of northeastern Japan that were located near Olympic activities. Drawing on 22 semi-structured interviews with local businesses and public-sector stakeholders, the analysis examines how bonding, bridging, and linking relationships interacted with event governance structures to shape planning participation, institutional access, and responses to disruption. COVID-19 is treated as a stress test of these governance relationships. Findings Geographic proximity to Olympic activities did not produce meaningful or evenly distributed participation. Most local stakeholders had limited involvement in planning, while institutional access was concentrated among selected actors, particularly accommodation providers, and cross-sector coordination remained weak. title: Clinical and Serological Evaluation and Management of Rheumatic Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease
abstract: In 2011, the American Thoracic Society (ATS) recommended that antibody testing be included in the evaluation of patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) to assess for an underlying connective tissue disease, particularly in cases of lingering diagnostic uncertainty, such as differentiating ILD from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.¹ Specifically, the ATS endorsed routine testing for antinuclear antibodies (ANA), rheumatoid factor (RF), and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti CCP) antibodies. However, autoantibody testing in isolation is rarely diagnostic and results must be interpreted within a clinical context. Accordingly, the interpretation of autoantibody testing and its implications for the diagnosis and management of rheumatic disease-associated ILD remain central to optimizing care in this patient population. Serology testing is best utilized as an adjunct rather than a standalone diagnostic tool. Over reliance on antibody results without clinical correlation can result in misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment. It is therefore important to integrate serologic data into the broader diagnostic workup of systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease-associated ILD.

title: Waste Opportunity Engine: Literature Survey and Proposed System
abstract: Waste management guidance for ordinary people usually stops at two choices: throw it away or recycle it. This paper surveys the research that a system like the Waste Opportunity Engine builds on and then presents the proposed system. The survey covers four areas: (1) the scale of the global waste problem, (2) circular economy thinking, which ranks reuse, repair and upcycling above disposal, (3) deep-learning methods for recognising items and materials from images, and (4) text-based (NLP) analysis for matching descriptions to stored solutions. The studies are compared in a literature review and grouped by theme. The survey finds that existing work is strong at classifying waste but largely stops there: it does not recommend ranked reuse, repair, upcycle and business options for an individual item. To address this gap, the proposed system accepts an item photo, a short text description, or both. A convolutional neural network identifies the item, material and condition, an NLP module extracts keywords from the text, and a condition-aware decision engine queries an SQL database of curated solutions to return ranked options, step-by-step guidance and a business idea. Each analysis is stored so that the solution database can improve over time

title: Financial Statements As An Information Base For Money Laundering Risk Assessment: A Comparison Among Italian Detection Methods
abstract: Annual financial statements are one of the information sources used to assess the risk that a firm is involved in money laundering, tax fraud or organised crime infiltration. This paper compares the detection tools based on the financial statements of Italian firms, developed along two distinct strands: academic research and the studies of the Financial Intelligence Unit for Italy (UIF). The five methodological approaches examined – a logistic regression model, two composite indicators, and two machine learning models – serve as tools for identifying firms linked to organised crime, companies issuing invoices for non-existent transactions, and firms interposed in complex tax fraud schemes. The comparison considers four dimensions: detection purpose and target, reference firms, information set, and analytical method. It shows that risk assessment depends on three main choices: which financial statement items to use, which firms to take as reference, and how the data are processed. As these choices vary across tools, financial statements do not provide a uniform information base, and differences in reference firms, validation conditions, and performance measures make reported results not directly comparable. title: Pengaruh Motivasi Kerja dan Iklim Organisasi terhadap Kepuasan Kerja serta Implikasinya pada Kinerja Perawat di Rumah Sakit Jasa Kartini Kota Tasikmalaya
abstract: Nurse performance is essential to hospital service quality and is influenced by work motivation, organizational climate, and job satisfaction. This study examined these factors and their relationships among 60 nurses at Jasa Kartini Hospital, Tasikmalaya. A quantitative descriptive and verificative design employed census sampling, questionnaires, interviews, observations, and documentation. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and path analysis with SPSS. Mean scores indicated relatively low work motivation (3.17) and job satisfaction (3.07), alongside relatively poor organizational climate (3.18) and nurse performance (3.11). Work motivation (path coefficient 0.490) and organizational climate (0.403) positively and significantly affected job satisfaction. Together, they explained 70.69% of job satisfaction variance (F = 85.827), leaving 29.31% attributable to other factors. Job satisfaction positively and significantly affected nurse performance (path coefficient 0.869; t = 9.208), explaining 75.52% of its variance. All reported relationships were statistically significant (p < 0.001). Strengthening motivation and organizational climate may improve overall satisfaction, nurse performance, and nursing service quality at the hospital.
venue: Journal of Management and Creative Business

title: Team Teaching for Maternal and Child Health Preparation Among Assistant Medical Officer Trainees: Confidence and Competency Outcomes
abstract: Background: Assistant Medical Officer (AMO) trainees are expected to perform maternal and child health (MCH) procedures safely during clinical placement, yet confidence may remain low when earlier exposure is fragmented. Methods: This single-group quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study evaluated a structured team-teaching intervention among 52 Semester 5 (Year 3 Semester I) trainees at the Training Institute, Ministry of Health Malaysia (ILKKM) Kota Kinabalu. The intervention involved two days of supervised practice covering 11 MCH procedures aligned with the Clinical Practice IV module. Competency was assessed during the structured training using the national Diploma in Medical and Health Sciences (DMHS) rubric, while confidence and satisfaction were measured using a content-validated questionnaire. The pre-intervention confidence assessment was conducted before team teaching, while the post-intervention confidence assessment was administered after trainees completed their subsequent two-week MCH clinical placement. Paired-sample t-tests were used to compare pre- and post-confidence scores. Results: Mean self-perceived confidence scores increased from 2.31 ± 0.36 after the team-teaching intervention and subsequent MCH clinical posting (p < 0.001), with a large effect size (Cohen’s dz = 3.02). Most trainees demonstrated competency at Scores 3 and 4 across the assessed proced…

title: Responsible AI In Credit Portfolio Growth: A Risk-Controlled Framework For Artificial Intelligence–Driven Lending In U.S. Banks
abstract: This study develops and validates GUARD (Governance, Underwriting integrity, Accountability, Resilience, Disclosure), a risk-controlled framework for the deployment of artificial intelligence in credit origination and portfolio management by U.S. banking organizations. It examines how lenders can convert AI-driven underwriting into sustained credit portfolio growth while retaining defensible control over fair lending exposure, model risk, and consumer explanation obligations, in a supervisory environment that between April 2025 and June 2026 moved decisively from prescriptive to principles-based expectations.
venue: International Journal of Business & Management Studies

title: ​Green Human Resource Management Implementation at PT United Tractors Tbk for Corporate Sustainability
abstract: Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) has drawn growing attention in heavy equipment and mining services as environmental pressures and stakeholder expectations intensify. This study examines how GHRM is represented in PT United Tractors Tbk’s sustainability reports for 2023–2025. A descriptive qualitative document analysis classified selected Global Reporting Initiative employment-related disclosures into five dimensions: recruitment and selection, training and development, performance management, compensation and rewards, and employee involvement, with stakeholder theory guiding the interpretation. The findings reveal an uneven distribution of environmental evidence across the five dimensions. Sustainability-linked leadership performance indicators and conservation programs provide the clearest environmental connections, whereas recruitment, training, and compensation disclosures mainly document general human resource practices that supply organizational context without establishing green competencies, environmental selection criteria, or employee-level green incentives. The study concludes that reported GHRM practices show varying degrees of environmental integration, with limited evidence of employee-level environmental implementation across several HR dimensions. This study is limited to a single company's sustainability reports from 2023–2025, restricting the generalizab…

title: The Mediating Role Of Organizational Commitment Between Total Reward Systems, Employee Attraction And Retention In Botswana’s Public Health Sector Keorapetse, A.
abstract: The service quality of public sector organisations in Botswana is generally considered to be less satisfactory than the private sector. One of the myriads of reasons is arguably reward and punishment system not being applied firmly and consistently. This research investigates the relationship between reward system and employee attraction and retention, as well as the extent to which these rewards influence workforce stability in the public health sector in Botswana. The study adopted a pragmatist approach using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. Employing semi-structured face-tox-face interviews and structured questionnaire to a stratified random sample of 228 doctors and nurses for data collection. For qualitative Thematic coding and categorisation for qualitative, while SPSS version 20.0, employing descriptive statistics and linear regression analysis were used. The linear regression analysis revealed that extrinsic rewards significantly drive employee attraction, while intrinsic rewards are the strongest predictors of retention. Social rewards play a complementary yet significant role, reinforcing the need for a balanced and integrated total reward system. To ensure loyalty, commitment and retain self-motivated star performers within the public health institutions in Botswana, it is critical that managers engender and place high premium on employees’ intrinsic r…

title: The Effect of Price and Store Atmosphere on Customer Loyalty
abstract: The rapid growth of coffee shops in Indonesia has intensified competition, making customer loyalty increasingly important for business sustainability. Although price and store atmosphere are widely recognized as potential determinants of customer loyalty, their relative contributions may differ across coffee shop contexts. This study examined the effects of price and store atmosphere on customer loyalty at Fuels Coffee in Bandung, Indonesia. Using a quantitative explanatory design, data were collected through a questionnaire administered to 97 customers selected using purposive sampling, with eligibility restricted to those who had made at least two purchases. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results revealed that price had a positive and statistically significant effect on customer loyalty (B = 0.475, p = .001), whereas store atmosphere showed no statistically significant effect (B = 0.197, p = .103). The overall regression model was statistically significant (p = .001) and explained 36.7% of the variance in customer loyalty (adjusted R² = .367). These findings demonstrate that price, rather than store atmosphere, was the significant predictor of customer loyalty within the examined model. The study provides empirical evidence that customers’ perceptions of price may play a more prominent role in fostering loyalty in this coffee shop context, highli…

title: Leveraging Machine Learning for Profit Forecasting and Cost Optimization Using Public Financial Data
Forecasting the Number of Tourist Visits to Semarang City Using the Holt-Winters Multiplicative and Fourier Series Analysis (FSA) Methods
abstract: Forecasting is a crucial process in strategic planning, including in the tourism sector, which is highly influenced by seasonal fluctuations and external factors. In Semarang City, the number of tourist visits has experienced significant changes in recent years, particularly due to the COVID-19 pandemic, which caused a sharp decline in 2020 and 2021. Nevertheless, a post-pandemic upward trend in visits has begun to emerge. To support adaptive, data-driven planning, accurate forecasting methods capable of capturing both trend and seasonal patterns are essential. This study aims to compare the Holt-Winters Multiplicative method and Fourier Series Analysis (FSA) in forecasting tourist visits to Semarang City. The data used consist of monthly tourist visit records from 2017 to 2024, obtained from the Semarang City Office of Culture and Tourism. Forecast accuracy was evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE). The results show that the Holt-Winters Multiplicative method produced a lower MAE of 44,498.31 and SMAPE of 6.76%, compared to the Fourier Series Analysis method. Therefore, the Holt-Winters Multiplicative method is considered more accurate in forecasting tourist visits. This study is expected to contribute to more effective tourism management and development strategies at the regional level.

title: Enhance EV station charge and discharge based on deep learning forecasting method incorporating renewable energy sources and multi-objective optimization algorithm
abstract: As electric vehicle charging station operations become more common, proper coordination of energy management is necessary to avoid high operational costs and carbon emissions caused by electric vehicle charging requirements, intermittent renewable sources, and fluctuating electricity rates. In this research, a forecast-based optimization methodology is created with the objective of optimizing the charge-discharge management of a renewable-powered electric vehicle charging station system involving photovoltaic generation, wind generation, fuel cells, electric vehicles, and stationary batteries. First, a recurrent neural network is used to predict relevant time series data, such as photovoltaic energy, wind energy, electric vehicle load demand, fuel cell energy production, and electric vehicle energy consumption. These forecasted data are then applied to a bi-objective energy management optimization problem, which is solved using NSGA-II. The objective is to minimize operating cost and emissions while considering power balance, grid energy exchange, and other operational constraints associated with the fuel cell, battery storage system, and electric vehicles. In this study, two scenarios are examined using one month of hourly data; Scenario 1 does not use stationary batteries, whereas Scenario 2 uses them. The forecasting results show robust predictions, with one-hour-ahead value…

Preparation and performance prediction of PES/TiO2 ultrafiltration membranes using machine learning
abstract: Purpose In this study, polyethersulfone (PES) and titanium dioxide (TiO2) were used as membrane materials and PVP-K30 was used as a pore-forming agent. PES/TiO2 ultrafiltration membranes were prepared using the nonsolvent-induced phase separation (NIPS) method to investigate the effects of PES concentration, TiO2 concentration, temperature and PVP-K30 content on membrane performance. The purpose of this study is to use machine learning to conduct an in-depth analysis of the relationship between membrane fabrication process conditions and membrane performance, thereby providing a data-driven basis for ultrafiltration membrane design and process optimization. Design/methodology/approach This study first completed the preparation of PES/TiO2 ultrafiltration membranes, measured and conducted a basic analysis of their performance. Given the complex relationship between membrane preparation conditions and performance, traditional methods struggle to fully reveal their underlying patterns. Based on this, this study introduced machine learning (ML) analysis methods and constructed three machine learning models, including gradient boosted decision tree (GBDT), random forest and extreme random tree. The authors conducted an in-depth investigation into the relationship between preparation conditions (including PES concentration, TiO2 concentration, PVP-K30 content and temperature) and mem…

title: Short-Term Reservoir Inflow Prediction Using Weather Forecast Data and ExtraTrees Regressor for Hydroelectric Power Plant Operations
abstract: Reliable short-term inflow forecasting is critical for optimizing hydroelectric power plant (HPP) operations, where water availability is directly influenced by dynamic and often extreme weather patterns. Inaccurate inflow estimations can result in either uncontrolled water spills or reservoir levels dropping below operational thresholds, both leading to reduced energy efficiency and potential operational risks. This study presents a data-driven inflow prediction framework utilizing the ExtraTrees Regressor algorithm, trained on four years of combined historical hydrological and meteorological data, and validated using independent weather forecast datasets. The model achieves a coefficient of determination (R²) of up to 82%, demonstrating strong predictive accuracy. By incorporating forecasted weather parameters into the predictive model, the proposed approach enables proactive reservoir management and more effective turbine scheduling, significantly reducing the incidence of emergency spill events. Findings from this research highlight the advantages of transitioning from conventional intuition-based methods to systematic data-driven strategies, offering enhanced reliability, operational resilience, and efficiency in hydropower generation planning.

Fundraising Tools as a Mechanism for Ensuring the Financial Sustainability of Cultural Projects
abstract: The article examines in detail the theoretical and methodological foundations of fundraising in the cultural sec-tor as well as its meaning to supply the financial sustainability of cultural projects and organizations. The au-thors investigate the concept of fundraising, analyze its evolution, and identify its tools (charity, philanthropy, sponsorship, endowments, and crowdfunding). Fundraising is presented as a complex system for the attraction of money, material resources, vocational assistance, and other kinds of support from private individuals, com-mercial companies, charity funds, and government institutions. The paper analyzes the content of this concept, traces the history of its formation and development, and shows how the lead-ups to the search of the cultural initiatives financing were changing. Particular attention is given to the fundraising key tools: sponsorship, phi-lanthropy, charity, grant support, endowments, and crowdfunding. The work makes a comparison by a few cri-teria: the goals for attracting finance, lasting the cooperation with donor, character of the represented support-ing and kind of profit that is obtained by the financier. It is highlighted that the effective evolvement of fundrais-ing activity is not possible with no integrated and coherent approach. The recommendations on the creation of the practice models for mobilization of resources, employ…

title: Nickel-Catalyzed Enantioselective Carbo-Carbonylation of Alkenes Using Formic Acid as a CO Surrogate: Access to Oxindoles Bearing Chiral Quaternary Carbon
abstract: Abstract Carbonylation reactions typically rely on toxic carbon monoxide gas, often under pressurized conditions. Herein, we report an enantioselective nickel-catalyzed carbonylative difunctionalization of activated olefins using formic acid as a safe and operationally simple CO surrogate under mild conditions. The reaction employs a chiral phosphine-based ferrocene ligand to furnish ester-functionalized oxindoles bearing stereogenic quaternary carbon centers in high yields and enantioselectivities. Isotopic-labeling and XPS studies support in situ CO generation and trapping by an alkyl-nickel intermediate.

title: Solvent-Free Synthesis of Highly Luminescent Solid-State Boric Acid-Assisted Carbon Dots for Stable and High-Contrast Latent Fingerprint Visualization
abstract: Abstract The development of efficient, stable, and environmentally friendly fluorescent materials for latent fingerprint visualization remains a major challenge in forensic science. Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as promising fluorescent nanomaterials owing to their low toxicity, tunable optical properties, and eco-friendly nature. However, their practical application in solid-state systems is often hindered by aggregation-induced quenching (AIQ), which can significantly suppress fluorescence emission. In this study, highly luminescent boric acid-assisted carbon dots (B-CDs) were synthesized through a simple, rapid, and solvent-free thermal process using citric acid, urea, and boric acid as precursors. Unlike conventional approaches, the developed method enables the direct formation of solid-state emissive carbon dot powders without requiring additional surface passivation, purification, or polymeric matrices. Structural and spectroscopic characterizations supported the successful formation of heteroatom-functionalized B-CDs that exhibit excitation-dependent photoluminescence and strong solid-state emission. The synthesized B-CDs exhibited a high solid-state photoluminescence quantum yield of 77.5%. The B-CDs showed strong short-term stability, retaining more than 95% of their initial PL intensity after 60 min exposure to 95% relative humidity and during short-term thermal trea…

title: Tipping points in coral reef ecosystems: Interplay of carbon cycle disruption and ocean warming
abstract: Coral reefs are among the most vital ecosystems on the planet, sustaining exceptionally high biodiversity and providing essential ecological services to coastal communities. However, coral populations have been steadily declining for decades, primarily due to stressors such as rising ocean temperatures and disruptions in the global carbon cycle. Mounting evidence suggests that coral reefs are rapidly approaching ecological tipping points, where even small increases in atmospheric carbon could trigger catastrophic shifts in ecosystem functioning and long-term stability. In this work, we develop and analyze a system of coupled nonlinear differential equations representing the dynamics of carbon concentration, global average ocean temperature and coral populations. Through a combination of rigorous mathematical techniques and computational simulations, we investigate the tipping mechanism within this system. Our analysis uncovers a rich set of dynamical features, including bifurcations, critical transitions and prolonged transient states. Importantly, some of these transitions culminate in coral extinction scenarios, while others reveal conditions under which reefs may persist or recover. A deep learning model has been applied to detect bifurcation using simulated coral reef data. These findings underscore the pressing need to comprehend the interplay between carbon emissions, cli…

title: Interface Engineering of Hydrated Tungsten Oxide via Carbon Nitride for Durable Electrochromic Energy Storage
abstract: Abstract Electrochromic smart windows demand high optical contrast, fast switching, long-term durability, and charge-storage functionality, yet hydrated tungsten oxides suffer from restricted ion transport and structural degradation during repeated ion insertion/extraction. Here, we present a carbon nitride-driven phase transformation strategy for a durable energy-storing electrochromic hydrated tungsten oxide. Under mild hydrogen annealing, orthorhombic WO3·H2O nanoplates containing an optimized 10 wt % carbon nitride (CNx) selectively transform into predominantly hexagonal WO3·0.33H2O nanorods (∼80%), accompanied by a relatively minor orthorhombic fraction (∼20%). The CNx promotes structural rearrangement while providing nitrogen-rich Li+-interactive sites that regulate interfacial ion transport and improve electrochemical reversibility. Supported by density functional theory, impedance, diffusion, and postcycling analyses, the optimized WHX-CNx10% film shows favorable Li+ insertion, improved charge-transfer kinetics, and excellent structural retention. The air spray-coated film in 3-electrode system delivers 57% optical modulation at 650 nm, coloration/bleaching times of 2.9/0.6 s, stable cycling over 20,000 cycles, and an areal capacitance of 16.9 mF/cm2. A 5 × 5 cm2 device further exhibits optical modulation of 52% at 650 nm with a coloration efficiency of ∼156 cm2/C. Thes…

title: Turning dirt into gold: the business case of soil carbon for agrarian pathways in arid climate
abstract: Introduction Agricultural carbon sequestration offers considerable potential for mitigating anthropogenic climate change, particularly in the low-organic-carbon soils of the Middle East. This study presents a foundational scenario-based assessment of soil carbon sequestration and economic feasibility. Materials and methods Crop production and market datasets from Jordanian statistics (1998–2023) were used to estimate potential soil carbon sequestration and economic performance. Using benchmarks from literature in comparable agroecological regions, four soil carbon management practices were evaluated across multiple crops for their carbon storage potential using Monte Carlo uncertainty and sensitivity analysis. Sensitivity of economic performance was assessed under optimistic/pessimistic scenarios. Results Among the evaluated practices, the highest carbon sequestration rate was achieved through increased Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), reaching a maximum of 27.44 metric tons of CO₂ per hectare per year (tCO₂/ha/year) under the high scenario for cucumbers. In contrast, barley showed the highest sequestration rate at 0.45 tCO₂/ha/year under increased SOC in the high scenario. Sensitivity analysis showed that ±20% uncertainty in the management coefficients resulted in practice-specific changes of 1.11 tCO₂/ha/year for increased SOC and 0.46 tCO₂/ha/year for improved cropland management.…

title: Carbon Source Substitution During Submerged Fermentation Alters Cordyceps militaris Extracellular Vesicle Metabolite Profiles and Anti-Photoaging Activity
abstract: Abstract Background: Cordyceps militaris extracellular vesicle-enriched preparations, operationally designated CMEVs in this study, are being explored as food-derived nanomaterials, but the effects of source material, fermentation stage, and carbon source on their characteristics and biological activity remain unclear. We compared CMEVs obtained from fruiting bodies and submerged liquid fermentation, selected a collection time, and examined the effects of four carbon sources on CMEV characteristics and protection against UVB-induced injury.Results: Compared with fruiting body-derived CMEVs, fermentation-derived CMEVs yielded more BCA-detectable protein per gram of source dry mass, had a more negative zeta potential, and showed a narrower particle-size distribution. In UVB-damaged HaCaT cells, fermentation-derived CMEVs resulted in higher cell viability, lower MMP1 and IL6 expression, and higher COL1A2 expression. The two source groups had similar particle-to-protein ratios. Although the BCA-measured protein concentration was highest on fermentation day 5, CMEVs collected on day 4 had a higher particle-to-protein ratio and a more uniform particle-size distribution. Day 4 was therefore selected for the subsequent experiments. Tre-CMEVs and Glc-CMEVs had similar protein concentrations, particle-to-protein ratios, and zeta potentials, while Tre-CMEVs showed a relatively narrow part…

title: One-Pot Green Synthesis of Low-Viscosity Acetal Epoxy Resins for Diluent-Free Industrial Processing and Closed-Loop Recycling of Carbon Fiber Composites
abstract: Abstract Recyclable epoxy thermosets and their carbon fiber-reinforced polymer composites (CFRPs) have faced three long-standing bottlenecks: complex synthesis and purification processes, inherently high viscosity incompatible with the industrial vacuum-assisted resin infusion (VARI) process—the dominant technology for manufacturing large wind turbine blades and aerospace composites—and incomplete recovery of individual composite constituents. While dynamic covalent bonds offer a promising route to epoxy recyclability, most existing recyclable epoxy systems fail to simultaneously overcome these hurdles. Herein, we report a green, scalable one-pot synthesis of a novel low-viscosity acetal epoxy resin (BCAE) that simultaneously addresses the synthesis, processing, and end-of-life recycling challenges of epoxy thermosets. This telescoped protocol eliminates intermediate purification steps, delivering BCAE with an ultra-low viscosity of 1.9 Pa·s at 25 °C—6.7-fold lower than commercial bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (DGEBA)—enabling diluent-free VARI fabrication of high-performance CFRPs. The cured BCAE networks exhibit dual recyclability: catalyst-free thermal reprocessability and mild acid-triggered degradation under ambient conditions. Most notably, we demonstrate a closed-loop monomer recycling combined with an open-loop upcycling system with key quantitative breakthroughs: carbon…

title: Nickel-Catalyzed C–O Cross-coupling of N -Boc-Protected Amino Alcohols with (Hetero)aryl Halides
abstract: Abstract The aryloxyalkylamine motif is a privileged pharmacophore found in bioactive molecules. However, achieving its direct and chemoselective construction via O-arylation of amino alcohols remains a significant challenge in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report a mild and efficient nickel-catalyzed C–O cross-coupling of N-Boc-protected amino alcohols with (hetero)aryl halides. This method employs bipyridine as the ligand and an organic amine as the base, circumventing the need for specific ligand systems and strong inorganic bases typically required in other protocols. The system exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad compatibility, particularly with regard to heteroaryl halides and amino alcohols derived from natural amino acids. Furthermore, the scalability of the reaction is demonstrated through gram-scale synthesis, highlighting its potential for practical applications.

title: Solar-driven photothermal-evaporation coupling: antibacterial-evaporation integrated wood-based photothermal materials for seawater desalination
Oerlikon Skyshield Integration in Indonesia's Layered Architecture: The Politics of Interoperability, Defense Governance, and Deterrence
abstract: Indonesia's layered air defense architecture requires interoperable systems that integrate local sensors and weapon systems with national command-and-control networks. However, the acquisition of advanced defense platforms does not automatically translate into integrated operational capabilities. This study examined how technical interoperability, organizational capacity, and defense governance influenced the strategic role of the Oerlikon Skyshield air defense system within Indonesia's layered air defense architecture. A qualitative case study approach was employed, drawing on semistructured interviews with Indonesian Air Force personnel, documentary evidence, and relevant scholarly literature. Data were analyzed through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification, supported by thematic coding. Source and methodological triangulation were applied to strengthen the credibility of the findings. The results identified three principal barriers: inadequate data communications infrastructure, limited personnel competencies in communications systems and cybersecurity, and insufficient middleware capabilities to standardize data exchange with the Indonesian National Air Operations Command (Komando Operasi Udara Nasional, Koopsudnas). These constraints limited shared air situational awareness and external target cueing, restricting Skyshield's operational r…

title: Conceptual Analysis of Productive Waqf Integration in Islamic Microfinance Ecosystem
abstract: Waqf has a strategic role as an Islamic economic instrument in supporting social development and community welfare in Indonesia. This study aims to conceptually analyze the integration of productive Waqf into the Islamic microfinance ecosystem. The method used is a qualitative approach with the type of literature review, where secondary data is collected from books, scientific journals, and related regulatory documents. The results showed that the integration of productive Waqf with Islamic Microfinance Institutions (LKMS) or BMT is a synergy between lasting social instruments and agile financial operational systems. In this model, LKMS acts as a nazhir who manages cash waqf to be distributed as financing for MSMEs with low margins or no cost of fund. This integration significantly encourages financial inclusion for unbankable communities and transforms consumptive aid into sustainable productive capital. In conclusion, this synergy is able to strengthen the economic resilience of the community at the grassroots level and encourage the independence of people from aid recipients (mustahiq) to become empowered individuals.

title: Recent Advances in Artificial Intelligence for Economic Dispatch of Sustainable Energy: A Systematic Review
abstract: This systematic review examines advances in economic dispatch (ED) and demand-side management (DSM) in power systems with wind and photovoltaic (PV) generation. Peer-reviewed journal articles published from 2018 to 2024 were identified through systematic searches of Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection. This review focuses on wind and PV generation due to the challenges their variability and forecast uncertainty pose for power balancing and operational scheduling. ED coordinates generation-side resources to reduce operating costs and emissions, while DSM adjusts the timing and magnitude of electricity demand to provide complementary flexibility. Therefore, the review classifies conventional optimization and artificial intelligence methods, evaluates their reported performance and practical limitations, and identifies research directions for coordinating generation-side dispatch with demand-side flexibility in renewable power systems.

title: Reassessing the environmental Kuznets curve in Germany through energy transition dynamics using an ARDL approach
abstract: Abstract Germany’s progress toward climate neutrality has often been interpreted through the lens of the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC), which suggests that economic growth eventually leads to declining emissions. This study re-examines the EKC hypothesis by integrating energy transition dynamics into the analysis of carbon dioxide emissions, economic growth, and energy structure in Germany. Using an Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) framework and long-term annual time-series data spanning 1980 to 2024, we compare a conventional EKC specification with an augmented model that explicitly incorporates renewable energy share and non-renewable energy consumption. Results from the conventional model initially support the EKC hypothesis, indicating a long-run decoupling between economic growth and emissions. However, once energy structure variables are included, the EKC relationship weakens considerably, revealing that emissions reductions are primarily driven by structural shifts in the energy system rather than income growth alone. Renewable energy expansion significantly lowers long-run emissions, while fossil energy use exerts strong upward pressure, particularly in the short run. The augmented model also exhibits faster adjustment toward equilibrium, suggesting that policy interventions accelerate environmental improvements. These findings highlight that Germany’s emission…

title: Political Confrontation and Energy Dependence: The Logic, Pathways, and Limits of Russia’s Diplomacy toward Japan
abstract: In this article, using the analytical frameworks of geopolitical economy and the process-tracing method, the author systematically deconstructs the theoretical foundations, historical evolution and the three-dimensional practical model of “trade-development-institutions” of Russian energy diplomacy toward Japan. The study shows that Russia employed comprehensive strategic hedging: by leveraging its energy resources, it not only obtained the necessary capital, technology, and impetus for the development of the Far East, but also, at cer-tain historical moments, effectively created a political split in Japan between “security alignment” and “energy realities”, thereby strengthening its own geopolitical resilience and exerting a profound influence on the energy architecture of Northeast Asia. In conclusion, it is argued that future Russia-Japan energy relations will evolve along a trajectory of “maintaining the achieved level, limited growth, and expansion of the agenda”, as well as in the context of possible extremely limited cooperation in such areas as low-carbon energy.

title: Methods for Transforming Energy Production through Equipment Modernization and the Implementation of Digital Technologies
abstract: The study aims to analyze the methods of equipment modernization, determine the conditions for their effec-tive use, and the sequence of actions during modernization. It examines aspects that have a significant impact on improving such indicators as competitiveness, reliability, and efficiency. The article also presents various methods of equipment modernization, identifies their differences and application possibilities at an enterprise, and identifies their advantages and disadvantages. A summary of all modernization methods is provided. Addi-tionally, the article analyzes the sequence of actions in the modernization process that ensures effective re-placement or retrofitting. A conclusion is formulated on all stages of the modernization process. The main digi-tal technologies that are part of modernization of energy enterprises and contribute to improving the efficiency and reliability of their operation are reviewed. The advantages and disadvantages of these digital technologies are described, along with the results of their application in energy production.

title: The edible energy return on investment in dairy-bred beef finishing in Ireland
abstract: Food production—including beef production—in the industrialised world relies heavily on fossil fuels. At the same time, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change mitigation pathways consistent with keeping global warming below 2 °C estimate reductions of approximately 70–90% in fossil fuel use by 2050 will be necessary. In Ireland, the trend in agriculture is consolidating on intensive dairy production. Male progeny from the national dairy herd are a co-product often sold to specialist beef farms for finishing. This study examined the Edible Energy Return on Energy Invested (EEROI) of a beef finishing farm in Ireland to determine its dependence on external energy inputs. Farm energy inputs were determined and set against the human-edible energy gained during finishing on the farm. Energy inputs included diesel, electricity, and the embodied energy of fertiliser, buildings, machinery, and other infrastructure necessary for beef finishing on the farm. Energy output was defined as the calorific content of the estimated human-edible carcass weight gained during finishing. Energy input totalled 958,938 MJ, and the energy output totalled 81,490.7 MJ, resulting in an EEROI of 0.08:1. When only recurring energy inputs were considered, the EEROI of the farm was 0.18:1 Renewable energy sources accounted for 2.48% of the total energy input. Despite efforts to decarbonise energy system…

title: Metaverse and NFT-Based Digital Ecosystems: Sustainability, Governance, and Energy Trade-Offs
abstract: Metaverse platforms and non-fungible token (NFT) markets are often framed as immaterial, frictionless layers of the digital economy. However, their expansion depends on energy-intensive infrastructures, complex governance arrangements, and regulatory choices that can amplify or mitigate environmental externalities. This article examines sustainability, governance, and energy trade-offs in metaverse and NFT-based ecosystems. The research treats China as a policy and regulatory laboratory. This is to explore the ideas of how "digital collectibles" and platform-based experiments have evolved under tighter constraints on cryptocurrency circulation. Building on a socio-technical perspective, the paper connects three levels of analysis. It maps the material footprint of immersive experiences and tokenized assets, focusing on consensus mechanisms, cloud and data center dependencies, and the risk of rebound effects. The exploration of governance addresses technical standards and platform accountability. In the meantime, it discusses the tensions between openness, interoperability, and enforceable rules. A comparison of regulatory pathways addresses their implications for sustainability metrics, user rights, and market design. The contribution of this research lies in the framework for evaluating whether metaverse and NFT ecosystems can credibly align with sustainability goals without r…

title: Power Allocation Optimization In Hybrid Energy Storage System Based On Low Pass Filter And Artificial Neural Network
abstract: This paper presents optimizing power allocation in hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) by combining Low Pass Filter (LPF) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) techniques. Conventional LPF-based strategies employ fixed cut-off frequencies that cannot adapt to dynamic operating conditions, resulting in suboptimal performance and reduced battery lifespan. This research proposes optimization framework that determines optimal cut-off frequencies through three approaches: cost-based, stress-based, and hybrid optimization. Spectral analysis of requested power confirmed that energy content is predominantly concentrated in low-frequency ranges (10^-6 to 10^-3 Hz), justifying the frequency-based power allocation strategy. The hybrid optimization method yielded an optimal cut-off frequency of 0.0013 Hz, balancing economic and technical considerations with a 15% reduction in battery stress compared to cost-based approaches while increasing system costs by only 8%. The implemented ANN model achieved predictive capability (R² = 0.9728) in determining optimal cut-off frequencies across various operating conditions. Performance evaluations demonstrated that the ANN-based approach produces nearly identical power allocation patterns compared to conventional LPF methods while executing approximately 120 times faster, enabling real-time adaptation to changing system conditions. The combined method…

title: Can regional value-chain integration decouple China's agri-food export growth from production-side direct CO2 attributed to export domestic value added? Evidence from belt and road partner economies
abstract: This study examines whether regional value-chain (RVC) integration can support agri-food export growth while improving the carbon performance of China's export sectors. We build a 2007–2023 bilateral country–industry–year panel for C01 agriculture, forestry, and fishing and C03 food processing across 39 economies currently classified as Belt and Road partners. Asian Development Bank multi-regional input–output tables identify bilateral value-added paths, while Chinese sectoral fossil-energy data and Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change emission factors are used to measure production-side direct fossil-energy CO 2 attributed to export domestic value added. The analysis combines logarithmic mean Divisia index decomposition, fixed-effects models, an external shift-share instrument, value-chain configuration tests, and a within–between decomposition. Four findings stand out. First, long-run carbon-intensity improvement more than offsets cumulative scale and structural pressures. Second, the baseline fixed-effects and IV estimates show a negative overall association between RVC cooperation and absolute production-side direct CO 2 , and this relationship remains negative in post-2013 samples. Third, within established partner–industry relationships, deeper RVC is significantly associated with lower carbon per unit of exports, while the export-scale and absolute-carbon coefficien…

title: ESG Integration in Venture Capital Investment Practices: Evidence from Saudi Arabia's Transforming Entrepreneurial Ecosystem
abstract: Purpose: This study examines the extent and pattern of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) integration within venture capital (VC) investment practices in an emerging market. Focusing on Saudi Arabia, it investigates how ESG considerations enter investment practices, the relative priority assigned to environmental, social, and governance dimensions, and the motivations and constraints shaping their adoption. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study adopts an exploratory and descriptive research design based on a structured survey of 21 VC firms operating in Saudi Arabia. The survey captures ESG practices across investment decision-making, monitoring and reporting, and formalization and infrastructure. It also examines the relative priority of the three ESG dimensions and the motivations and constraints associated with ESG integration. Organizational and investment characteristics of participating VC firms are used to contextualize the findings. Findings: The findings reveal an emerging but uneven pattern of ESG integration. ESG considerations are relatively more evident in investment decision-making, including investment evaluation and, in some cases, rejection of investment opportunities, but remain less developed in formal monitoring, reporting, and organizational infrastructure. ESG integration is distinctly governance-focus, with governance receiving substantially gre…

title: Profitability, Listing Age, Auditor Reputation, and Internet Financial Reporting in Indonesian Energy Companies
abstract: This study examines the relationship between profitability, listing age, auditor reputation, and Internet Financial Reporting (IFR) among energy companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2021–2025. Secondary data were collected from financial statements and corporate websites. Purposive sampling yielded 33 companies and 165 firm-year observations. After removing 16 outliers and one observation due to the Cochrane-Orcutt correction, 148 observations were analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS version 24. IFR was measured using content, timeliness, technology, and user support indicators, while profitability was measured by Return on Assets (ROA), listing age by years since the initial public offering, and auditor reputation by Big Four affiliation. The results indicate that profitability has no significant relationship with IFR (B = −0.014, p = 0.431), whereas listing age (B = 0.003, p < 0.001) and auditor reputation (B = 0.019, p = 0.043) have significant positive relationships. The three variables are jointly significant (F = 21.736, p < 0.001), explaining 29.7% of IFR variation (adjusted R² = 0.297). These findings suggest that longer-listed companies and firms audited by Big Four accounting firms demonstrate higher IFR disclosure, while profitability is not significantly associated with IFR. Although limited to profitable energy companies, thre…

title: The Fate of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) in Municipal Solid Waste Incineration: Atmospheric Emissions from a Waste-to-Energy Plant
abstract: Abstract The atmospheric fate of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) represents a very recent field of research. While ISO and CEN standards are yet under development, PFAS have been identified during the past years in atmospheric emissions, ambient air, and deposition. As high-quality field data are currently scarce, the objectives of this study were to (i) characterize atmospheric PFAS emissions of a state-of-the-art waste-to-energy (WtE) plant under representative operational conditions and (ii) evaluate the emission impact in ambient air in the vicinity of the plant. Results suggest a contribution from the WtE plant at the nearest ambient monitoring location, 450 m downwind of the plant, with a measurable contribution and distinct PFAS fingerprint closely matching the emission profiles independently characterized at two grate incinerator lines. Quantified PFAS emissions do not exceed the temporary assessment framework for ambient air in Flanders. Furthermore, optimization of the activated carbon (AC) dosage achieved a 95% reduction in emissions at line 1, with subsequent emission levels approaching those of field blanks. The waste treatment sector represents a critical frontier of environmental management. Building experimental evidence of potential PFAS releases will be key to ensure comprehensive strategies for responsible PFAS management in the years ahead.

title: In silico guided design and in vivo evaluation of Diacerein loaded SLNs embedded in situ gels for sustained intra-articular osteoarthritis therapy
A Web-Based Registry Framework Linking Transfusion Practice to Long-Term Patient Outcomes: Design and Single-Center Feasibility Study
abstract: Abstract Blood transfusions are among the most common medical interventions performed worldwide. Several comprehensive databases link transfusions to routinely collected health data but do not include the indication and the decision-making basis for a particular administration, nor patient-reported long-term outcomes. We developed a web-based registry for the standardized assessment of transfusion practice and patient outcomes, designed for an observation period of up to 30 years. The framework combines clinical data captured at the point of care with patient-reported outcome measures collected through automated digital follow-up, ensures privacy by design through physical separation of identifying and medical data, and codes diagnoses and procedures in SNOMED CT. We evaluated feasibility in a single-center pilot at Goethe University Hospital Frankfurt (11 September 2024–15 January 2026), with patient-reported follow-up collected through 13 August 2026. A total of 408 patients were enrolled, yielding 1,298 administrations across nine treatment categories in a predominantly cardiac surgical cohort. The pilot demonstrated that the registry integrates into routine clinical workflows, captures the parameters required for guideline-adherence monitoring, and supports sex-disaggregated, descriptive analyses of transfusion practice. Follow-up was completed by 12.5% of patients at 3 mon…

title: Parametric Optimization of Ethanol-Based Adsorption Working Pairs for Sub-Zero Ice Production from Low-Grade Heat: A Source-Driven Design Framework
abstract: Thermally driven adsorption refrigeration offers a compressor-free pathway to sub-zero ice production from low-grade heat. Systematic design guidance for the 65–160 °C range remains limited: existing comparative studies lack consistent system-level constraints, rarely treat cycle time as a coupled variable, and have not addressed the thermodynamic penalties of sub-zero evaporator operation. This study presents a transient lumped-parameter model of a two-bed adsorption ice-making system comparing five ethanol-based working pairs: four activated carbon variants (Maxsorb III, ACF(A-20), KOH4-PR, KOH6-PR) and the metal–organic framework MIL-101(Cr). The Dubinin–Astakhov parameters of all five pairs reproduce the equilibrium measurements of their source studies, with a pooled coefficient of determination of 0.979 over 146 points. At the cycle level, the model reproduces two published chillers: MIL-101(Cr)/ethanol within 4.1% in coefficient of performance (COP) and 7.3% in specific cooling power (SCP), and ACF(A-20)/ethanol within 6.2% in cooling capacity and 5.5% in COP. Performance is mapped across a two-dimensional design space of regeneration temperature and adsorption half-cycle time. KOH4-PR/ethanol delivers the highest specific cooling power from 85 °C upward, reaching 136 W/kg at 160 °C, while Maxsorb III/ethanol activates from 65 °C and performs within 6% of KOH4-PR in SCP a…

title: Efficacy of statistical and design interventions for improving reproducibility in biomedical research
abstract: Abstract Over the past two decades, failures to replicate published findings in biomedical research have led to a perceived reproducibility crisis. Several interventions at the level of inferential statistics and experimental design have been proposed for improving reproducibility. These include raising the power by increasing the sample size, redefining the threshold for statistical significance, focusing on a minimally important difference, adding a penalising term for between-study variation, and combining data from multiple study centres. We used simulations to investigate the effectiveness of these interventions on measures of reproducibility. Artificial data sets were created by repeatedly sampling from defined parametric distributions based on published biomedical studies (i.e. real-world data sets). Reproducibility measures included the probability of positive findings, the probability of consistent inferential outcomes and the chance of capturing the true effect size. The results were mixed: some of the proposed interventions could improve reproducibility, while others had detrimental effects on reproducibility. Notably, the interventions affected the various aspects of reproducibility differently.

title: Kinetic Model for Describing the Spring Effect and Incomplete Dissolution in Low-Solubility Drug Formulations Based on the Quality-by-Design (QbD) Approach
abstract: Background/Objectives: Enhancing the bioavailability of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) with low solubility –classified under the Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS) as class II and class IV –is a major challenge in pharmaceuticals development. Stabilizing APIs in amorphous form significantly increases their apparent solubility but results in complex dissolution profiles characterized by the “spring effect,” a temporal high concentration peak during dissolution. These dissolution profiles are very challenging to be quantitatively evaluated due to the lack of appropriate mathematical models compatible with a Quality-by-Design (QbD) approach. Methods: A kinetic model was developed by considering the mechanistic aspects of the process. The model postulates three stages of the dissolution: hydration and dissolution of the amorphous API within the carrier, diffusion of the dissolved API into the medium, and equilibrium-driven interactions between the dissolved API and its thermodynamically stable crystalline form. Results: This model provides insights into release acceleration, slow final dissolution, and the spring effect, and elucidates scenarios where complete dissolution cannot be achieved due to the absence of sink conditions. While microscopic molecular phenomena –such as liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) and polymeric crystallization inhibition –are exte…

title: From symbolic to substantive: How subsidy design shapes cooperative roles and high-quality rural industrial development?
abstract: Introduction Government subsidies do not necessarily produce high-quality rural industrial development (HQRID), as different subsidy designs elicit different behavioral responses from cooperatives and smallholders. This study examines how subsidy design shapes the strategies of local governments, cooperatives, and farmers. Methods Drawing on the Dingzhuang Grape Cooperative in Jurong, China, this study builds a tripartite evolutionary game model to examine how creation support and function support shape the strategies of the local government, cooperative, and farmer. Results The results distinguish two contrasting pathways. Creation support tends to induce symbolic compliance, in which cooperatives adopt formal structures without providing training, quality control, or market access, leading the system toward a low-quality equilibrium. Function support aligns cooperative incentives with verifiable performance and encourages substantive services that connect smallholders to higher-value markets. Three conclusions follow. First, the transition to substantive service requires function support that gives cooperatives sufficiently strong incentives. Second, substantive services lower the quality-premium share that farmers require, strengthening the economic case for high-quality production. Third, function support is bounded by fiscal capacity, and excessive performance-linked payme…

title: How to tackle inequities in bereavement support for ethnically diverse communities: a national qualitative study using experience-based co-design
Rule-Based Geometric Placement and Optimization-Ready UV Parameterization for Generative Facility Layout Design in BIM Environments: A Proof-of-Concept Preparation Methodology
abstract: Generative design (GD) in Building Information Modelling (BIM) frequently yields infeasible or uninformative alternatives. Within the scope of this study, we examine how GD outcomes relate to preparation before optimization: how placement rules are encoded and how the search space is parameterized so that an evolutionary engine can exploit a stable genotype–phenotype mapping. We present a three-module preparation framework for facility layout GD in BIM, implemented in Dynamo with the NSGA-II-based Revit GD engine. Module A abstracts spaces as rectangular units and maintains a list of valid, unoccupied candidate locations through surface-based containment tests and Boolean-mask filtering. Module B enumerates discrete rotation and adjacency scenarios and prunes true collisions with a tolerance-controlled intersection test (16 of 32 raw scenarios rejected in a worked example). Module C replaces shuffle-based randomization, which re-maps a genotype to a different layout at every evaluation, with a deterministic, locality-preserving normalized-coordinate (UV) encoding. Modules A and B are demonstrated through worked geometric examples and Module C through a synthetic proof-of-concept run with three space groups and piping-length objectives on an irregular site, in which later-generation layouts showed reduced routing values and clustering of connected spaces, consistent with the rep…

title: Support-Modulated Synergy in Dual-Atom Catalysts: Toward Rational Design and Enhanced Mechanisms for CO2 Photoreduction
abstract: With the escalating global energy crisis and intensifying greenhouse effect, solar-driven photocatalytic CO2 reduction technology for producing high-value chemicals or fuels has emerged as a highly promising and crucial strategy to address energy shortages and environmental issues simultaneously. Dual-atom catalysts (DACs), owing to ultrahigh atom utilization, flexibly tunable electronic structures, and unique dual-site synergistic effects, exhibit significant advantages in overcoming the activity limitations of conventional single-atom catalysts (SACs) and optimizing the reaction kinetics of CO2 reduction. As an indispensable component of DACs, the support not only stabilizes the bimetallic active sites and prevents agglomeration, but also modulates the electronic states and coordination environments of the active sites through metal-metal and metal-support interactions, thereby enhancing CO2 adsorption and activation, accelerating charge separation and transfer, and regulating reaction pathways. In this review, we systematically summarize recent advances in DACs for photocatalytic CO2 reduction. Firstly, the design and synthesis strategies alongside advanced characterization techniques, particularly operando spectroscopies and machine learning, for DACs are discussed. Secondly, the synergistic mechanisms between dual atoms and the regulatory effects of various supports, inclu…

title: The Effect of Wordwall-Assisted STAD Cooperative Learning Model to Improve Students' Problem-Solving Ability in Two-Variable Linear Equation Systems for Grade VIII Students at SMP St. Yoseph Medan
abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of the Student Teams Achievement Division (STAD) cooperative learning model assisted by Wordwall on the mathematical problem-solving abilities of eighth-grade students of St. Yoseph Catholic Private Junior High School Medan in the 2025/2026 Academic Year and the improvement of students' mathematical problem-solving abilities after the model is implemented. This study uses a quantitative approach with the Pre-Experimental Design method using the One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. The research sample consisted of 36 students. Data analysis used normality tests, Paired Sample t-Test, and N-Gain. The results showed that the average pretest score of 50.806 increased to 80.167 in the posttest. The results of the hypothesis test obtained tₕᵢₜᵤₙg = 53.303 and tₜₐᵦₑₗ = 2.030, so that H₀ was rejected and Hₐ was accepted. The N-Gain test results obtained an average of 0.611, categorized as moderate. Thus, it can be concluded that the Student Teams Achievement Division (STAD) cooperative learning model assisted by Wordwall has a significant effect and is able to improve students' mathematical problem-solving abilities.

The role of genetic distance in modulating intraspecific plant–soil interactions among a diverse assemblage of tropical tree species seedlings
abstract: Abstract Microbial specialization on host species can promote plant diversity through plant–soil interactions that affect seedling survival and performance. While these processes are typically studied at the interspecific level, emerging evidence suggests that plant–soil interactions can be genotype-specific, contributing to intraspecific density dependence (iDD). However, iDD remains poorly understood in tropical tree species, particularly with respect to its strength and frequency. We hypothesized that genetic distance among conspecific trees should modulate the strength of iDD, and the direction of the effect—positive or negative seedling response—should reflect the net balance of plant–microbe antagonistic and mutualistic interactions. Using a reciprocal planting experiment across eight tropical tree species, we show that genetic distance between conspecific individuals significantly influences seedling responses, consistent with iDD. Yet, the direction of this effect was variable: Castilla tunu showed higher survival and Wettinia aequalis greater biomass in soils from more genetically distant conspecifics, consistent with negative iDD; Inga marginata exhibited positive iDD; five species exhibited no pattern. These findings demonstrate that genotype-specific plant–soil interactions can generate biologically relevant but variable impacts on seedling responses. This highlight…

Participation without power: community-based organisations and the limits of collaborative forest governance in Ghana's Offinso Forest District
abstract: Purpose Community-based organisations (CBOs) are widely promoted as the institutional link between state forestry agencies and forest-fringe communities in sub-Saharan Africa, yet evidence on whether this arrangement transfers genuine authority to communities, rather than simply relabelling their exclusion, remains limited. This paper examines how forest-fringe households in Ghana's Offinso Forest District evaluate the governance role of CBOs and asks whether that evaluation is grounded in functioning participatory mechanisms or in something else. Design/methodology/approach The paper draws on a structured household survey of 300 respondents across four forest-fringe communities (Abofour, Derma, Asempaneye and Akumadan), analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests of association, independent-samples t-tests and multiple linear regression. Findings Respondents endorse CBOs' governance role almost unanimously, yet the mechanisms that would make that role substantive-joint planning, training, incentives and transparent decision-making are reported as absent or minimal by the same respondents. A regression model explaining 47% of the variance in governance evaluations shows that perceived institutional barriers are the strongest positive predictor of positive CBO evaluation, while satisfaction with consultation mechanisms is a significant negative predictor, net of demo…

title: Rhizobium-assisted organic-mineral fertilization improves faba bean productivity and soil functioning in marginally saline soil
The Role of China in the Formation of a New Balance of Power in Central Asia
abstract: The article examines China’s role in reshaping the balance of power in Central Asia. Unlike the researchers that reduce the proper state’s attitude to military capabilities or to a simple sum of trade indexes, the author proposes an operational model of the countries’ features consisting of the following five groups of indicators: economic dependence, infrastructural connectivity, institutional density, security, and the diplomatic agency of the region’s states. Based on a comparative analysis of China, Russia, the EU, and the United States as well as case studies of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan, the article shows that China is forming the most stable economic and infrastructural pole of influence, but it is not turning this region into a monolithic sphere of control. Central Asian states use the China factor to diversify routes, trade, and external relations, however, their range for maneuver is distinct: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan possess broader negotiating auton-omy, whereas Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan are more sensitive to debt and infrastructure limits.

Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning based demand response and energy management for heavy industries with discrete manufacturing systems
abstract: Energy-centric decarbonization of heavy industries, such as steel and cement, necessitates their participation in integrating Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and effective Demand Response (DR) programs. This situation has created the opportunities to research control algorithms in diverse DR scenarios. Further, the industrial sector’s unique challenges, including the diversity of operations and the need for uninterrupted production, bring unique challenges in designing and implementing control algorithms. Reinforcement learning (RL) methods are practical solutions to the unique challenges faced by the industrial sector. Nevertheless, research in RL for industrial demand response has not yet achieved the level of standardization seen in other areas of RL research, hindering broader progress. To propel the research progress, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL)-based energy management system designed to optimize energy consumption in energy-intensive industrial settings by leveraging dynamic pricing DR schemes. The study highlights the creation of a MARL environment and addresses these challenges by designing a general framework that allows researchers to replicate and implement MARL environments for industrial sectors. The proposed framework incorporates a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) to model energy consumption and production processes w…

title: Energy poverty and children’s subjective well-being: evidence from young lives data
abstract: This study examines the impact of energy poverty on the subjective well-being of children in four developing countries: Ethiopia, India, Peru, and Vietnam. We assess energy poverty using a multidimensional approach, leveraging data from the Young Lives study, which conducted surveys in 2006, 2009, 2013, and 2016 (Rounds 2 to 5). Our analysis focuses on the young cohort (Rounds 3 to 5) and the older cohort (Rounds 2 to 5), as these rounds include questions on children’s subjective well-being. To mitigate potential endogeneity concerns and establish causal relationships, we employ a two-stage least squares regression, using residential electricity prices at the country level as an instrumental variable. Our findings reveal that energy poverty significantly reduces children’s subjective well-being, with boys and older children more affected. Robustness checks confirm the validity of these results. Additionally, we find that health status mediates the impact of energy poverty on children’s well-being, highlighting the importance of targeted policy interventions.

title: Market-oriented operational strategy for biomass-geothermal combined power generation and hydrogen production plant
Capacity remuneration mechanisms for decarbonized power systems
abstract: Motivated by generation system adequacy concerns, many European countries have introduced capacity remuneration mechanisms (CRMs) to ensure sufficient investments in power generation . However, it is uncertain whether the existing CRMs will promote sufficient adequacy and flexibility in a decarbonized power system , where supply and demand will become more weather-dependent. We assess the effectiveness of a centralized capacity market, a strategic reserve , and a decentralized capacity market via capacity subscriptions in a climate-neutral, weather-driven power system. We develop a co-simulation of two agent-based models simulating myopia in both operational and investment decisions. We simulate weather uncertainty by running the model with 40 different weather years. Our results from a case study based on the Netherlands indicate that a strategic reserve may increase electricity price volatility in the long-term. A centralized capacity market is more cost-effective than a strategic reserve, but administratively setting its parameters is prone to over- or underprocurement. Capacity subscription allows consumers to select their desired level of reliability. Results indicate that these decentralized capacity markets may yield a clearer signal for the needed dispatchable capacity and promote demand-side response, but it may be challenging to provide long-term certainty for investo…

title: Local energy monitoring to support smart energy management and decarbonized town development
abstract: Introduction With the increase in variable renewable energy and liberalization of the electricity retail market, the integrated energy management of demand and supply has become crucial, complementing traditional energy-saving efforts. Therefore, high-resolution energy demand-side information, accounting for household attributes and owned equipment, is essential. However, previous studies have identified energy consumption based on surveys of utility bill payments; this approach does not provide detailed, hourly data on electricity demand, which changes over time owing to lifestyle patterns and weather conditions. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the actual electricity consumption in residential buildings in Shinchi Town using the developed electricity monitoring system.Material and Method In support of regional disaster recovery initiatives, we developed a regional information and communication technology (ICT) system as a network interface for residents. As part of a social experiment, network terminals of the local ICT system were distributed to approximately 100 households in the town. Power monitoring data were collected via equipment installed in home distribution boards and centrally managed by a cloud server.Results and Conclusion We analyzed electric power consumption patterns, focusing on household attributes, seasonal variations in hot-water-supply device usage, an…
